# Factory learnings ledger

## 4K IS THE DEFAULT (Miguel, 2026-08-10 — "worth it 100%")

- Deliverables render 2160x3840. Mechanism (CLI has no scale flag): keep the
  1080x1920 design space, add `zoom:2` to `#root` and set
  `data-width="2160" data-height="3840"`. Text/SVG/logos re-rasterize truly
  crisp; layout geometry is untouched (verified frame-identical on run 5).
- Faces: cut at native 4K — `crop=2208:2160:816:0,scale=2160:2116` from the 4K
  cut master (the crop region exceeds 2160, so no upscaling). The 1080
  face_bottom files are legacy.
- Outro chip signs `@migueltorrezai` (not "Miguel Torrez AI") since 2026-08-10.
  Chip text is lowercase — some gen chip classes carry text-transform:uppercase;
  force `text-transform:none` inline on the handle span.
- **THE BED IS `bed_split_v2.mp3`** (2026-08-10): the original bed_split.mp3 has
  a vocal intro Miguel rejected — NEVER use it again. v2 = same jazzy 87 BPM
  brief, strictly instrumental, 51.96s. When forking old projects, swap the
  project-local `assets/music/bed_split.mp3` for v2 (batch of 2026-08-10 did
  this for all 30 run-5 4K projects). Any pipeline change that touches audio
  MUST re-confirm which bed ships — assuming the bundled bed cost a full
  30-video re-render.
- 4K render cost ≈ same order as 1080 (~2 min/video). **Do NOT run multiple 4K
  renders in parallel**: 4 concurrent renders × 3 workers each made the face
  <video> intermittently fail to paint and HyperFrames' blank-clip coverage
  gate (correctly) aborted 16 renders on 2026-08-10. Safe mode: ONE render at
  a time with `-w 8`; the per-render workers parallelize fine, cross-render 4K
  video decode does not. Never disable the coverage gate to "fix" this. Raster embeds (x-cards) are the
  only soft element at 4K — re-render cards at 2x when they matter.
- Template: `shorts_run5/run_4k_batch.sh` (faces → patch → render → +120ms
  audio remux → 4K 3-ups at 1080-wide cells).

## A/V SYNC (2026-08-10, fixed)

- Recordings before 2026-08-10 have audio ~120ms EARLY vs video: Shure MV7+
  (USB, ~10ms) vs ZV-E10 → Cam Link 4K (~120ms). Measured via bilabial frame
  strips (p/b lip release 3-4 frames after the Scribe burst, consistent across
  recordings). OBS now has +120ms sync offset on the MV7+ (both profiles) —
  recordings AFTER 2026-08-10 are natively synced; do NOT double-compensate.
- Run-4/run-5 output mp4s were remuxed with audio +120ms (stream copy).
  Consequence: captions/top-zone animations (timed to the transcript clock)
  lead the shifted audio by ~120ms in those files — acceptable trade, lip sync
  wins. The cut masters in shorts_run1/cuts/ were NOT shifted (transcript
  timings still match them exactly); builds from those masters inherit the
  120ms lag and need the same remux post-render.
- Audit method (reusable): pick words starting p/b/m after >=0.18s gaps from
  transcript_tight.json, extract 12-frame mouth strips at the word start
  (burst at cell 8), read the strip — lips must release at the burst cell.

## Seeded from run 3 (2026-08-09)

- [productivity] Tween helpers carrying `opacity` only in FROM vars render
  invisible under direct seek (boundary `tl.set(opacity:0)` wins). Always put
  opacity in TO vars.
- [meatwrapper] White filled rounded nodes on cream read as "tweet cards" to the
  Gemini judge. Use dashed borders or tinted fills for non-tweet nodes.
- [all] Snapped `steps()` counters must LAND inside the phrase naming them.
- [fablevssol] Caption echo: top-zone text repeating 3+ consecutive caption
  words verbatim is a real QC fail. Key terms must compress, not transcribe.
- [audit] GSAP fromTo immediateRender paints later tweens' from-values at build
  time (phantom visibles). geometry_audit.py primes the timeline before
  sweeping; renders are unaffected because they sweep forward.
- [whiteboard] Annotations drawn OVER content (rings, strokes, outro chip on
  dimmed canvas) must carry `data-overlap-ok` or the geometry audit flags them.

## Gate-chain pass, run 3 (2026-08-10)

- [hermes_diagram] Law 8 escape that BOTH other gates missed: geometry audit is
  0-error and Gemini QC v3 passed, but `ladder.png` is a 362x352 raster blown up
  to 465x452 in a 1080-wide frame. Its fine print (`24 tools -> full listing`,
  `3,320 tools -> server hint + search`) is ~11px in-frame = unreadable on a
  phone. **Neither gate 1 nor gate 3 measures source-vs-rendered pixel ratio** —
  geometry only sees boxes, Gemini reads the frame at full res so small type
  looks fine to it. Cheap deterministic check worth adding: flag any `<img>`
  whose natural width < its rendered width (upscaled raster = legibility risk).
  Only the headwords survived at short-size; crop to the crucial region instead.

  short — an orphan ordinal the viewer cannot resolve. Crop the number out.

  caption: Miguel says "procedural disclosure" (verbal slip), the card shows
  PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE (the real term). Only "disclosure" overlaps, so it is
  under the 3-consecutive-word caption-echo bar and it fixes a factual error.
  Do not "correct" the graphic down to the misspoken word.
- [all] `frame_review.py` prints an IDLE-MOTION CANDIDATE block only for >6s
  runs where dedup dropped nothing. A lone `[still Ns before this]` marker is
  the OPPOSITE signal (confirmed stillness = law 1 compliance), not a candidate.
  Do not report those markers as idle candidates.
- [all] Tweet-discipline check reads straight off the frames: hermes tweet is up
  0.0-~3.0s with the claim line ringed at 2.3s and zero metrics in the crop —
  inside the 2-4s window. Reading 3 frames around the open is enough to clear
  Law 3; no need to parse the timeline.
- [all] A beat handoff can leave the top zone fully EMPTY for ~1s (hermes
  t=50.7, only the caption chip on cream). No law forbids it, but it reads as a
  dead frame right before the outro — worth a hold-over on the outgoing element.

## Gate-chain pass — grokbuild / whiteboard (2026-08-10)

- [grokbuild_whiteboard] **Zero-ink layout wrappers are the #1 source of fake
  geometry errors.** All 6 errors + all 6 warnings in this project trace to two
  wrapper patterns, none visible in the render:
  (a) full-canvas beat groups `<div id="w-A|w-C|w-D|w-E|w-F|w-PH"
  style="left:0;top:0;width:1080px;height:862.5px">` — their bottom edge IS the
  caption seam, so every beat group emits a "within 24px of caption seam"
  warning, and their box covers everything, so they "collide" with siblings
  (w-C ∩ wo-chipw, w-E ∩ w-hl0);
  (b) the outro chip wrapper `<div id="wo-chipw" style="width:885px;
  text-align:center">` whose visible ink is only the centered inner `<span
  class="ctachip">` — it produced 4 of the 6 errors (vs w-h1, w-h3, w-os1,
  w-ring2). Fix: put `data-overlap-ok` on centering wrappers and beat groups, or
  size the wrapper to its content. Do NOT "fix" the children.
- [grokbuild_whiteboard] The wrapper also has no opacity of its own (only the
  inner span animates), so the audit sees it live from 47.5s–68.5s while the
  chip is not painted until 72.7s. A geometry window that does not match when the
  element is actually visible on screen = look for an unanimated wrapper.
- [grokbuild_whiteboard] The LEARNINGS-noted escape "cost-axis line strikes
  through the GROK BUILD label" does NOT appear in the rendered frames: at 47.7s,
  56.3s, 64.7s and 68.3s the axis rule sits above the label row and the
  OPEN SOURCE / GROK BUILD / FRONTIER labels clear it. Verify escapes against
  frames before reworking a generator.
- [grokbuild_whiteboard] Checklist labels that are 2-word verbatim echoes of the
  concurrent caption ("generate videos", "generate images", "handle workflows")
  stay under the 3-consecutive-word caption-echo fail line and read as the
  approved Steps & Checklist move. Two words is the working ceiling.
- [gate 2] Frame filenames switch to MMSS past 60s: t=1:04.7 is `f_0104_666.jpg`,
  NOT `f_0064_666.jpg`. Reading late frames by seconds silently 404s.
- [gate 2] Idle-motion candidates are printed in `manifest.md` only when a >6s
  run survives dedup; a manifest with no IDLE section = zero candidates, it is
  not a missing feature. This one had 52/219 states and clean stillness holds of
  5.7s / 4.7s / 3.7s.

## Gate-chain pass — hermes / whiteboard (2026-08-10)

- [gate1] **`overflow:hidden` odometer counters produce phantom collision ERRORS.**
  Root cause found in `geometry_audit.py`: when an element has no background and
  no border it is measured by a DOM `Range.selectNodeContents()` box (`cr`, used
  for collisions at lines 212-213) — and a Range box IGNORES `overflow:hidden`.
  A roll-up counter (`<div id="wow" style="height:74.6px;overflow:hidden">`
  wrapping a 5-row 373px strip translated by GSAP) is therefore measured 5x too
  tall, reaching ~300px UP the canvas into whatever sits above it. Verified
  numerically on hermes_whiteboard: reported `wn2 ∩ wow = 41%` reproduces exactly
  as 183.7x92.6 / (367.5x112.5) = 41.1%, and `wow ∩ wpay = 43%` the same way —
  yet the rendered frames at 42.7s / 46.3s / 50.7s show the two elements far
  apart with clean whitespace. Fix on the generator side: give the clipping
  wrapper a background/border or `data-overlap-ok`. Real fix: skip `cr` when
  `getComputedStyle(el).overflow` is hidden/clip. Every Counter & Meter lane
  short with a rolling odometer is exposed to this.
- [whiteboard] Extend the existing overlay rule: the Law-9 KEY TERM debut drawn
  over the dimmed icon grid is also an intentional overlap and needs
  `data-overlap-ok`. hermes_whiteboard's other "error" (`wg ∩ wk1 = 89%`,
  13.55-15.05s) is exactly that — PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE center-stage on the
  faded 12-tool grid, which is the lane's whole point. So on this short BOTH
  gate-1 errors were non-defects: one undeclared intentional overlay, one
  pipeline measurement bug. Zero pixels needed changing.
- [whiteboard] The lane worked as designed here and is worth copying: one canvas
  from 3.7s to 50.7s, grid -> X-strikes -> arrow -> TOOL SEARCH -> ONE TOOL
  LOADED, with the context meter and its counter persisting the whole way and
  the canvas shrinking into the outro instead of cutting. 45 distinct states from
  163 samples, longest hold 4.7s, zero idle candidates.

## Run 4 build pass — deepresearch / icon (2026-08-10)

- [deepresearch_icon] **The v1.1 seam promotion turns every full-zone zero-ink wrapper into a
  build-blocking ERROR.** run-3 `deepresearch_icon` wrapped its whole outro in
  `wrap("ow", 0, 44, 576, 416, ...)`; that div's bottom edge sits at design y=460 = 862.5px =
  SEAM_Y exactly, so under v1.1 (`SEAM_Y-12 < bottom <= SEAM_Y+2` = error) it fails, where in
  run 3 it was only the "within 24px" warning. Any lane whose outro (or beat group) uses a
  zone-height wrapper is exposed. Fix: place the outro atoms directly in the section — do NOT
  reach for `data-bleed`, which silences the seam law rather than obeying it.
- [deepresearch_icon] **Meters belong INSIDE their plate, and that is also the honest way to
  kill the `floating` warning.** `geometry_audit.py` skips any `.rule` whose drawn extent is
  >=90% contained in a `shot`/`isBox` atom (ltile/node/shot/chip). Moving each agent progress
  meter from "12px under the tile" to "inset in the bottom of the tile" removed 4 warnings AND
  satisfies FILL THE SHAPE. A meter placed just below a tile can never pass: the end-proximity
  test needs `ey <= tile.bottom + 14px`, which a visually comfortable gap always exceeds.
- [deepresearch_icon] The run-3 3-dot/2-line "connection" glyph is broken **provably**, not just
  visually: its two links start at (0.28u,0.385u) and (0.52u,0.305u) and run 0.28u at ±56°,
  landing at (0.437,0.153) and (0.677,0.537) — none of which is any of its three dot centres
  ((0.50,0.19), (0.23,0.73), (0.77,0.73)). Rebuild it with centre-to-centre segments (compute
  length = hypot, angle = degrees(atan2), transform-origin left center). STANDARD's ASSET
  HEALTH note is confirmed by arithmetic, not taste.
- [gate2] **Opaque zone pairs make black holes at every cut.** Sections are opaque full-zone
  backgrounds on ascending track indices, so the incoming zone covers the outgoing one from its
  `data-start` — anything the incoming beat does not paint until its first tween is a *dead
  frame*, not a crossfade. run-3 `deepresearch` beat 4 opened its panel at `CUE["read"]`=34.32
  while the beat starts at 33.30: **1.0 second of fully black top zone**, which the Gemini
  visual gate lists as a FAIL kind ("blank or black zones") and which gate 1 cannot see at all.
  Same class at the CTA: the outro's first logo popped at t0+0.16 = 5 black frames. Rule of
  thumb: **every beat must paint something within ~0.1s of its own data-start.**
- [gate2] This is the second run-4 confirmation that gate 2 is the only gate that catches
  timing/emptiness defects: gate 1 was 0-error and gate 3 passed on the first call *after* the
  fix — had the dead frames shipped, gate 3 would have been the only thing between them and
  Miguel, and it is a paid judge with known noise.
- [deepresearch_icon] Warning classes it is correct to ship with (all `floating`, verified
  against frames): an arrow whose shaft is measured without its head (the audit reads
  `ruleRect`, and `arrow()` reserves the last 12 design px for the triangle, so a shaft always
  stops ~22px short of the target edge); diagonal connectors, whose AABB mid-left/mid-right
  points are not their endpoints; strike-through rules over struck rows. 10 such warnings here
  vs 16 in run 3, with the only real finding (seam) fixed.
- [deepresearch_icon] Judge-noise datapoint for the next worker: run 3's second QC call on this
  same lane failed with "Caption displays 'one drop a day' instead of matching spoken audio" —
  the judge read the outro's serif tagline (design y=282, ~529px, nowhere near the 862.5px
  seam) as a caption. Run 4 kept the tagline, moved it above the FOLLOW node, and QC passed
  first call with zero errors. If that verdict reappears, it is noise: check the y-position of
  the text before touching the design.

## Run 4 — deepresearch / checklist (2026-08-10)

- [deepresearch_checklist] **The caption pill rises ABOVE the seam — the audit's seam
  band is not the real no-go line.** `.scappill` is centred on the seam
  (`translateY(-50%)`), so at the largest caption size its TOP edge sits ~57px above
  design y=460, i.e. around design y=430. `geometry_audit.py` only flags bottoms in the
  838-864px band (design 447-461), so an outro stack ending at design y=437 audits
  0-error/0-warning and still gets visibly overlapped by the pill. Verified on the
  run-3-style outro: chip bottom 819px vs pill top ~806px. **Rule: no top-zone ink below
  design y≈420** (≈788px). Every lane's outro/CTA stack is exposed to this.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **Arrow shafts that stop short of their head read as floating
  ends.** `geometry_audit.py` measures the inner `.rule`, not the triangle, so the run-3
  `arrow()` (shaft = length - head) always ends `head` px shy of the target box —
  22.5px at head=12, past the 14px `CONNECTOR_END_TOL`. Fix in the generator: run the
  shaft the FULL length and position the head over its last `head` px (same colour, the
  render is pixel-identical). Killed 3/3 floating warnings in one edit; this is the same
  warning class the hermes/deepresearch run-3 projects all carried.
- [deepresearch_checklist] Fading only a connector's inner `.rule` leaves its wrapper
  opaque, and the audit keeps measuring it — run 3's key-term underline stayed "on
  screen" 10.5-14.5s after it was invisible. Give the wrapper an id and `leave()` it too.
- [deepresearch_checklist] `isBox` in the audit is `ltile|node|shot|chip` — a `.card`
  panel is NOT a box, so any connector terminating on a card is always "floating".
  Adding `node` to the panel's class list (as `class="abs card node"`) makes it anchorable
  without changing the render (`.card` is defined after `.node`, so it wins the paint) and
  without joining the `abs node` equality group (the group test uses `startswith`).
- [deepresearch_checklist] **FILL THE SHAPE, implemented cleanly:** make the tick a CHILD
  of its checkbox at `left:0;top:0;width:100%;height:100%` with the box's radius minus the
  border. It fills the shape exactly, inherits the rounded-square language, and is
  invisible to the collision pass (identical rects → the ≥0.96 containment skip). Beats
  the run-3 pattern of a sibling circle laid over a square box, which was both the banned
  shape and a collision candidate.
- [deepresearch_checklist] To centre a checklist block AND keep the boxes on a shared left
  edge, wrap the rows in `display:inline-block; text-align:left` inside a full-width
  `text-align:center` div carrying `data-overlap-ok`. Exact centring with zero text-width
  estimation — the alternative (fixed label widths) mis-centres by 7-15px because Poppins
  800 advances are unpredictable.
- [deepresearch_checklist] Two real defects passed BOTH free gates and were only caught by
  reading headless screenshots before rendering: the 6-bar "employee" brief sitting on the
  card's bottom border (containment skip hides it) and the outro/caption overlap above.
  **A 30-line playwright screenshot script over the built HTML is the cheapest gate in the
  chain** — it costs seconds, runs before the 68s render, and sees what neither the
  geometry audit nor the manifest can.
- [deepresearch_checklist] Checklist-lane beat 1 has an unavoidable sparse window (one row
  on cream, 3.3-7.4s) because the key term cannot debut before its first utterance and the
  logos cannot precede the naming. Gemini QC v3 passed it clean — do not stuff the top zone
  to fill it; sparse beats text (law 4).
- [deepresearch_checklist] Clean run: geometry 3 rounds (0/3w → 0/0 → 0/0), 46 distinct
  states from 149 samples, 0 idle candidates, longest hold 4.0s, QC v3 pass on round 1
  (0 visual, 0 semantic errors).

## Run 4 build — hackers / icon (2026-08-10)

- [hackers_icon] **geometry_audit.py only measures SECTION CHILDREN, so a
  full-zone group wrapper makes a whole short unauditable.** `SNAPSHOT_JS` does
  `atoms = Array.from(sec.children)` — one level, no descent. The run-3 hackers
  generator wrapped every beat in `<div id="bN-g" style="width:1080px;
  height:862.5px">`, so the audit saw exactly 5 boxes (4 beats + `o-g`), scored
  "0 errors, 5 seam warnings", and never looked at a single tile, label, ring or
  chip. Deleting the wrappers immediately surfaced a REAL error the gate had been
  blind to for two runs: the two key-term display lines overlapped 24% (the
  opening stepped lines by 1.06x the font size while `wordline`'s own glyph box
  is 1.10x). Any generator whose audit output is only wrapper-shaped findings is
  not actually being audited — check `report.json`'s element ids against your
  real ids before trusting a 0-error verdict.
- [hackers_icon] You do NOT need DOM wrappers for group opacity/dim/move. GSAP
  accepts a comma-joined multi-selector (`tl.to("#a,#b,#c",{opacity:0})`), so an
  ex-wrapper "group" becomes an explicit id list and every atom stays a
  measurable section child. Two gotchas: (a) exclude any element that was
  already faded out from a later group DIM, or `to(opacity:0.26)` RESURRECTS it
  from 0 (the beat-3 crack bar); (b) group fade-INs are usually redundant once
  the wrapper is gone, because each child's own `pre()` already sets opacity 0
  at t=0.
- [hackers_icon] `hlring()` built rings with `class="abs"` only, so the audit's
  `isRing` exemption never fired and highlight rings were judged as solid boxes.
  Add `class="abs ring"` + `data-overlap-ok`. (Rotated rings are also auto-exempt
  via the `rotated` check, which is why the tilted cage ring never flagged.)
- [hackers_icon] BUILD ORDER is about connectors and chrome, NOT about
  slot-then-fill. Delaying beat 1's three dashed slots to 0.3s before each logo
  left the whiteboard holding one 12px kicker for 3.3s, and staggering the
  5-segment meter track left two orphan blocks with no visible scale. Both were
  pulled EARLIER after a screenshot sweep. The defect Miguel named is a connector
  drawn before its node (the beat-3 arrow existed 0.7s before the plate it points
  at) and chrome for content that never starts — a slot that visibly receives its
  own logo 2s later is the flagship lane's whole choreography.
- [hackers_icon] Cheap pre-render check worth copying: drive the same
  `SNAPSHOT_JS` from geometry_audit.py in Playwright, screenshot the top zone at
  ~20 chosen timestamps, and read them as one contact sheet. It costs ~15s, needs
  no render, and it is the only thing that catches DEAD AIR (empty top zone, a
  0.25s blank-cream beat handoff, a meter with no track) — geometry audit sees no
  violation in an empty frame and Gemini rarely calls it.
- [hackers_icon] Outro defect class confirmed on this video: the four check
  badges sat at y=326 while the orange underline occupied 325.2-332.2 — the
  "AI icons touching the divider" Miguel flagged is literally a corner-badge
  offset colliding with the rule. Deleting the badges fixed both the seam law and
  OUTRO ALIGNMENT, since checkmarks on outro logos assert nothing.
- [hackers_icon] A highlight ring and a same-colour baseline rule 4px apart read
  as one doubled line, and a ring whose box is crossed by a full-width rule reads
  as broken. Neither is catchable by the audit (thin bars are collision-exempt,
  rings are annotation-exempt) — both were found by reading gate-2 frames. Give
  terracotta rings ~12px of air from terracotta rules, and size a ring to the
  marks it holds rather than to the whole row.
- [gate2] `frame_review.py`'s 16x16-gray dedup can collapse caption-only changes
  (a ~500x76px pill in a 1080x960 crop moves the 256-cell mean by ~1-2, under the
  2.0 threshold). A `[still 4.0s]` marker therefore does not prove the frame was
  frozen — hackers_icon's 7.7-11.7s "hold" contains a logo landing at 10.5s.
  Read the frames at both ends before calling a long gap a defect or a virtue.

## Run 4 — grokprice / counter (2026-08-10)

- [grokprice_counter] **DUPLICATE DOM IDs SILENTLY DISABLE ANIMATIONS, and no gate
  sees it.** Run 3's grokprice counter named the beat-4 header chip `cp0` AND the
  capability tiles `cp0..cp3`, so `#b4-cp0` resolved to the chip: the REASONING
  tile received no tween at all and sat fully painted from the beat's first frame
  (25.2s, ~2.4s early), while the chip fired its entrance twice. Gate 1 cannot
  catch it (`key_of` collapses both atoms to one key, and a permanently-visible
  element is perfectly legal geometry); Gate 3 passed it too. Cheap standing check
  to run on the emitted HTML before every render:
  duplicate `id="..."`, tween selectors with no matching id, and section-child ids
  that carry no tween at all. All three were clean after the fix (129 ids, 68
  selectors, only `b2-odw` untweened and that one legitimately inherits its parent
  tile's entrance).
- [grokprice_counter] **Display serif with `line-height:0.9` collides through its
  FONT inline box, not its CSS box.** Gate 1 measures unpainted text with a DOM
  Range, which returns the inline box (~1.25em for Instrument Serif) centred on a
  0.9em line box — i.e. ~18px of negative half-leading bleeding out of the top AND
  bottom of the layout box at fs 100px. Three of my round-1 errors were exactly
  this (`−40%` kissing the meter above it, outro `FOLLOW` kissing its kicker).
  Budget ~0.2em of invisible margin above and below any `.ser`/`.serink` block.
- [grokprice_counter] **frame_review.py's dedup is blind to hollow rings.** A 3px
  terracotta highlight ring over ~470x230px of dark canvas moves the 16x16
  grayscale signature by ~0.7 mean abs diff against a 2.0 threshold, so a REAL
  Law-5 highlight event is collapsed and the manifest reports a `[still 4.7s]`
  hold across it. Do not "fix" a hold the manifest reports without extracting the
  mid-hold frame with ffmpeg first — mine showed the ring exactly where it should
  be. Corollary: solid fills, tiles and text all trip the dedup fine; only thin
  strokes are invisible to it.
- [grokprice_counter] **New Gate-3 judge-noise class: tweet duration inherits the
  beat's duration.** The visual judge failed the short with "tweet on screen for
  approximately 8 seconds (00:00-00:08)"; the tweet actually left at 3.05s and
  00:08.52 is where the enclosing DARK section ends. Refute deterministically by
  sampling the card's rect in the rendered mp4 and printing the white-pixel
  fraction per second (0.892 at 0.5/1.5/2.5/2.9 → 0.000 from 3.1 on). Re-running
  the unchanged gate then passed clean, visual and semantic. Suspect this class
  whenever a duration complaint matches a section boundary rather than an element.
- [grokprice_counter] **METERS COMPLETE has a legitimate escape hatch: make the
  BASELINE bar the one that reaches 100%.** Miguel's complaint was a bar that grew
  full then retracted to 60% and sat there. A two-bar WAS/NOW chart where WAS
  fills the whole track and NOW lands on its exact proportion reads as data, not
  as an unfinished meter — and it is the same language the cheap-vs-regular
  comparison already used. Rule of thumb: every track on screen must either be
  full or be visibly the short bar of a pair whose partner is full.
- [grokprice_counter] **Animate meter fills by `width`, never `scaleX`.** scaleX
  squashes the fill's `border-radius` horizontally, so a 25%-filled bar has a
  flat-ish cap while its track keeps a full pill radius — a FILL THE SHAPE
  violation that is invisible in code review and obvious on a phone. Width tweens
  (with the element authored at `width:0` and `immediateRender:false`) keep the
  cap identical to the track at every frame.
- [grokprice_counter] Segmented meters are a trap for the same law: four segments
  with `border-radius` only on the outer two produce pinched joints, so the bar
  never reads as finished even when the last segment lands on the track's end.
  One continuous fill stepping to 100% is the fix.
- [grokprice_counter] The dashed placeholder slot is a good build move but ONLY
  when it is the tile's exact silhouette — same box AND same radius. Run 3 used
  the `.slot` class default (r16) under r20 tiles, so the dashed corners poked out
  around every filled tile. Pass the tile's radius through to its slot. Bonus: the
  same slot->tile language applied to the price cells removed a ~0.6s near-empty
  cream handoff frame at a beat boundary.
- [gate2] A beat opening that shows only a logo row on an empty canvas for ~0.6s
  still gets kept as a distinct state by the 3fps sampler, so it is worth reading
  the frame right after every `data-start` boundary — that is where dead handoff
  frames hide.

## Run 4 build — deepresearch / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [deepresearch_diagram] **BUILD ORDER has two failure modes, not one.** Fixing
  "stem before its logo" by firing each stem on its own logo just moves the dangle
  to the far end: the stem then hangs toward a rail that does not exist yet (3s of
  a wire into nothing). A shared rail/bus is one harness — lay it only after every
  node it touches exists, then the tap-ins, then the drop. Same rule for any
  many-to-one connector (the beat-2 convergence lines must wait for the panel).
- [deepresearch_diagram] **An opacity-0 rule still measures full size.** The run-3
  key-term underline was faded + hard-killed but kept `scaleX:1`, so gate 1 saw a
  live 168px connector for 5s after it visually left (one phantom `floating`
  warning). Exits for drawn rules must collapse `scaleX`, not just opacity.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **The v1.1 seam ERROR fires on zero-ink layout wrappers.**
  The run-3 outro wrapped its whole composition in `<div left:0 top:44 w:576
  h:416>` whose bottom edge is *exactly* the seam (862.5) — an automatic gate-1
  error now. Lay outro atoms directly in the zone, or size the wrapper to content.
  Every lane that reused that `wrap("ow", 0, 44, 576, 416, ...)` helper is exposed.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **Beat handoffs need a hold-over.** Beat 4 owning the
  screen from 33.30 while its first element was cued on a spoken word at 34.32
  rendered a fully blank cream top zone for ~1.0s. Gate 1 cannot see it (nothing to
  measure) and Gemini passed run 3 with it in place — only gate 2's frame read
  catches it. Fix by extending the outgoing beat to ~0.06s before the incoming
  beat's first cue, not by adding an early placeholder.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **Same class, container edition:** a panel/card that lands
  on a cue and waits 1.9s for its rows is "chrome before content". Pace the fill so
  the container's contents start ~0.5s after it lands and the LAST item still hits
  the word that justifies it.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **Gate 2 dedup is blind to cream-on-cream.** A white node
  with a grey border, and a dashed grey placeholder, both move the 16x16 gray
  metric by less than the 2.0 threshold, so `distinct_states` undercounts and a
  3s "stillness gap" can actually contain two build events. Do not treat a gap as
  proof of stillness on the cream canvas; a Playwright seek + screenshot at 4-6
  chosen times before rendering is the cheap way to verify low-contrast builds
  (it also caught the key term debuting *on top of* the dashed slot, with the
  dashed border running straight through the display type).
- [deepresearch_diagram] Arrow helper fix worth copying: making the head overlap the
  shaft (`shaft = length - head*0.5`, head positioned at `length - head`) keeps the
  tip exactly on the target edge AND puts the measured rule end within the audit's
  14px tolerance — dropped 7 false `floating` warnings with zero visual change.
- [deepresearch_diagram] `.card` is not in the audit's box set (`ltile|node|shot|
  chip`), so connectors terminating on a card always read as floating. Adding
  `node` to the card's class list makes the panel a real edge — honest, and it does
  not change the rendering (`.card` wins the shared properties).

## Run 4 build pass — hackers / kinetic (2026-08-10)

- [hackers_kinetic] **`growx()` never painted its line at all.** The helper put
  `opacity` in the FROM vars only (`fromTo({scaleX:0,opacity:1},{scaleX:1,...})`)
  with a boundary `tl.set({opacity:0},0)` — the exact class LEARNINGS bullet #1
  warned about, still live in the run-3 generators. Under the renderer's
  per-frame SEEK the boundary set wins, so the guardrail crack line is
  **invisible in every run-3 `hackers` lane that used it**. Verified by DOM probe
  (`tl.fromTo("#b3-cr",{scaleX:0,opacity:1},{scaleX:1,duration:0.5,...})`) plus
  zoomed screenshots before/after. Fix: opacity ALSO in the TO vars. Audit your
  own helpers for this — geometry_audit and Gemini QC both pass a missing
  element happily; only looking at pixels catches it.
- [hackers_kinetic] **geometry_audit only measures DIRECT children of each
  `.clip` section.** A per-beat full-canvas group wrapper therefore reduces the
  whole audit to ONE atom per beat: run-3 `hackers_kinetic` audited 5 atoms in a
  67s short and could only ever report the 5 wrapper seam warnings. Emitting
  scene atoms directly into the `<section>` is what makes gate 1 real (it
  immediately found a genuine outro collision). Coordinates are unaffected —
  the section is already the positioned ancestor at 0,0.
- [hackers_kinetic] Once flattened, **every element whose entrance is not an
  opacity tween needs an explicit opacity gate** (`set 0 @0` + `set 1 @t`).
  `barfill` reveals (translate) and `wordline` slams (children animate, the
  container does not) otherwise present a full-size box to the audit from t=0 —
  five rising chart bars "collided" with a cage that appears 3s later.
- [hackers_kinetic] **Highlight rings need `class="ring"`.** `isRing` is a class
  check; a ring is otherwise a bordered box with `hasBg` true and collides with
  the very thing it highlights. Mandatory for any generator that flattens.
- [hackers_kinetic] **HIGHLIGHT DISCIPLINE, concrete recipe:** draw the ring rect
  CONCENTRIC with its target and give it the target's rotation. transform-origin
  defaults to each box's own centre, so concentric + equal rotation = the same
  pivot and the ring tracks a tilted element exactly. Verified on the -3deg test
  cage (hackers backlog item) at 48.7s.
- [hackers_kinetic] A ring pushed INSIDE its target reads as a third welded
  shape, not a highlight: a 164x34 capsule ringing the crack across a 140-wide
  plate looked like a bar bolted through the box. Rings belong outside with
  padding; when the target splits, size the ring for the split extent rather
  than jumping to a sub-region.
- [hackers_kinetic] **Display wordlines measure ~1.34x their font-size** via the
  DOM Range box (and start ~0.07*fs below the layout box top), regardless of the
  CSS `line-height` you set. Stacking two lines at 1.12x pitch produced a real
  20% collision ERROR; 1.18x still kissed at 16%. Use >= 1.38x pitch for stacked
  display lines.

## Run 4 — grokbuild / icon (2026-08-10)

- [grokbuild_icon] **Zone-sized phase wrappers hide their children from gate 1
  entirely.** `geometry_audit.py` only enumerates the DIRECT children of a `.tz`
  section, so every element inside a `phase_open()` wrapper was never measured —
  run-3 grokbuild_icon beats 1 and 3 were effectively unaudited (1 wrapper atom
  vs 24 real atoms once flattened). Flatten phases (kill them with a
  comma-joined group selector in `out()` instead of animating a wrapper) and you
  get honest geometry AND you delete the whole "wrapper bottom == caption seam"
  class that v1.1 turned from a warning into a build failure. Every element
  still needs its own opacity entrance; `grow`/`growy` bars are invisible at
  scale 0, so nothing leaks at frame 0.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Measure the caption pill, don't reason about the seam.** The
  pill is 115px tall with `translateY(-50%)` over the seam at 862.5, so its TOP
  edge is 805px = design y 429.3 — 33px above the line the audit checks. Gate 1
  can report 0 warnings while ink visually kisses the pill. Working floor for
  this factory: no top-zone ink below design y 410 (= 768.75px).
- [grokbuild_icon] **A long stillness gap in `frame_review` is NOT proof of a
  frozen frame.** 62.0s->69.0s printed as a 7.0s hold, but a ring pop, a mono
  line and six caption changes happen inside it: on a dark canvas those score
  max 2.33 on the 16x16 dedup vs the 2.0 threshold. Extract mid-gap frames with
  `ffmpeg -ss` before believing (or reworking) anything — and never report the
  gap as idle motion, which is the opposite signal.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Blank zones are gate 2's unique catch — no other gate sees
  them.** Three sections opened 1.0-1.7s before their first element entered
  (black 7.2-8.9, empty cream 27.4-28.5, empty dark 41.7-43.0); geometry audit
  is silent (nothing to measure) and Gemini passed run 3 with them. Cheap
  deterministic pre-render check: sweep the timeline at 0.1s and count atoms
  with `op >= 0.30` inside `.tz` sections; any run longer than ~0.4s with zero
  atoms is a dead frame. Fix by moving the CUT, not the content — **visual
  section bounds do not have to equal content-plan beat bounds** (mine ended up
  0.00 / 8.72 / 28.24 / 42.62 vs beats 0 / 7.22 / 27.38 / 41.70).
- [grokbuild_icon] Anchoring an element to its spoken cue is not enough — check
  it against its section END too. The beat-0 ring landed at 7.04 and the cut
  came at 7.22, so the payoff of the whole opening flashed for 0.18s.
- [grokbuild_icon] `data-bleed` (not `data-overlap-ok`) is what suppresses the
  seam/clipped/margin checks; `data-overlap-ok` only exempts an element from
  collisions. If you keep zone-sized wrappers you need `data-bleed` on them —
  but flattening is the better fix.

## Run 4 — grokprice / kinetic (2026-08-10)

- [grokprice_kinetic] **BLANK-HANDOFF: a whole-factory defect class that all
  three gates miss.** Every beat section paints an opaque background at its
  `data-start`, so it covers the outgoing beat instantly — but if the incoming
  section's FIRST element animates in from `opacity:0` (popo/slam at t0+0.08),
  the top zone is genuinely EMPTY for 2-4 rendered frames. Measured on the
  run-4 grokprice kinetic build before the fix: 8.52-8.60, 25.18-25.26 and
  48.06-48.20 were flat charcoal with only the caption chip. geometry_audit
  cannot see it (nothing is drawn = nothing to flag), Gemini QC v3 passed it,
  and frame_review only catches it when its 3fps grid happens to land inside the
  window (t=48.0 caught the outro one; the other two were invisible to every
  gate). Run 3 shipped this on every short. **Fix: the first element of each
  section must be frame-0 safe** — `settle` (already opaque, scale only), never
  a fade/pop. **Detection recipe:** `ffmpeg -ss <section_start+0.02>` + a
  stddev check on the top zone; blank ≈ 10-14, content ≈ 23-38.
- [grokprice_kinetic] **A 0-warning `floating` result can mean "not checked".**
  geometry_audit skips the connector-end law entirely when a section contains no
  `isBox` atom (`if underline or not boxes: continue`), and `chip`/`card`
  wrappers do NOT qualify (the chip's painted `<span>` is not a direct child of
  the section). To make "arrows terminate AT box edges" actually verified, put
  class `node` on the two atoms the arrow joins and stop the rule/tip 7 design
  units (13px) from each. Two same-class nodes stay under the 3-element
  `unequal` grid check, so nothing else fires.
- [grokprice_kinetic] **Measure glyphs, don't estimate them.** A one-off
  headless-Chromium metrics pass (same FONTS block, widths returned in design
  units, cached to `gen/_measure_<item>.json`) makes strike bars, connector
  ends, kicker centring and the outro accent rule exact instead of eyeballed.
  Guard it with `document.fonts.check('800 100px Poppins')` etc. and hard-fail:
  fallback-font metrics would silently disagree with the render, which DOES load
  the webfonts.
- [grokprice_kinetic] **frame_review can silently drop a real event.** The
  beat-4 note fading in at 45.10 never produced a distinct frame — small grey
  mono type on a dark canvas is under the 2.0 mean-abs-diff dedup threshold. A
  long "[still 4.7s]" gap is therefore NOT proof that nothing happened; probe
  with `ffmpeg -ss` before concluding an element failed to render.
- [grokprice_kinetic] Strike-through / connector height: `0.47 * font-size`
  below the text-box top sits visibly BELOW the optical middle of Instrument
  Serif digits; **0.40 is right**. Judge it on a rendered frame, never on the
  line box.
- [grokprice_kinetic] When a beat's content is timed to words that arrive 2+
  seconds after the beat starts, don't pad with chrome — re-read the sentence
  and make the list BE the sentence. "On top of just being a cheap model, it's
  fantastic at reasoning, and it also gives you..." is literally a 5-item
  enumeration, so item 1 (CHEAP - $0.30/1M) lands at the beat open and the dead
  zone disappears without inventing anything.

  862.5px seam line** (measured: pill = 114.6px tall, `translateY(-50%)` on the
  seam). The audit's seam law (error when bottom is 850.5–864.5, warning from
  838.5) does NOT catch content that touches the pill — run 3's "x premium+ =
  free" ring bottomed at 798.75px, cleared every gate, and touched the captions

  Putting row labels directly ABOVE their meter (<=32 design px) removes the warning for
  every fully-drawn bar — this lane went from 9 warnings (run 3) to 4.
- [fablevssol_counter] A build-time caption-echo guard is cheap and catches what the eye
  misses: normalise the transcript, scan only the ZONE html (never the caption clips) for
  any 3 consecutive spoken words, whitelist the model names law 2 forces on screen
  ("claude fable 5", "gpt 5 6 sol"). It caught "RETURNS ON YOUR AI TRAINING" and
  "SWITCH EVERY SINGLE DAY" before a single frame was rendered.
- [fablevssol_counter] METERS COMPLETE has a clean resolution for capability scorecards:
  drop invented ratings (94/90/92/96) and make ONE meter complete in discrete ticks as he
  names each item, with a plated icon under each segment. It satisfies the law, removes
  numbers he never said, and kills the "wall of meters" monotony in the same move. A
  reset bar is legitimate only if it visibly FILLS then EMPTIES — a bar parked half-full
  is the bug Miguel named.

## Run 4 — fablevssol / icon (2026-08-10)

- [fablevssol_icon] **Dark-zone logo plates: the fix is a LIGHT plate everywhere, and
  dark-square logo FILES must be swapped, not plated.** Measured in the workspace logo
  library: `openai.png` and `grok.png` are pure-black artwork (mean opaque RGB 0,0,0),
  so run 3's `.ltile.od` dark plate (#1B1B21) made the Sol mark effectively invisible on
  beat 4's dark ground. Worse, `kimi.png` is a full-bleed DARK SQUARE (112x112, 92%
  opaque, mean RGB 44,45,47) — on a light plate it renders as a dark rounded box inside
  a rounded white box, i.e. a FILL THE SHAPE break that no plating can fix. Swapped for
  `deepseek.png` (transparent blue mark, still a frontier model so law 11 holds). Cheap
  pre-flight: `PIL alpha>200 fraction + mean opaque RGB` per logo before designing a grid.
- [fablevssol_icon] **`geometry_audit.py`'s floating-connector law fires on ANY painted
  rule**, not just arrows: balance beams, strike-throughs and meter tracks all expose a
  `:scope > .rule` child and get their ends checked. run 3 carried 5 such warnings on
  this short. `data-bleed` on the non-connector wrapper is the honest opt-out (the check
  short-circuits on `bleedOk`) and took the short to 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- [fablevssol_icon] **Never wrap zone elements in a layout div to move them as a group.**
  The audit's atoms are only DIRECT children of the section, so a wrapper does not merely
  add a fake box (the grokbuild_whiteboard failure mode) — it hides every child from the
  audit entirely. Re-authoring beat 7 as two full-zone phases sharing one geometry was the
  correct alternative to reflowing a group.
- [fablevssol_icon] **A 3-word verbatim caption-echo check is cheap at build time.**
  Normalise the transcript, build its trigram set, scan the ZONE html only (seam captions
  are supposed to be verbatim), whitelist product names ("claude fable 5", "gpt 5 6 sol").
  It caught "i work with both" (he says "actually work with both") and the outro's
  "EVERY SINGLE DAY" (he says "each and every single day") before either reached a render.
- [gate2] **Scaffolding is the BUILD ORDER trap.** Every empty dashed slot and empty frame
  in the run-3 icon lane read as chrome-standing-before-content: a dashed DESIGN frame hung
  empty for 2.1s, and beat 7 painted a divider + 4 empty slots 7.5s before any content
  existed. Deleting the scaffolding fixed FILL THE SHAPE *and* BUILD ORDER in one move —
  the plates are one shape each and they arrive on their own word.
- [gate2] **A top-zone chip printing the same two words as the concurrent seam caption is a
  visible double caption** even though 2 words is under the echo bar (chip "WRONG QUESTION"
  directly above the pill "wrong question."). The word-count rule is necessary, not
  sufficient — read the frame. Reframing forward ("the real question") costs nothing.
- [gate1] **0 errors on round 1 does not mean the composition is right.** All five defects
  Gate 2 found on this short — double caption, a beat with 65% of the zone empty, a chip
  15 real px off the caption pill, a field row docked 20px low, a 2-line payoff crowding
  the seam — were invisible to the geometry audit, which was 0/0 the whole time.
- [gate1/gate2] **Pre-render contact sheets are the cheapest gate in the chain.** Driving

  empty-frame and dark-logo defects before a 2-minute render was spent. Worth running
  between the geometry audit and the render on every build.
- [factory] The shared scratchpad `/private/tmp/claude-502/.../scratchpad` is used by ALL
  parallel builders — a helper written as `shots.py` was gone by the next call. Prefix

## Run 4 — grokbuild / kinetic (2026-08-10)

- [grokbuild_kinetic] **Full-canvas phase wrappers make Gate 1 blind.** `geometry_audit.py`
  only measures `sec.children` — direct children of a `<section>` clip. Every element
  inside a `phase_open()` `<div>` is therefore invisible to it, so in run 3 the whole of
  beats 2 and 4 went unaudited and the only findings were the wrappers' own phantom seam
  warnings. Emitting ONE `<section>` clip per phase (own `data-start`/`data-duration`/
  `data-track-index`) restores coverage — 4-20 measured atoms per phase here — and the 7
  run-3 seam warnings vanish because there is no zero-ink full-canvas box left.
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **Do not cross-dissolve two terminal screens.** With one section per
  phase I first added a 0.26s fade-in on each incoming clip; because both screens put their
  prompt at the same y, the render ghosted `$ g▮` typing on top of the outgoing
  `grok build --features` (verified at t=41.67). Hard cuts are correct for this lane — but
  then every phase must have an element already painted at its first frame (prompt with no
  opacity tween, a static label, or a `settle()` on the headline), otherwise the cut lands
  on an empty canvas.
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **frame_review's dedup silently eats small real events.** The 16x16
  grey / 2.0 threshold did not register a 78px highlight ring, a 13px label or a 168px
  bracket, so the manifest printed `[still 6.7s before this]` across a stretch containing
  three genuine events. A long `[still Ns]` marker is an instruction to pull direct ffmpeg
  frames and check, not evidence of a dead beat (the inverse of the idle-candidate rule).
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **SVG is a free lane for design energy.** A whole chart — gridlines,
  gradient area, a curve that strokes itself on via `strokeDashoffset`, milestone dots, a
  mono axis label — lives inside ONE atom, so the audit sees a single box while GSAP still
  animates the inner nodes by id (children of an atom are never measured). `strokeDashoffset`
  is a pure numeric tween and stays seek-safe. This is how the "quite bland" evolution chart
  got the lane's full design energy without adding a single collision risk.
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **"ex xAI" was never stutter-filtered.** Scribe collapsed Miguel's
  spoken "ex xAI" into a single `xAI,` token spanning 10.84-11.76 (0.92s for two syllables).
  Nothing to whitelist in the stutter regex — restoring the phrase needs a per-video caption
  fixup keyed on `(start_time, token)`. Same trap for any other swallowed word.
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **Prompt strings are top-zone text and count against Law 4.** The
  terminal command `$ release grok-4.5` matched three consecutive caption words ("release
  Grok 4.5") — a real caption-echo fail hiding in lane chrome. Diff every command line
  against the concurrent caption, not just labels and key terms. ("ship grok-4.5" fixed it.)
- [grokbuild_kinetic] A spectrum axis drawn full-width before its cheap end is populated
  leaves ~9s of bare rail running into empty canvas. Grow the rail in two discrete events
  keyed to the tiles that actually land on it, and end brackets ON a plate rather than in
  the gap between two tiles.
- [grokbuild_kinetic] Logos that ship their own dark square badge (kimi.png) still need the
  standard light plate, but give the `<img>` a concentric inner border-radius: without it
  the tile reads as a sharp box inside a rounded box (FILL THE SHAPE), with it it reads as
  an app icon. Cursor and Codex artwork plate fine as-is.

## Run 4 build — hackers / counter (2026-08-10)

- [hackers_counter] **Gate 1 is nearly blind when a scene lives inside one
  full-zone wrapper.** `geometry_audit.py` measures only a section's DIRECT
  children (`Array.from(sec.children)`), so the run-3 pattern of one
  `<div id="b1-g" 1080x862.5>` per beat meant the audit saw exactly ONE atom per
  section — every internal collision, clip and seam-touch was invisible, and the
  only findings were the wrappers' own seam warnings. Flattening the scene (atoms
  as direct children of the section, group exits emitted per element instead of
  by fading a wrapper) is what makes gate 1 mean anything. Cost: you must then
  declare intentional overlays honestly (`ring` class + `data-overlap-ok`).
- [hackers_counter] **Zero-ink clipping containers are "visible" to the audit
  from t=0.** A `barfill`/odometer wrapper has `overflow:hidden` and no opacity of
  its own, so it is painted (op=1) the whole time even though the fill inside is
  translated off-stage. Every bar/odometer needs an explicit opacity gate
  (`set opacity 0 @0` + `set opacity 1 @t`), else it collides with things it has
  not visually appeared next to yet.
- [hackers_counter] **A DOM Range rect measures the font's NATURAL line box, not
  your `line-height`.** Two stacked display lines at fs=58 measured 152px tall
  each while spaced 115px apart → a real 24% "collision" on the headline, with
  zero glyph contact. Leading must be >= ~1.2x font-size (1.3x is comfortable) for
  stacked `wordline`s, which is also the honest reading of "even spacing between
  lines". The audit's 0.20 text-pair tolerance exists for exactly this class.
- [hackers_counter] **The design floor is the caption PILL, not the seam line.**
  `SEAM_Y` is 862.5 but `.scappill` is `translateY(-50%)` on the seam, so its top
  edge sits ~800 on frame. Content bottoms must stay above ~768 (y=410 in 576-unit
  zone space); a 24px-from-seam clearance still collides with the pill.
- [hackers_counter] **Beat sections paint their own opaque cream at `data-start`,
  so an entrance tween that BEGINS at t0 leaves a 4-frame blank flash.** The
  incoming section covers the outgoing one instantly (higher track index), but its
  first element is still at opacity 0. Fix: PRE-ROLL the beat's opening chrome
  ~0.35s before the boundary — the tween runs while the section is still hidden,
  so the cut lands on an already-painted frame. Elements with no opacity tween
  (e.g. `wordline` + a y/scale-only settle) are immune, which is why the outro
  never flashed. Four blank/near-blank zones in this short were all this class.
- [hackers_counter] **Gate 2 is the only gate that catches dead air.** Geometry
  was 0/0 and the composition was correct at every checked moment, yet the render
  had a fully empty top zone at three beat boundaries and a lone 12px label
  holding for 2.0s. Read the handoff frames specifically (t0 of every beat and
  every sub-scene), not just the "interesting" ones.
- [hackers_counter] **A gap bracket narrower than ~4x its own height stops reading
  as a measurement and reads as an "H" glyph.** Run 3's closed gap (44 wide x 20
  tall, and crossfaded from a wide one) looked broken; one element resized in a
  single tween at 56x14 reads correctly.
- [hackers_counter] **A highlight ring must never crop a partial run of a segment
  grid** — there is no gap wide enough to land its edge in, so it visibly cuts
  through one segment. Ring the whole gauge, or ring a different object.
- [hackers_counter] Cheap pre-render check worth copying: drive the project in
  headless Chromium and screenshot the top 920px at ~12 chosen times BEFORE
  rendering. It caught a mis-fitted ring, a ring cutting a chip, and the cage
  label/ring collision at zero render cost (a render is ~90s + a gate-2 pass).
- [hackers_counter] The hackers backlog fix works and is worth generalising: a
  highlight on a rotated target must carry the same rotation in its initial
  `set` (`hlring(..., deg=-3)`), and because the ring rect is concentric with the
  cage the tilt keeps them locked. Do NOT rotate the ring with a separate tween.

## Run 4 build pass — hermes / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [hermes_diagram] **A collector bar classed `abs node <suffix>` is the honest way to let
  MANY connectors terminate on one line.** `geometry_audit.py` anchors a connector end only
  to an `isBox` atom (`ltile|node|shot|chip`), so a trunk/bus drawn as a `.rule` gives every
  stem a floating end AND is itself scored as a two-loose-end connector. Give the bar
  `class="abs node bus"` with inline `border:none;background:TERRA_L` and animate it with
  `scaleX/scaleY` (its rect is 0-height until it grows, so the audit skips it entirely
  mid-tween): it becomes a real box, `thin_bar()` keeps it out of the collision pass, and the
  class suffix keeps it out of the same-size equality group. Six stems + one door arrow on
  beat 4 and three stems + one arrow in the outro, all anchored, **0 floating warnings** —
  against 18 warnings on run 3's version of this exact lane.
- [hermes_diagram] **Design the connectors axis-aligned and the whole `floating` class
  disappears.** Diagonal connectors are measured by their AABB, whose mid-left/mid-right
  points are not the endpoints, so they can never anchor. Every connector in this short is
  horizontal or a 90° rotation; combined with the full-length shaft + overlaid head, gate 1
  came back 0/0 on the FIRST build. Zero-warning is reachable, not just zero-error.
- [hermes_diagram] **The Nous mark ships with its own hard SQUARE frame** (a ~5px black
  border on `ai-models/nous-research.png`). Dropped into our rounded `.ltile` that is a sharp
  box inside a rounded box — the exact mismatch v1.1's FILL THE SHAPE bans, and at tile size
  the frame is pure noise. Fix in `stage()`: scan in from each edge while the row/col mean is
  < 100, crop, resize to 512, and re-mask the corners at the tiles' own 0.26 ratio. Then
  render it with `pad=0` so the artwork IS the plate. Applies to every lane that shows Nous.
- [hermes_diagram] **Emptying a container to make a point creates a blank zone.** Beat 3
  removes three of four tool schemas on "being very picky" — run 3's move left a 296x224
  white void for 14 seconds, which is a listed visual-gate FAIL kind and also hides the
  point. Replacing each removed block with a dashed `free` placeholder at the same rect fills
  the shape, states the claim better (the space is FREE, not gone), and is invisible to the
  collision pass (identical rects hit the >=0.96 containment skip).
- [hermes_diagram] **A 3.7s no-dedup gap in `frame_review` can be thin-ink BUILD events, not
  a hold.** 42.7-46.3s here shows "still 3.7s" because a 5px terracotta trunk plus six 4.9px
  stems cannot move a 16x16 grayscale mean by 2.0 — yet comparing the frames at both ends
  shows the entire bus/stem/arrow build happened inside it. Read both ends before recording a
  stillness number, and never file it as an idle-motion candidate.
- [hermes_diagram] Retiring `ladder.png` retires a whole defect cluster at once: the
  `upscaled` warning, the ~11px unreadable sub-lines (law 8), AND the orphan "1. THE LADDER"
  ordinal from the source article. Three coded tier rows (`24 -> FULL LISTING`,
  `830 -> NAMES ONLY`, `3,320 -> HINT + SEARCH`) carry the identical facts in real type. A
  left accent bar whose opacity encodes the tier also fills the gutter that right-aligned
  numerals leave, so the rows read as a stack instead of three hanging indents.
- [gate 2 / all] Pre-render playwright screenshots keep paying: on this short they caught the
  Nous square frame and the white void, neither of which gate 1 (0 errors, 0 warnings) nor
  gate 3 (pass, first call) would have reported. Screenshot BEFORE the 3-minute render, every
  time.

## Run 4 build — meatwrapper / icon (2026-08-10)

- [meatwrapper_icon] **A rotated arrow whose rule is still `scaleX(0)` is NOT invisible to
  gate 1.** `geometry_audit.py` skips a connector with `d.w < 2 || d.h < 2`, but a collapsed
  2.6-design-px bar rotated ~29 deg has an AABB of 2.4 x 4.3 render px — both over 2 — so it
  reports a floating end for the entire time BEFORE the arrow draws (mine fired 1.1-4.0s on
  two fan arrows that only exist from 12.6s). Fix: author connector wrappers at `opacity:0`
  and set them live inside `arrow_in()`. Straight (0/180 deg) arrows never showed this because
  their collapsed AABB is 0 x 4.9.
- [meatwrapper_icon] **Giving id-less wrappers an id can SURFACE findings, not hide them.**
  `key_of()` falls back to `sec/cls/x,y`, so two arrows sharing the same left/top (a fan out of
  one point) collapse into ONE atom and the audit dedupes them. After adding ids the second one
  appeared. A 0-warning report on wrapper-less connectors is not proof they were all measured.
- [meatwrapper_icon] **The audit's 14px connector tolerance is RENDER px = 7.4 design px at
  S=1.875.** Every "floating" warning in my round 1 was a visually comfortable 8-12 design px
  tail gap (15-22 render px). Working convention that produced 0 warnings across 11 connectors:
  **tip exactly ON the target box edge, tail 4 design px off the source box edge.** With the
  v1.1 arrow helper (shaft = length - head*0.5) the drawn rule then ends 5.5 design px = 10.3
  render px short of the tip, comfortably inside tolerance.
- [meatwrapper_icon] A meter TRACK declared `class="abs node"` with all of `.node`'s paint
  overridden inline (`background`, `border:none`, `display:block`, `border-radius`) makes the
  audit treat the fill as a bar living inside a box (its `inside` test) instead of as a
  connector with two floating ends. Honest — the track really is a drawn box — and it does not
  join the equality group unless 3+ share the class string.
- [meatwrapper_icon] **METERS COMPLETE has a third resolution: delete the meter.** Besides
  "fill it" and grokprice's "pair it with a full bar", a track whose whole point is ZERO (my
  beat-2 "VALUE ADDED") can never satisfy the law. The display numeral (`0%`) carries the claim
  better and removes an element. Removing beats faking.
- [meatwrapper_icon] **For opaque-section dead frames, a frame-0 composition beats an earlier
  entrance.** I first tried a 0.12s LEAD on each incoming beat's first tween; a 0.42s `popo` is
  still only ~30% opaque at the cut, so the handoff frame was still near-empty. Authoring the
  incoming cast visible (`hide=False`) + `settle()` at the section start paints the beat's very
  first frame and reads as a deliberate cut. Verified on the render at 16.7s / 40.0s / 55.0s.

  This video's beat 3 section starts on "Now," (25.76) while its cue anchor "in order to avoid

  against the transcript for 3-consecutive-word runs. Two survived from run 3 here — "ANY AI
  TOOL" (vs "any AI tool whatsoever") and the "THE MEAT WRAPPER" sub-label duplicating the

- [gate2] **A manifest frame with no caption pill does not mean a caption dropout.** My

## Run 4 build — productivity / icon (2026-08-10)

- [productivity_icon] **The dead-frame class has a fix that costs one number per beat:
  PRE-ROLL the beat's first element.** Sections are opaque cream on ascending tracks,
  so the incoming zone covers the outgoing one from its own `data-start` and anything
  that starts *at* t0 shows a blank cut frame. Starting each beat's first element
  0.10-0.20s BEFORE its section's `data-start` fixes it completely: the clip is hidden
  during the pre-roll, so the tween runs invisibly and the element is already painted
  on the section's very first frame. Gate 1 never sees it (it only measures ACTIVE
  sections), and unlike grokbuild_icon's "move the CUT" fix it needs no re-cut and no
  content-plan change. Verified at all five boundaries here (5.50 / 13.36 / 24.92 /
  35.82 / 44.06).
- [productivity_icon] **A pre-render dead-frame scan that counts ATOMS misses
  near-empty frames.** My 0.1s sweep counting `.tz` atoms with `op >= 0.30` reported
  "NONE" while the 44.02 cut still shipped ~0.35s holding nothing but a 15px mono
  kicker — gate 2's frame read is what caught it. If you copy the scan, threshold on
  painted INK AREA (sum of w*h*op of non-ring atoms, e.g. < 3% of the zone = dead),
  not on a non-zero atom count.
- [productivity_icon] **TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH also bans numbers inherited from the
  SOURCE ARTICLE, not just "corrected" misspeaks.** Run 3's beat 2 showed a
  "3-4 WEEKS -> 10 HOURS" before/after receipt; "3-4 weeks" appears NOWHERE in
  Miguel's transcript — it came from the tavily case study the screenshot is from.
  It passed geometry, Gemini visual and Gemini semantic in run 3. Cheap standing
  check: grep every on-screen number against `transcript_tight.json` before shipping;
  a number no gate disputes is not the same as a number he said.
- [productivity_icon] **Arrow DIRECTION is a Law-11 claim and no gate checks it.**
  My beat-4 stem ran DOWN from the AI AGENT node to the three tool marks — i.e. "the
  agent produces the tools", the exact inverse of "the tools to build these type of
  agents". geometry_audit only measures where a connector's ends land, and Gemini
  passed a render containing it. Read every connector as a sentence in the frame
  review; flipping it to `uparrow` was a one-line fix.
- [productivity_icon] **Deleting the text labels under a logo row is the cheapest way
  to satisfy HIGHLIGHT DISCIPLINE.** Miguel's backlog item here was "the $20-100/month
  highlight collided with neighbours" — the collision was structural: the three tool
  NAME labels occupied exactly the band the price ring needed. LAW 2 already says a
  logo IS the label, so removing them bought 39px of air above the ring *and* deleted
  three top-zone strings that were verbatim spoken tool names.
- [productivity_icon] **Solve for the render width from the source width instead of
  waiting for the `upscaled` warning.** Max safe design width = natural * 1.15 / 1.875
  (722px source -> 442.7u). Setting `PHOTO_W = 440` and asserting
  `px(PHOTO_W) <= natural * 1.15` in the staging function makes the law unbreakable at
  build time; run 3 rendered the same crop at 885px (1.23x).
- [productivity_icon] **A generator that draws every bar with `barfill` gets ZERO
  floating-connector warnings by construction — because it also gets zero of the
  check.** `geometry_audit.py` looks for a `.rule`/`.ruleY` class; the productivity
  chassis never emits one, so `isRule` is false for every atom and the whole floating
  pass is skipped. Silence there is not evidence your connectors terminate correctly:
  on this chassis you must verify arrow ends by reading frames.
- [productivity_icon] Clean run for the record: geometry 5 rounds all 0/0 (the first
  build was already clean; the other four rounds were composition work), 65 atoms
  measured across 7 sections, 56 distinct states from 186 samples, 0 idle candidates,

## Run 4 build — meatwrapper / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [meatwrapper_diagram] **A `leave()` fromTo bakes opacity:1 onto its element for the
  ENTIRE timeline before it, and a `tl.set()` switch-on recorded afterwards restores 1,
  not 0.** Chain: at build, `fade(sel,t,d,0,1)`'s immediateRender paints opacity 1; the
  audit's prime (progress 1 -> 0) rewinds the set to whatever it *recorded*, which is
  that 1. Measured on `d3aow`: opacity 1 from t=1s while the render showed nothing, so a
  connector drawn at 33s was audited as floating from 28s. Fix: switch-ons must be
  `fromTo` with opacity in the FROM vars (`fade(sel,t,0.01)`), never `tl.set`. This is the
  seeded "opacity in TO vars" learning striking from the other side — the same rule
  applies to any element whose only "on" is a set.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] **A collapsed `scaleX(0)` rule is NOT invisible to gate 1 when it
  is steeply diagonal.** `geometry_audit.py` skips a rule only when `d.w < 2 or d.h < 2`;
  a 2.6px-thick bar rotated 147 degrees still measures 2.65 x 4.11px with zero width, so
  `retract()` does not save you. Carry the connector's visibility on the arrow WRAPPER's
  opacity (author it `opacity:0`, fade in on draw, fade out on exit) — then the whole atom
  drops below the audit's 0.15 opacity floor and nothing invisible occupies geometry.
  Bonus: it replaces the shaft+head+scaleX exit dance with one call.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] **Highlight boxes measured off a SOURCE asset go stale when the
  asset renders narrower than it was measured.** The @steipete claim is one line in the
  1000px source and TWO lines at 470 design px, so run 3's ring bottom cut straight
  through "same night]". Gate 1 cannot see inside a raster, gate 3 passed it twice, and
  gate 2's 512px manifest frame is too small to be sure — the proof is a 1:1 `ffmpeg`
  crop of the card's rect in the rendered mp4. Re-measure every asset hit-box against the
  RENDER, not the source, whenever the render width differs from the measuring width.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] **Grouping a named pair into one plate is the honest fix for "the
  arrow points at half of it"** (Miguel's "you -> ChatGPT/Claude arrow centered"). The
  connector gets a real box centre to address; the two logo tiles stay measurable section
  children because a child fully inside a parent is skipped by the >=0.96 containment
  rule; and the plate doubles as the frame for the dashed-slot -> logo choreography.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] **A ring can never go on a node that connectors terminate on** —
  the shafts cross its border and it reads as broken (run 3 ringed the beat-3 AI tile with
  both loop arrows landing on it). Give the highlight its own uncrossed target or drop the
  ring; shrinking it inside the box just turns it into a selection outline.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] Beat composition, not just beat content: run 3 pinned this lane's
  beat 3 to design y=104-172 and left the bottom 60% of the canvas empty for 7s. Neither
  gate flags it (nothing is blank, nothing collides). Lay a beat so its FIRST phase sits
  on the zone's optical centre line and later phases grow downward.
- [gate2] Three separate stillness gaps on this short (5.7s / 3.0s / 4.3s) each contained
  real events the 16x16-gray dedup could not see: small mono labels fading in on dark, a
  cream-on-cream node plus its connector, and a thin terracotta arrow on dark. That is now
  three lanes reporting the same thing — treat EVERY reported gap as unverified until a
  headless seek + screenshot at its midpoint says otherwise, and never "fix" a hold on the
  manifest's word alone.

## Run 4 build — meatwrapper / kinetic (2026-08-10)

- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **Every short in the factory drops a caption frame at
  roughly half its phrase boundaries.** `build_captions` has shipped since run 1
  with `phrases[i]["t1"] = next_t0 - 0.02`. At 30fps a 0.02s gap swallows a whole
  frame whenever a boundary lands inside it — verified on the first run-4 render:
  at t=54.46 the seam is completely bare between cap50 and cap51, while 54.35 and
  54.47 both carry a pill. Butt-joining the phrases (`t1 = next_t0`) fixes it with
  no overlap, because clip visibility is `[start, start+duration)`. Deterministic
  check worth running on every render: sample the caption band every frame and
  count frames with no terracotta pixels — this short went from a mid-video
  dropout to 7 blank frames, all before the first spoken word at 0.22s.
- [gate2] **`frame_review.py`'s frame timestamps run ~0.13s LATE against the mp4.**
  `f_0054_333` does not show t=54.333, it shows ~54.46 (proved by ffmpeg-extracting
  both: 54.333 has a caption, the manifest frame does not). Harmless for reading
  states, fatal for adjudicating single-frame events — always re-extract with
  ffmpeg at the exact time before calling a one-frame defect real or fake.
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **The cheapest gate in the chain is a whole-video
  dead-frame scan, and it is deterministic.** Decode the top zone at 96x77 gray,
  take each frame's modal value as its background, and flag frames where <0.4% of
  pixels differ by >28. 1771 frames in ~4s, and it proves the "opaque zone pair
  makes a black hole at the cut" class is absent — something gate 1 cannot see and
  gate 3 charges money to guess at. This short: 0 near-empty frames.
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **A cross-out's WRAPPER outlives its ink.** `cross_el`
  fades the inner `.rule`, but the rotated wrapper keeps opacity 1, so the audit
  keeps measuring it. It is invisible while its host panel is alive (the rule is
  >=90% contained in a box, so the floating check skips it) and becomes a
  `floating` warning the instant the panel is killed. Give the wrapper an id and
  `leave()` it with the rest of the block. Corollary worth copying: drawing the
  cross over a real panel whose class list includes `node` is the honest way to
  exempt a rotated stroke, instead of reaching for `data-bleed`.
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **Fix for "highlight was on too-small code text": build the
  code line out of OBJECTS.** `you = interface(human, ai)` became `you = ` +
  an INTERFACE hero node + a HUMAN node + a plated Claude tile, with the parens and
  comma as the only raw glyphs. The three speech-synced rings then land on
  100-250px boxes instead of 45px glyph runs, the logo satisfies LAW 2 inside the
  same line, and the X-cross has a real box to sit on. Ring pad 6 + 14 design px
  between pieces keeps every ring 8 design px clear of its neighbours
  (HIGHLIGHT DISCIPLINE: highlights must respect collisions).
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **Author the whole signature with dashed slots at the beat's
  first frame.** Building a centred row left-to-right leaves it visibly off-centre
  for seconds (2.7s here). Slots that are the EXACT silhouette of what lands in
  them keep the composition centred and complete from frame 1, and they are the
  approved slot->content language, not "chrome before content".
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] Poppins 800 at fs 86 measures ~15 design px ABOVE its
  layout box under `line-height:1.05` (the audit's Range rect returns the glyph
  inline box, ~1.40em here, not the line box). A mono label 20 design px above a
  big number collides at 55%; 54 design px of clearance is the working number.
  Same family as the grokprice `.ser` finding, but Poppins bleeds more than the
  0.2em budgeted there — measure, do not assume.
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] Clean run for the record: geometry 7 rounds
  (1err -> 0/0 -> 1warn -> 0/0 x4), 48 distinct states from 177 samples, 0 idle
