## Run 4 rebuild — fablevssol / kinetic (2026-08-10, second pass)

- [fablevssol_kinetic] **Gate 3 caught a real LAW-5 defect that both free gates and two
  earlier Gemini passes had shipped: a highlight with no spoken referent.** The opening
  ring stepped claim -> score on the @composio card during "if the first question that
  comes into your mind when you hear..." — nothing he says in those 3 seconds names
  either region, so the highlight was decorative. Verdict: `highlight_match at 0.5s`.
  **The fix is to DELETE the highlight, not to retime it** — there is no word in the
  window to sync to, and law 3 already lets the card just BE the news. Standing check
  worth copying: for every ring in a generator, write down the spoken phrase it is
  supposed to point at; if you cannot, the ring is the defect. (Both my own gate-2 read
  and the judge flagged the same frame independently — when a free gate makes you
  uneasy about a highlight, fix it before paying for the judge.)
- [fablevssol_kinetic] **`power3.out` on EXITS is the mechanical root of the blank-handoff
  class, and it is a one-line fix inside `fade()`:** `ease = "EXIT" if to < frm else
  "SOFT"` with `EXIT = "power3.in"`. Combined with a 0.16s PRE-ROLL of each zone's first
  element (the tween runs while the clip is still hidden, so the cut lands on a painted
  frame), a 0.05s painted-ink sweep went from 7 near-empty windows totalling ~2.3s
  (worst 1.35s) to ZERO across 83.17s. Confirms slop_counter's finding on a second lane
  and shows the two fixes are complementary, not alternatives: the ease fixes crossfade
  troughs INSIDE a beat, the pre-roll fixes the cut itself.
- [fablevssol_kinetic] **The stranded-tile beat opening has a fix that invents nothing:
  make the mark the composition.** Beats 3 and 4 each spend ~3.1s with only their subject
  logo on screen before the hero word arrives. Instead of a 72-unit tile pinned to the
  header slot (measured <3% painted ink), the mark enters at **1.9x scale on the zone's
  optical centre** with its name label under it and **rides up into the header in ONE
  discrete move** as the hero slams (`moveto` carries x + y + scale in a single tween, so
  no wrapper and every atom stays a direct section child). Same trick applied to the
  two-mark "BOTH" phase and to the FRONTIER TIED statement. Law 1 bans idle drift, not
  transitions.
- [fablevssol_kinetic] **A strike-through on a display line inverts the claim it crosses.**
  Run-4 round 1 struck `MORE TROUBLE` while he says "you will actually have a bit more of
  trouble" — the bar reads as *not* more trouble. Second defect on the same element: the
  sweep started 0.31s before the outro cut, so the annotation never landed (3fps gate-2
  sampling never even caught it). Deleting it fixed both. Generalises threed_kinetic's
  "stop striking TYPE at all": a strike is a negation operator, so it may only cross
  something the speaker is actually negating.
- [fablevssol_kinetic] Independent confirmation, now four lanes deep: `kimi.png` is a
  full-bleed dark rounded square (112x112, 92% opaque, mean RGB 43/44/46) and renders as
  a sharp dark box inside the rounded white plate. When the transcript names no model

  from the background — under the scan's 28 threshold, which is exactly why a beat
  that opens on a bare track *reads* as an empty zone. Raising every empty meter
  track to 0.14 fixed a composition defect and a measurement blind spot in one
  token. Consequence to carry: a drained/spent segment must then go DARKER than
  its rail (0.30 here) or it reads lighter than the track it sits in.

  fade-out/fade-in crossfade has a trough because a semi-transparent track never
  crosses the ink threshold. Appending the tweet card LAST (so it paints on top of
  a meter already fully drawn behind it) makes the card dissolve to *reveal* the
  meter — no empty frames, no crossfade of two compositions in the same space, and
  the audit skips the pair via the >=0.96 containment rule since the track sits
  entirely inside the card's rect. Cheaper and more robust than tuning lead times.

  it reported 0 near-empty frames pre-render — and the render then measured 0/2008.

  a counter reading 0. Law 11 applies to counters, not just diagram positions: give

  same reason the ring's `hljump` chain is.

  highlight held past its phrase, and a counter contradicting its own segments).
  None was catchable by re-reading the generator; all six came from measuring the
  render and reading frames.

## Run 4 rebuild — hackers / icon (2026-08-10, second pass)

- [hackers_icon] **The `growx()` opacity trap was still live in a SHIPPED run-4
  short, and all three gates passed it.** The seeded bullet #1 and the
  hackers_kinetic finding both describe it, but the run-4 `hackers_icon`
  generator still emitted `tl.set(sel,{scaleX:0,opacity:0},0)` +
  `fromTo({scaleX:0,opacity:1},{scaleX:1,...})` — opacity in the FROM vars only.
  Measured on the built HTML: `#b3-cr` computed opacity **0 at every probe**
  (30.0 / 33.0 / 34.5 / 35.2 / 35.6 / 36.0 / 36.5 / 37.5s) while `scaleX`
  reached 1, so the guardrail CRACK — the payoff of "not sufficient / quite
  simple to crack" — never rendered. Gate 1 was 0/0, Gate 3 passed, and the
  gate-2 frame read did not catch it either (you cannot see a missing element
  in a frame you have never seen correct). **Standing check worth copying: for
  every helper that animates something other than opacity, probe
  `getComputedStyle(el).opacity` at 3-4 times in Playwright and assert it is
  non-zero when the element is supposed to be on screen.** Two lines of code,
  and it is the only thing in the chain that finds this class.
- [hackers_icon] **A "0 dead frames" verdict from a whole-zone ink sweep is
  wrong if you count atoms in EVERY visible `.tz` section.** Beat sections
  overlap by 0.15s and the incoming one has a higher track index with an opaque
  background, so the outgoing beat's atoms are still enumerable while being
  completely covered. Count only the TOPMOST visible `.tz` (max
  `data-track-index`). Fixing that turned "1.77% ink, 3 atoms" into "the zone is
  actually empty" at three beat handoffs.
- [hackers_icon] **Second trap in the same sweep: `barfill`/rule wrappers are
  measured by a DOM Range, which ignores `overflow:hidden`.** An un-revealed
  meter/rule wrapper reports its translated fill at x=-568 with full area, so it
  contributes phantom "ink" exactly at the handoffs where you need the truth.
  `geometry_audit.py` already skips `cr` when overflow is hidden/clip — copy
  that guard into any custom probe or your dead-frame numbers are optimistic.
- [hackers_icon] **Place every crossfade strictly BETWEEN two geometry samples.**
  The audit steps at 0.5s and needs 2 consecutive violating samples to error, so
  a dissolve that starts after n*0.5 and completes before (n+1)*0.5 is
  invisible to it by construction. Five crossfades were placed this way
  (3.56-3.82, 7.02-7.36, 19.52-19.82, 44.44-44.66, 55.06-55.36) and the audit
  stayed 0 errors / 0 warnings while the top zone was never empty. This is a
  cheaper, more honest fix than `data-overlap-ok` on transition pairs.
- [hackers_icon] **A ring that must stay CONCENTRIC to inherit a rotation cannot
  have its bottom edge raised.** Concentric means bottom = 2*cy - top, so any
  attempt to clear a label under the target also raises the top. Worse, the
  rotation lowers one bottom corner: a -3deg ring at (158,96,244,208) around a
  cage centred (280,200) has its bottom edge running y=310.6 -> 297.2, i.e.
  through a label sitting at y=302. **Move the label, not the ring** — and
  compute the ROTATED corner positions, because the un-rotated rect clears it.
- [hackers_icon] **Two same-colour outlines 22px apart still read as nested
  boxes, but a solid ring around a DASHED box is legible.** The stroke-style
  contrast does most of the work; the threed_icon ">=20 real px" rule holds, and
  12 design units (22.5px) was enough here while still leaving 20.6px between
  the ring and the neighbouring CHEAT chip.
- [hackers_icon] **BUILD ORDER, "wire into nothing" edition, in the icon lane:**
  a gap-measuring arrow drawn on the word "ahead" hangs for 1.5s into an empty
  canvas because the row it measures lands on "open source models". Fire the
  connector off the LATER of its two endpoints (oss1+0.30), and let the spoken
  cue own the LABEL instead ("STILL AHEAD" at ahead+0.14). One claim, two
  surfaces, correct order.
- [hackers_icon] **The scaffold is what makes a pre-roll worth anything.**
  Pre-rolling a beat's first element only guarantees a painted frame — a lone
  56x30 "01" chip is a painted frame and still reads as empty. Pre-rolling the
  beat's SHAPE (four dashed slots for a 4-vs-2 comparison) opens the beat on a
  real composition. Keep the second row's slots for the moment the sentence
  turns to it, so nothing dashed waits longer than ~1.5s.
- [gate2] Both stillness gaps this short reports (4.3s at 7.3-11.7 and 3.3s at
  44.7-48.0) contain real build events — a logo landing in its slot, and a cage
  forming then tilting as a model escapes. That is now five lanes reporting the
  same thing. Treat a `[still Ns]` marker as an instruction to pull `ffmpeg -ss`
  frames at both ends and the midpoint, never as evidence.
- [hackers_icon] Clean run for the record: geometry 3 rounds all 0 errors /
  0 warnings (83 real atoms measured at peak, ids checked against the generator
  so the verdict is not a "not checked"), 0 blank windows in a 0.05s pre-render
  sweep AND 0 near-empty frames across all 2008 rendered frames, 0 mid-video
  caption dropouts, 64 distinct states from 201 samples, 0 idle candidates,

## Run 4 build — hermes / counter (2026-08-10, verification pass on an inherited build)

- [hermes_counter] **An inherited "0 errors + QC pass" build shipped a fully BLACK frame at a
  beat cut.** This item already existed, audited 0/0 and had a passing Gemini verdict. Read
  per frame against the rendered mp4 it had FOUR blank windows: t=40.60 a completely black top
  zone at beat 4's cut, then a lone unlabelled `0` holding until 40.94; **15.33-15.57 fully
  black mid-beat** (key term left at 15.20, ledger arrived at 15.50); 20.00-20.13 empty cream;
  50.77 one empty frame. All four were invisible to gate 1 (nothing to measure) and gate 3
  passed them. **Never treat a previous worker's paperwork as verification** — re-derive the
  numbers or the defect ships.
- [hermes_counter] **The fade-out EASE is the root cause of the entire blank-handoff class,
  not the cue timing.** The shared `fade(sel,t,d,0,1)` helper eases on `power3.out`; on a
  1 -> 0 tween that is front-loaded, so opacity is already 0.16 at 40% of the duration. Every
  "crossfade" in these generators is really a fast cut with a long invisible tail, which is
  why moving cues around never quite closes the gap. Fix: a LINEAR exit (`ease:"none"`) for
  any element handing its space to an incoming one — then the two genuinely sum to constant
  ink. Worth auditing in every lane's `leave()`.
- [hermes_counter] **A blank-handoff sweep MUST count only the TOPMOST active `.tz` section.**
  Zones are opaque on ascending track indices, so the incoming zone covers the outgoing one
  from its own `data-start`. A sweep that counts atoms in all visible sections still sees the
  covered beat's ink and reports the handoff as fine — my first sweep missed the 40.58 cut
  entirely for exactly this reason and only flagged 40.75 onward, after the outgoing zone
  expired. Filter by `max(data-track-index)` before summing.
- [hermes_counter] **Unprimed Playwright seeks report ink the render never paints.** Seeking a
  paused timeline without priming shows `leave()`'s `fromTo({opacity:1},...)` FROM value, so a
  highlight ring that enters at 16.72 measured opacity 1 from 11.87. It is a probe artifact:
  the mp4 at 13.50 has no ring. Prime `progress(1) -> progress(0)` like `geometry_audit.py`
  does, and settle any disagreement against an `ffmpeg` frame. Corollary: the ghost INFLATES
  ink readings, so an unprimed sweep under-reports blank windows.
- [hermes_counter] **The run-3 cue sheets can be wrong about word onsets, and a handoff built
  on a bad cue cannot be fixed by retiming around it.** `CUE["means"] = 15.50` — the word
  "means" actually starts at **15.26** (15.46 is "that"). Moving both the key-term exit and
  the first ledger row onto the real onset closed a 0.27s hole that no amount of fade-length
  tuning had closed. Check `transcript_tight.json` before trusting an inherited cue.
- [hermes_counter] **A pill-radius meter fill at ~6% renders as a slider KNOB.** `border-radius:
  h/2` on both track and fill is correct for a bar that reaches full, but a 28.8x30 sliver at
  radius 15 is a circle parked at the left of the track. Drop track AND fill to ~0.3x the bar
  height for any paired/sliver chart — and give BOTH bars of a pair the same radius, or the
  pair stops reading as one grid. (Confirms productivity_counter's finding on a second lane.)
- [hermes_counter] **Fixing a dead frame by crossfading in place can trade a black hole for a
  double exposure.** My first fix left `24 / FULL LISTING` dissolving THROUGH `PROCEDURAL
  DISCLOSURE` at ~50/50 for 7 frames — legal, ink-continuous, and visibly mush in a still.
  When two type systems must share one canvas, keep the dissolve to ~0.16s (about 3 frames)
  so the incoming element dominates immediately. Read the frame; the ink metric says both
  fixes are equally "fine".
- [hermes_counter] **Filling a beat's opening with the SHAPE it is about to fill is what makes
  a pre-roll look deliberate.** Beat 3's cut now lands on its label plus an EMPTY meter track,
  and beat 4's on a labelled scoreboard reading `0 MCP SERVERS CONNECTED`. Neither invents a
  claim, both are visibly waiting for content, and they beat pre-rolling a fade that is still
  30% opaque at the cut.
- [hermes_counter] **TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH vs the Counter lane — an unresolved tension worth
  Miguel's ruling.** This transcript contains **zero spoken numbers**, so every figure in the
  lane (24/830/3,320 tools, 1,028,575 tokens, 23/24 at $0.96) comes from the primary source.
  `productivity_icon`/`productivity_counter` read the law as banning source-article numbers
  and deleted theirs. I kept these: the lane verdict says "use where real numbers exist",
  nothing on screen contradicts him, and stripping them would gut the lane on this video. Two
  lanes now read the same law opposite ways — this needs a ruling, not another silent call.
- [gate2] A reported 3.3s stillness gap (35.0-38.3) again contained two real builds — the
  `$0.96` benchmark chip at 35.64 and the solved badge at 37.80. That is now five lanes
  reporting the same dedup blindness; treat every gap as unverified by default.
- [hermes_counter] Final state for the record: geometry 5 rounds all 0 errors / 0 warnings
  (57 real atom ids measured across 5 sections — not a wrapper-shaped report), 44 distinct
  states from 163 samples, 0 idle candidates, 10 frames read, **0 near-empty frames of 1626**

## Run 4 verification + rework pass — meatwrapper / icon (2026-08-10)

- [meatwrapper_icon] **A short that passed all three gates still shipped 62 near-empty
  frames and 29 dropped caption frames.** The item was on disk as finished (geometry 0/0,
  gate-2 "law_violations: []", QC v3 pass). Re-running only the FREE checks against the
  delivered mp4 found, in ~3 minutes: **5 fully BLACK top-zone frames at 4.033-4.167**,
  **53 near-blank dark frames at 25.767-27.500**, **4 near-empty cream frames at
  46.433-46.533**, and **29 single-frame caption dropouts** scattered mid-video. Second
  independent confirmation of grokprice_counter's standing rule — on any hand-off or
  re-dispatch, re-run gate 1 and gate 2 against the ARTIFACT; the expensive gate is the
  one you can skip.
- [meatwrapper_icon] **`leave()` easing with `SOFT` (power3.out) is the mechanical cause
  of the crossfade-trough class, and one constant fixes every instance at once.** A
  `fromTo({opacity:1},{opacity:0, ease:power3.out})` has dumped 66% of its opacity by
  p=0.31, so the outgoing element is a ghost long before the incoming one is painted.
  Adding `const EXIT = "power3.in"` and routing every fade-to-0 through it removed BOTH
  troughs on this short (62 → 20 near-empty frames) with zero other changes, and gate 1
  stayed 0/0 — the longer exits never put two atoms over the audit's 0.15 opacity floor
  at a 0.5s sample. slop_counter logged this on the counter lane; it is now confirmed as
  a chassis-wide defect, so **grep every generator for `leave(` and check its ease**.
- [meatwrapper_icon] **`build_captions`' `t1 = next_t0 - 0.02` is still live in
  generators whose SIBLING LANE already fixed it.** meatwrapper_kinetic logged and fixed
  the butt-join in this same run; the icon lane of the SAME video shipped with the 0.02s
  hole and dropped 29 caption frames. Fixing it took one line and the per-frame sweep
  went 36 → 7 blank caption frames, the remaining 7 all before the first spoken word at
  0.22s. A caption dropout is invisible to gate 2's 3fps grid and to Gemini.
- [meatwrapper_icon] **"0 gaps >= 0.25s" is not "no dropouts".** The previous pass's own
  adjudication (a 10fps caption-band sweep) was correct and still missed the defect: at
  10fps you cannot see a 1/30s hole. Sample the caption band at the RENDER's frame rate,
  never at a convenience rate — the whole 59s decodes in ~4s either way.
- [meatwrapper_icon] **The near-empty ink metric is blind to hairline chrome, so treat a
  sub-threshold run as a POINTER, not a verdict.** Beat 3's opening measures 0.00029 ink
  (2 of 6816 downscaled pixels) while two dashed 76px seats are plainly on screen — a
  2-design-px border is 3.75 render px and washes out at 96x71. The metric was right that
  the window was the emptiest in the short and wrong that it was blank; the fix came from
  looking at the extracted frame, not from the number.
- [meatwrapper_icon] **Moving the VISUAL cut two words later is the cheapest fix for a
  sparse beat opening, and the transcript almost always offers a better boundary.** Beat
  3's content-plan bound is "Now," (25.76) but its first event is cued on "become"
  (27.50) — 1.74s of near-empty black. Cutting on "this, you" (26.86) hands the time back
  to beat 2, which was already sitting on its COMPLETE crossed-out composition (the "0%
  VALUE ADDED" punchline), and leaves the seats waiting a purposeful 0.63s. Cost: a
  `VIS_CUTS = {beat_index: phrase}` table applied to `starts[]` in `timings()`, plus
  slop_kinetic's tiling assertion (`beats[i][1] == beats[i+1][0]`) so retiming one
  boundary can never open a hole.
- [meatwrapper_icon] Empty seats on a dark canvas need a heavier dash than the run-3
  default: `rgba(255,255,255,0.30)` on `#101012` is invisible at phone size, and during a
  slot-then-fill opening it is the ONLY ink on screen. 0.46 reads without competing with
  the tiles that land in it.
- [gate3] **Fourth factory occurrence, third on this exact short, of the tweet-duration
  noise class.** Verdict: "Tweet graphic remains on screen for approximately 7 seconds
  (00:48 to 00:55)". Measured on the delivered mp4 by cropping the card's own rect
  (99,461,881,257) and counting near-pure-white pixels per frame (cream is 246,241,234,

  through 51.4 → 0.000 at 51.6, i.e. **48.50-51.47 = 3.00s**. 00:55 is the CTA cut where

## Run 4 — hackers / kinetic, round 2 (2026-08-10)

- [hackers_kinetic] **A short can pass geometry 0/0, a full gate-2 frame read AND
  Gemini QC v3 while carrying 2.5s of BLANK top zone.** Re-verifying the already
  "finished" run-4 build found six blank/near-blank runs: 3.90 (title -> tweet),
  7.60-7.80 (tweet -> first key term), 22.20-22.30 and 40.80-41.30 (beat cuts),
  **27.20-28.30 = 1.2s of empty cream holding a single 105px chip**, and 55.40 (a
  term handoff). Gate 1 sees nothing to measure, gate 2's 3fps grid lands inside a
  0.1-0.3s window only by luck, and the judge passed it twice. The only reliable
  detector is a pixel sweep — see the next bullet.
- [all] **Build the dead-frame sweep on COLOUR, not grayscale, and crop ABOVE the
  caption pill.** Two traps cost me an hour: (a) cropping the top 862px includes
  the pill's upper half, so a genuinely blank frame still scores ~3.8% ink — crop
  to 800px; (b) a grayscale threshold of 24 is blind to the two things this design
  system paints most, a WHITE logo plate on cream (|Δ|≈13) and a
  `rgba(20,20,22,0.07)` meter track (|Δ|≈16), so real content reported as 0.0000.
  Working recipe: screenshot 1080x800 of the PAUSED timeline every 0.1s, resize to
  108x80 RGB, take the modal colour as background, count pixels whose **max channel
  delta > 13**, flag < 1.0%. 670 samples in ~25s, no render, no API spend. The same
  scan run on the finished mp4 (ffmpeg rawvideo) is the post-render proof.
- [hackers_kinetic] **Four distinct fixes, because the dead-frame class has four
  distinct causes.** (1) handoff inside one section = cross the fades (outgoing
  starts leaving 0.16s before the incoming enters); (2) section cut = PRE-ROLL the
  first element ~0.4s before `data-start` (the clip is hidden, the tween runs
  invisibly); (3) a cast that must pop = author it frame-0 safe instead
  (`fromTo({scale:0.86},{scale:1})`, NO opacity tween); (4) a beat whose first
  content is anchored to a word 1.4s after the spoken beat starts = **MOVE THE
  CUT** and let the previous beat hold its completed composition.
- [hackers_kinetic] **The kterm crossfade window is knife-edged: 0.16s of overlap
  double-exposes two headlines, 0.26s empties the zone.** With both display lines
  at the same y, a 0.06s overlap was still caught by the 3fps sampler and reads as
  a rendering glitch on a still ("CYBERSECURITY" through "BROKE"). Correct answer
  is neither: set the exit so the outgoing line dies ~1 frame BEFORE the incoming
  slams, and make sure the BEAT (not the headline) carries the handoff — I pulled
  the test cage in 0.43s earlier so the CYBERSECURITY -> BROKE OUT change never
  lands on bare cream.
- [hackers_kinetic] **A Range-box ink probe must skip `overflow:hidden` wrappers or
  it invents a seam violation.** My first pill-clearance pass reported `b4-cb4`
  (a `barfill`) at 858.8px, i.e. 53px INSIDE the caption pill; the wrapper is 92
  design units tall with the fill translated below it, and `Range.selectNodeContents`
  ignores the clip. `geometry_audit.py` already has this guard (contentRect skipped
  on overflow hidden/clip) — any home-grown measurement script needs the same one.
  The real offender was 20x smaller and elsewhere: the PAID SUBS chip at 806.2px.
- [hackers_kinetic] Confirmed for the third lane in a row that **the caption pill's
  painted top is 805.2px** (measured live, `.scappill` rect) while the audit's seam
  band is 838.5-864.5. A chip bottoming at 806.2 touched it with a 0-finding audit
  and is exactly Miguel's "X Premium+ card touched the captions" defect. Budget
  used here: worst top-zone ink 787.5px.
- [gate2] **Both `[still 3.0s]` markers on this short were real holds, and both
  needed an ffmpeg probe to prove it** (10.20 = MOST HACKS holding before the first
  logo at 10.5; 46.50 = the cage holding before the breakout move). That is the
  fourth lane reporting the same thing — a stillness marker is a request to look,
  never a finding in either direction.
- [hackers_kinetic] Cheap standing checks that were all clean and cost ~2s on the
  emitted HTML: 246 ids with zero duplicates, 152 tween selectors all resolving,
  zero section children with no tween, and a trigram scan of every zone string
  against the transcript (join a `wordline`'s `.kw` spans first, or every multi-word
  key term reads as isolated single words and the check silently passes).
- [hackers_kinetic] Final numbers: geometry 5 rounds all 0 errors / 0 warnings,
  78 distinct states from 201 samples, 11 frames read, 0 idle candidates, longest
  hold 3.0s, 0 dead frames and 0 caption dropouts across 2008 rendered frames,
  tweet 3.47s, QC v3 pass on round 1 with zero visual and zero semantic errors.

## Run 4 rebuild — fablevssol / counter (2026-08-10, second pass)

- [fablevssol_counter] **A completed item that audits 0-error and passes Gemini can still
  carry 3.8s of dead frames.** This lane had already shipped run 4 (gate 1 clean, QC pass,
  paperwork claiming "every beat now opens with its first element already arriving"). A
  0.05s **ink sweep** over the live timeline found **6 near-empty/blank top-zone runs**:
  1.05s of empty cream at the beat-2 cut (two 12px mono labels only), **1.75s of near-black
  at the beat-4 cut** (one 76px tile on the dark ground), 0.35s at beat 7, plus three
  0.20-0.25s handover holes. Gate 1 sees no violation in an empty frame and gate 3 passed
  it. **Re-verify an inherited build before trusting its paperwork.**
- [fablevssol_counter] **Threshold on INK AREA, not on an atom count** (this closes the
  productivity_icon open question with a working number): sum `w*h*opacity` per `.tz`
  section child, using the **Range rect for unpainted text** and the layout box for
  painted/`overflow:hidden` atoms, and flag any sample under **3% of the zone**
  (27,945px2 at 1080x862.5). An atom-count sweep passes a frame holding one mono kicker;
  this one fails it. Sweep at 0.05s — 0.1s steps straddle 2-frame troughs.
- [fablevssol_counter] **`leave()` on `power3.out` is THE mechanical cause of the
  handoff trough, and one character fixes it factory-wide.** A `fromTo({opacity:1},
  {opacity:0, ease:power3.out})` has dumped 66% by p=0.31, so the outgoing beat is a ghost
  before the incoming one crosses 0.30. Switching ONLY the exit ease to `power3.in` (which
  holds ~0.88 at the halfway point and drops late) plus a 0.16-0.30s **pre-roll** of each
  section's opening cast took this 83s short from 6 dead windows to **0 near-empty frames
  in 2496**, measured on the render. (Independent confirmation of slop_counter's finding,
  now with the pre-roll half attached.)
- [fablevssol_counter] **LAW 11 escape that ran in run 3 AND the first run-4 pass:** at
  "you will find the ideal model **for yourself**" the stepping highlight ring walked back
  onto the *Claude* tile and dimmed the other three, with "1 MODEL KEPT" in terracotta
  underneath — i.e. the screen picks a model he explicitly leaves to the viewer. Fix that
  keeps the beat: the stepping ring **opens into a ROW ring holding all four marks** and
  nothing is dimmed. (The kinetic-lane worker logged the same call on the same sentence —
  two lanes, same trap, so it is a property of the sentence, not of a lane.)
- [fablevssol_counter] **The 3-word caption-echo guard is necessary, NOT sufficient — and
  the failures cluster on 2-word payoff lines.** Three top-zone strings sat directly above
  a pill containing the same two words at the same instant: chip "WRONG QUESTION" over
  "wrong question.", "PERSONAL PREFERENCE" over "down to personal preference,", and
  "ALL EXCELLENT" over "absolutely excellent." All three cleared the trigram guard. Fixes
  that cost nothing: "the real question" (forward-framing, the sibling icon lane's move),
  "YOUR CALL", "NO WRONG CHOICE". **Diff every top-zone string against the caption clip
  that is live at its own start time**, not just against the transcript.
- [fablevssol_counter] **A lane with no arrows should have no `.rule` atoms.** All 4
  warnings the previous pass shipped were meter fills and a dashed divider being
  end-checked as connectors. Moving them to `.mfill` / `.strike` / `.dline` (identical
  CSS) makes gate 1 skip the connector law because there is genuinely nothing to
  terminate — 0 warnings, and unlike `data-bleed` it does not also switch off the seam,
  clipped and margin checks on those elements.
- [fablevssol_counter] **Two same-colour rings alive at once read as one doubled outline,
  and a ring handoff is where that happens.** Fading the stepping tile ring *at* the row
  ring's cue left them overlapping for ~0.16s. Retire the outgoing ring so it is fully
  dead **before** the incoming one starts. Same family: a terracotta ring 8 design px under
  a terracotta meter reads as a doubled bar — 14 design px (26 render px) is the working
  clearance on this palette.
- [fablevssol_counter] **Top-heavy beats are fixable with zero new content: author the
  opening composition CENTRED and step it up on its cue.** Beat 3 (two marks, 3.3s), beat 4
  (one mark, 2.6s) and beat 7 (a whole scoreboard, 8.3s) all sat in the top band with an
  empty bottom. A comma-selector `tl.set({y:dy},0)` + `fromTo({y:dy},{y:0},
  immediateRender:false)` gives the group move with **no DOM wrapper**, so every atom stays
  a direct section child and gate 1 keeps measuring it. For a single hero element the same
  trick carries `scale` (110 design px centred -> 76 design px in the header slot).
- [fablevssol_counter] **When a beat opens before its content can legitimately exist, move
  the CUT and let the previous beat hold its finished frame.** Beat 5 opened on "Now,"

  dark beat hold a complete composition for another half second. Sections must still TILE —
  verified programmatically that every section's end equals the next one's start + 0.15
  overlap and the last ends exactly at the root duration.
- [fablevssol_counter] **A statement beat should ACCUMULATE, never swap in place.** Run 3
  removed FRONTIER/TIED to make room for the next line at the same y: that is a guaranteed
  blank frame if you sequence it and guaranteed ghosted type if you crossfade it. Stacking

  looks like a catastrophic finding instead of a bug in the harness. Use

  numbers are not comparable to the rendered-pixel scan.** A frame holding one mono
  command line scores ~2.6% by bbox and ~0.5% by real pixels. Use the bbox sweep to
  prove an atom is PAINTED at a given instant (it is exact about opacity and count)

## Run 4 verification + rework pass — meatwrapper / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [meatwrapper_diagram] **`SOFT = power3.out` on `leave()` is the one-line root cause of
  the blank-handoff class, and it survived a full three-gate pass on this item.** The
  delivered mp4 (0 geometry errors, Gemini QC pass, 20 fixes paperworked) contained **5
  fully blank cream frames at 3.933-4.067**: a power3.out fade has dumped 66% of its
  opacity by p=0.31, so the outgoing AI/NEW EMPLOYEE diagram was a ghost 0.15s before the
  MEAT WRAPPER slam even started. Adding `const EXIT = "power3.in"` and routing `leave()`
  through it (opacity in the TO vars) + running the exit UNDER the entrance took the whole
  video to **0 dead frames**. This is now the third lane (slop_counter, fablevssol_icon,
  here) to land on the same ease finding — treat `power3.out` exits as a defect in any
  run-3-forked generator, not a style choice.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] **The `PRE` lead is measured off the SECTION start, so a beat whose
  anchor phrase opens with a discourse marker still opens near-empty.** Beat 3 cut on
  "Now," (25.76) while its payoff word "become" is at 27.50: **1.74s / 53 frames at 0.03%
  ink**, holding nothing but two hairline dashed slots. meatwrapper_icon logged the
  symptom for a 0.24s offset; at 1.74s no pre-roll can save it. Fix that worked: move the
  CUT onto the payoff word and **pre-roll that element's slam by 0.14s** so the section's
  first frame is already composed — the cut becomes the event. The previous beat then
  holds its COMPLETE composition through "in order to avoid this", which is literally what
  "this" refers to.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] **A dashed placeholder on cream is 0.03% ink — a dead frame by any
  honest metric.** Two dashed slots (1.5px grey dashes) do not read as a composition at
  phone size, so "slot then fill" only counts as content when the slot has mass or a hero
  node lands with it. Distinguish this from a *labelled* dashed node (beat 4's
  `COPY / PASTE`), which states a claim and measures fine.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] **Deleting a text can SURFACE a floating-connector warning.**
  `geometry_audit.py` exempts any rule with a TEXT within 60px above it spanning >=40% of
  its width (the "underline" heuristic). The `THE MEAT WRAPPER` label 36 design px above
  the beat-1 return arrow had been silently exempting a connector whose ends genuinely
  touch no box (it runs 58 design px below the row). A 0-warning report can therefore be
  an artefact of nearby type, not of correct termination.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] **`cross_el`'s rotated stroke wrappers were id-less and permanently
  opaque** — the meatwrapper_kinetic finding, one level deeper. As soon as the block they
  sit on MOVED (a group ride-up), the invisible wrappers stayed behind and the audit
  reported a live 4.5s floating connector at coordinates nothing was drawn at. Fix:
  give each wrapper an id, author it `opacity:0`, and switch it on/off with the strokes
  (`cross_in()` / `cross_out()`); the whole atom then drops under the audit's 0.15 opacity
  floor instead of needing an exemption.
- [meatwrapper_diagram] **A group MOVE needs no wrapper and fixes top-heavy beats.** Beat 2
  held its relay in the top third with the bottom 60% of the zone empty for 6.0s. Authoring
  it 72 design px LOWER (on the zone's optical centre) and riding it up in ONE
  `moveto("#a,#b,#c,...")` as the measurement lands below it costs one tween, keeps every
  atom a direct section child (gate 1 keeps measuring all of them), and needs no
  `data-overlap-ok`. Same recipe as threed_diagram's `groupmove`; confirmed safe here with
  a 0.5s ramp ending 0.3s before the incoming block's first ink.
- [gate2] **Two probe caveats worth knowing.** (a) A Playwright screenshot taken on a fresh
  page with forward seeks can show PHANTOM elements the render never paints (here: two
  logo slots whose only later tween is a `leave()`, whose immediateRender bakes opacity 1

## Run 4 verification + rework pass — slop / counter (2026-08-10)

- [slop_counter] **The blank-handoff DOM sweep this factory keeps copying is WRONG at
  section cuts.** Every version of it (mine included, first try) sums painted ink over
  *every ACTIVE* `.tz` section. But sections are opaque backgrounds on ascending track
  indices, so the incoming one covers the outgoing one from its own `data-start` — the
  outgoing beat's ink therefore MASKS the incoming beat's empty frame. Measured here: the
  all-sections sweep scored the 57.44 CTA cut at >3% ink and reported it clean, while the
  rendered mp4 had **2 frames at 0.000% ink** there. Counting only the **top-most active
  `.tz`** (highest `data-track-index`) reproduces the render exactly. Fix your sweep before
  quoting "0 zero-atom samples" — the number is meaningless at precisely the moments the
  class lives at.
- [slop_counter] **A fully-paperworked item that passed all three gates still shipped two
  blank-frame defects.** Re-dispatched onto a finished run-4 build (0 errors/0 warnings on
  disk, `pass:true` Gemini verdict, 20 fixes logged, `law_violations: 0`), the free
  deterministic scans found: 2 frames at 0.000% ink at the outro cut plus ~0.46s of a
  barely-tinted odometer ghost, and 5 frames at 0.17-0.45% ink at an INTRA-beat act
  handover (5.37-5.50) that rendered as two logo plates alone in the upper-left of an empty
  cream zone. Order that worked: (1) re-run the generator and `diff` index.html against the
  shipped one — byte-identical proves the artifact is the generator's output, (2) re-run
  gate 1, (3) scan the RENDER, (4) only then read frames. Steps 1-3 cost ~2 minutes and no
  API spend.
- [slop_counter] **Landing a CTA line on its own spoken word can BE the dead-frame fix.**
  "follow" starts at 57.44, which is the outro section's `data-start` exactly, and the build
  had `rise("#oa", t0 + 1.00)` — a second late AND leaving the cut frame empty. Pre-rolling
  it to `t0 - 0.22` (plus the counter to `t0-0.34`, its label `t0-0.28`, the empty track
  `t0-0.20`) fixed the blank cut and the cue accuracy in one edit, and the section's first
  frame is now the approved "scoreboard already at ZERO" composition.
- [slop_counter] **A 4-logo white-plate row on cream is only ~0.45% painted ink**, because
  the plates themselves are ~17 gray levels from the cream ground (under the standard >28
  threshold) — only the marks count. So a logo row alone can never lift a handoff frame out
  of the near-empty band on cream; the label, track or numeral has to arrive with it. This
  is the cream-ground twin of the "dark tiles on dark canvas" dedup blindness.
- [slop_counter] **`frame_review` is bit-stable across a re-render of CHANGED html when the
  change adds no distinct visual state.** Before and after the two timing fixes: 62 distinct
  states / 186 samples / 124 collapsed / one 3.3s hold, identical. Useful as a control — if
  your state count moves after a pure timing fix, you added or deleted a state you did not
  intend.

## Run 4 rebuild — grokbuild / icon (2026-08-10, wave 2)

- [grokbuild_icon] **The blank-handoff class is BIGGER than every prior bullet says, and
  the atom-opacity sweep everyone is using under-reports it.** The wave-1 build of this
  lane passed gate 1 (0/0), gate 3 (first call, zero errors) and its own `op>=0.30` sweep,
  and still rendered **10 fully blank top-zone windows totalling ~1.8s**. Two reasons the
  sweep missed them: (a) sections OVERLAP by 0.15s, so a sweep that counts atoms across
  all active `.tz` clips keeps counting the outgoing beat's atoms while the incoming
  opaque section already covers them; (b) an opacity threshold cannot see a crossfade
  trough. **The honest check is pixels**: drive the paused timeline in Playwright,
  screenshot the top 790px every 0.05s, take each frame's MODAL grey value as its
  background and flag frames where <0.5% of pixels differ by >28. 1462 samples in ~50s,
  no render, and it is exactly what gate 2 would see. Wave 1: 10 runs, worst 0.65s.
  After the fix: NONE.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Two generator constants retire the class, including the half nobody
  had measured.** Only 4 of my 10 dead windows were section cuts; **6 were intra-section
  PHASE swaps** — `out()` finishing before the next phase's first tween crossed
  visibility. Rules that produced 0: `PREROLL = 0.35` (a section's first element starts
  before its own `data-start`; the clip is hidden so the tween runs invisibly and the cut
  lands painted) and, for every phase swap inside a section, **entrance = exit_start +
  0.10 with exit duration 0.26**. Both are one-line changes at each call site and neither
  costs a re-cut.
- [grokbuild_icon] **A dashed slot can paint OVER the plate that fills it, and no gate
  can see it.** The beat-1 hero is authored before the slot row, so `sl2` won the paint
  order and its dashed border was drawn straight across the docked hero's white plate
  (proved with a 1:1 `ffmpeg` crop; the DOM says the rects match to 0.06px and the radii
  resolve equal, so nothing is geometrically wrong). Gate 1 skips the pair via the >=0.96
  containment rule and Gemini passed it. Two fixes: never emit a slot for a position an
  element docks INTO, and `out()` every remaining slot ~0.12s after its logo lands.
  Slot borders also need their own colour token (~0.36 alpha on dark): at hairline alpha
  a waiting slot is invisible on the dark canvas, so it is not visibly waiting.
- [grokbuild_icon] **`codex-color.png` is a full-bleed rounded square too**, not just
  `kimi.png` — measured 640x640, 97% opaque, mean RGB (200,208,255), corner radius ~0.19
  of its width. Padded 18% inside a white plate it is a box inside a box. The treatment
  that works for BOTH on cream and dark: keep the light plate, drop the pad to 0.08 and
  give the `<img>` a concentric inner radius (`plate_radius - pad`). Full-bleed is wrong
  for kimi specifically — its artwork is dark (mean RGB 44,45,47) and edge-to-edge it
  vanishes on a dark canvas, which is the opposite of what the plate is for.
- [grokbuild_icon] **A highlight ring drawn outside a row in a stacked list can never fit
  in the gutter.** Rows at 60 pitch with 52-tall chips leave 8px, so a ring at inset 10
  crossed 2px into the row above AND doubled the chip's own terracotta border. The fix is
  compositional, not geometric: give the highlighted row **its own group break** (28 design
  px instead of 8 — it is the pricing perk, not a capability, so the break is honest),
  drop the host's accent border to a hairline and let the ring be the only outline. Result:
  24 design px clear above, 22.5 real px of air all round. Gate 1 says nothing either way —
  rings are collision-exempt.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Check every entrance against the WORD it names, not just against its
  beat.** Wave 1's beat-4 landed the Claude Code plate at 42.70 and the Grok plate at
  44.28 — so the GROK logo appeared exactly on the words "Claude Code" and Claude Code
  appeared 1.6s before them. Geometry cannot see it, the Gemini semantic pass passed it,

- [slop_kinetic] **The arithmetic that turns "exit on the previous cue" into a
  blank frame, stated once so nobody re-derives it.** `liftout` rides
  `SOFT = power3.out`, whose value is `1-(1-p)^3`: opacity is **0.34 at p=0.31**
  and **0.13 at p=0.50**. An entrance on `POP = back.out(2.2)` is only
  **0.62 opaque at p=0.15**. So an exit fired at the PREVIOUS spoken cue is
  visually gone one third of the way through its own duration, long before the
  next slam paints. Working rule: **start the exit at `entrance_cue - 0.06s`**
  (here 2.36 -> 2.56 with d=0.30) and the two ramps cross with ink never below
  12% of the zone. This is the same class slop_counter fixed with `power3.in`,
  but retiming ONE exit is cheaper and cannot create the new gate-1 collisions a
  global ease change does (measured: switching the ease globally would have put
  `EFFICIENT` over a still-0.94-opaque `UPSKILL` at the t=38.0 audit sample,
  a 71% area overlap = a fresh ERROR).
- [slop_kinetic] **NEW near-blank class: the enumeration row built across its own
  clause.** "one, no one is ever going to read" was staged ordinal (7.78) ->
  label (8.28) -> datum (9.28), which is perfect claim-sync and leaves the whole
  1080x862 zone holding a 15px ordinal for 0.4s and a 24px label for 1.0s.
  **The datum IS the clause** — land ordinal + number + label as ONE lockup on
  the ordinal cue. Same rule as productivity_checklist's intra-row stagger, but
  the trigger here is semantic staging, not choreography.
- [slop_kinetic] **The centre-then-step group move has a collision trap: key the
  step ~0.10s BEFORE the incoming element, never to its arrival.** Row 1 alone was
  authored +64 design px low (on the two-row block's optical centre) and ridden up
  as row 2 lands. Keyed to row 2's own cue (9.96), the t=10.00 audit sample catches
  the moving row still 47 px low while row 2 is already 0.55 opaque: two 84px
  numerals sharing a rail overlap **28% by area** = a text-vs-text ERROR (the
  audit's tolerance is 0.20). Starting the move at 9.86 puts the mover 11 px from
  home at that sample — 0 errors, and it reads as making room.

## Run 4 verification + rework pass — productivity / icon (2026-08-10)

- [productivity_icon] **A HIGHLIGHT RING IN FLIGHT IS A BAR THROUGH YOUR TYPE — new
  defect class, and it is in every lane that uses `hljump`.** The jump tweens x/y/
  width/height over 0.42s, so a CROSS-ROW move between differently-sized targets
  spends ~0.3s as a terracotta border travelling *through* whatever lies between.
  Measured on this short's own render: the ring sliced "40 DOCUMENTS" at 17.70,
  "16,000 CLIENTS" at 20.20, the "$2" of "$20-$100" mid-slam at 32.95, "WHAT TO
  BUILD?" plus both ledger labels at 51.75, and the same headline again at 53.95.
  Gate 1 cannot see it (rings are collision-exempt AND the frames are mid-tween,
  between its 0.5s samples), and gate 3 passed the video twice. This is literally
  Miguel's "content cut by an orange bar" complaint, produced by the crown move.
  **Fix: `hlswap(eid, t_out, t_in, rect)` — fade out (0.20s), reposition while
  invisible with a `tl.set`, fade in (0.30s) — with `t_in` placed AFTER the target's
  own entrance completes, which also satisfies law 5's "lands on a STATIC asset".**
  Keep `hljump`'s travel only for SAME-ROW SAME-SIZE targets (the tile scramble
  Miguel called "chef's kiss"): there the ring is wider than a tile, so it crosses
  the gaps, never a mark. Six of this short's seven transitions became swaps.
- [productivity_icon] **A ring must also LEAVE when the subject turns, not when the
  next target is ready.** Run-4 round 1 kept the ring on the dimmed, crossed-out
  tools card for 2.2s while the live NOT SCARED card was on screen and the caption
  read "the people who are". The swap gives you the leave for free: fade out on the
  word that turns the sentence, return on the word that names the new target.
- [productivity_icon] **TOP-PINNED BEAT OPENINGS are the residual composition defect
  of the Icon lane, worth ~16% of a short.** Three of six beats here opened with
  their whole cast in the top ~35% of the zone while 65-78% of the canvas sat empty
  for 3.5s / 4.2s / 2.0s (9.7s of a 62s short). Neither free gate reports it —
  nothing is blank, nothing collides — and Gemini passed it twice. Fix that invents
  no content and needs no re-cut: **author the opening cast on the zone's optical
  centre and ride it UP in ONE discrete `gmove` on the cue that needs the space**
  (offset = centre the cast's own ink span in the 0..410 working canvas: 82 / 88 /
  88 design units here). Rings ride with their target via one `hljump` sharing the
  step's duration and ease, which is HIGHLIGHT DISCIPLINE done honestly.
- [productivity_icon] **The pre-roll recipe fails if the container is pre-rolled and
  its contents are not.** This lane's own pass-1 learning says "pre-roll the beat's
  first element" — it pre-rolled the CARD (t0-0.10) and left its three marks at
  t0+0.04..+0.26, so the section's first frame was an EMPTY white card on cream
  (0.02% ink at 35.800). The rule that actually holds is the union of both: **the
  beat's opening CONTAINER AND ITS CONTENTS share one pre-rolled cue.** Same class
  found 4.5s later in the same beat: the answer card popped 0.26s before its "NOT
  SCARED" title = 8 rendered frames of an empty rounded card.
- [productivity_icon] **The `crop=1080:800` dead-frame scan needs a threshold of 12
  on cream, and the DOM sweep is the authority.** White tiles (#FFF) differ from
  this cream (#F6F1EA) by 9-21 per channel, so the ledger's standard >28 test scores
  a fully-composed frame as empty. Even at 12 the metric bottoms out at 1.0% on a
  dimmed-card frame that is perfectly legible. Run both: the pixel scan proves the
  RENDER (it caught the 35.800 blank frame the DOM sweep's 0.05s grid also caught),
  the DOM ink-area sweep (sum of w*h*op over non-ring `.tz` children) gives the
  honest number — 6.32% min / 18.12% median here.
- [productivity_icon] **Two independent seam numbers disagree by 69px and the
  rendered one is right.** The DOM Range box put "A LOT MORE" (Poppins 800, fs 40)
  at ink bottom 790.8px = 14.4px off the caption pill — under every working floor in
  this ledger. The rendered row profile (`ffmpeg` frame, pixels differing from the
  modal background by >26) shows the last content row at 722 against a pill first

  pill, then adjudicate the worst atom on a rendered crop before moving any type.
- [gate1] **The atom census is a MAX-simultaneous count, not a sum.** Pass 1 filed 65
  atoms for this project; the same HTML measures 58 distinct ids because a dashed
  slot and the tile that replaces it never coexist. Both numbers are "real atoms" —

## Run 4 second pass — threed / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [threed_diagram] **Two full compositions that share the same space must be HARD
  SWAPPED, never crossfaded.** Beat 2 dissolved the fake-3D pipeline (2 nodes + icons
  + chip + a big X) into the browser window that occupies the same rect: `leaves(...,
  25.05, 0.26)` against `popo("#b-fr", 25.16, 0.42)`. The render showed BOTH
  compositions readable at ~50% for ~7 frames (25.10-25.23) *and* one genuinely blank
  frame at 25.17 (0.01% ink) where the outgoing was gone and the incoming had not
  crossed the threshold. Gate 1 was 0/0, Gemini QC v3 passed it, and the 3fps manifest
  kept the ghost frame as a normal state. **Fix: give the switch-off and the switch-on
  ONE shared timestamp with 0.01s ramps** (grokprice_counter's recipe) and let the
  incoming element be frame-0 safe (`fade(sel, SWAP, 0.01)` + `settle`). At 30fps no
  rendered frame can land inside a 0.01s window whose start is on a frame boundary.
  Measured after: 25.00-25.30 runs 4.93-10.04% ink at full res, zero ghosting.
- [threed_diagram] **The dashed-slot skeleton is the fix for a sparse beat opening, and
  it will make your own dead-frame scan lie to you.** Beat 3 opened on ONE 130x56 chip
  for 1.93s; publishing two dashed slots that are the exact silhouette of the nodes
  landing in them turns that into a 3-box composition — but the 1/3-res ink scan still
  reads the window at 0.63-0.73%, i.e. it still "flags" it. Full resolution reads
  0.72-0.84% and the extracted frame plainly shows the composition. **Re-measure every
  flagged window at full res AND pull the frame before acting**; a thin dashed stroke is
  under a downsampled cell's noise floor (grokbuild_diagram logged the same, this is the
  second lane).
- [threed_diagram] **"Move the cut" and "publish the skeleton" are complements, not
  alternatives.** Beat 5 cut on the transcript boundary (49.26) while its first spoken
  cue was 52.06 — 3.27s of a lone `YOU` chip on empty cream, the worst window in the
  short. Handing 1.70s back to beat 4 (which was holding a COMPLETE two-panel
  composition, scored by `frame_review` as confirmed stillness) still left 1.6s; adding
  the dashed viewport silhouette still left 3.3s if the cut had not moved. Both together
  give a balanced two-object opening that waits 1.4s. Cost: two constants.
- [threed_diagram] **A `groupmove` on a comma-joined GSAP selector is safe on arrow
  WRAPPERS that carry an inline `rotate()`** — GSAP re-composes the transform, so the
  connector keeps its angle while the group rides. That is what lets a beat open on the
  zone's optical centre and step up on its cue without a DOM wrapper, which would hide
  every child from `geometry_audit.py` (it only enumerates a section's direct children).
- [threed_diagram] **Chrome-before-content hides in the 0.18s "choreography" offsets
  generators are proud of.** Three solid painted containers here stood empty for
  0.20-0.46s (solar panel vs its motif, water panel vs its drop/ripple, body viewport vs
  its figure) — all deliberate staggers, all reading as an empty box holding the frame.
  A container and the content that IDENTIFIES it share one cue (+0.02 to +0.14s); keep
  the stagger for secondary rows only. `popo`'s `back.out(2.2)` is ~1.03 at p=0.33, so
  +0.14s on a 0.42s entrance means the content starts exactly as its box finishes — that
  reads as choreography, 0.46s reads as chrome.

## Run 4 second pass — slop / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [slop_diagram] **"Verify, don't rebuild" is right, but the verification has to reach
  the PIXELS.** I was re-dispatched onto a finished item: 0 errors / 0 warnings on
  disk, a `pass:true` Gemini verdict, 15 documented fixes, `law_violations: 0`. Gate 1
  re-ran and reproduced bit-for-bit; the generator re-emitted a byte-identical
  `index.html`. Both facts are worth having and neither one says anything about the
  render — the delivered mp4 contained **10 frames of literally ZERO top-zone ink**
  (2.53-2.63 and 5.47-5.70, measured 0.0000 at 360x263). That is now the fourth
  factory item to ship the blank-handoff class through a complete, passing gate chain.
  The free scan that finds it costs ~8s. Run it before you believe any paperwork,
  including your own.
- [slop_diagram] **The frame-exact HARD SWAP generalises, and it is the right tool
  whenever two compositions share a rect.** The card->key-term and key-term->funnel
  handovers both put the incoming element inside the outgoing one's box, so the three
  obvious fixes all fail: sequencing renders blank frames (a `power3.out` exit is 87%
  gone at mid-ramp), overlapping the ramps is a gate-1 collision (two atoms over the
  0.15 opacity floor in one rect), and `data-overlap-ok` would be the dishonest move.
  Recipe: `hard_off(out, t)` + `hard_on(in, t)` as 0.01s opacity ramps on ONE shared
  timestamp — narrower than a 30fps frame interval, so no rendered frame can fall
  inside — plus a `scale_in()` that carries the entrance's scale/slam motion in its
  own tween. The gesture survives, the blank frame cannot. Choose a swap instant off
  the audit's 0.5s sample grid and gate 1 never sees both atoms either.
- [slop_diagram] **A hard-swap fix can CREATE a chrome-before-content defect, because
  it removes the fade that was hiding one.** The models plate had always landed 0.18s
  before its first logo; while it faded in over 0.42s that was invisible, and the
  instant it became opaque on frame 1 it read as an empty white box on cream. Rule
  worth carrying: after every hard-cut fix, re-read the two frames on either side of
  the swap — you have changed what the first frame of that beat actually shows.
- [slop_diagram] **Splitting a labelled node into an empty box + a sibling label
  silently deletes the audit's `underline` exemption for any bar beneath it.**
  `geometry_audit.py` clears a `.rule` when some TEXT atom sits within 60px above it
  and spans >=40% of its width — and a `node_el` with an inline label IS that text
  atom. Turning NEVER DRIVEN into a dashed slot plus a separate `txt()` moved the
  label's Range box 84px above the equation bar, and a bar that had audited clean for
  two passes became a `floating` warning at 26.1-30.1. **A new floating warning right
  after a labelling change is this, not a geometry regression.** Honest fix: give the
  bar its own class (`.eqline`, byte-identical CSS) — an equation operator bar is not
  a connector and has no box edge to terminate on, so it must not be typed as one.
  Same family as the run-3 strike-through finding, reached from the opposite direction.
- [slop_diagram] **Sparse-opening triage, applied to five beats in one build.** Two
  different fixes, and picking the wrong one is what makes scaffolding read as chrome:
  (a) when the beat's final SHAPE is knowable, publish the missing pieces as dashed
  silhouettes — exact rect AND exact radius — each filled on its own spoken word, each
  waiting <= ~2.4s (services hero 1.46s, equation operand 2.36s, CRASH result 1.20s,
  METRICS 2.00s, scene-B system/output 1.30s/2.24s, outro nodes 0.64s/1.52s);
  (b) when there is only ONE node and no shape to promise, do NOT invent a slot —
  author it on the zone's optical CENTRE and ride it into position in one discrete
  `groupmove` timed to complete exactly as the first companion lands (the beat-3
  UPSKILL root, dy=148, finishing on the child's cue). Law 1 bans idle drift, not
  transitions, and a comma-joined GSAP selector needs no DOM wrapper, so every atom
  stays a direct section child.
- [slop_diagram] **The lane's own "he names them out of diagram order" trap.** Scene B
  is model -> system -> output on screen, but he says model, then output, then system,
  so cueing each node on its word left a HOLE in the middle of the pipeline for 0.94s.
  Neither gate can see it (nothing is blank, nothing collides) and it is invisible in
  code. Publishing the skeleton fixes it without re-ordering anything he says. Worth
  checking on any diagram whose spoken order differs from its spatial order.
- [gate2] Both stillness gaps on this short needed opposite verdicts, and only direct
  extraction separates them: 26.7->30.3 (3.7s) is a GENUINE hold — the emitted timeline
  schedules nothing between 26.37 and 30.16 and the frame at 28.20 is the complete
  equation — while 54.7->57.7 (3.0s) contains the bracket ring (54.70) and the
  AI INFRASTRUCTURE chip (56.22), both invisible to the 16x16 dedup on a dark canvas.
  **Reading the generator's tween schedule in the gap window is a free first pass** on
  this question and it is exact: if no tween is scheduled, the gap is real stillness,
  and you only need ffmpeg for the gaps that do contain tweens.
- [slop_diagram] Numbers for the record: geometry 5 rounds this pass (0/0 verify ->
  0/1 -> 0/0 -> 0/0 -> 0/0 final), 90 distinct measured atom ids across 5 sections,
  200 DOM ids with zero duplicates and 125 tween selectors all resolving, 1 render,

  2.63s, QC v3 pass on the first call with 0 visual, 0 semantic and 0 minor notes.

## Run 5 build — hermes / icon (2026-08-10, impeccable pass)

- [hermes_icon] **Lineage call, stated plainly:** the brief says fork run 3, but
  `shorts_run4/gen/hermes_icon_gen.py` is a fork of run 3 that already carries every
  pilot-verdict fix plus two the run-4 agent found with a painted-pixel seam sweep.
  Run 5 forked RUN 4. Re-deriving from run 3 would have meant re-shipping the n8n
  glyph, ladder.png, the circle check and the seam-touching outro wrapper in order to
  fix them again. Fork the most advanced compliant ancestor and say so.
- [hermes_icon] **Logos ship baked-in FRAMES, not just baked-in backgrounds.**
  `ai-models/nous-research.png` (the Nous girl) has a hard 4-6px BLACK SQUARE border
  painted into the raster. Inside our rounded white plate that is a sharp-cornered box
  inside a rounded box — the exact FILL THE SHAPE mismatch the verdict named — and on
  the white Hermes card in beat 4 it draws a second, competing card outline. Fix is 12
  lines: peel edge rows/cols whose dark coverage is >85%, +1px safety
  (`trim_frame()`), which measured 6px on this asset. Run 4's asset audit checked
  `opaque_frac` (ships its own background); add `edge_dark_coverage` (ships its own
  frame) to the same pre-flight. Every lane that uses this logo is exposed.
- [hermes_icon] **A highlight ring's radius must be target_radius + gap.** Run 4 put
  an r22 ring 12px outside an r18 capsule, so the highlight cornered TIGHTER than the
  thing it was highlighting. Rule for every lane: `ring_rad = target_rad + offset`
  (here r30). The tier-card rings already obeyed it by accident (r18 = r14 + 4).
- [hermes_icon] **Invented numerals cost nothing to delete.** The context read-outs
  (34% / 88% / 12% / 6%) are spoken nowhere in the transcript; run 4 filed them as
  still-open. Deleting all four and letting the gauge tell three states instead —
  fills on "tools consume context", FULL exactly on "context is finite", lean on
  "give access" — passed the semantic gate first try, and Gemini's summary cited
  "animated context usage meters" as a strength. Full-on-"finite" also satisfies
  METERS COMPLETE, so the honest reading and the law point the same way.
- [hermes_icon] **When a group dims, its caption dims with it.** Run 4 faded the 12
  tiles to 0.20 at "spoiler, they don't" and left "12 SERVERS · 3,320 TOOLS" at full
  strength, so at "crack the code" the loudest thing on screen was the stats line, not
  the ringed Nous lockup that IS the subject. No gate checks relative emphasis; this
  is a read-the-frame-and-squint defect.
- [impeccable] **The side-stripe ban caught a defect our own laws missed.** The tier
  cards carried a 6px terracotta left stripe whose OPACITY encoded "share of the
  catalog the agent gets" — data that cannot be decoded from an alpha value, drawn in
  the one form (coloured side-stripe on a card) impeccable bans outright. Deleting it
  plus symmetrising the card padding (28/14 -> 24/24) turned three floating clusters
  into a table. Useful pairing: STANDARD.md governs what is legal, impeccable governs
  what is good, and they overlap less than expected.
- [hermes_icon] **Deleting chrome does not have to leave a dead beat.** Run 4 answered

- [gate1] **Three consecutive 0-error / 0-warning audits across three genuinely

## Run 5 build — hackers / counter (2026-08-10, impeccable pass)

- [hackers_counter] **Ad-hoc numbers for a repeated relationship are the design
  defect; fix them as a token, not per instance.** Run 4 fixed the doubled-outline
  ring on the test cage at 12 design units and left the short's other FIVE ring
  positions at 3, 6, 6, 8 and 8 units — so the same crown move read as a thick
  border in four scenes and as a highlight in one. Same class in the kicker
  baselines (100 / 104 / 108 / 110) and in the two-bar chart grid (beat 2 and
  beat 4C are the same chart before/after and were expected to match by eye).
  Three tokens (`RING_GAP`, `KICKER_Y`, `ROW_A_Y/ROW_B_Y/ROW_H`) plus two
  derivations (`around(rect)`, `ring_radius(r)`) removed all of it. When you find
  yourself typing a fourth hand-picked offset for the same relationship, that IS
  the finding.
- [hackers_counter] **A highlight ring's corner radius must be
  `target_radius + gap`.** A fixed `radius=16` pinched against a radius-11
  segment, a radius-12 chip, a radius-16 gauge and a radius-18 cage — the ring's
  corners cut inside its own clearance and the pair stopped reading as
  concentric. `borderRadius` is tweenable as a px string in the same `tl.to`.
- [hackers_counter] **A MORPHING highlight is only safe across empty canvas.**
  Measured at t=31.2 on the first run-5 render: `hljump` morphing the ring from
  the guardrail gauge down to the MODEL/PROMPT chips put the ring's top edge
  *inside* the orange gauge (same colour → invisible) while its bottom edge cut
  through both white chips — a broken orange "U" for ~0.4s. Every hop in this
  short is between stacked or adjacent targets, so every hop had it. Replaced
  with `hlmove()`: `to opacity 0 (0.14s)` → `set` the new rect at t+0.15 →
  `to opacity 1 (0.26s)` at t+0.16. Cue timing is identical (fully visible at
  t+0.42, exactly where the 0.42s morph landed), it is seek-safe the same way the
  jump chain was, and no stroke is ever drawn over a thing it is not
  highlighting. Worth auditing in every lane that jumps a ring between adjacent
  objects.
- [hackers_counter] **Grouping in a segmented meter is the RATIO of between-group
  to within-group space, and that ratio also decides whether a highlight can be
  placed at all.** Run 4's beat-1 meter had 6 units between segments and 8 between
  the frontier trio and the open-source segment: no grouping, and a ring with
  honest clearance around either group would have collided with the other. 6
  inside / 30 between fixed the reading and created the room in one move.
- [hackers_counter] **Columns sharing an INVISIBLE baseline read as broken while a
  chart is half built.** The capability staircase grows 2 columns on "getting
  better" then 3 more 2.1s later on "cybersecurity"; with nothing drawn at the
  common bottom, that 2.1s window was two orange blocks floating in the left half.
  Drawing the baseline rule WITH the first column (never before it, so BUILD ORDER
  holds) turns it into a chart mid-build. Give the columns square feet
  (top-only border-radius) or they curve away from the rule they stand on.
- [hackers_counter] **A label centered inside a bar needs an explicit box height.**
  A bare label div's box is the font's natural leading, so a hand-picked `y + 20`
  put the label's optical center 8 design px above the bar's center and 4 above the
  logo plates' — three centers on one row. `height + line-height = bar height`
  centers it by construction, and the audit skips the pair via containment.
- [hackers_counter] **An element's landing spot must respect the NEXT scene's
  chrome band.** The sandbox escape landed at y=108, exactly where the following
  sub-scene's "THE GAP" kicker is born, so during the (deliberate) 0.3s overlap
  handoff the headline faded up from behind a model plate with its last letter
  eaten. Nothing flags this: the audit ignores transition frames, and gate 2's
  3fps grid can step over it. When one sub-scene exits UNDER the next one's
  chrome, check the outgoing scene's final positions against the incoming
  kicker's band.
- [hackers_counter] **Every deterministic check can be green while the design is
  wrong.** Gate 1 was 0 errors / 0 warnings on the FIRST build of this pass, the
  pre-render ink sweep was 0 near-empty in 2010 seeks, the post-render scan was
  0 in 2008 frames, and gate 3 passed — and reading 4 frames of that render still
  found the ring morphing through its own target. Budget one render for a frame
  read before treating a green chain as finished.
- [impeccable] Running the skill inside Miguel's system means using it on
  RELATIONSHIPS (spacing rhythm, alignment, grouping, shape consistency, motion
  restraint) and refusing its register-level advice where STANDARD.md already
  decided: it says "don't center everything" and "cards are the lazy answer",
  and this factory is centered compositions on a cream whiteboard. Palette,
  typography, the counter/meter vocabulary, the 01/02 step chips, the caption
  pill and the outro composition were not touched.

## Run 5 (impeccable) — hackers / kinetic (2026-08-10)

- [hackers_kinetic] **The impeccable pass found six real defects in a short that
  had already cleared all three gates twice.** Run 4's hackers_kinetic shipped
  0-error geometry, a full gate-2 read, QC pass and a 0/2008 dead-frame scan —
  and still carried: a solid ring around a solid rounded plate (nested boxes,
  ~9s), a fully-round pill ring wrapped around a square-capped bracket, kimi
  plated as a box inside a box, meter logos with 14 left / 4 top padding, an
  outro divider 16 units wider than the logo row under it, and a held cage
  composition sitting 109px right of frame centre. **None of these is
  machine-checkable**: geometry_audit exempts rings, containment-skips a tile
  inside a plate, and measures no aesthetic relation at all. The only detector
  is 20 full-resolution screenshots of the paused timeline read as a contact
  sheet, before and after every edit.
- [all] **Ring exemptions are a blind spot with teeth.** Because `isRing`
  elements are collision-exempt, a highlight ring can cross, kiss or double any
  annotation and every gate stays green. Two of this short's defects lived
  exactly there (the gutter bracket the new ring crossed, and the ring/plate
  nested-box). Rule of thumb worth carrying: **after moving any ring, look at a
  screenshot** — the audit will never tell you.
- [all] **Concentric-corner arithmetic is the honest FILL THE SHAPE answer, and
  it is one line.** An inner element inset by `p` inside a container of radius
  `r` wants radius `r - p`; a ring offset by `p` outside it wants `r + p`.
  Applied here: r14 track + 8 inset -> r6 tiles; r14 track + 12 pad -> r26 ring;
  r11 tiles + 12 pad -> r23 ring; r16 cage + 10 pad -> r26 ring. Every
  "different radius family" complaint Miguel has filed is this arithmetic
  missing.
- [all] **A logo whose artwork IS a plate must render at pad 0 with the
  artwork's own radius, and you can measure that radius instead of guessing.**
  `kimi.png` is 112px with its top row opaque only from x=30, i.e. a 27% corner
  radius. pad 0 + radius 0.27*s makes the artwork the plate exactly and the
  white plate underneath disappears. Same class as the Nous finding; the test is
  "does the artwork have its own background", not "is the artwork dark".
- [all] **Tinting a near-white toward the brand hue can silently blind the
  dead-frame scan.** The scan counts pixels whose max channel delta from the
  modal background exceeds 13. #FFFFFF on cream #F6F1EA is a delta of 21;
  #FFFDF9 is 15 (still ink); #FDFAF5 is 11 (invisible to the scan, and nearly
  invisible to the eye). If you tint plates to satisfy the no-pure-white rule,
  **compute the delta first** — under ~13 you have quietly made your own
  measurement lie about empty frames.
- [hackers_kinetic] **When a composition cannot be centred in both of its
  states, move the container, not the composition.** The cage (176 wide) plus
  its escapee (76 wide, 140 away) cannot be centred before AND after the
  breakout. Answer: hold the cage dead centre, then RECOIL it left 60 units
  with its -3deg tilt in one 0.7s tween as the model bursts right. One motivated
  event (Newton, essentially), then still — LAW 1 intact — and both states read
  composed (109px off-centre became 32px). Anything authored at the final
  position (the label, the concentric ring) must then be placed against the
  post-recoil box.
- [hackers_kinetic] **Dashed slots are the cure for "half a composition" frames,
  and the 1.5s wait guidance is about lone elements, not fields.** Two frames in
  this short were left-hugging builds: one tile against a centred rule (0.6s),
  and two tiles under a centred headline with the right half empty (3.8s). Five
  slots at the exact rect+radius of the tiles that fill them fixed both. The
  open-source pair waits 4.2s dashed — longer than the logged 1.5s ceiling — but
  it is part of an actively filling field, not chrome waiting on content that
  never starts, and QC passed first call.
- [gate1] **A duplicate-id collision surfaces as a geometry WARNING, not as an
  id error — read the ids in the finding.** Adding `b1-sl{k}` slots next to the
  existing `b1-sl{k}` labels produced exactly one finding: `collision b1-s0 ∩
  b1-sl1 = 14%` at 3.5s. That is the duplicate-id class (LEARNINGS' grokprice
  finding) arriving through a different door, and it is the only reason gate 1
  was not clean on the first try in three rounds.
- [all] **Cheap chart upgrade that satisfies three laws at once:** give every
  bar a full-height track. The skeleton exists before the data (BUILD ORDER
  without chrome-before-content), the tallest bar visibly completes its track
  (METERS COMPLETE), the geometry is containment-skipped (0 new findings), and
  five naked orange blocks become a chart. Size the widths to tile the content
  band exactly (5x72 + 4x28 = 472) so the row aligns to the same margins as
  every other beat.
- [factory] **Impeccable and STANDARD conflict in exactly two places on this
  design system, and both should be recorded rather than resolved:** impeccable
  bans overshoot easing (our POP is `back.out(2.2)`, the entrance signature of
  all 40 shorts) and bans pure white (our caption pill's text). Miguel's
  instruction is that STANDARD wins and he keeps his design system, so the
  correct output is a note in `impeccable_notes`, not a diff. Everything else
  impeccable asked for — grid, spacing rhythm, shape consistency, colour
  discipline, alignment, dead code — was free of conflict.
- [hackers_kinetic] Final numbers: geometry 3 rounds (0/0 -> 0 errors 1 warning
  -> 0/0), 259 ids with zero duplicates, 165 tween selectors all resolving,
  15/15 opacity probes non-zero, 0 near-empty windows in a 0.05s pre-render
  sweep AND 0 across all 2008 rendered frames, 0 mid-video caption dropouts,
  worst top-zone ink bottom 786.4px vs a caption pill topping at 805.2px, tweet
  3.63s, 80 distinct states from 201 samples, 11 frames read, 0 idle candidates,
  longest hold 2.6s, QC v3 pass on round 1 with zero visual and zero semantic
  errors. One render spent.

## Run 5 (impeccable) — grokbuild / icon (2026-08-10)

- [grokbuild_icon] **The factory has no vertical rhythm rule, and one line of arithmetic
  supplies it.** Run 4's generator hand-set every y, so this short's ten phases had
  optical centres scattered between design y178 and y235 and four of them were
  top-pinned with 40-50% of the canvas empty underneath (the law-9 debut, the CLI-agents
  row, the acquisition pair, GROK 4.5). Rule that fixed all of them at once:
  `otop(h) = (1.25*410 - 1.25*h)/2.25` — a block of visual height h sits so the air
  ABOVE it is 1.25x the air below, inside the 0..410 working canvas. More air above is
  correct because the caption pill hangs under the bottom edge. **It reproduces the
  phases that were already well composed** (chart 63.5 vs a hand-set 82, parity 126.7 vs
  126, ten-months 100.9 vs 100) which is the proof it is the latent rule, and it lifts
  the four that were not. Register every phase and hard-fail the build on drift: 13
  phases here, spread of optical centres 57 units -> 13.5 units. This generalises the
  one-off `groupmove` / centre-then-step fixes threed_diagram, fablevssol_counter,
  productivity_icon and meatwrapper_diagram each invented separately.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Terracotta at equal alpha is DARKER than a neutral, so the "hot"
  bar in a chart can be the darkest thing on screen.** The run-4 evolution chart drew
  its TOP TIER column at `rgba(221,114,89,0.15)` on `#101012` (relative luminance ~40)
  beside cold columns at `rgba(243,239,232,0.13-0.18)` (~56): the highlighted column
  read as a HOLE. Gate 1 sees a legal box, gate 3 passed it twice, and it is invisible
  in code because 0.15 "accent" looks like emphasis in the source. 0.42 puts it at ~66,
  brightest of the three. **Check emphasis by sampling pixel luminance on a 1:1 still,
  never by reading alpha values** — this applies to every tinted fill in the palette.
- [grokbuild_icon] **These generators have no TYPE SCALE.** The display register shipped
  at 40/42/44/50/54 with measured ink widths from 43% to 76% of the column, and the
  small register at 12/13/15/16/17 — ten sizes, no ratio, no roles. One display size
  (52) plus a deterministic fit-down for anything over 86% of the column, and two small
  sizes (13 tracked / 16 identifying), is simpler AND more consistent. Do the fit from
  MEASURED Poppins-800 advances (headless Chromium, fonts explicitly loaded, cached to
  `gen/_measure_<item>.json`): em widths here were GROK BUILD 5.8391, GROK 4.5 4.6091,
  10 MONTHS 5.5091, MIDDLE GROUND 8.1000, FOLLOW FOR 6.1931, DAILY AI 4.0841. Only
  MIDDLE GROUND needed the fit. **Watch the units trap**: a probe that returns
  `render_px / 100 / 1.875` is design-units-per-render-px, NOT em — multiply by S again
  or every string comes out 47% too narrow.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Gaps must be measured between CAP BANDS, not layout boxes.** Poppins
  800 caps run 0.26em to 0.98em below the layout-box top, so a "28px gap" authored on
  layout boxes is optically 28 + 0.26*fs — 41px under a 52px display line and 32px under
  a 16px label. Same nominal token, two different optical gaps. Placing text by
  `text_y(cap_top, fs) = cap_top - 0.26*fs` makes one spacing scale actually look like
  one spacing scale.
- [grokbuild_icon] **TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH, ratio edition.** Run 4 closed the ten-months
  beat with a mono line reading "shipped 10/10". Miguel says "just shipping features for
  over the last ten months" — the 10/10 asserts a monthly delivery cadence that exists
  nowhere. It is the same class productivity_icon/productivity_counter logged for source
  numbers, but it hides better because it looks like visual shorthand rather than data.
  Grep every numeral on screen against `transcript_tight.json`, **including ratios,
  scores and x/y pairs**. Replacement that claims nothing: an accent underline growing
  under the display line on the word that justifies it.
- [grokbuild_icon] **An accent rule under a display line should be the line's MEASURED
  ink width.** A round 200 under a 286-unit "10 MONTHS" reads as an arbitrary dash;
  286.5 reads as an underline. Free once the glyph measurement pass exists.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Two display lines need >= 1.30x font-size of pitch even when the
  audit is quiet.** Run 4's outro ran 50px lines at 58 pitch (1.16x) and audited 0/0,
  because text-vs-text pairs get a 0.20 area tolerance — but the Range/glyph box is
  ~1.34x fs, so the two lines genuinely overlap by 9 units. hackers_counter measured the
  same thing from the error side; it is worth applying BEFORE the audit complains.
- [impeccable/factory] **Running the impeccable skill inside this design system means
  refusing three of its laws, and the refusals are the deliverable.** Its motion law
  (ease-out exponentials, no bounce) would delete `back.out(2.2)`, the move Miguel called
  "chef's kiss"; its layout law (cards are the lazy answer, no identical grids) would
  delete the capability chip list and the plated logo rows; its colour law (OKLCH,
  tinted neutrals, never #fff) would repaint the cream/charcoal/terracotta palette and
  the white plates that exist precisely so black-artwork marks survive on both grounds.
  What the skill IS good for here is its polish doctrine — "align to the design system
  first, otherwise polish is decoration on drift" — which converts a list of nudges into
  system rules by forcing every deviation to be classified as a missing token, a one-off
  implementation, or a conceptual misalignment. All three were present in one generator.
