## Run 5 (impeccable) — deepresearch / checklist (2026-08-10)

- [deepresearch_checklist] **A 0.01s "hard swap" is NOT automatically frame-exact, and the
  arithmetic is worth stating once.** The factory's frame-exact swap recipe (grokprice_counter,
  slop_diagram, threed_diagram) says "give the switch-off and the switch-on ONE shared timestamp
  with 0.01s ramps, narrower than a 30fps frame interval, so no rendered frame can fall inside".
  That is only true if the window does not STRADDLE a frame boundary. Authored on the raw cue
  3.26, the ramp runs 3.26-3.27 and the rendered frame at 98/30 = 3.2667 lands at p=0.67 of both
  ramps: measured 0.70 opacity on the outgoing tweet card under a 0.96-opacity incoming row, i.e.
  exactly the double exposure the recipe exists to prevent. Fix is one helper:
  `swap_at(t) = ceil(t*FPS)/FPS + 0.011`, emitted with THREE decimals (the usual `{:.2f}`
  formatting cannot even represent it). Verified frame-by-frame: frames 98 and 269 carry only the
  outgoing element, 99 and 270 only the incoming.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **The checklist lane needs TWO row vocabularies, and conflating them is
  a TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH problem, not a style one.** Run 4 ticked "DEEP RESEARCH" and "THEN BUILD"
  in beat 1, where nothing is completed — he is describing an order of operations. A tick is a
  claim of completion. Splitting the language fixes it: an ORDINAL PLATE (`01` / `02`, same
  rounded square, same 40px size as a checkbox, 01 filled terracotta because it is the thesis)
  for a step you are about to take, and a CHECKBOX only where the tick lands on a word that
  justifies it (beat 2's enumeration, the outro's promise). Bonus: it removes the "two empty
  checkboxes holding the frame" reading that is cosmetically identical to the defect Miguel named.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **Publish a container's empty CONTENT SLOTS, not the container.** The
  ledger already knows "an empty container waiting for content is a defect above ~3.5s" and
  "dashed slots are the approved slot-then-fill language", but those are usually applied to the
  container itself. Here the employee card was a blank box for 5.7s. Drawing the six empty
  brief LINES inside it (low-alpha pills at the exact rect and radius of the lines that fill them,
  identical height and pitch in BOTH cards so the only difference is the count) makes the beat
  state its whole argument at its first frame and turns the fills into the events. Each line then
  writes in with a scaleX sweep — the "brief being written" reading — and identical rects hit the
  audit's >=0.96 containment skip, so it costs nothing at gate 1.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **A findings panel should arrive PRESENT-BUT-UNREAD, not empty.** Run 4
  popped five research rows into an empty panel one at a time, which (a) held an empty container
  for 1.9s and (b) claimed the findings arrived sequentially — but the agents had already produced
  them; he is READING. Authoring all five at 0.30 opacity from the panel's first frame and inking
  each one on the reading beat fixes the composition and the semantics in the same edit. Gate 1 is
  unaffected: rows inside the panel hit the containment skip.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **Measure the glyphs and you can keep exact centring AND gate-1
  coverage.** The run-4 outro centred its checklist with `display:inline-block` inside a
  full-width `text-align:center` div — exact centring, but the wrapper hid all nine children from
  `geometry_audit.py` (the same blindness class as `phase_open()`). Measuring the three Poppins 800
  labels in headless Chromium (cached to `gen/_measure_<item>.json`), taking
  `block_w = box + gap + max(label_w)` and placing every atom at `(576-block_w)/2` gives the same
  shared left edge and the same exact centre with every row a direct section child. Atom census
  went 4 -> 8 in the outro.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **A row's box and its label must share ONE tween start.** The
  productivity_checklist intra-row-stagger finding reproduces at 40ms: `popo(box, t)` +
  `popo(label, t+0.04)` renders a labelless checkbox — literally Miguel's named defect, one frame
  long. Caught on a pre-render contact sheet, invisible to all three gates.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **Deleting elements was the highest-value part of the impeccable pass.**
  Six went: the key-term underline (an ornament with no spoken referent, and one fewer `.rule` for
  the connector law), the four logo NAME labels (law 2 says the logo IS the identification), three
  invented badge chips ("x4" asserts a count of agents he never states — he says "multiple"), the
  employee card's verdict tick (it overloads the lane's tick vocabulary; the terracotta title and
  the 6-vs-2 lines already carry the verdict), a beat-2 meter label duplicating the row above it,

- [deepresearch_checklist] The sparse window this lane cannot design away, with numbers: beat 1

  debut before its first utterance (law 9) and the logos cannot precede the naming. Every filler
  is chrome — a labelless dashed row above "THEN BUILD" is the named defect. Third pass on this

- [gate2] Seventh-plus confirmation of the dedup blindness, this time on terracotta-on-dark:

- [factory] **Run 5's honest fork base is the run-4 generator, not run 3.** The run-4
  `grokbuild_diagram_gen.py` IS the run-3 fork with every v1.1 law and the whole backlog
  already applied and twice verified. Re-deriving those 20 fixes from `gen3/` would have
  spent the run's whole budget reproducing known work; forking the corrected descendant
  makes run 5's delta exactly what the run-5 contract asks for — the impeccable pass.
  State the base in the paperwork so the clerk can check it.
- [grokbuild_diagram] **A ring on a HOT node inside a tight stack is TWO defects at once,
  and the border-tween fix deletes both plus an atom.** The `x premium+ = free` leaf was
  authored hot (terracotta border) AND ringed 10 design px outside, in a stack whose row
  pitch is 54 with 46-tall rows = an 8-unit gutter. So the ring crossed into the row above
  *and* doubled the leaf's own border. Fix: the leaf arrives NEUTRAL like its siblings and
  its `borderColor` + inner label `color` + the icon `<g>`'s `attr:{stroke}` tween to
  terracotta on the word "free". GSAP's AttrPlugin is in core, so the SVG stroke tweens
  with the rest — verified on the render at 41.0s. Fifth lane to land on the same class
  (hackers_icon, threed_icon, slop_counter, hermes_diagram, here): treat "ring on a
  bordered node" as banned, not as a judgement call.
- [grokbuild_diagram] **Lowering a dashed slot's FILL to make its dash read pushes the
  frame under your own dead-frame threshold.** Strengthening the dash (0.26 on cream /
  0.42 on dark, up from the `hair` token) is right — the run-4 slots read as SOLID grey
  plates at phone size, i.e. chrome standing before content. But dropping the fill from
  `soft` (0.07) to 0.035 in the same edit took the beat-0 skeleton from 24.5% ink to
  2.5%, and the hero->slot handoff to 0.69%: an alpha under ~0.06 on cream moves a pixel
  by <13 levels, which is exactly the ink metric's threshold. **Change the dash token,
  never the plate's mass.**
- [grokbuild_diagram] **Two mono labels at nearly the same y, one outgoing and one
  incoming, double-expose during a 0.18s handoff.** The card's `BENCHMARK` (design y 106)
  faded up at `PHOTO_IN+0.10` while the acquisition's `EX XAI` (design y 104) was still
  ~50% opaque — two different words on one line for ~4 frames. Neither gate can see it
  (it is a transition frame, and both atoms are legal). Rule: let the incoming card's
  BODY carry the handoff and land its LABEL after the outgoing block is fully dead. The
  general form: at any cut, diff the outgoing and incoming atom y-bands for text pairs.

  boxes on the source (`arrow x265-362 y15-183`, `dot x250-281 y200-230`, `label

  WHITE gutter along its top edge. The new 504x222 box lets the card be sized straight

  upscale line — with the label the same size on screen and no dead field.
- [grokbuild_diagram] **The evidence card's highlight should be its own border, because
  the source already ships a pointer.** The Artificial Analysis crop contains a
  hand-drawn purple arrow aimed at the entry; a terracotta ring on top of it is

  of that arrowhead. `tl.to("#card",{borderColor:"rgb(221,114,89)"})` is one discrete

- [grokbuild_diagram] **Four build-time guards, ~50 lines, all passed first try, and they

## Run 5 (impeccable) — deepresearch / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [deepresearch_diagram] **A rail must be a BOX, not a `.rule`.** Every one of the 7
  floating warnings this lane inherited from run 4 came from two rails drawn with
  `line_el`: a `.rule` is end-checked itself AND gives every stem that meets it a
  floating end, because a rule is not in the audit's box set. Re-emitting each rail as
  `class="abs node bus"` with an inline background (thin_bar keeps it collision-exempt,
  the `bus` suffix keeps it out of the same-size equality group, `scaleX` still draws
  it) took the short to **0 errors / 0 warnings with zero `data-bleed` and zero new
  `data-overlap-ok`**. This is hermes_diagram's collector-bar trick generalised: use it
  for any rail, including the outro's.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **Opacity-gate the connector WRAPPER and add an
  untweened-section-child check, and the whole phantom-connector class closes itself.**
  Authoring every `arrow()` / `line_el()` / `strike_el()` wrapper at `opacity:0` and
  switching it on inside the draw helper means a collapsed rotated shaft never reaches
  the audit (it drops under the 0.15 opacity floor). The cheap enforcement is a
  build-time check that every `<div id=... class="abs">` inside a `.tz` section is the
  target of some tween — it fails loudly on exactly the wrappers you forgot.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **Many-to-one convergence must be a COLLECTOR, never N
  diagonals meeting at a point.** Run 4's four convergence lines started 24 units below
  their agents (in mid-air, under a detached meter) and met at one point on the panel's
  top edge: the meeting point reads as a knot, and no diagonal can ever anchor because
  the audit takes a rule's AABB mid-left/mid-right as its ends. Stems off each node's
  bottom edge -> one horizontal rail -> one drop with a head is orthogonal, anchors at
  both ends, and (bonus) it is the same harness the producer row already used, so the
  short gains one connector vocabulary instead of two.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **A wrapper-free group move creates a defect no gate can see:
  a moving atom is never judged.** While the four centred logo tiles stepped out to the
  full row, the incoming fifth tile landed where a moving tile still was — plates
  overlapping for ~0.3s, invisible to gate 1 (it only reports atoms static across two
  consecutive samples) and to gate 3. Schedule incoming siblings AFTER the move
  completes, and re-read a contact sheet across the move window.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **Precondition for any x-step: no atom in the group may have an
  x-based entrance.** Beat 4's rows had to move from `slidex` to `rise` before the panel
  could step left; otherwise the group tween clobbers the entrance. (Same rule on y.)
- [all] **The "1485/1485 non-empty frames" class of claim is usually measured on the
  wrong crop.** The run-4 paperwork for this item asserted zero blank frames; a 0.04s
  DOM ink sweep over the TOP-MOST active `.tz` found **four zero-ink windows** in the
  same composition (0.28s at 3.08 where the tweet's `power3.out` exit finished before
  the task's entrance started, plus the 25.48 / 34.26 / 45.60 cuts). The inherited scan
  had cropped 1080x862, which includes the caption pill's top half — terracotta on every
  frame. Crop 1080x790. The DOM sweep is the cheaper detector because it runs before the
  render and names the section.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **An impeccable-style composition read finds a different class
  of defect than any gate, and it is worth doing on an already-passing short.** Reading
  32 pre-render stills as contact sheets before touching the generator surfaced: the
  same hero node rendered in two typefaces across a cut (Poppins in beat 1, mono in beat
  2), two different bar systems for the two "briefs" (16px vs 13px, so the thinner brief
  read heavier), terracotta doing five jobs at once so the law-5 highlight had nothing
  left to signal with, a 7.9s left-anchored beat, and a 3.6s top-pinned beat. None of
  those is machine-checkable; all of them are obvious side by side.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **Accent discipline is a law-5 enabler, not a taste call.** The
  beat-2 panel was filled with solid terracotta content bars while the connectors,
  meters and border were also terracotta; the highlight event (border -> terracotta on
  "your context") was therefore invisible as an event. Neutral ink for CONTENT, accent
  for flow/progress/attention only, and the same highlight now reads instantly.
- [gate3] **Beat-aggregation noise, third distinct flavour** (after tweet-duration and

## Run 5 build — fablevssol / icon (2026-08-10, impeccable pass)

- [factory] **Run 5 was forked from the run-4 GENERATOR, not from run 3, and the reason is
  worth stating for every run-5 worker.** The brief's step 1 names `shorts_run3/gen3/
  <video>_gen.py`, but run 5's contract is "run 4 PLUS impeccable as a design reviewer" —
  so the only variable that should differ between the two runs is the design pass.
  Re-deriving the run-3 chassis would have re-imported every defect class run 4 spent two
  passes retiring (zone-sized wrappers hiding atoms from gate 1, `power3.out` exits, blank
  handoffs, dark logo plates, `kimi.png`). Declare the lineage in the paperwork.
- [fablevssol_icon] **The 3-word trigram guard is necessary and NOT sufficient, and the
  sufficient version is ~40 lines.** Read every zone element's OWN first tween time out of
  the emitted tween strings (`tl.fromTo("#id",...,T);`), find the caption clip live at
  `T+0.25`, and fail the build on a 2-word CONSECUTIVE run or 3+ shared non-stopword
  tokens. Four strings in a fully gate-passing run-4 build were verbatim double captions
  the trigram scan could not see: `PERSONAL`/`PREFERENCE` stacked over "comes down to
  personal preference", `ALL EXCELLENT` over "absolutely excellent", a chip reading
  "preference" over "which one do I prefer", and a chip reading "faster" over "allows you
  to work faster". Whitelist only what a law forces on screen (model names, feature names
  like "fast mode"), and let the mandated law-9 key-term debut through — it necessarily
  shares its own word with its own pill.
- [fablevssol_icon] **A resting highlight is a claim.** A ring that jumps across a row is
  choreography, but whichever tile it stops on becomes the subject of everything the beat
  says afterwards. My beat-7 scramble ended on the Sol tile and then held 3.3s over four
  crossed-out models — i.e. "Sol is the one that fails". Retire a scramble ring when the
  scramble ends and let the marks that follow carry the claim. Same family as the
  already-logged "ring walks back onto Claude at *for yourself*" (law 11), but the trigger
  is the ring's REST position, not its path.
- [fablevssol_icon] **Size a strike-through with `canvas.measureText` using the element's
  own font AND `letterSpacing`, never a per-character guess.** "WHO WINS?" at fs 62
  measures **365.0 design px** of ink (advance 367.1) against the run-4 estimate of 324 —
  a 20px shortfall at each end that is obvious in a gate-2 frame and invisible in code.
  Same pass gives the optical middle for free: baseline-in-box minus half the cap ascent
  puts Poppins 800 caps' optical centre at **0.526 * fs** below the layout-box top.
- [fablevssol_icon] **The wrapper-free ride generalises from "fix a sparse beat" to "lay
  out the whole short".** Five of seven beats here opened with their entire cast in the
  upper third while 60-75% of the canvas sat empty — 11.7s of an 83s short, invisible to
  every gate (nothing is blank, nothing collides). Author each beat's cast at its FINAL
  rect and offset it DOWN at build time with ONE comma-selector
  `tl.fromTo(group,{y:+dy},{y:0},cue)`: the beat opens on the zone's optical centre and
  steps into the header layout as one discrete event. Costs one tween per beat, invents no
  content, needs no re-cut, and every atom stays a direct section child. Two constraints:
  (a) no member may have a y-based ENTRANCE, and (b) any later y-tween on a member — a
  highlight ring's own jumps — must carry the SAME offset in its own tween or it snaps back
  to y:0 mid-move.
- [fablevssol_icon] **A compile-time ink budget retires SEAM IS SACRED as a discovery.**
  Every element helper registers `top + 1.30*font_size` (or `y + h` for boxes) and the
  build `raise SystemExit`s above design y 400 (=750px). Run 4 shipped this same lane with
  15.4px of clearance off the caption pill's painted top (805.2px) and a 0-warning audit;
  with the budget the shipped worst case is 736.5px = **68.7px clear**, and it is a build
  error rather than something to find in a frame.
- [all] **The dead-frame scan threshold has to follow the GROUND, not the ledger default.**
  On this cream (#F6F1EA) a `#FFFFFF` logo plate is only ~13 levels away, so the widely
  copied ">28 difference" test scores a full four-plate composition as empty. Working
  recipe: `crop=1080:790` (above the pill), 108x79 **RGB**, modal colour as background,
  count pixels whose **max channel delta > 13**, flag under 1%. It returned 0/2496 dead
  frames here with a minimum of 3.012%, and every low reading was a real composition when
  extracted. Pair it with the DOM ink-AREA sweep over the **topmost** active `.tz` only.
- [fablevssol_icon] **Deleting a highlight can be the law-5 fix twice over.** The opening
  ring stepping claim -> score on the @composio card has no spoken referent in its window

  the card as ONE still, complete composition for its whole 3.17s — which `frame_review`

  the card just BE the news.
- [fablevssol_icon] **The impeccable skill's useful contribution here was composition and
  hierarchy, never palette or type family** — and its three real conflicts with STANDARD.md

  law-4 pass together; they find the same objects from opposite directions.

## Run 5 (impeccable) — grokprice / kinetic (2026-08-10)

- [factory] **Run 5's brief says "identical contract PLUS impeccable"; the honest
  base is therefore the RUN-4 generator, not run 3.** `shorts_run4/gen/
  grokprice_kinetic_gen.py` is itself the run-3 fork with every v1.1 fix and two
  dead-frame passes already in it. Re-forking run 3 would have re-derived ~40
  logged learnings by hand and almost certainly shipped worse. Lineage is stated
  in the paperwork and proven by re-running the generator and diffing
  `index.html` (byte-identical, md5 be422ba372caf18ad49bae62e9b672c3).
- [grokprice_kinetic] **The residual defect class after three runs of law-fixing
  is COMPOSITION, and it is invisible to all three gates: elements authored at
  their FINAL position while the composition is still half-built.** Four
  instances on one short, none of which any gate can report (nothing is blank,
  nothing collides, nothing echoes): a lone `$0.50` parked 127/138 design units
  left of centre because `x0` was computed for the finished row (1.2s in beat 1,
  **3.8s in beat 2** — under a centred lockup and above a centred table, i.e.
  three axes on one screen); a one-row list pinned at design y112 with 65% of the
  zone empty; a two-row list pinned there for **4.4s**; and a struck price
  landing in the top third right after a tweet card vacated the zone's centre.
  Standing check worth adding to every build: for each beat, list the moments
  where the cast is INCOMPLETE and ask where that partial cast is optically
  centred. Gate 1 measures the final frame; nobody measures the frames on the way
  there.
- [grokprice_kinetic] **Two fixes cover the whole class and both are wrapper-free
  and prime-safe.** (a) CENTRE-THEN-STEP for a half-built row: author it centred
  and step onto the row axis on a real cue — here the strike, which is also the
  gesture that opens the gap the second price lands in. (b) AUTHOR-LOW-AND-RIDE
  for a growing list: author the opening cast N units lower (each stage optically
  centred) and ride it home in ONE `tl.fromTo` on a comma-joined selector, timed
  to complete 0.06-0.08s BEFORE the next item lands, so the two never share a
  slot and no audit sample sees both mid-flight. Costs one tween each, invents
  nothing, and every atom stays a direct section child.
- [all] **`gmove`-style group tweens must emit ONLY the axes they move.** A
  helper that always writes `{x:PX, y:PY} -> {x:0, y:0}` makes two moves on one
  target mutually destructive: the later tween's `immediateRender` bakes `y:0`
  and silently cancels the earlier lift. Emitting just the requested axis let a
  price carry a step in x AND a dock in y as two independent tweens (and, better,
  let them be merged into one diagonal settle).
- [grokprice_kinetic] **The measured Poppins cap constant belongs in the
  generator, not only in LEARNINGS.** `slop_kinetic` measured Poppins 800's caps
  at 0.26em-0.98em (optical middle 0.62*fs) and every generator since has still
  centred icons and lockup wordmarks on the CSS line box — 3-4 design units (6-8
  render px) high, in every lane, on every row. One constant (`CAP_MID = 0.62`)
  and `icon_top = 0.62*fs - size/2`, `label_top = plate/2 - 0.62*fs` fixes the
  whole factory. Nothing in the gate chain can see it; it is visible instantly
  once you look for it.
- [grokprice_kinetic] **"Remove the evidence when the point is made" is a
  reflex that manufactures empty zones.** Run 4 lifted the pricing table out at
  14.66 and left the lower 55% of a dark beat empty until the cut at 16.82. There
  was no law requiring the exit. Letting the receipt RECEDE (opacity 0.45) while
  its highlight retires and the takeaway chip ticks forward states the same
  "here's what it means" beat, keeps the composition complete to the cut, and
  costs one `fadeto` instead of two `liftout`s. Corollary: the factory needs a
  `fadeto()` at all — `fade()` always starts from 0, so it can never dim or
  retire anything, which is probably why elements get deleted instead.
- [grokprice_kinetic] **A dashed slot works for a RASTER card too, and it makes
  the swap free.** Publishing the receipt's exact rect + exact radius at the
  beat's frame-0-safe opening filled 1.86s of empty dark zone, and because the
  slot and the card have IDENTICAL rects the crossfade hits the audit's >=0.96
  containment skip at every sample. Do NOT give the card a `rise`/`scale`
  entrance in that pattern: a 28-unit lift makes the pair 0.845 overlapping and
  turns a free crossfade into a collision candidate.
- [grokprice_kinetic] **A tally/counter must be anchored to what it counts.** Run
  4 pinned all five ghost numerals to a fixed y=168 whatever the list was doing.
  Authoring numeral k on the optical centre of the k-row list gives a clean
  28-unit progression, reads as that list's own number at every stage, needs zero
  extra tweens (each numeral just has its own `top`), and — the part that
  mattered — lets the numeral ride with the group if you also make its exit
  opacity-only. A `y` in the exit vars is what stops a swapped element from ever
  joining a group move.
- [gate2] **Seventh independent confirmation that a `[still Ns]` marker is an
  instruction to probe, not a finding.** The single 5.0s marker here (33.7->38.7)
  contains two `yoyo` scale ticks at 35.52/35.66; extracting 35.40 / 35.62 /
  35.80 / 36.60 with ffmpeg shows IMAGE GEN and VIDEO ANALYSIS visibly enlarged
  in the middle two. A tick that returns to rest is the single hardest event for
  the 16x16 dedup: it is small, it is brief, and it ends where it started.
- [gate3] **A semantic minor_note can be refuted by the short's own asset.**
  "Speaker mentions SpaceX AI instead of xAI" reappeared here (grokprice_icon
  logged it in run 4). Our card already prints what he says, and the tweet
  rendered at t=0 in this very video reads "As Elon promised, SpaceXAI has cut
  cached-input pricing" — so the judge is disputing the world, not our visual.
  When a note's subject is the SPEAKER, check the on-screen sources before
  assuming a TRANSCRIPT-IS-TRUTH violation on screen; grokprice_icon's rule
  (a note correcting Miguel = a card contradicting him) has this exception.
- [grokprice_kinetic] Clean run for the record: geometry 5 rounds, all 0 errors /
  0 warnings (atom census 56 real ids across 5 sections — 10/12/11/19/4, zero
  wrappers, zero nulls); 118 DOM ids with 0 duplicates and 57 tween selectors all
  resolving; deepest zone ink 738.7px against a live caption-pill top of 805.2px
  (66.5px clear); 0 near-empty frames of 1554 (min ink 2.297%, median 14.31%) and
  0 windows under 1% across 1035 pre-render samples; caption band blank only in
  0.00-0.17s before the first spoken word; tweet on screen 3.27s; 47 distinct
  states from 155 samples, 0 idle candidates, 16 frames read; QC v3 pass on the

## Run 5 (impeccable) — fablevssol / counter (2026-08-10)

- [fablevssol_counter] **A pure TRANSLATE cannot re-lay a composition, and that is the
  hidden limit of the factory's "author it centred and ride it up" recipe.** Beat 7's
  phase 1 owns the zone ALONE for 8.3s and then has to SHARE it with the switching half,
  so run 4 authored it at its compact two-column positions and translated it down — for
  those 8.3s a ~110-design-px strip floated in the middle of an empty canvas (no gate
  reports it: nothing is blank, nothing collides). The recipe only works for a beat that
  keeps its shape. Fix: give each atom **its own vector**, plus its own `scale` for the
  boxes that must resize (odometer 1.45x, meter 1.40x), all on ONE shared timestamp —
  `tl.set(sel,{x,y,scale},0)` + `fromTo(..., immediateRender:false)` per element. Still
  no DOM wrapper, so every atom stays a direct section child gate 1 can measure, and a
  0.50s move placed off the audit's 0.5s sample grid is never static enough to be flagged.
  Alone it is a centred column (kicker / hero counter / unit / labelled bar / payoff
  chip, design y 84-376); on "Whereas" it re-lays itself into the top strip.
- [fablevssol_counter] **Meter TICK marks must follow the GROUND, not the fill.**
  `meter_el` hardcoded `rgba(255,255,255,0.55)` ticks, which is right on the dark canvas
  and wrong on cream: white-on-light reads as GAPS in the bar, so a 100%-filled ladder
  looks segmented and pinched — exactly the FILL THE SHAPE complaint Miguel made about
  segmented meters. Use `rgba(17,17,17,0.30)` on cream / `rgba(255,255,255,0.55)` on dark.
- [fablevssol_counter] **An EMPTY meter track is DATA whenever the bar's claim is that it
  returned to zero.** The beat-7 "BACK TO ZERO" reset bar had nothing visible to sit on at
  `rgba(17,17,17,0.10)`. 0.16 is the working floor on this cream (hackers_counter measured
  0.07 as invisible; 0.10 is still under the eye's floor at phone size). Same token also
  makes every "scoreboard at zero" beat opening legible instead of near-blank.
- [fablevssol_counter] **Dimming an accent line so the next one wins is a symptom of a
  flat type scale.** Three stacked display lines at 44-46px needed TIED washed to 0.42 for
  the conclusion to read — and terracotta at 0.42 on cream is a pastel that reads as a
  render fault (the documented ~0.40 floor). Giving the conclusion the size step instead
  (46 -> 56, ratio 1.22) removed the dim entirely and satisfies the >=1.25 hierarchy rule.
- [fablevssol_counter] **A struck-out key term keeps the largest type on screen, so its
  replacement must carry the ACCENT.** Run 4's beat-1 payoff was a neutral grey 15px chip
  under a dimmed 62px `WHO WINS?` — the dead idea outranked the live one in both size and
  colour and the frame had no focal point at all. One token (chip kind neutral ->
  terracotta) fixes it.
- [fablevssol_counter] **The mate in a "both" pair must LEAVE when the sentence turns to
  one model — parking it dimmed is worse than removing it.** Run 4 held the Sol mark at
  0.24 in the top-right corner for all of beat 3 while the subject was Claude, which (a)
  keeps a dead element holding the composition asymmetric and (b) leaves the name label
  "CLAUDE FABLE 5" centred BETWEEN two marks, where it appears to label both. Retiring it
  lets the subject take the zone axis with its name underneath.
- [fablevssol_counter] **Two marks read as ONE claim only at a tight gap.** At 124 design
  px apart with nothing between them the "I use both" pair reads as two separate things;
  at 56 it reads as a couple. Beat 1 gets away with 104 only because the serif "vs" sits
  in the gap.
- [fablevssol_counter] **TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH also bans RHETORICAL invented numbers.** The
  run-4 sign-off rolled an odometer 0 -> 60 -> 100 under "PERCENT WORTH FOLLOWING". It is
  a joke, but in the Counter lane it wears the clothes of data, and it is also impeccable's
  banned hero-metric template. "7 / DAYS A WEEK" on a seven-segment week bar that completes
  is a direct restatement of "AI news and AI tutorials each and every single day" and
  satisfies METERS COMPLETE in the same move.
- [fablevssol_counter] **The generator's own id self-check is blind to the comma-joined
  multi-selector the whole factory now uses.** `re.findall(r'"#([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)"')`
  requires the closing quote immediately after the id, so `tl.to("#a,#b,#c",...)` matched
  NOTHING and those tweens were never validated (slop_kinetic logged the mirror-image bug —
  a false positive — but the silent-skip half is worse). Match `"(#[A-Za-z0-9_,#\-]+)"` and
  split on commas: 130 selectors validated here against 106 before.
- [fablevssol_counter] **LAW 5, confirmed across two lanes of the same video: the
  claim -> score ring on the @composio card has no spoken referent.** While the card is up
  (0-3.1s) Miguel says "the first question that comes into your mind when you hear" —
  nothing names either region. The kinetic lane was failed by Gemini for exactly this
  (`highlight_match at 0.5s`) while the counter lane passed the same choreography twice
  with zero notes, i.e. the judge is a coin flip on it and the law is not. Deleting both
  rings (not retiming — there is no word to sync to) leaves the card holding still 2.7s,
  which `frame_review` scores as confirmed stillness. threed_icon's rule holds again: a
  defect logged by a SIBLING LANE of the same video is almost certainly in yours.

## Run 5 build — grokprice / icon (2026-08-10, impeccable pass)

- [grokprice_icon] **The impeccable pass's highest-value move on this chassis was a
  GRID, not a polish detail.** Run 4 carried four competing measures in one 52s short
  (154 / 150 / 152 / 96-wide tiles, 480 and 504-wide cards, 22 / 19 / 13 / 20-unit
  gutters). Collapsing them to ONE content column — 480 units, margins 48/48, three
  148-unit columns with 18-unit gutters, `PLATE = (480 - 4*18)/5 = 81.6` for the
  5-logo row — made every beat land on the same edges, and it is cheaper than it
  sounds: three constants (`COL_W`, `GUT`, `TILE_W`) plus a `COL_X` tuple. The
  geometry audit cannot see this class at all (`.tile` is not in its `ltile|node|
  shot|chip` box set, so the same-size equality group never fires on this chassis),
  which is exactly why it survived two runs.
- [grokprice_icon] **A `stack(heights, gaps)` helper that optically centres a beat's
  tiers in the 0..410 working canvas is worth more than any per-element nudge.** Run
  4's tops were hand-picked: beat 2 ran design y 40..401 (bottom margin 9, top 40)
  and beat 1 left 22 units between the rival row and the ring but 12 between the ring
  and the −40% numeral. Twelve lines of helper replaced every magic number and made
  "even spacing between lines" (law 7) a property of the generator instead of a
  review finding.
- [grokprice_icon] **Balance a beat for its LONGEST-HELD phase, not its fullest.**
  Beat 2's full composition is lockup + table + chip, but the chip only exists for
  the last 1.8s of a 7.3s beat. Centring the three-tier stack put the 5.6s
  lockup+table phase 34 units high; centring the PAIR and letting the chip take the
  reserved space below is the correct trade. Generalises to any beat whose payoff
  arrives late.
- [grokprice_icon] **Deduplication is a law-8 move, not a taste move.** Run 4 showed
  the same three prices twice simultaneously — three coded price cells AND the source
  pricing table — which is what forced the crowding in the first place. Deleting the
  cells left the real table as the evidence, the band highlight as the crown move and
  one `−40%` chip carrying the only number he says. It also retired a 1.0s flash chip
  ("−40% ON CACHED INPUT") that sat one second before the cut directly above a pill
  reading "cached inputs." — a near-double-caption the 3-word trigram guard cannot see.
- [grokprice_icon] **Placeholder hierarchy: a dashed slot on a DARK canvas must be a
  RECESS, never a lighter panel.** My first attempt gave the dark slots a light fill
  (`rgba(255,255,255,0.13)`) so the pixel dead-frame scan would register them; that
  made an EMPTY slot (rgb 47,47,49) lighter than a FILLED `.tile.d` (#1B1B21 = 27,27,33)
  and inverted the hierarchy — the placeholder read as more present than the content.
  `rgba(0,0,0,0.30)` plus a 0.50-alpha dash is the fix: the gap reads as a hole, the
  tile as a raised panel. On CREAM the opposite already holds (white tile above,
  5.5%-ink slot below the ground), so the rule is: the slot must sit on the far side
  of the canvas from its tile.
- [grokprice_icon] **"A box with a label is content waiting; a box without one is
  chrome" decides the slot-then-fill question for CARDS too.** I first opened beat 2
  on an unlabelled 480x185 silhouette waiting 0.64s for the pricing table. Even at
  0.64s it is chrome. Letting the table own the cut with a scale-only `settle`
  (already opaque, so frame-0 safe) gives the section's first frame 38.6% ink and
  costs nothing — the "slot" language is for a shape whose CONTENT is enumerable
  (three tiles arriving on three spoken words), not for a single hero asset.
- [grokprice_icon] **The top-pinned beat opening has a wrapper-free fix that is now
  three lanes deep, and this is the cheapest version of it.** Beat 3's lockup + tile
  row hold the screen 6.2s before the `$0.30` payoff can exist; in their final
  position they leave the bottom 42% of the canvas empty. Authoring them on the
  TWO-TIER optical centre and riding them up `lift = (WORK_BOT - two_tier_h)/2 -
  y_lock` = 55.5 units in one `tl.fromTo("#a,#b,...",{y:PX},{y:0})` 0.36s before the
  slam costs ONE tween and no re-cut. Include the dashed slots in the mover list even
  though they are already faded — they are authored at the same y and the group must
  agree; a mover at opacity 0 is invisible to gate 1 anyway.
- [grokprice_icon] **Colour discipline is a factual check, not a style one.** Run 4
  gave the rivals' "prices rising" badges and Grok's "price dropped" badge the SAME
  terracotta. One accent carrying two opposite meanings on one screen is a law-11
  problem wearing a design hat. `.badge.n { background: INK }` for the rivals keeps

- [grokprice_icon] **One emphasis per claim.** Beat 1 had the rivals dimming to 0.30,

## Run 5 build — deepresearch / icon (2026-08-10, impeccable pass)

- [deepresearch_icon] **A whole `floating`-warning class is a DESIGN choice, not an audit
  limitation.** Run 4 shipped this lane at 0 errors / **7 warnings**, all diagonals (4
  convergence lines into the context card, 3 fan arrows into the outputs), with the standing
  advice "a diagonal can never anchor — ship it". Re-authoring both fans as ORTHOGONAL
  harnesses (stem -> a `class="abs node bus"` bar -> drops; taps -> bus -> stem) took the
  same content to **0 errors / 0 warnings on the first build and every build after**, with
  zero `data-overlap-ok` / `data-bleed` anywhere in the short. The bus is a real box, so both
  ends of every tap anchor; `thin_bar()` keeps it out of the collision pass; it grows on its
  own axis so it measures nothing until drawn. Diagonal connectors are worth designing out,
  not exempting.
- [deepresearch_icon] **A connector that leaves a multi-row panel at ONE row's height is a
  LAW-11 claim and no gate checks it.** Three horizontal output arrows landed within 3-13
  design px of three finding row centres — one of them a row he strikes out — so the picture
  asserted "this finding produced that output", which he never says. Worse, the stem sat on
  the panel's vertical centre, which was also the middle output's centre, so stem + middle
  arrow rendered as ONE straight line and privileged that output. Fix: route many-to-many
  through a shared bus, and put the feed stem on a y that is neither a row centre nor an
  output centre (a gap midpoint). Gate 1 is 0/0 either way; only reading the frame as a
  sentence finds it.
- [deepresearch_icon] **The frame-exact hard swap is confirmed through the real renderer, and
  the timestamp must fall BETWEEN two frame times.** `hard_off(card, 3.07)` + `hard_on(flow,
  3.07)` with 0.01s ramps: frame 92 is at 3.0667 and frame 93 at 3.1000, so no rendered frame
  lands inside the window. Measured white fraction of a band only the card occupies: 0.989 at
  3.033 -> 0.000 at 3.100, no ghost frame, no blank frame, and gate 1's 0.5s grid never sees
  both atoms. Note the generator formats tween times `{:.2f}`, so pick the two-decimal value
  that sits in a frame gap (3.07 works, 3.06 does not — 3.0667 falls inside it).
- [deepresearch_icon] **"Both cards at the cut" is a hidden dead-frame class that every ink
  metric passes.** Publishing a comparison PAIR up front left the right-hand card EMPTY for
  **5.0s** (26.2->31.2) while the narration was still describing the left one — no blank
  frame, no collision, so gate 1, the ink sweeps and Gemini all cleared it in run 4. The fix
  is to follow the sentence: ONE card centred, gaining its brief and its title, stepping
  aside on the clause that introduces the second, which lands in the room it made. Balanced
  at every instant, zero empty containers, and wrapper-free via a comma-joined selector.
- [deepresearch_icon] **The "empty container" test has a cheap upgrade: put ONE structural
  word in it.** The beat-1 dashed slot waits 6.2s for the key term to dock into it — far past
  every documented ceiling — and read as chrome. Labelling it `FIRST` (one word, absent from
  the transcript, purely positional) turns it into content waiting and states the claim the
  beat is making. A label that is not in the transcript costs nothing against law 4.
- [deepresearch_icon] **A beat should open on its own subject.** Beat 3 opens on the words
  "an AI agent", so the agent mark now enters at 1.5x on the card's optical centre and rides
  up into its header slot as the brief arrives. Run 4 opened the same beat on a 240x232 card
  holding a 52px mark against 70% empty white. Same atoms, one extra tween, and the opening
  frame becomes a composition instead of a container.
- [impeccable] **On this chassis the highest-yield impeccable findings are all token-level and
  invisible to every gate**: (a) a FLAT TYPE SCALE — run 4 ran five near-identical small sizes
  (16/14/13/12/11) so every label read like every other label; collapsed to 52/30/15/12, each
  step >= 1.25x; (b) DUPLICATED TOKENS — `.node` was r13/border .20 and `.card` r16/border .16
  and beat 4 puts both in one frame, i.e. two corner languages side by side; (c) ACCENT PER
  GROUND — TERRA and TERRA_L were mixed on both canvases, costing contrast in both directions.
  One accent per ground (TERRA on light, TERRA_L on dark), one radius, one border alpha.
- [impeccable] **Two conflicts worth recording because they will recur.** (1) impeccable bans

  about WHICH frame something is on must come from a frame-index select, never from a seek.

  a white panel on cream** (they differ by ~10-16 levels), so a "min ink %" dead-frame
  scan in this palette reports painted frames as blank. This short's two lowest frames
  at delta>18 (0.89% at t=34.27, 1.39% at t=3.07) are a fully painted review panel and
  a fully painted YOUR TASK under a fading tweet — both confirmed at full resolution.
  Use delta>10 (min ink here: 4.26% at t=4.23-4.40, over all 1485 frames) or pull every
  low frame at full res before calling anything a dead frame. This supersedes the
  earlier "crop above the pill at 790" learning: the crop was only half the problem.
- [deepresearch_diagram] **Gate 2's 16x16 dedup drops low-contrast state changes, so the
  manifest is NOT a complete state list on cream.** Neither the short's ONLY law-5
  highlight (the context panel's border going terracotta at 24.80, cut at 25.48) nor the
  last output node landing at 44.46 got a kept frame — 45 states from 149 samples and the
  crown move is in none of them. Verify the highlight and each beat's final node with
  targeted pre-render stills off the paused timeline; the manifest alone cannot clear

  panel, still at 45.20 shows ANYTHING plus its arrow complete 0.64s before the cut.)

  deepest inked row.** At delta>10 the deepest row is 805px at t=0.27 — the caption
  pill's own antialiased top edge popping in, not content. The reliable pair is the
  generator's build-time design-space seam budget (deepest content ink design y=408 =
  765px) against the pill's painted top measured on a still (row 806 on every sampled
  frame) = 41px clear.
- [factory] **A verification pass on an item that already passes all three gates should
  re-run only the free gates and re-measure the paperwork's own numbers.** Here every law
  verdict survived (geometry round 5 = 0/0 on the unchanged HTML, 24 frames + 7 stills =
  0 violations) but TWO hand-rolled measurement claims did not: the dead-frame min ink
  and the tweet duration (2.97s -> 3.00s at a 0.30 white-fraction threshold). Gate
  verdicts are the durable part of paperwork; hand-rolled measurement prose is the
  fragile part, and it is where an adversarial clerk will find you.

  coin-flip style change.** Re-running the on-disk generator and diffing the md5 of

## Run 5 second pass — hermes / icon (2026-08-10, dead-frame + outro build order)

Re-dispatched onto an item that already had 0-error geometry, a passing Gemini
verdict and complete paperwork. Re-verifying it end to end found a real defect
that had survived three runs and six gate passes.

- [hermes_icon] **THE DEAD FRAME WAS REAL AND THREE RUNS SHIPPED IT.** The run-3
  gate pass filed "hermes t=50.7, top zone fully EMPTY, worth a hold-over" as a
  no-law-forbids-it note. It was still there in run 4 and in run 5 round 1:
  measured on the delivered render, frames 50.7667 and 50.8000 carry **0.0000%
  ink** — a literal blank charcoal canvas on the cut into the outro, while the
  voice is already saying "Follow". Nothing catches it: geometry_audit sees no
  boxes so it cannot violate anything; frame_review's dedup treats the blank as
  just another distinct state; Gemini passed it twice. **A note in LEARNINGS is
  not a fix — if a gate cannot fail it, it will ship every run.**
- [gate1/gate2/all] **Cheap deterministic dead-frame detector, worth porting to
  every lane.** Crop the visual zone, take the modal RGB as the background, count
  pixels >28 L1 from it. Any frame under ~0.05% ink is a dead frame. On this
  short: beat 4 holds at 29.28%, the blank read 0.0000%, the fixed first outro
  frame reads 7.6058%. Run it as a consecutive-frame sweep across every zone cut;
  it costs one ffmpeg call and catches a class all three gates are blind to.
- [hermes_icon] **BUILD ORDER's real hiding place is the outro.** The law was
  written about diagram stems preceding logos, but the same violation sat in the
  exit screen: six decorative logo tiles entered at 50.86-51.55 and FOLLOW FOR
  DAILY AI — the line that IS the outro — only landed at 51.40. Chrome before
  content, the law's own words, in the one composition every viewer sees last.
  Check the outro against BUILD ORDER, not just the diagram beats.
- [all] **The frame-0 vocabulary generalises.** `settle()` + rendering the element
  already opaque (`hide=False`) is how the tweet card carries t=0; the same pair
  is the fix for ANY zone whose first frame would otherwise be blank. A `popo` at
  `t0 + 0.12` guarantees an empty frame, because a fromTo starts at opacity 0.
  Rule: every zone's first painted frame needs an element authored for it.
- [hermes_icon] **Sync the CTA to the word, not to the cut plus a stagger.** CTA
  50.74 is the exact onset of "Follow" in transcript_tight. The element carrying
  that word now lands on the zone's first frame instead of trailing the voice by
  0.66s, and the finished composition holds still 1.73s instead of 1.53s (build
  1.90s -> 1.70s). Zero tweens added: four re-timed, one changed helper.
- [gate2] **frame_review manifest timestamps run ~0.1s (3 frames @30fps) ahead of
  a frame-accurate decode**, measured consistently on both renders here: the
  manifest's `f_0050_666` shows post-cut content that a decoded sweep puts at
  50.7667, while the true 50.6667 frame is still the previous beat. Fine for
  reading states, wrong for any cut-adjacent claim. Use
  `-vf "select='between(t,a,b)'" -vsync 0` (decodes from the start) rather than
  `-ss` fast-seek or a sampled manifest frame when timing a hard cut.
- [all] **Re-verify inherited paperwork by re-running the generator and hashing
  the HTML.** `shasum -a 256` on index.html before and after a regenerate proved
  byte-identical output, which is what actually licenses trusting an inherited
  mp4/verdict pair. It costs seconds and it is the only check that proves the
  delivered render matches the committed generator rather than some lost
  intermediate state.
- [gate1] **Now five consecutive 0-error / 0-warning geometry audits on this
  project**, across compositions that differ by eight impeccable defects plus a
  reworked outro choreography. Gate 1 never moved. It measures legality; it has
  no opinion about whether anything is on screen at all.

  15.8u / 29.6px past the end of it. The rule for the factory: any rule,
  underline, divider or bracket that closes a ragged-right block takes
  `max()` over every member of that block, never the nearest one. A straight
  edge invites comparison with everything above it, which is exactly why a
  30px shortfall reads as a mistake while ragged text does not.
- [all] **A hand-set coordinate is where a design token goes to die.** This
  generator owns `CAP_MID = 0.62` (the measured Poppins 800 optical cap centre)
  and applies it to every row icon and every lockup label — and then authored
  the beat-4 highlight ring at a literal `y=328`, so the ring's centre sat
  671.8 vs 664.7px, i.e. 7.2px high, with 32.6px of air above the caps and
  18.2px below: the row sat low inside its own highlight. Grep pattern worth
  running on every generator: a numeric literal in an element's `top` argument
  whose siblings compute theirs from the token.
- [gate1+gate2+gate3] **All three gates passed both defects, and that is
  correct behaviour, not a gate bug.** geometry_audit measures LEGALITY
  (collisions, clipping, margins, seam, equal grids) — concentricity of a
  highlight with its target and flushness of a rule with its block are neither
  illegal nor blank. frame_review shows them, but only to an agent who MEASURES
  the frame instead of looking at it. Gemini called both renders clean. The
  detector for the whole class is free arithmetic on the emitted HTML: element
  rects against the generator's own measured glyph widths, which is how both
  defects were pinned to 0.05px and 7.2px before anything was re-rendered.
- [gate2] **An unchanged frame_review header is NOT evidence that a fix landed.**
  Before and after moving two elements by 29.6px and 7.1px the manifest was
  identical: 47 distinct states from 155 samples, 108 collapsed, same single
  `[still 5.0s]` marker. The 16x16 grey dedup cannot see geometry edits of that
  magnitude. Verify a fix by reading the specific frames that contain it (here
  22.0/24.3 for the rule and 43.3/46.0 for the ring), never by diffing the
  summary line.
- [gate3] **Judge noise is asymmetric across calls on the same label.** Two
  qc_v3 calls, both pass: call 1 on the inherited render returned the familiar
  "speaker mentions SpaceX AI instead of xAI" semantic minor_note, call 2 on the
  shipped render returned zero notes with the same prompt and the same video
  content in that region. The presence or absence of a minor_note carries no
  signal; only `errors` does. Do not rework, and do not celebrate, on a note.
- [factory] **`ffprobe format=duration` is not a stable identity for a render.**
  Two renders of compositions differing only by two static rects reported
  51.800000 and 51.840000; the video track was 1554 frames @ 30fps = 51.8s in
  both. The format duration follows the audio/mux tail. Paperwork should quote
  the video-track frame count (stable, exact) and treat a sub-0.1s duration
  delta between renders as noise rather than a change.
- [grokprice_kinetic] Clean run for the record, all measured against the shipped
  mp4: geometry 2 rounds this dispatch, both 0 errors / 0 warnings; build guards
  118 ids (0 dup), 57 tween selectors all resolving, deepest zone ink 738.7px vs
  a caption-pill top of 805.2px, 0 caption-echo trigrams; near-empty scan over
  all 1554 frames min ink 2.965% (t=3.50s, the deliberate one-number beat),
  median 14.96%, 0 frames under 1% or 2%; section-open ink 6.04 / 6.93 / 5.94 /
  4.07% so no blank handoff; idle_motion_scan idle_drift=no long_static=no; 47
  distinct states, 16 frames read, 0 law violations; QC pass with 0 visual and 0
  semantic errors on the first call for the shipped artifact.

## Run 5 verification + rework pass — hackers / counter (2026-08-10)

- [hackers_counter] **METERS COMPLETE has a failure mode the ledger never wrote down:
  the COMPARISON PAIR where NEITHER bar completes.** The two-bar "who is ahead" chart
  rested at FRONTIER 440 and OPEN SOURCE 372 of a 472-unit track — measured on the
  shipped render as 824 and 697 of 885 track px, i.e. the LEADING bar sat at 93.1%
  with a visible unfilled remainder, in both of its appearances. Every documented
  escape assumes you have already named a baseline ("make the BASELINE bar the one
  that reaches 100%", grokprice_counter); a two-bar comparison has no obvious
  baseline until you pick one, which is exactly why this shape keeps surviving.
  Naming FRONTIER the baseline (it fills the track, OPEN SOURCE lands on its
  proportion beneath it) satisfies the law, states the claim he actually makes and
  changes nothing else. Measured after: 884 of 885 px.
- [hackers_counter] **An unfilled remainder on the leading bar is an invented claim,
  not a style choice.** It turns the track's END into an unstated maximum: "frontier
  is at 93% of something" is a number nowhere in the transcript. This is the
  TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH / invented-numbers class (productivity_counter) arriving
  through geometry instead of through type, which is why no echo scan or numeral
  grep can see it.
- [hackers_counter] **Read a short's meters as ONE SYSTEM before judging any of
  them.** Inspecting the offending beat alone, a 93%-filled bar looks like a
  considered proportion. Listed side by side, this short had four meters and three
  of them completed (beat 1's segmented track fully populated 57..519 inside a
  52..524 track, beat 3's gauge lighting 12/12 before its deliberate drain, the
  outro bar at 100%) — the fourth was the odd one out. That framing turns a
  judgement call into a one-line finding, and it is impeccable's polish.md
  "conceptual misalignment" category rather than a cosmetic nudge.
- [hackers_counter] **The same chart shown twice must not REGRESS between
  appearances.** Beat 4C re-entered the open-source bar at 330 — 42 design units
  SHORTER than its own beat-2 state 30 seconds earlier — and then grew it, under a
  label reading CLOSING. The generator's own comment said "the before and after of
  one measurement must not shift on screen", so the intent was documented and the
  DATA still contradicted it. When two beats share a grid, diff their VALUES too,
  not just their coordinates.
- [hackers_counter] **Widening a gap bracket is bounded from below, and the number
  is on record: 56 design units at h=14.** A bracket narrower than ~4x its own
  height stops reading as a measurement and reads as an "H" glyph (logged in run 4
  from the other direction). That floor is what decides how far a "closing gap" may
  actually close — here 100 -> 56 units, not to zero.
- [hackers_counter] **A verification edit that only makes elements BIGGER cannot
  create a dead frame, so the expensive pre-render ink sweep is skippable.** No
  opacity and no timing changed, so ink could only increase; the 4-second
  post-render scan was the honest adjudicator and returned 0 near-empty frames of
  2008 (min 2.555%, median 16.49%) — identical to the superseded render. Reason
  about what your edit can and cannot break before re-running a 25-minute sweep.
- [hackers_counter] **A highlight ring around a FULL bar reads better than one
  around a partly-filled track.** Once FRONTIER filled its track the ring's gap
  became cream against a solid terracotta mass, instead of a same-colour stroke
  sitting near a grey track edge. The fix for the law improved the crown move for
  free — worth expecting, since a ring is only as legible as the contrast in its
  own gap.
- [factory] **Sixth-plus confirmation, now with the opposite result worth recording:
  an inherited item CAN be clean.** Re-running the free chain against this artifact
  before trusting its paperwork found the deterministic claims all TRUE — geometry
  re-ran 0 errors / 0 warnings, the generator re-emitted a byte-identical
  index.html (md5 32d261eaf3253fddb58718a1cf48405f), frame_review reproduced 72
  states / 201 samples / 129 collapsed exactly, 0 dead frames of 2008, caption band
  blank only outside speech. The prior pass's dead-air work genuinely held. The one
  real defect was a DESIGN claim no scan measures. Verification is still mandatory;
  what it finds is shifting from blank frames to claims.
- [gate3] **Re-rendering voids the verdict, and that is the correct trade.** The
  ledger's "never re-call Gemini on a byte-unchanged mp4" has a mirror: once the
  mp4 changes, the verdict on disk is evidence about a file that no longer exists.
  Re-earned here on the first call, 0 visual / 0 semantic / 0 minor notes, verdict
  written 13:01 against a render finished 12:59.
- [impeccable] **polish.md's design-system discovery step is the highest-yield part
  of the skill on this chassis, and it works on a short exactly as on a UI.** "Find
  the system, note the conventions, identify drift, then NAME THE ROOT CAUSE as a
  missing token / a one-off implementation / a conceptual misalignment" is what
  turned "that bar looks a bit short" into "this is the one meter in the short that
  does not complete, and completion is a law". Its companion rule — "a clean script
  result is never proof the design is strong" — has now held twice on this single
  item: five 0/0 geometry rounds, a clean ink scan and a Gemini pass, with a real
  design defect standing the whole time.

  That is the mirror of productivity_counter's rule (never file a collision off a mid-tween

## Run 5 — fablevssol / counter, RE-DISPATCH verification + fix pass (2026-08-10)

- [fablevssol_counter] **A STRIKE-THROUGH is a mark that must be MEASURED against its
  target, and it is the one mark no gate can see.** The beat-1 stroke through
  `WHO WINS?` was hand-authored `150..426` (design), a stale constant from a smaller
  setting of that line; the 62px display line actually inks `106.1..470.4`, so the
  stroke crossed the middle 76% and left the W's left arm and the whole `S?`
  un-struck — a cancel mark that stops short of what it cancels, on the law-9
  key-term frame, shipped through 4 renders and 2 green gate chains. **Why every gate
  is blind:** geometry_audit exempts thin bars from collision *by design*
  (`thin_bar`: lo<=14 and ratio>=8), so a strike can never be measured against the
  text it crosses; Gemini reads "struck-out heading" from any stroke through the
  middle; and frame review only catches it if you deliberately compare the two
  extents. Fix: author the stroke to the measured glyph run + a small overhang
  (`101..475`, ~5px each side, centred on 288). Verified in the delivered pixels:
  stroke `189..890px` against text ink `199..882px`.
- [factory] **The generalisation worth keeping: after the gates are green, go hunting
  for marks authored by EYE rather than by measurement.** Applied to every decorative
  element in this short (strike, tile rings, dashed slots, comparison rule, meter
  tracks, outro week bar) the sweep produced exactly one hit — everything else fits by
  construction (rings concentric with their plates, slot = the tile's exact silhouette,
  the beat-3 ring and its meter share one 400px column). One measured hit per short is
  a good return for ten minutes.
- [fablevssol_counter] **Not every left-weighted row is the defect that dashed slots
  fix.** Beat 4 holds ONE left-aligned icon tile for 5.7s under a centred lockup, which
  looks exactly like the beat-6 left-weight defect — but each icon sits under the meter
  SEGMENT it names, so its x is a claim (law 11), and `slot_el`'s own docstring rule
  ("legitimate only because every slot visibly receives its logo within ~1.4s") bans
  scaffolding a 5.7s wait, which would also edge into Miguel's banned empty-checkbox
  pattern. Diagnosed, deliberately not changed. Restraint is part of the pass.
- [factory] **Cheap composition-balance gate the factory does not have:** decode the
  render at 2fps, crop the top 800px, compute the ink bounding box per frame and compare
  the block centre with the zone centre. Sustained offsets are the "floating strip in an
  empty canvas" class stated as a number instead of a vibe. Here: worst sustained offset
  is beat 2's 6.8s long phase at 10.6% of the usable canvas above centre (inside normal
  optical-centring practice → correctly reports nothing to do); every other flag is a
  build stage that resolves in ~1.1s. The factory's own grokprice_icon learning
  ("balance a beat for its LONGEST-HELD phase") is what this measures.
- [factory] **A hand-rolled seam probe must skip overflow:hidden/clip wrappers.** Using
  the Range rect on an odometer window reports a phantom ink bottom of **1277px** (deep
  past the 862.5 seam) — the exact class `geometry_audit.py` already fixed. Skip clipped
  wrappers and the same sweep reports the true 779.6px (`#c2p` mid-rise) against a live
  caption-pill top of 805.2px.
- [factory] **Verifying an inherited item from disk is cheap and it is the only thing
  that makes its paperwork yours.** Re-running the generator and diffing `index.html`
  (byte-identical, md5 `a2a84d39…`) proved the inherited mp4 came from the gen file on
  disk; re-auditing reproduced 0/0; re-running gate 2 reproduced the manifest exactly
  (80 distinct states from 250 samples, 170 collapsed, the same single `[still 3.0s]`
  marker); re-measuring reproduced the seam clearance to 0.1px (779.6 vs 805.2 = 25.6)
  and the atom census exactly (112 atoms, 10/13/15/11/21/16/20/6). Total cost ~2 minutes,
  and it is what let this pass spend its render on a real defect instead of a rebuild.
- [fablevssol_counter] **Re-measuring meter completion belongs in the DOM, not in
  pixels.** Driving the delivered composition's own timeline and reading each `.mfill`'s
  computed `scaleX` at the end of its beat is exact and takes seconds: 1.00 for the two
  ladders, the weekend bar, the returns bar and the outro week bar; 0.87 / 0.96 for the
  two benchmark scores (data on a labelled 23-task scale: 20/23 and 22/23); and the
  beat-7 reset bar profiled 0 → 0.30 at 75.0 → 0 at 76.0, the deliberate escape.
- [gate 2] A one-element change that alters nothing else reproduces the manifest
  **exactly** — same distinct-state count, same collapsed count, same stillness marker.
  That identity is itself evidence the fix was surgical; a shifted state count after a
  supposedly local edit means the edit was not local.

## Run 5 — fablevssol / icon, VERIFICATION + REWORK pass (2026-08-10, second dispatch)

- [fablevssol_icon] **A `ride()` group is a COORDINATE FRAME, and every y-tween on a member
  must live inside it.** The inherited run-5 build ran beat 7B's SHUFFLING label through
  `y:8 -> y:0` at 71.92 while every other member of its ride group sat at `y:88` design px,
  so the section label detached from the row it names and floated **165 render px above it
  on empty cream for 3.6s** (71.92 -> 75.52). It shipped through a 0-error / 0-warning
  geometry audit, a `pass:true` Gemini verdict on both layers, and a written impeccable
  review. The generator's own docstring already stated the constraint ("no atom in the
  group may have a y-based ENTRANCE") — a comment is not a check. The check is ~20 lines:
  parse every `tl.fromTo("SEL",{FROM},{TO},T)` out of the emitted HTML, pick the
  comma-selector ride tweens, and assert each member's y-tweens end at `dy` before the ride
  and at `0` after. One mismatch across 5 groups here; zero after the fix. Mind the regex —
  `opacity:0` contains the substring `y:0`, so match `(?<![A-Za-z])y:`.
- [fablevssol_icon] **The ride must fire when the space is USED, not when the previous event
  ends.** Beat 6 lifted at `CUE["give"]-0.10` (58.26) while PICK YOURS lands at 62.14, and
  beat 7B lifted at `CUE["day"]+0.30` (75.52) while MORE TROUBLE lands at 77.78 — 3.9s and
  2.3s of the exact defect `ride()` exists to fix, fired early. Set **ride start = payoff cue
  minus ride duration** so the lift ENDS on the frame the payoff rises into; the two become
  one composite event and the beat holds the optical centre until then. When a group member
  appears DURING the lift (beat 6's row ring `i6rr`, cued at `CUE["ideal"]`), it must join the
  group or it draws at `y:0` while its own tiles are still 66 design px lower.
- [fablevssol_icon] **Measure top-pinning instead of arguing about it.** Per-frame ink
  centroid over the top-zone crop at 6fps (modal-colour ground, max-channel delta > 13); a
  window counts when the centroid sits above 34% of the zone AND no ink reaches below 72%.
  Inherited render: **11.50s in 4 windows** (10.00-12.33, 49.83-53.33, 58.33-62.00,
  75.67-77.67). Delivered: **5.83s in 2**. This is the only metric in the factory that makes
  "the beat opens on the zone's optical centre" falsifiable rather than a paperwork claim,
  and it is what turned two taste observations into fixable findings.
- [fablevssol_icon] **You cannot add a second `ride()` to a group that already rode.** Both
  tweens carry `immediateRender`, so the later-created one wins the build-time y and the
  element sits at the WRONG offset for the entire window before its first lift, then snaps
  when the earlier tween starts. To ride a beat twice, author it in the offset frame and ride
  UP by `-dy`. This is exactly why beat 5's 3.50s top-pinned window (the 5-tile field row
  building under an empty lower half) was left OPEN rather than half-fixed — the safe form is
  a bigger change than a verification pass should make to a passing build overnight. Beat 2's
  2.33s window carries the beat-1 dock choreography and has the same shape of risk. Both are
  one clean job for the next run, and the mechanism is now written down.
- [factory] **Second dispatch onto one item: the run-4 rule holds and it pays.** This item
  already had a generator, project, 0-error report, delivered mp4, `pass:true` verdict and a
  filed paperwork JSON when I was dispatched. Verifying rather than re-forking found a real
  defect the first pass missed. Cheapest proof that the shipped pixels came from the shipped
  source: copy `index.html` aside, re-run the generator, `diff`. Three seconds, and it also
  re-runs every build-time guard (seam budget, caption-echo, id/selector resolution).
- [gate3] **Third independent confirmation that `pass:true` carries no information about what
  the free gates can measure.** QC v3 passed the render carrying the detached-label defect
  exactly as cleanly (0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes) as it passed the fixed one.
- [gate2] **Manifest timestamps are dedup REPRESENTATIVES, not exact seek times.** A state
  filed as `f_0101_666` here showed the post-lift composition the timeline only reaches at
  ~62.0. When a frame's content disagrees with the code by a few tenths, settle it by decoding
  a contiguous window (`ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf trim=start=A:end=B,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS`) — `-ss`
  BEFORE `-i` is a keyframe seek and can be off by a whole GOP, which is how I nearly logged a
  ring-swap "bug" that a 63-frame ink sweep showed was frame-exact at 61.74.
- [fablevssol_icon] Delivered numbers for the record: geometry 4 rounds (2 inherited + 2 here),
  every one 0 errors / 0 warnings; 0 ride-offset mismatches across 5 groups; 80 distinct states
  from 250 samples, 0 idle candidates and NO stillness marker (longest kept-frame gap 2.7s);
  37 manifest frames read across two renders plus 4 full-res crops; 0 blank frames of 2496
  (min ink 4.383% at t=50.267, median 15.06%); 7 pill-free frames, all outside speech; tweet
  3.20s in one run with zero metrics; top-pinned composition 11.50s -> 5.83s; QC v3 pass on the
  FIRST call against both renders. Render 3 took 47.2s wall at `-q high`.

## Run 5 verification + rework — grokbuild / icon (2026-08-10, second impeccable reader)

- [grokbuild_icon] **A run-5 item that passed all three gates AND a full impeccable pass
  still shipped three composition/asset defects, and one of them had already been fixed
  by the SIBLING LANE of the same video in the same run.** `grokbuild_diagram` measured
  and re-cropped `grokbuild_chart_crop.png` this run; the icon lane still placed it whole.
  threed_icon's habit generalises and is worth making standard: before declaring an
  inherited item clean, grep LEARNINGS for your VIDEO (not just your `video_lane`) and
  diff your ASSET HANDLING against the sibling lanes', because the generators are forks
  of one file and the assets are shared.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Measure a source raster's EDGE ROWS before placing it, not just its
  ink box.** `grokbuild_chart_crop.png` is 828x456 with **39 rows of pure white along its
  top edge** (a gutter from the source page) and ~48% empty mint field below the entry;
  all of its ink lives in x246-702, y13-234. Inside our rounded mint card that gutter
  reads as a second card header, and no gate can see it (it is inside a raster). Cheap
  pre-flight to add to the existing `opaque_frac` / `edge_dark_coverage` asset audit:
  count pure-white and pure-background edge rows/cols.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Law 8 is a MAGNIFICATION lever, not only a cropping rule.** Cropping
  to (200,40,560x260) let the card be placed at **1.125x** of its new natural width
  instead of 0.951x of the old one — so the crucial entry text renders 1.22x larger on a
  phone while the CARD gets smaller (420x231 -> 336x156 design). Solve the placement from
  the audit's own arithmetic (`natural * 1.15 / 1.875` is the ceiling) and a tighter crop
  buys legibility instead of costing it.
- [grokbuild_icon] **Bar-chart columns standing on a baseline need TOP-ONLY
  border-radius.** A fully rounded column leaves a ~16px triangular gap of canvas at each
  bottom corner, so three columns read as floating plates hovering over a line rather than
  bars on an axis. Gate 1 is structurally blind: the baseline is a thin bar and thin bars
  are collision-exempt. Second lane to land on this (hackers_counter logged the rule in
  its own run-5 pass) — make it a chassis default.
- [grokbuild_icon] **The centre-then-step fix has a MIRROR TRAP: it can un-centre the
  state you were not looking at.** The spectrum beat spent 5.5s with its ink centroid at
  design x 385-391 under a headline centred on 288 (left 40% of the zone empty). Offsetting
  the whole beat by -90 from t=0 centred that window and immediately created a **2.0s
  LEFT-hug** on the lone Grok tile that opens the beat — the same defect mirrored, measured
  at 97 units off. Root cause worth stating: when the beat's SUBJECT already sits on the
  zone centre in the final layout, no static offset can be right for both partial states.
  The axis has to make room TWICE — the subject steps aside as the expensive end grows
  (47.94), everything steps back as the cheap end lands (55.40) — two wrapper-free
  `fromTo`s, each caused by an arriving element, each completing before anything is
  scheduled into the room it makes. **Check the centroid of EVERY partial state, not just
  the one that caught your eye.**
- [grokbuild_icon] **Deterministic detector for the whole half-built-composition class,
  ~20 lines and no render:** decode the top zone at 270x200, take each frame's modal
  colour as background, and print the horizontal ink CENTROID and ink SPAN of everything
  below the headline band every 0.5s. Superseded render: 385-391 vs a zone centre of 288
  for 5.5s. After the fix every RESTING state reads 280-300 (worst 12 units). Span and
  centroid disagree usefully: a centred span with a left-heavy centroid is an axis with
  one loaded end (legitimate, and it is what this beat looks like for 1.3s while the
  frontier tiles are still coming); both off-centre is the defect.
- [gate2] Eighth-plus confirmation of the dedup blindness, this time BRACKETED instead of
  sampled: all three `[still Ns]` gaps on this short (3.0s / 4.7s / 6.3s) contain real
  builds — a cream-on-cream chip tick (29.40 vs 31.33), a terracotta span bar (53.00 vs
  53.80) and a 3px ring on a dark canvas (64.10 vs 64.90). Reading the GENERATOR's tween
  schedule for the gap window first tells you exactly which two timestamps to bracket, so
  each adjudication costs two `ffmpeg -ss` frames instead of a bisection.
- [factory] **The impeccable pass is not one-shot.** A second impeccable reader on an
  already-impeccable'd, three-gates-green, fully-paperworked item found three real defects
  in one pass. Gate 1 was 0 errors / 0 warnings before AND after, the pre- and post-render
  ink sweeps were 0 dead frames before AND after, and gate 3 passed clean both times. Its
  entire yield here was composition balance and asset craft, which nothing in the
  deterministic chain measures.

## Run 5 verification + rework — deepresearch / checklist (2026-08-10, second dispatch)

- [deepresearch_checklist] **The sibling-lane rule paid off again, and this time the
  sibling had already written the fix down.** `deepresearch_icon` logged in run 5: "a
  connector that leaves a multi-row panel at ONE row's height is a LAW-11 claim and no
  gate checks it". The CHECKLIST lane of the same video shipped the identical defect
  through a 0-error/0-warning audit, a full gate-2 frame read and a Gemini verdict with
  zero notes: beat 4's three output arrows left the review panel 11 / 1 / 13 design px
  from the ARCHITECTURE, LIMITATIONS and EDGE CASES row centres, so the picture asserted
  "this finding produced that output" — and the third arrow paired a **struck-out** row
  with an output. **Before declaring an inherited item clean, grep LEARNINGS for your
  VIDEO, not your video_lane, and check every fix the siblings logged.**
- [deepresearch_checklist] **The arithmetic that makes this defect unavoidable, so nobody
  tries to retune it away.** An output stack at 76-unit pitch beside a row list at
  44-unit pitch cannot place three horizontal connectors without at least one landing on
  a row centre; moving the ys only changes WHICH finding is falsely implicated. And a
  5-row panel's own vertical centre IS a row centre (rows 150/194/238/282/326, panel
  centre 237), so "leave from the panel's middle" is the same bug. The stem must leave
  from a GUTTER midpoint (216 here) and a COLLECTOR RAIL must carry the fan-out.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **A collector rail costs zero geometry findings if you author
  it right, and the recipe is four properties.** `class="abs node bus"`, inline
  `background/border:none/display:block/text-align:left`, `opacity:0`, `transform:
  scaleY(0)` with `transform-origin:center top`, grown one segment per node. It is a real
  box so both ends of every tap anchor (`isBox = ltile|node|shot|chip`); `thin_bar()`
  (min side <= 14px and ratio >= 8) exempts it from collisions once drawn; the collapsed
  rail is under the audit's 0.15 opacity floor so it is never measured mid-tween; and the
  equality group keys on the FULL class string, so `abs node bus` never joins the
  `abs node` group. Result: 0 errors / 0 warnings with **zero `data-overlap-ok` and zero
  `data-bleed` in the whole short**.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **BUILD ORDER for a rail whose nodes arrive on three different
  spoken words:** grow ONE SEGMENT PER NODE (stem after node 1 lands, rail to node 2's
  tap, rail extended to node 3's tap as that node arrives, each tap after its own node).
  The ledger's "lay the rail only after every node exists" would have compressed the
  whole harness into the last 0.5s before the cut — the payoff-flashes-before-the-cut
  defect. Segment-per-node keeps every connector after its node AND leaves the completed
  picture holding 0.5s.
- [deepresearch_checklist] **Dropping a `hero` variant is a gate-1 improvement as well as
  a design one.** Three output nodes where one carried `.node.hero` are two groups of
  1+2; identical nodes are one clean group of three same-size rects. The hero border was
  also `TERRA_L` — the DARK-ground accent — painted on a cream beat, while terracotta in
  this short means verdict/tick/meter/flow. Colour meaning is a factual check, not taste
  (grokprice_icon logged the same class from the badge side).
- [deepresearch_checklist] **Ninth confirmation of the 805.2px caption-pill top, plus a
  correction to how the deepest ink is measured.** A Range-box sweep over every `.tz`
  atom reports 752.1px on this short; SKIPPING the Range on painted atoms and on anything
  with `overflow:hidden|clip` (which `Range.selectNodeContents` ignores) reports 736.2px
  — the naive number is pessimistic by ~16px. Measure the pill, then measure ink the way
  the pixels do: painted box for painted atoms, Range only for unpainted text.
- [factory] **Re-verifying a completed run-5 item cost ~25 minutes and one render, and the
  free evidence all reproduced bit-for-bit**: generator re-run byte-identical (md5
  b5d64678…), geometry audit identical 0/0, `frame_review` identical 45 states / 149
  samples / 104 collapsed / 5.3s longest gap / 0 idle candidates, whole-render dead-frame
  scan 0 of 1485. **Every deterministic number was right and the composition still
  contained a law violation** — which is the fifth-plus time this ledger has said it:
  scripts prove legality, only reading the frames as SENTENCES proves correctness.
- [gate3] Never re-call Gemini on a byte-unchanged mp4 — but DO re-call it after a
  re-render: the verdict on disk describes the artifact it judged and nothing else. The
  fixed render passed on the first call with 0 visual errors, 0 semantic errors and one
  complimentary minor note.
- [deepresearch_checklist] Numbers for the record after the rework: geometry 6 rounds
  (4 build + 2 this pass, every one 0 errors / 0 warnings), atom census 14/9/25/17/8 =
  73 real ids with the id-less atoms all connector wrappers, 161 DOM ids with 0
