## Run 5 (impeccable) — fablevssol / kinetic (2026-08-10)

- [factory] **A PART-BUILT inherited item is more dangerous than a finished one, and mtimes
  are how you find out.** This lane arrived with a generator, a project and an 80MB mp4 —
  and the mp4 was written at 09:32 while `index.html` and the generator were rewritten at
  09:36, with no QC verdict and no paperwork. So a render existed that **no HTML on disk
  could account for**. The finished-item protocol ("re-run the free gates, don't rebuild")
  does not apply: there was nothing to attribute. Order that worked: `stat` all five
  artefacts first, re-run the generator and diff `index.html` (byte-identical, md5
  aa965ece9028176d1a7680903c2ea5bf), then treat the render as absent. Cheap standing check
  for any hand-off: **if the mp4 is older than the generator, the mp4 is not evidence.**
- [fablevssol_kinetic] **The highest-yield impeccable finding on a mature generator is a
  hardcoded constant sitting next to the derived value that was written to replace it.**
  `layout()` computes `b5a_lift = 88.3` (the offset that centres beat 5's two-line setup
  block on the optical axis) and `beat5()` used `lift = 56.0` three lines away — run 4's
  hand-picked number, carried into run 5 unnoticed, pinning the line 32 design units (60
  render px) high for the 2.4s it owns the zone alone. Gate 1 cannot see it, gate 3 passed
  it, and it is invisible in code review because both lines look deliberate. **Grep every
  beat builder for a float literal and ask which `LAY[...]` key was supposed to supply it.**
- [fablevssol_kinetic] **A beat can be laid out perfectly for its FINAL cast and broken for
  most of the time it is on screen.** Beat 7 phase B places the three DAY cards at the top
  edge and the hero word 60 units below them — correct at 78.0s, and at 73.6s it is two
  islands of ink with a **144-design-unit (270px) void through the middle of the zone for
  3.0s**, because the hero cannot arrive until 75.22. Geometry was 0 errors / 0 warnings,
  the DOM ink sweep never dropped under 3%, and the pixel scan never dropped under 1%:
  nothing is blank, nothing collides, so **no gate in the chain measures this class**. Fix
  that costs one tween: open the DAY row directly ABOVE the mark row (the pair is then
  centred on the optical axis), ride it home in ONE move completing exactly as the hero
  slams into the space it vacates, and retime the last card so all three land before the
  move starts. Same shape as the beat-6 finding below — the general test is **"list the
  moments where the cast is INCOMPLETE and ask where that partial cast is centred".**
- [fablevssol_kinetic] **A group ride must be caused by the element that needs the room.**
  Beat 6's ride was keyed to `them + 0.66` — an offset with no referent — so the block
  stepped into its header layout **1.7s before** the serif line arrived to fill the space,
  leaving 40% of the canvas empty. Re-keying it to `weekend - 0.44` (completing as the line
  lands) fixed it, and the stepping ring had to join the group offset (`sety` + one
  `moveto` with x unchanged) so it stayed locked to the tile it was highlighting. A ride
  fired early is not a smaller defect than a ride missing — it manufactures the empty frame
  it was added to prevent.
- [all] **The crown move is also a defect generator: a travelling highlight ring is a BAR IN
  FLIGHT, and gate 1 is structurally blind to it twice over** (rings are collision-exempt
  AND the crossing frames fall between the audit's 0.5s samples). Measured here: the beat-6
  tile ring is exactly one grid pitch wide (96u ring, 72u tile, 24u gap), so at 25-50% of a
  0.32s `power3.out` hop its left border sits inside the mark it is leaving and its right
  border inside the mark it is arriving at — ~3 rendered frames per hop, times 3 hops, plus
  the beat-3/4 node hops doing the same across the UI / UX labels. That is literally
  Miguel's "content cut by an orange bar", produced by the move he called chef's kiss.
  **Fix without losing the gesture: split the vocabulary by GESTURE, not by lane.** A
  deliberate one-at-a-time walk SWAPS (`hlmove`: fade out 0.14s, reposition while
  invisible, fade in 0.26s, fully lit at cue+0.42 = exactly where the old travel landed,
  and it now lands on a STATIC asset per law 5); a scramble TRAVELS (beat 7's six hops are
  0.16-0.44s apart and six fades at that spacing read as a flicker — the darting IS the
  claim). Two ring behaviours in one short is not inconsistency when the motion carries the
  meaning; it is the product register's own "motion conveys state" rule.
- [fablevssol_kinetic] **Meter TICK marks laid over the FILL read as notches, so a bar whose
  law is to complete looks segmented.** `rgba(255,255,255,0.55)` at 1/3 and 2/3 over a full
  terracotta fill on dark made METERS COMPLETE look like four pinched segments at phone
  size. Worse, 1/3 and 2/3 of the track are **not** the gutters between three equal cards:
  with `NODE_W=140, NODE_GAP=24` the gutter centres are at 0.3248 and 0.6752, i.e. the
  ticks missed the columns they were marking by 4 design units. Deleting the ticks and
  landing the fill's intermediate steps on the gutter centres makes each stage visibly
  finish under its own card, and the cards ARE the scale. (Companion to the counter lane's
  "ticks must follow the ground" — the deeper rule is that a completing bar should carry no
  cross-strokes at all.)
- [fablevssol_kinetic] **A hero numeral without its unit label is chrome — and it is also
  the sparsest measurable frame in a short.** Beat 6 opened on a bare `3-4` whose label
  arrived 0.98s later; that window was the only stretch in the render under 1% painted ink
  (6 frames at 0.995%). Landing the numeral and its unit as ONE lockup took it to 2 frames
  at 0.997%. Generalises the counter lane's "a big unlabelled 0 held an empty row": the
  threshold is not the duration, it is whether the number has a referent on screen.
- [all] **The pixel dead-frame scan's 1% line is exactly where a legitimate display numeral
  on cream lands, and the DOM sweep disagrees by 3x.** The same instant measured 0.997% by
  pixels (crop 1080x790, 360x263 RGB, modal background, max-channel delta > 13) and **3.2%**
  by DOM ink area, because a Range box for a 105u-wide word at fs 58 is 105 x 81 design
  units of *box* against maybe a third of that in *ink*. Neither number is the verdict —
  an `ffmpeg -ss` extraction is, and it showed a full-size terracotta hero numeral. Quote
  both metrics and the frame, never one number.
- [gate2] **A manifest with NO stillness marker and NO idle block is the healthy signature,
  and it is worth stating positively.** 83 distinct states from 250 samples with 167
  collapsed, longest kept-frame gap 2.7s — under `frame_review`'s 3.0s threshold, so it
  printed neither. Six lanes have now logged "a `[still Ns]` marker is an instruction to
  probe"; the inverse is also true — **the absence of markers is not a missing feature and
  needs no ffmpeg adjudication at all.**
- [fablevssol_kinetic] Zero `data-bleed` and zero `data-overlap-ok` in the whole short, and
  the reason is structural: the lane draws NO connectors, so giving strikes their own
  `.strk` class (identical CSS) means the connector-termination law is never run rather than
  being exempted. A lane with no arrows should have no `.rule` atoms — confirmed on a second
  fablevssol lane.
- [fablevssol_kinetic] Clean close: geometry 3 rounds, every one 0 errors / 0 warnings (atom
  census by the audit's own `key_of`: 103 distinct measured atoms across 8 `.tz` sections —
  10/9/12/10/16/14/24/8, peak 13 simultaneous, only 3 id-less and all of them strike/rule
  wrappers); 210 DOM ids with 0 duplicates, 105 tween selectors all resolving, 0 untweened
  section children, 76/76 opacity probes lit; 2 renders (the second bought by a gate-2
  finding, none by geometry); 83 distinct states from 250 samples, 0 idle candidates,
  25 rendered frames read; 0 fully blank frames of 2496 (min ink 0.997%, median 12.25%);
  caption band blank only before the first spoken word and on the last frame; tweet on
  screen 3.13s with zero metrics; deepest zone ink 736.8px against the caption pill's
  painted top of 805.2px (**ninth** independent confirmation of that constant) = 68.4px

## Run 5 (impeccable) — hackers / icon (2026-08-10)

- [hackers_icon] **I inherited a run-5 build that had passed nothing.** The generator,
  project, a 0-error geometry report and a render already existed; there was no gate-3
  verdict, no paperwork, and the `.fr` frames dir was still on disk — i.e. gates 2 and 3
  had never been closed. First move was to prove the generator reproduces its own
  `index.html` byte for byte (md5 identical), which makes the existing render legitimate
  evidence about that HTML; only then is a verification pass worth anything. **If you pick
  up a half-finished item, regenerate and hash before you trust ANY of its numbers.**
- [hackers_icon] **The factory's dead-frame floor is a design instrument, and it was
  failing silently in the flagship lane.** A 0.05s pre-render ink sweep of the inherited
  build returned **92 near-empty samples**, 75 of them one continuous run from 7.05s to
  10.50s: the beat-1 scaffold (kicker + three dashed slots) holding the whole zone at
  **0.375% painted ink** while the sentence walked to "Anthropic". A 2.5-unit dash at
  alpha 0.28 shifts a downsampled cell ~29 grey levels against the scan's 28 threshold,
  so half the perimeter is invisible to the metric — and at phone size the slots are
  invisible to the eye too (LAW 8). 3.4 units at 0.34 with a 0.055 tint took that window
  to 1.84% and the whole sweep from 92 to 1. **Every lane using `slot()` as its
  slot-then-fill vocabulary is exposed: run the ink sweep, not just the audit.**
- [hackers_icon] **Entrance scale is a dead-frame parameter.** The one remaining
  near-empty frame in the first render (t=55.13, 0.949% of 2008) was the closing row's
  swap: four plates entering at `scale 0.72` cover 52% of their final area, so the handoff
  frame was half-painted. Returning to the lane's default 0.86 made it full without
  touching the choreography. Look at entrance scale before you invent a pre-roll.
- [hackers_icon] **The morphing-highlight defect the counter lane found is worse in the
  icon lane, and no gate can see it.** `hljump()` morphed the beat-1 ring from the
  open-source pair at the BOTTOM of the zone to the frontier row at the TOP — 0.42s of a
  terracotta stroke sweeping through the OPEN SOURCE kicker, three name labels and three
  plates. Rings are collision-exempt at gate 1, dedup is blind to thin strokes at gate 2,
  and gate 3 passed it. Ported `hlmove()` (out 0.14s → set at t+0.15 → in 0.26s): same cue
  timing, nothing ever drawn over a thing it is not highlighting. **Grep every generator
  for `hljump` and check what the path crosses.**
- [hackers_icon] **`FILL THE SHAPE` on full-bleed artwork is pad 0 or nothing.** Round 1
  cut kimi's pad from 20% to 8% and called it fixed; 8% around a 93%-opaque BLACK square
  is still a white frame around a black box — the same defect one step smaller. The
  honest form is pad 0 with the plate taking the artwork's OWN radius, measured off the
  alpha channel (first opaque x on rows 0 and 1 solves r − √(2r−1) = x): kimi 0.27·s,
  codex 0.18·s. Test is "does the artwork ship its own plate", never "is the artwork
  dark".
- [hackers_icon] **A full-bleed radius must propagate to every silhouette that references
  the tile.** Gate 2 caught the second half at 26.9s: the dashed slot kept the nominal
  radius 16 while kimi's plate now drew at 20.5, so the slot's dashed corners poked out
  around the tile that had just filled it. One `tile_radius(key, s)` helper feeding both
  the tile and its slot closes it. Same class as run 3's r16-slot-under-r20-tile finding,
  arriving through the FULLBLEED door.
- [hackers_icon] **A kicker's distance from its row IS the ring's clearance budget.** With
  the kicker 14u above its row, a ring with an honest 12u clearance lands 0.4px under the
  kicker's glyph box (measured at 19.2s: `b1-hl` bottom 160.8px, ring top 161.2px). You
  cannot fix that by moving the ring — concentricity forbids it. Introduce a `KICK_DROP`
  (45u here) that is ring clearance + air, apply it to every kicker in the short, and
  re-centre the block afterwards.
- [hackers_icon] **Two objects in one exit stack must derive from ONE span.** The outro
  divider was sized from the headline (357.9u) and the mark row from its own tiles plus a
  hand-picked gap (328u), so a deliberately centred composition was 15 units off on each
  side. Deriving the row's gap from the divider span makes both share their two edges
  exactly. Third lane to file this; it is a one-line fix (`gap = (uw − 4·s)/3`).
- [hackers_icon] **Some compositions cannot be centred in both states, and the answer is
  arithmetic, not a tween.** Beat 3 runs a model column LEFT of a 150u plate, then RIGHT
  of it, inside a 472u band. Solving for both centres gives contradictory bounds
  (P ≥ 254 and P ≤ 172), so the plate position run 4 chose is already the optimum. The
  honest fix was shortening the landing distance (dx 378 → 336, held frame 96px → 56px
  off centre), not inventing a recoil to hide the imbalance. **Do the algebra before you
  add motion.**
- [hackers_icon] **When a group dims, its CONCLUSION dims with it** (hermes_icon's rule,
  confirmed in a second lane). The plate ghosted to 0.26 while the solid 345×75px CRACKED
  chip stayed at full strength, so the loudest thing on screen was the previous claim
  while the subject was a 4.5px ring around the models walking past. 0.5 keeps it legible
  and subordinate. No gate measures relative emphasis; this is read-the-frame-and-squint.
- [hackers_icon] **A highlight must retire with its claim.** The cage ring held 7.2s, the
  last 4.3s of it on an EMPTY cage while the sentence had moved to the model that got out.
  Fading it as CHEAT lands costs nothing and is what LAW 5 actually says.
- [gate1] **Fourth consecutive lane reporting the same thing: a clean gate-1 report is
  evidence of legality, never of quality.** Three rounds, all 0 errors / 0 warnings, and
  the audit could not see any of the eleven defects this pass fixed (morphing ring, white
  frame on a black logo, slot fringe, ring radii, ring/kicker crowding, two content widths
  in beat 4, outro overhang, 96px composition drift, emphasis inversion, an expired
  highlight, 92 near-empty samples). Budget the render and the frame read regardless.
- [hackers_icon] Final numbers: geometry 3 rounds all 0/0 (111 real atoms, ids checked
  against the generator), 234 DOM ids with zero duplicates, 117 tween selectors all

  near-empty 92 → 1 (that one at t=44.65 is not frame-aligned), **0 near-empty frames in

  worked: (1) `stat` every artefact and read the QC json FIRST, (2) re-run the generator
  and diff `index.html` against the shipped one (byte-identical, md5
  5eac49cddc23b52a5f1faec18abf819a — proves the mp4 came from that generator), (3)
  reproduce the judge's complaint on the delivered PIXELS before believing or refuting
  it. Total cost before any edit: about three minutes.
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **The verdict "the arrow overlaps and enters the box instead of
  stopping at the box edge" was NOT judge noise, and it was not our arrow.** A 1:1 crop
  of the render at 15.5s shows the terracotta highlight ring drawn around the data row
  INSIDE an embedded raster whose source ships its own hand-drawn purple arrow at that
  exact spot: the ring's top-left border crosses the arrow and the arrowhead ends inside
  the ring. Gate 1 is structurally blind (rings are collision-exempt AND the arrow is
  pixels inside an `<img>`, not an atom). **Standing rule: never ring a region of a

  instead.** That is now the FIFTH lane to replace a ring with a border tween

  first where the crossing object was inside a raster.
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **A "highlight the row" problem is usually a CROP problem.** The

  WHITE gutter along its top edge, so the readable line sat in a band across its middle

  units — 29% SMALLER on screen while its only readable line renders 17% LARGER** — the
  source's own arrow enters from the card's top edge, and the highlight becomes the
  card's border because the card IS the data point. Law 8 and the ring defect have one
  fix. (The sibling diagram lane measured the same box independently; grep LEARNINGS for
  your VIDEO, not just your video_lane.)
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH, ratio edition, confirmed on a second lane
  of the same video.** The shipping beat closed with a mono line reading `shipped 10/10`.
  The only numeral spoken anywhere in this 73s transcript is "4.5" (checked with a regex
  over `transcript_tight.json`), and 10/10 asserts a per-month delivery SCORE nobody
  states — in a lane made of terminal output it wears the clothes of data. Replacement
  that claims nothing: an accent underline growing under the completed `10 MONTHS
  SHIPPING` lockup on his own payoff word ("unbelievable"), which is the same underline
  the intro already draws under GROK BUILD. `grokbuild_icon` logged this exact string in
  its own lane; a sibling lane's TRANSCRIPT finding is almost always live in yours.
- [impeccable/all] **The polish lens' drift triage is the part worth importing into this
  factory verbatim.** Classify every deviation as a MISSING TOKEN, a ONE-OFF
  IMPLEMENTATION or a CONCEPTUAL MISALIGNMENT, because the fix differs by category:
  patch the value, swap to the shared component, or rework the flow. All three were
  present in one generator — missing token (nine small type steps 13/14/15/16/17/18/19/
  20/22 and four display steps with no ratio; no optical-centring constant), one-off
  (the chart beat was the only screen of ten with no command line; a ring where every
  other highlight is a border), conceptual (a cut landing 1.2s before its own subject can
  be named). Naming the category is what turns a list of nudges into constants.
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **CAP_MID = 0.62 is worth a helper, not a comment.** Poppins 800 /
  JetBrains Mono caps run 0.26em-0.98em below the layout-box top, so a text block's
  optical middle is 0.62*fs down. Every capability row here had THREE centres (icon 14,
  name 15.4, check 13 design units) and both display operators sat 3-7 units low against
  the plates they join. `cap_top(mid, fs) = mid - 0.62*fs` fixed all of them in one edit.
  grokprice_kinetic logged the constant; putting it in the generator as a function is
  what stops the next fork re-deriving it.
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **A dashed placeholder's ALPHA is a measurement, not a taste call —
  and it moves your own dead-frame metric.** `rgba(243,239,232,0.34)` on #101012 was the
  thinnest window in the whole short (0.996% ink at 17.65s, the parity beat's two empty

  ground) took the 0.05s pre-render sweep from one sub-1% sample to **zero**, min ink

  the ground and a light fill makes the EMPTY slot brighter than the plate that fills it
  (grokprice_icon's inverted-hierarchy trap).
- [grokbuild_kinetic] **"Move the cut" beats "add chrome" again, and the tell is the
  beat's own LABEL cue.** The cost beat cut at 46.30 while its group label was cued at
  47.30, so the render opened on a bare 62-unit plate with ~85% of the zone empty for a

  element that NAMES its subject; if the gap is over ~0.3s, the cut is in the wrong place.

## Run 5 (impeccable) — hermes / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [hermes_diagram] **A run-5 generator can be a run-4 BODY wearing a run-5 DOCSTRING.**
  The inherited `shorts_run5/gen/hermes_diagram_gen.py` opened with a 50-line impeccable
  plan (items A-M, written in the past tense) and a project generated from it at 09:26 —
  but `diff shorts_run4/gen/hermes_diagram_gen.py shorts_run5/gen/hermes_diagram_gen.py`
  was 77 lines, ALL of them the docstring plus the `R5` paths. Not one design change was
  in the code: the tier rows still carried the banned side stripe the header said had
  been deleted, and the type scale the header said was collapsed to 11/13 still ran
  10/10.5/11/12/13. **Diff an inherited generator against its ancestor before trusting
  its header**, and when you finish, rewrite the header to match the code (the plan is
  not the work).
- [hermes_diagram] **impeccable's side-stripe ban was load-bearing, and deleting it
  exposed the real defect.** The three tier rows carried a 6px terracotta LEFT stripe
  whose opacity encoded "share of the catalog the agent is handed" — undecodable from an
  alpha value, and the one form impeccable bans outright. Run 4's own comment admitted
  the stripe existed to "fill the gutter that right-aligned numerals leave": the numeral
  column was 84px wide for a 30px "24". So the ban removed a decoration AND surfaced the
  typesetting bug under it. Fix: a ledger line (count+unit lockup left, outcome right,
  symmetric 16/16 padding) has no gutter to fill. When a banned element has a stated
  justification, the justification is usually the actual defect.
- [hermes_diagram] **A read-out must agree with the state it sits on — a new defect class
  next to METERS COMPLETE.** The context-window cap rule swept to FULL on "context is
  finite" (correct, complete) and then stayed full for 18 seconds while three of the four
  schema slots below it were emptied to `free`. Three gates passed it twice. Reaching
  full satisfies METERS COMPLETE; STAYING full while its subject changes is a lie. It now
  retracts to the one schema still loaded, which also cleared the space the corner check
  badge needed. **Check every persistent read-out against the last state change beneath it.**
- [hermes_diagram] **Grammar consistency is a design property AND a factual one.** This
  short says many-to-one three times (tier stack -> node, six servers -> hub, three
  sources -> FOLLOW) and run 4 drew it three different ways; the beat-2 version sent one
  arrow out of the MIDDLE tier row, which quietly claims "the 830-tool tier feeds the
  node". A collector spine on the stack's right edge with ONE arrow leaving it fixes the
  claim and the inconsistency in the same move (and audits clean: the spine is
  `class="abs node <suffix>"`, a real box to the audit, never a `rule`).
- [hermes_diagram] **A hand-computed lockup width cannot centre a lockup.** Estimating a
  chip's padding plus a mono track put the inherited Nous/Hermes lockup's INK 20 design
  px left of the axis it claimed. The reliable construction is a full-width flex row with
  `justify-content:center`: `geometry_audit` measures an unpainted atom by its Range rect
  (its ink), and a 1080px-wide box is excluded from BOTH the margin check (`w <
  FRAME_W*0.95`) and the offcenter check (same bound), so it is honest and invisible at
  once. Same trick works for any centred cluster whose width you would otherwise guess.
- [hermes_diagram] **A 30fps pre-render ink sweep is the cheapest blank-handoff detector
  in the chain.** Seeking the paused timeline and summing visible atoms' area x effective
  opacity over all 1625 frames took ~2 minutes and found exactly two near-blank handoffs
  (t=3.60 tweet->agent node, t=15.43 key term->tier stack) that gate 1 cannot see and
  gate 2's 3fps grid can step over. Both were closed by lengthening the OUTGOING exit so
  it overlaps the incoming entrance; with `power3.in` exits the outgoing element keeps
  ~70% of its opacity two-thirds of the way through, so a 0.30s exit really does carry
  the handoff. Post-render scan then confirmed 0 near-empty frames of 1626.
- [hermes_diagram] **Adding discrete events SHORTENS stillness gaps, which is the good
  kind of churn.** Same footage, same laws, same lane: run 4 reported 47 distinct states
  with a 3.7s longest hold, this pass reports 51 states with no gap over 2.33s — because
  the silhouette hand-off, the spine, the cap retraction and the hub's step are all real
  events. Do not read a shorter longest-hold as "more motion"; law 1 counts idle drift,
  and the idle-candidate count stayed 0.
- [hermes_diagram] **The hub that steps aside.** "If you have a Hermes agent" is about the
  agent, so the agent now arrives on the zone's optical centre and translates to its
  final position in ONE 0.5s move as the six server rows slide in. Authoring it at its
  FINAL rect and using `tl.fromTo(x: <offset> -> 0)` means immediateRender parks it at the
  offset from build time, the audit measures the moved rect live, and the geometry stays
  0/0. A reposition is a transition, not idle motion — but keep the incoming elements
  0.2s behind the move so nothing crosses.
- [gate1/impeccable] **Three consecutive 0-error / 0-warning audits while eight design
  defects were being fixed.** geometry_audit saw none of: the banned side stripe, the
  five-step type scale, the two columns that shared no edge, the alpha ramp that encoded
  nothing, the caption louder than its subject, the cap rule contradicting its own slots,
  the off-axis lockup, or the middle-row arrow's false claim. A clean gate-1 report is
  evidence of legality, never of quality — the second lane to log this in run 5.

## Run 5 (impeccable) — hermes / counter (2026-08-10)

- [factory] **A dispatch can land on a HALF-BUILT item, and that is a third state the

  agent stopped at 09:36; I arrived at 13:01). The right first move is the same as for a

  (md5 `90a34e887823c4da80072eb1b91ca540`) proved the inherited gate-1 verdict belonged to

  re-deriving 20 known fixes. Check `ps` and artifact mtimes first — a half-built item and
  a concurrently-building item look identical on disk.
- [hermes_counter] **The blank-handoff class has a case where NO ease and NO overlap can
  help: when the incoming element sits inside the outgoing one's box.** The tweet card
  (design y126-297) and the catalog odometer (y65-184) share the zone's centre, so any
  cross-dissolve puts two atoms over the audit's 0.15 opacity floor in one rect — a
  guaranteed gate-1 collision — while sequencing them leaves a hole. Measured before the
  fix: **0.035% top-zone ink at t=3.50**, under 1% from 3.50-3.90, in a build that had
  already passed gate 1. The frame-exact HARD SWAP is the only free answer: pick a
  timestamp whose 0.01s ramp window contains no k/30 (3.61-3.62 sits between frames 108 at
  3.6000 and 109 at 3.6333), switch the outgoing off and the incoming on there, and carry
  the motion with a scale-only tween. Verified frame-by-frame: 108 is the last card frame,
  109 the first catalog frame, and gate 1 never sees both because the ramp is off its 0.5s
  grid.
- [hermes_counter] **LAW 11 applies to a counter's WHOLE trajectory, and both obvious
  timings are lies.** Beat 4's odometer rolled 0 -> 6 -> 12 in two tweens while its twelve
  logos arrived in two cascades: at t=42.30 the screen read "6 MCP SERVERS CONNECTED"
  beside ONE landed tile, two mid-pop and three empty slots. Rolling to 6 only after six
  had landed just swaps it for the mirror lie (0 beside four tiles, the hackers_counter
  defect). The honest form is **one tick per named object** — 13 odometer values, a roll at
  `tile_t + 0.14` (back.out(2.2) is past 1.0 at p=0.33, so the plate is painted before the
  number that counts it moves) — with the tile stagger widened 0.06 -> **0.10** because
  consecutive `odo_to` fromTos on one target fight for the same `y` if they overlap.
  Verified with a Playwright probe comparing the visible digit to the count of tiles at
  opacity >= 0.75 at 15 timestamps: the counter never leads, and trails by at most 0.14s.
- [gate3] **A `highlight_match` verdict is CHECKABLE ARITHMETIC on the source asset, not a
  judgement call.** Round 1 failed with "Highlight box outlines the wrong sentence instead
  of 'near infinite number'". PIL row-profiling of the 1000x356 tweet crop puts line 1's
  ink at rows 164-198 and line 2's at 211-245; the ring band ran 149-245, so its lower half
  sat on "MCP and plugin tools with high accuracy. You save a" — the opening of the MONEY
  sentence he never says. The judge was right. Ringing line 1 only (band 152-208) passed
  round 2 with zero errors of either kind. **Before filing a highlight verdict as noise,
  row-profile the raster and convert the ring's design rect into source rows** — it costs
  one PIL call and it decides the question.
- [hermes_counter] **Composition balance is the residual defect class, and a clean ink
  sweep is not evidence against it.** Three of five sections opened with their partial cast
  pinned to the top edge — beat 1 for 3.4s (~50% of the zone empty), beat 3 for **6.3s**
  (74% empty), beat 4 for 1.58s (85% empty) — while gate 1 was 0 errors / 0 warnings and
  the pixel sweep was clean at all three. Nothing is blank and nothing collides, so no gate
  can report it. Fixes, all wrapper-free: rides for beats 1 and 3 (`tl.set(sel,{y:dy},0)` +
  `fromTo(...,immediateRender:false)` on a comma-joined selector, caused by an arriving
  element), and the grid's own dashed skeleton for beat 4.
- [hermes_counter] **A group ride creates a scheduling constraint the ledger states only
  half of.** Beyond "no member may have an entrance on the move's axis": the SIBLING that
  motivates the move must land after the move COMPLETES. Beat 3's row 2 was cued on "picky"
  (26.30) — the same instant the ride starts — which would have dropped it into the space a
  still-travelling atom occupied. Retiming it to "things" (26.88), 0.16s after the ride
  ends at 26.72, costs nothing: the transcript almost always offers a later word.
- [hermes_counter] **An empty meter track at `rgba(17,17,17,0.10)` is why "scoreboard at
  zero" openings read as blank cream.** The factory keeps prescribing that opening and then

- [hermes_counter] **The tweet-band white-fraction probe must use a frame-INDEX select.**
  `ffmpeg -ss` is not frame-exact, so a seek-based measurement of a hard swap is wrong by up

- [gate1] **Write the tween-selector guard before the first render, and split the

  also overshoots the box.** Run 4 struck `YOU` (beat 2) and `COPY / PASTE` (beat 4) with
  two full-width strokes: at phone size both words are unreadable, and because an X spans

  first half on a diagram node; this is the second lane, and the fix is the same —
  **ghost the box to 0.42 and ride a rounded-square ✕ badge on its top-right corner**

  atoms and two permanently-opaque wrappers leave the generator entirely.

  PIXELS.** The inherited `TWEET_CLAIM = (0.0357, 0.4825, 0.8776, 0.2902)` came from "a
  printed coordinate grid over the SOURCE"; measured on the staged 980x286 crop the claim's

  Recipe: threshold the raster, print the dark-row runs and ink columns, and author the box
  in raster px with explicit padding (12/12/12/6 here — the bottom pad has to clear the
  byline 13 rows below the claim's descenders).

  BOTH connectors terminate on (the class meatwrapper_diagram logged for this same video;

  nothing moves at all. Author the offset as `dy = ROW_PREV - ROW_FINAL` rather than as

## Run 5 (impeccable) — productivity / checklist (2026-08-10)

- [productivity_checklist] **A generator lineage lets ONE component drift, and nobody sees it
  because every beat looks fine on its own.** The run-3 -> run-4 fork shipped the SAME
  checklist row at four sizes (h 76/66/62/64, box 38/34/34/36, label 40/27/25/30) across six
  beats plus a fifth variant in the outro. Gate 1 cannot see it (each row is legal geometry),
  gate 3 cannot see it (each frame is fine), and gate 2 only shows it if you put two frames
  side by side. **Collapsing to ONE list row (h 64 / box 34 / label 27, pitch 82) plus ONE
  deliberate hero row is only safe if you measure**: all 12 row labels are measured in
  headless Chromium at the real `.lbl` letter-spacing (-1.5px at 100px) and asserted against
  the card's available width at build time. Tightest: "16,000 CLIENTS CHECKED" at 331.3 of
  380 design px, which an advance estimate would have called at ~374 and shipped clipped.
- [productivity_checklist] **The fix for a beat that owns the zone alone as a top strip is to
  AUTHOR IT CENTRED and move on a word, but the trigger word must come BEFORE the arrival.**

  each at the band centre (design y 44..402, centre 223) and stepping to the final layout on
  "actually" / "running" / "just" — one `tl.set` + one `fromTo` on a comma-joined selector,
  no DOM wrapper — fixes all three. **The non-obvious half: if the move fires on the SAME word
  that brings the incoming element, the outgoing block travels through the space the new
  element is landing in.** Firing 0.3-0.8s earlier, on the preceding word, means the
  composition is settled before anything arrives, and it reads as making room rather than
  being pushed.

  crosses the band where the incoming element lands.** Beat 3's plate would have to pass

  that cost nothing: lower the whole beat by 26 design px AND enlarge the plate 84 -> 108

  is a legitimate answer to a sparse frame when the extra ink is the beat's own subject.**
- [productivity_checklist] **A highlight must hug what EXISTS, not what will exist.** The
  run-4 price ring was 472 design px wide around a 332px number and 160px tall while

- [productivity_checklist] **A ring must ride a make-room move on the SAME timestamp and the
  SAME duration as its target.** The ring positions itself with GSAP x/y, so it cannot be a
  member of the group's y-tween (two tweens writing y). Emitting a `ring_jump` to the

- [threed_kinetic] **A ring's bottom stroke landing on its own caption is a whole

  bottom of 360. `isRing` elements are collision-exempt, so gate 1 is structurally

  the run-4 render with both in place. **Rule worth making a chassis default: a

  below the RING, not below the figure.**

  finding was about horizontal centroid; the same generator family top-ANCHORS every

  state in the short — authored at its FINAL height with the bottom 40% empty.
  Working threshold after doing both: **>4s of a held partial state → author it on
  the zone's vertical axis and step it up in ONE motivated tween as the element that
  needs the room arrives; <=2s → leave it top-anchored and spend the effort on the
  beat's dashed skeleton instead.** The step-up costs one `tl.to` on a comma

  at those sizes. Solve the spacing from that arithmetic and the audit never sees it.
- [threed_kinetic] **Poppins 800 caps occupy 0.175em–0.875em of their line box, so

  looked evenly spaced in code and read as a hierarchy inversion on screen: the two
  lines of ONE sentence sat 50.4 optical units apart while the theme mark above them

## Run 5 (impeccable) — slop / kinetic (2026-08-10)

- [slop_kinetic] **The factory has been guessing its own cap heights, and one
  20-line probe ends it.** `gen/_probe_slop_kinetic.py` renders each register at a
  known size and reads the painted rows back: **Poppins 800 caps = 0.149-0.880em**
  (the run-4 comments say 0.26-0.98em), Instrument Serif italic = 0.048-1.019em,
  JetBrains Mono gloss = 0.453-1.200em, tracked `.kick` = 0.272-1.029em. The
  consequence is not academic: run 4's `STRIKE_R = 0.62` put the FERRARI bar's
  centre at 0.641em when the true glyph middle is **0.515em**, so on the shipped
  render the strike crossed the word at 70% of its height. Solve it as
  `cap_mid - RULE_H/2` and the constant disappears. Every lane that positions a
  bar, an icon or a small label against a big word is exposed to this.
- [slop_kinetic] **A text line's DOM Range box is the FONT'S EM BOX, not its line
  box — measured per register, so leading has a hard floor.** On this stack:
  Poppins **-0.19 .. +1.21em** of its layout top (h = 1.40em, at line-height 1.04),
  Instrument Serif -0.20 .. +1.10, JetBrains Mono 0.00 .. +1.33. Since
  `geometry_audit` collides text on that box with a 20%-of-the-smaller tolerance,
  two display lines set 30 design units apart (56px of clean air between the
  visible glyphs) overlap **35%** and are a build-blocking ERROR. The honest fix is
  to put the tolerance INTO the layout maths:
  `gap = max(scale_step, bleed_below(up) + bleed_above(down) - 0.16*min(em_box))`.
  For a 52-over-116 pair that floor is **44.9 units**; it explains why run 4's
  hand-set 47.5 passed and a "cleaner" 30 does not.
- [slop_kinetic] **`geometry_audit`'s thin-bar exemption is what fixes the rule
  thickness.** `thin_bar()` exempts a bar from the collision law only while its
  short side is <= **14px**. A proportional rule (0.072em) would draw SLOP's
  underline at 15.7px, which promotes it to a solid and makes the FERRARI strike
  collide with its own word. So the design system gets ONE `RULE_H = 7.0` design
  units (13.1px) with radius h/2 — a token set by the tool, not by taste.
- [slop_kinetic] **A y-ENTRANCE inside a group that carries a parked y offset
  silently cancels it.** The now-standard "author at final coordinates, park at an
  offset, step home" idiom breaks the moment one member enters with `rise()`:
  its tween ends at `y:0`, so that line drops onto its neighbour while the rest of
  the group stays parked (beat 4's "yourself first" printed straight through
  UPSKILL at 31.6s — 0 geometry errors, invisible to frame_review, caught only on
  a still). Rule: **every atom in a step group enters on scale, opacity or x.**
  Guard it — and note the trap in the guard itself: **"opacity:" ends in "y:"**, so
  a substring test flags every entrance in the file. Match `(?:^|,)\s*y:`.
- [slop_kinetic] **A parked group STANDS IN the space its own incoming rows will
  occupy, so the step must be keyed to the FIRST arrival.** Keying beat 5's step to
  the middle row (so the intermediate states would be less off-centre) put the
  parked METRICS exactly where KPIS lands: a still at 45.2s shows KPIS printed
  through it. The parked state is only safe while nothing else is painted in the
  space it borrows.
- [slop_kinetic] **Step lead is arithmetic.** `SOFT` = power3.out, so a mover has
  covered `1-(1-lead/d)^3` when the incoming element starts painting: **0.10/0.32
  leaves 32% outstanding** (2.9 design units of clearance on an 83-unit park), while
  **0.20/0.36 leaves 8.8%** (22 units). The run-4 note "key the step ~0.10s before"
  is only safe for small parks; scale the lead with the distance.
- [slop_kinetic] **Vertical rhythm, stated as one function.** Ten held
  compositions had optical centres scattered from design y150 to y247 in a field
  whose centre is 214 (0..429, the caption pill's painted top). `stack()` sums the
  VISIBLE glyph bands, adds the gaps and solves for the tops; the residual on the
  delivered render is under 5 design units everywhere. Pair it with `left_for()`
  (block width from the widest atom) and a left-aligned block keeps its editorial
  rail while sitting centred in the frame — which is what STANDARD law 7 asks for
  and what run 4's hard `RAIL = 64` was breaking on beats 4 and 5.
- [slop_kinetic] **Proximity inversion is a real, recurring defect class in icon
  rows.** Run 4 put 22.8 units between a row's word and its OWN gloss and only 15.8
  between that gloss and the NEXT row's word, so every gloss read as belonging to
  the row below. TIGHT(16) inside / STEP(30) between fixes it — and 16 is also the
  floor the em boxes allow, so it is the tightest honest value.
- [gate2] **Headless-Chromium stills that seek the same page repeatedly can retain
  a 1px stale column from the previous seek.** A cream 1x20px sliver appeared at
  x=746 (exactly the previous frame's UPSKILL right edge) in a screenshot whose DOM
  had nothing within 300px of it; re-shooting that one time on a fresh page gave a
  clean frame. Verify a suspicious sliver before rebuilding a generator over it.
- [slop_kinetic] **The impeccable pass found seven defects in a short that had
  already cleared all three gates twice** — a highlight ring cutting through the
  line it highlighted (run 4's ring ended at 0.775 of the card, body line 2 runs to
  0.791), a strike 22px below the optical middle, four underlines floating 70-140px
  under their words, a grey Poppins "kicker" that was the widest and second-loudest
  element in its beat, two left-pinned blocks leaving the right third empty, the
  gloss proximity inversion, and ten off-axis compositions. **None is
  machine-checkable**: geometry_audit measures boxes, frame_review reads 3fps
  states, Gemini passed all of it. The only detector is full-resolution screenshots
  of the paused timeline, read as a contact sheet, before and after every edit.
- [slop_kinetic] Final numbers: geometry 2 rounds (1 error -> 0 errors / 0
  warnings), 58 real atoms across 6 `.tz` sections (17/3/4/12/18/4, zero wrappers),

- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **A ring around a node that CONNECTORS TERMINATE ON and a ring
  around an ALREADY-ACCENTED node are the same defect, and this short had one of each.**
  Beat 3 ringed the AI tile 8 units out while both loop arrows land on that tile's left
  edge — the shafts crossed the ring and it read as broken (visible on a pre-render still

  — one doubled outline (still at t=18.4). **Both fixes are the same move**: tween the
  TARGET's own `borderColor` on the cue. It removes an atom, it cannot be crossed, it is
  a single discrete event, and the accent then means exactly one thing. That is now SIX
  lanes on this class (hackers_icon, threed_icon, slop_counter, hermes_diagram,
  grokbuild_diagram, here) — treat any ring drawn outside a bordered or connector-fed box
  as banned, not as a judgement call.
- [gate2] **A ring -> border-tween swap makes `frame_review`'s stillness gaps GROW, and
  that is the fix working, not an event going missing.** hermes_diagram predicted it; this
  build confirms it. Replacing beat 3's ring pop with a 2px border-colour change turned a
  populated stretch into a `[still 4.0s]` marker at 31.7-35.7. Two `ffmpeg -ss` probes
  (33.20 terracotta / 34.90 neutral) settle it in ten seconds. Expect the marker count to
  rise whenever you retire rings.
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **`disp_top()`-style cap-band placement is only half the story:
  budget the RANGE box, judge the CAP band.** Placing the `0%` numeral so its measured cap
  band sat one spacing token below the VALUE ADDED label produced the pass's only geometry
  error (86% collision). Poppins 800 measures fasc 1.05 / fdesc 0.35 = a 1.40em inline box
  against a 1.05 line box, so the DOM Range rect — the thing `geometry_audit` collides on —
  starts **0.175em ABOVE** the layout box while the first painted row is 0.170em BELOW it.
  The two numbers are 0.345em apart (30 design px at fs 86). Place type by the cap band,
  then add the Range overhang to the gap above it.
- [all] **`canvas.measureText` + `fontBoundingBoxAscent/Descent` derives all of it in
  three lines**, so no lane needs to re-measure Poppins by hand:
  `baseline = (lh*fs - (fasc+fdesc)*fs)/2 + fasc*fs`, then `cap_top = baseline - asc*fs`,
  `range_top = baseline - fasc*fs`. Measured here: Poppins 800 fasc 1.05 / fdesc 0.35 /
  cap asc 0.705; JetBrains Mono 500 fasc 1.02 / fdesc 0.30 / cap asc 0.74. Ink widths in
  em: MEAT WRAPPER 7.701, BUILDER 3.921, EVERY DAY 5.367, AI VIDEOS 4.796, BAD OUTPUT
  7.065 (at ls 2.0/15 em). Run 4's accent rules were a hand-picked 200 under a 446.7-unit
  word — a dash, not an underline.
- [all] **`codex-color.png` joins `kimi.png` in the "the artwork ships its own rounded
  background" class**: 640x640, opaque fraction 0.97, opaque at the top edge, first opaque
  pixel on row 3 at x=92 (0.144w) => corner radius ~0.19w. Padded 20% inside a white plate
  it is a rounded box inside a rounded box. Treatment that works on cream AND dark: keep
  the light plate, pad 0.08, and give the `<img>` a CONCENTRIC inner radius
  (`plate_radius - pad`). The pre-flight is two numbers per logo — opaque fraction and a
  top-edge alpha probe — and it takes seconds: openai 0.36 / claude 0.39 / claudecode 0.42
  are transparent artwork and plate normally.
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **The residual defect class after four runs of law-fixing is
  still COMPOSITION, and gate 2 is where you see it.** Three findings on the first render,
  none machine-checkable, none blank, none colliding: HUMAN -> YOU is a complete two-node
  statement for 3.9s and, authored at its final x, hugs the left edge with the right 40%
  of the canvas empty (t=8.0); the beat-4 code plate holds ONE line inside a 296x166 box
  for 3.0s (t=40.0); and the phase A -> B swap ghosted the crossed-out panel THROUGH the
  incoming agent plates for ~7 frames because both compositions occupy the same rect
  (t=46.4). Fixes: centre-then-step, publish the pending CODE LINES as low-alpha slots at
  their exact rects, and shorten the exit to 0.14s against a 0.10s entrance lead.
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **"Publish the container's empty CONTENT SLOTS" works for code,
  and it is the one filler that asserts nothing.** Ghosting `copy()` / `paste()` would put
  words on screen before he says them; two low-alpha BARS at the exact rect of the lines
  that replace them state the panel's shape, make each fill an event, and are
  containment-skipped by gate 1 (identical rects). Panel ink went from a third of the
  plate to a stated three-line block with zero new claims.
- [all] **A wrapper-free group ride must COMPLETE before any connector between its members
  draws.** First attempt keyed the beat-4 ride to the tweet card, which put both loop
  arrows mid-draw while their plates were still travelling. Keying it to `aitoai - 0.52`
  (0.46s, done 0.06s before the first `arrow_in`) fixed the reading and costs nothing —
  and the space the ride opens is exactly what the source card lands in 0.38s later.
- [all] **Two build guards worth ~50 lines that turn two laws into compile errors**, both
  clean on the first build here: a SEAM budget parsing `top:` + (`height:`|`font-size:`)
  out of every `.tz` atom and failing above design y410 (prints "deepest zone ink design
  y=405.7" on every build — the real floor is the caption pill's painted top at 805.2px,
  a constant now measured by ten lanes, NOT the audit's 862.5px seam LINE); and a
  3-consecutive-spoken-word echo scan over the zone HTML with tags collapsed to a
  `zzsepzz` sentinel. Neither exists in any run-3-forked generator by default.
- [all] **A raw `#RRGGBB` in a hand-written tween string kills the build through the id
  self-check** (`tweens target unknown ids: ['DD7259']`) — deepresearch_diagram logged it,
  and it bit again the moment a lane added a `borderColor` tween. Route every colour in a
  tween string through a hex->`rgb()` helper rather than remembering.
- [gate1] **Give `arrow()`'s wrapper an id.** It is the prerequisite for letting a whole
  connector join a comma-selector group move (GSAP re-composes the inline `rotate()`), and
  it also stops two arrows that share an origin from collapsing into ONE audited atom via
  `key_of`'s `sec/cls/x,y` fallback. Zero new findings here: 0 errors / 0 warnings in the
  three audits after the change.
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] **LAW 3 has a timing half nobody had written down: on-screen
  claims that come from the SOURCE must not precede the source.** "REPORTS A BUG" /
  "FIXES IT" are the @steipete card's words (his sentence is "build an AI to AI system"),
  and run 4 landed them 1.1s BEFORE the card appeared — so for 1.1s the short asserted a
  third party's claim as its own. Landing them after the card is up and its claim ringed
  costs one constant and turns them into annotation of visible evidence.
- [meatwrapper_kinetic] Clean close: geometry 5 rounds (baseline 0/0, then 1 error -> 0/0
  x3, the last on the shipped HTML), atom census 84 measured atoms across 5 sections

## Run 5 (impeccable) — slop / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [slop_diagram] **An ungated zero-ink wrapper does not just pollute gate 1's atom set,
  it MASKS blank-frame defects from every ink scan.** `rule_el()` emitted its wrapper with
  no id and no opacity gate, so a 180x6 design-px zero-ink box was a live, static,
  MEASURED direct child of tz-b1 for the whole beat (and a second in tz-b2). Gate 1 let it
  through on a technicality — a `.rule` child makes an atom collision-exempt, and the
  `.eqline` bar is saved instead by the thin-bar test — so run 4 never saw it. The real
  cost was elsewhere: every blank/ink sweep counts PAINTED ATOMS, and a wrapper at
  opacity 1 counts. The moment I gated it (mirroring `arrow_in`/`arrow_out` with
  `rule_in`/`rule_out`), a genuine zero-atom render frame appeared at t=13.90 — the
  funnel→services handover, present in the shipped run-4 mp4, invisible to four passes of
  scanning. **Any atom your scans count must be an atom the viewer can see.**
- [slop_diagram] **Composition balance needs a HELD-COMPOSITION census, not a frame scan.**
  Group a 0.05s timeline sweep into windows where the painted atom SET is stable for
  >= 0.45s, and print each window's ink bbox, optical centre and fill fraction beside its
  still. On a short with 0 geometry errors, 0 warnings and a first-call Gemini pass, nine
  held compositions sat 45-112 real px above the zone's optical axis for 0.75-5.4s each
  (worst: design y96 against an axis of y217). None of that is machine-checkable by any
  existing gate and all of it is obvious in one table. The zone's usable band is design
  y24 (frame margin) → y410 (ink floor), so the axis is y217; a `block_top(ink_h)` helper
  does the arithmetic once. After the pass, 30 of 35 held compositions land within 5px.
- [slop_diagram] **A diagram that grows rank by rank needs ONE stage-move stop PER RANK.**
  Run 4 already knew to author a lone node centred and ride it up; it applied a single
  move and dropped the tree to its FINAL position the instant the first child arrived, so
  the 2-rank tree then sat in the top 54% of the zone for 5.4s. One move just relocates
  the imbalance from the start of the beat to its middle. `stagemove(sels, y0, [(t,y,d),
  ...])` — comma-joined GSAP selector, no DOM wrapper, every atom stays a direct section
  child — and each stop is CAUSED by the rank that arrives. Five beats here; the
  precondition is unchanged (no atom in the group may carry a y-based entrance).
- [slop_diagram] **GSAP handles `y` on a wrapper that already carries `transform:rotate()`
  with `transform-origin:left center`.** Four of the five stage moves carry arrow wrappers
  (including 90° ones) and the measured rects are correct before, during and after every
  move. Worth knowing, because the alternative — excluding connectors from a group move —
  breaks the geometry of the thing you are moving.
- [slop_diagram] **geometry_audit measures an unpainted text atom by its RANGE box, and
  Poppins' ascent+descent is ~1.35em against `.disp`'s line-height of 1.05** — so ~0.15em
  of invisible leading hangs off EACH side. Re-centring the beat-2 equation put the `+`
  operator 6% into the operand node below it (round-1 ERROR) while the font boxes cleared
  by 4px. Budget an operator gap that holds `1.35 * font-size` and position the glyph by
  its Range box: `top = gapTop + (gap - 1.35*fs)/2 + (1.35 - 1.05)*fs/2`. Same family as
  the run-4 `slop_counter` note about display numerals, generalised to both sides.
- [slop_diagram] **Law 7's "same-theme cards = same size" is NOT enforced by gate 1** when
  the cards carry different className strings, or when fewer than 3 share one: the three
  TERMS of one equation were 76 / 76 / 82 design px and audited clean for three passes
  (`f1`/`f3` are `abs node od hero`, `f2` is `abs node od dash` → two 2-member groups,
  both skipped by `len(g) < 3`). Same-rank sizing has to be a generator invariant. Same
  for the two logo plates (96 vs 92) and the two pipeline stages (76 vs 80) in one beat.
- [slop_diagram] **The cheapest real defect the spacing pass found: SIX design px** (11 on
  screen) between adjacent nodes in the beat-4 control row, in a short that used 40
  between the tree's columns. "Nothing touches anything" was holding by luck. One
  `COLGAP` constant for every sibling row, with the outer margin falling out of the
  arithmetic, fixes it and reads better at phone size.
- [gate2] **`frame_review`'s `f_MMSS_mmm` filename can lag the actual sampled frame by
  ~4 frames (0.13s).** A faint READERS node in `f_0007_666` looked like a BUILD ORDER
  violation against a 7.78 cue; exact-decode measurement (`select='between(n,222,240)'`
  plus per-frame ink inside the element's own rect) shows 0.0000 through frame 233
  (7.767) and first ink at frame 234 (7.800) — exactly on cue. Adjudicate build-order
  questions by frame index, never by the manifest label.
- [impeccable] **Run it in the PRODUCT register and drop every default that fights
  STANDARD.md** — no system fonts, no 1.125 type scale, no 150-250ms motion cap, no
  Restrained-palette reduction of the terracotta accent. What paid: composition balance
  (nine top-pinned beats), spacing rhythm (ten arbitrary gap values → one 4-step scale),
  shape consistency (three same-rank size breaks), consistency of affordance (three beats
  opened on a bare node while three opened on a dashed skeleton) and accent discipline
  (one content label in terracotta was making the law-5 highlight unreadable as an event).
- [impeccable] **A composition pass changes what your instruments can see, so re-run them
  after it, not just before.** Two of this build's defects were CREATED by the pass:
  re-centring the equation moved the `+` into the operand node (gate 1, round 1), and
  gating the phantom wrapper exposed a blank handover frame that the phantom had been
  hiding. Both are cheap; both would have shipped if the probes had only run up front.
- [slop_diagram] Where the measurements overruled the tidier composition: the services
  beat "wants" to open on all three shapes at once, but that leaves a dashed slot waiting
  2.94s, over the factory's measured 2.4s slot-then-fill ceiling. Hanging it on the word
  "AI" at 14.64 gives a 2.16s wait and shrinks the lopsided window from 1.35s to 0.65s.
- [slop_diagram] Numbers for the record: geometry 3 rounds (0e/1e/0e; final 0 errors,

  tz-outro 9, peak 16 simultaneous and ZERO null-id atoms; build-time guards 207 ids with
  0 duplicates, 132 tween selectors all resolving, deepest authored ink design y408.0,
  0 caption trigrams; 1243 pre-render ink samples at 0.05s with 0 zero-atom windows;
  1 render; 0 of 1863 frames under 0.4% top-zone ink (min 0.92%, crop 1080x790); caption
  band blank only in the 8 frames before the first spoken word; tweet on screen 2.63s with
  a frame-exact exit; deepest painted ink 764.6px against a pill top of 805.2px = 40.6px

## Run 5 (impeccable) — productivity / counter (2026-08-10)

- [productivity_counter] **A tweened highlight JUMP between adjacent targets is a GATE-3
  failure, not just a manifest artefact.** Run 4's learning was "never file a highlight
  collision off a 3fps frame, probe the rest position first" — true, and it hid the other
  half of the story. Gemini failed this short at round 1 with *"the red highlight bounding
  box for Codex is misaligned and overlaps the adjacent Grok Build icon"*, and the full-res
  probes CONFIRMED it: concentric on Grok at 30.00, concentric on Codex at 30.90, but at
  30.55 the travelling box straddles a 36-unit gap and cuts the Codex plate's left edge for
  ~0.4s. hackers_counter's `hlmove()` (fade out 0.14s → `set` the new rect at +0.15 → fade
  in 0.26s, fully visible at +0.42 exactly where the jump landed) fixes it in both lanes.
  **Rule: `jump()` is only legal across empty canvas. Stacked scoreboard rows and a tool
  row are both "adjacent".** Ring rest positions are still innocent until probed; the
  TRAVEL is the thing that is guilty.
- [productivity_counter] **hlmove() guarantees exactly ONE ringless frame per hop in a 3fps
  manifest, and that frame is the fix working.** t=29.333 shows no highlight anywhere;
  probes at 29.10 and 29.60 show it concentric on Claude Code and then on Grok Build. Do
  not reopen this as a dropped highlight.
- [productivity_counter] **An odometer's roll CADENCE is a claim-sync surface.** Round 2
  failed with two `claim_sync` errors ("displays 60% while speaker says 90%", "displays
  11,000 while speaker says 16,000"). Both counters DO land on the spoken value inside its
  phrase — the defect is the WINDOW: run 4's 0.24s spacing × 3 steps left 0.80s of
  unspoken intermediates for a ~1fps judge to photograph. Tokenising the cadence
  (`ROLL_STEP = ROLL_D = 0.15`, chain starts 0.02s BEFORE the anchor word, lands 0.43s
  after) halves it and passed. **Step must be >= duration or consecutive `roll()` tweens
  override each other mid-flight.** Every Counter & Meter short with a 3+ step odometer is
  exposed to this.
- [productivity_counter] **A beat that OWNS THE ZONE ALONE before it is joined needs a
  composition for that state — this is the biggest visible run-4 → run-5 delta and no gate
  reports any of it.** Four of six beats authored their layout for the final crowded state
  and then held it top-anchored while the rest of the canvas sat empty: beat 4's tool row
  5.5s with the bottom half empty, beat 6's card pair 9.7s, beat 5's single statement 3.3s
  plus 1.3s of a lone kicker, beat 2's post-photo strip. Two fixes, both already in the
  factory's vocabulary: (a) author at the final position, `tl.set` a `y` offset at 0 and
  tween it to 0 on a discrete spoken event (shape preserved → one comma-joined selector);
  (b) put the missing half on the canvas as a DASHED SLOT of the exact box + radius. Gate 1
  is 0/0 either way and `frame_review` scores the empty half as confirmed stillness.
- [productivity_counter] **The dashed slot is the cheapest answer to "this beat is
  two-thirds empty", including for rows.** Beat 3's three stats are spoken 5.6s apart; three
  dashed RAILS at the beat open make it a scoreboard from frame one without printing a
  single unspoken word (BUILD ORDER is intact: the rails are the silhouette the content
  lands in, exactly like beat 4's tool slots). Bonus: size the highlight band to the rail
  and a row's rail LIGHTING UP *is* the ring — one shape, two states.
- [productivity_counter] **A light rule drawn over a meter fill is a hole in the bar.** Run
  4 marked 30% on a full terracotta track with a 3px CREAM divider; it reads as a gap, the
  same defect class as fablevssol_counter's white ticks on cream. Fix: two SEGMENTS that
  tile the track (muted slice + terracotta remainder), square where they meet, rounded at
  the track's own ends — `border-radius: R 0 0 R` / `0 R R 0`. METERS COMPLETE still holds
  because the two segments cover the track exactly, and the comparison becomes the shape.
- [productivity_counter] **"Same conceptual weight gets the same visual weight" is the
  lens that finds repeated-component drift.** Beat 3's three stat rows were three different
  components: icons 84/46/46, numbers 50/44/44 starting at x=176 vs x=134, labels under the
  numbers, highlight bands 500 vs 400 wide. One `statrow()` on a real grid (icon column at
  the content margin, name column, RIGHT-ALIGNED number column ending on the same margin)
  makes one honest 460-unit band correct for all three — an identical-width highlight is
  only honest when the content actually spans both margins.
- [productivity_counter] **A right-aligned number column is what makes a scoreboard read as
  a table.** Left-aligning "10" / "40" / "16,000" after a name of variable length gives a
  ragged numeric edge and forces per-row highlight widths; right-aligning them to the
  content margin fixes both, and `align="right"` on the existing `odometer()` is the whole
  change.
- [productivity_counter] **`seg_ring()`'s segment weight must derive from its diameter.**
  Run 4 hardcoded 6.5 × 17, which only works at one size and is precisely why the gauge
  could not join an icon column. `sw = 0.077d, sh = 0.202d` reproduces run 4's look at d=84
  and still reads at d=48.
- [productivity_counter] **A per-atom re-lay needs one formula, not eyeballed offsets.**
  With transform-origin at the element centre, `x = L2 - L + W(S-1)/2` and
  `y = T2 - T + H(S-1)/2` places any authored rect exactly on any target rect at any scale.
  Wrapped in a `relay(sel, authored, target, t)` helper it is 3 lines per atom, keeps every
  atom a direct section child (gate 1 still measures it), and a 0.50s move placed off the
  audit's 0.5s sample grid is never static enough to be flagged.
- [productivity_counter] **impeccable's absolute bans overlap our laws less than expected,
  but where they do they are sharper.** "Nested cards are always wrong" is FILL THE SHAPE
  restated, and it found the check/cross plates inside the beat-5 cards that survived run 3
  AND run 4. Its "no restated headings" cut DAILY from the outro kicker once the meter under
  it said 7 DAYS A WEEK. Its motion restraint took the short from 13 highlight events to 9
  by noticing that a drawn strike-through, a tint fill and a card's own entrance were
  already carrying the emphasis a ring was being added to repeat.
- [productivity_counter] **The outro bar is the easiest place in the factory to ship pure
  decoration.** A full-width terracotta rule that animates to 100% under FOLLOW carries no
  data — in the Counter lane that is a broken chart wearing a divider's clothes. Seven
  discrete cells that fill on "each and every single day", labelled 7 DAYS A WEEK, restate
  the spoken line, satisfy METERS COMPLETE and are FILL THE SHAPE-clean (each cell is its
  own shape and fills completely, unlike ticks cut into one track).
- [productivity_counter] Numbers for the record: forked RUN 4 (stated in the paperwork);
  geometry 7 rounds, all 0 errors / 0 warnings; 81 distinct atom ids across 7 sections
  (8/11/17/17/8/12/8, zero nulls, zero wrappers) from a 1242-sample 0.05s sweep; a live
  `.tz` clip at every one of those samples (19 show 2 = the designed 0.15s handoffs, never
  0); 0 blank samples inside the composition; deepest painted ink 767.3px against a
  measured pill top of 805.2px = 37.9px clearance (**ninth** confirmation of that
  constant); 6 renders; 63 distinct states from 186 samples, 0 idle candidates, longest
  hold 3.3s (both 3.3s gaps probed and shown to contain real events the 16x16 dedup cannot
  see: the BETTER TOOLS strike at 39.9 and the THIS YEAR label at 51.5); 10 frames read;
  QC v3 pass on round 3 with 0 visual, 0 semantic and 0 minor notes; generator re-run and
  diffed byte-identical against the shipped index.html.

## Run 5 (impeccable) — threed / icon (2026-08-10)

- [threed_icon] **A pre-render STILL SHEET is the cheapest gate in the factory and it
  sits before gate 1's cousin, not after it.** 45 Playwright screenshots of the real
  timeline (~2 min, zero API cost, `_stills_threed_icon.py`) found four defects on a
  build that was already 0 errors / 0 warnings: an invisible label, 7.8s of a
  top-pinned row on empty canvas, a 6.5s empty browser box, and a highlight ring that
  cut through the head of the figure it annotated. Each one would otherwise have cost
  a render plus a gate-2 round to discover. Shoot stills BEFORE the first render, not
  after the first failure.
- [threed_icon] **A helper whose only tween is `settle()` must be created
  `hide=False`, and nothing in the guard chain will tell you otherwise.** `settle()`
  animates scale, never opacity, so a `caption(...)` left on its `hide=True` default
  renders at opacity 0 forever. `check_ids` passes (the id exists, the tween resolves),
  the echo guard passes (the text IS in the html), the seam guard passes, and gate 1
  skips it because `effOpacity < 0.15`. The beat-3 "2D" label was invisible in the
  first build and only a still showed it. If your generator has both a `hide` default
  and a scale-only entrance, assert the pairing at build time.
- [threed_icon] **Read the anchor's FIRST word before disputing a cue.**
  `find("we create applications")` returns 34.20 ("we"), not 34.42 ("create"). A
  measured frame showed a group move "firing 0.26s early"; it was firing exactly on
  time and my mental model of the anchor was wrong. Measuring the render (ffmpeg +
  numpy on the tile's white rows, 9 timestamps) settled it in one call — do that
  before touching a generator that the audit says is clean.
- [threed_icon] **`CONNECTOR_END_TOL` is 14 PIXELS, so the design-unit ceiling for a
  connector's stand-off is 7 (13.1px), not 8 (15px).** One design unit is the whole
  floating-connector warning class on this chassis. Run 4's `+7` was not luck.
- [threed_icon] **When no annotation shape can mark a target without crossing its
  host, the emphasis belongs to HIERARCHY, not to a better rectangle.** Three runs
  each invented a different wrong ring for "all of the organs of the human body":
  run 3 ringed the heart and its arc grazed the lungs; run 4 ringed the torso cluster
  and silently excluded the BRAIN while the line says ALL; run 5's rect around all
  three cut straight through the head, because the brain lives inside it. The fix is
  to dim the body to 0.26 and let the three organs stand alone — which is also
  literally the claim ("shown as 3D models"). Test for this class: if the target set
  is nested inside the host, no ring exists.
- [threed_icon] **The outro is the last place generators still hang events off `t0 +
  offset` instead of spoken words, and it costs the short its thinnest frame.** Run 4's
  `t0+0.34 / +0.86 / +1.20 / +1.52` left three small logo tiles alone on the zone for
  0.34s at the cut (5.25% ink area, the global minimum). Re-anchoring to "Follow" /
  "tutorials" / "news" / "every single day" raised the global minimum to 6.84% and
  improved sync at the same time. Grep your generator for `t0 +` in the outro.
- [threed_icon] **An empty container that IS the subject of the sentence is still an
  empty container.** Run 4 held a 400x214 empty dark browser for 6.5s and filed it as
  "known accepted" on the grounds that it was the subject. Putting the page inside it
  (a hero block + two copy rules, on screen from the beat's first frame) cost three
  elements and turned a box into a claim — and it made the NEXT event legible, because
  "a 3D video behind" can now slide out from behind something.
- [threed_icon] **`seam_guard` cannot see chips: their font-size lives on the inner
  span.** hermes_icon logged the gap; the fix is a second regex pass keyed on
  `style="...top:..."><span class="chip|ctchip" ...font-size:Npx`, with
  `height = fs*1.35 + 2*pad` (pad 6 for `.chip`, 9 for `.ctchip`). Verified against the
  live DOM: estimated deepest ink 399.0 vs measured 399.0.
- [threed_icon] **DOM ink-area and pixel ink disagree in BOTH directions, so neither is
  a dead-frame detector alone.** A white tile at opacity 0.8 on cream scores ~7.7% DOM
  ink area and 0.26% pixel ink; a bare highlight ring scores 0% DOM ink area and a few
  hundredths of a percent in pixels. Use DOM ink-area (pre-render, 0.05s grid) to find
  windows with no COMPOSITION, and the pixel scan (post-render) to find frames with no
  PAINT. This build: 0 windows below 3% DOM ink area in 1597 samples, 0 fully blank
  frames in 2395, and the 12 lowest pixel frames were all adjudicated cream compositions.
- [gate2] **Second confirmation that the 16x16 dedup can swallow a genuine BUILD, not

## Run 5 build — productivity / icon (2026-08-10, impeccable pass)

- [productivity_icon] **`z-index` on a top-zone atom paints it OVER the NEXT beat,
  and run 3 AND run 4 both shipped it.** The beat-1 strike bar carried
  `z-index:6`. `.clip` sections are `position:absolute` with `z-index:auto`, so
  they open NO stacking context — the bar was promoted into the ROOT stacking
  order and painted straight across the beat-2 case-study card for the whole
  0.15s section overlap (measured on the render at t=5.467 and 5.500, a terracotta
  rule through "tavily + Fieldway"). Gate 1 measures rects and has no opinion
  about paint order; Gemini passed it twice. DOM order inside a section already
  puts a later sibling on top, so the property was never needed. **Standing check
  worth one grep per generator: `grep -n "z-index" gen/*.py` — any z-index on a
  section child is a cross-beat bleed waiting for the next overlap.**
- [productivity_icon] **A travelling ring passes THROUGH the plate it is
  travelling toward, and the fix is paint order, not choreography.** The tile
  scramble Miguel called "chef's kiss" is a same-row same-size travel, and the
  run-4 note justified keeping it because "the ring is wider than a tile so it
  crosses the gaps, never a mark". That arithmetic does not hold on a 3-tile row:
  ring 120 wide, tile 96, gutter 40 — mid-flight BOTH vertical borders sit on
  tiles, and a full-resolution crop at 29.467 shows the border cutting the Grok
  plate. **Emitting the ring BEFORE the tiles (so it paints behind them) keeps the
  scramble and deletes the defect**: mid-travel only the ring's top and bottom
  arcs show in the gutter, and at rest the ring is RING_PAD clear of every tile so
  nothing occludes it. Cheaper than converting the travel to a swap, and it keeps
  the move Miguel praised.
- [productivity_icon] **LAW 5 is about where a ring LANDS, and with a travelling
  ring the landing is `t_start + duration`.** The run-4 rule ("t_in AFTER the
  target's entrance completes") was written for `hlswap`, where t_in IS the
  landing. Applying the same 0.42s lag to an `hljump` with a 0.42s travel put the
  ring on the Claude Code tile while the caption pill read "Groq Build," — a
  0.84s window, half of it wrong. Working arithmetic: `lag + travel == the
  target's entrance duration` (0.16 + 0.26 = 0.42 against a 0.40s `popo`), which
  lands the ring on a settled target inside its own spoken phrase.
- [impeccable] **polish.md's design-system DISCOVERY step is worth more than every
  other part of the skill on this chassis, and the reason is that it forces a
  CENSUS.** Listing this short's font sizes, ring pads, corner radii and centre
  axes side by side turned four vague impressions into four missing tokens: 21
  font sizes with no ratio, four ring pads (8/10/11/12, including one ring with 8
  above its target and 4 below), a flat radius 16 on every ring regardless of what
  it framed, and TWO composition axes (288 and 282) in one short. Each fixed once,
  as a token, instead of per element. Miguel's "if you are going to fill gaps, the
  gaps have to make the shape" is the same complaint arriving from the other side:
  **a ring's corner radius must be `target_radius + pad`**, which is one line and
  retires the whole class.
- [productivity_icon] **A highlight sized to a LAYOUT BOX is the type-lane twin of
  the ring-radius defect.** The 90% ring was 356 units wide around 164 units of
  ink and the price ring 456 around 318 — 54 units of dead air per side against 12
  above, i.e. the ring looked like a panel rather than a highlight. Sizing both to
  MEASURED ink plus one pad is free once a glyph-metrics pass exists, and it is

- [productivity_icon] **Balance a beat for its LONGEST-HELD phase, and check WHICH

## Run 5 (impeccable) — threed / diagram (2026-08-10)

- [threed_diagram] **Both X-strikes in this short crossed the words they struck, and
  all three gates shipped it twice.** The 2D MOCKUP strike put a 3.4px bar through
  "M✕CKUP" and the beat-2 strike put two through "VIDEO FILE" and "FLAT PAGE". Gate 1
  structurally cannot see it (`if a["rotated"] or b["rotated"]: continue` in the
  collision pass), gate 2 keeps the frame but the strike reads as intentional, gate 3
  reads at full resolution where the type still resolves. **Any diagonal drawn ACROSS a
  labelled node is a law-8 defect by construction** — the ghost (0.42) + rounded-square
  ✕ badge riding the corner is the only strike-equivalent that survives a phone screen
  (slop_diagram logged the recipe; this is the second lane to need it).
- [threed_diagram] **`geometry_audit`'s corner-badge exemption forces a badge to sit
  MOSTLY inside its host.** `frac` is the fraction of the BADGE covered by the card and
  the threshold is 0.5, so the visually classic 50/50 corner badge measures 0.25 and
  errors out. Inset by 0.74 of the badge's own size (54.8% covered, ratio 0.13) still
  reads as a corner badge and passes. Same arithmetic sized beat 6's check badges (52.9%).
- [threed_diagram] **A connector that lands on the centre of a 3-tile row lands on the
  MIDDLE TILE.** Run 4's single arrow from AI MODEL to x=288 was geometrically perfect
  (row centre = node centre) and semantically wrong: on screen it reads "AI MODEL ->
  OpenAI" (law 11, factual placement). Fix is the distributor harness — stem off the
  node's bottom edge, one rail spanning the tile CENTRES, one drop per tile. Author the
  rail as a real box (`node bus`, 3 design px tall so it is thin-bar collision-exempt),
  never as a `.rule`, so the stem above it and the drops below it terminate on a genuine
  box edge instead of reporting `floating`.
- [threed_diagram] **A highlight ring drawn a constant 10 design px outside a rounded
  panel is not concentric unless its radius grows by the same 10** — and either way it
  reads as a doubled border at short size AND forces the incoming connector to cross it
  (which HIGHLIGHT DISCIPLINE bans). Animating the panel's OWN `borderColor` to
  terracotta is one element instead of three, deletes the collision, keeps the timing,
  and is the same move deepresearch_diagram landed independently. Use `fromTo` with
  `immediateRender:false` so no build-time from-value paints a highlighted border on
  frame 0 and a direct seek stays deterministic.
- [threed_diagram] **GSAP tween-order trap when one beat needs TWO group moves:**
  `fromTo`'s immediateRender paints from-values at BUILD time in creation order, so a
  second `groupmove` on the same atoms silently overwrites the first one's opening
  offset (the composition starts at the wrong y). Either give every groupmove
  `immediateRender:false` and let a single opening tween own the offset, or author the
  atoms at the LOW position and ride exactly once — which is what beats 1/3/4/6 do here.
- [threed_diagram] **A build-time guard that greps tweens for `"#..."` reads a CSS
  colour literal as a selector.** `borderColor:"#DD7259"` failed the "tweens target
  unknown ids" check. Parse the selector out of each tween's FIRST argument
  (`tl\.\w+\("([^"]+)"`) and split on commas; that keeps comma-joined group selectors
  working and stops colours from being mistaken for ids.
- [factory] **The impeccable pass finds a different defect class than the three gates,
  because it measures COMPOSITION rather than correctness:** ink centroid vs zone
  centre, margin above vs below, icon-to-plate ratio against the short's own family,
  whether a column shares one axis. Four of this item's six beats were authored
  top-hung (2-4x more air below than above, incl. the first 5s of the hook) and every
  gate was green on all of them. A ~40-line numpy pass over pre-render stills
  (bbox + centroid + margins per still) is the cheapest way to see it, and it is what
  made the critique specific enough to fix in constants.
- [factory] **Check when the outro's identity chip FINISHES, not just that it exists.**
  Run 4 completed the "Miguel Torrez AI" chip 0.17s — five frames — before the last
  frame of this short. No law covers it, no gate measures it, and a closing composition
  that resolves after the viewer has gone is wasted. Land the last element ~0.5s before
  the cut (moved both closers one cue earlier here: the chip now holds for 0.57s).
- [factory] **Any ffmpeg rawvideo crop used for an ink scan needs an EVEN height.**
  `crop=1080:795` makes yuv420p emit a garbage bottom row, so every frame "inks" the
  crop's last row and the deepest-inked-row number is meaningless (it reported row 794
  on 1144 frames that are demonstrably clean when the frame is extracted). Use an even
  crop AND require a minimum ink width (>=8px) on the deepest row: a 1-3px hit there is
  compression ringing off the terracotta caption pill sitting just below the crop.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — agentreviews / icon (2026-08-11)

- [asset-audit] **X photo metadata can describe the original while the returned URL
  downloads a smaller derivative.** This post reported 1514x1442, but the first file
  was only 1200x1143 and its judged crop was 1113x844. The generator's first guard
  compared authored CSS width without the 2x 4K root zoom, so it incorrectly approved
  a 1.58x physical upscale. Fetch `name=orig`, probe the saved file, crop without
  downsampling, and include every project/root scale in the physical-pixel assertion.
  The shipped proof is 1405px intrinsic and 1404.375px rendered (0.9996x).
- [cue-binding] **Semantic cue aliases must be audited, not just selector ids.** The CLI
  loop used asset key `claude`, while the timing table called the same cue `cc`; the
  generic fallback quietly assigned Claude the later Codex time. Geometry, duplicate-id,
  selector, and caption checks all passed while the highlight landed on an empty slot.
  Use an explicit asset-key-to-cue-key map and verify every named mark on its encoded
  word-start frame.
- [frame-review] **A clean pre-render still does not replace encoded-state review.** The
  final circuit crossed the small `03` marker only in the encoded closing state, and the
  mistimed Claude tile was also visible only when the spoken cue and rendered frame were
  read together. This pilot needed two full rerenders after static composition was green;
  both defects were found by exact word-time probes and fixed before the shipped encode.
- [pipeline] **`frame_review.py`'s video-id registry must map to full transcript paths,
  not assume every cut lives in `shorts_run1`.** Run 6 added a `TRANSCRIPTS` registry so
  `--video-id agentreviews` resolves its own tight transcript without a one-off CLI path.
  Keep the video id mandatory in paperwork, because it proves claim-sync review used the
  intended transcript rather than an adjacent recording.
- [agentreviews_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 71.979s, 63 butt-joined
  captions, zero audio offset, source proof static for 3.45s at 0.9996x intrinsic, Gate 1
