## Run 6 (impeccable) — erdos / counter (2026-08-11)

- [take-detection] **Not every raw carries the spoken "No." discard marker.** The
  erdos recording is 9 restarts with no verbal kill word at all, so run-6's
  `build_cut.py` marker logic finds nothing. The portable adaptation: key takes on
  the SCRIPTED OPENING (here "A mathematician just ..."), and count a take complete
  only when it reaches the spoken SIGN-OFF ("next video"); last complete opening
  before the final sign-off wins. `build_cut_erdos.py` keeps every other run-6
  contract byte for byte (silence cap, 30fps master, native-4K crops, edl shape).
  Also cap the take end at `source_duration - 0.02`: this sign-off ended 0.34s
  before the recording did, so the stock `+0.45` tail ran past EOF.
- [source] **The URL you are handed may be the QUOTE, not the news.** The approved
  post was @amasad quoting @Qiaoqiao2001's "I solved 6 open Erdős problems in 5
  days". Fetch with `referenced_tweets` + `referenced_tweets.id.author_id`
  expansions or the actual claim never appears in the payload, and the card would
  have credited the wrong handle. Neither post carried media, so the card is coded.
- [law-3] **A coded source card needs a provenance assertion, not just discipline.**
  The generator asserts the on-card quote is byte-identical to the fetched JSON's
  first line and greps the whole composition for metric words (like/repost/view/
  reply/bookmark). That turns "we didn't fake the tweet" from a promise into a
  build failure. The card's own text is then exempted from the Law-4 caption-echo
  scan via a `data-source-quote` marker — otherwise the tweet's "GPT-5.6 Sol"
  legitimately collides with the spoken triple "gpt 5 6".
- [law-5] **A ring that only reaches full opacity 0.08s before its own exit is a
  defect the geometry gate cannot see.** Anchoring the claim ring on "six Erdos
  problems" put its 0.34s fade-in against a fade-out scheduled at reveal-0.22.
  Anchor a highlight on the START of the clause it answers and kill it WITH its
  host, then check the arithmetic: fade_in_end vs fade_out_start is the real
  on-screen window.
- [law-5] **"Ring re-lands on a static asset" and "ring lands inside the spoken
  word" fight each other when the asset is born on that same word.** The search
  glyph and the ring were both cued on "Google++", so the encoded frame at 20.67s
  showed the ring still on the calculator. Fix the ORDER, not the ring: let the
  asset arrive one clause early ("literally just"), so it is settled when the ring
  jumps 0.06s into the naming word.
- [charts] **A trend stroke drawn through column CENTRES cuts the taller columns.**
  Between two centres the segment sits lower than the next column's top edge near
  that column, so an 8-unit offset ran the stroke straight through the last two
  bars' corners. 20 units of clearance on a rising 5-bar staircase clears every
  bar; verify with a rendered frame, not with the endpoint arithmetic alone.
- [asset-judge] **When a post ships no media, judge the CODED card as it will ship.**
  `judge_assets_erdos.py` seeks the real GSAP timeline in headless Chromium, screen-
  shots the card in context plus a 1:1 crop, and hands both to Gemini with the
  narration. That caught nothing this time but it PROVED the Hungarian `ő` in
  "Erdős" renders as a real letter rather than tofu, which no deterministic gate
  checks. Also mind the CDN: the first Chromium launch on this machine can stall
  past a 30s `wait_for_function`; use geometry_audit's bounded evaluate loop.
- [gates] **Concurrent 4K renders did NOT corrupt this one, but verify the face.**
  Another session's grokpublish render started mid-way through the erdos encode.
  HyperFrames' coverage gate passed and full-frame probes at 0.1 / 12 / 24 / 36 /
  46.2s all show a painted face. Probing 5 full frames costs seconds and is the
  cheap proof that the 2026-08-10 blank-clip class did not recur.
- [pipeline] **`qc_v3.py` now resolves transcripts through a `TRANSCRIPTS` registry**
  (run-1 ids still derive from `STEMS`, later runs register their own full path),
  matching what `frame_review.py` already did. Both accept `erdos`.
- [erdos_counter] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 46.315s, 1389 frames, 41

## Run 6 (impeccable) — grokpublish / icon (2026-08-11)

- [intake] **Take detection has a SECOND marker form the ledger never wrote down.**
  `build_cut.py` finds the last spoken "No." and takes everything after it. This raw
  restarts on TRUNCATED WORDS instead — Scribe emits them with a trailing hyphen
  ("Vi-", "N-") or an ellipsis ("As you...") — so the `text == "no"` test matches
  NOTHING and the whole 82s file would have been treated as one take, shipping four
  abandoned openings. Widen the marker test to `norm == "no" OR text endswith
  "-" / "..." / "…"`, then (a) assert the resulting take start against a
  hand-verified constant and (b) re-scan the CHOSEN take for any surviving marker.
  Both guards are three lines and they make a silent 40-second error impossible.
- [sync] **A bilabial strip alone cannot settle sync, because the transcript's word
  start is ambiguous between a stop's CLOSURE and its RELEASE.** On "brand-new" the
  lips CLOSE exactly on the word-start frame and release three frames later, which
  reads as a 100ms video lag if you assume the timestamp marks the burst, and as
  perfect sync if you assume it marks the closure. The whole-video adjudicator that
  settles it: decode a small mouth crop for every frame
  (`crop=340:260:1020:2790,scale=68:52,format=gray` at 4K), take the fraction of
  pixels under 70 as a mouth-openness signal, resample the audio RMS to the same
  frame grid, z-score both and cross-correlate over ±12 frames. Here the curve is
  smooth, unimodal and peaks at **lag 0** (r=0.1031) with monotone falloff either
  side. The absolute r is low because darkness is a crude proxy — read the PEAK, not
  the magnitude. Two decoded arrays, ~40s, no API spend. (A /p/ before an open vowel
  is still the cleanest single-word case: "public." releases exactly on its burst
  cell.)
- [all] **The caption-band scan everybody copies measures the WRONG band on a 4K
  split short.** Cropping "everything below the pill top" includes the FACE video,
  and skin tone plus an orange cap logo score as near-terracotta, so the scan
  reported **0 blank frames on a video that legitimately has 7**. The pill's painted
  top is 1610 at 4K and the face video starts at 1725, so `crop=2160:110:0:1610` is
  the only band where the sole terracotta is the pill. It then returned the true
  answer: 7 pill-free frames, all before the first spoken word at 0.219s.
- [grokpublish_icon] **REJECTING the source post is a legitimate LAW 3 outcome, and
  it deletes three defect classes at once.** The Gemini asset judge ruled the
  rendered @grok card "reject — a source post that merely restates text", which was
  literally true: the post's wording is a near-verbatim restatement of the narration,
  and its one extra fact ("SuperGrok Heavy users") is a source claim Miguel never
  makes. Shipping ZERO third-party assets means the documented gate-3
  tweet-duration noise class cannot fire, there is no attribution to place, and
  there is no upscaled raster to defend under law 8. STANDARD only ever *permits* a
  tweet; it never requires one.
- [asset-judge] **The judge can be confidently WRONG about what an image contains,
  and the refutation is one decoded frame.** It ruled a demo still "use — clearly
  shows the gameplay running inside the app interface"; the frame at that timestamp
  is a white title card reading "Share apps from web", with no interface and no
  gameplay. Extract and LOOK at the frame behind a positive ruling, not only behind
  a rejection. (The measured rejection stands on arithmetic: only ~23% of the
  1920x1080 promo frame carries the phone mockup, so a legible 442x997 crop needs
  1.27x upscaling at any usable size, past the 1.15x ceiling.)
- [grokpublish_icon] **A GROUND FLIP is where cross-cut continuity dies, and no gate
  can see it.** Beat 4 ended with app -> Grok -> browser plus two connectors and a
  lit terracotta address bar; beat 5 re-authored the same three nodes in the same
  seats and silently dropped the connectors AND reset the address bar to grey — two
  elements the viewer had just watched arrive, flipping out on an opaque cut. Gate 1
  measures each section independently, the ink sweep counts area, and the judge
  passed the class in run 3/4/5 shorts. Rule: **when an incoming beat inherits an
  outgoing beat's cast, diff the two sections' atom lists AND their internal states,
  not just their coordinates.** Cheap form: a `hot=True` flag on the shared helper so
  the inherited element is authored in its post-highlight state.
- [grokpublish_icon] **A wrapper-free "absorb" merge must be solved in DISTANCE, not
  duration.** `power3.out` covers 49% of its travel in the first 20% of the tween, so
  a 120-design-unit merge over 0.5s renders sampled frames with both outer nodes at
  ~50% opacity sitting ON TOP of the hub they merge into — the crossfade-mush class,
  arriving through a move instead of a fade. Shortening the duration does not help
  (the ease is the problem). 56 units over 0.34s keeps the movers 17 design units
  clear of the hub plate at the instant they are still 50% visible. Solve
  `distance * (1-(1-p)^3) < gap` at the p where opacity is still readable.
- [grokpublish_icon] **ZERO highlight rings is a viable Icon-lane build, and it is
  the cheapest way to retire six lanes' worth of ring defects.** hackers_icon,
  threed_icon, slop_counter, hermes_diagram, grokbuild_diagram and meatwrapper_icon
  have all logged travelling rings, rings on bordered nodes, or rings crossing
  labels. This short has none: every emphasis is a border or fill tween on its exact
  spoken referent (a card's border on "feature", an address-bar pill on "domain", a
  dashed row's stroke on "future") plus one accent rule under the subject on "Grok".
  Nothing can be drawn over a thing it is not highlighting, and gate 3 passed round 1
  with zero notes. Expected cost, so nobody reports it as a regression: `frame_review`
  keeps FEWER distinct states (37 here), because a 2-3px border change cannot move
  the 16x16 grey signature.
- [factory] **Two sessions editing `pipeline/frame_review.py` and
  `shorts_run3/qc_v3.py` in the same run WILL collide.** A parallel run-6 builder had
  already added its own `TRANSCRIPTS` dict to `qc_v3.py` and rewired the main block
  to use it; inserting mine produced TWO `TRANSCRIPTS = {...}` definitions where the
  second silently shadowed the first, so my video_id would have been unreachable and
  theirs would have been the only one registered. Nothing errors. **Grep for the
  symbol you are about to define before defining it, and re-read a shared pipeline
  file immediately before editing it** — a stale read is how you delete a sibling's
  registration.
- [grokpublish_icon] Clean run for the record: fork base = the run-6
  `agentreviews_icon_gen.py` chassis with grokprice's Grok branding; geometry 3

## Run 6 (impeccable) — langchain / kinetic (2026-08-12)

- [gate1] **Run the geometry audit on the 1080 DESIGN copy, never on the `projects_4k`
  copy.** `zoom:2` doubles every `getBoundingClientRect()` while
  `document.documentElement.clientWidth` stays 1080, so every element is measured at 2x
  against a 1x frame. Auditing the 4K project reported "0 errors, 2 warnings" (b1-ant and
  b1-lc "within 20px of frame edge"); the same HTML on the 1080 copy is **0 errors, 0
  warnings**. Proof: `b1-lc` measures `x=305.6 right=774.4` on the design copy and
  `x=611.2 right=1548.8` on the 4K copy, i.e. 469px past the right edge of a frame it
  never touches. The three sibling run-6 builds all audited `projects/`, which is why
  nobody hit this before. The dangerous direction is the other one: a 2x mismeasurement
  can also MASK a real margin or seam violation.
- [all] **One element, ONE tween per property — a `settle()` stacked on a bespoke scale
  tween silently wins the overlap.** The ant was authored to debut at 1.85x and shrink
  into its seat on "40", but it also kept the chassis' frame-0 `settle` (scale 0.968→1,
  0.46s). Both start at t=0 and both animate `scale`; the settle won. The ENCODE ran the
  hook at scale 0.98 for 0.46s, jumped to 1.85, then shrank — a grow-then-shrink nobody
  designed. Gate 1 passes (it samples static boxes), gate 3 passes, and **the live page at
  t=0.6 looked correct**, so only a measurement of the encoded frames caught it: terracotta
  ink bbox 74.7du at t=0.0-0.4 then 140.8du at t=0.6, against 76.1du at scale 1. Grep each
  atom for how many tweens touch the same property before shipping.
- [all] **`popo` (POP = `back.out(2.2)`) is effectively INVISIBLE for its first ~2 frames,
  because a back ease does its overshoot at the END.** Pairing a 0.12s `power3.out` exit
  with a `popo` entrance 0.10s later left frame 224 (t=7.467s) encoded as **uniform cream**
  — the outgoing block had reached 2% opacity while the incoming card had not started
  painting. The arithmetic that sized the exit assumed the entrance ramps like the exit;
  it does not. Fix the OUTGOING fade (0.12s → 0.22s) rather than moving the incoming
  element off its spoken cue. After: 0 frames under 1% ink, 0 blank, global minimum
  max-channel deviation 44/255.
- [all] **A fixed-delta "dead frame" scan reports BLANK on any frame sampled in a fade
  tail.** Two separate ink metrics called this short blank at 7.43-7.47s; extracting
  t=7.433 showed the complete composition at ~17% opacity (terracotta-on-cream delta 27,
  under a 34/255 bar). Measure ink against **each frame's own modal background** (a
  two-reference cream/dark test scores dark display type on a cream ground as background
  and undercounts every cream section), and report **max-channel deviation** alongside the
  ink fraction — that, not the fraction, is the blank test. Only then did the ONE real
  blank frame (maxdev 7/255) separate from the two fade-tail false positives.
- [sync] **The mouth-openness x audio-RMS cross-correlation adjudicator is NOT reliable on
  bearded footage, and this build could not reproduce its lag-0 anchor.** Miguel's beard is
  dark, so a fixed darkness threshold measures beard rather than mouth aperture. The peak
  moved from **-3 to +6 frames** across crop and threshold choices on the same video, with
  r as low as 0.048 (flat noise). Worse, running grokpublish's own crop/threshold on
  grokpublish's own shipped render gives **lag -3, r=0.068**, not the documented lag 0 —
  so there is no validated zero-reference to calibrate against. Do not ship a sync verdict
  from this method alone.
- [sync] **Use bilabial RELEASE BURST vs LIP RELEASE instead — it is direct, physical and
  cheap.** For each word-initial /p/ or /b/: find the burst acoustically as the peak of
  >3.5kHz energy on a 2ms hop (the transcript timestamp is only a search hint, because a
  stop's word-start is ambiguous between closure and release), find the lip release as the
  frame where mouth openness crosses the midpoint of its local range, and difference them.
  Five events on this short: +1.7 / -19.0 / +14.3 / +5.7 / -48.7 ms, **median +1.7ms
  (+0.05 frames)** — decisively in sync, refuting the -2 frame correlation reading. Also:
  /m/ is a nasal and is NOT a valid bilabial probe (the lips stay closed while voicing
  continues, so there is no burst); and verify the mouth crop by EXTRACTING it first — the
  inherited grokpublish window was mostly beard, chin and neck on this framing.
- [law3] **The metric-word guard must be scoped to the VISUAL ZONE, not the whole page.**
  erdos greps the entire composition for like/repost/view/reply/bookmark, which works only
  while the narration happens to avoid those words. Here Miguel says "just LIKE this AI
  agent", so the whole-page grep failed the build on a CAPTION. Captions are verbatim
  speech and are exempt by law 4's own logic; a metrics row can only ever be drawn in the
  top zone, so the top zone is the correct and complete scope.
- [law4] **The trigram guard cannot see the worst caption echo, because the worst one is a
  BIGRAM alone in the pill.** `BODY WEIGHT` on screen passed the 3-consecutive-word bar,
  but the caption at that exact moment is the two words "body weight," and nothing else —
  literally captions x2, which is the defect law 4 exists to prevent. The machine check is
  necessary and not sufficient: read the caption phrase list against the on-screen term
  list, moment by moment. Fixed to `ITS OWN WEIGHT` (one shared word). A 2-word overlap
  inside a 4-word caption (`AI AGENTS` vs "AI agents handling more") stays fine.
- [type] **A shrunk multiplier needs an optical lift, and the amount is derivable.**
  Poppins 800 draws U+00D7 at nearly digit width and full digit weight, so `40×` reads as
  "40 X"; dropping it to 0.62em fixes the hierarchy but drops its centre **0.086em of the
  parent** below the digits' cap-band middle, because the glyph is centred on the math axis
  of its OWN em box. `position:relative;top:-0.14em` on the span restores it and, being
  relative, does not change the measured lockup width. Measure the composed MARKUP, not
  the plain string, or the centring is wrong by the size difference.
- [source] **`referenced_tweets: null` is the check that separates this case from erdos.**
  The handed URL was @LangChain's own first-party announcement, not a quote, so the news
  post IS the fetched post. The judge ruled the coded card **use** at ≤4s while also
  setting `restates_narration: true` — correct here, because the narration is derived FROM
  the post, the opposite direction to grokpublish where @grok restated a claim Miguel had
  already made. "Restates" is only a rejection ground when the POST is the derivative one.
- [transcript] **Close the "did Scribe mis-transcribe" question with the audio, not with
  the script.** Scribe wrote "over **a** LangChain" where the scripted line is "over at".
  A 500ms spectral probe across 8.60-9.10s shows no stop closure and no high-frequency
  burst anywhere between the two words (hi/lo band ratio 0.011-0.15 through continuous
  voiced energy): no /t/ was released, Scribe is right, and the caption keeps the spoken
  form. This is the open question logged against hermes in the run-3 notes; the method that
  settles it is 20 lines and no API spend.
- [anchors] **Make the timing-anchor lookup fail loud on AMBIGUITY, not just on absence.**
  This narration says "40 times" twice ("40 times their body weight" and "40 times the
  request volume"). The inherited `find()` returns the FIRST match, so a shorter anchor
  would have silently pinned the hero's emphasis tick to the wrong clause 3.4s away. Three
  extra lines: collect all hits, raise on 0 and raise on 2+.
- [langchain_kinetic] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 768 frames, 25.6s, 26
  captions; take detection on a marker-less 14-take raw agreed across two independent

## Run 6 — grokpublish / icon, v2 defect fix (Miguel, 2026-08-12)

Two defects Miguel caught by WATCHING the shipped short that all three gates passed.
Both are systemic classes, not one-offs.

- [all] **`vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` silently opts a stroke OUT of the design-unit
  system, and it is the one place `px()` gets forgotten.** Every measure in a factory
  generator is design units converted by `px()` (S = 1080/576 = 1.875). Non-scaling-stroke
  deliberately freezes the stroke against the viewBox transform, so `stroke-width` is read
  in CSS pixels instead — meaning an authored `3.4` renders at **3.4 design-space px, not
  px(3.4)=6.4**. In grokpublish this put EVERY connector below the weight of the chrome it
  joins: plate borders are px(2)=3.75 and dashed placeholder outlines are px(2.4)=4.5, so a
  dashed SLOT out-weighed the solid arrow feeding it, and the flagship lane's connectors
  were the thinnest ink in the frame. Run 5's connectors were viewBox-scaled and landed
  ~6.2px, which is why Miguel read the regression instantly as "very slim compared to round
  5". **Rule: if a path carries non-scaling-stroke, its width MUST go through `px()`; if it
  does not, the width is already in viewBox units and must NOT.** Grep every generator for
  `non-scaling-stroke` and check the neighbouring `stroke-width` against that rule.
- [4K] **Do NOT blame the zoom for this — measure the CTM before compensating.** The obvious
  theory is that `zoom:2` breaks non-scaling-stroke and the 4K path halves it. Measured on
  the built pages: element `getScreenCTM().a` is **1.875 at 1080 and 3.751 in the zoom:2 4K
  project (ratio 2.02x)**, so non-scaling-stroke tracks the root zoom correctly. A generator
  that "fixed" the 4K thinness by doubling the width would have shipped double-weight
  connectors. One `getScreenCTM()` probe settles it before any edit.
- [gate1] **Second independent confirmation: audit the 1080 DESIGN copy, never `projects_4k`.**
  Same finding as langchain the same night. `zoom:2` doubles every
  `getBoundingClientRect()` while `clientWidth` stays 1080, so elements measure at 2x against
  a 1x frame — it fabricates margin/edge warnings and can equally MASK real ones.
- [all] **A connector must TRAVEL WITH the node it connects, or it becomes an arrow pointing
  at nothing.** grokpublish beat 5 collapsed its outer plates into the hub with
  `x:±56, opacity:0` over 0.34s, while the two arrows between them merely faded in place over
  0.20s. Measured on the encode at t=23.50: the app plate's right edge sits at 287.7du and
  arrow 1's centre at 217.5du — a full-strength arrow INSIDE the plate it should point away
  from, for ~6 frames. Gate 1 samples every 0.5s and rings/connectors are collision-exempt;
  gate 2's 16x16 grey signature does not move for a 56-unit connector; gate 3 passed. **No
  gate in the chain can see this class.** The fix is to give the connector the SAME tween as
  its endpoint (same distance, duration and ease), so the group collapses as one object.
- [all] **"Inherited across a cut" is not a licence to skip the entrance.** The same two
  connectors were the only elements of beat 5's inherited cast with no entrance tween at all
  — every plate settled across the cut while the arrows simply appeared at full strength.
  Inheriting an element's POSITION is correct (that is the ground-flip fix); inheriting it
  with no motion while its neighbours settle is what reads as "it just appears". Give the
  whole inherited cast the same settle.
- [process] **Three green gates plus a clean paperwork record still do not prove a short is
  right.** This one shipped with 0 geometry errors, 0 idle candidates, a first-call QC pass
  and an independent clerk review, and both defects were still there — one a units bug
  visible in every beat, one a 6-frame detachment. The only detector that found them was a
  human watching the video. Keep the gates, but treat "all gates green" as necessary, never
  sufficient.
- [grokpublish_icon v2] Shipped record after the fix: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1215 frames, 40.512s;
  connector strokes now 5.6px (distributor bus) and 6.4px (chain arrows), measured 4 -> 7
  physical px at 4K on the same frame; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings** on the 1080 copy;
  Gate 2 37 distinct states from 122 samples, 0 idle candidates (unchanged from v1, as
  expected — neither fix moves the grey signature); Gate 3 **pass, 0 visual, 0 semantic** on
  the first call; audio provably untouched (decoded stream md5-identical to the pre-fix
  render, both fixes video-only); 1 additional render.

## Run 6 — grokpublish / icon, v3 connector PROPORTION redesign (Miguel, 2026-08-12)

Miguel watched the v2 encode and the arrows were still wrong. Two independent causes, and
the units one had been "fixed" in v2 on a wrong inference.

- [all] **Matching a spec number is not matching a composition. Connector weight is
  RELATIVE to local chrome.** v2 restored the connectors to run 5's CONNECTOR width and
  declared the class closed. Wrong reference class: run 5's icon diagrams are drawn on
  light plates with hairline chrome, while this beat's plates carry px(2)=3.75 borders and
  coded glyph strokes that measure **20 physical px at 4K** — so a "correct" 6.4-design-px
  connector is a THIRD of the weight of the thing it joins and reads as a floating "→"
  glyph. Measure the chrome of the beat you are drawing into (border widths, glyph stroke
  widths, plate size) and size the connector against THAT, never against another lane's
  number. Here: shaft 6.0du (11.25 design px, ~1.1x the glyph strokes) with a FILLED 17x21du
  triangular head; the distributor bus 5.0du (9.4 design px, exactly the tile glyph weight).
- [4K] **`vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` lays the stroke down in DEVICE pixels, so a
  `zoom:2` 4K project renders every such stroke at HALF the weight its own 1080 design copy
  shows.** The v2 note reasoned from `getScreenCTM().a` (1.875 at 1080, 3.751 at zoom:2)
  that "non-scaling-stroke tracks the root zoom" — the CTM describes the GEOMETRY transform,
  not the stroke, and the encode refutes it: an authored `stroke-width=px(3.4)=6.4` renders
  **6.4 physical px at 4K** (column profile at design x=210: 6px core + 2px of antialiasing),
  i.e. 3.4 design px. Every connector shipped at half its intended weight while the 1080
  audit copy looked right. **Do not use non-scaling-stroke in a zoomed factory project at
  all** — a plain viewBox-space stroke needs no units rule, because `svg_free` maps 1 viewBox
  unit to 1 design unit on both copies. The generator now states it once: no connector
  carries non-scaling-stroke, and no connector width passes through `px()`.
- [law7] **"Arrows terminate AT box edges" is a statement about BOTH ends.** The old arrows
  were authored in a 45du box starting 8du clear of the source plate, with the head tip 1du
  short of the target — an 8du floating tail that no gate flags (connectors are
  `data-overlap-ok`, so the collision and connector-end laws skip them entirely). Author the
  connector as `chain_arrow(source_edge, dest_edge, cy)` so the span IS the gap and the
  geometry cannot drift: measured after, tail gap 0.0du and tip gap 0.5du (the antialiased
  apex subpixel).
- [motion] **A filled head cannot be revealed by a dash sweep, so it needs its own cue.**
  `draw()` animates strokeDashoffset; a `fill`-only triangle ignores it and would pop in at
  frame 0. Split the primitive into `.shaft` (dash sweep) and `.head` (0.22s POP keyed to
  70% of the sweep), which also enforces BUILD ORDER — the head lands as the shaft arrives,
  never before. Inherited-across-a-cut copies (b5) are authored complete with NO sweep and
  no head tween: the build belongs to the beat that built it.
- [process] **When a fix is "the same defect again", re-measure the ENCODE before trusting
  the previous session's root cause.** v2's diagnosis was half right (the width was in the
  wrong units) and half wrong (it believed the 4K render was fine), and the wrong half was
  supported by a live-page probe. One column profile through the shipped frame — 8 lines of
  PIL — separated the two causes in a minute and would have caught it in v2.
- [grokpublish_icon v3] Shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1215 frames, 40.512s; chain-arrow
  shaft **6 -> 22 physical px** at 4K (3.4 -> 11.25 design px), head **22 -> 70 physical px**
  wide and 2.9 -> 16.5du long, tail gap **8.0 -> 0.0du**, distributor bus 5.6 -> 18.75
  physical px, hook wave deliberately pixel-identical; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings** on
  the 1080 copy, first round, buying no render; Gate 2 37 distinct states from 122 samples
  (unchanged — a stroke weight cannot move the 16x16 grey signature), 0 idle candidates, 14
  frames read including all six in the 19-23.4s window; Gate 3 **pass on the first call, 0
  visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; decoded audio md5 byte-identical to the pre-fix render
  (ed4b8d1c4eaa63ad123fe5aa69c7c402), video-only; 1 additional render (4 total for the video).

## Run 6 — grokpublish / icon, v4 centring + entrance + causality pass (Miguel, 2026-08-12)

Miguel watched the v3 encode and found three more defects. All three were confirmed on
decoded frames BEFORE a line was changed, and all three are classes, not one-offs. Two of
them are now permanently detectable by the gates.

- [all] **An absolutely positioned child is measured from its parent's PADDING box, so
  `left:pad` on a bordered card is silently `border + pad`.** `plate()` placed its glyph svg
  at `left:pad; top:pad` while sizing it `w - 2*pad`. The result is a card whose glyph sits
  `border` px down and right of centre with a `2*border` margin asymmetry — px(2)=3.75px
  here, on EVERY plate in the short. Measured on the v3 encode at t=11.0: both phone cards
  had 50px of white above the phone and 35px below at 4K, the browser card 40/27. Nothing
  else was wrong with the phones. **Rule: any absolutely positioned child of a bordered box
  must inset by `pad - border`, or the box must not use `border-box` borders for chrome.**
  Miguel reported the asymmetry correctly and its DIRECTION the other way round — measure
  the frame before you trust either the report or your own reading of it.
- [gate1] **The geometry audit now owns this class.** New `glyph` law: a plate whose ONLY
  visible child is one img/svg must centre it, warning above 2.0 design px, opt-out
  `data-glyph-ok`. Calibrated over six known-good projects — grokprice_icon 0.00,
  meatwrapper_icon 0.00, deepresearch_icon 0.01, hermes_icon 0.01 (46 plates), erdos_counter
  0.05, agentreviews_icon 0.10 — against the defect class at 3.75px (grokpublish v3) and
  3.05px (hermesjourney, the same bug, found by the new law). **The tolerance is 2.0 and not
  the 4.0 that first suggested itself: the defect this law exists for measures 3.75px, so a
  4px gate would have been blind to the very thing it was written for.** Set a tolerance
  from the measured defect and the measured noise floor, never from a round number.
- [gate1] **"Contains one glyph" must mean the glyph IS the content.** The first draft counted
  only img/svg children and produced two false positives immediately: agentreviews `s3-t*` at
  11.07px (a logo correctly centred UNDER a terminal title bar) and hermesjourney `c-card` at
  282px (an avatar beside copy lines). Counting EVERY visible child and requiring exactly one
  removed both. A card that also carries chrome is a COMPOSITION, and centring is not a claim
  it makes.
- [all] **A fixed `strokeDasharray` is a pop-in generator: the sweep does not start until the
  offset drops below the path's REAL length.** `draw()` parked `strokeDasharray:2400` on
  paths of ~453 units (the b3 distributor tree) and ~290 units (the hook wave). On a 0.55s
  `power3.out` the visible portion only begins growing at 6.7% of the tween, so the authored
  half-second draw executed in **0.037s — about one frame**. Measured on the v3 encode, the
  tree region went 2.70% -> 18.88% ink between the frames at 12.500s and 12.533s. **Fix:
  `pathLength="100"` on every swept path**, which renormalises the geometry so 100 -> 0 is
  exactly empty to exactly full. No dash number ever needs to know a path's length again.
- [motion] **A connector DELIVERS its destination; it never trails it.** Beat 4 ran arrow1
  (19.04) -> browser card (19.78) -> arrow2 (20.82), so the card that the second arrow exists
  to deliver materialised a full second before that arrow was drawn. Three green gates and two
  previous fix passes had all looked straight at it. Re-choreographed to strict delivery
  order, one event per spoken word: arrow sweeps, head lands ON the destination slot's edge,
  THEN the card materialises at that head and the dashed slot retires. Verified frame-exact —
  at 20.50 the arrow is complete (tail 340.0du on the hub edge, tip 383.5du on the slot edge)
  and the slot is still empty; the card region is still ground at 20.733 and materialises at
  20.867. **Choreography law: nothing on screen may precede the thing that causes it.**
- [gate2] **Stillness -> one big step -> stillness is a machine-detectable pop-in signature.**
  frame_review now marks a kept frame whose preceding sample was a drop, whose diff is a
  large-element spike, and whose following sample is a drop. Calibrated on the v3 encode:
  dedup noise 2.0-3.1, real element arrivals 4.0-16, whole-ground section cuts 148-166 (cuts
  are not pop-ins, hence the ceiling); `POPIN_SPIKE=4.0`, `POPIN_CUT=60.0`. It fired on the
  v3 defect at 12.67s. It is a MARKER, never a failure — a legitimate 0.4s pop trips it too,
  and 12.67s still marks on the FIXED encode because at 3fps the tree's 0.18s drop stage is
  below the dedup threshold. The reviewer resolves each one; that is the whole job.
- [gate3] **A new QC rule needs its exemptions written the same day, and two failed rounds is
  how you find them.** The pop_in line added to the visual prompt failed the video twice
  before it was right: round 2 flagged dashed slots at a section's FIRST frame, which the
  frame-0-safe law positively requires to be authored on-screen, and round 3 flagged a 0.4s
  POP that **Gemini's ~1fps video sampling physically cannot resolve**. Both guards are now
  in the prompt — openings are never a violation, and an entrance the sampling cannot resolve
  must not be reported. The video was not touched between rounds. When a gate you just wrote
  fails, first ask whether the gate or the work is wrong.
- [colour] **A de-emphasis token is not a structure token.** The tree was `MUTED` #716B63,
  which this system uses for secondary strokes INSIDE glyphs — as load-bearing structure it
  read as neither chrome nor accent, which is exactly how Miguel described it ("outside the
  palette"). It is now `INK` #141416: literally the plate-border charcoal rgb(20,20,22) at
  full strength, and at 9.4 design px exactly the weight of the tile glyph strokes it feeds,
  so the tree is the same drawn language as the artifacts. The accent stays where the beat
  already spends it (one TERRA element per tile), so connective tissue never out-shouts
  content.
- [grokpublish_icon v4] Shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1215 frames, 40.512s; phone-card
  glyph margins **50/35 -> 42/43** physical px at 4K and browser **40/27 -> 33/34**, worst
  live-page glyph deviation **7.50 -> 0.60** physical px across 27 plates; distributor tree
  **0.037s -> 0.71s** build (drop, rail spreading 5.1 -> 159.7 -> 326.1 -> 387.2du out of the
  axis, then stubs) in INK at 18.73 physical px; beat 4 re-ordered to arrow-then-card with the
  v3 arrow proportions and the ride-their-plates collapse untouched; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0
  warnings** first round including the new glyph law; Gate 2 37 distinct states from 122
  samples, 0 idle candidates, 5 pop-in markers all resolved, 12 frames read; Gate 3 **pass, 0
  visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; decoded audio md5 byte-identical to the pre-fix render
  (ed4b8d1c4eaa63ad123fe5aa69c7c402), video-only; 1 additional render (5 total for the video).

## Run 6 — grokpublish / icon, v5 connector language PORTED from the run-5 reference (Miguel, 2026-08-12)

Third rejection of the same element. The fault was the DIRECTION, not the execution: v3 was
told to build "thick filled-head arrows in the confident task-diagram language of the run-5
icon winners", and that sentence is self-contradictory — **the run-5 winners have no
arrowheads anywhere.** Two whole fix passes were spent tuning a number inside a primitive
this design system does not own.

- [all] **The factory's connector language is HEADLESS ACCENT LINES. Direction is carried by
  the DRAW SEQUENCE, never by a head.** The approved reference is the "YOUR TASK" tree in
  `shorts_run5/gen/deepresearch_icon_gen.py`, visible at t=20 of
  `shorts_run5/output_4k/deepresearch_icon.mp4`: `line_to(..., thick=2.6, color=<ground
  accent>)` for stems and drops, `bus_el(..., thick=3.0)` for the rail, all plain rectangular
  divs — butt ends, no caps, no joins, flush on the box edges they touch. Verified on the
  reference 4K frame: stubs 10 physical px, rail 12 physical px, **arrowheads found: 0**. A
  connector's job is to say "these two things are joined, in this order"; the sweep already
  says the order.
- [process] **When a reviewer rejects the same visual twice, stop tuning parameters and go
  find the approved reference.** v2 changed the width. v3 changed the width again and added a
  head, with a whole paragraph of reasoning about sizing connectors against local chrome. All
  of it was internally consistent and all of it was answering a question the design system had
  already settled. The fix took one `grep` of a run-5 generator plus one measured frame. **A
  measured reference outranks a reasoned invention, always** — and "match the local chrome
  weight" is exactly the kind of plausible principle that manufactures a house style nobody
  approved.
- [all] **Port the RULE, not the literal hex, when the reference's token is ground-specific.**
  The reference draws its tree in its ground's accent (`TERRA_L` #DD7259 on dark). Copying
  that hex into this short would have put two different terracottas in one video. The ported
  rule is "a connector tree is drawn in its ground's accent", which resolves to TERRA #C4573A
  on the cream b3 ground — byte-identical to the reference's own `TERRA` — and TERRA_2 #E68569
  on the dark b4/b5 ground. v3 used MUTED (the de-emphasis token) and v4 used INK (chrome
  charcoal); both were wrong, because a connector tree is ACCENT.
- [all] **"One grammar everywhere" has a boundary, and it is the word CONNECTOR.** The hook's
  sea line is drawn with the same `svg_free` machinery and the same `.shaft` class, but it
  joins no boxes — it is water under a longship. It keeps MUTED and round caps. A metaphor
  element that happens to be a stroke is not a connector, and forcing it into the connector
  grammar would be cargo-culting the rule instead of applying it.
- [gate2] **A weight change can silently retire a pop-in marker, and that is not a fix.** The
  12.67s marker present on v4 disappears on v5 — not because the tree's entrance changed (it
  is the same 0.71s drop-rail-stubs build) but because 2.6/3.0du ink moves less of the 16x16
  grey signature than 5.0du did, dropping the diff under `POPIN_SPIKE`. Thresholded heuristics
  track ink, not intent. Never read a marker disappearing as evidence that anything improved.
- [grokpublish_icon v5] Shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1215 frames, 40.512s; chain links
  **6.0du + 17x21du filled head -> headless 2.6du** (9.75 physical px at 4K, butt caps, tail
  gap 0.02px and end gap 0.00px against the plates they join); distributor tree **5.0du INK ->
  3.0du rail + 2.6du drop/stubs in TERRA** (11.24 / 9.74 physical px, matching the reference's
  measured 12 / 10); zero arrowheads anywhere in the short; every v4 behaviour preserved
  (link sweeps first and the card materialises at its end, 0.71s tree build, links settle
  across the cut and ride their plates at the collapse); Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings**
  first round; Gate 2 37 distinct states from 122 samples, 0 idle candidates, 9 frames read at
  540px side by side with the extracted reference frame; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0
  visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; decoded audio md5 still
  ed4b8d1c4eaa63ad123fe5aa69c7c402, unchanged across v3/v4/v5; 1 additional render (6 total).

## Run 6 (impeccable) — elevenagents / icon (2026-08-12)

- [take-detection] **There is a THIRD marker form, and the bare-token "no" test actively
  misfires on it.** This raw has no spoken "No." anywhere (the erdos class) AND its restarts
  are punctuated by Scribe as an ellipsis on a COMPLETE word — "11...", "for...", "have...",
  "because..." — never as the hyphenated fragment grokpublish taught us to look for. Worse,
  inheriting grokpublish's `norm(text) == "no"` test fails the build on the WINNING take,
  because the narration says "you no longer have to" four times inside it. A spoken discard is
  a whole sentence, so Scribe punctuates it: the marker test must require `^no[.,!?]$`, not the
  bare token. The portable detector that survives all three forms is the one erdos found and
  this build confirms: key takes on the SCRIPTED OPENING after a >=1.5s pause, and count a take
  complete only when it reaches the spoken SIGN-OFF. Here that is 5 openings, exactly 1
  complete, no marker logic needed at all.
- [brief] **The winning take is the whole brief.** The dispatch named Twilio as one of the
  channels, and take 1 does say "SMS, Twilio, Telegram, and WhatsApp" — but take 1 dies
  mid-sentence and the last complete take says "SMS, WhatsApp, and Telegram" and never says
  Twilio. TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH prunes the BRIEF, not just the visuals: no Twilio mark was
  drawn, no Twilio logo was downloaded, and the channels debut in his order. Check the brief
  against the chosen take before planning a single beat.
- [asset-judge] **A first-party announcement can be rejected on its CLAIM SET while passing
  every pixel test.** ElevenLabs' own hero graphic is 3840x2160 (0.48x at the content column,
  no upscale problem, phone-legible) and is literally the same hub-and-channels diagram this
  short codes — and it still cannot ship, because it puts Zendesk, Slack, Intercom, telephony
  and email on screen as equal claims that Miguel never makes. Two further disqualifiers that
  generalise to any vendor artwork: its inner panel is a DOTTED canvas (banned outright by the
  pilot verdict) and its connectors carry arrowheads, which this factory's grammar does not
  own. Looking at a vendor diagram to validate a coded design is not the same as shipping it.
- [logos] **Check the artwork's COLOUR, not just the registry key.** `assets/logos/registry.json`
  already had `elevenlabs` — and it is the WHITE Wikimedia wordmark, which is invisible on this
  system's white plate, so the beat that was planned around it had no usable asset. The square
  black "II" symbol mark was fetched from Simple Icons and registered as `elevenlabs-mark`
  alongside it. A registry hit is not an availability check until you have opened the file.
- [gate2] **Border-tween emphasis is invisible to BOTH free detectors, and the fix is a FILL,
  not a fatter border.** grokpublish logged that a zero-ring build keeps fewer distinct states;
  this build found the floor of that trade. Six cued emphases inside one 9.7s beat — all of
  them 2-3px plate borders going terracotta — produced a **7.7s "still" run** in frame_review
  and `long_static=YES` from idle_motion_scan, because neither a 16x16 grey signature nor a
  luminance heuristic can see a colour-only edge change. Filling the CODED glyph with the
  ground accent on the same cue (a brand mark can never be recoloured, so the coded person is
  where this short is allowed to spend colour) restored the delta and split the run into 21.0 /
  23.0 / 24.0 / 25.0 / 27.3 / 31.3. **Rule: in a beat whose only events are colour changes, at
  least one of them must move real ink area — otherwise you have shipped a beat that no free
  gate, and few viewers at arm's length, can actually see.**
- [motion] **A white plate crossfading on a charcoal ground spends its middle frames as a GREY
  CARD.** Measured on the pre-render sheet at the collapse: a plate at ~36% opacity over
  #242427 reads as a broken or disabled tile in any single-frame review, and with `power3.in`
  it is unavoidable for ~6 frames. Give exiting PLATES a shrink (scale 0.74) with the fade so
  the same frames read as a deliberate exit; thin accent lines need no such treatment, because
  a 2.6du stroke has no grey-card failure mode.
- [timing] **Budget the END of a reduction, not just its start.** The first cut of the closing
  beat had the last element (the accent rule) completing 0.2s before the outro cut — the erdos
  defect class from the other direction, and one no gate reports. Re-budgeted so the fades end
  31.70, the hub lands 32.14, the lockup completes 32.32 and the rule completes 32.54, leaving
  the finished composition standing for 0.46s. Author the last arrival to complete >=0.4s
  before its own section boundary.
- [anchors] **Repeated clauses make anchor ambiguity the normal case, not the edge case.** This
  narration says "you can do that directly" three times and "Telegram, you" twice, so
  langchain's raise-on-2+ lookup fired TWICE during this build; a first-match `find()` would
  have silently pinned two hook cues to the payoff beat 21 seconds away. Keep the guard, and
  expect it to fire on any script built from parallel "if you want X" sentences.
- [elevenagents_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1113 frames, 37.12s; take

## Run 6 (impeccable) — slowfrontier / kinetic (2026-08-12)

- [law4] **The trigram guard's real blind spot is EQUALITY, and it is worth a build guard.**
  langchain found the class by hand (`BODY WEIGHT` on screen while the pill read exactly "body
  weight,") and wrote "read the caption phrase list against the on-screen term list, moment by
  moment". This build automated that reading: for every caption phrase, take every text atom
  on screen while the pill shows it (its spoken cue to its section's end) and fail if the word
  SETS are equal. It caught **four** cases the 3-gram guard passed, three of them in one beat.
  Equality is the right bar rather than overlap: a proper noun on screen while it is spoken is
  laws 2 and 9 doing their jobs, but a pill whose entire content is the line above it is a
  second caption track. Worst surviving overlap here is 2 of 3 caption words, non-identical.
- [law2 vs law4] **When the narration is a LIST OF PROPER NOUNS, the two laws collide, and the
  logo is the resolution.** "GPT 5.6 Sol, Mythos preview, Fable 5 preview" with those three
  strings set beside their marks is captions x2 three times over — and STANDARD's own Kinetic
  verdict says "trim text volume, never redundant with captions", while law 2 says "its LOGO,
  **not a text pill**". So the names came off, the marks went from 60 to 120 design units, and
  the row now says the one thing the spoken list does not: two of the three came from the same
  lab (Mythos preview and Fable 5 preview are both Anthropic, TechCrunch 2026-04-07). An
  unlabelled VERTICAL list reads as a list missing its labels; the same three marks in a ROW
  read as a set, so the accumulation was re-laid horizontally with horizontal re-centring.
- [intake] **The discard-marker rule is a LOWER BOUND, not a competing answer.** langchain
  requires the content rule and the marker rule to AGREE; this raw breaks that, and correctly:
  six restarts are truncated words Scribe marks, but two are clean, fully-formed abandoned
  openings ("AI research." at 65.18 and again at 67.36) that carry no marker of any kind.
  Equality would have failed the build; trusting the marker would have shipped 4.5s of two
  abandoned openings. The marker rule can only ever UNDER-shoot, so assert
  `content_start >= marker_start` and let the content rule decide. Ten openings, one sign-off,
  word 79 at t=69.70.
- [api] **`cap_mid()` takes the ELEMENT top, not the cap top `stack()` returns.** Feeding it a
  `stack()` value puts a strike-through `CAP[kind][0] * fs` too low — 9.2 design units on
  62-unit type, which crosses the lower half of the letters instead of the middle. No gate can
  see it: the element is `data-overlap-ok` by construction, so the audit skips it, and a 3fps
  encode review reads it as "a strike is present". A full-resolution still was the only
  detector, and the fix is `cap_mid(top_for_cap(kind, cap_top, fs), fs)`. Measured 222.7
  against a true middle of 213.5, then +0.04 after.
- [sync] **CALIBRATE an estimator before believing a number from it — this one has a +-100ms
  resolution.** langchain's bilabial burst-vs-lip-release method read +1.7ms over 5 events and
  was adopted as primary. Run with ONE fixed crop and threshold over four SHIPPED, independently
  verified run-6 renders from the same camera and session it returns medians of **-19.0
  (langchain), +27.5 (erdos), +79.0 (slowfrontier), +107.7 ms (grokpublish)**, with ~+-100ms
  spread inside each. All four are in sync. The visual half is why: "openness crosses the
  midpoint of its local range" lags the burst by however long the mouth takes to reach
  half-open, which is vowel-, loudness- and beard-dependent. It cannot answer a one-frame
  question. Three sibling renders and ten minutes is the whole calibration.
- [sync] **Verify the CHAIN, not the percept — it is exact, cheap and it has no threshold.**
  Sync here is a property of a four-link pipeline, and every link is measurable: (1) the raw is
  natively synced (era rule), (2) the cut trims video and audio with identical source windows
  through one concat filter, asserted from the container's own stream start times
  (video-minus-audio = **0.000s**), (3) the face crop and the m4a are derived from that master
  with no offset, (4) the composition places both at data-start 0. So "is the render in sync"
  reduces to two exact cross-correlations against the cut: the speech envelope at 1ms
  (**peak lag 0ms, r=0.967**, next best 0.734 at -7ms) and the mouth-window frame signature at
  1 frame (**peak lag 0, r=0.9993**, next best 0.933 at +-1). Same pixels, same samples, no
  perceptual threshold anywhere.
- [gate2] **The frame_review manifest's time labels drift, so they cannot settle a build-order
  question.** Matched against exact extractions, the labels here sit at -0.067s, +0.133s,
  +0.133s and +0.267s from the frame they actually show. That is fine for the manifest's job
  (which words were being spoken around this state) and useless for "did this element appear
  before its cue" — a rule that looked 0.07s early on a manifest frame measured, on exact
  extraction, 0px at 42.733 and 404px at 42.766 against a 42.739 cue. Settle causality with
  colour-keyed ink measured inside the element's own design-space box at exact times: all six
  cues on this short land within one frame, and the `!=` operator lands 0.04s after BOTH the
  operands it joins.
- [verify] **Threshold a surface detector on the ENCODED colour, not the authored one.**
  The source card is authored `#FFFCF8` on a `#F6F1EA` ground; h.264 quantisation delivers
  (251,250,243) and (243,239,230). The authored triple finds **nothing** (0 frames), so the
  first sweep reported a card that was on screen for 3.7s as absent. Sample the real pixels
  first, then set the threshold between the two measured values: peak 29528 sampled px for the
  card against a 271 px median for the three roll-call plates, a 100x separation.
- [type] **On a SHORT word, height is the binding constraint, not width.** `FAST` fits the
  516-unit band at 176 design units and breaks the 410 seam floor at 429.9 while doing it. The
  width fit is the only one the lane's `fit()` knows about, so a one- or two-syllable hero needs
  its own height cap; here 157.2 is where the ink reaches the floor and 148 ships.
- [slowfrontier_kinetic] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1461 frames, 48.704s, 42
  captions, 10 sections, 31 atoms; take detection on a partly marker-less 10-opening raw with
  the marker rule demoted to a bound and both an `EXPECTED_TAKE_START` and an
  `EXPECTED_TAKE_WORDS` assertion; one transcript token adjudicated with EDL-mapped evidence
  (Scribe wrote `Sol,` on the raw and `Soul,` on the cut, 27ms apart in the source); Gate 1 **0
  errors / 0 warnings across 3 rounds** on the design copy (106 ids, 0 duplicates, 32 tween
  selectors all resolving, 0 untweened section children, 1 `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 0
  `non-scaling-stroke`); Gate 2 **49 distinct states from 146 samples**, 97 collapsed, 0 idle
  candidates, 1 stillness marker (3.3s), 5 pop-in markers all resolved on decoded frames, 13
  frames read; `idle_motion_scan` idle_drift=no long_static=no; render sweep min ink 1.93%,
  median 9.80%, **0 frames under 1%, 0 blank**, min max-channel deviation 178; caption band
  pill-free on 10 frames, all before the first spoken word or after the last; source card 3.70s
  measured from pixels, contiguous, under the 4s ceiling; marks 0.42x intrinsic at 4K; deepest
  authored ink design y=400.0 against a 410 floor; sync at lag 0 on both streams with NO remux;
  Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; 2 renders, the extra

## Run 6 (impeccable) — stolenapp / kinetic (2026-08-12)

- [intake] **The ">=1.5s pause before a scripted opening" heuristic can REJECT the winning
  take, because Scribe hides the pause inside the trailing word.** Miguel trails off ("Copying
  applications and...") and stops for about two seconds before the real take, and Scribe emits
  word 356 `and...` as a **1.89s-long word** running 190.710-192.600 against the take opening at
  **192.609** — a measured inter-word gap of **0.009s**. A gap test with any sane threshold
  throws away the only complete take in a 17-opening raw. A restart boundary is a discard
  MARKER **or** a real gap, and on a trailing-off restart only the marker survives; the content
  rule (last opening reaching the sign-off) decides, and every opening's boundary kind is
  recorded rather than used as a filter.
- [intake] **The elevenagents punctuated-marker rule is not a nicety, it is load-bearing on any
  take that argues about a negation.** This narration says "speed is **no** longer the moat"
  twice inside the winning take, so grokpublish's `norm(text) == "no"` test fires on words 50
  and 102 of the tight transcript and the closure re-scan fails the build on the take it exists
  to ship. `^no[.,!?]$` is the test: a spoken discard is a whole sentence, so Scribe punctuates
  it.
- [brief] **A brief can survive its own take's death.** The dispatch described a thesis ending
  ("your unfair advantage is your WHY, which is why he doesn't AI-generate his videos") and
  Miguel really does say it — at 145.62-155.02 of the raw, inside take 8, which never reaches
  the sign-off. The LAST COMPLETE take ends on distribution / brands / relationships instead.
  elevenagents said TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH prunes the BRIEF; this build is the case where the
  pruned material is the most quotable line in the recording. Check the brief against the chosen
  take before planning a beat, and be ready to throw away the reason the video was commissioned.
- [law4] **When the caption pill is ONE WORD and that word is your list item, the fix is to add
  information, not to delete the item.** At 27.18 the pill reads exactly "relationships," and
  nothing else, so a bare `RELATIONSHIPS` on screen is token-identical — the defect
  `guard_caption_identity` exists for. slowfrontier's answer (drop the names, grow the logos)
  does not exist here: distribution, brands and relationships have no marks. Numbering all three
  rows (`01 / 02 / 03`, muted, at the row's own size, on one optical left edge) clears the guard
  legitimately AND says the thing the spoken line cannot show — Miguel's ORDER, which is what
  "and most importantly" is about. Rendering the index inside the SAME element is what makes it
  a real token; a `::before` bullet or a margin-only separator would be invisible to `norm()`.
- [gate2] **A white plate on the cream ground is INVISIBLE to a modal-background ink sweep, and
  that is a metric artifact, not a defect — but the metric still found a real one.** `#FFFCF8`
  on `#F6F1EA` deviates by 12/255, under the 34 threshold, so a 96-unit plate scores only its
  blue glyph. The sweep reported **152 frames under 1%** in two windows; the first (0.00-2.83s)
  was this artifact plus a genuinely thin hook, and the second (32.47-34.63s) was a section
  opening on a 24-unit kick label for 2.16s with nothing else on screen. Both openings were
  promoted from kick labels to 52-58 unit display lines: **152 -> 16 frames**, and the 16
  survivors are the deliberate cold open, all before the first spoken word finishes. Report the
  ink fraction WITH its explanation, and treat a low-ink window as a question about the design
  before it is dismissed as a threshold quirk.
- [buildorder] **A causality probe needs the element's COLOUR and its PARKED OFFSET, or it
  lies in both directions.** slowfrontier established exact-time extraction as the way to settle
  build order; running it here produced three false "EARLY" flags and two false "OK"s before it
  was right. (1) A rule's band sits inside the descender zone of the line above it and a strike's
  band sits inside the word it crosses, so a generic modal-background count is saturated by the
  neighbour and cannot move — rules and strikes must be counted on terracotta pixels only.
  (2) This lane PARKS an incomplete cast off-axis with `sety` and steps it home when the next
  line lands, so an atom measured before its section's step is **not at its authored top** —
  three rules read 0% either side purely because the band was 51 / 36 / 30 design units off the
  ink, and two texts read "OK" off a neighbour's ink. With both corrections, all 20 atoms
  measure **0.00% before their cue** and visible after.
- [law3] **Measure the card's screen time from pixels BEFORE believing the timeline.** The
  authored section was 4.14s against the judge's 4.0s ceiling and encoded at **4.133s** — a law-3
  violation no gate reports, because gate 1 measures geometry, gate 2 samples at 3fps and gate 3
  passed the video. Moving the section cut one word later (off "Now," onto "due") and pulling the
  next cut back one word (onto "has") brought it to **3.267s** and cost nothing else.
- [source] **A quote-tweet's card belongs to the QUOTED author, and that must be asserted, not
  remembered.** The handed URL was @rileybrown quoting @alexcooldev's "some random guy copied all
  of my apps on the App Store 1:1" — the erdos trap, second sighting. The judge rejected the
  quoter's card on `claims_not_in_narration` ("In 6-12 months every profitable app will be
  replicated within 3 days", "Autonomously"): Miguel's winning take says neither. `guard_provenance`
  now asserts three things — the card's sentence is a whole paragraph of the QUOTED post, it is
  NOT a paragraph of the quoting post, and the card's handle is the news author's. Also: the
  sibling fetcher downloads only the top-level author's avatar, which is the wrong face on a
  quote, so it now pulls one for every user in the payload.
- [assets] **A vendor post's second paragraph can be disqualified by the RENDER ENGINE before
  any judgement of value.** The news post's paragraph 2 ends in a skull emoji and the HyperFrames
  render browser has no emoji font, so it would ship a tofu box that every deterministic gate
  passes. Exclude on that ground explicitly and record it, rather than letting a taste argument
  stand in for a capability fact.
- [law2] **One named platform is still law 2.** The narration names exactly one product — the App
  Store, twice — and `assets/logos/` had no mark for it. Fetched from Simple Icons (the
  elevenagents path), rasterised to 1024px, registered as `appstore` with its SVG source
  alongside, and plated in the opening beat so the platform is on screen before the theft is
  described. A registry with 54 logos and no App Store is a gap worth closing once.
- [type] **Under a plate, HEIGHT binds the hero, not width.** `ONE DAY` fits the 512-unit band at
  117 design units, but with a 96-unit plate and a 58-unit line above it the ink crosses the 410
  seam floor at 98. Shipped at 94 (deepest authored ink 405.3). slowfrontier found the same on a
  short word with nothing above it; a plate makes it bind much earlier.
- [paperwork] **A blanket video-id rename inside an inherited script can fabricate a measurement.**
  Forking `verify_slowfrontier_sync.py` with a global string replace renamed its four-video
  calibration table's `slowfrontier: +79.0ms` entry to `stolenapp: +79.0ms` — another video's
  number, presented as this one's, in the JSON a clerk audits. Read every inherited constant after
  a rename, not just the code paths.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — grok46 / icon (2026-08-12)

- [take-detection] **There is a FOURTH raw shape, and it breaks the "key on the scripted
  opening" rule as literally written: the opening WORDING changes between restarts.** This
  raw opens "Grok 4.6 and Grok 4.7 just got announced by Elon Musk", then "Now, Grok 4
  points f-", then twice "Elon Musk just announced Grok 4.6 and 4.7". Keying on a phrase
  finds 2 of the 4 takes and silently ships an abandoned opening; keying on the first token
  finds 1. The portable form is to key on the **stem every opening shares** — here the token
  `Grok` anywhere inside the first 8 words after a >=1.5s pause — and keep the sign-off as
  the completeness test. 4 openings, exactly 1 complete. It also carries BOTH known marker
  punctuations at once (an ellipsis on a complete word AND one hyphenated fragment), which
  is more evidence the marker rule is only ever a lower bound: asserted
  `content_start 46.68 >= last marker 39.04` and left the content rule to decide.
- [gate2] **A skeleton-only opening is the weakest first second in the factory, and the
  dead-frame scan is what tells you.** The hook was authored frame-0-safe in the approved
  way — three dashed slots, everything else arriving on its word — and it measured **2.58%
  top-zone ink with a 28/255 max-channel deviation for 1.2s**, against 4.18-4.36% on the
  shipped run-6 siblings. Frame-0 safety is a floor, not a target. The fix is to ask what
  the video's SUBJECT is: a brand mark is an identity, not a claim, so the Grok mark can
  stand on the axis at t=0 while the VERSIONS still land strictly on their spoken names.
  Ink 2.58% -> 3.53% and the opening now has something to look at.
- [all] **Split a reduction's horizontal and vertical legs onto two cues, or the
  intermediate state is not a composition.** Collapsing a 3-plate row into one plate that
  must end at the hub seat has two wrong answers and both were measured on encodes: retire
  the others first and ride later, and the survivor sits alone at the far LEFT for 2.6s;
  ride both legs at once, and it sits alone at the TOP of an empty charcoal frame for 3.4s
  (t=14.67). Riding x on "will not be new" and y on "They will be" makes every held frame
  balanced — centred on the axis first, raised only when the key term needs the room. Same
  parked-at-final-rect mechanics, two `fromTo`s on two properties, no wrapper.
- [motion] **`tree_bus(flip=True)` — the connector grammar has a second topology, and it
  costs one flag.** Three beats here say "these things feed the model" and two say "this
  model has these attributes". Same headless 2.6/3.0du rules, same butt caps, same accent
  role; the mirror puts the hub at the BOTTOM, authors every path in the direction it is
  swept, and reverses the build to stubs -> rail -> drop. Direction stays a property of the
  DRAW SEQUENCE, which is the only thing this system has instead of arrowheads — and it
  means a "sources feed a model" beat cannot be mistaken for a "model owns its facts" beat.
- [law2] **A technique is not a tool, and its acronym is its mark.** Law 2 mandates logos
  for named tools and MODELS; SFT and RL have no logo, and inventing a "reward star"
  pictogram would have shipped a glyph nobody can decode. Miguel says both acronyms himself
  at 51.34, so `term_plate()` (a plate whose whole content is 34-unit mono type) is the
  honest identity — and because it is an identity chip rather than a sentence, a one-word
  plate beside its spoken name is law 2 doing its job, not a second caption track.
- [law4] **Automate the caption-identity guard with each atom's REAL window, not its
  section's.** slowfrontier's guard compares word SETS; scoping it to the section would have
  failed this build on a term that is not on screen yet. Registering `(text, t_on, t_off)`
  per typeset atom at author time makes the check exact, and it immediately earned its
  keep: the pill from 15.92 to 16.58 is literally "same old," so the SAME OLD term is cued
  0.06s AFTER "good old" instead of on its own phrase. 16 atoms, 0 collisions, and the
  timing decision is proved rather than argued.
- [captions] **The stutter policy has a third form: an immediate REPETITION of a complete
  word.** "huge impacts in, in AI models" carries no partial word and no marker, so the
  `endswith("-")` filter every generator inherits passes it straight into a pill. The pilot
  verdict says the FOOTAGE is not re-cut but a stutter never reaches the captions, so
  `clean_tokens` now drops a token whose normalised form equals the next one's within 0.5s.
  Audio untouched, pill reads "huge impacts in AI".
- [logos] **A registry hit is still not an availability check, and the second failure mode
  is COLOUR.** elevenagents found a white wordmark invisible on a white plate; this build
  found `deepseek` registered as the BLUE #4D6BFE whale, which would have put a second
  colour on a system with exactly one accent per ground. Simple Icons' monochrome square
  mark was fetched and registered as `deepseek-mark` before use, with the reason written
  into the entry so the next builder does not re-litigate it.
- [gate2] **A tree BUILD is invisible to the stillness detector, so measure the accent ink
  in the element's own box.** The 4.3s stillness marker over the DeepSeek beat survived
  moving the tree build 1.0s earlier, because 2.6-3.0du of stroke cannot move a 16x16 grey
  signature — the marker is tracking ink area, not events. Three exact decodes inside the
  tree's design-space box settle it in seconds: 0 accent px at 40.20, 1658 at 40.60, 2244 at
  41.00. Never resolve a stillness marker by looking at the marker.
- [grok46_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1707 frames, 56.917s container /
  56.879 authored, 46 captions, 9 sections, 70 atoms; take detection on a 4-take raw whose
  opening wording shifts, asserted against hand-verified constants for BOTH the start
  (46.68) and the word count (155), with the marker rule demoted to a bound; the cut kept
  all 155 spoken words; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings across 5 rounds** on the 1080 design
  copy (138 ids, 0 duplicates, 71 tween selectors all resolving, 0 untweened section
  children, 10 `data-overlap-ok` — connectors only — 0 `data-bleed`, 0
  `non-scaling-stroke`); Gate 2 **42 distinct states from 171 samples**, 129 collapsed, 0
  idle candidates, 12 pop-in markers and 4 stillness markers all resolved on decoded
  frames, 10 frames read plus two native-4K crops of the tree junctions;
  `idle_motion_scan` frames=228 idle_drift=no long_static=no; render sweep **0 of 1707
  frames under 1% top-zone ink and 0 blank**, min 3.53%, median 12.28%; caption band
  pill-free on 6 frames, all before the first spoken word at 0.199s; deepest authored ink
  design y=333.7 against a 400 floor; sync at **lag 0 on both streams** (audio r=0.9818 at
  1ms resolution, video r=0.9993 at 1 frame) with NO remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST
  call, 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; zero third-party assets, zero rings, zero
