  geometry.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — agentreviews / icon, REBUILD after a rejection (2026-08-12)

Session B built this video, Miguel rejected it outright ("they really sucked") and every
artifact was deleted, so nothing survived to diagnose. Built clean-slate from the APPROVED
grokpublish v5 chassis. Six findings, all of them classes.

- [gate1] **A connector authored with `x0 > x1` is INVISIBLE, and the geometry audit reports
  it as zero errors.** `chain_line(eid, x0, x1, ...)` computes `span = x1 - x0`, so calling it
  with the endpoints in the wrong order produces a wrapper of NEGATIVE width. The audit's
  collector drops any element measuring under 1px (`if (r.width < 1 || r.height < 1) continue`),
  so four of this short's eight structural links did not exist and the sweep still returned **0
  errors / 0 warnings**. The build guards did not see it either: the ids exist, the tweens
  resolve, the dash sweep runs on a path nobody can see. Only the pre-render contact sheet found
  it. **A gate that skips an element cannot fail it — "0 errors" is a statement about what the
  audit measured, not about what is on screen.** The reverse-sweep primitive now takes the span
  in reading order and carries the direction in a `reverse` flag instead of in the argument
  order, so the mistake is unmakeable.
- [all] **A round cap is half a stroke wider than its path in EVERY direction, and that is where
  a glyph breaks out of its own container.** The work-document check was drawn `M26 52 L44 70
  L76 30` with `stroke-width="11"` and `stroke-linecap="round"` inside a page spanning x 16-86:
  the path ends at 76, but the CAP ends at 81.5, and at 4K the check visibly escaped the black
  page onto the white plate. Gate 1 does not measure inside an svg, gate 2's 3fps thumbnails are
  too small, and gate 3 passed the frame. **Solve a glyph's bounds on the CAPPED extent, never on
  the path**, and pull a full-resolution 4K crop of every dense composition before shipping — the
  third build in a row where the full-res still is the only detector that fired.
- [gate2] **"Frames under 1% ink" is the wrong alarm on a cream ground; the right one is a
  measured RUN LENGTH.** The whole-video ink sweep reported 105 frames under 1%, which looks
  alarming and is mostly a metric artifact: a WHITE plate on a CREAM ground deviates by ~12,
  under the 34 threshold, so a perfectly composed frame carrying one white plate scores as
  nearly empty. Grouping the under-threshold frames into contiguous RUNS separated the artifact
  from the defect instantly — six runs, five of them 0.03-0.73s frame-0-safe openings, and one
  genuine **3.47s stretch of two bare dashed slots**. That one was the only part of the short
  that read as an empty screen, and it was invisible to all three gates. Report runs, not counts.
- [icon] **When a beat opens on nothing, the fix is the SPINE, not more chrome.** The way-3
  opening was rebuilt to re-establish the short's own two-agent motif in the seats it had held
  since the hook, so the third way starts from the same picture the first two answered and the
  medium seat between them is once again the thing being filled. Frame 0 goes from two dashed
  boxes to a composed diagram, ink at that beat's minimum triples, and the short gains a spine
  the viewer can actually follow: **agent — [medium] — agent**, with the medium being a platform,
  then a terminal, then one API key.
- [gate2] **An 8.3s "still" run is a real reading, even when four cued events happened inside
  it.** The error beat lit two plate borders, popped three accent dots INSIDE one plate's svg,
  swapped them for a check and filled two figures — and frame_review collapsed the entire
  34.0-42.3s window into one state. Everything had happened inside single plates or in colour
  only. Adding ONE geometric move on the same cue (the document scales 1.14 and settles back
  when the errors are caught) split it into 3.3s runs. **The elevenagents rule generalises: ink
  INSIDE a plate is not ink for this purpose — the detector, and the viewer at arm's length,
  only see an element's outline change.**
- [logos] **Optical mark size is a measurement, not a taste call.** Eight marks from six sources
  landed at wildly different apparent sizes at a fixed pad (Codex 0.51 of its plate against
  Grok 0.61) because each vendor bakes in different whitespace. Decoding each mark's ink bounding
  box and solving the pad so every footprint lands near 0.58 — with the two visually DENSE marks
  (a solid bee, a solid tile) pulled to ~0.52 because ink area reads as size too — took ten
  minutes and removed the whole class. Also: a mark's own light-mode colour can be a MEDIA QUERY
  (the official Buzz favicon repaints itself yellow under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`), and an
  `<img>`-embedded SVG resolves that against the render host, not the page, so the staged copy
  must pin it while the registry copy stays the unmodified official file.
- [law11] **"No mark available" and "no mark is TRUE" are different rulings, and the second one
  is the interesting one.** Miguel says "Buzz was created by Jack Dorsey, the creator of
  Twitter". This factory's connector grammar can only assert "A is joined to B", so a link from
  the Buzz mark to a Twitter mark would state that Buzz connects to Twitter, which is false —
  the real relation is a shared founder, and it is not expressible without inventing a text
  label. The beat ships as a 4.6s hold on a complete composition instead, which is the only long
  stillness in the short and the right trade: **a hold is a smaller defect than a false diagram.**
- [agentreviews_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 2163 frames, 72.107s, 64 captions,
  12 sections, 114 direct section children; take detection on a raw carrying BOTH marker forms
  (2 punctuated discards, 6 truncations) with 8 scripted openings and exactly 1 complete take,
  asserted against three hand-verified constants, and one in-take truncation whitelisted by exact
  string; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings across 6 rounds** on the 1080 design copy (206 ids, 0
  duplicates, 115 tween selectors all resolving, 0 untweened section children, 30
  `data-overlap-ok` — connectors only — 0 `data-bleed`, 0 `non-scaling-stroke`, 0 caption-echo
  trigrams and 0 caption-identity collisions); Gate 2 **56 distinct states from 216 samples**,
  160 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, longest stillness 3.3s, 15 pop-in markers all resolved on
  decoded frames, all 56 states read plus three full-resolution 4K crops; `idle_motion_scan`
  idle_drift=no long_static=no; render sweep min ink 0.772%, median 4.457%, **0 truly blank
  frames**, min max-channel deviation 77; caption band pill-free on 6 frames, all before the
  first spoken word at 0.199s; sync at lag 0 on BOTH streams against the cut (audio r=0.982 at
  1ms resolution, video r=0.9996 at 1 frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO remux; Gate 3
  **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; 8 official brand marks, all
  monochrome, none upscaled; zero third-party assets, zero rings, zero arrowheads; 4 renders,
  every extra pass bought by an ENCODED-FRAME or FULL-RESOLUTION finding and never by geometry.

- **Gate 1 now catches ghosts (2026-08-12, after agentreviews rebuild; approved by Miguel).**
  The audit used to skip any atom under 1px silently, so a connector span authored with
  `x0 > x1` rendered at negative width and simply did not exist — four of eight structural
  links missing while Gate 1 said "0 errors"; only a pre-render contact sheet caught it.
  `geometry_audit.py` now records every sub-1px sighting in an active clip (unless a child
  element actually renders) and raises a `ghost` ERROR for any atom that never reaches 1px
  across the whole timeline. Verified both ways: a synthetic zero-width atom fails the build
  (exit 1), and the three fresh run-6 projects still pass 0/0. Builders: keep authoring spans
  in reading order with a `reverse` flag for direction — the gate is the backstop, not the fix.

- **RUN-6 REVIEW VERDICT (Miguel, 2026-08-12) — three laws supersede run-6 conventions.**
  (1) COLOR MARKS: brand marks always ship in original brand colors; the monochrome-marks
  convention (grok.png precedent, deepseek-mark, black ElevenLabs "II") is RETIRED — any
  earlier entry in this file saying "brand marks ship monochrome" is overruled. Accent
  discipline still governs our own shapes, never a brand's palette. (2) UNIQUE VISUALIZATION:
  icons+diagrams are the floor; every short plans at least one bespoke animated scene-level
  visualization at the story's peak beat (hermes tools video + the boat = named precedents;
  shorts_run5/gen/hermes_icon_gen.py = reference). Clean-but-generic loses to unique-and-catchy.
  (3) REAL TWEET: X sources ship as the actual tweet media with the hermes tweet_block()
  treatment (highlight ring lands on the claim as Miguel says it), never as a coded
  re-creation; provenance judging keeps checking accuracy/legibility, but the run-6 pattern of
  rejecting real tweets for "claims Miguel doesn't say" and rebuilding them as cards is over.
  Full text in STANDARD.md "RUN-6 REVIEW VERDICT". No re-renders of the shipped batch.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — hermesjourney / icon, REBUILD after an artifact wipe (2026-08-13)

First build under the RUN-6 REVIEW VERDICT's three new laws. A previous session built
this video and deleted every artifact on wind-down, so nothing survived to diagnose and
nothing was reconstructed; the only fossils are two lines in `geometry_audit.py`'s own
calibration table (`hermesjourney_icon` measured 3.05px of glyph drift, and a `c-card`
false positive), both of which the current chassis satisfies by construction.

- [law13] **The bespoke visualization is not something you invent — it is something the
  SOURCE already draws, and the source's own demo video is where you find it.** The brief
  said "a timeline of every memory and skill", which reads as a horizontal rail, and a rail
  is the retired V09 lane. Decoding the attached 53s demo (frames at 8s and 34s) showed
  `/journey` actually renders a RADIAL constellation: concentric date rings, oldest at the
  core, newest outside, scattered with orange "skill" dots and cyan "memory" diamonds, with
  a legend reading "core = oldest · outer = newer". Ten minutes of `ffmpeg -ss` turned a
  banned lane into a 9.4s scene that is honest to the product, unique to this short, and
  animated by construction — the graph GROWS outward, week by week, which is literally the
  sentence being spoken over it. **Look at the vendor's own artifact before designing the
  coded rebuild; rejecting it as shipped media (law 8) does not mean ignoring it.**
- [law12] **"Ships in its original brand colours" and "is monochrome" are not in conflict,
  and the distinction is worth stating in the paperwork.** Nous Research's official mascot
  artwork IS black-and-white line art, so shipping the Nous girl in black is her own palette,
  not the monochrome reduction the verdict retired. The test is not "is it grey" but "did we
  strip anything". Miguel's standing rule still binds harder: Hermes is the NOUS GIRL, never
  the pixel-art "H" — enforced here by a compile-time guard that fails the build if the
  string `hermes-agent` ever reaches the page.
- [law14] **The "real tweet" of the run-5 reference is a RENDERED EMBED, not a screenshot
  somebody took, and that distinction is what makes the law implementable.**
  `shorts_run1/render_x_cards.py` builds the card from the API payload in headless Chromium.
  Three corrections that path needs before it can ship in 2026: render at
  `device_scale_factor=2` (a 1000px card is fine at 1080 and a **1.8x upscale at 4K**, the
  exact law-8 class the audit warns about — 2000px lands at 0.92x); draw NO metrics markup
  at all rather than cropping the row off afterwards; and make the verified badge
  CONDITIONAL — run 1's template drew the blue check unconditionally, and @witcheer's payload
  says `verified: false`, so shipping it would have been a fabricated credential.
- [law14] **Place the highlight ring from a MEASUREMENT the renderer hands you.** The card
  renderer wraps the claim in `<span id="p2">`, reads its bounding box in the same pass that
  screenshots the card, and writes the rect as fractions of the card. The generator then
  converts through the card's own design width and height. No fraction was ever guessed, and
  a re-render with different text re-derives the ring for free.
- [all] **GSAP defaults an SVG element's `transformOrigin` to the USER-SPACE ORIGIN, so the
  inherited `pop()` would have fired all 43 constellation nodes out of the graph's centre.**
  Every scale tween on a shape inside an svg needs an explicit `transformOrigin:"50% 50%"`.
  This is invisible to every gate (the atom is the svg div, which never moves) and the
  pre-render contact sheet is what catches it.
- [all] **A dash sweep whose `strokeDasharray` EQUALS `pathLength` leaves a visible notch on
  a closed path.** The dash's two butt ends meet at the start point, and on all three swept
  time rings that point sits at 12 o'clock directly under the ring's own label, where the eye
  already is (~1px gap, measured on a 2x contact sheet). Use `strokeDasharray: 102` against
  `pathLength="100"`: the dash overlaps itself by 2 path units so the joint closes, and the
  zero point is unchanged because 102 offset still shows exactly nothing.
- [geometry] **A square box around a circle is empty in all four corners, and gate 1 measures
  BOXES.** Two rounds of collision ERRORS came from labels straddling the graph box's edge,
  not from anything visible. The first fix is structural and worth keeping: size the box's
  half-side to `outer radius + label gap`, so every annulus label is CONTAINED and the
  containment exemption applies by construction. The second is honest declaration: the graph
  layers are illustration CANVASES that labels, a plate and a legend legitimately sit on, so
  they carry `data-overlap-ok` rather than a legend's letter-spacing being tuned until its
  Range rect stops one design unit short of an invisible edge. Nothing is lost — a label
  crossing a ring STROKE was never visible to gate 1 either.
- [all] **A fixed fraction-of-step angle jitter is a collision generator on the inner ring of
  a radial layout, and the failure hides behind the choreography.** At 0.62 of a 35du step,
  two neighbours could close to 13du with a 19du node diameter. It never showed on screen
  only because ring 1 alternates species and half its nodes arrive on a later cue. Solve the
  jitter amplitude in ARC LENGTH from the required centre-to-centre distance, then ASSERT the
  realised minimum at import time — the seed is fixed, so that assertion is a proof rather
  than a sample.
- [gate2] **A 16x16 grey signature of the whole top zone cannot see 43 nodes landing inside a
  364-unit graph, so "18 distinct states" is a statement about the detector.** The elevenagents
  and grok46 finding ("ink INSIDE a plate is not ink for this purpose") generalises one level
  down: inside a large svg, a 19du node is the same blind spot as a border tween. The answer is
  not to inflate the design; it is to measure the events directly. A colour-keyed pixel count
  inside each element's own design-space box, extracted at exact times 0.10s before and 0.45s
  after each cue, produced a clean monotone staircase (0 -> 52,468 for the hook's second stage,
  0 -> 43,333 for the claim ring, and 634 -> 10,692 -> 17,332 -> ... -> 103,951 across the
  constellation), and it doubles as the causality proof: three cues measure literally 0 before.
- [gate2] **Make the growth test ABSOLUTE, not a ratio.** A ratio bar (`after > before*1.15`)
  fails on the fourth wave of a filling graph, because each cue's "before" already carries the
  previous wave still arriving and one node is a smaller fraction of a growing total. `+2000
  key pixels at 4K` is about two thirds of ONE node's ink, which is a change a viewer can see,
  and it is the same bar at the start and at the end.
- [all] **Two elements swapping the same seat need their tweens to OVERLAP, and the arithmetic
  has to be done in the direction of the ease.** The key term's `retire` ended at 6.20 and the
  core's `pop` began at 6.24, and those 0.04s rendered as ONE FULLY BLANK CREAM FRAME
  (max-channel deviation 0/255) — the langchain class, in a build that had already read that
  entry. Starting the incoming element 0.14s BEFORE the outgoing one is gone costs nothing
  visually, because `EXIT` is `power3.in` and the term still holds ~49% opacity at 80% of its
  own fade.
- [law11] **A chart's rings can assert less than a diagram's arrows, and that is why this
  short has no connectors at all.** The narration says the agent learned memories and skills
  week after week; it never says any one of them relates to any other. The source post does
  claim that ("it also lists each node, so you can see your interconnected skills and
  memories") and it was dropped from the card for exactly that reason. Concentric time rings
  assert only "later = further out", which is what the tool asserts and what "week after week"
  means — so the whole video ships with zero connectors, zero arrowheads and zero node labels,
  and there is nothing in it to be factually wrong about.
- [hermesjourney_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 537 frames, 17.900s, 19
  captions, 4 sections, 27 direct section children; take detection on a 7-opening raw with
  exactly 1 complete take, keyed on the shared stem "Hermes Agent now" and asserted against
  hand-verified constants for both the start (68.699) and the word count (67), with the single
  discard marker demoted to a bound; one transcript token adjudicated with EDL-mapped evidence
  (Scribe wrote "Pokémon." on the raw and "Pokemon." on the cut, the same utterance to 1ms on
  the preceding word); Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings** on the 1080 design copy across 5 rounds
  (57 ids, 0 duplicates, 28 tween selectors all resolving, 0 untweened section children, 2
  `data-overlap-ok` — the two graph canvases — 0 `data-bleed`, 0 `non-scaling-stroke`, 0
  caption-echo trigrams, 0 caption-identity collisions, deepest authored ink y=394.0 against a
  400 floor); Gate 2 18 distinct states from 54 samples, 0 idle candidates, 0 stillness markers,
  2 pop-in markers both resolved on decoded frames, all 18 states read plus three native-4K
  crops and a 30-still pre-render contact sheet; `idle_motion_scan` frames=72 idle_drift=no
  long_static=no; render sweep min ink 0.762%, median 10.56%, **0 truly blank frames**, min
  max-channel deviation 221/255, one 0.30s sub-1% run (the deliberate term-to-core handoff);
  caption band pill-free on 6 frames, all before the first spoken word at 0.179s; the REAL
  tweet on screen **2.833s** measured from pixels, contiguous, at **0.9225x** with zero
  metrics and no fabricated badge; 15 cued events all proved to move ink on the encode; sync
  at **lag 0 on both streams** against the cut (audio r=0.9866 at 1ms, video r=0.9994 at 1
  frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0
  visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; 4 renders, every extra pass bought by an ENCODED-FRAME
  or measured finding and never by geometry.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — smallteams / DIAGRAM (2026-08-13, the lane's port onto run-6 law)

First Diagram of run 6, so the build is also the port: run 5's `hermes_diagram_gen.py` LAYOUT
system (one margin, columns on shared baselines, many-to-one collectors, dashed silhouette
hand-offs, key term centre stage) on the approved run-6 chassis, with the whole run-5
connector layer deleted and replaced by the headless language.

- [lane] **Porting a lane means deleting its connector layer, not tuning it.** run-5 Diagram
  is built on `arrow()` (shaft + filled head), `line_el`/`bus_el` widths in mixed units,
  fixed `strokeDasharray` sweeps and `ring_el()` highlights — four things the current law set
  bans or supersedes. The port is mechanical once stated: arrows -> `chain_line`/`drop_line`
  with butt caps and ZERO heads (direction is the draw sequence), every stroke in viewBox
  space with no `non-scaling-stroke` anywhere, `pathLength="100"` on every swept path, rings
  -> border tweens and glyph fills on the exact referent, `ghost_el` -> `slot()` at the exact
  rect and radius. What survives from run 5 is the thing worth forking: the LAYOUT grammar.
- [gate1] **Make the ghost class unmakeable rather than detectable.** agentreviews found that
  `chain_line(a, b)` with `a > b` renders a negative-width wrapper the audit skips. Gate 1 now
  raises a ghost error, but the cheaper fix is upstream: this file's `chain_line`/`drop_line`
  raise a BUILD error if the span is not authored in reading order, and direction is a
  `reverse` flag on the path. A guard that fires at build time costs no render and no gate.
- [law13] **A merge must be solved in DISTANCE, and it must converge on a REAL target.** The
  bespoke scene is six expert tokens travelling into a three-figure team plate. First cut:
  they rode straight down and faded from 0.42d, and the pre-render sheet showed six
  full-strength white cards parked ON TOP of the team for ~4 frames — grokpublish's
  crossfade-mush class, arriving through a move. `power3.out` covers 66% of the travel in the
  first 30% of the tween, so the fix is to start the dissolve at 0.30d and finish it at 0.80d
  (the visible life is spent ABOVE the plate) and to give each token a horizontal leg onto ITS
  own figure. The figure centres are not guessable: they are solved through the plate's pad
  AND the svg's letterboxing (`_T_SVG_X + cx * _T_SCALE`), which put them at 232.3 / 288.0 /
  343.7 against a naive 172 / 288 / 404.
- [law14] **The REAL TWEET has to survive the 4K scale test, which is what retires the run-5
  card renderer.** hermes rendered a 1000px X-embed card and placed it at 900 render px:
  honest at 1080, a 1.8x UPSCALE the moment the project zooms to 4K. Re-rendering the same
  markup at `device_scale_factor=2` gives a 2000x1026 raster that lands at 1762 physical px
  (0.881x) — a downscale on BOTH copies — and the same pass removes the metrics row from the
  markup entirely, so law 3 cannot be violated by a crop that slips. The ring's rect comes
  from the card's own live DOM (`claim_rect_fraction`), so it lands on the claim paragraph by
  measurement rather than by eye.
- [law3] **"Restates the narration" is the wrong test; "asserts what he does not say" is the
  right one.** The rejected asset here is the post's OWN attached figure — OpenAI's Figure 6,
  a 5-point line chart of outside-occupation message share by workspace seats. It fails on
  three measured grounds (smallest text 18px in a 1294px image = 10.3px at 1080-equivalent at
  the largest non-upscaling size; 1.36-1.43x upscale at the content column; and four bucket
  labels plus five percentages Miguel never speaks). The figure still did its job off-screen:
  its 2-5 and 6-15 seat buckets are where the spoken "1 to 15" comes from, which is what makes
  the coded chip honest.
- [law12] **A brand's own colour can be black.** COLOR MARKS retires monochrome REDUCTIONS,
  not marks whose brand colour happens to be black: `openai.png` ships as the black blossom
  because that IS OpenAI's mark (and ChatGPT's), beside the clay Claude sunburst and the
  four-colour Gemini spark. The test is "is this the official artwork", never "is it colourful".
- [gate2] **A low-ink OPENING is a design question three times in one build, and the answer is
  different each time.** The pre-render sweep and the encode sweep between them found three:
  b0 at 8 frames under 1% (fixed by standing the solid AI tile — the video's SUBJECT, an
  identity rather than a claim — on the axis at frame 0, the grok46 rule), b5 at 0.9s of five
  dashed slots (fixed by landing the figures on "you" instead of "remember", 0.6s earlier),
  and one truly blank frame at 6.53s (max-channel deviation 9/255) where the tweet card's exit
  finished 0.10s BEFORE its own section cut — fixed by pushing the exit ACROSS the cut, where
  the next section's opaque ground covers it. Three symptoms, three different causes; the only
  thing they share is that no gate would have failed the build for any of them.
- [gate2] **A colour-only or single-plate event is invisible to the 3fps dedup, so verify it by
  decoding, not by reading the manifest.** Two states never survived dedup here: the tweet ring
  (a 3.4du stroke on a white card) and the third brand mark arriving in a row of three. Both
  are obvious to a viewer and both were confirmed on exact decodes (ring painted at 5.20 /
  5.80 / 6.20; all three marks and their stubs at 40.60 / 41.00 / 41.30). "Not in the manifest"
  is a statement about the 16x16 grey signature, never about the frame.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — gptvoice / icon (2026-08-13)

First build under the RUN-6 REVIEW VERDICT's three new laws. Six findings, all classes.

- [intake] **A FIFTH raw shape, and it is the one where the pause heuristic does the most
  damage: Scribe folds a restart's whole silence INTO the marker word.** Word 56 `No.` is
  timed **28.659 -> 44.599 — a 15.9-second "word"** — so the ">=1.5s gap before a scripted
  opening" test finds only 2 of the 8 openings in this raw and would have shipped an
  abandoned one. This is stolenapp's finding at ten times the scale, and it settles the
  question: **key on the opening PHRASE with NO gap filter at all**, and let the sign-off
  decide completeness. `GPT Voice` as a two-token phrase also cannot collide with the two
  `ChatGPT` utterances, because `norm("ChatGPT.") == "chatgpt"` — a phrase key is safer than
  a token key for exactly that reason.
- [intake] **Scribe's word ONSETS are systematically ~0.10-0.14s LATE in this recording, and
  the sibling head formula (`scribe_start - 0.22`) can therefore open a short INSIDE the
  discard it is trying to cut.** Here the final `No.` abuts the winning take: measured on a
  10ms RMS/ZCR envelope the marker's last voiced sample is 65.365 and the `G` of GPT starts
  at **65.380**, a 15ms window — while `65.519 - 0.22 = 65.299` lands 65ms inside the marker.
  Calibrate the lateness on a CLEAN opening first (take 1: Scribe 6.639 against a first
  speech sample at 6.540), then set the head from the envelope, assert it lies between the
  two measured events, and add a 0.03s AUDIO-ONLY fade for the decay. The fade cannot touch
  sync: the video and audio source windows stay identical, so it changes amplitude, never
  placement.
- [law13] **The bespoke scene is a SPINE, not a set piece — the same picture carrying a
  different meaning in four consecutive beats beats four different pictures.** One layout
  runs from beat 2 to beat 5 (`[you] — channel — [far end]`) while the far end changes (your
  computer -> a block of text -> ChatGPT -> another person) and the CHANNEL changes state.
  The payoff this buys is impossible with discrete scenes: beat 3 draws the speech-to-text
  era on lane A and leaves lane B as a dashed EMPTY lane for five seconds, and beat 4 flips
  the ground and **fills the lane that was dead** — the viewer already knows what that lane
  means, so the arrival lands as an argument rather than as an entrance.
- [law13] **A waveform lane is worth building from the SHORT'S OWN AUDIO, and it costs 20
  lines.** `envelope(t0, t1, n)` reads fixed windows of `cuts/<id>/audio.wav` and returns
  normalised RMS buckets, so every bar height on screen is the sound in the viewer's ears at
  that moment, and a rebuild is byte-identical. Two rules make it read: expand the curve
  (`x**0.72`) because a speech envelope compressed into 60 design units is otherwise a flat
  kerb, and author the second lane on a **HALF-PITCH offset with one fewer bar**, so when the
  two lanes ride onto one axis at the peak they INTERLEAVE (two voices at once) instead of
  one wave hiding the other. Measured on the encode: constant terracotta ink (61196 -> 61199
  px) with the centroid travelling 164.8 -> 186.8 design units against an authored 187.0 —
  which is also how you prove to a gate that a pop-in marker is a MOVE.
- [law14] **A wrapped claim needs PER-LINE highlight rects, and the union box is a trap.** The
  `@OpenAI` claim wraps across two lines, so the span's `getBoundingClientRect()` returns a
  box that starts at the paragraph's left edge and covers BOTH lines — i.e. a "highlight" over
  the entire tweet, which scopes nothing and quietly defeats law 5. `getClientRects()` returns
  one rect per line; two marker-pen fills on those exact rects read as a pen over a wrapped
  phrase. Emit the fractions from the render script (`plans/x_card_<id>.json`) so the
  generator lands them by measurement instead of hermes' hand-tuned 0.030/0.418/0.940/0.272.
  Also: render the card at `device_scale_factor=3` (3000px for a 1000px card) so it is a 0.61x
  DOWNSCALE at 4K, and never draw the metrics row at all — there is then nothing to crop and
  nothing to leak.
- [law12] **"Colour marks" has a boundary, and it is the brand's own palette.** Three of the
  four marks here are coloured official artwork; OpenAI's blossom ships BLACK, because black
  IS OpenAI's brand colour — law 12 retires monochrome REDUCTIONS of marks that have a
  palette, and OpenAI has none. The corollary is a placement rule: a mark whose artwork IS a
  rounded tile (the ChatGPT app icon, green #74AA9C) goes BARE at the node rect, because a
  coloured square inside our white plate is plate-on-plate; a transparent GLYPH (Claude,
  Gemini) goes on the house white plate. And a registry MISS is cheap to close: the official
  ChatGPT icon was fetched from Wikimedia, rasterised unmodified and registered before use.
- [gate2] **A dissolve that ends ON a section boundary always spends its last frame as a
  ghost.** The tweet card's 0.18s fade ended exactly at the b0/b1 cut, so frame 118 (3.933s)
  held a 20%-opacity card on cream and scored **0.05% top-zone ink — the only under-1% frame
  in the render**. There is no fade curve that fixes this; the fix is to let the CUT be the
  exit, which is the grammar every other beat in the short already uses. After: **0 of 1031
  frames under 1%**, min 1.22%, median 7.78%.
- [gptvoice_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1031 frames, 34.368s container /
  34.339 authored, 30 captions, 7 sections, 50 direct section children; take detection on an
  8-opening raw carrying BOTH marker forms with exactly 1 complete take, asserted against two
  hand-verified constants plus a measured head window; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings on both
  rounds** on the 1080 design copy (97 ids, 0 duplicates, 51 tween selectors all resolving, 0
  untweened section children, 14 `data-overlap-ok` — 11 wave lanes, 1 connector, 2 markers —
  0 `data-bleed`, 0 `non-scaling-stroke`, 0 caption-echo trigrams, 0 caption-identity
  collisions over 5 text atoms, 0 glyph-centring warnings); Gate 2 **29 distinct states from
  103 samples**, 74 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 4 pop-in markers and 1 stillness marker all
  resolved on exact decodes, all 29 states read plus four native-4K crops; `idle_motion_scan`
  frames=137 idle_drift=no long_static=no; render sweep **0 frames under 1% top-zone ink, 0
  blank**, min 1.22% median 7.78%, min max-channel deviation 215; caption band pill-free on 2
  frames, both before the first spoken word at 0.039s; the REAL tweet on screen **3.967s
  measured from pixels** against a 4.0s ceiling, contiguous, zero metrics; 4 official marks,
  3 of them coloured, none upscaled; sync at **lag 0 on both streams** (audio r=0.9769 at 1ms,
  video r=0.9995 at 1 frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO remux; Gate 3 **pass on the

## Run 6 (impeccable) — builders / counter (2026-08-13, first build under the three new laws)

- [law13] **A bespoke visualization needs an EXACT unit, and the unit is what makes it an
  argument instead of a decoration.** THE BUILDER FIELD is a dotted globe of exactly 250 dots,
  because 1/250 = 0.4% — the only number this take speaks — so "one lit dot" IS his statistic
  rather than a picture of it. Two geometry findings make that count buildable: (a) a hex
  lattice clipped to a circle can only land on the counts its symmetry allows (scanning the
  spacing from 9 to 14 design units at R=112 gives **241 or 253 and nothing between**), while a
  Vogel/sunflower disc gives uniform density at ANY N; (b) the `+0.5` term in
  `r_i = R*sqrt((i+0.5)/N)` is load-bearing — without it points 0-3 sit at 0 / 0.06R / 0.09R and
  overlap at any usable dot radius, and with it the minimum spacing is 10.95 units against a 3.8
  unit radius. The whole short then runs on ONE object in four states (250 grey → ONE lit →
  all 250 → 88 lit), which is also what makes it verifiable: counting connected terracotta
  components inside the field's own box on the shipped encode returns **0 / 2 (dot+ring) / 250 /
  250 / 88**, exactly the authored states. Report blobs, not area — an area ratio reads the
  single enlarged, ringed dot as "10 dots".
- [law12] **COLOR MARKS makes a vendor's PACKAGING visible in a way monochrome never did.**
  `codex-color.png` is the flower on an OPAQUE white rounded square; on a white plate that ships
  as **a plate inside our plate** (the run-5 nous/openrouter class). The monochrome reductions
  the run-6 siblings used hid this for a month. The fix is a connectivity test rather than a
  colour edit: near-white pixels that REACH the image border are packaging and become
  transparent, near-white pixels that do not (the `>_` knockout inside the flower) are the mark.
  Two thresholds matter — build the white mask on `alpha > 16` and take the bbox on `alpha > 24`,
  or the ground's ANTIALIASED edge survives, the trim reports the full 640x640 canvas and
  silently does nothing. Only a full-resolution 4K crop found it; the 3fps gate-2 thumbnails and
  gate 3 both passed the frame.
- [logos] **With trimmed artwork, optical sizing becomes arithmetic.** Solve the rendered box from
  the TRIMMED aspect so `mean(w, h) = 0.56` of the plate: a 640x401 mascot lands at 57.8x36.2 and
  a 480x480 flower at 47.0x47.0 design units — both mean 47.0, so two completely different
  silhouettes read at the same size without a taste argument.
- [law14] **The REAL TWEET artifact is an X-STYLE CARD RENDERED FROM THE API PAYLOAD, not a
  screenshot of x.com.** The law names hermes' `tweet_block()` as canonical, and hermes' image is
  `shorts_run1/x_cards/card_*.png` — Playwright rendering the fetched text, avatar and handle in
  X's visual language, cropped to the crucial region. Three things that bite: screenshot with
  `omit_background=True` or the template's body colour ships as grey triangles in the card's
  rounded corners; render at `deviceScaleFactor=2` so 492 design units at the zoom:2 4K root
  (1845 physical px) is a **0.92x downscale** instead of a 1.85x blow-up; and when the display
  name and the @handle are the same string ("@levelsio"), print it once — printing the real
  duplicate reads as a bug.
- [law14] **"Claims Miguel doesn't say" is now a placement question, not a rejection.** This
  card's paragraph carries "(about 30 million people)", which the take never says. Under the
  2026-08-12 verdict the ring scoping the claim is the answer, and the alternative — cropping
  mid-paragraph — would be editing the source. Gate 3 passed it first call with 0 semantic
  errors, which is the first evidence that the new law works as written.
- [law3] **Key the card's screen-time detector on the ONE photographic region, not on a
  near-white area threshold.** This short also carries a 260x180 white app-window plate, which
  puts an area threshold within 1.4x of the card. The avatar's GREEN pixels are unique in the
  whole composition: 98 px when the card is up, **0** when it is not. Measured 3.533s against the
  4.0s ceiling — after the first encode measured 4.200s and no gate reported it.
- [gate2] **A slow staggered wave is the honest way to fill a windup, and it doubles as the
  stillness fix.** "The people who are going to be able to pull it off in this new economy" is a
  4.3s windup with nothing to show. Dimming 162 of the 250 dots over **2.4s** (one event, one
  ease) IS the claim — not everyone pulls it off — and it kept `frame_review` at **0 stillness
  markers** where a 0.3s dim would have collapsed 27.4-31.7 into a single state. A long duration
  is not idle motion; a loop is.
- [frame-0] **Two openings failed the ink sweep for the same reason, and both fixes were free.**
  A beat may open on its SUBJECT (the product's wireframe standing on the axis) but never on
  nothing, and a beat's structural chrome (two empty bar tracks) must be authored opaque rather
  than faded in over 0.26s — 5 frames under 1% top-zone ink is the whole difference. The
  surviving 3-frame run is the agentreviews metric artifact: `rgba(20,20,22,0.12)` tracks on cream
  deviate by 26/255, under the 34 threshold, on a frame that was extracted and looked at.
- [law4] **The caption-identity guard fires on the first single-word chip you write.** "AGENCY"
  against a pill reading exactly "agency," is the stolenapp defect, and the answer generalises:
  add information rather than delete the item. "ENOUGH AGENCY" is his own qualifier and says the
  thing the two brand marks cannot — the account is not the requirement, the amount of agency is.
- [all] **A label is part of the object it names.** When the product cube rides from the axis into
  its seat, its label rides with the same distance, duration and ease; authored at the seat it
  labelled empty ground for 0.94s. Same root cause as grokpublish's connector that failed to
  travel with its plate, in a lane with no connectors at all.
- [layout] **Stacking two chips cost the callback its scale.** Beat 6's requirement pills stacked
  vertically capped the field at R=84 — a visibly smaller globe than the one the short had been
  arguing on. Side by side in one 492-unit row they fit above the field at its full R=112, so the
  callback is literally the same object. Symmetry also matters: both empty seats are authored at
  the cut, because "what does it take" IS two empty seats, and bringing the second in later left
  one slot floating off-axis for 7.5s.
- [paperwork] **The blanket-rename trap has a second sighting.** Forking the sync verifier renamed
  slowfrontier's +79.0ms calibration median into this video's id — another video's measurement,
  presented as mine, inside the JSON a clerk audits. Read every inherited constant after a rename.
- [builders_counter] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1197 frames, 39.915s container /
  39.900 authored, 38 captions, 8 sections, 47 atoms, 250-dot field asserted in every state at

  EOF-capped; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings across 3 rounds** on the 1080 design copy (111 ids, 0

  Gate 2 **50 distinct states from 120 samples**, 70 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 0 stillness

## Run 6 (impeccable) — perplexity / icon (2026-08-13)

First build written to all three RUN-6 REVIEW VERDICT laws at once: colour marks, a bespoke
scene-level visualization, and the real tweet.

- [law12] **"Original brand colour" is not the same as "colourful", and OpenAI is the case that
  proves it.** The verdict retires monochrome reductions, so the reflex is to reach for the most
  saturated file in the registry. OpenAI's knot has no colour version: black IS the mark, and
  `openai.png` ships unmodified beside a #22B8CD Perplexity and a #D97757 Claude. The ruling to
  write down is per-mark and factual — *what colour is this mark in its own brand system* — not
  "pick the colourful one". The registry's monochrome variants (`perplexity.png`,
  `claude-black.png`) stay on disk and were deliberately not chosen, which is worth recording
  precisely because a clerk cannot tell a deliberate choice from an unexamined default.
- [law12] **Optical mark sizing is now an ink-AREA problem, not just an extent problem, because
  colour marks differ far more than silhouettes did.** All three marks here are near full-bleed
  (extent 0.94-1.00 of their canvas) but their ink AREA runs 27.7% (Perplexity's open line mark),
  36.9% (OpenAI's knot) and 39.7% (Claude's solid sunburst). Padding solved on extent alone makes
  the open mark read small. Pads: 0.19 / 0.23 / 0.23, decided on decoded pixels in ten minutes.
- [gsap] **A scale tween inside an SVG needs a transform origin, and GSAP FOLDS the origin shift
  into the element's final matrix — so a wrong origin parks the element permanently off its seat,
  and no gate in this factory can see it.** `pan_drop()` first passed `svgOrigin:"230 122"` (the
  balance's pivot) to a fromTo that animated opacity, y AND scale. At the end of the tween, with
  scale back at 1, the product measured `matrix(1,0,0,1,-27.92,-15.87)` — 28 design units left and
  16 up, i.e. hanging outside its own bowl for the rest of the beat — and the coin inherited
  `(18.4,-16.3)`, which its later shrink then scaled. Re-aiming at the element's own bbox centre
  (`transformOrigin:"50% 50%"`) shrank the residual to `(-4.41,-3.43)` but did NOT remove it. The
  fix that removes it is to **drop the scale leg**: a pure translate has no origin and therefore no
  residual (measured `matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)`, with the product's centre exactly on its bowl's in all
  three tilt states). Gate 1 treats the whole illustration as one atom, gate 2 samples 3fps
  thumbnails, gate 3 passed the video — the only detector was reading `getComputedStyle().transform`
  off the paused timeline, which costs one Playwright call.
- [law13] **A physical metaphor's PAYOFF has to be caused by something already on screen, and the
  cheapest cause is the object you were going to make smaller anyway.** The balance's first design
  had the peak ("which is a steal") slam the beam further with nothing added — a rotation with no
  cause, which is exactly what law 12's plausibility rule bans. The second design rained three new
  tiles into the pan to justify it, which is a new object at the peak and a cramped one at 22
  design units. The shipped answer needs neither: the COIN COLLAPSES to 0.55 and the beam answers,
  because a lighter price side IS a heavier value side. One object, one cue, and the metaphor's
  meaning ("a steal") is the animation itself rather than a caption under it.
- [law13] **Shrink about the CONTACT POINT, not the centre, or the object levitates out of the
  thing that is holding it.** The coin scaled about `"50% 50%"` lifts its own bottom edge by
  `r(1-s)` = 12 design units and ends the beat hovering 8 units above the bowl (measured: coin
  bottom 286 vs bowl top 301). `transformOrigin:"50% 100%"` keeps the contact point fixed — the
  8px overlap into the bowl is identical before and after the shrink — and the matrix is then an
  exact pure scale about the bbox bottom centre, verifiable by arithmetic.
- [composition] **Paint the container LAST if you want it to hold something.** A pan whose bowl is
  drawn before its contents reads as a coin *in front of* a bowl; the same geometry with the bowl
  painted after reads as a coin *in* it, because the bowl's front edge covers the object's bottom.
  Free, and it is the difference between an illustration and a pile of shapes.
- [composition] **Optical centring must be solved on the INK when the box carries motion headroom.**
  The balance's box is 220 design units tall only because its pans need 45.6 units of travel each
  way; its ink at rest spans 158.5. `otop(220)` hung the whole illustration 35 units low in the
  band. `otop(ink_h) - ink_top` is the general form, and any beat whose element reserves room for
  a move needs it.
- [law14] **The factory's "actual tweet" has always been a rendered card, and that is the right
  reading of the REAL TWEET law.** hermes's `tweet_block()` ships
  `shorts_run1/x_cards/card_Teknium_*.png` — a faithful X rendering of the fetched payload, not a
  screenshot scraped from x.com. So Law 14's "never a coded re-creation" bans re-typesetting the
  CLAIM in our own design language; it does not ban rendering the post's own text, avatar, handle
  and badge from the API JSON. This build renders at 2000px (so the 492-unit column is a 0.92x
  DOWNSCALE, never an upscale), hard-fails if the paragraph split does not rejoin to
  `display_text` byte for byte, and writes each paragraph's box as a FRACTION of the card so the
  highlight ring is seated from a measurement instead of an eyeball.
- [verify] **"Is the source card on screen?" needs TWO windows, because every dark beat in an Icon
  short carries white plates.** A single "is this region white?" probe reported a phantom 3.0s card
  over the hook (the window sat on the ChatGPT plate); moving it reported a phantom 2.1s card (the
  new window sat inside the hook pair's PARKED position, 78 design units right of their final
  seats, for the 1.9s before they ride). The shipped probe requires white INSIDE the card's bottom
  padding AND charcoal in the zone's left margin at the same time, and the window is chosen against
  a written list of every white rect any dark section ever occupies, parked positions included.
  Result: exactly one segment, 5.900-9.533s = 3.633s, under the 4.0s law-3 ceiling.
- [claim-sync] **Cue a noun's icon on the NOUN, not on the verb that governs it.** `find("read
  images,")` returns the start of *read*, so the photo tile landed 0.44s early and a 3fps review
  frame showed it while the pill still said "you. It can read". Anchoring on `"images,
  documents."` moves it to 10.54 — measured 0 dark px in the tile's own box at 10.55 and 31280 at
  10.65. The anchor string is the cue; read it as a sentence, not as a lookup key.
- [gate2] **A caption pill that CHANGES WIDTH is a pop-in marker, because the review crop includes
  the seam.** Two of this build's five markers (14.67s, 24.33s) had no visual event at all: the
  balance measured 184903 dark px identically at 23.90, 24.00, 24.20, 24.33, 24.50 and 24.60 while
  the pill's terracotta area went 149469 -> 86320 at 24.20. Check the pill before hunting the
  canvas.
- [perplexity_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 930 frames, 31.019s container /
  30.980s authored, 30 captions, 8 sections, 40 direct section children; take detection on a
