  frames=124 idle_drift=no long_static=no; render sweep **0 frames under 1% top-zone ink, 0
  blank**, min 6.53%, median 15.61%, min max-channel deviation 197 — the strongest ink record in
  the run-6 fleet; caption band pill-free on 6 frames, all before the first spoken word at 0.199s;
  real tweet **3.633s** measured from pixels with a two-window probe; 3 brand marks in their own
  colours at 0.42x intrinsic, card at 0.92x, nothing upscaled; deepest authored ink design y=368.0
  against a 400 floor; sync at **lag 0 on both streams** (audio r=0.9799 at 1ms, video r=0.9987 at
  1 frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual
  errors, 0 semantic errors, 0 visual minor notes**; 2 renders, the extra one bought by a single
  ENCODED-FRAME finding and never by geometry.

- **2026-08-13 REVIEW (5-short round) — two new laws + verdicts.** Miguel's per-video review:
  builders "great short and great viz"; hermesjourney "absolutely amazing… this is the level of
  quality I expect" (now a named Law-13 reference build); perplexity "FANTASTIC use of the scale"
  but the 2x2-grid connector reads off; gptvoice highlight praised but every wave/lane beat drifted
  off its anchors; smallteams "really nice" except person glyphs off-center in their cards at the
  start. New laws: **CENTERED COMPOSITION (Law 15)** — mediating elements sit on the axis between
  their anchors; varying-size sequences keep a stable optical center (normalize or fade in place).
  **NO DEAD SLOTS (Law 16)** — every drawn lane/slot must activate in its beat; deliberate
  emptiness as storytelling does not survive review ("lost real estate for nothing"). Fix passes
  ordered for gptvoice, perplexity, smallteams before publish; builders + hermesjourney approved
  as-built.

- **Gate 1 glyph centring now covers composed cards and FAILS builds (2026-08-13, approved by
  Miguel — "we need to make the best shorts system ever").** The old check required a glyph to be
  its plate's ONLY child and merely warned, which is exactly how the smallteams person figures
  (glyph + label composition) shipped off-centre. New: (1) solo-glyph violations are ERRORS;
  (2) composed cards get a NEAR-MISS check per axis — a glyph whose centre lands within 15% of the
  card's span from the card centre but outside the 2.0px tolerance is intended-centred-plus-bug;
  deliberate side placements (25-40% off-axis) are never judged; svg/img children under 16px are
  decoration and exempt; `data-glyph-ok` still opts out. Verified: synthetic +5px composed card
  fails the build at the production 0.5s step (blip demotion means very short clips need 2+
  samples — unchanged general behavior); all 10 untouched approved projects re-audit 0/0.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — perplexity / icon FIX PASS: the 2x2 grid connector (2026-08-13)

Miguel's review: "perplexity computer is not bad but on the 2x2 grid of elements, the line
connection between perplexity/claude with the grid looks off... FANTASTIC use of the scale."
One defect, in b4; the balance scale was praised and not touched. Render 3 of this build.

- [geometry] **`chain_line` is an edge-to-edge primitive between two BOXES, and a 2x2 GROUP is
  not a box.** The shipped b4 joined each mark to the group with one horizontal bar ending on
  `GRP_X`, the group's bounding-box left edge, at `LINK_CY`, the axis between the two anchors.
  Those two constraints are individually correct and jointly fatal: the block's own centre line
  is the 14du GAP between its tile rows, so the bar's butt end landed on a bounding box that has
  no ink there. Measured on the shipped encode, the terminus sat **12.91du (48.4px at 4K) from
  the nearest tile pixel** — and that pixel was diagonal, on the top tile's 15du corner arc; the
  bar's own row ran 107du to the right without touching anything. A connector whose destination
  is a SET must be a fork, not a line: `fork_side()` here (the horizontal mirror of `tree_bus`,
  precedented by agentreviews' `tree_up` — "a mirror is not a new primitive") puts the stem on
  the same axis and one stub per ROW on the facing tile's straight side. Fixed: all four termini
  now measure **2.13du** from tile ink, which is the plate's own 2du border, i.e. flush.
- [gate1] **The floating-connector law does not run on SVG connectors, and its 14px tolerance
  would have passed this anyway.** `isRule` requires a `.rule`/`.ruleY` child, so every
  `svg_free` connector in the icon lane is invisible to that check — 0 warnings meant "never
  evaluated", not "clean". Worse, had it run: `CONNECTOR_END_TOL = 14.0` and the terminus sat
  13.2px below the top tile's bottom edge, passing by 0.8px. Both are wrapper-BOX tests; neither
  can see a stroke ending 48px from ink inside a wrapper that nearly touches. The generalisable
  rule is that box-proximity is not ink-proximity wherever the target has a corner radius — a
  15du radius moves the real ink 11.6du away from the box corner by construction.
- [gate2] **A 2.6du stroke is invisible to the 16x16 grayscale dedup, so every connector build
  reads as a pop-in.** The 17.00s marker fired identically on both encodes. Resolution is always
  the same and always cheap: count the accent's pixels inside the connector's own design box on
  exact decodes. Left fork 0 → 400 → 534 → 4146 → 4579 → 5215 → 5223 over 15.80-16.40, right
  fork 0 → 513 → 2896 → 4305 → 5036 → 5238 over 16.40-16.90. Progressive, not a pop.
- [composition] **A rail that overshoots its outermost stub is chrome, not a join.** The first
  fork ran its rail the full 190du height of the block, as a bracket. It seats identically and
  looks wrong: 44du of free rail past each end reads as a frame drawn AROUND the group instead
  of a connection INTO it, and it is the floating tail the grammar bans. `tree_bus`'s rails end
  exactly on their first and last stub; the mirror must too. Rendered both, looked, dropped it —
  the grokpublish v5 lesson holds, the only way to pick a connector treatment is to see it.
- [method] **Prove a fix pass is surgical with a frame diff, not with a claim.** Mean absolute
  RGB against the previous encode over 21 samples: visual zone 0.0000 outside b4 (11 of 15
  samples exactly zero, the rest under 0.072 of 255 = encoder noise), 0.115 → 0.523 inside it,
  and **exactly 0.0000 at 15.0s** — the tiles' regroup ride is pixel-identical and the first
  difference appears only when the fork starts drawing at 15.86. Cut, audio, captions, tweet
  card, balance scale and outro are bit-stable, which is the claim the review verdict requires.
- [perplexity_icon v2] Gates re-run green: Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings** with the build guards
  unchanged (89 ids, 41 tween targets, deepest ink y=368.0); Gate 2 **37 distinct states from 93
  samples**, 56 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 0 stillness markers, 5 pop-in markers — the same
  profile as v1; deterministic rescan 0 dead frames, min ink 6.5284%, source card 3.633s, sync
  lag 0 on both streams with no remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call**, 0 visual errors, 0
  semantic errors, 0 visual minor notes. One render spent.

## Run 6 — smallteams / DIAGRAM, FIX PASS v2 (2026-08-13, Miguel's centring verdict)

Miguel on the shipped short: *"really nice, just the fact that at the beginning the people are
not centered for some reason."* One defect, one beat (the b0 hook), and the "for some reason" is
the whole lesson: **the layout was right and an entrance moved it.**

- [gsap][law15] **GSAP pivots an SVG scale tween at `(bbox.width/2, bbox.height/2)` taken as an
  ABSOLUTE point in the element's local user space — it ignores `bbox.x`/`bbox.y` — and bakes an
  origin compensation into the element's transform ATTRIBUTE that SURVIVES the tween's own end
  state.** With `transformOrigin:"50% 50%"` on the three team figures (bbox x 28..92, y 35..128,
  so half-size (32, 46.5) but true centre (60|150|240, 81.5)) every figure came to rest at
  `transform="matrix(1,0,0,1,-8.96,-13.02)"` = `-(32, 46.5) x (1 - 0.72)`, the from-scale. That is
  **-5.54du, -8.06du** — 21 x 30 physical px at 4K — for the whole 3.72s hook, while the byte-
  identical plate in b2/b3/b4/outro (no scale tween on `.f*`) was centred all along. Decoded
  proof: b0 ink-centre-vs-plate-centre measured (-5.73, -6.93) at 1.60s against (-0.13, +1.07) at
  7.20s in the same short. **`svgOrigin` does not fix it and makes it worse** — the same residual
  divided by 0.72, (-12.44445, -18.08334).
- [gsap] **The fix is authoring, not a tween argument.** An 8-variant harness against gsap 3.14.2,
  each variant measured for END residual AND mid-tween centre drift: `transformOrigin` residual
  -8.96/-13.02; `svgOrigin` -12.44/-18.08; wrapper-translate + origin `0 0` ends clean but drifts
  10.4 x 15.1px mid-tween; `transform-box:fill-box` + no origin var ends clean but drifts 9.1 x
  11.4px; `clearProps` ends clean but pops from the wrong pivot. **Only one variant is clean on
  both axes: author the shapes with their INK BOX AT THE LOCAL ORIGIN, place them with a wrapper
  `transform="translate(...)"`, put `transform-box:fill-box; transform-origin:50% 50%` on the
  group, and pass NO origin var to the tween.** Then GSAP's `(w/2, h/2)` pivot IS the true centre:
  0.00du drift at every sample and a pure-translate matrix at rest. Rule for every generator:
  **a group you are going to scale gets its own box; percentages are for elements, not for GSAP.**
- [law15] **A dashed seat is the person's card, so it is centred ON THE PERSON, not on a round
  number.** The seats were authored at y=14 h=128 (centre 78) while the figure ink centres at
  81.5, so every person sat 3.5 user units (2.17du) low inside its own dashed card at the hook —
  21 units of air above the head against 14 below the feet. Seat y=17.5 makes seat centre =
  figure centre = 0.00. Solve the placeholder from the thing that lands in it, never the reverse.
- [gates] **This class is invisible to all three gates by construction, and that is the finding
  worth keeping.** Gate 1 measures the plate's `svg` BOX (dead centre — `plate()`'s
  `pad - PLATE_BORDER` inset was already correct) and skipped composed cards entirely; Gate 2's
  16x16 grey signature cannot see a 20px shift inside a plate; Gate 3 passed v1 on the first call
  with 0 notes. A human caught it in one viewing. The same-day hardening of `geometry_audit.py`
  (composed-card near-miss check, glyph violations promoted to ERRORS) closes the static half —
  but a residual TWEEN transform is only visible if you measure the live DOM at the tween's END,
  which is now the check to run whenever a glyph is scaled.
- [discipline] **Fix the named defect, and prove the rest did not move.** The 0.93du offset of the
  team glyph's own ink centre (81.5 vs the viewBox's 80) is inside tolerance and identical in
  every scene Miguel approved, so it was left alone rather than shifting approved frames for no
  perceptible gain; the expert token's -2.87du person is a deliberate person+spark composition in
  the scene he praised. Evidence that nothing else changed: same 1310 frames, same 43.669s
  container, same 40 Gate-2 states from 131 samples with the same 10 pop-in markers, same tweet
  screen time 2.767s, same ink sweep (0 under 1%, 0 blank, min 1.06%, median 4.41%), sync lag 0
  on both streams, and every geometry constant (`FIG_CX`/`FIG_CY`/`EXP_TRAVEL_*`) unchanged so the
  absorb still converges on the same three head centres.
- [smallteams_diagram v2] Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings** (twice, the second against the hardened
  composed-card audit); Gate 2 **40 states, all read**, centring confirmed by eye and by a
  before/after crop of the same 1.60s frame; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual, 0
  semantic, 0 minor notes**; after-measurements (-0.13, +1.07)du at the hook — the exact figure
  the untouched b2/b3 plates measure — and 0.00du drift through the pop itself. 1 render.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — gptvoice / icon, FIX PASS v2 (2026-08-13, laws 15 + 16)

Miguel's review kept the story, the waveform mechanic and the two-colour back-and-forth
("we do have the back and forth with two different colours") and rejected the geometry of
the channel in all four beats that carry it. Five findings.

- [law15] **Centring is a GRAMMAR, not a constant: an element that mediates between two
  anchors is CENTRED while it is alone, and splits SYMMETRICALLY when a second one joins.**
  The first build authored the channel as two PERMANENT lanes at ±40du, which is centred as
  a pair and wrong at every instant one lane is empty — a solo wave floated 40.0du above the
  plates' centre line for 2.7s in b2, 1.2s in b4 and 3.5s in b5 (measured on the encode:
  accent-ink centroid −150.0px against a 768.75px axis). The fix that makes this
  unmakeable is an authoring trick: author the lane at its SPLIT seat and park it on the
  axis with `ride_y`, so the solo state and the split state are the same element and the
  split is a real 18du move rather than two independently authored layouts.
- [law15] **The right split distance is the ANCHOR'S OWN BAND.** At ±18du on a 60du lane the
  two lanes occupy 157..253 — exactly the 96du vertical extent of the plates they join — and
  read as one mass centred on the axis. The number was not taste: the old build reached that
  state for 2.8s as the tail of a 22du merge, and that frame is the one Miguel's own review
  singled out as reading right. ±40 reads as two rows with a hole; ±18 reads as one channel.
- [law16] **Deleting a dead slot COSTS INK, and the replacement has to be the beat's own
  grammar.** Removing b3's never-filling lane took the whole-video sweep from 0 frames under
  1% top-zone ink to 14 in one 0.467s run (min 0.709% at 10.933s) — the dead lane had been
  *balancing the metric* while reading as broken to the eye. The fix was not chrome: the
  voice wave was the ONE wave in the short with no dashed silhouette, so it got the landing
  slot every other wave already had, and it fills 0.42s later on its own cue. After: 3
  frames in one 0.100s run, min 0.969%. **Plan the replacement in the same edit as the
  deletion** — a beat that loses a drawn element always opens thinner.
- [measure] **"Is it centred" must be measured on ACCENT-ONLY ink, never on all ink.** Dashed
  slots and white plates on cream contribute border pixels that drag an all-ink centroid
  toward the axis and hide the defect: b3 measured −10.5du on all ink and **−41.75du on
  accent-only**, and the difference was entirely the dead lane sitting below the composition.
  One channel test isolates the accent on both grounds — `r - b > 40 and r > 110` — because
  cream (246,241,234) scores 12, charcoal (36,36,39) scores −3 and the ChatGPT green
  (116,170,156) scores −40, while both terracottas score 138 and 125.
- [gate2] **A composition fix can REMOVE gate-2 markers, and that is corroborating evidence.**
  Two of the first ship's four pop-in markers disappeared without a single timing change:
  11.00 (the b2→b3 section cut) stopped registering a step once beat 3 opened on a complete
  skeleton instead of a half-empty one, and 21.67 (the lane merge) stopped registering once
  the merge travelled 18du from a seat already on the axis instead of 22du from 40du out.
- [gptvoice_icon v2] Shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1031 frames, 34.368s container /
  34.339 authored, 30 captions unchanged, 7 sections, 46 direct section children (−4);
  Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings on both rounds**; Gate 2 **29 distinct states from 103
  samples**, 74 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 2 pop-in markers both previously adjudicated,
  `idle_motion_scan` frames=137 idle_drift=no long_static=no; render sweep min 0.969%,
  median 7.488%, one 0.100s under-1% run, 0 blank, min max-channel deviation 215; the REAL
  tweet still 3.967s from pixels, contiguous, zero metrics; **decoded audio md5-identical to
  the approved encode** (4d3f912a39c027d212d1b8d41a9a689d), so lag-0 sync carries over with
  no remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; after-
  measurements: solo lanes +0.16 / −0.04 / −0.04 / −0.05du, split pairs −18.08/+17.68,
  −18.07/+17.92 and −18.07/+18, the b4 merge −0.04du, the b3 chain −1.75du (full-ink
  +0.41du), and the channel and both b5 segments now centred on 288 exactly (they leaned
  1du right). 2 renders, the extra one bought by the ink measurement above.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — mathvoice / KINETIC (2026-08-13, laws 12-16 in the Kinetic lane)

The longest raw of the batch (540.88s, 836 words, 33 openings) and the lane's first
build under the three 2026-08-13 laws. Seven findings.

- [intake] **A raw can contain ZERO discard markers of the punctuated kind and still be
  fully detectable — but only if the marker rule was already demoted to a bound.** This
  540s recording has 33 `using only` openings, 32 truncations ("f-", "s-", "pro...",
  "mathem...") and **not one spoken "No."**. A build that required `^no[.,!?]$` to fire
  would have nothing to key on; slowfrontier's demotion of the marker rule to a LOWER
  BOUND is what makes the raw tractable, and here bound and content rule agree exactly
  at word 718. Also the fourth sighting of grok46's stem rule with a new twist: the
  opening key must be a PHRASE, because the bare stem `using` fires 38 times and one of
  those five non-openings is INSIDE the winning take ("...problems USING the new feature
  by ChatGPT"). A token key would have split the take it exists to ship.
- [law15] **This lane gets horizontal centring for free and that is exactly why it can
  lose it.** Every atom a Kinetic build normally draws is a full-frame-width centred text
  box whose centre cannot drift, so `left_for()` and `ctxt()` have carried the x axis
  unexamined through five shipped shorts. The moment a beat draws a RUN OF BOXES the
  freebie stops: the first cut of the climb drew six columns one at a time, left to
  right, and every partial state sat in the left half of the frame with the right half
  empty — smallteams' defect, in the axis nobody was watching. The fix is not a
  horizontal park: it is to **draw every slot from the beat's first frame** and animate
  the property that carries the meaning (height), which makes the composition centred by
  construction, keeps the opening frame at 4.7% ink instead of 1.5%, and satisfies LAW 16
  before the beat starts. `z.moved()` now asserts the centre of every tween-reached state,
  because `_check()` only ever sees AUTHORED rects.
- [law16] **A payoff line is a promise the picture has to keep.** The collapse first
  landed as six SEPARATE flat segments under a line reading `SAME STARTING LINE` — a
  caption its own picture contradicts. Closing the gaps needed a number, not a taste
  call: each column widens about its own centre to the pitch plus **1.5 design units**,
  which is the largest overlap that stays under the geometry audit's 3.0-PHYSICAL-px
  collision floor (1.5 x 1.875 = 2.81px, and `intersect()` gates on ox > 3.0) and the
  smallest that removes the antialiasing hairline. Measured on the shipped encode: 880
  consecutive cream pixels along the bar row, **zero non-solid pixels** at any of the
  five joins. Corner radii went to zero in the same edit — at radius 3 the merged floor
  pinched at every seam.
- [timing] **"Every element lands on its word" is not the same as "every element gets
  read", and only the CUE TABLE shows the difference.** Render 1 passed all three gates
  and was wrong: LAW 9's key term `CHATGPT VOICE` completed at 13.52 against a 13.779
  section cut, so the term the law puts centre stage existed whole for **0.26s — eight
  frames** — and the bespoke scene's payoff lockup completed at 21.02 against a 21.319
  cut, 0.30s. No gate reports this: Gate 1 measures geometry, Gate 2 samples at 3fps and
  dedups stillness away, Gate 3 passed with zero notes. The check is arithmetic —
  `section_end - (cue + entrance_duration)` for the LAST atom of every section — and the
  fix is to move the boundary onto a later spoken cue, not to speed the entrance up. Four
  boundaries moved (b4 to "frontier", b6 to "can", b8/b9 to "very close") and a fourth
  atom that could not clear the bar was retired outright: b7's `SO DOES THE REST` landed
  at 25.62 against a 25.859 cut, and the section that follows IS the rest, so the argument
  is completed by the cut instead. Minimum terminal hold went 0.26s -> 0.76s.
- [law13] **A bespoke scene can be built from the LANE'S OWN material, and it should be.**
  No new glyph vocabulary was invented here: the climb is bars, which is what this lane
  already draws as rules and strikes, and the whole scene is `scaleY + scaleX + y` on six
  divs. What makes it an argument rather than a chart is that both halves are the same six
  elements (the ground rises into a climb in b5, the climb falls back to ground in b6),
  the collapse has TWO stages because he says "dropped **again** significantly", and the
  ground inverts on the word "dropped" so the section cut IS the drop. Cost: 60 lines.
- [law15] **Two centred configurations make every frame between them centred, and that is
  a design tool, not a coincidence.** The collapse interpolates linearly from a centred
  full-climb state to a centred flat state, so every intermediate frame is centred without
  a single extra keyframe — the half-collapse stage exists because of the word "again",
  not because centring needed it. Verified on the ENCODE, not asserted: the resting bar
  measures 220.0..241.6 design y against an authored 220.0..242.0, and with its token row
  the scene ink runs 186.0..241.6 for a centre of **213.8 against the axis 214.0**.
- [law14] **A card whose job is provenance must not invent provenance.** Two things the
  sibling template would have shipped: a hard-coded blue verified check (this author's
  payload says `verified: false` — a badge nobody earned, on the one surface that exists
  to be believed) and four grey corner notches, because a Playwright ELEMENT screenshot
  keeps the page paint in the corners a border-radius cuts away. `omit_background=True`
  with a transparent body fixes the second; reading `verified` from the payload fixes the
  first. Also the third sighting of the erdos trap: the handed URL was @gdb's "congrats on
  the amazing result!" quoting the mathematician's own post.
- [mathvoice_kinetic] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1114 frames, 37.141s
  container / 37.13 authored, 33 captions, 10 sections, 46 direct section children; take
  detection on a 33-opening raw with zero punctuated markers and exactly one sign-off,
  asserted against two hand-verified constants plus a measured head window (onset 501.930,
  Scribe 30ms late, 2.08s of silence before the take, no audio fade needed); the cut kept
  all 118 spoken words; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings across 4 rounds** on the 1080 design
  copy (111 ids, 0 duplicates, 47 tween selectors all resolving, 0 untweened section
  children, 2 `data-overlap-ok` — the two marker fills — 0 `data-bleed`, 0
  `non-scaling-stroke`, 0 caption-echo trigrams, 0 caption-identity collisions over 17
  registered text atoms); Gate 2 **50 distinct states from 111 samples**, 61 collapsed, 0
  idle candidates, 0 stillness markers, 6 pop-in markers all resolved on exact decodes, 11
  frames read plus three native-4K crops; `idle_motion_scan` frames=149 idle_drift=no
  long_static=no; render sweep **0 of 372 sampled frames under 1% top-zone ink, 0 blank**,
  min 3.49%, median 13.15%, min max-channel deviation 131; caption band pill-free on 5
  frames, all before the first spoken word at 0.140s; the REAL tweet on screen **3.667s
  measured from pixels**, contiguous, zero metrics, no badge; 1 coloured mark, bare, 0.31x
  intrinsic at 4K, card 0.65x; sync at **lag 0 on both streams** (audio r=0.9542 at 1ms,
  video r=0.9995 at 1 frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO remux; Gate 3 **pass on
  the FIRST call, 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; 2 renders, the extra one bought by
  a TIMING measurement and never by geometry.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — grokimagine / icon (2026-08-13)

- [transcript] **A KEYTERM can manufacture a mis-transcription, and the transcript is then
  wrong in a way TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH does not protect.** The raw pass wrote "Grok Imagen"
  four times, because `execution/transcription_vocabulary.json` carries `Imagen (Google
  image model)` and has no entry for xAI's product: Scribe had a standing prior for exactly
  the wrong token. The langchain method settles it in twenty lines and no API spend, and
  here it REFUTES Scribe rather than confirming it. The discriminator is the stress and the
  syllable-2 vowel: *imagine* is /ɪ ˈmæ dʒ ɪn/ with an OPEN vowel carrying the loudest
  frame, *Imagen* is /ˈɪ m ə dʒ ɛn/ with a reduced schwa. Measured on 5ms frames across all
  four raw utterances plus both cut utterances: syllable-2 median F1 600-700 Hz and
  syllable 2 loudest in **5 of 6, with 0 measuring as Imagen**. The fix belongs in the
  BUILD's keyterm list (drop `Imagen`, add `Grok Imagine`) and never in the shared
  vocabulary file, where Google's Imagen is a legitimate entry. Corroborated independently:
  the source post writes both "Grok Imagine" and "Imagine Omni".
- [intake] **A SIXTH raw shape: the first attempt uses a DIFFERENT SCRIPT, so it shares no
  stem with the others and grok46's stem rule cannot reach it.** Attempt 1 opens "This one
  new platform is going to change the way that we generate assets using AI."; attempts 2
  and 3 both open "AI video generation has one major problem". A phrase key finds two of
  three openings and a stem key finds nothing common at all. The portable answer is to run
  the rules SEPARATELY and require them to agree on the winner: the content rule (phrase +
  sign-off, last complete take wins) picks word 136, the gap rule (>=5s inter-word silence,
  safe here only because the two real gaps measure 24.94s and 27.07s) independently picks
  the same word AND recovers the orphan attempt so it can be asserted rather than absorbed,
  and the marker rule stays a lower bound. Three rules, one answer, six asserted constants.
- [law13] **The bespoke scene is the SOURCE'S OWN PICTURE, and it is in the artifact you
  rejected.** The attached demo is a leaker's watermarked screen recording — rejected on
  three measured grounds — but decoding five of its frames is where this short's peak beat
  comes from: the leaked composer's left rail reads *Images / Audio / References*, and the
  References panel holds ONE saved card, a sprite sheet of the same character in many
  poses. That is the whole feature in one image, and it is what beat 5 codes. The
  hermesjourney rule generalises: rejecting an asset as MEDIA is not a reason to stop
  looking at it.
- [law13][law15] **A scene that GROWS must decide what it is a picture OF, and the wrong
  choice costs eleven seconds of the frame.** The reference sheet's first design built a
  centre COLUMN and expanded sideways, which is a defensible reading of "not only inside a
  single workflow, but across your entire workspace" — and it left an 88-unit-wide
  composition in a 576-unit zone for the eleven seconds before the outer columns arrived.
  A workflow is a SEQUENCE OF SHOTS, so a workflow is a ROW and the workspace is the rows
  stacked: same sentence, same object count, and the field fills the frame from its first
  seat. The boundary then grows in HEIGHT alone, which is also why it can never drift off
  the axis. **When a beat can grow in two directions, pick the one whose FIRST state is a
  composition.**
- [law15] **A composition that grows downward from a fixed anchor is off-centre for its
  whole life, and the fix is to park the small state where it belongs.** Authored for its
  final two-row state the field sat 78 units high for the eleven seconds it was one row;
  authored for the one-row state the final state would sit low. The one-row cast is parked
  at +80 (`otop(240) - 16`) and rides home on the SAME cue that brings the second row in,
  so making room IS the workspace opening up. The same move fixes the hook, where three
  shots held the optical centre alone until the key term needed it (`otop(114) = 164.4`,
  ridden to 87 on `consistency,`). A block hanging in the upper third is the pre-render
  contact sheet's most common catch and no gate reports it.
- [all] **An "absorb" is a contradiction when the NEXT beat inherits the cast.** Beat 3's
  first cut absorbed three media tiles into the hub on `all in one` — the approved
  grokpublish move, solved in distance, and it looked right on its own. Beat 4 then
  re-authors the same three tiles in the same seats, so the shipped sequence was: three
  tiles dissolve into the hub, cut, all three come straight back. That is the ground-flip
  class from the other direction, and only the pre-render sheet showed it because gate 1
  measures each section independently and gate 2's 3fps sampling reads the two states as
  two legitimate frames. **A reduction is only safe when the beat that inherits the cast
  agrees the reduction happened.** The replacement — one solid ENCLOSURE drawn around the
  three — says `all in one` without destroying anything, and it plants the rectangle whose
  growth is the payoff eleven seconds later.
- [tokens] **A DASHED box and a SOLID box must mean different things, or the lane loses its
  clearest token.** This system's dashed-plus-tint rect always means "an empty seat waiting
  to be filled". Drawing the `all in one` boundary and the workspace boundary in the same
  dashed token would have made two full containers read as two empty slots. They are solid
  accent strokes with no fill — one new token, used exactly twice, with the second use the
  payoff of the first.
- [all] **Crossfading two whole glyphs LIGHTENS the part they share, and the fix is to
  duplicate only the part that differs.** The subject swap stacks two portraits and
  crossfades them; two identical solid busts at 50% composite to 75%, not 100%, so the
  figure visibly greys for the length of the dissolve. Drawing the shared body ONCE and
  duplicating only the crown means the only thing that dissolves is the hair, which is the
  only thing that is changing. (Opacity also has no transform origin, so this cannot
  reproduce the smallteams residual-matrix class.)
- [design] **Three silhouettes are one too few for a payoff that must change everything.**
  With subjects a/b/c and a reference of `a`, one of the three payoff frames has to start
  as the reference and its snap changes nothing — a dead event at the emotional peak. A
  fourth silhouette exists for exactly that reason: all three start wrong, all three
  visibly change on `consistent.`
- [4K] **A `fill` tween belongs on a glyph part that HAS a fill.** `fig_fill` sets both
  stroke and fill; the collar here is an OPEN stroked V with `fill="none"`, so filling it
  closed the path into a solid triangle whose straight top edge left a 2-design-unit black
  sliver of the bust above it. Four emphasised frames stopped matching four unemphasised
  ones. The collar was ALREADY terracotta, so the tween had no effect except the damage.
  Gate 1 measured 0 errors, gate 2's 3fps thumbnails cannot resolve two design units, and
  the only detector was a native-4K crop — the fourth build in a row where that is true.
- [law4] **The caption-identity guard's fix can live in the CAPTION, and sometimes that is
  the honest one.** `CONSISTENCY` centre stage while the pill reads exactly "consistency,"
  is the stolenapp defect, and the usual answer is to add information to the on-screen
  term. Here the pill was one word only because a 0.33s gap forced a break; gluing
  `consistency`->`and` makes it "consistency, and this platform", which removes the double
  READ the law exists to prevent and improves the caption. The guard was not weakened, and
  the key term stayed on its own spoken word.
- [gate2] **A four-point ink RAMP separates the three kinds of pop-in marker in one pass.**
  Sampling t-0.20 / t-0.10 / t / t+0.13 with a ground-independent ink metric plus the
  pill's own accent area classifies every marker without a judgement call: a real entrance
  ramps (54381 -> 73513 -> 77813 -> 100150), dedup noise is identical at all four points
  AND in the pill (5.00s, 33.33s), a colour-only emphasis is flat within 0.15% (12.67s), a
  caption WIDTH change moves the pill while the zone holds (32.33s, 40.33s), and a section
  cut is a step down from a different composition (46.33s). Ten markers, ten answers, one
  script.
- [measure] **A verification metric must be chosen per GROUND, or it measures the
  background.** `dark_px` counts the charcoal ground on every dark section (121751 of
  129600 px "before" a tile lands), `white_px` counts the cream ground on every cream one,
  and a dashed 30%-alpha border is neither dark nor white nor accent. Three fixes, all
  cheap: `white_px` for plates on dark, a `light_px` threshold for dashed seats on dark, and
  a modal-background `any_ink` for anything on cream. The first run of the causality probe
  reported six failures and every one of them was the metric.
- [grokimagine_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1503 frames, 50.112s container /
  50.080 authored, 44 captions, 8 sections, 67 direct section children; take detection on a
  3-attempt raw whose first attempt uses a different script, three independent rules agreeing
  on word 136 (t=162.320, 155 words) with six hand-verified constants asserted and the head
  boundary measured from a 10ms envelope (161.930 < 162.100 < 162.310); one transcript token
  adjudicated acoustically against a keyterm-induced error; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings
  across 5 rounds** on the 1080 design copy (130 ids, 0 duplicates, 68 tween selectors all
  resolving, 0 untweened section children, 9 `data-overlap-ok` — connectors and the two
  enclosures — 0 `data-bleed`, 0 `non-scaling-stroke`, 0 arrowheads, 0 ghosts, 27
  `pathLength="100"` paths, 0 caption-echo trigrams, 0 caption-identity collisions over 4
  typeset atoms, deepest authored ink y=374.0 against a 400 floor); pre-render ink sweep 501
  samples with min 0.700% in one 0.2s frame-0 window and median 9.308%; Gate 2 **48 distinct
  states from 150 samples**, 102 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 1 stillness marker and 10
  pop-in markers all resolved on exact decodes, all 48 states read plus four native-4K crops
  and a 45-still pre-render contact sheet; `idle_motion_scan` frames=200 idle_drift=no
  long_static=YES at 30.5s, resolved by measuring the tree's accent ink (528 -> 16619 ->
  21712 across 30.2-30.8) and the seat row (0 -> 14807 -> 20420 across 27.6-28.6); render
  sweep **0 of 1503 frames under 1% top-zone ink, 0 blank**, min 3.188%, median 16.057%, min
  max-channel deviation 28; caption band pill-free on 9 frames, all before the first
  spoken word at 0.280s; 20 cued atoms all measured 0 before their cue; the REAL tweet on
  screen **3.433s measured from pixels**, contiguous, at 0.9225x, zero metrics, no fabricated
  badge, one ring seated from the renderer's measured paragraph box; 1 official mark in its
  own brand colour at 0.267x intrinsic, nothing upscaled; sync at **lag 0 on both streams**
  (audio r=0.9775 at 1ms, video r=0.9989 at 1 frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO
  remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; 2 renders,
  the extra one bought by a FULL-RESOLUTION finding and never by geometry.
- [mathvoice_kinetic] **The transcriber does not get to spell a real person's name.** Miguel
  called mathvoice excellent and flagged exactly one defect: Scribe heard the mathematician as
  "Terturian" and the caption pill typeset it that way, while the REAL tweet card sitting
  directly above it in the same beat read "David Turturean" — his own account's display name.
  One short, two spellings of one man's name, three seconds apart, and the wrong one was ours.
  This is now STANDARD law 14 PROPER-NOUN SPELLING: display copy follows the SOURCE PAYLOAD's
  letters (`plans/x_card_*.json` → `author.name` / `author.username`), the transcript follows
  Miguel's sound, and they are allowed to disagree because one is read by the eye and the other
  by a string matcher. The mechanism generalises the slowfrontier `CAPTION_FIX` (Soul → Sol) and
  the grokimagine Imagen → Imagine call: a module-level `CAPTION_SPELLING` dict plus a
  `respell(words)` applied INSIDE `build_captions()` after `clean_words()`, returning a display
  copy with the timing fields passed straight through, and `sys.exit()`ing if a declared fix
  never fires — a silent no-op ships the wrong name, which is the failure mode that hurts.
  What must NOT change is as important: `SUBS["david"] = "david terturian solved"` stays in
  Scribe's spelling because it is matched against the transcript's own tokens to place the b2
  cut, and `cuts/mathvoice/transcript_tight.json` is never edited. Blast radius measured, not
  assumed: **exactly one line** differs in each of the two index.html files (cap4), same
  `data-start` 4.26, same `data-duration` 1.58, same `font-size` 51.0px — because `cap_font()`
  is length-driven and both spellings are 9 characters, so the pill did not move a pixel.
  Re-gated green on the new encode: Gate 1 0 errors / 0 warnings, Gate 2 50 distinct states from
  111 samples with 0 idle candidates and 0 stillness markers (numerically identical to the
  superseded render, which is exactly what a glyph-only change should produce) plus decoded 4K
  caption-band crops at 4.70/5.20/5.70 reading "problem. David Turturean solved" and a single
  frame at 5.00 showing card and pill agreeing, Gate 3 pass on the first call with 0 visual,
  0 semantic, 0 minor notes. Cost of the fix: one Gemini call. Two operational notes for the
  next fix pass: a spelling correction does NOT need a re-cut or a re-transcription (no
  ElevenLabs spend), and it DOES invalidate the clerk verdict — the second key checks hashes,
  so any re-render must be re-clerked or the paperwork is quietly lying.
- [grokimagine_icon] **A faithful card that reads as a rendering bug is not provenance.** The
  handed URL was @XFreeze QUOTING @blankspeaker, and the quote-to-original rule (stolenapp)
  mechanically picked the quoted post. The payload was rendered honestly and the result on
  screen was "@blankspeaker" printed beside an empty white disc — because that account's
  display name is a single U+FE0F variation selector and its avatar is a pure-white 400x400
  JPEG. Miguel: *"why do we have a @blankspeaker on the grok imagine video on the X tweet? I
  also told you that I prefer when you use the actual tweet card in videos."* Two agents had
  already documented both facts (the v1 renderer's docstring names the invisible name AND the
  blank avatar, and even explains the workaround of printing the handle as the name line) and
  neither treated them as a REASON. That is the lesson: a source's purpose is to make the claim
  credible to the eye, so an attribute that defeats credibility is a selection input, not a
  rendering problem to route around. It is now STANDARD law 14 ANONYMOUS-ORIGINAL EXCEPTION —
  ship the credible quoting post when the quoted original's account is visually anonymous.
  Three mechanics worth reusing. (1) The exception is ASSERTED from the payload, not
  remembered: the renderer fails the build if the handed post stops quoting that id, and fails
  it *the other way too* if the quoted account ever acquires a visible display name, at which
  point the ordinary rule returns. (2) The 1052-character quoting post was rejected in v1 as
  illegible — correctly on the arithmetic (~738 design units in a 400-unit band) and wrongly on
  the remedy, because hermesjourney already ships a byte-exact PREFIX under law 8 and a
  truncation is not a splice. Two paragraphs, `text.startswith(shown)` asserted, 872 characters
  dropped, and the card lands at 2000x920 = a 0.9225x downscale. (3) The ring must be seated
  from the renderer's OWN measured rect, handed over as fractions of the card, because the same
  fix that moved the card moved the highlight — and `verify_grokimagine_buildorder.py` was
  carrying that box as hardcoded design units, so it silently measured empty white paper on
  both sides of the cue (0 -> 0 accent px) and reported `causality_all_ok=false`. Derive the
  probe box from the same artefact the generator reads, or a moved element gets measured in the
  wrong place. Same class in the render verifier: its card-detection window was the card's
  bottom padding, chosen because it sat below every competing white rect on a 1306px card; on a
  920px card that band moves up into the crowd. Replaced with an AREA discriminator over the
  card's whole authored rect (the card fills 0.843-0.913 of it, the highest any other dark
  frame reaches is 0.310), which cannot be invalidated by the card changing height again.
  Blast radius proved rather than asserted: the decoded audio md5 is byte-identical to the
  superseded encode (6030ce19fbae8e82bd67fa9cd5b01488) and Gate 2's manifest is numerically
  identical — 48 distinct states from 150 samples, 102 collapsed, the same 10 pop-in markers,
  the same single stillness marker at 32.3s, 0 idle candidates. Re-gated green: Gate 1 0
  errors / 0 warnings, Gate 2 all 48 states read plus a native-4K decode of the new card at
  7.90 (real avatar, "X Freeze", @XFreeze, the X glyph, ring around "SpaceXAI is preparing the
  biggest Grok Imagine upgrade yet" while he says "SpaceX AI is gearing up for the newest
  launch of Grok Imagine"), Gate 3 pass on the FIRST call with 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor
  notes. Card screen time re-measured from pixels at the identical 3.433s (6.367-9.767),
  under the 4.0s ceiling. Cost: one Gemini call. And the mathvoice operational note held —
  a re-render invalidates the clerk verdict, so `clerk_grokimagine_icon.json` was marked STALE
  rather than left certifying a hash that no longer exists.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — heygen / icon (2026-08-13)

The seventh raw shape, the first build to add a brand mark to the workspace registry,
and the first payoff this factory has had to RE-SIZE because the pre-render sheet said
it could not be read. Eight findings.

- [intake] **A raw can carry THREE completely different scripted openings, and then no
  single key can see the take.** grok46's stem rule and mathvoice's phrase rule both
  assume one opening that drifts; grokimagine met a raw whose FIRST attempt used another
  script and asserted it as a one-off pre-roll. This 201s session rewrites the hook
  TWICE: seven "Did you nail your latest short take…" attempts (0.88-61.82), two "If you
  filmed a short and…" (83.94-98.20), then six "Has this ever happened to you?…"
  (120.58-200.72), of which exactly one reaches the sign-off. The portable move is to
  stop treating the non-winning script as noise: each family is keyed on ITS OWN phrase,
  counted, and the three are asserted to TILE the raw in order (`starts == sorted(starts)`,
  `starts[0] == 0`, every opening inside its own block). 15 openings, 3 families, 1
  complete take, and a rewrite can no longer be absorbed into a neighbouring take.
- [intake] **The gap rule can be WRONG rather than merely weak, and the honest response
  is to demote it in the file that uses it.** grokimagine could require the content and
  gap rules to AGREE because both of its real gaps measured >24s. Here the four >=5s
  silences (8.94 / 5.40 / 22.12 / 22.38) separate the three SCRIPT FAMILIES while the
  eight within-family restarts sit on 1.30-4.66s, so the gap rule answers word 171 where
  the content rule answers 282 — a 43-second miss. Demanding agreement would have failed
  a correct build; deleting the rule would have thrown away a real bound. It is asserted
  as `171 <= 282` and its own opening count is asserted too, so it still fails loudly if
  the raw changes shape. **Every rule gets the standing the raw earns it, per raw, in
  writing.**
- [law8][law13] **The pre-render contact sheet is the only gate that can see whether a
  PAYOFF is legible, and it caught this one.** Beat 6's argument is that each frame's
  mouth re-shapes to the word beneath it. The first cut drew four 114-wide frames, which
  puts the mouth at 15 design units and the difference between adjacent visemes (rx 6.6
  vs 9.6) at 4.8du = **9 physical px on a 1080 encode**. Gate 1 measures boxes and passed
  0/0; Gate 2's 3fps thumbnails cannot resolve it; Gate 3 passed the shipped build without
  a note. Only a 42-still sheet of the paused timeline showed four identical-looking
  faces at the emotional peak. Two fixes, both arithmetic: the viseme spread went to rx
  5.2-12.4 (20 vb units wide, 6 tall) and the row went from four 114-wide frames to
  **three 156-wide** ones in the same 492 column — a 37% bigger mouth. **A payoff has a
  minimum size, and it is set by the smallest difference the argument depends on.**
- [law15] **Dropping to an ODD number of tiles put the hero on the axis for free.** With
  four frames the hero had to travel 63 design units sideways to become frame 1; with
  three, `HERO2_DX = 288 - FR_CX[1] = 0.0` and the take does not move at all when it
  becomes its frames — it simply gains a neighbour on each side, which is also the better
  reading of "the entire video". The legibility fix and the centring fix were the same
  edit, and that is not a coincidence: an odd row is centred on a TILE, an even row on a
  GAP.
- [law12] **A wordmark lockup needs a plate shaped like the lockup, not a square.** Every
  mark this factory has shipped was square-ish, so `mark_plate()` took one `size`. HeyGen's
  official logo is 1.687:1 (stacked "Hey/Gen" with the colour mark at top-right), and in a
  square plate it floats with 40% dead air — FILL THE SHAPE from the other direction.
  `mark_plate()` now takes a width, derives the height from the MARK'S OWN viewBox ratio
  (165.62/98.193) and pads proportionally on both axes, so the plate's aspect IS the
  mark's and the padding is uniform in relative terms. Measured: 0.351x / 0.293x / 0.234x
  of intrinsic at the three placements, nothing upscaled.
- [law12][assets] **Registering a missing mark is a build step, and the official file can
  be a public-domain vector.** `heygen` did not exist in `assets/logos/registry.json`. The
  favicon is 48px (an 8x upscale at any usable size) and there is no press-kit PNG, but
  Wikimedia Commons carries `File:HeyGen_logo.svg` — public domain, credited to heygen.com,
  with all six brand gradients as real `linearGradient` defs. Chromium rasterises it
  faithfully (cairosvg is not trusted with `gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` inside a
  translated group); `heygen-color.png` is the lockup at 2000x1186 and `heygen-mark.png`
  is the colour mark alone, cropped by measuring the ink box of just the gradient paths
  (user units x 106.65-165.65, y 0-57.85) after splitting the file at its `<g fill="#000000">`
  text group — and then VERIFIED against `heygen.com/favicon.ico` to prove the crop is the
  brand's own app icon and not an invention. The video ships the LOCKUP: Miguel's Hermes
  ruling (nobody recognises the bare glyph) applies to a four-petal pinwheel too, and the
  lockup reads the brand's NAME beside the key term.
- [law13] **The bespoke scene came from the asset the judge rejected — again — and this
  time it also wrote a later beat.** The attached demo reel is the vendor's own, not a
  leak, and it is still rejected for shipping on three measured grounds (1.708x upscale at
  the content column; 56.8% near-black / 10.4% acid green / mean luma 55.2 over 445,290
  sampled pixels against this system's cream and terracotta; full sentences burned into
  every beat, i.e. a second caption track under LAW 4). Nine decoded frames later it had
  supplied both the peak and the recap: its picture of the feature is a **five-frame strip
  of ONE take** captioned "video · the take you keep" over a "new audio · '…TODAY…' ·
  right date" bar, and its script runs "You nailed the take." -> "Then the date changed.
  Don't reshoot it." -> "Same take. Lips re-synced." Beat 6 is that strip in this
  factory's language; beat 7's FRIDAY -> MONDAY token is that date change. **Read the
  rejected asset before designing, every time.**
- [gate][measure] **A verification window that worked on the last short can be arithmetically
  impossible on this one, and you can prove that before decoding a frame.** grokimagine
  detects its tweet card by white AREA over the card's authored rect (>0.5) because the
  highest any other dark frame reached was 0.310. Ported here it would be a coin flip: this
  short's b5 fills the same rect to 49% (the take at 7.7% plus the transcript page at 42%)
  and b6 to 62% (three frames spanning the full column) — computed from the layout table,
  not sampled. The replacement discriminates on SHAPE, which is what the card uniquely has:
  white across the FULL 492-unit content column on TWO rows at once (4K y=560 and y=1100).
  Measured on the encode the card scores 1.0000/1.0000 while the best non-card DARK frame
  reaches 0.6639/0.8222 over 589 dark frames. Also worth keeping: the first version of that
  probe reported its margin against ALL non-card frames, which included the cream beats
  (white everywhere, excluded by the charcoal test) and therefore printed a flattering
  1.0000 — **a margin is only a margin among the frames the other tests let through.**
- [heygen_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1100 frames, 36.672s container /
  36.639 authored, 37 captions, 9 sections, 37 direct section children; take detection on a
  raw with THREE scripted openings, 15 openings across 3 asserted families, 21 markers
  before the take (11 punctuated "No." + 10 truncations) and 0 inside it, head measured on a
  10ms envelope (163.270 < 163.320 < 163.460, Scribe 20ms late); the cut kept all 141 spoken
  words with no micro-cuts; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings across 3 rounds** on the 1080
  design copy (95 ids, 0 duplicates, 38 tween selectors all resolving, 0 untweened section
  children, 2 `data-overlap-ok` — the two drops — 0 `data-bleed`, 0 `non-scaling-stroke`, 0
  arrowheads, 2 `pathLength="100"` paths, 0 caption-echo trigrams, 0 caption-identity
  collisions over 5 typeset atoms, deepest authored ink y=382.4 against a 400 floor); a
  TIMING CUE TABLE parsed from the shipped timeline (min terminal hold 0.54s, median 0.64s,
  two boundaries re-cued before the render); Gate 2 **35 distinct states from 110 samples**,
  75 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 0 stillness markers, 2 pop-in markers both resolved on a
  four-point ink ramp, all 35 states read plus 7 native-4K decodes and two 42-still
  pre-render sheets; `idle_motion_scan` frames=147 idle_drift=no long_static=no; render sweep
  **0 of 1100 frames under 1% top-zone ink, 0 blank**, min 7.736%, median 24.262%, min
  max-channel deviation 223; caption band pill-free on 6 frames, all before the first spoken
  word at 0.199s; the REAL tweet on screen **2.633s measured from pixels**, contiguous, at
  0.9225x, zero metrics, no fabricated badge, one ring seated from the renderer's measured
  paragraph box; 1 official mark in its own six brand gradients at 0.351x intrinsic, newly
  registered, nothing upscaled; sync at **lag 0 on both streams** (audio r=0.9754 at 1ms,
  video r=0.9997 at 1 frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO remux; Gate 3 **pass on
  the FIRST call, 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes**; **1 render** — the three defects
  this build had were all caught on the paused-timeline sheet, which costs nothing.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — personalapps / DIAGRAM (2026-08-13, the run's second Diagram)

The shortest raw of the batch (105.64s, 212 words) and the lane's second build, so the port
already existed and the budget went to the argument. Eight findings.

- [intake] **A raw can contain FOUR attempts in THREE different scripts and ZERO punctuated
  markers, and the phrase key then has to be long enough to exclude the take's own opening
  words.** mathvoice met a stem that fired inside the winning take; this is the same trap one
  level up. `you can now` fires FOUR times here and the fourth is *inside* the winner
  ("...you can now use AI, GPT 5.6 Sol"); `you can now use ai to build` fires exactly twice,
  because token 5 diverges (`to` vs `ai`). The rule to write down is not "use a phrase" but
  **extend the key until it separates the openings from every in-take utterance, then ASSERT
  that the shorter key still collides** — otherwise a later edit shortens it back and nothing
  fails. Attempts 1 and 3 share no key with the winner at all (attempt 3 is a different
  script) and are recovered by the gap rule alone, asserted by first word, tail word and tail
  end so neither can be absorbed. Three rules, one answer, word 58 / t=56.959 / 154 words.
- [transcript] **Two Scribe passes over the same speech DISAGREE, and that disagreement is a
  free acoustic experiment.** The raw pass wrote `off-the-shelf`, the cut pass wrote
  `off-the-shelves`. Measured on 10ms frames, the only fricative after the /l/ vowel runs
  41.02-41.10 at ZCR 0.53-0.65 with periodicity <=0.25 and monotonically decaying energy —
  unvoiced /f/. A *shelves* ending needs a voiced /v/ before its /z/ and there is no voiced
  frame anywhere between the vowel and the frication; the true final /z/ of the very next
  word ("tools") measures periodicity 0.32-0.37, which is the control sitting 60ms away. The
  mathvoice `CAPTION_SPELLING` + `respell()` mechanism carries the fix, and this is its first
  use on a COMMON noun — the law is about display copy following the evidence, not about
  proper nouns specifically.
- [law6] **The immediate-repetition guard needs a punctuation discriminator, or it deletes
  emphasis.** "very, very concisely" has a 0.061s gap, so the chassis's `<0.5s` rule would
  have dropped one `very` from Miguel's own sentence. Both tokens are complete words (0.380s
  and 0.200s) and Scribe comma'd the first. **A stutter is an UNPUNCTUATED repeat**; skipping
  the drop when the previous token ends in a comma costs one clause and keeps TRANSCRIPT IS
  TRUTH intact.
- [law13] **The bespoke scene can be ONE TOKEN carried through the whole short rather than a
  scene built for its own beat.** A CELL IS A FEATURE, A BOX HOLDS CELLS: an off-the-shelf
  product is a plate with nine grey cells, your own software is the same plate with exactly
  one terracotta cell. Everything else follows — the hook's app, the shelf's 27, the one that
  lights, the one that comes off the shelf, the shell built around it, and the outro are all
  the same object at different counts, so the 15.0s payoff reads as a callback instead of a
  new picture. It also makes the exact unit free (builders): 27 stand there and he needs 1,
  so "one lit cell" IS the claim. **Design the token first and the scene falls out of it.**
- [law13] **Solve the lit cell's position through the GLYPH's lattice, not by hand.** Nine
  cells on a 3x3 lattice that exactly fills the glyph box put the middle cell's centre on the
  plate's centre by construction, so centring the middle box on AX puts the lit cell on AX
  too — and the drop that takes it off the shelf needs no tuned x in any beat (LAW 15). The
  geometry selftest asserts it before anything renders. Corollary: keeping the cells INSIDE
  the box plate's glyph means retiring a box retires its nine cells, so nothing can be left
  behind in b8.
- [gate2][ink] **The pre-render ink sweep and the encode ink sweep measure different things,
  and a beat can pass one and fail the other.** The pre-render sweep sums box AREA x opacity;
  the encode sweep measures deviation from each frame's own modal colour. b3 standing its mark
  alone on the axis scored **4.5% pre-render and 0.66% on the encode for 20 frames**, because
  a white plate on cream deviates 15/255 and *is not ink at all* — the only counted pixels
  were the 56du indigo mark. The extracted 4K frame was perfectly legible, which is exactly
  why this needs measuring: the defect is not "blank", it is "one small tile alone in a large
  field". The fix that answers both metrics AND the composition is the mathvoice rule — draw
  every seat from the beat's first frame — which also retired the park-and-ride the beat had
  been using and made it centred by construction. After: **0 of 1381 frames under 1%**.
- [law11] **A coded glyph can accidentally BE a brand mark, and only a contact sheet finds
  it.** "YouTube thumbnails" drawn as a dark rounded rect with a centred triangle knocked out
  of it is YouTube's play mark in the wrong colours, i.e. the claim "he built YouTube" — which
  he never makes. The universal image glyph (horizon, peak, accent sun) cannot be misread as a
  brand and is the honest object anyway. The general rule: **when a coded glyph names a
  product, check whether you have drawn that product's LOGO by accident.**
- [composition] **Two trees around one row is a fence, and it is usually the wrong sentence
  too.** b4's first cut fed the model DOWN into eight prompt chips and gathered them again
  below: two rails and sixteen stubs meeting each chip's top and bottom edge centres in the
  same accent, so the eye joins them THROUGH the chip. Deleting one tree fixed the picture and
  the causality at once, because **the prompts are INPUTS** — eight gather into the model, the
  model delivers the app. When a diagram looks busy, check the direction of the arrows before
  reaching for the styling.
- [guards] **Two new build-time guards, each closing a class that shipped past all three gates
  before.** (1) A TERMINAL-HOLD assertion — `section_end - (last cue + entrance)` >= 0.30s for
  every section — which is mathvoice's finding turned into a failure; it fired twice during
  authoring (b4 at **-0.05s**, b6 at **-0.32s**) and both were fixed by re-timing rather than
  by speeding entrances up. (2) A SVG-SCALE guard asserting every scale tween targets a bare
  `#id` (a DIV), which makes smallteams' residual-matrix class unmakeable rather than merely
  detectable. A guard that fires at build time costs no render and no gate.
- [paperwork] **The self-audit is worth writing even when you are the one who wrote both
  files.** Re-deriving all 78 paperwork claims from disk before handing over found two numbers
  wrong — the source post is 447 characters, not 443, and the shipped paragraph is 214, not
  210 — both of which a clerk would have bounced. Character counts are the class to watch: they
  are the only numbers in the record that get typed from reading rather than from a probe.
- [personalapps_diagram] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1381 frames, 46.037s container /
  46.010 authored, 42 captions, 10 sections, 82 direct section children; take detection on a
  4-attempt / 3-script raw with ZERO punctuated markers, three independent rules agreeing on
  word 58 (t=56.959, 154 words) with both orphan attempts asserted and the head measured from a
  10ms envelope (56.700 < 56.739 < 56.910, Scribe 49ms late); the cut kept all 154 spoken words;
  Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings across 4 rounds** on the 1080 design copy (147 ids, 0
  duplicates, 83 tween selectors all resolving, 0 untweened section children, 16
  `data-overlap-ok` — 12 connectors, 2 law-14 rings, 2 copy plates — 0 `data-bleed`, 0
  `non-scaling-stroke`, 0 arrowheads, 35 `pathLength="100"` paths, 0 caption-echo trigrams, 0
  caption-identity collisions over 3 typeset atoms, deepest authored ink y=376.0 against a 400
  floor); pre-render sheet 55 stills + a 461-sample ink sweep that found three defects no gate
  reports; Gate 2 **41 distinct states from 138 samples**, 97 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 0

  sweep **0 of 1381 frames under 1% top-zone ink, 0 blank**, min 1.19%, median 4.87%, min
