## Run 6 (impeccable) — oneprompt / KINETIC (2026-08-13, the lane's horizontal axis)

A tutorial with no source, whose deliverable is a sentence: one prompt, four tools, and a
prompt the viewer is meant to screenshot. Nine findings.

- [law15] **This lane has never had to solve its horizontal axis, and three rows in one
  build made it unavoidable.** mathvoice found that a run of boxes can sit in the left half
  while every full-width text atom stays centred for free, and fixed it by drawing all six
  slots from frame 0. That fix does not generalise: a row of BRAND MARKS cannot be drawn
  before its marks arrive, because a ghosted logo is worse than no logo and a dashed seat
  under a coloured app tile is plate-on-plate. The general answer is the horizontal twin of
  the lane's own `stepy`: author every mark at its FINAL seat and carry ONE x offset per
  stage, `dx(n) = (W_full - W_n) / 2`, released as each mark lands. One mark is centred, two
  are centred, three are centred, four are centred, and because a mark's entrance is
  scale+opacity the offset is never cancelled. `guard_shifts` now checks both axes, because
  `stepx` creates the identical trap sideways. Three rows in this build use it: four marks in
  b2, five session stubs in b4, two marks in b8.
- [law15] **A composition that RESERVES space is off-centre until the thing it reserved for
  arrives, and no gate can see it.** The bespoke scene's list is `[tick box][gap][stubs]` and
  the stubs land 0.17s before the boxes do, so the landing state was three rows spanning
  140..482 — held, still, and 23 design units right of the axis. `geometry_audit` measures
  AUTHORED rects and never sees a tweened destination; Gate 2 samples that beat at 3fps and
  reads the two states as two legitimate frames; Gate 3 passed it. The detector had to be
  built: a 0.1s live-DOM sweep of the visible ink box across the whole timeline, with each
  flagged sample re-probed 0.10s either side so a deviation is classified as a HOLD or a
  TRANSITION by measurement rather than by argument. 416 samples, two flags, both proved in
  motion (max 6.58 units for 0.2s while the boxes scale in). The fix is the lane's own
  grammar: the rows land centred on THEMSELVES, parked at `-BOX_ROOM` = half the box column,
  and ride the remaining 23 units right on the cue that brings the boxes in — so making room
  IS the list becoming a checklist.
- [gate3] **"Very clean but generic" has a machine-readable form and it is
  `no_added_value`.** Render 2 passed Gate 1 with 0/0, passed Gate 2 with 0 idle candidates,
  and Gemini failed it on one semantic error: 5.3s of two text lines and a rule at 13.5-18.8,
  on the beat that explains the MECHANISM. The finding was correct and the right response was
  a picture, not an argument. What replaced it is worth more than the beat: five session
  stubs arrive one per spoken beat and a terracotta thread wipes underneath all five while
  every session brightens — which is what "recurring memory" looks like — and the stub is the
  SAME atom the bespoke scene is built from, so the beat teaches b5's vocabulary before b5
  needs it. **A diagram that seeds the next scene is cheaper than a diagram that only
  decorates its own.** The Kinetic lane's licence to be typographic is not a licence to be
  typographic on the beat that carries the explanation.
- [law13] **A scene can be made centred BY CASTING, and on a 6-wide grid that forces even
  group sizes.** The field's ten repeats are three groups whose OWN centroids are each the
  grid centre (2.5, 2), so the composition is centred after group A alone, after A+B, after
  A+B+C, and after the other twenty leave — four held states, zero corrective offsets. The
  sizes are 4, 4 and 2 and could not have been anything else: a 6-column grid centres on
  column 2.5, and no set of integer column indices of ODD size can average to 2.5. The
  constraint that looked like a taste decision is arithmetic.
- [intake] **A SEVENTH raw shape: Scribe runs EARLY, because the loudest thing near the take
  is not the take.** gptvoice's Scribe ran late and mathvoice's ran 30ms late; this one reads
  170.660 against a measured first phoneme of 170.94, i.e. **0.28s early**, because a lip
  transient fires at 170.68-170.77 and Scribe annexed it. The trap is that the transient
  peaks at 0.0089 normalised RMS and the /h/ aspiration it precedes only reaches 0.0096 — the
  noise is LOUDER than the speech, so no threshold can separate them at any level and the
  sibling `scribe_start - 0.22` fallback opened the cut 0.49s before the first sound with the
  smack inside it. **Duration separates them**: the onset is the first 10ms window that HOLDS
  above the floor for 0.15s, which is longer than any transient and shorter than any
  syllable. The transient then becomes the noise floor the head must clear, and the head is
  asserted inside the measured 0.18s of silence between them.
- [law4] **The honest way to take a caption-echo exemption is to make it checkable.** This
  short's deliverable IS a sentence Miguel speaks, so the prompt on screen is a deliberate
  double read and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. Two mitigations make it a
  read-then-follow rather than a transcription: the field is complete and STATIC from the
  section's first frame, 0.50s before he starts reading it, and the only thing that moves
  afterwards is the marker pen, whose three fills land on the three phrases his own pauses
  cut the prompt into. And the exemption is bounded by a new guard rather than by intent:
  `guard_prompt_fidelity()` compares the rendered lines, normalised, against the SPOKEN span
  of `transcript_tight.json` token for token and kills the build on any drift. The rejected
  source screenshot is exactly why it exists — it types "chat HISTORY" and drops "help", two
  words off the prompt Miguel dictates, and it was the single most tempting asset available.
- [law14][source] **A source can be REJECTED on its wording rather than on its quality.** The
  handed post is the technique's origin and its attached screenshot is a real, legible
  ChatGPT Work session showing the feature working — and shipping it would have put a
  DIFFERENT prompt on screen in the one beat that exists to hand the viewer the prompt. Law 3
  disposes of the card separately (it is a tip, not news, and the take cites nobody), but the
  screenshot needed a harder test than legibility. **Zero third-party assets is a legitimate
  and now machine-enforced outcome**: `guard_no_third_party()` requires the verdict to claim
  zero, every asset in it to be ruled reject, every `<img>` src in the build to be a declared
  registry mark, and all declared marks to actually render.
- [gate2] **A pop-in adjudicator needs a channel per EVENT KIND and a window wider than the
  longest entrance.** grokimagine's four-point ink ramp reported three false "non-monotone"
  results here for three different reasons, and each one names a missing instrument.
  (1) `.scappill` carries `translateY(-50%)`, so the caption pill lies ENTIRELY inside the
  top-1725px zone every sibling sweeps — meaning every caption WIDTH change is a change in
  "top-zone ink" (12.33: "help automate" -> "for me?", 1.65% of the crop). Splitting the crop
  at y=1400 (deepest authored visual ink 1241px, tallest pill box ~1497px) gives two
  independent signals. (2) The tick boxes arrive as `rgba(20,20,22,0.09)`, which deviates
  from cream by about 20 and is invisible to a >34/255 ink threshold; a `light` channel at
  >12/255 sees them ramp 10.66 -> 11.82%. (3) A group of stubs turning terracotta changes NO
  area at all, so only an ACCENT channel sees it (0.00 -> 4.24%). And the window itself was
  too narrow: the sibling's -0.20..+0.13 is 0.33s while entrances here run 0.30-0.46s, so a
  marker whose event started earlier reads flat — 23.33's group-A tint was already 75%
  complete at the first sample. Five points from -0.45. Fourteen markers, fourteen answers,
  zero judgement calls.
- [process] **An instrument invoked with stderr suppressed can certify a stale artifact.** The
  build verifier crashed after the b4 rebuild (a causality selector named an element that no
  longer existed), it was invoked as `... >/dev/null 2>&1`, and the summary print read the
  PREVIOUS run's JSON off disk and reported `all_ok True` on a project that had changed. Two
  fixes, both permanent: the probe now `sys.exit`s with the offending selector instead of
  subscripting `None`, and a verifier is never run with its stderr closed. A verifier that can
  be stale is worse than no verifier, because it converts an unknown into a false certainty.
- [assets] **`chatgpt-color.png` has three rounded corners and one square one, and that is
  the SVG's own geometry.** The bottom-right corner of the registry's ChatGPT tile is a
  straight V/H pair where the other three carry 577.4-unit arcs, faithfully rasterised from
  the Wikimedia source the registry documents. It is visible at 315px on a dark ground.
  Shipped UNCHANGED anyway, on two grounds: altering brand geometry is precisely what law 12
  exists to prevent, and mathvoice already shipped this exact asset at this exact size through
  a detailed Miguel review that flagged only a surname. Recorded here so the next builder
  spends the ten minutes on something else — and so that if Miguel ever does call it, the fix
  is a registry repair rather than a per-build workaround.
- [oneprompt_kinetic] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1248 frames, 41.600s container /
  41.60 authored, 44 captions, 10 sections, 108 direct section children; take detection on a
  14-opening raw by THREE agreeing rules (content phrase `one simple` walked back over the
  here's/here-is fragment, gap >=2.0s, marker as a lower bound including a genuine spoken
  "No." at 43.42) landing on word 383, t=170.660, 156 words, with the head measured from a
  10ms envelope by SUSTAIN rather than level (transient ends 170.76 < head 170.84 < onset
  170.94); the cut kept all 156 spoken words; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings across 4 rounds**
  on the 1080 design copy (184 ids, 0 duplicates, 109 tween selectors all resolving, 0
  untweened section children, 13 `data-overlap-ok` — three marker fills and the ten gathering
  stubs — 0 `data-bleed`, 0 `non-scaling-stroke`, 0 caption-echo trigrams, 0 caption-identity
  collisions over 10 registered text atoms, 2 declared law-4 exemptions both asserted);
  prompt fidelity asserted at 15 tokens against the transcript AND re-read off the shipped
  DOM; Gate 2 **58 distinct states from 125 samples**, 67 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 0
  stillness markers, 14 pop-in markers all resolved on five-point three-channel decodes, all
  58 states read plus four native-4K crops and a 48-still pre-render contact sheet;
  `idle_motion_scan` frames=166 idle_drift=no long_static=no; render sweep **0 of 416 sampled
  frames under 1% top-zone ink, 0 blank**, min 2.051%, median 12.073%, min max-channel
  deviation 190; live-DOM LAW 15 sweep **416 samples, 0 held off-axis states**, 2 transients
  proved in motion (max 6.58 units); 25 cued atoms and 4 colour resolutions all measured 0 or
  unchanged before their cue; **0 third-party assets**, 4 official marks in their own brand
  colours at 0.308-0.785x intrinsic, nothing upscaled; sync at **lag 0 on both streams**
  (audio r=0.9644 at 1ms, video r=0.9994 at 1 frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO
  remux; Gate 3 pass with 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes; 3 renders, one bought by a
  LAW 15 finding no gate reports and one by GEMINI, never by geometry.

- **2026-08-13 EVENING REVIEW (5-short staging round) — verdicts + two laws.** mathvoice's Climb
  Collapses = "very nice visualization... the type of unique visualization that we need" (second
  named Law-13 reference of the day). grokimagine silhouettes approved. heygen REJECTED for drawn
  human faces -> **NO FACES (Law 17)**: coded humans are silhouettes/solid glyphs only, face detail
  never ships; abstract stand-ins for face-driven stories; real photos (face crop, tweet avatars)
  exempt. mathvoice + oneprompt flagged for underlines wider than their words -> **UNDERLINE = WORD
  SPAN (Law 18)**: underline width comes from the measured ink span of the underlined words, never
  the lockup or a constant; anything longer reads as a divider. Fix passes ordered for heygen
  (scene redesign to silhouette treatment), mathvoice + oneprompt (underline widths).

- **2026-08-13 [mathvoice_kinetic] LAW 18 fix pass — the advance box is not the ink, and
  `max(aw, bw)` is not a rule.** Miguel's remark ("the line goes beyond the actual size of the
  words that you're underlining... it looks like it's meant to be a divider when in reality it's
  an underline") resolved into TWO distinct bugs in one lane, only one of which anybody would
  have guessed. **(1) The rule measured the wrong LINE.** Both offending sites wrote
  `rule_w = max(aw, bw)` over a two-line lockup and then drew the rule under ONE of those lines:
  b1's rule sits under `ONLY HIS VOICE` (ink 1609px at 4K) but wore `AN OPEN PROBLEM`'s 1912px,
  overhanging by **303px — 153 left, 150 right, 19% wider than the words**; b9 repeated it exactly
  under `SOON MOST OF IT` at **+274px**. `max()` reads like a safety margin and is in fact a
  guarantee that the rule is as wide as the WIDEST line, which is the one it is not underlining
  half the time. A third site (b7) used the same `max()` and looked innocent purely because its
  underlined line happened to be the wider one — an accident that would have flipped the day
  somebody reworded the copy. **(2) Even the two "correct" sites overhung**, because the width
  they took was `getBoundingClientRect().width` — the ADVANCE box — and a display line's advance
  box carries 5-18 physical px of empty side bearing past its last letter at these sizes. Measured
  on decoded frames of the shipped render, every one of the five rules exceeded its words: +303,
  +5, +15, +274, +17. **The ruler that fixes both**: canvas `TextMetrics.actualBoundingBoxLeft/
  Right`, measured in the SAME headless page that measures the DOM, with the element's own
  computed font and letter-spacing copied onto the context — it reproduced the five decoded-frame
  ink widths to within **0.61-2.19px at 4K** before being trusted. Two traps on the way in:
  `document.fonts.check()` returns FALSE if no element in the page uses the face at load, so a
  probe that appends its spans after `fonts.ready` silently measures a fallback font and its ink
  numbers are another typeface's (caught by asserting canvas advance == DOM advance, which is now
  a build-time exit); and chip strings are padded and uppercased by CSS, which canvas cannot see,
  so they get no ink measurement at all. **The fix is a primitive, not five edits**:
  `Z.underline(name, M, target, text, top, fs)` sets `left = (576-adv)/2 + lsb` and `width = ink`,
  which seats the rule on the letters instead of on the paper around them, and
  `guard_underlines()` makes the law structural — every `.strike` in the page must have come from
  it (no hand-set widths can reach a render), and each rule declares the atom it underlines while
  the guard independently finds the atom nearest above it and asserts they are the same. That
  second check is the one that would have caught this class on the first build. **Gotcha inside
  the guard**: "directly above" cannot be read off ink BOTTOMS. These lockups are all-caps and
  `ink_span` returns the font's full box including descender depth, so a rule set one cap-gap
  below the cap bottom still sits inside the line's ink band and NO atom ever clears it — the
  first version of the guard exited with "b1-u underlines nothing". Read it off ink TOPS. Result:
  five rules re-cut, **5 lines changed per project and nothing else** (identical tops, heights and
  tween times), every rule now ending 1-3px INSIDE its words' ink on decoded 4K frames (the
  residual is antialias fringe the pixel mask counts as ink and the layout maths does not), Gate 1
  0/0, Gate 2 50 states / 111 samples unchanged from three previous renders, Gate 3 pass first
  call with 0/0/0. Side note worth keeping: centring the rule on its words' INK rather than on the
  frame axis moves it up to 1.4 design units off-centre where a line's two side bearings differ —
  that is correct (an underline rides its own words) and invisible to the geometry audit, whose
  centring rules judge glyphs inside plates and centred TEXT boxes, and a rule is neither.

- **[heygen_icon — LAW 17 fix pass, 2026-08-13] A face is not a detail you can tune; it is a
  class you delete.** Miguel rejected the first cut outright ("the human avatars are a big
  no-go… this one with the faces? Absolutely not") and LAW 17 was written from that remark.
  The instinct on a rejection like this is to soften the offending ink — smaller eyes, a
  subtler mouth. That is the wrong move and it costs a render: the class has to leave
  entirely. `g_face()` put two knocked-out white eyes and one accent mouth into **ten**
  plates through a single function, so the whole violation was one function wide — worth
  checking before assuming a rejection is local. The build that ships draws a SILHOUETTE
  (solid bust + solid head, nothing else), which is the grokimagine treatment Miguel named
  as acceptable in the same sentence he rejected this one.

- **[heygen_icon] When the law forbids the thing the story is about, borrow a glyph the short
  already earns.** This short is literally about lip sync, so the banned ink was the payload.
  The replacement is a VOICE BAND — five rounded accent bars where a mouth would be, in the
  SAME grammar as the real audio waveform the short already ships in b5 (`g_wave`). Nothing
  new had to be invented, and the rhyme is free: the wave that lands BESIDE the take in b5 is
  the wave that lives INSIDE it in b6, so "re-sync" reads as one object moving into another
  rather than as an abstraction standing in for a face. General rule for LAW 17 stand-ins:
  look for an element the composition has ALREADY established before designing a new one.

- **[heygen_icon] Make replacement states shape-distinct, not size-distinct, and assert them
  into their container.** The four mouths differed by ellipse radius, which the first
  pre-render sheet had already caught once as unreadable. The four band states differ in
  SILHOUETTE — rail / hump / block / comb — with a spread of up to 14 viewBox units of bar
  height (29 physical px in a 156-wide frame at 1080, 58 px at 4K), so the payoff reads at
  arm's length. `_voice()` checks every bar corner against the head circle and refuses to
  build if a state pokes ink out of the figure; the worst shipped corner sits at radius 21.1
  of 22. A state table with a geometric assertion beside it cannot drift into a defect later.

- **[heygen_icon] The redesign found a defect three green gates had missed: DECODE THE BEAT
  AND LOOK AT IT.** Both b6 annotation rings were seated 25.6 design units (48.6 physical px
  at 1080, 97 at 4K) BELOW the ink they annotated — the lip-sync ring sat on the subject's
  chest. `HERO2_DY` subtracted `ROW_PARK` a second time, parking the hero 25.6du high, which
  also meant the b5→b6 cut was never the pixel-continuous arrival the plan claimed. Geometry
  audit could not see it (a ring is collision-exempt and its box was legal), frame review had
  read the frame at 3fps without measuring, and Gemini passed it twice. What found it was a
  paused-timeline still of the redesigned beat, followed by `getBoundingClientRect()` on the
  live DOM. **When a beat's annotation is seated from one element's rect while the annotated
  element is parked by a different formula, the two WILL drift — derive both from the same
  seat and assert they agree at build time.** The fix carries its own guard: it compares the
  parked rect to the b5 take seat and refuses to build if they ever separate again.

- **[heygen_icon] Prove the untouched layers are untouched, don't just claim it.** A fix pass
  scoped to one element class should be able to show that everything else survived. The
  cheapest proof is the decoded-audio md5: `ffmpeg -vn -f md5` on the new render returned
  `9e3b51f14eb4ed140cd53586b3c2fd9c`, byte-identical to the rejected cut, which settles the
  cut, the voice, the bed and the sfx in one line. Alongside it, an unchanged census (37
  captions, 9 sections, 1100 frames, 95 unique ids, one renamed id) makes the scope of a fix
  pass auditable instead of asserted. Shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1100 frames, 36.672s
  container / 36.639 authored, 117,631,941 bytes, sha256 `a07b2160…`; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0
  warnings across 2 rounds** (0.5s and 0.25s steps); Gate 2 **35 distinct states from 110
  samples**, 0 idle candidates, 0 stillness markers, 2 pop-in markers both re-resolved on
  frame-granular ink ramps, all 35 states read plus six native-4K decodes and two full-
  resolution crops of the payoff row; render sweep **0 of 1100 frames under 1% top-zone ink**,
  min 7.9348%, median 24.039%; sync **lag 0 on both streams** (audio r=0.9754 at 1ms, video
  r=0.9997 at 1 frame), no remux; Gate 3 pass with 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes.
  Two renders total — the second bought entirely by the drawn faces.

- **[factory] Mark the clerk record STALE the moment a shipped artefact is replaced.**
  `clerk_heygen_icon.json` verified sha256 `888a064d…` against a video that no longer exists
  on disk. A two-key system whose second key still reads green on a deleted artefact is worse
  than no second key, so a fix pass must stamp the old record `STALE` with the reason and the
  superseding sha before it finishes, and leave the fresh clerk pass to an independent agent.

- **[oneprompt_kinetic] LAW 18: an underline's width is a MEASUREMENT, never a lockup number.**
  Miguel: "sometimes you are underlining a few elements and the line goes beyond the actual
  size of the words that you're underlining — that is a no-go… if not it looks like it's meant
  to be a divider when in reality it's an underline." This lane had five rule elements and
  four of them were underlines; all four were wrong, in two different ways. The gross failure
  was `rule_w = max(aw, bw)` in a three-row lockup (headline / rule / second line): the rule
  is sized by whichever line is WIDER, but it wipes in and then holds alone under the FIRST
  line for 1.36s (b1) and 0.64s (b9) before the second line exists. For that whole hold it was
  **1.84x** and **1.43x** the words above it — 438px of overhang per side at 4K. The subtle
  failure hit the two rules that already "came from the text": `M.w(text, fs)` is the ADVANCE
  box, which carries the first glyph's left side bearing, the last glyph's right side bearing
  and `.pop8`'s -0.02em trailing letter-space, so it ran 5/2px (b2) and 12/7px (out) past the
  actual glyphs. **"Width = the text's width" is not the law; "width = the text's INK" is.**
  Before/after on decoded 4K frames, overhang left/right in px: b1 438/433 → -1/-1, b2 5/2 →
  0/0, b9 291/289 → -1/-1, out 12/7 → 0/-1.

- **[oneprompt_kinetic] Measure the ink in the SHIPPED construction, or you buy a second render.**
  The first ink probe rendered each phrase at design size 100 in a plain left-aligned span and
  scaled the result down. It agreed with the decoded frame within 0.27 design units on three
  strings and was **5 units (0.8%) wrong on FOR DAILY AI** — enough to leave the rule one pixel
  past the final I on b2 as well. Side bearings do not survive that scaling with the rounding
  the rasteriser applies at the shipping size. The fix: the probe now reproduces the shipped
  construction exactly — `ctxt`'s full-width centred box inside a `zoom:2` wrapper at the
  shipping font-size — screenshots the 2160-wide row, and reads the first and last column
  whose darkest pixel is ≥50% covered. **Those columns ARE the render's columns.** Placing both
  CSS edges on exact multiples of 0.5px then makes the bar paint the ink's span and nothing
  else, and a guard refuses any rule edge that is not a whole 4K pixel. Flush went from
  "within a pixel" to exact.

- **[factory] Give the law a primitive and a ledger, not a convention.** `Z.underline(name,
  text, fs, top, M)` cannot be handed a width — it reads the ink of the words it is given, and
  a size that was never probed is an AssertionError. Its sibling `Z.divider(..., why=...)` must
  state in the source why it underlines nothing. `guard_underlines` then proves the three
  things that matter: every `.strike` in the markup is a declared underline or a declared
  divider (so a hand-set width cannot come back), each underline's rendered left/width equals
  its words' measured ink and sits under an atom that really carries those words, and no
  declared divider sits directly under a text atom. The divider test needed one non-obvious
  detail: the type's recorded ink box carries the font's full descender range (1.41em for
  `pop`) whether or not the string has descenders, so a legitimate underline 12 units below the
  CAP line starts INSIDE that box — the predicate is "the rule's top is in the lower half of
  the type's ink and no more than 40 units below it", not "the rule is below the box". b4's
  memory thread clears that at 77.7 units and stayed untouched, as it should: it runs under a
  row of five stubs, not under a phrase, and its width is the row's own span.

- **[factory] A width-only fix must leave the advance table alone — and prove it.** Adding the
  ink probe invalidated the measurement cache signature and forced a full re-measure of the 14
  advance widths every font size and stack in the build is derived from. All 14 came back
  **identical**, so no size, no lockup, no centre moved, and the two `index.html` files differ
  from the approved render on **exactly four lines** — one per underline (`diff` verified). The
  gates then behaved exactly as that scope predicts: Gate 1 0 errors / 0 warnings, Gate 2 the
  same **58 distinct states from 125 samples** with the same 67 collapsed and the same 14
  already-adjudicated pop-in markers, `idle_motion_scan` frames=166 idle_drift=no
  long_static=no, the live-DOM sweep unchanged at 416 samples / 0 held off-axis / 0 causality
  failures, and Gate 3 pass with 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes
  (`run6_oneprompt_kinetic_v3`). Shipped: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1248 frames, 41.600s,
  131,758,805 bytes, sha256 `37a0c1e0…`. Two renders in the pass, the second bought entirely by
  that one residual pixel on b2 — and worth it, because the alternative was a fudge constant
  inside the one law that exists to keep hand-set numbers out of rule geometry.

- **[heygen_icon] Two rejections on the same element class means the CONCEPT is wrong, not the tuning —
  delete the class, do not restyle it.** v1 drew faces ("the human avatars are a big no-go"); the LAW 17
  fix pass restyled them into silhouettes with an abstract voice band where the mouth had been, and Miguel
  rejected that too: *"you really have to move away from the idea of using a human silhouette because
  putting things in front of its mouth looks extremely weird."* The second fix was, in hindsight, the same
  answer in a different colour — the figure stayed, and an object still sat on its face, in a short that is
  literally about a mouth. LAW 17's ADDENDUM is the general rule: **when the story is about a face, a mouth
  or an expression, the human figure leaves the composition entirely.** v3 removed `g_subject()`,
  `_voice()`, `VOICE_STATES`, `VOICE_REGION`, `HEAD_C`, `HEAD_REGION` and the three-frame strip from the
  generator — not recoloured, gone — and told the story on the OBJECTS a creator actually touches.

- **[heygen_icon] When you drop a figure, replace it with the objects the story already owns, and the
  short writes itself.** The cast became a video-player card (THE TAKE: ink viewport, knocked-out play
  mark, one accent detail = the progress on its own scrubber), its transcript page (STRUCK and rewritten in
  place), its audio track (a waveform with a span CUT OUT, refilled and sealed), and in the bespoke beat its
  film rail (the video track). Every beat that used to happen to a person now happens to a thing: the take
  is recorded (its own scrubber sweeps to FULL on "recording a Short" — one object, one meter, so the
  separate accent bar under the hero was deleted), handed over, read, corrected, re-synced and kept. **The
  test for a stand-in is not "is it abstract enough" but "is it the thing the viewer would actually be
  holding".**

- **[heygen_icon] The bespoke beat got better, not worse, for losing the figure.** THE RE-SYNC TIMELINE:
  the take rides out of b5's exact seat to payoff size with its audio track; a RETICLE — four corner
  brackets — closes on the take's own frame on "detect your face" (what detection looks like on a video,
  drawn with no face in it); the FILM RAIL sweeps in as one `pathLength="100"` stroke and reaches full width
  on "the entire video"; on "to match" the span of PICTURE carrying the swapped line lights accent INSIDE
  the rail, exactly above the swapped audio — one span, drawn twice, in one colour, needing no annotation;
  and on "needs to be said" a playhead sweeps both tracks together while the card lights. Law 15 falls out
  by construction: the cut span is centred on the strip by the bar table itself (its middle lands on 103.0
  of a 206-unit viewBox, asserted at build time), so the rail's accent span, mapped from the same numbers,
  is centred too.

- **[heygen_icon] Three design defects died on STILLS, one on the ENCODE, none on a viewer.** (1) The first
  b6 layout left an 86du hole between the card and the audio for 2.3s while the rail was still to come —
  fixed with the lane's own dashed-slot grammar, the exact rect and radius of what lands in it. (2) "To
  match" was first a tall ring spanning both tracks; the still showed its interior was mostly empty white
  and that it cut through the rail — replaced by the accent span inside the rail. (3) A headless drop from
  the rail into the waveform ended in mid-air, because the composition axis falls in a GAP in the bar table
  — re-aimed upward to run between two real edges. **A connector into a bar chart must terminate on a
  drawn edge, not on a coordinate; the axis of a strip of bars is usually a hole.**

- **[heygen_icon] The frame-review dedup is blind to thin moving marks — adjudicate a payoff on native
  decodes, never on the kept-frame count.** The redesign's first render drew the playhead as a 3.2du
  hairline, and Gate 2 collapsed the ENTIRE payoff (25.0s → 27.0s) into stillness: a 12px-wide vertical mark
  at 4K contributes ~0.125 mean-abs-diff on a 16x16 grey grid against a 2.0 threshold, so the one moment the
  short exists for measured as no visual event at all. The fix was to give the payoff mass — a knob on a 5du
  stem, 16du across — and the verification was to decode 22.40 / 25.90 / 26.30 / 26.70 from the encode and
  look. The gap still collapses after the fix, which is the lesson: **"no distinct frame" is evidence about
  the DETECTOR, not about the video, whenever the moving element is thinner than a dedup cell.**

- **[heygen_icon] Mid-sweep frames are the proof a build is progressive.** Gate 2 flagged a new pop-in
  candidate at 22.33s; the native decode at 22.40 shows the film rail 78% through its 0.72s sweep with the
  dashed slot still visible to its right — the exact opposite of an element arriving fully formed. A pop-in
  marker is cheapest to resolve by decoding the frame INSIDE the entrance, not the ones around it.

- **[heygen_icon] The v2 park assertion earned its keep across a full redesign.** b6's whole geometry was
  rewritten (new card size, new seats, new objects) and the build-time comparison of the parked rect against
  `(MID_X, B5_FRAME_Y, MID_W, MID_H)` on all four numbers came along unchanged — so the reticle, seated
  through `sub_rect()` from the authored seat, cannot annotate a rect the card is not in. **A guard written
  for one defect is worth more when the code around it is thrown away.** Shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps,
  1100 frames, 36.672s container / 36.639 authored, 116,752,159 bytes, sha256 `56a76c79…`, decoded audio
  md5 `9e3b51f1…` byte-identical to BOTH rejected cuts; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings**, Gate 2 **34
  distinct states from 110 samples**, 0 idle candidates, 3 pop-in markers all resolved, every state read and
  confirmed to contain ZERO human figures; `idle_motion_scan` frames=147 idle_drift=no long_static=no;
  render sweep 0 of 1100 frames under 1% top-zone ink, min 8.2278%, median 26.266%; sync lag 0 on both
  streams; Gate 3 pass with 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor notes. Four renders total — two bought by the
  human-figure class, one by a hairline.

## Run 6 (impeccable) — hermessteps / DIAGRAM (2026-08-14, the run's last video and its third Diagram)

The batch's 19th and final short. Ten findings.

- [intake] **When the IDEA and the TRANSCRIPT disagree about a NUMBER, the disagreement is
  the first thing to settle and the cut script is where to settle it.** The Notion idea is
  titled "The six steps of learning for Hermes agents"; the token `six` appears in NONE of
  the 624 transcribed words, both script families say FIVE, and the winning take says "Here
  are five hidden settings that you can modify to make your Hermes Agent learn faster." A
  count is not a framing choice a builder gets to make, so it ships as an ASSERTION beside
  the take-detection asserts — `five hidden settings` must be present in the chosen take and
  `six` must be absent from its tokens — which means a future edit cannot quietly restore
  the idea title's number. The confirmation came from the REJECTED source image, whose own
  artwork enumerates exactly five in exactly his order and wording: **reading the rejected
  asset settled the short's central question before a frame was cut.**
- [intake] **An EIGHTH raw shape: two script families that tile, with the framing drifting
  INSIDE the winning family.** heygen met three families whose openings were stable; here
  family B rewords itself across twenty attempts ("that you can modify to improve the way
  through which" -> "that change the way through which" -> "you can modify to make your
  Hermes Agent learn faster"), so the key can only be the four tokens all twenty share
  (`here are five hidden`) and everything after that is drift. **Key on the INTERSECTION of
  the attempts, not on the best one.**
- [intake] **The gap rule earned an EQUALITY on this raw, and saying so is the point.**
  heygen demoted it to a bound because its silences separated script blocks; grokimagine
  required agreement because both its gaps were >24s. Here a >=2.0s rule answers word 392,
  the same word the content rule answers, so it is asserted as `gap_opens[-1] == first`.
  Three raws, three different standings for the same rule, each written down in the file
  that uses it. **Every rule gets the standing the raw earns it, per raw, in writing.**
- [law13] **A SPINE beats a set piece, and a spine that is a CYCLE can carry its own
  payoff.** The loop is on screen from frame 0 to the outro: five dots on a muted ellipse
  are the hook's promise, each dot BLOOMS into a station when its setting is named, the
  segment LEAVING that station sweeps toward the next, and 44 seconds later the fifth
  segment reaches the first station and the cycle closes. Nothing new enters at the payoff —
  the fifth dot was drawn in the hook and the fifth segment was authored with the other four
  — so the climax is caused entirely by objects the viewer has been watching for a minute.
  The corollary that made the two registers work: **the station glyph is the mechanism's
  THUMBNAIL and the detail band is the same mechanism at FULL SIZE**, so a map-plus-detail
  layout reads as one object opened rather than as two unrelated pictures.
- [law13][geometry] **In a vertical frame the free space is HORIZONTAL, and a cycle should
  spend it there.** The first cut drew a 104du circle, which is what the 232du of vertical
  budget allows once the detail band is subtracted — and it left 113du of dead cream on each
  side and forced 54du stations carrying 71du glyphs. The same height stretched across 364du
  of width carries 60du stations, an 88du mascot and 83du of visible segment. An ELLIPSE is
  not a stylistic softening of a circle here; it is what the aspect ratio pays for.
- [law15][geometry] **On an ellipse, equal parametric angles are NOT equal spacing, and
  "even spacing" is a geometry law.** At 168x102 the five 72-degree stations sit 129-175du
  apart — a 35% spread the eye reads immediately. Solved by walking the perimeter and
  bisecting on ARC LENGTH (172.2du x5, realised spread 0.01du) and asserted in the selftest.
  The same class bites the segment endpoints: a segment must clear the plate's ROUNDED
  silhouette `(half - r)*sqrt(2) + r`, not the square half-diagonal. Using the square
  diagonal left 14du of grey base ring at both ends of every segment, and at the payoff
  frame — the one where the cycle closes — that read as a DASHED ring rather than a closed
  one. The real silhouette leaves 6du and 22% more lit arc.
- [gate][pre-render] **A tween that is never authored renders COMPLETE, and the contact
  sheet is the only thing that can see it.** `arc_state` initially declared only the
  ALREADY-lit segments; the four that had not lit yet carried no `strokeDashoffset` at all,
  so they rendered fully drawn and the HOOK opened on a loop that was already closed — the
  exact opposite of the short's argument, in its first frame. Gate 1 is 0/0 on it (the atom
  is a canvas that never moves), Gate 2 would have read it as a legitimate state, Gate 3
  passed a build with it. **Declare EVERY member of a set's state at every beat's first
  frame, not just the ones that changed.**
- [law1] **When the ring is already the accent colour, the thing that travels it cannot be.**
  The lap pulse shipped terracotta on a terracotta ring and two "lap" stills were
  indistinguishable from the held ring. A DARK bead on a lit ring reads at a glance and
  needs no new geometry. General form: **a highlight's colour is chosen against what it
  travels over, not against the palette.**
- [gate][tooling] **`idle_motion_scan.py`'s crop is hard-coded `crop=1080:820:0:0`, which on
  a 2160x3840 master reads only the TOP-LEFT QUADRANT of the top zone.** Run directly on the
  4K encode it reported `long_static=YES at 13.8s` — a corner where nothing happens in that
  beat. Run on a 1080x1920 downscale of the same file, where the crop means what it was
  written to mean, it returns `long_static=no`. `idle_drift` (the only condition it exits
  non-zero on, and the only one LAW 1 is about) is `no` either way. **Downscale before
  running it on a 4K master; do not edit the shared script, and do not report its 4K
  long_static reading as a finding.**
- [paperwork] **The self-audit found three wrong numbers and all three were the same class:
  typed from reading rather than produced by a probe** (face_std claimed 34.9-46.3 against a
  measured 73.12-74.07; the source post claimed 1258 characters against 1275; the discard
  markers claimed 6 punctuated / 18 truncations against a measured 4 / 20). The third one
  lived in the CUT SCRIPT's docstring and in its edl text as well, so the honest fix was not
  to correct the paperwork against a file that disagreed with it: the script was fixed, the
  split became a build-time assertion and a derived edl field, the cut was re-run, and all
  five cut media files were hashed before and after to prove they are BYTE-IDENTICAL — so
  the media that fed the shipped render is provably unchanged. **When a claim and an
  artifact disagree, fix the artifact and prove the chain, then re-state the claim.**
- [hermessteps_diagram] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1932 frames, 64.405s
  container / 64.389 authored, 65 captions, 10 sections, 92 direct section children; take
  detection on a 2-family raw with 25 scripted openings (5 + 20), three rules ALL landing on
  word 392 (t=318.880, 232 words) with the gap rule asserted as an equality and the marker
  split (4 punctuated / 20 truncations) asserted separately, the head measured on a 10ms
  envelope by SUSTAIN (transients end 318.680 < head 318.760 < onset 318.860); the cut kept
  all 232 spoken words (two Scribe-pass spellings, zero drops, diffed token by token); Gate 1
  **0 errors / 0 warnings across 3 rounds** on the 1080 design copy (181 ids, 0 duplicates,
  93 tween selectors all resolving, 0 untweened section children, 16 `data-overlap-ok` — 10
  ring canvases and 6 connectors — 0 `data-bleed`, 0 `non-scaling-stroke`, 0 arrowheads, 83
  `pathLength="100"` paths, 0 svg scale tweens, 0 underlines, 0 caption-echo trigrams, 0
  caption-identity collisions over 6 typeset atoms, terminal-hold guard firing twice during
  authoring and passing at 0.36s, deepest authored ink y=395.0 against a 400 floor); 58
  pre-render stills over 4 rounds plus a 644-sample ink sweep that found four defects no gate
  reports; Gate 2 **46 distinct states from 193 samples**, 147 collapsed, 0 idle candidates,
  2 stillness markers both explained, **19 pop-in markers all resolved** (15 on five-point
  three-channel decodes, 4 on targeted probes inside the element's own design-space box), all
  46 states read plus 4 native-4K crops and 3 full-res decodes of the archive/delete
  sequence; `idle_motion_scan` frames=258 idle_drift=no long_static=no on the 1080 downscale;
  render sweep **0 of 1932 frames under 1% top-zone ink, 0 blank**, min 2.136%, median
  5.644%, min max-channel deviation 248; the LOOP counted rather than measured — 0/1/2/3/4/4/
  5/5/5 lit segments at nine times, every reading equal to the authored expectation, plus 5/5
  on the outro's own midpoints; the SKILL ROW proved through four states (5 black sparks -> 5
  terracotta -> 2 greyed -> 1 archived at 985px of surviving plate white -> 1 deleted at 0);
  caption band pill-free on 5 frames, 4 before the first spoken word at 0.119s and 1 after the
  last at 64.239; **0 third-party assets**, 1 official mark in its own published black line
  art at 0.0911x intrinsic, nothing upscaled; sync at **lag 0 on both streams** (audio
  r=0.9695 at 1ms, video r=0.9993 at 1 frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO remux;

## Run 7 (impeccable) — mcphidden / ICON (2026-08-15, first Fable 5 builder batch)

The connectors story told in the connector grammar — the meta-move planned, not
discovered. Genuinely new lessons only; everything else ran on the run-6 rails
and simply held.

- [law13] **When the story IS the grammar, dash-state is a narrative register.** This
  system already had two connector states (dashed slot = empty seat, solid accent = live
  join). A story about HIDDEN connectors gets a third for free: a DASHED, MUTED link with a
  static dash pattern, revealed by opacity, never swept — dashed-and-dim reads "exists,
  unseen" because the viewer already knows the vocabulary. The arc is then structural: the
  hook states the claim as a ghost link between the two chat apps, the bespoke scene docks
  real accent lines into revealed ports, and the outro re-states the hook composition with
  the link solid. Rule of thumb: a ghost link's dash pattern and its draw mechanism must not
  share machinery — pattern via `stroke-dasharray` on an UNSWEPT path, reveal via opacity;
  a `pathLength` sweep on a patterned path would fight its own dashes.
- [law13][composition] **DOM paint order is a reveal mechanism.** The hidden drawer is
  authored BEFORE the panel (painted under it), parked beneath the panel's solo seat, and
  ridden out as the panel rides left — so "opens a hidden panel" is real occlusion ending,
  not an opacity trick, and the two rides are plain single-property `x` tweens. The one
  trap: the covering plate is itself invisible until ITS entrance, so the drawer needs
  `opacity:0` until a `tl.set` flips it on at a moment it is provably covered (here 5.40s,
  a full second after the panel lands). An instant set while occluded is invisible by
  construction and costs no tween budget.
- [ink] **A beat that waits for its spoken cues can leave the whiteboard EMPTY, and only
  the deterministic ink sweep sees it.** b2 originally popped both tool marks on their
  names (24.3/25.6) inside a section starting 20.56 — 3.77s under 1% ink, 55 fully blank
  frames, and Gate 1 (0/0), Gate 2 (dedup collapses emptiness into one kept frame) and the
  stillness map all passed it. The fix is the chassis' own seated-cast pattern: marks settle
  at the section's first frame, and the NAMING moment becomes a hot-border emphasis on cue
  (law 5's move), so claim-sync survives while the canvas never goes blank. Corollary for
  every future builder: run the whole-video ink sweep BEFORE spending Gate 3 — on this
  build it was the only detector that fired, twice cheaper than a Gemini round.
- [anchors] **A bound anchored on a phrase can land on its ARTICLE and silently eat a
  terminal hold.** `find("a business or")` returns the start of "a" (27.24), not
  "business" (27.40) — 0.16s of hold gone with no visual symptom. The in-generator
  terminal-hold guard (assert every non-outro section's last recorded event ends >=0.28s
  before its bound) caught it at build time; anchor the bound on the content word and keep
  the guard in every fork of this file.
- [gate2] **A hot-border transition fires the pop-in detector exactly like an entrance.**
  The 25.33 marker on the shipped encode decomposes into the claudecode plate's border
  going terracotta (progressive: 18757 -> 25683 -> 25936 accent px over 0.3s) plus the
  caption pill shrinking 172k -> 64k px (the perplexity pill-width class). Resolve hot
  transitions the same way as entrances: count the accent inside the element's own box on
  exact decodes, never trust the 16x16 grey signature near a colour-only event.
- [law12] **The MCP mark is registered and black IS its colour** (simple-icons v16, CC0,
  the openai.png precedent; modelcontextprotocol.io renders it black-on-light). Registered
  as `logos.mcp` -> `ai-models/mcp-mark.svg` with measured extent 0.902x1.000 and ink
  30.5% (open line mark -> pad 0.19). SVG marks stage and render fine through `mark_plate`'s
  `<img>` — no rasterisation needed, and they re-rasterise crisp in the 4K twin.
- [mcphidden_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1313 frames, 43.776s container
  / 43.760 authored, 42 captions, 6 sections, 59 section-prefixed ids of 116 total; take
  detection on a 14-opening ONE-family raw (phrase key 'There are hidden' asserted MINIMAL,
  gap rule an EQUALITY, marker rule INAPPLICABLE with zero pre-take markers — a NINTH raw
  shape: the marker-less single-family raw), 1 complete take (word 349, t=147.380, 152
  words), head measured on a 10ms envelope with the one 20ms transient OUTSIDE the cut;
  Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings across 3 rounds** (116 ids, 60 tween targets, 0 untweened,
  11 overlap-ok, 23 pathLength paths, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 arrowheads, 0 echo trigrams,
  11 identity-checked atoms, deepest ink y=372 against a 400 floor); 33 pre-render stills
  x3 rounds, connector termini verified against INK (dock butts flush on socket ink, 2du
  border class); Gate 2 **34 distinct states from 131 samples**, 97 collapsed, 0 idle
  candidates, 1 stillness marker explained, **5 pop-in markers all resolved on exact
  decodes**; idle scan no/no on the 1080 downscale; render sweep **0 of 1313 frames under

## Run 7 — harness / DIAGRAM (2026-08-15, first Fable 5 builder batch, the run's first Diagram)

- [gsap] **A scale TWEEN replaces a PARKED scale, and no gate can see the collapse.** GSAP
  transform components are independent: an atom parked with `tl.set(..., {x, y})` keeps its
  park through any scale tween, but an atom parked with a SCALE (`scale:1.579` standing in
  for its pre-dock size) loses it the instant `settle()`'s fromTo runs — the fromTo's scale
  leg overwrites the component, and the element quietly collapses to its authored size at
  the beat's open while holding its parked position. Three parked brains and the nameplate
  tile were all doing this (120→76du, 120→44du, 76→52du), Gate 1 was 0/0 (authored boxes),
  and the 3fps thumbnails read the wrong sizes as legitimate states. Found by READING the
  contact sheet against expectations and then measuring `getBoundingClientRect` + computed
  transform on the paused timeline. The fix is authoring law, not a tween argument: **an
  atom parked at a scale gets NO independent scale tween** — its park `set()` keeps it a
  tween target for the audit, its entrance (if any) must END at the parked scale (the b7
  pop runs 0.95→1.25, not 0.76→1), and the ride that releases the park carries `scale:1`.
  Verified with an 8-point live-DOM size table before re-rendering. Distinct from the
  smallteams residual-matrix class: that was an SVG origin artifact; this is plain component
  replacement on DIVs, and it fires on every author-final-park-bigger pattern the factory's
  own gptvoice rule produces.
- [gate2] **A review thumbnail's TIMESTAMP can lie, not just its resolution.** Near the
  dense b3→b4 boundary the frame_review JPGs lag their labels by ~0.4s: the frame labelled
  23.0s lacks the world tiles while the DECODED 23.0 frame carries them (tile box
  cream-white 81225 empty → 66863 at 22.80 → 64872 at 23.00; fork 0 → 3318 → 17332 across
  23.0–23.6, exactly as authored). The first read of the manifest suggested the build's
  cues ran late; direct decodes proved the ENCODE exact and the thumbnails shifted.
  Extends the heygen dedup lesson one level: "the manifest is a statement about the
  detector" now covers the extraction clock too — adjudicate timing on `ffmpeg -ss` decodes
  of the encode, never on review JPGs.
- [law13] **A dock is a grammar, not a scene: give the shell an openable side and every
  beat inherits the move.** The cage's four separately-classed strokes (built in
  personalapps so a boundary could BREAK) here let a machine's TOP physically retract and
  draw shut — and once b3's first dock teaches open→travel→close→click, the b4 transplant,
  the b5 market dock and the b7 Sol-into-Claude-Code finale are all the same three tweens
  at different seats. The peak beat cost nothing new; it had been rehearsed twice before it
  happened. (Also the third sighting of the metric-per-ground class: the pop-in probe read
  0 for the MUTED market shells on dark/terra channels — grey strokes need a
  cream-deviation channel.)
- [law12] **When two official marks share a glyph, the shared glyph can BE the claim.**
  ChatGPT's app tile IS OpenAI's blossom on green, so the b0 peek (the white blossom card
  sliding out from behind the green tile) and the b6 peel draw "the GPT model behind
  ChatGPT" with zero invented artwork — the brand system's own redundancy carries the
  thesis. Check the registry for glyph collisions before treating them as a defect; this
  one was the argument.
- [intake] **The gap rule can answer with a DISCARD, and the bound demotion absorbs even
  that.** This raw's last >=8s silence opens a 5-word abandoned take ("ChatGPT is lying to
  you.") 2.94s before the real one, so the gap rule under-shoots onto an opening that is

  pass (with the batch keyterms) wrote `5.6 Sol` — adjudicated ACOUSTICALLY per grokimagine
  and this time the keyterm was CONFIRMED, not refuted: two frication bands, a stressed
  open nucleus (RMS 0.2755, ZCR 0.03) and a voiced lateral coda are /sɒl/, a separate word.
  The audio decides in both directions.

## Run 7 (impeccable) — appsdistrib / KINETIC (2026-08-15, first Fable 5 builder batch)

The batch's longest raw (422.55s, 709 words, ten drifting scripted attempts plus five
marker fragments) and the lane's first build by a Fable 5 builder. Nine findings.

- [intake] **A NINTH raw shape: a discard marker INSIDE the winning take that is a
  STUTTER, not a boundary — and the sibling assertion rejects the only complete take.**
  Word 697 `ma-` ("latest news on the ma- on the latest model releases") is a
  self-truncation Scribe marks exactly like a restart, 2.1s BEFORE the spoken sign-off.
  Every sibling cut asserts "no discard marker inside the final take"; here that
  assertion fails the take it exists to ship. The discriminators that separate a mid-take
  stutter from a restart are structural, not acoustic: no opening key ever fires after
  it, no >=2.0s gap follows it, the sentence resumes 0.08s later, and the sign-off lands
  behind it. Assert the in-take marker set EQUALS the expected stutter (index, text) and
  hand it to the captions as drop material — never widen the tolerance to "some markers
  are fine".
- [law6] **The FOURTH stutter form: the false start a dropped truncation leaves behind
  is a BIGRAM immediate repetition, invisible to the unigram rule.** Dropping `ma-`
  leaves "...news on the | on the latest..." — grok46's equal-next-token test sees
  nothing (the,on are not adjacent-equal). A declared bigram pass (pair i,i+1 ==
  normalised pair i+2,i+3 within 0.5s -> drop the first pair) fixes the pill, and like
  CAPTION_SPELLING it must be ASSERTED to fire exactly the declared number of times: a
  silent no-op captions the stutter, a trigger-happy pass eats real speech (the
  personalapps "very, very" class one level up).
- [intake] **Validate the SIGN-OFF key against the raw, not just the opening key: a dead
  take can reach the outro line and die.** The sibling sign-off ('follow for more ai
  news') fires TWICE on this raw — the w247 attempt gets all the way into "follow for
  more AI news and tutorials ... the latest new, the, the LU" before collapsing. Keying
  completeness on it would have shipped a take that never closes. 'see you in the next'
  fires once; the REJECTED key's count (2) is asserted so a re-transcription that changes
  the shape fails loudly. Same standing logic as the gap rule: every key gets the
  standing the raw earns it, in writing.
- [law14] **The quote-to-original rule now has an ACCURACY exception, and it is asserted
  in both directions.** The handed URL is @levelsio QUOTING @thepatwalls (erdos trap,
  fourth sighting) — but the quoted original argues profit margins and Meta ads, claims
  Miguel never makes, while the QUOTING post's own ladder ("More competition -> harder
  to get attention on your app") IS the thesis. grokimagine's exception shipped the
  quoting post on credibility grounds; this build extends it to accuracy grounds — the
  stronger reason, since a ring cannot scope the eye to a matching claim that does not
  exist. The renderer asserts the handed post still quotes that id AND that the quoted
  post still carries the disqualifying claim set ('Profit margins' tripwire), so a
  payload change forces a re-judge instead of silently flipping the ruling. Also the
  builders_counter printed-once rule got its second sighting (@levelsio's display name
  IS the handle) and is asserted (name == '@'+username or the two-line who-block must
  come back).
- [law15] **A checklist block centred for its WIDER row holds every earlier partial
  state off-axis — mathvoice's class in a new costume, fixed with oneprompt's dx
  grammar.** b8's block width comes from DISTRIBUTE; the 1.1s row-1-alone state sat 66du
  left of centre on the contact sheet. Park the first row's cast right by exactly
  (tw2-tw1)/2 and release on the second row's cue (setx/stepx, the horizontal twin of
  stepy): the visible ink is centred at every held instant and the ride to the shared
  left rail IS the checklist forming.
- [gate1] **geometry_audit reads className off every atom, and a bare top-level `<svg>`
  crashes it — SVGAnimatedString is not a string.** The audit's collector stores
  `a.className` raw; on an svg element that is an object and `check_sample` dies on
  `.startswith`. Wrap the svg in a positioned DIV (the icon lane's `svg_free` shape,
  which is why no sibling ever hit this) and park/tween the WRAPPER; the path keeps its
  own id for the dash sweep. Do not edit the shared script mid-run.
- [verify] **An accent-coloured element is invisible to a dark-ink counter, and a probe
  band that ignores the lane's park/step dy measures empty ground — two metric errors in
  one verifier, both adjudicated on decoded frames.** The summit token (terra) can never
  register as a 7th dark brick run: [1,6] + a terra-px probe IS the correct final state,
  and writing `expect [1,7]` was the builder's error, not the render's. And the b6 cell
  probe read 0 cells on a frame whose cell is plainly visible because it probed the
  FINAL band at a PARKED time — the grokimagine measured-in-the-wrong-place class,
  second sighting, now in a step-group lane: every probe band must carry the dy of ITS
  OWN held state, and mid-ride timestamps are not probe times.
- [law10][law13] **An unlabelled miniature of a stacked-brick scene reads as a BATTERY.**
  The outro's first theme glyph (26x9 bricks, no labels) was a charge indicator to any
  fresh eye. A scene reprised in miniature keeps its LABELS (BUILD / DISTRIBUTE at mono
  12) — the words are what make it the short's signature rather than a status icon —
  and the lockup gives up a step of type size to pay for the room.
- [guards] **The terminal-hold guard costs three lines as bookkeeping instead of a
  parser.** Every section records its own last event completion (`Z.ev`) as it authors
  tweens, and the guard asserts >=0.30s against the cut. It fired twice during
  authoring (b6 meter wipe trimmed 0.42 -> 0.36s, the b8 `?` re-cued) and both fixes
  were re-timings, exactly as mathvoice prescribed.

## Run 7 (impeccable) — billionusers / COUNTER (2026-08-15, first Fable 5 builder batch)

The restart-heaviest raw of the batch (349.9s, 751 words, 20 openings on one stem) and
the lane's first Fable build. Genuinely new lessons only; the run-6 rails held.

- [intake] **An EIGHTH raw shape: the CLEAN PUNCTUATED ABANDON.** Two attempts here end
  "Over one billion people are users of ChatGPT." — fully punctuated, no ellipsis, no
  hyphen, no spoken "No." — and just stop. The marker rule cannot see that boundary BY
  CONSTRUCTION (its three signatures all live on the final token, and this final token is
  clean), so on this raw the last discard marker sits 8 words and 3.4s before the winner
  and the marker rule earns exactly its bound standing. And the winning take opens 0.94s
  (measured voiced-end to sustained onset) after the abandon — below any usable gap
  threshold — so BOTH auxiliary rules are bounds and the content rule alone (opening
  phrase + sign-off, LAST complete take wins) picks the take. Distinct from appsdistrib's
  ninth shape (a marker INSIDE the take): this is an attempt whose END carries no marker
  at all. Also on this raw: a near-miss attempt reaches "And I'll see..." — six words
  short of the sign-off — so a sign-off key on "see" instead of the "next one" bigram
  would have shipped a take with no ending.
- [intake] **A silence that runs to the take window's END is the take's TAIL, not an
  interior pause.** The silence-cap logic treats every detected silence as interior:
  trim, keep 0.16s, resume. On the last one that produced a 0.08s orphan segment of
  nothing after the sign-off (survived the sibling <0.05s filter by 30ms). The rule that
  fixes the class: a silence whose end reaches the window end TERMINATES the cut at
  voice_end + 0.35s. Measured, the voice dies at 349.367 and the raw runs to 350.0 —
  the orphan was pure room tone with a concat seam in it.
- [transcript] **A keyterm ADDITION can manufacture a mis-transcription in an ADJACENT
  proper noun.** grokimagine's finding was a standing vocab entry poisoning a new word;
  this is its mirror: ADDING `ChatGPT Work` (this take's product) gave Scribe a prior for
  product-shaped "X Work" splits, and the cut pass turned "Claude Cowork" — which BOTH
  independent raw utterances transcribe correctly — into "Claude Code Work". Adjudicated
  on a 5ms envelope + ZCR: between the /oU/ of "Co" and "work" the signal stays voiced at
  0.028-0.066 RMS with ZCR 0.03-0.06 and never reaches stop closure — a /w/ glide, no
  /d/; Claude's own /d/ release (ZCR 0.36) and work's final /k/ (0.38) are the controls
  either side. The mathvoice `respell()` mechanism had to grow: the fix here is a token
  SEQUENCE (("Claude","Code","Work,") -> ("Claude","Cowork,")), merging the second and
  third tokens' timing, still asserted to fire exactly once, transcript file untouched,
  timeline anchors keyed on the transcript's own tokens.
- [law6] **The unpunctuated-repeat stutter rule has a false-positive class: the
  deliberately DOUBLED product name.** "Google Plus Plus." repeats "Plus" at a 0.06s gap
  with no punctuation on the first — every signature of grok46's third stutter form — and
  dropping it would change his claim to "Google Plus". personalapps' punctuation
  discriminator cannot save it (no comma). A REPEAT_OK whitelist pair ((plus,plus)),
  asserted to fire exactly once, is the honest fix: the guard stays hot for real stutters
  and the name survives because the build DECLARED it, not because the rule got softer.
- [law13] **A bespoke scene can be TWO meters at right angles, and then the reduction and
  the completion are the same object.** THE ADOPTION POOL: his two spatial claims are one
  liquid measured on two axes — the surface spreads CENTER-OUT to complete the full
  column on "a mile wide" (meter completes), and the depth fill under the same surface
  wets ONLY the first band of a 162-unit rail on "an inch deep", ring on the wet inch.
  builders' I5 defense (a deliberate reduction must be the SUBJECT of its beat, opposite
  something that completes) gets a sharper form here: the reduction IS the completion's
  own object seen from the other axis. Encode-verified: surface 0.9928 full, wet band
  0.9604, rail below the wet 0.0271, ring at 10246 accent px.
- [ink] **Naked TRACK_BG is invisible to the encode ink metric, and the fix is a
  PRIMITIVE, not a patch.** rgba(20,20,22,0.12) on cream deviates 26/255 — under the
  metric's 34 threshold (the agentreviews artifact) — so every beat that opens on bare
  tracks opens metrically blank. Render 1 measured a 31-frame and an 18-frame under-1%
  run at two section opens. One change to the shared track() primitive (2px solid
  rgba(20,20,22,.28) border) made every empty track real ink in all six beats that draw
  one, reads as a deliberate design system, and took the shipped encode to 5 isolated
  transition blips (1-2 frames each, min max-channel deviation 100/255, 0 blank).
- [ink] **A section bound is also an INK decision.** The other half of the 31-frame fix
  was moving b1's bound from "Let me explain" to "When you look at": the hook's dimmed
  scene (grey odometer, dimmed meter, faded mark) holds real ink through the pivot line,
  and the news beat then opens 0.23s before its card can land instead of 1.27s. When a
  beat's first content arrives late, ask whether the CUT is early before adding chrome.
- [gate1] **A bare positioned `<svg class="abs">` crashes the geometry audit.** An SVG
  root's className is an SVGAnimatedString — a dict in the audit's JS bridge, no
  .startswith — and the audit dies with AttributeError before measuring anything. Every
  sibling wraps positioned svg in a div; now it is a rule with a reason instead of a
  habit: **positioned atoms are DIVs; svg lives inside.**
- [gate2] **Two dedup blind spots can stack into one fake stillness window.** A 4.7s
  "still" marker (35.3-40.0) contained the dial tick sweep (thin strokes — the perplexity
  2.6du class) AND the ChatGPT mark landing (a white plate on cream is ~12/255 at 16x16
  grey). Both proven on exact decodes: mark-seat white px 0 -> 751 -> 5639 across its
  38.88 cue, progressive on three frames. White-plate-on-cream entrances are structurally
  invisible to Gate 2 — the meter census and per-cue decode probes are the instrument
  that sees them.
- [verify] **A probe key must be re-chosen against the composition's OWN palette, and its
  threshold is measured, not inherited.** builders' card detector keys on avatar GREEN;
  here the ChatGPT knot is green and stands in two beats. The replacement keys on the
  article screenshot's dark NAV BAND with its rows derived from the staged card.png's own
  pixels — and the first threshold (0.55) turned out to sit 0.01 above the hook's
  odometer digits sweeping the same rows (0.5397 dark, glyph strokes). Measured both
  populations, set 0.65: card 0.8524, best non-card 0.5397, real margin both ways
  (heygen's margin rule, new sighting).

## Run 7 (impeccable) — mythos / ICON (2026-08-16, first Fable 5 builder batch)

The batch's two-family raw (568 words: an abandoned question-only era, then a rewritten
opening) and a build that survived a mid-chain context break. Genuinely new lessons only.

- [ink] **Two same-ground beats can hide a FULLY BLANK hole at their seam, and only the
  whole-video ink sweep sees it.** b6 (dark) opened at "In" (29.86) with its first child
  popping on "cybersecurity," (30.00) — so b6's opaque ground covered b5's held wall for
  0.14s: 5 frames of uniform rgb(33,37,36), max-channel deviation 0. Gate 1 was 0/0
  (authored boxes are fine), Gate 2's dedup collapsed the hole into the section-swap kept
  frame, and dark-to-dark reads as a normal cut on thumbnails. The fix solved ink and
  claim-sync in ONE move: bound moved onto the word itself ("cybersecurity," 30.06, the
  billionusers bound-is-an-ink-decision class) plus a FRAME-0-SAFE settle() for the term —
  the section's first frame carries full ink and the key term now debuts exactly ON its
  spoken word. Rule of thumb: a section whose first child enters by pop() on a cue LATER
  than its bound is structurally blank in between; either pull the bound to the cue or
  switch the opener to settle.
- [verify] **An odd crop dimension crashes raw-video decodes silently-late: ffmpeg's
  yuv420p path rounds `crop=1705:...` down to 1704 and the numpy reshape throws.** The
  inherited verify script had NEVER completed a run — its exit-1 stderr was still on disk.
  Causality/probe crops must be even-dimensioned (1px nudges are harmless), and a verify
  script existing is not a verify RUN: check for its output file, not its file.
- [resume] **A context break voids freshness, not work: re-run what is cheap, re-measure
  what is claimed.** On resume, the Gate 1 report (23:08) predated the final index.html
  (00:04) — re-ran it (0/0); the mouth-window "verified by extraction" docstring claim was
  re-extracted and re-read; the ring's apparent clipping of "private." in a review JPG was
  adjudicated on a full-resolution decode (JPG artifact — the ring encloses all four
  lines). Artifacts on disk are claims about the past; gates attach to the present files.
- [transcript] **The raw-take-vs-tight token diff is a mandatory check, and it can flag a
  FUNCTION word no keyterm touched.** Diffing the 135 raw-take tokens against the 134
  tight tokens surfaced exactly two variants: 'one hundred'->'100' (formatting) and raw
  'had' vs tight 'have' — a caption-visible conflict. Adjudicated acoustically (5ms
  RMS+ZCR): a 35ms voiced approximant stage then a 50ms voice-bar dip whose floor
  (0.012-0.03) never approaches true closure (head-silence control 0.0004) and no /d/
  release burst before "been"'s /b/ — a /v/, so the tight pass's 'have' ships. The
  cookbook grows: /v/ vs /d/ separates on closure FLOOR vs the raw's own measured silence
  floor, plus burst absence — never on the dip's mere existence.
- [intake] **When a session rewrites its opening mid-way, the shared stem makes the
  phrase key a family separator only after EXTENSION — and the collision is asserted.**
  Family A (9 openings, "Did you know that Claude [Fable] Mythos ...?", abandoned) shares
  'Did you know that Claude' with family B's winner; the key had to run through 'saved'
  to fire only in B (13 openings). heygen's family tiling + personalapps' extended stem
  in one raw; the assertion that the short stem DOES collide is what keeps a
  re-transcription from silently flipping eras.
- [gate2] **Probe hygiene, two repeat sightings in one build: a white-count metric
  saturates on CREAM (min channel 234 passes any white threshold — key pop probes on the
  element's ACCENT ink there; white only on dark grounds), and a probe box must carry the
  PARK of its own held state** (the term probe read 0 at the authored seat while the term
  sat parked 92du lower; grokimagine's measured-in-the-wrong-place class). Both were the
  builder's probe errors, both resolved by re-measuring — the composition was right.
- [guards] **The terminal-hold guard is chassis contract; a fork that loses it ships
  thinner holds SILENTLY.** This fork dropped the in-generator guard and the OFFENSE
  label's hold landed at 0.26s (convention: >=0.28-0.30) — found only during paperwork
  measurement, decode-verified still-and-complete (3744 cream px pixel-identical at
  39.60/39.70/39.80) so it shipped, but the guard would have re-timed it for free at
  authoring. Carry the guard in every future fork; measuring after the fact is the
  expensive version of asserting before.
- [mythos_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1314 frames, 43.819s container /
  43.799 authored, 41 captions, 8 sections, 115 ids, 56 tween targets, 5 overlap-ok, 12
  pathLength paths, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 arrowheads; take detection on a 568-word
  TWO-FAMILY raw (A: 9 question-only openings abandoned; B: 13 openings on the extended
  key), 22 pre-take discard markers (7 punctuated "No." + 15 truncations, last ends
  1.70s before the head), gap + marker rules both demoted to bounds, content rule alone
  picking word 433 (t=274.72, 135 words), head measured on a 10ms envelope (sustained
  onset 274.710, Scribe 10ms late, cut head asserted inside the measured <=0.0004 RMS

  paused-timeline stills incl. a bound-first-frame proof; Gate 2 **32 distinct states
  from 131 samples**, 9 pop-in markers all resolved on exact decodes, the 5.0s stillness

  56.9->47.0); encode sweep **0 of 1314 frames blank** (render 1 had 5 — the seam hole
  above), min ink 0.867%, median 11.54%, 4 under-1% frames in 3 transition blips; REAL
  tweet 3.133s from pixels, ring enclosing the whole claim paragraph, badge
  payload-true, zero metrics, card at 0.9225x; marks claude 0.380x / firefox 0.113x

  renders — the second bought by the ink sweep's seam hole, never by geometry; Gemini
  calls: exactly 1.

## Run 7 (impeccable) — hermesvoice / ICON (2026-08-16, Opus 5 builder)

The batch's FOUR-FAMILY drifting raw (413 words, 13 attempts, the opening re-worded
on almost every one) and the run's first voice/privacy story. Genuinely new lessons
only; the run-6/7 rails held everywhere else.

- [intake] **A TENTH raw shape: the DRIFTING SCRIPT, where the key is a single VERB
  and minimality runs BACKWARDS.** Every sibling asserts its phrase key is minimal by
  showing a shorter key COLLIDES. Here the opening drifts through four families
  ("You can now clone your voice" / "I can now clone your voice" / "...your ENTIRE
  voice" / "I can clone your voice"), so no phrase survives — but the verb `clone`
  fires exactly 13 times, once per attempt, with zero in-take collisions. The key is
  already one token, so the assertion has to run the other way: EXTENDING it must buy
  nothing (`clone your` resolves to the identical 13 indices), and the gerund
  `cloning` — a fragment at w70 — is asserted to fire once and not be matched. When a
  raw drifts, key on the one word the script cannot re-word, and prove the extension
  is redundant instead of proving the contraction collides.
- [intake] **Recovering an opening INDEX from a mid-phrase key needs a punctuation
  stop, not a token whitelist.** Walking back from a `clone` hit over the prefix set
  {i, you, can, now} is correct until hit 244, where the previous token is the discard
  marker "Now..." — which normalises to `now` and is swallowed, reporting the opening
  one word early. The stop condition that fixes the class is textual, not semantic:
  halt at any token carrying terminal punctuation or a truncation dash. Every opening
  in every raw is preceded by exactly that.
- [intake] **The "spoken No." count is a REGEX claim, and a startswith test silently
  inflates it.** The edl recorded 2 spoken discards on a raw that has none: the
  filter was `text.lower().startswith("no")`, which matches the truncations "Nous..."
  and "Now...". The detector's own punctuated regex says 0. Corrected by a new
  `--edl-only` path that recomputes and rewrites edl.json WITHOUT re-encoding —
  because re-running the cut would rewrite audio.wav and silently stale the tight
  transcript cached against it. Rule: every recorded field must be produced by the
  same predicate that produced the decision, and a bookkeeping fix must never be able
  to touch media.
- [law17] **A voice story is a FACE story, and the addendum bites before you notice.**
  Every natural sketch for "you talk to it and it talks back" is a person: a speaker,
  a listener, a silhouette with a soundwave at its mouth. The addendum bans all of it.
  What replaced them: chat bubbles whose CONTENT is a waveform (a voice message is an
  object, and it is also real product anatomy), a boundary that is a machine, a cloud
  that is the alternative. The build page-greps for figure vocabulary so the class
  cannot creep back in a later pass.
- [law13] **A bespoke scene can be a QUESTION rather than a mechanism: does the thing
  cross the wall?** THE VOICE THAT NEVER CROSSES THE WALL draws the machine as a real
  boundary with Hermes inside it, and puts the whole argument in the pipeline's SHAPE
  — waveform -> SPEECH TO TEXT -> text lines -> TEXT TO SPEECH -> waveform, all of it
  inside. The counter-example is then drawn AND KILLED: a cloud lands outside, a
  dashed muted leak rises toward it, and a plug snaps onto the wall exactly where the
  two meet. Two claims ("the whole chain is in here", "nothing gets out") answered by
  one drawing. Transferable: when a story is spatial, build the SPACE and let the
  shapes inside it carry the sentences.
- [law19][composition] **A left-to-right BUILD is a Law-19 trap, and the fix is to
  make the group symmetric and let each part's own growth carry the direction.** The
  five-atom voice pipeline wanted to build left to right (the flow), which puts the
  first element 178du off-axis while it is alone. Cascading displacements across five
  atoms is unreadable. What works: the group arrives together on AX, and the two
  waveforms grow OUTWARD from the centre — symmetric at every instant, and each
  wave's own direction still reads as flow. Law 19 never had to fire.
- [ink][stills] **A `settle()` is scale-only, so an element that is meant to ARRIVE
  must be opacity-gated — and the contact sheet is the only place you see the
  difference.** "NOUS RESEARCH" and the outro handle were both entering by settle, so
  both were painted at their beat's frame 0 and merely ticked at their cue 1.5s and
  1.0s later. Gate 1 sees authored boxes, the ink sweep sees MORE ink (not less), and
  Gate 3 passed it. Only reading the Gate-2 sheet against the narration showed the
  name standing there before it was said. Corollary that also fired: an ungated
  handle appears before the rule that sits ABOVE it, inverting BUILD ORDER.
- [stills] **A wrapper parked at `scaleX:0.02` paints a visible ink sliver.** The
  pre-render census caught the same 1.3du tick sitting on THREE beats' opening frames.
  Gate the opacity until the growth's own cue; every gated beat still cleared 2.9%
  ink without it, and the geometry audit's ghost rule is satisfied because the atom
  reaches full size later in the timeline.
- [craft] **A centred header inside a card and a vertical connector on the axis cannot
  coexist — and the fix is a naming CONVENTION, not a nudge.** The machine's "YOUR
  MACHINE" header sat exactly where the leak had to run. Moving the label OUTSIDE the
  boundary (below it) matched what the cloud and the outro miniature already did, so
  every named object in the short now labels itself the same way and the axis band
  inside the machine belongs to the story.
- [craft] **An annotation must not be the colour of the band it lands on — second
  sighting, now on a wall.** The wall plug was TERRA_2 on a wall that is TERRA_2 by
  that moment: measured invisible on the stills sheet. Deep TERRA at 10du against the
  3du wall reads as a plug sitting proud of it (the billionusers sounding-ring class,
  generalised: check the annotation's colour against the state of its TARGET at the
  annotation's own time, not against the ground).
- [craft] **MOCK-UI ANATOMY includes ORIENTATION.** The chat beat shipped its first
  render with YOUR message left-aligned and the other party's avatar on the right —
  the mirror of every real chat app. Colored marks and honest controls are not enough;
  a UI that is laid out backwards is lorem chrome with better parts. Asserted now:
  mirrored side margins, the avatar centred on its own message row and never touching
  its bubble, and YOUR message first.
- [gate2] **A colour-turn ramp must be measured as COLOUR, not as a pixel count.** The
  21.33 pop-in marker looked instantaneous under a "pixels near TERRA" probe (0 ->
  17,509 in one sample) purely because a partial transition already falls inside the
  tolerance. Mean RGB over the same band shows five distinct decoded values across
  0.4s. When the event IS a colour, the metric has to be the colour.
- [verify] **The probe-placement class fires again the moment a composition moves.**
  Re-orienting the chat left the `b3_youwave` probe rect on the old seat, so it read 0
  on a frame whose waveform is plainly accent. Third sighting (grokimagine,
  appsdistrib, here): when a beat's geometry changes, re-derive every probe band that
  points into it — the composition is not the thing that is usually wrong.
- [hermesvoice_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1321 frames, 44.053s
  container / 44.019 authored, 40 captions, 8 sections, 127 ids, 69 tween targets, 4
  overlap-ok, 0 pathLength paths, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 arrowheads; take detection
