- **2026-08-16 GROUP-INK CENTERING IS A BUILD-TIME ASSERT, NOT A LAYOUT HOPE (mcphidden v3).** Both
  of Miguel's last two mcphidden defects were the same failure: a lockup positioned inside a
  BORDERED container using border-box arithmetic, when absolutely-positioned children lay out in
  the PADDING box — every child silently shifts +border on both axes. The ADD CUSTOM CONNECTOR
  lockup measured +2.53du right / +2.40du low of its dashed pill's centre on decoded 2160px (the
  2.4du dashed border, plus the 110du label box's advance slack around the 107.5du text run); the
  CUSTOM drawer's field rows sat 14du-left/22du-right in their card (the 2du card border compounding
  an off-axis FIELD_X). The pattern that fixes the CLASS: (1) define the group's INK span from
  measured constants (plus glyph + measured text-run width, never the nominal advance box — the
  mathvoice lesson applied to lockups); (2) place the group by solving for the padding-box position
  that centres that ink in the BORDER box; (3) assert at build time that the computed ink centre
  equals the container centre within 0.3du, so any future edit that breaks centring kills the build
  instead of shipping. Decision rule for rows-with-edge-ports: dashed docking sockets are BORDER
  FURNITURE (they stay seated on the card edge so line butts land on socket ink); the rows centre on
  the CARD'S OWN AXIS — the same axis as the card's header — not in the interior-minus-socket zone
  (that would move rows AWAY from the gap the eye complains about). Verified on decoded pixels:
  lockup residual (-0.40, -0.53)du (sub-pixel at 1080, was ~10px at 4K); field ink 19.47..119.73 in
  the 140du card, symmetric. Law 15's actual test stays perceptual: measure, fix, then LOOK at the
  still the way the reviewer will.

- **2026-08-16 THE SOCKET RULING IS OVERTURNED — INTERIOR FURNITURE LIVES FULLY INSIDE ITS CARD
  (mcphidden v4, Opus fix pass).** The v3 pass RULED that dashed docking sockets are "border
  furniture" that stay seated on the card's right edge so a dock line's butt lands on socket ink.
  Miguel overturned that ruling from a screenshot: "the dashed checkboxes touch the edge of the
  CUSTOM card — it's annoying." The law is now in STANDARD.md: sockets, ports and any interior
  furniture live FULLY INSIDE their card with a visible margin, never touching, straddling or
  hanging off the edge; connector lines MAY cross the card border to reach an interior socket, and
  that crossing is normal, not a defect. Measured on the v3 encode: socket ink 377.87..393.87du
  against a card border box of 252..392 (interior edge 390.13) — 3.73du across the border ink and
  1.87du fully outside the card. The fix that also kills the class: give the card a uniform
  CARD_PAD and pin the row's two atoms `left:CARD_PAD` / `right:CARD_PAD`, so the layout engine
  centres the field+gap+socket group in the REAL padding box; then derive the dock line's x0 from
  the socket's own right edge so the butt lands mid-stroke on its ink. After: socket ink
  364.00..380.00 with a clean 10.13du of white before the card's border, measured on the shipped
  encode. Builder judgment does not survive Miguel's eye — when a ruling exists only because it was
  convenient for the grammar, expect it to be overturned.

- **2026-08-16 VERIFY EVERY ANNOTATION FROM INSIDE ITS ACTIVE WINDOW (mcphidden v4).** The ADD
  CUSTOM CONNECTOR highlight ring shipped visibly off-centre through THREE verification passes
  because it is on screen for 1.98s (9.62-11.60) and every check that ran — the geometry audit's
  0.5s sweep, the stills sheet, the frame-review manifest, the Gemini pass — either sampled elsewhere
  or judged the frame as a whole. Nobody ever decoded a frame from the ring's own window and measured
  ring ink against pill ink on all four sides. When someone finally did: L 8.800 / R 5.600 / T 8.800
  / B 5.600du, centre off (-1.600, -1.600)du = 6px each way at 4K. STANDARD.md now carries this as a
  VERIFICATION RULE, and `shorts_run7/gen/measure_mcphidden_beat.py` is the detector: it seeks the
  paused timeline to each annotation's active window and prints live-rect margins in design units.
  A beat-long annotation is exactly the thing a static-state check cannot see.

- **2026-08-16 CHROMIUM FLOORS BORDER WIDTHS, SO EVERY HAND-COMPUTED CARD CENTRE IS WRONG — AND
  WRONG BY A DIFFERENT AMOUNT IN THE 4K COPY (mcphidden v4).** The deep root cause behind all four
  mcphidden centring defects, not just the padding-box offset the v3 pass named. A 2du border
  authors as 3.75px, and Chromium's used value is FLOORED to whole CSS pixels: it paints at 3px
  (1.600du) in the 1080 audit copy and at 7px of 7.5 (1.867du) in the 4K `zoom:2` copy. So any
  constant of the form `width - 2*PLATE_BORDER` or `left = W - child` is off by a resolution-
  dependent amount, and a fix verified on 1080 stills can still be wrong on the shipped 4K encode.
  Stop doing the arithmetic. Four structural moves cover every case: (1) an annotation goes INSIDE
  the same box as its target (the ring became the panel's last child, and concentricity dropped from
  1.600du to 0.033du with no measurement at all); (2) symmetric interior furniture is pinned
  `left:P` / `right:P`; (3) a row anchored to a GLOBAL axis is seated from the card's centre with
  `top:50%` + `margin-top` (this caught a fifth defect nobody had noticed: the CUSTOM card's rows
  sat 1.6-1.87du BELOW the port axis, so every cable entered its 16du port off-centre); (4) a
  centred mono header uses `left:0;right:0` plus `text-indent:{letter-spacing}` — `text-align:center`
  counts the trailing letter-space as advance but never paints it, which parked both b1 headers
  exactly ls/2 = 1.1du left of their own axis. Back each move with a build-time assert AND a page
  grep that pins the structure (`b1-panel < b1-add < b1-ring < b1-t0`), so a future edit that
  reverts to arithmetic kills the build.

- **2026-08-16 A FIX PASS THAT ONLY FIXES WHAT IT WAS TOLD IS A FAILED FIX PASS (mcphidden v4).**
  Two Fable fix passes each shipped this short with a new visible defect, because each measured
  exactly the elements named in the brief. The Opus pass was ordered to distrust every existing
  constant and sweep the whole beat: the two named defects came with FOUR more of the identical
  class (drawer rows off the port axis, panel row stack 1.93du off the card axis, both card headers
  1.1du off, the seated-port pin 0.73du off) plus one measured-and-reported non-fix (the whole b1
  stage sits 17du left of AX while the mark pair directly above it is centred on AX exactly — every
  other beat in the short centres its stage, so b1 is the lone exception; not changed because
  centring it moves the panel's ride distance and the brief fenced the choreography). Rule: when a
  defect class is identified, grep the beat for every instance of the class before rendering, and
  report the ones you deliberately did not touch with numbers, so the reviewer decides instead of
  discovering.

- **2026-08-16 DERIVE THE STAGE FROM THE AXIS, NEVER HAND-SET ITS SEATS (mcphidden v5).** The v4
  sweep measured the b1 two-card stage sitting 16.93du (63px at 4K) LEFT of AX — decoded ink
  42.133..500.000, centre 271.067, frame margins 42.1/76.0 — while the Claude/ChatGPT mark pair
  directly above it measured 225.067..350.933, centre 288.000, dead on axis. Two elements in the
  same beat disagreeing about where the middle is, which is the loudest version of a Law 15 miss.
  Cause: three hand-set seats (PANEL_X 42 / DRAWER_X 252 / TILE_X 452) that were each individually
  reasonable and collectively off-axis; 42 in particular is the ZX text-zone edge, which reads like
  a deliberate seat and is why three reviews let it pass. The fix is not "move them 17du", it is to
  stop authoring seats at all: declare the parts and the gaps, sum them into STAGE_W, and let
  `PANEL_X = centered(STAGE_W)` place the whole stage — every downstream constant (the solo-ride
  distance, the socket's right edge, both dock-line ends) then derives. After: ink 58.933..517.067,
  centre 288.000, margins 58.933/58.933 on the decoded encode. Two asserts pin it (stage centre ==
  AX, and margins mirrored about AX). Corollary worth its own line: when you move a stage, assert
  the invariants the move could silently break — here the reveal depends on the parked drawer being
  FULLY occluded by the panel at its solo seat, so that containment is now a build-time assert too.

- **2026-08-16 A COMPENSATED MOVE MUST BE PROVEN UNCHANGED, NOT ASSUMED (mcphidden v5).** Centring
  the stage changed PANEL_SOLO_DX 151 -> 134, which is exactly the arithmetic that is supposed to
  leave the panel's Law-19 centred opening where it was. "Supposed to" is not evidence. Proven three

  showed b2/b3/b4/outro BIT-IDENTICAL (mean 0.00000, max 0.0), which is what lets the earlier
  pop-in adjudications carry over verbatim instead of being re-argued.

- **2026-08-16 A NEW GATE-2 MARKER AFTER A GEOMETRY CHANGE IS NOT NOISE — DECODE IT (mcphidden v5).**
  The stage move added a sixth pop-in marker at 16.33s that v4 did not have, purely because moving
  the pixels changed which frames survive the 16x16-gray dedup, so a caption swap became a
  kept-frame boundary. The tempting read is "same 37 states, same everything, must be nothing." The
  correct move is the one the ring escape taught: decode it. 97,959 pixels changed between 16.10 and
  16.33, but only 81 above y=425du and the visual zone above the chip has mean abs diff 0.00153 —
  caption only. The tile it could have implicated was independently cleared by a flat bright-pixel
  count (26,276 from 15.90 through 18.00) with a visible back.out overshoot across its real entrance
  at 15.50 -> 15.60 -> 15.70. Marker counts move when geometry moves; adjudicate every new one from
  pixels, never from the fact that the total state count matched.

## Run 7 (impeccable) — gpttranscribe / KINETIC (2026-08-16, the Opus fleet)

The batch's cleanest raw (368 words, 13 attempts on one stem, 16 discard markers all before
the cut) and the run's first ONE-RENDER build. Genuinely new lessons only.

- [gate1] **Gate 1's CONCENTRIC exemption is blind to two CENTRED TEXTS stacked on the same
  axis, and that is a whole shape of defect, not an edge case.** `check_sample` skips a
  collision when the two atoms' centres are within 20px on BOTH axes and the overlap is
  >=0.70 of the smaller — a rule written for a glyph inside its plate. But every `ctxt()`
  atom in this lane is `left:0; width:576; text-align:center`, so any two of them are
  automatically concentric on x, and the exemption collapses to "are they within 20px
  vertically" — which is LESS than one display line's leading. b6's terracotta
  `WORD FOR WORD` sat bodily on top of the grey `TRANSCRIPT` label (measured overlap ~0.80
  of the smaller atom, centres 9px apart) and the audit reported **0 errors / 0 warnings**.
  The pre-render contact sheet caught it in one look. Rule for every centred-type lane: two
  centred texts within ~20px of each other vertically are INVISIBLE to Gate 1 — their
  spacing is a stills question, always.
- [law13] **When one lockup has to serve two beats, declare the differing middle as a
  FIXED-HEIGHT SLOT and stack once.** THE RESOLVE needs a line of type under the plates in
  b6 and a row of timestamps under them in b7. Stacking each beat independently puts the
  plates at different y's, makes the continuity assertion an approximation, and (this
  build's first cut) produces the collision above as a side effect. Declaring
  `band_h = max(cap_h(band_fs), cap_h(stamp_fs))` and stacking plates/band/label ONCE gives
  both beats an identical plate seat AND an identical label seat, so the b6→b7 cut moves
  nothing at all and BOTH seats are asserted equal rather than one of them. A shared lockup
  is cheaper than a shared assertion.
- [law13] **A transformation reads as one substance only if the two states share a SPAN,
  not merely a centre.** The waveform's bar gap is derived — `(row_w - N*BAR_W)/(N-1)` —
  from the plate row's MEASURED width, so sound and words occupy the same left and right
  edge to the pixel. The collapse then looks like the audio becoming the words in place;
  with a hand-set gap it looks like one object being swapped for another. Same family as
  THE OCEAN's "one body, no seams", stated for a transformation rather than a magnitude.
- [verify] **A near-white probe SATURATES on cream, and the tell is an impossible NUMBER —
  check the probe before you check the render.** The law-3 card-window probe keyed on
  `min channel >= 200` and reported **19.1s of card across three windows** for a card
  authored at 3.62s; two of the three "windows" were cream sections, because cream
  (246,241,234) has min channel 234. Re-keyed on PURE white (`min >= 250` AND channel
  spread `<= 4`) it measures 1.12-1.27M px with the card up and **exactly 0** at nine
  sampled times without it — 3.600s, contiguous. The mythos white-on-cream class again, but
  the transferable part is the heuristic: **a probe whose answer contradicts an authored
  constant by 5x is a broken probe, not a broken render.**
- [verify] **A DIMMED element is no longer its own colour, so a colour probe reads its
  departure as "nothing happened".** The nine film cells dim to opacity 0.26 over #101012 =
  (76,75,73). A cream-keyed probe over the cell band reads a FLAT 34,228 px across the whole
  16.08-16.78 collapse (it is only ever seeing the three cells that stayed bright) — a
  perfect, and perfectly false, "no change". Probing the measured BLEND colour instead shows
  the real 103,008 → 100,418 → 54,664 → 8,900 → 48 ramp. Rule: **when an element's opacity
  is animated, the probe key is the blend at the state being measured, never the element's
  authored colour.**
- [gate2] **A pop-in marker can decompose into a caption swap PLUS a law-19 displacement
  landing one sample apart, and reading either alone mis-attributes it.** The 1.33s marker:
  the caption band had already changed at 1.20 (29,398 px) while the visual zone was still
  bit-identical (0 changed px), and the visual zone then ramped 170,948 → 193,396 → 295,512
  across 1.33-1.55 — the OpenAI mark riding up for the incoming chip over its authored 0.36s.
  Split every marker into (caption band, visual zone) FIRST; the two channels routinely move
  on different frames and the dedup collapses both into one kept state.
- [intake] **A ONE-TOKEN opening key, and the minimality assertion that has to run the other
  way.** Every prior raw needed its key made LONGER until it separated openings from in-take
  utterances (personalapps, mcphidden, mythos). Here the 13 attempts share only `OpenAI`, and
  `OpenAI` never occurs inside a take body — so minimality is vacuous and the risk inverts.
  The assertion this raw needs is that the natural extension `OpenAI just helped` covers only
  **8 of 13** openings (missing words 3, 7, 10, 122, 123), so a future edit cannot quietly
  lengthen the key and silently drop five attempts. **Assert against the failure mode the raw
  actually has, not against the one the last raw had.**
- [intake] **A spoken "No." separated from its own attempt by a long pause makes the gap rule
  disagree by exactly ONE opening — a tenth raw shape, and both halves of the disagreement
  are assertable.** Word 8 `just...` → 1.57s of silence → word 9 `No.` → 0.03s → word 10
  `OpenAI`. The marker got orphaned from the attempt it kills, so the gap rule opens on the
  MARKER and the phrase rule on the ATTEMPT. The decisive last element is identical (word
  207), so the rule earns a standing no previous raw produced: **EQUALITY on the boundary,
  one documented disagreement elsewhere.** Assert the boundary AND both set differences
  ({9} extra, {10} missing) — the disagreement is data, and pinning it is what stops a
  re-transcription from silently changing the shape.
- [law6] **The punctuated-repeat protection deserves a COUNT assertion, not just a live code
  path.** `very, very, very good` survives the unigram stutter rule only because the first
  two carry commas (personalapps' discriminator). Asserting `kept_punctuated_repeats == 2`
  turns a silent dependency into a build-time fact: a re-transcription that drops one comma
  now kills the build instead of shipping "very good". Same shape as asserting a declared
  respell fires — protections that only ever run silently should be counted.
- [render] **Three composition defects, ONE render.** All three (the concentric overlap, an
  outro miniature too small to read on a phone, a timeline whose 14 word-blocks read as one
  bar at a 4du gap) died on pre-render contact sheets; the whole-video ink sweep then cleared
  the encode-to-be (0 of 468 samples under 1%) before the render was launched. The sequence
  that produced it, and the one to keep: build → Gate 1 → 48 stills → fix → repeat → ink
  sweep → render.
- [gpttranscribe_kinetic] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1403 frames, 46.805s
  container / 46.74 authored, 46 captions, 9 sections, 188 ids, 104 tween targets, 0
  untweened children, 18 `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0
  arrowheads; take detection on a 13-opening ONE-family raw (16 discard markers = 5

  frame) on a mouth window re-derived and extraction-verified for this framing, 0.000s

## Run 7 (impeccable) — cursordeal / COUNTER (2026-08-16, the batch's shortest raw)

84.0s of raw, 148 words, three attempts at one opening and NOT ONE discard marker.
The intake was over in minutes and then the raw handed over the build's single most
expensive finding. Genuinely new lessons only.

- [intake] **The SUSTAIN head rule inverts when a take opens on a short function word,
  and the ledger's other half is the fix: silence DURATION.** oneprompt's rule (the
  onset is the first 10ms window that HOLDS above the floor for 0.15s) exists so a
  transient LOUDER than speech cannot open the cut early. Here it failed the other way:
  the take opens on "A company", and "A" is an 80ms voiced schwa followed immediately by
  the STOP CLOSURE of company's /k/ (40ms of near-silence). Nothing holds 0.15s until the
  second syllable, so sustain returned 42.179 and HEAD_LEAD put the cut head at 42.079 —
  40ms INSIDE the first word, which would have shipped a chopped attack on frame 0.
  Adjudicated acoustically before trusting the head: the "transient" measured RMS 0.1984 /
  ZCR 0.117, the same voiced signature as the "com" of "company" (0.2627 / 0.0996) and
  nothing like the room-tone controls (ZCR 0.14-0.33 at negligible amplitude) — it is
  SPEECH. The rule that survives: **the onset is the END of the last >= 0.30s run of
  sub-threshold windows** (silence measured by duration, exactly as the ledger says), with
  the sustain onset demoted to a cross-check that the run ended on speech rather than on a
  door slam — speech may lead the sustain onset by at most ~0.35s (here 0.14s). Then
  assert the head sits INSIDE that measured run. After: 0.10s of measured silence, then
  the whole word.
- [intake] **A raw can leave BOTH auxiliary rules non-standard in opposite directions,
  and that is the strongest state to be in.** Zero discard markers of any kind (both
  abandoned attempts end CLEANLY PUNCTUATED and just stop — billionusers' eighth shape
  occurring at EVERY boundary, and mcphidden's zero-marker case, second sighting), so the
  marker rule is INAPPLICABLE, asserted as exactly zero. Meanwhile exactly two inter-word
  gaps >= 1.0s exist in the whole raw (3.58s, 4.00s) and both sit at attempt boundaries,
  so the gap rule earns a full EQUALITY with the content rule. One rule that cannot speak
  and one that agrees exactly is a better epistemic position than two soft bounds — and
  both standings are written down as assertions, so a re-transcription that changes the
  shape fails loudly instead of silently re-deciding the take.
- [law13] **A crush is a meter run backwards, and the space it leaves is the only gauge
  you need.** THE COLLAPSE: one solid column (the $1.5M contract) standing on a ground
  rule is compressed about its own base to exactly 250/1500 of its height — 0.50s on
  power3.in, a 7% overshoot, a 0.16s settle, a boom under the moment — and the rect it
  vacated is then revealed as a three-sided dashed silhouette and MEASURED by a vertical
  dimension read whose word is his own: LEVERAGE. THE OCEAN's principle transposed to a
  price: one substance, two magnitudes visible at once (what it was, what it is), no
  paired gauges, nothing to misalign because the ghost, the ticks, the rule segments and
  the stub all derive from the same four constants. The transferable move is the
  measurement: a reduction becomes an argument the moment you put a dimension read on the
  emptiness instead of a second bar next to it.
- [craft] **Two adjacent clipped halves cannot impersonate one solid object.** The
  cracking slab is authored as two complementary clip-path polygons so it can part along
  a jagged seam — but before the crack they anti-alias against each other and paint a
  faint light zigzag down an UNCRACKED stone (invisible on thumbnails, obvious on the
  first full-resolution crop). Two fixes, both needed: the halves overlap by 0.7du across
  the seam so the AA gap cannot exist, and the intact slab is a THIRD element (one plain
  div) with the halves invisible until the crack, swapped in on a frame where they
  reproduce the solid exactly (mcphidden's instant-set-while-identical move). An object
  that must break later still has to be ONE object until it does.
- [law14] **Per-line highlight rings cannot be PADDED — line boxes are adjacent by
  construction.** billionusers' card rings padded each `getClientRects()` line box by 8du;
  on a two-line claim that means the rings overlap by twice the padding and cross at their
  corners, which is what the first 4K encode shipped. Rings are annotations, so the
  MOCK-UI rule applies to them too: size them off RENDERED INK. Measuring the glyph ink
  inside each line's own column and padding THAT gives rings that hug the words with a
  real gap (6.0 CSS px here), asserted at render time so a font or wrap change fails the
  build instead of shipping a crossed pair.
- [law15] **The centred-mono correction is per-STRING, not per-system.** `text-align:center`
  really does count the trailing letter-space it never paints (mcphidden), and a
  `text-indent` of one tracking unit corrects it — measured, that moved four labels from
  ~1.3du left to under 0.25du. But glyph side bearings can exceed that term and flip its
  sign: the hero odometer (negative display tracking, "8" and "%" bearings) measured
  **2.03du RIGHT** of the axis and needed a measured -4.05du indent, while a label on a
  filled segment needed only a quarter of the standard correction. Fifteen centred atoms
  were measured on decoded pixels; two needed per-atom numbers. Do not derive this from
  the em arithmetic — measure each centred atom the way the reviewer will look at it.
- [ink] **An ink floor is not a composition floor.** The pre-render sweep found the b1
  beat holding 1.42% ink for 0.3s after the source card retired — above the 1% rule and
  still an empty whiteboard, because a kicker plus the top half of the caption pill is
  most of that number. The card now retires INTO the dashed slot it came from, so the
  beat closes on the composition it opened with. Corollary for the sweep: read the low
  frames, do not just check the threshold.
- [gate2] **The metric-per-ground class, third sighting, and the fix is the mean.** The
  200-glyph field's dim reads as a hard step to a dark-pixel counter (441107 -> 54198
  across two frames) purely because the opacity tween crosses the counter's threshold;
  the MEAN luminance of the same rows ramps 175.7 -> 179.2 -> 194.1 -> 212.5 -> 217.3 ->
  220.5 -> 223.2 and shows the tween. When a pop-in marker sits on an OPACITY event,
  adjudicate it with a mean, never with a thresholded count.
- [cursordeal_counter] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1196 frames, 39.872s
  container / 39.859 authored, 37 captions, 7 sections, 99 ids, 44 tween targets, 7
  overlap-ok, 0 pathLength, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 arrowheads; take detection on a
  three-attempt raw with ZERO markers (marker rule INAPPLICABLE and asserted, gap rule an
  EQUALITY, opening key asserted three tokens because "a company" fires inside the winner,
  sign-off asserted a bigram because "next" fires twice), head by the new silence-run rule
  (onset 42.039, sustain 42.179, head 41.939 inside a measured 0.57s run), tail by the
  trailing-silence rule; the cut kept all 130 spoken words and the raw-take-vs-tight diff
  is three PUNCTUATION-only tokens; ZERO keyterms added (nothing is named in the take —
  "Cursor" is spoken once, inside the abandoned second attempt) and therefore ZERO brand
  marks drawn, guard-enforced; Gate 1 **0 errors / 1 by-design warning across 4 rounds**
  (the one first-round error was the ghost silhouette's wrapper reaching into the crushed
  stub); 81 pre-render states with per-state ink + 15 full-resolution crops + 16 centring
  measurements before any 4K spend; Gate 2 **47 distinct states from 120 samples**, 73
  collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 1 stillness marker and all 7 pop-in markers resolved on
  exact decodes, every annotation verified from INSIDE its own active window; idle scan
  frames=159 idle_drift=no long_static=no; encode sweep **0 of 1196 frames under 1% ink,
  0 blank**, min 1.13%, median 9.42%, min max-channel deviation 112; caption band
  pill-free on exactly 3 frames, all before the MEASURED voice onset at 0.100s (the first
  pill opens on that onset rather than on Scribe's 0.219); REAL tweet **3.4s measured from
  pixels**, contiguous, badge payload-true, zero metrics, card at 0.9075x; the crush
  measured 0.1632 against an authored 250/1500 = 0.1667; sync **lag 0 on both streams**
  (audio r=0.9814 at 1ms, video r=0.9996 at 1 frame) on a mouth window re-verified by eye
  for this framing, 0.000s cut-master delta, NO remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call,
  0 visual / 0 semantic / 0 minor**, Gemini calls: exactly 1; **2 renders**, the second
  bought by the card's overlapping rings and by nothing else; independent Fable 5 clerk

## Run 7 — doers / DIAGRAM (2026-08-16, batch 2, Opus builder)

The org chart that flips, and the field that stops being countable. Genuinely new
lessons only; everything else ran on the harness rails and simply held.

- [intake] **A TENTH raw shape: two script families that ALTERNATE, with the winner in
  the MINORITY one — so the key must be CONTRACTED, not extended.** Family A ("AI is
  getting rid of managers", w0/8/21/175/201) and family B ("AI is firing managers",
  w70/74/207) interleave as **A A A B B A A B**, and the only complete take is the last
  B. mythos' fix for a two-family raw was to EXTEND the key until it fired in one family
  only; here that is exactly backwards — A's key misses the winner entirely and B's key
  hides five real attempts, which would make both cross-rules meaningless. The key is the
  two-token stem `ai is` that BOTH families share: it fires exactly 8 times, and it is
  asserted MINIMAL because the one-token `ai` fires 16. General form: **when the eras
  alternate, key on the intersection; when the eras are sequential, extend past it.**
  Both family counts are asserted so a re-transcription cannot silently merge them.

- [intake] **The marker rule can be an EQUALITY, and this is the first raw that earns it.**
  The winner opens 0.400s after a spoken "No." — so `last_marker(206) + 1 == first(207)`,
  asserted as an equality rather than the usual lower bound. The same 0.400s is what
  demotes the GAP rule to a bound that UNDER-SHOOTS ONTO A DISCARD (the harness class,
  second sighting): at >=1.5s its last opening is w201, the five-word abandoned attempt
  "AI is getting rid of... No." that the marker rule exists to kill. Three rules, three
  different standings, on one raw — and the standings are opposite to what the same three
  rules earned on harness. **Standing is per-raw, always, in writing.**

- [intake] **The cleanest demonstration yet that a head is chosen by SUSTAIN and never by
  level.** On the script's own 10ms envelope the lip transient at 111.500 reads 0.03941 —
  1.82x the run's measured threshold (0.02161) and **1.87x the 0.02111 of the take's own
  onset RAMP window** at 111.860, which sits just BELOW that same threshold. A pure level
  rule therefore fires on the SMACK and not on the speech. The edl now records
  `level_rule_would_fire_on_the_transient: true` as a probed field rather than a claim,
  alongside `last_transient_windows_above_threshold: 1` against
  `sustain_windows_required: 15`. Scribe's word start was 111.870, dead on the measured
  onset — 0ms late, the tightest of the batch.

- [law13] **When a story counts, make the COUNT the visualization and hold the band still.**
  The fan under the flipped chart densifies on the numerals he speaks — 5 -> 10 -> 20 ->
  200 — with the tiles narrowing from 44du to 1.5du inside a band whose top and bottom
  NEVER move. Law 15's rule for swapping elements of different sizes ("normalise sizes so
  height and centering stay consistent") is what makes the swap read as density instead of
  as a composition move, and it is enforced by construction: `field_geometry` solves each
  state's x0 from its parts so every density is centred on AX, and every state shares the
  240..306 ink band. At 200 the stub and the tile ARE the same mark — at 1.5du they cannot
  be told apart — so the agent becomes one rect spanning rail->tick; the ink band is
  unchanged, which is the point. The payoff is that "hundreds" is the one number you
  cannot draw as individuals, and the picture says so.

- [verify] **A bespoke count must be COUNTED on decoded frames, not asserted from the
  source.** `col_runs` over the tick band returned 5 / 10 / 20 / 200 / 200 / 8 at the six
  moments that matter. The one place it first disagreed with itself was the terracotta
  census (193 instead of 200): at 5.6 physical px with 3px gaps the loose `r-b>40` mask
  bleeds neighbours together. The INK census on the identical geometry is the control, and
  a stricter mask (`r-b>80 & r>130`) restored 200. **A census that changes with its
  threshold is a statement about the mask; find the threshold with a margin on both
  populations, then report the number.**

- [law13][ink] **Overlap the dissolve with the arrival, or the canvas empties.** The peak
  beat kills a top node, two trees and a three-plate row while ONE 88du plate climbs
  through the vacated layer. Sequenced, that leaves ~1.1s of a single white plate on cream
  — 0.9% ink on the encode's own metric, i.e. metrically blank. Staggering the row's exit
  ACROSS the climb (m1 at 14.10, m0 at 14.40, m2 at 14.62 while the plate rides 14.45 ->
  15.30) and retiring the company cage LAST, 0.26s before the tiles land, keeps ink
  continuous — and it tells the story better, because the builder is seen passing through
  the layer as it clears. Measured: 0 of 1248 frames under 1%, min 1.852%.

- [gate1][ink] **A pre-render sweep that measures BOXES cannot see the defect the encode
  measures in PIXELS — so measure pixels before rendering.** The sibling contact-sheet
  script scores painted bounding-box area; billionusers already proved a naked track has
  plenty of area and no ink. This build added a second sweep that screenshots the paused
  1080 timeline every 0.2s and scores it with the ENCODE's own metric (fraction of the top
  zone deviating >=34/255 from the frame's modal grey). It reported min 1.825% and ZERO
  samples under 1% before a single frame was encoded, and the shipped sweep agreed
  (1.852%). It also priced the hook: a 64du white plate on cream measures ~0.8%, which is
  why the opening manager stands at 144du.

- [gsap] **`grow()` with a hard-coded `{scale:1}` FROM value is the harness clobber class
  one level down.** On a SCALE-PARKED atom the tween's first frame snaps the element to its
  authored size and then shrinks it — an 88du pop where a 64du lean-in was authored. Gate 1
  is 0/0 on it (the box is legal at both ends), the 3fps thumbnails read the wrong size as
  a legitimate state, and only the pre-render contact sheet showed it. The fix is a
  parameter with a reason (`grow(..., frm=PARK_SCALE)`), not a re-timing.

- [gsap] **`fade()`'s implicit frame-0 `set` blanks any atom that starts VISIBLE.** Two
  `tl.set(..., 0)` calls on the same element resolve in insertion order, so a `fade()`
  added later than an explicit `set(opacity:1, 0)` wins and the element is invisible for
  the whole first half of its beat. The b2 label lost 2.4s to this and, because its park
  was also never released, it came back at the OLD seat under the vacated builder. The fix
  is a primitive — `refade()`, a fromTo with no frame-0 set — plus a `set(y:0)` fired while
  the label is provably invisible. **An instant re-seat under cover costs no tween budget
  and is the honest way to move a thing between two beats' seats.**

- [law15] **Park only what RIDES — a phase-only atom parked like a travelling one moves the
  whole opening composition.** b4's meter was authored at its phase-1 seat and then parked
  by the same dy as the plate and label that ride up later, putting it 40du low and taking
  the beat's opening union to centre 259.8 (47.8du off the band centre). Gate 1 could not
  see it (each atom's own box is legal), the geometry selftest could not see it (it checks
  AUTHORED seats), the stills sheet showed a composition that merely looked a little low —
  what found it was a causality probe reading **ZERO** because the element was not where
  the generator said it was. The guard is a **parked-seat table**: every parked atom
  declares `(authored_y, dy, expected_rendered_y)` and the build dies if they disagree.
  **A probe that reads zero is evidence about the geometry, not just about the moment.**

- [timing] **Express a stagger as a TOTAL SPREAD, never as a per-element `each`.** The same
  `each: 0.02` that reads as a ripple across 5 tiles runs 0.38s across 20 and was still
  arriving when the next numeral was spoken. `field_state` now takes a spread, derives
  `each = spread/(n-1)`, and RETURNS its own end time so the build can assert every density
  finishes before the next cue (5 by 16.30 vs 16.60; 10 by 17.16 vs 17.72; 20 by 18.28 vs
  18.38; 200 by 18.76 vs 19.14). The same arithmetic fixed the terminal-hold guard, which
  had been fed `each * n` where GSAP's `from:"center"` actually spans `each * (n-1)/2`.

- [gate2] **A 3.0s "stillness" marker over a beat that visibly completes is the thin-mark
  blind spot, and the decode says so in one line.** The 11.33 -> 14.33 gap contains the
  delegation tree drawing to completion: terra px inside the tree's own box 176 -> 5,767 ->
  13,241 across 11.40/11.70/12.00. Its strokes are 2.6-3du (10px at 4K), which a 16x16 grey
  signature cannot see — the perplexity class. The OTHER stillness marker (37.33 -> 41.00)
  is real and legal: the outro holds and "daily AI" fades on its cue. **Two identical
  markers, opposite verdicts, both settled on pixels.** The harness thumbnail-clock class
  also reappeared: the f_0018_333 JPG shows the flooded 200-state although the DECODED
  18.30 frame counts exactly 20.

- [law3] **A market claim needs a source, and that is what separates this ruling from
  harness'.** harness rejected its handed post because the take was a pure thesis citing
  nobody. This take OPENS on "AI is firing managers" — a report about the hiring market —
  and @swyx's post is the market report the Notion idea was captured from, matching all
  three load-bearing assertions (bear market for "heads of X" managers / bull market for
  AI-native ICs / "1 year experience managing 10 agents > 10 years experience managing
  10-100 people"). Shipped for 2.867s measured from pixels, ringed on the bull-market line
  under "the type of builder people are actually looking for". Also: appsdistrib's
  printed-once rule generalises — "swyx" and "swyx" differ by exactly the '@' glyph, so the
  card prints `@swyx` once and the renderer asserts `name.lstrip('@').lower() == username`.

- [law15] **Report the centring you deliberately did NOT fix, with numbers.** While b0's
  manager row and its empty seat stand alone (2.22 -> 5.42) their union is 156..340, centre
  248 — 36du below the band centre. Centring the pair needs seats at 120..304, which leaves
  no room for the 46du key term that lands at 60..122.6 on "builder." and takes the beat's
  final union to centre 200. LAW 9 and the chart's continuity with b1 both win; the
  alternative is either no key term or a b0 layout that jump-cuts into b1. Written into the
  generator beside the cue, into the plan, and into the paperwork — the mcphidden rule that
  a reviewer should DECIDE rather than DISCOVER.

- [doers_diagram] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1248 frames, 41.600s container /
  41.589 authored, 40 captions, 8 sections, 107 ids (48 section-prefixed), 49 tween
  targets, 0 untweened children, 17 `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 139 `pathLength=100`
  paths, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 arrowheads, 0 svg scale tweens, 0 caption echoes, 0
  caption identities over 11 typeset atoms carrying 6 distinct strings, 0 tokens dropped by

## Run 7 (impeccable) — mathconjecture / KINETIC (2026-08-16, Opus 5 builder)

A 136s raw whose opening was REWRITTEN rather than drifted, and the lane's first
rigid-body scene. Genuinely new lessons only.

- [intake] **A TENTH raw shape: the opening is not drifted, it is REWRITTEN — three
  script families that share no head phrase at all, only a TAIL.** Every intersection
  key the factory has used so far (`over the wrong thing`, `one simple`, `using only`)
  lives at the HEAD of the attempt, because the attempts were the same sentence said
  badly. Here A is "AI just SOLVED yet AGAIN another impossible math problem", B is "AI
  NOW MANAGED TO SOLVE another near impossible math problem", C is "AI just MANAGED TO
  SOLVE yet another ALMOST impossible math problem": the verbs, the adverbs and the
  qualifier all change, and the only 2 tokens all three share are the last ones before
  the noun — `impossible math`. Keying on the TAIL still works and is still exact (7
  hits, every one inside an opening line, zero inside a body), because the walk-back
  finds each attempt's own first word from wherever the key sits. The portable rule:
  the intersection key does not have to be at the head of the line, it has to be
  UNIQUE to opening lines — check the tail before concluding a raw has no key.
- [intake] **The gap rule can be strictly WEAKER than the content rule and still earn
  its equality, and saying so in writing is the point.** On this raw >=2.0s sees only 2
  of the 7 openings (families C2/C3/C4 restart after 1.40-1.96s pauses) and 2 of its 4
  hits are pre-roll FRAGMENT starts, not openings at all. It still answers word 188.
  Assert all three facts — the equality, the openings it MISSES, and the hits that are
  not openings — so a re-transcription that changes the shape cannot quietly promote a
  rule that was never carrying the weight.
- [transcript] **A raw-vs-tight token diff can be NET ZERO and still contain the
  build's most important finding.** 157 words in, 157 words out, but four tokens differ:
  the raw heard `5.6o,` as one token where the cut hears `5.6` + `So,`, and the raw's
  `we will` became `we'll`. The two changes cancel in the count. The `So,` is a 0.140s
  abandoned discourse start bracketed by 0.12s and 0.18s of silence with the clause
  restarting on "which" — and the fact that the RAW pass annexed the same audio into a
  NUMBER rather than hearing a word is independent evidence it is vestigial. Diff
  tokens, never word counts; a balanced diff hides exactly the thing worth finding.
- [law14][law11] **A source crop can be ruled by FACTUAL PLACEMENT, not just
  legibility.** The real post's second paragraph names Feige's 1/e conjecture (posed
  2006). The short's peak beat is "conjectures that have been standing for over 50
  years" — a claim Miguel makes about the CLASS. Printing the name would have put a
  20-year-old problem on screen next to a 50-year claim and manufactured an adjacency
  he never made. Law 8 (symbolic notation, unreadable at short size) disposes of the
  same paragraph independently, which is what makes the ruling safe: TWO reasons, either
  sufficient, and the renderer asserts the dropped remainder still contains "Feige" so a
  payload change forces a re-judge instead of silently widening the crop.
- [law13] **A ground rule drawn the length of BOTH footprints removes the horizontal
  problem from a rotation entirely.** A tower that tips 90 degrees about its foot ends
  ~half its own height off-axis, and chasing that with a step reads as the camera
  sliding. Draw the ground as `TOWER_W + TOWER_H` and the scene's x-extent is the same
  standing and fallen, so no state needs an offset — and the empty half is not dead
  space, it is the distance the fall will cross. Then CLOSE the ground onto the fallen
  body (scaleX about its right edge) while body and ground ride back onto the axis and
  the labels stay put: the fallen bar and its label end concentric, and the ground it no
  longer needs is not a slot left empty (LAW 16) but a distance already travelled.
  Measured on the encode: 304.5 design units of rule standing, 218.7 fallen.
- [law13][law1] **The containment of a rotation is provable at build time, and the
  proof is three lines.** Every point of the tower is (dx, dy) with dx in [-W, 0] and dy
  in [-H, 0] relative to a bottom-right pivot; under rotate(th) for th in [0, 90] the
  y-part `dx sin th + dy cos th` is <= 0 everywhere (both terms are a non-positive
  number times a non-negative sine/cosine) so nothing ever sinks below the ground, and
  the x-part lies in [-W, H] — exactly the ground rule's own span. Write the algebra in
  the docstring and the beat has zero frame-margin exposure without a single probe.
- [ink] **Ghosting is a centring trick with an INK floor, and 0.11 is under it.** The
  50-stratum tower is authored complete and ghosted so the "years accumulating" rise
  never changes the ink box — the mathvoice draw-every-slot rule, opacity edition, and
  it makes the beat centred by construction. But at 0.11 opacity, cream-on-dark blends
  to a modal deviation of ~16/255 and the beat's opening measured 0.5-1.0% top-zone ink
  for 17 frames: the stolenapp under-1% class, invisible to Gate 1 and to Gate 2's
  dedup. 0.28 puts the blended stratum at ~44 deviation and the opening at 3.66%.
  A ghost has to be a DIM THING, not an absent one.
- [ink] **The whole-timeline ink sweep belongs BEFORE the render, not only after it.**
  Driving the 1080 project's own timeline at 0.20s steps with the encode sweep's exact
  method (modal background, >34/255 deviation) costs ~3 minutes of headless Chromium and
  found the second under-1% window (a lone person glyph opening b4 at 0.70%) that would
  otherwise have cost a third 4K render. Same instrument, same numbers, no encode.
- [gate3] **`no_added_value` is answered by DELETING a beat as readily as by adding a
  picture.** Gemini named two text-only sections back to back for 7.2s. The temptation
  is to decorate the weaker one; the fix was to notice that the picture already existed
  one section earlier — an empty dashed seat with a terracotta `?` in it IS "maybe, we
  don't really know" — and hand it the sentence. One section deleted, one mono line
  added, the type beat that remains is 2.5s and the judge passed clean. The oneprompt
  rule generalises: the response to `no_added_value` is a picture, and the cheapest
  picture is one the short has already earned.
- [verify] **A generator that DUMPS its own geometry closes the typed-not-probed class
  structurally.** The hermessteps finding (a verifier that retypes design constants is
  a claim nobody checked) has been fixed per-number in every build since. Writing
  `gen/_geom_<name>.json` at build time — every recorded box, every park/step state —
  and having the encode verifier read its probe bands from that file removes the failure
  mode instead of policing it. It also caught its own class of bug immediately: with the
  states in the file, a probe that read the FINAL band at a PARKED time (b3's week
  cells, 0 of an expected 6) was obviously wrong rather than mysteriously wrong.
- [verify] **A probe band must carry its state's dy in TIME as well as in space.** The
  grokimagine wrong-place class has a temporal twin: b3's parked probe at t=8.20 was
  measuring a band the strip had already begun leaving (the step releases at 8.079).
  Moving the probe to 8.00 turned 0 into 6. Every parked probe needs a timestamp that
  precedes `cue - STEP_LEAD`, not merely the cue.
- [law4] **A product name under its own brand mark is a caption echo by the letter of
  the trigram rule, and the honest fix is a DECLARED exemption channel.** `GPT-5.6`
  normalises to "gpt 5 6", which is exactly what he says. Dropping it leaves a bare
  blossom naming a company when the sentence names a model (law 2 wants the mark, law 14
  wants the payload's spelling). The oneprompt discipline applies: add a
  `data-proper-noun` channel, declare `PROPER_NOUNS`, and assert the rendered set equals
  the declared set — the guard is extended and checkable, never widened.
- [law4] **Design around the caption-identity guard instead of exempting it.** The
  measure label wanted to read `50 YEARS`, and the pill at 22.12 is exactly "50 years." —
  token-identical, a guaranteed failure. Authoring it as TWO one-token atoms (`50` big in
  terracotta, `YEARS` in mono beneath) is both guard-clean and a better lockup than the
  string would have been. The appsdistrib rule (change the atom, never weaken the guard)
  is cheapest when applied at design time rather than after the guard fires.
- [mathconjecture_kinetic] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1433 frames, 47.787s
  container / 47.76 authored, 44 captions, 12 sections, 223 ids, 142 tween selectors;
  take detection on a 7-opening raw across THREE rewritten script families keyed on the
  2-token TAIL intersection 'impossible math' (7 hits, nowhere else), sign-off 'catch you
  in the next' (1 hit; both sibling keys asserted at 0 and 1), gap rule earning an
  EQUALITY while missing 5 of 7 openings (asserted), marker rule a lower bound (7
  truncations, 0 spoken "No.", 2.72s clear), zero in-take markers; head measured by
  SUSTAIN (onset 84.950, Scribe 10ms late, 2.82s of silence, ZERO transients); the cut
  kept all 157 spoken words (diffed token-for-token, four orthographic differences that
  cancel); Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings across 5 rounds** on the 1080 design copy (0
  duplicate ids, 0 untweened section children, 5 `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 0
  `non-scaling-stroke`, 0 caption-echo trigrams, 0 caption-identity collisions, 2
  declared law-4 exemption classes both asserted set-equal); the bespoke FIFTY-YEAR
  TOWER verified by COUNT on exact decodes (**50 stratum runs standing at 21.90, 50
  runs across the fallen bar at 24.60**), its gauge 36087 terra px measuring -> 0 once
  cleared, its ground 304.5 -> 218.7 design units as it closed onto the body, `SOLVED`
  0 -> 2885; the reprise verified as arrival THEN fall (cell luminance [167,199,199,199]
  -> four lit one per beat -> heights [86,86,86,86] -> [33,86,86,86] -> [33,33,33,33]);
  Gate 2 **57 distinct states from 143 samples**, 86 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 0
  stillness markers, 7 pop-in markers all adjudicated on decoded ramps (five entrance
  overshoots, two section cuts), all 57 states read plus four native-4K crops and a
  frame-by-frame decode of the b9 swap; `idle_motion_scan` frames=191 idle_drift=no
  long_static=no; encode sweep **0 of 1433 frames under 1% top-zone ink, 0 blank**, min
  1.185%, median 6.411%; caption band pill-free on 4 frames, all before the first word at
  0.119s; the REAL tweet **3.800s measured from pixels**, contiguous, at 0.65x, zero
  metrics, no badge, one ring verified on a decode from its ACTIVE window; ONE brand mark
  (OpenAI, bare, 0.52x); sync at **lag 0 on both streams** (audio r=0.9634 at 1ms, video
  r=0.9991 at 1 frame) with a 0.000s cut-master delta and NO remux; Gate 3 **pass, 0
  visual, 0 semantic, 0 minor** on call 2 (call 1 named a real `no_added_value` defect);
  3 renders, both extra ones bought by ink and by Gate 3, never by geometry.

## Run 7 (impeccable) — chatgptphone / ICON (2026-08-16, Opus 5 builder)

The batch's most-restarted raw after billionusers (300.2s, 690 words, 27 attempt
openings across two wording eras) and the first build to carry TWO recurring
objects instead of a cast. Genuinely new lessons only.

- [ink][tooling] **A pre-render ink sweep that does not crop the encode scan's BAND and
  report the encode scan's THRESHOLD is not a detector — it is a different instrument
  that agrees with nothing.** This build wrote one (the mcphidden prescription: buy the
  blank-canvas finding before the render, not after), ran 468 samples, and reported
  "0 under 1%, min 1.512%" on a project whose encode then measured **3 FULLY BLANK
  frames** and two under-1% runs. Two independent errors, either of which alone hides
  the defect: (1) it clipped 460du of "top zone", but the caption pill is authored at
  `top:460du` with `translateY(-50%)`, so the clip contained the pill's upper half and
  EVERY frame measured ~3% ink that was the caption — nothing can ever read blank;
  (2) it used the strict 34 threshold (the agentreviews artifact), which cannot see a
  WHITE PLATE on cream (deviation 15), so a beat whose whole content is a white card
  reads as empty. The encode scan crops 1580 of 3840 (=421du) and thresholds at 13 for
  exactly these reasons. Fixed sweep: same band, and BOTH thresholds reported — 13 as
  the claim-bearing metric, 34 as a strict companion. It then found the real windows
  immediately and the shipped encode measures 0 under 1% / 0 blank.
- [law11] **A glyph that collides with another glyph in the same composition is a
  FACTUAL error, not a style choice.** `g_deck` was drawn as "a slide on a stand" —
  which is a MONITOR, the exact object this short's computer already owned — so the
  middle capability read as "the desktop" under a label saying PRESENTATIONS. Gate 1
  measures boxes, Gate 2 reads 512px thumbnails, and neither can see that two glyphs
  mean the same thing; a full-resolution still can. Redrawn as a stack of slides
  (nothing in the system stacks screens). Rule for the next builder: before drawing a
  glyph, inventory the short's OWN objects and check the silhouette against them.
- [law19] **Law 19 has a VERTICAL axis, and a beat whose first cast is a top-band row is
  the same defect in a different costume.** b1 and b4 both opened with a lone mark
  seated at y=48 in an otherwise empty zone — horizontally dead on AX, vertically parked
  in anticipation of a lower stage that would not arrive for 1.8s / 5.0s. The fix is
  `stepy()`, the twin of appsdistrib's `stepx`: park the row DOWN so it opens optically
  centred in the empty zone, then ride it UP as the lower stage arrives. Measured on the
  encode: the solo tile's green ink spans 250.13..325.87du, centre **288.00**, at the
  parked seat. A beat can be off-centre on the axis nobody is checking.
- [ink] **A handoff is ONE cue, not two.** Cueing an exiting atom and its replacement
  separately left 0.25s of near-empty canvas between them (0.206% ink measured at
  16.75). Cueing the envelope's lift-off and the first capability's arrival at the SAME
  instant removed the dip AND turned two events into one move: the mail lifts as the
  document lands under it. The crossing that looked like a collision risk on paper reads
  as a handoff on the still.
- [gate1][guards] **The geometry audit exempts `data-overlap-ok` atoms from collisions —
  which makes a connector drawn straight through a LABEL structurally invisible to it.**
  Render 3 shipped three b4 stems running through their own product names ("CLAUDE CODE"
  with a rule through the E). Gate 1: 0/0. Gate 2's 512px thumbnails: unreadable at that
  size. Only a native-4K crop showed it. The durable fix is a generator-side guard —
  intersect every `data-overlap-ok` box against every text atom's box, per section, and
  refuse to build — **proven to fire by rebuilding the old geometry with it enabled**
  (`connector b4-feed crosses the type of b4-lgp`). Layout consequence: in the one beat
  where connectors LEAVE marks downward, the labels go ABOVE the marks. A label under a
  mark is exactly where the stem has to run.
- [transition] **A lit state carried across a section cut and re-authored neutral changes
  in ONE frame, and that reads as a flicker, not as an event.** b2 ends with the three
  work plates hot terracotta; b3 re-authored the same plates with the neutral border, so
  at the 22.48 cut they measured 25,010 -> 16,411 ink px — the whole delta being the
  terra border switching off between two frames. Fix: author b3's plates HOT (pixel-
  continuous with b2's last frame) and add `cool()`, the deliberate opposite of `hot()`,
  firing as the desk closes around them. Verified as a real ramp on decodes: the border
  strip reads (222,174,158) -> (212,198,191) -> (232,231,227) -> (237,237,232) across
  23.28-23.52. Corollary: **whatever a beat ends lit, the next beat must open lit.**
- [law13] **A collapse works when the frame it collapses INTO was already the frame it
  collapsed OUT of.** THE DESK COLLAPSE: the three objects Miguel names (reports /
  presentations / CRM) enter in b2 on a conveyor, the DESKTOP closes AROUND them in b3
  (its border going hot on "the only place where you could get stuff done"), and on
  "Well, no longer." the desk shrinks to 34% and fades while the phone rises from its
  centre and the three objects converge out of a 324du-wide row into an 86du-wide
  column, 88 -> 40du, into three dashed slots that go solid as they land. Nothing new
  enters at the payoff. Two authoring rules made it cheap: the objects are SIBLINGS of
  the desk (a child would inherit the desk's shrink), and each travels with a single
  `to` carrying x+y+scale from its AUTHORED rect — never a park at a scale, so the
  harness scale-clobber class cannot fire. Encode-verified by count: desk-only regions
  10,166 -> 0 ink px, work row outside the phone column 39,194 -> 0, all three phone rows
  9,998-10,283 terra border px and 13,111-13,522 glyph px.
- [law15] **A conveyor's park offsets are derivable, so make the layout function return
  them and assert every partial state.** `row_seats(n, w, gap)` returns the n seats AND
  the n park offsets `(n-k)*(w+gap)/2`, and refuses to build unless every cast of
  1..n measures centred on AX. Encode-verified on the shipped file: the row's ink span
  midpoint reads 288.93 / 291.73 / 290.40du for the one-, two- and three-object states
  (tolerance 4du, the residual being each glyph's own asymmetry inside its plate).
- [verify] **Three probe errors in one verifier, all one class: a probe box that
  something ELSE can occupy.** (a) the "desk stand" band sat inside the phone's
  footprint, so the phone's own border reported the desk as still present; (b) the
  phone-row boxes are phone-SHAPED, not phone-EXCLUSIVE — the middle work object stands
  in the same column, so the "before" terra count was the desk scene; (c) a
  deviation-from-cream counter on a DARK section returned the identical number before
  and after the event (the harness metric-per-ground class, now on its fourth sighting,
  committed by a builder who had just read the rule). One sentence covers all three: a
  probe box must be exclusive to the thing it measures — in SPACE, and on the GROUND's
  own palette.
- [intake] **The punctuation on the discard-marker test protected real speech for the
  first time, and this raw is the proof to cite.** The winning take says "Well, **no**
  longer." at word 636 — a bare `no` INSIDE the take. A token-only "No" test cuts the
  winner in half there. Asserted in both directions: zero punctuated `No.` anywhere in
  the raw, and word 636 is the bare token, is not a marker, and lies inside the chosen
  span.
- [intake] **When the shorter key never collides with in-take speech, minimality has to
  be argued from the other end.** All 27 attempts share "You can now", and so do the
  truncated fragments ("You can now connect...", "You can now re..."), so shortening the
  key only catches MORE openings, never narration — the personalapps test (shorter key
  must collide) simply does not fire. It fires at TWO tokens: "you can" hits 31 times
  including w600 "you can create reports", inside the winner. So the minimal key is the
  shortest one whose collision set is EMPTY INSIDE THE CHOSEN TAKE, not the shortest one
  with a unique hit count. Also new: the gap rule earned **DECISION-equality** here (the
  last >=2.0s silence opens exactly the chosen take) without set-equality (at >=1.0s the
  gap set and the phrase set differ at four indices) — a third standing between
  hermessteps' full equality and heygen's bound, recorded as such in the cut script.
- [chatgptphone_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1402 frames, 46.741s
  container / 46.719 authored, 43 captions, 6 sections, 127 ids, 70 tween targets, 3
  data-overlap-ok, 0 data-bleed, 7 pathLength paths, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 arrowheads,
  0 caption echoes, 22 identity-checked atoms, deepest authored ink y=391.6 against a
  400 floor; take detection on a 27-opening TWO-ERA raw keyed on the attempts'
  intersection 'You can now' with the 2-token collision asserted inside the winner,

## Run 7 (impeccable) — deepseekbox / COUNTER (2026-08-16, Opus builder fleet)

The hardware-cost story on the billionusers chassis, and the run's most expensive
lesson about the ink metric. Genuinely new findings only.

- [law13] **CAPPED vs OPEN: when a story opposes a one-time cost with a recurring one,
  make the LID the only difference.** THE CAP (b6, the peak beat) generalises THE OCEAN's
  principle past "one body": two channels share a floor, a width, a fill colour and a fill
  grammar, and the entire argument is carried by what sits on top of each — a DGX pod plate
  that closes one (overhanging 11du each side so a lid reads as a lid), nothing at all on
  the other. The machine is literally the cap. The corollary is what made it work and is
  the transferable half: **the open column must not be drawn as a bounded slot.** A dashed
  silhouette with a ceiling inverts the meaning — "it never stops" becomes "one more payment
  and it's full", which is law 16 read backwards. The fix is a track primitive with
  `border-top:0` and square top corners whose height is EXACTLY its filled cells, asserted at
  build time, so no rim can ever read as an unfilled slot. Encode-verified: cells
  [0,0,0,0,0] -> [0.996,0.983,0.996,0.996,0.996] across 44.9-47.3, lid 0 px at 42.6 -> 4228
  px at 43.9, cell 4 clearing the lid by 9du.
- [ink] **A WHITE PLATE ON CREAM IS INVISIBLE TO THE INK METRIC BY CONSTRUCTION, AND SO IS
  ANYTHING PARKED AT LOW OPACITY.** Three renders were spent on one beat. Render 2: b2 opened
  on a dashed seat (SLOT_C at 42% alpha = ~21/255 on cream, under the 34 threshold) — 43
  frames under 1%. Render 3 replaced it with the pod itself, the chassis' seated-cast fix,
  and measured WORSE (70 frames): the plate body deviates 15/255, its .15-alpha border 34,
  and the 8du vent slots at 0.20 alpha vanish entirely under the encode's 8x downsample, so
  only the black half of a lockup survives. Render 4 fixed it at the PRIMITIVE level — vent
  slots 12du at 0.42 alpha, plate borders .26 on every plate, the model badge and the
  machine's name seated in their sections' first frames — and swept 0 frames under 1%.
  The trap inside the trap: enlarging the slots changed NOTHING on the first attempt because
  a separate "grilles come up" tween had parked them at `opacity:0.35`, i.e. exactly the
  state the metric cannot see. **Anatomy is not an event.** Slots, borders and marks stand
  from the section's first frame; save the cues for things that carry meaning (here both
  power LEDs on "these are personal supercomputers").
- [ink] **A PRE-RENDER INK SWEEP THAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE THE ENCODE METRIC EXACTLY IS WORSE
  THAN NONE — IT BLESSES THE CANVAS THAT WILL FAIL.** Mine reported min 1.795% while the
  shipped encode reported 0.68% over the same beat, and I trusted it through two renders.
  Two mismatches, both mundane: it cropped to the SEAM (which pulls in the top half of the
  caption pill, a large terracotta blob) instead of the encode's 0-429du zone, and it
  measured full-resolution pixels against a FIXED cream ground instead of downsampling to
  270x201 against each frame's own modal ground. The downsample is the whole point: it blurs
  thin ink — a dashed border, a tracked kicker, a 2du plate edge — below the threshold, which
  is precisely the ink a designer reaches for when a beat feels sparse. After alignment the
  two agree to 0.04 percentage points (2.088% vs 2.051% at the same timestamp). Copy the
  encode's crop AND its scale AND its ground rule, then validate the pair on one timestamp
  before believing either.
- [gate3][law1] **A DETERMINISTIC REFUTATION WAS AVAILABLE AND THE DESIGN WAS STILL WRONG.**
  Gate 3 failed the b6 chevron: "the double arrow drifts continuously upward while displayed."
  The decode says otherwise — the chevron's ink bbox is pixel-static from 46.95 to 47.55 (top
  81.20du, bottom 120.93du, 13 consecutive frames at 10462 +/- 3 px) and the only change is a
  0.25s `pathLength` reveal. The factory's refutation path was open. It was still the wrong
  call to take it: an UP-pointing arrow revealed from its lower arm upward *reads* as an
  arrow travelling up, on the peak beat, in a lane whose first law is NO IDLE MOTION — and the
  draw carried no information the shape does not already carry. Removed (fade only), re-rendered,
  first-call pass. Rule of thumb: a judge finding that is factually wrong can still be
  perceptually right; ask what the viewer sees before reaching for the evidence.
- [intake] **A TENTH RAW SHAPE: the raw's LARGEST gap is nowhere near the winning take.**
  10.04s of silence sits mid-abandon at t=139.06, 25 words before the winner, while the winner
  itself opens after only 1.62s. A max-gap rule mis-fires onto garbage, and the last-gap form
  answers the winner at >=1.5s but an abandoned attempt at >=2.0s — so on this raw the gap rule
  is not merely demoted to a bound, it is THRESHOLD-FRAGILE, and both thresholds' answers belong
  in the edl instead of a lucky constant. The marker rule meanwhile earns a clean EQUALITY here
  (the last discard marker is the token immediately before the take), and the raw exercises
  every marker signature the factory knows: 1 punctuated spoken "No." plus 6 truncations.
- [law6][transcript] **The two transcription passes can disagree about the CLASS of the same
  non-word — check the caption BEFORE spending time on the acoustics.** The raw pass wrote
  `o-one` (a partial word, internal hyphen so the trailing-hyphen test correctly cannot see it);
  the cut pass, with this batch's keyterms, wrote `uh,` (a filler) for the same 0.4s. Both
  classes are law-6 drop material and the shipped caption is identical either way. Adjudicated
  anyway for the record — LPC formants F1 438 / F2 1485 against the following "one" at F1 554 /
  F2 1487 is the same articulatory target cut short, where a canonical /ʌ/ sits near F1 650 /
  F2 1200 — but the first question is always whether the disagreement can reach the screen.
- [captions] **A dropped filler leaves a GAP that strands the next word as its own pill, and the
  fix is a BACKWARD merge, not a threshold nudge.** Dropping `uh,` left a 0.321s hole that the
  >0.32s gap rule broke on, shipping "run," alone for half a second mid-sentence (and "this,"
  later). Raising the threshold re-chunks the entire video; merging a lone pill into the phrase
  before it re-forms exactly the sentence he spoke ("powerful enough machine to run,") and
  touches nothing else. Assert the merge count like every other declared caption edit.
- [law4] **The caption-identity guard fires on the HOOK's own key term, and GLUE is the honest
  fix.** Law 9 wants the key term centre stage; here it is "$12,000", and the hook's terminal
  gap stranded the price as a lone "$12,000." pill directly under an odometer showing the same
  glyphs — a real double caption. Gluing ("for","$12,000.") makes the pill "a full-time employee
  for $12,000.": the duplication is gone, not the check.
- [law12] **NVIDIA registered — the official lockup's BLACK wordmark is a colour mark, not a
  monochrome reduction** (the mcp/openai precedent). Wikimedia File:NVIDIA_logo.svg is uploaded
  by Nvidia under Apache-2.0: green eye #76B900 + black wordmark, 5.47:1, rasterised 2000x366
  via headless Chromium on a transparent ground. Mechanical note for wide lockups: the
  square-plate `solve_inner` targets mean(w,h)/plate, so a 5.47:1 wordmark on an 84du plate
  solves to 79.3du wide — 2.3du of margin. Size a wide badge by explicit width against its
  plate. Second note: a single `inner` solved once for the LARGEST plate makes every smaller
  plate carry a proportionally bigger mark (0.69x and 0.75x against the intended 0.58x) — solve
  per plate.
- [verify] **Three probe errors, one class, three costumes.** A lid probed at its
  post-displacement seat at a pre-displacement time (0 px, "the lid never landed"); a
  dark+terra centroid mask that cannot see NVIDIA's green eye and reported a centred pod 15du
  right of where it stands; and a modal-ground centroid INVERTING on a solid terracotta plate
  (the crop's modal colour becomes the fill, so the "ink" is the label and the corners). Each
  probe box must carry the park of its own held state, and each key must be chosen against the
  composition's own palette — including the palettes brand marks bring with them.
- [gate1] **A butted end-cap needs its STAGE derived from the axis.** The outro emblem's ink cap
  seated ON the bar's end produced the only two geometry-audit errors this build ever raised;
  butting it fixes the overlap but moves the group's centre by cap/2 unless the bar's seat is
  solved from bar+cap. The mcphidden stage lesson in the smallest possible composition.

## Run 7 (impeccable) — livetranslation / ICON (2026-08-16, Opus builder, the batch's second Icon)

The translation story told as a race between two fronts. Genuinely new lessons only;
everything else ran on the mcphidden v5 rails and simply held.

- [law13] **"Real-time" is drawable as a constant small LAG, not as speed — and the lag is
  a build-time assert.** THE LIVE REWRITE puts one sentence in three word cells and runs two
  fronts through the SAME seats: English lands SEND / THE / CONTRACT, and the Spanish rewrite
  chases it — ENVÍA fires 0.20s BEFORE the last English word has even landed. Nothing moves,
  nothing resizes, no second row appears; the only thing on screen is the distance between the
  two fronts, which IS the claim. The generator asserts the whole argument (first rewrite before
  the last arrival, both fronts monotone left-to-right, no cell rewritten before its own word
  exists), so a later re-timing that flattens the chase into a sequence kills the build instead
  of shipping a different short. Transferable rule: when a story's subject is LATENCY, draw two
  processes on one substrate and let their offset be the whole picture — a race needs no track.
- [law13][motion] **A live transcript REPLACES; it does not dissolve — and both softer options
  fail on frozen frames.** Three treatments of the same word swap were measured on decodes:
  a 50/50 crossfade renders a legible double word ("ISENDA") for multiple frames; a sequential
  fade-out/fade-in leaves the cell WORDLESS for exactly one frame when the crossover lands on a
  frame boundary (measured on render 1 at 17.767s — a tinted, hot-bordered empty box); an INSTANT
  `tl.set` swap has neither, and it is also the truer behaviour for the object being drawn. The
  0.24s border+tint tween around it carries all the continuity the eye needs. Rule of thumb: for
  a state CHANGE of the same atom, animate the container and switch the content.
- [ink] **The dead-frame metric counts a WHITE PLATE ON CREAM as ink, and a per-glyph estimate is
  off by an order of magnitude.** The sweep downscales to 108x79 and thresholds at max-channel
  delta > 13 against each frame's modal colour — and white (255,253,249) against cream
  (246,241,234) is 15. So the whole plate counts, and a lone 76du mark on cream is ~2.4% ink, not
  the ~0.5% a glyph-area-plus-border estimate predicts. This build nearly redesigned every beat's
  GROUND around that wrong model. Read the metric's source before designing around it; the
  threshold that matters (13) is far below the deviation at which a human would say "that is
  visible" (~34).
- [law19] **A displacement must start within ~0.15s of the arrival that causes it.** b7's mic ride
  began 0.44s before the hub popped, so the beat held a lone plate sitting OFF-centre with nothing
  on its way in — Law 19's defect wearing Law 19's costume. The sibling's own spacing is the
  number: mcphidden rides 0.08-0.14s ahead of the pop. Under ~0.15s the move reads as CAUSED; over
  it, it reads as drift.
- [build order] **One stem may precede ONE node; a 1→N fan may not.** The grokpublish causality
  pattern (draw the connector, pop the destination at its end) is safe for a single stem because
  the eye reads it as delivery. The same pattern on a 1→3 fan leaves a bare rail with three stubs
  pointing at empty ground for half a second, which reads as unfinished. The discriminator is the
  destination COUNT, and the fix is to invert the order: nodes first, fan joins what is already
  there.
- [mock-ui] **A product surface arrives FURNISHED; speech drives what happens INSIDE it.** The
  copilot panel first deferred every row to its spoken cue and therefore stood half-empty for
  4.2s — the same "unfinished UI" defect Miguel called on the mcphidden drawer, reproduced from
  the opposite direction (there it was too little anatomy, here it was the right anatomy arriving
  too late). The fix furnishes the panel in 1.3s (header, three checkpoint rows, divider, two
  LABELLED update fields) and reassigns the spoken cues to ticks and fills. Corollary: an empty
  dashed field WITH its label is real UI; an anonymous dashed box is lorem.
- [annotation] **Pin an annotation on all four sides INSIDE its target and concentricity stops
  being a measurement.** The mcphidden lesson said nest the ring in the same box; pinning it
  `left/top/right/bottom: -7` makes it SIZE itself off the target too. Measured on the shipped
  4K encode: centre offset (0.001, -0.001)du with gaps 4.533/4.534/4.534/4.533 — no arithmetic,
  nothing that a floored border width can falsify, and identical in the 1080 and 4K copies.
- [law3] **Measure a card's screen time from a colour that exists NOWHERE else in the short.** The
  verified badge's #1D9BF0 appears only inside the post, so counting it per frame turns "the card
  is on for 3.94s" from a timeline claim into a pixel measurement (116 frames, one contiguous
  window 6.033-9.867 = 3.867s, ceiling 4.0). Cheaper and stronger than any card-shaped detector,
  and it cannot be fooled by a fade.
- [intake] **A TENTH raw shape: the single-family raw where BOTH auxiliary rules are demoted, and
  each demotion is asserted as a SET RELATION.** 13 openings on one scripted line; the marker rule
  can never find more than 10 of them because two abandoned takes die on clean punctuation (the
  billionusers class), and the gap rule finds 12 because one restart came back in 0.50s. Instead
  of writing "these rules are bounds" in prose, the build asserts `set(gap) < set(phrase)` (STRICT
  subset), asserts exactly WHICH index the gap rule misses, and asserts exactly which two abandoned
  takes carry no marker. A re-transcription that changes the raw's shape then fails loudly instead
  of silently shifting the take.
- [gate2] **Second sighting of the harness thumbnail-clock class.** The review JPG labelled 17.666s
  showed an empty middle cell; the DECODED 17.667 frame carries "THE" at 4954 dark px, identical to
  17.60. Every timing dispute in this build was settled on `ffmpeg -ss` decodes of the encode, and
  the one real defect the JPG was pointing at (a wordless frame 0.1s later) was found by decoding
  the whole swap window frame by frame rather than by trusting either the label or the pixel.
- [clerk] **A cross-model clerk earns its keep on the PROSE, and one pass is not enough.**
  gpt-5.6-sol ran 66 / 72 / 87 checks over three passes and reproduced EVERY measurement in this
  paperwork exactly, every time. It found ten discrepancies and not one of them was a number the
  build got wrong: pass 1 caught a cleanup block written in the past tense before the cleanup
  happened, plus "every on-screen term follows transcript_tight verbatim" (false of 38 demo and
  mock-UI atoms that were never quotations), plus three roundings that flattered the build
  (0.43 for 0.434; one axis ratio published for two). Pass 2 falsified the REPLACEMENT sentence —
  "no atom restates a spoken phrase in different words" is a semantic claim two lexical guards
  cannot prove, and it named the counterexamples ('LIVE TRANSCRIPT' on screen while he says "live
  transcription"; 'daily AI' while he says "each and every single day"). Pass 3 caught the atom
  inventory being hand-written instead of derived, and "byte for byte" said of a byte-exact
  PREFIX. Three transferable rules: (1) publish measurements at full precision, because any
  rounding a clerk can call favourable IS favourable; (2) never write a semantic claim a guard
  cannot prove — declare the exceptions instead, which is stronger and survives; (3) DERIVE
  inventories from the shipped artifact, never type them. And the sequencing rule the first
  finding teaches: write the cleanup claim AFTER the cleanup, not before.

  data-overlap-ok, 13 pathLength paths, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 arrowheads, 0 scale parks; take
