  sweep **0 of 1697 frames under 1% ink, 0 blank**, min 1.7112%, median 10.677%, min max-channel
  deviation 121; caption band pill-free on 8 frames, all before the first word at 0.239s; REAL TWEET
  **3.867s measured from pixels**, contiguous, at 0.8812x/0.88036x, zero metrics, badge payload-true;
  1 colour mark at 0.393x intrinsic, nothing upscaled; both rings verified from INSIDE their active
  windows; sync **lag 0 on both streams** (audio r=0.9797 at 1ms, video r=0.9991 at 1 frame), 0.000s
  master delta, NO remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual, 0 semantic, 0 visual minor
  notes**; independent gpt-5.6-sol clerk over THREE passes (66/72/87 checks) reproducing every
  measurement exactly and finding ten discrepancies, all of them PROSE or precision, each fixed
  and re-clerked; 2 renders — the second bought by a one-frame
  wordless cell that only a per-frame decode of the swap windows could see, never by geometry.
- [deepseekbox FIX PASS 1 — measure the mouth before you blame the transcriber] Miguel: "it's
  NVIDIA DGX Spark, not DGX Pod." The short named the wrong NVIDIA product in TWO places — the b2
  typeset plate label ("DGX POD") and the caption pill ("on two NVIDIA DGX Pods."). The tempting
  move is to assume Scribe misheard "Sparks" and respell it as a transcription fix. **That would
  have been a lie in the paperwork.** The adjudication is acoustic and it is cheap: word 62 spans
  9.739-9.979 (0.240s); the 30ms immediately before its vowel carries **2.2-2.9%** of its energy
  above 4kHz, while the SAME speaker's /s/ onsets in the SAME recording run 30-90% ("supercomputers",
  "subscription": mean high-band over the first 80ms 7.2% and 10.0%) and his /p/ onsets sit at 3.7%
  and 6.1%. The target's first 80ms measures **1.1% — below even the plosives**. There is no /s/
  before the stop, so /sp-/ is acoustically impossible; LPC-14 puts the nucleus at F1 758 / F2 879
  (a low BACK rounded /ɒ/) with no /r/ window and no velar closure gap, and 240ms total cannot hold
  the ~80-120ms of /s/ that "Sparks" needs. **He genuinely says "Pods". It is a MISSPEAK, not a
  mistranscription** — and that is the distinction that decides which law applies. Law 14
  PROPER-NOUN SPELLING governs either way (display follows reality, never the misspeak), but the
  RECORD has to say which one it was. Two transferable rules. (1) **In-recording controls beat
  absolute thresholds**: never judge a phoneme against a remembered number — pull the same speaker's
  known /s/ and known /p/ from the same cut and let the target fall between them. Two minutes of
  numpy replaced a guess that would have been wrong. (2) **A misspeak correction must never touch
  the timing tokens.** ANCHORS keeps the SPOKEN form ("NVIDIA DGX Pods") because it is matched
  against the raw transcript for cut placement; the respell runs inside build_captions, AFTER
  clean_tokens and AFTER anchor resolution, and the GLUE pair is re-keyed onto the CORRECTED token
  ("dgx","sparks") because glue reads the respelled stream. Get that order wrong and the anchors
  fail loud — which is the design working. RESPELL_EXPECT={"Pods":1} pins the hit count so a
  re-transcription can never silently change the caption. Gate 2 for a text fix is not "look at a
  frame": decode **every** frame the name appears on. Typeset window frames 207-512 (306 frames):
  302 segment to exactly **8 ink column-runs** (D,G,X,S,P,A,R,K) where "DGX POD" would give 6, and
  the 4 exceptions are the exit fade (ink 14-40px against a 3,809px median). 20 distinct label
  states across the settle, **a representative of each read natively — all 20 read "DGX SPARK"**.
  Caption window frames 243-312: 69/70 share a byte-identical word-width signature, 5 distinct
  states, **all 5 read "on two NVIDIA DGX Sparks."** Glyph-run counting is the right deterministic
  discriminator for a text swap because it is invariant to encode noise and it distinguishes the
  two candidate strings by construction. All three gates green (Gate 1 0/0; Gate 3 pass, 0 visual,
  0 semantic on the FIRST call), sync unchanged at 0-frame lag, 2009 frames and 66.987s identical,
  size 197,379,050 -> 197,382,523 (+3,473 bytes, the wider glyph run) — the size delta is itself
  evidence the change was text-only.

- **2026-08-17 REVIEW: FIRST ZERO-REMARK ROUND.** Miguel on the 8-video Opus fleet (after the single
  deepseekbox fact fix): "all of the things you built were amazing honestly. no remarks." First
  full batch to clear review untouched — the 19-law + reference-build + active-window-verification
  system now produces approval-grade output on the first pass. All 12 staged shorts approved and
  scheduled (6 on 2026-08-17, 6 on 2026-08-18).

- **BED VOLUME LAW (Miguel, 2026-08-17): data-volume 0.13 -> 0.065.** Measured: bed_split_v2 is
  mastered ~6 dB hotter than the voice recordings (-16.4 vs -22.2 dBFS median), so the old 0.13
  gain left only an 11.9 dB authored voice-over-bed margin (15.7-17.4 dB measured on final mixes)
  vs the 18-25 dB standard for speech content — Miguel heard it: "the music is a bit too high."
  New default 0.065 (-6 dB) lands ~18 dB authored / low-20s measured. Builders: never trust a
  volume constant's face value — the SOURCE loudness of each file is part of the mix math. SFX
  volume 0.18 unchanged (transient, not competing with speech).

- **Bed remix 2026-08-17 addendum:** mathconjecture's builder had hand-set its bed at 0.16 (not the
  then-standard 0.13) — hottest mix of the fleet at a 15.0 dB margin. The AUDIO MIX LAW constant is
  0.065, and volume constants are not free parameters. All six batch-B shorts remixed and verified:
  decoded pixels identical to the approved renders (worst frame diff 0.0004), margins now 19.4-23.0
  dB. Candidate gate check: add pause-floor margin >=18 dB to the deterministic render sweep.

- **2026-08-17 (run 8, airtable/icon builder): THE 2026-08-17 FILMING SESSION IS ~6.5 dB QUIETER
  THAN THE SESSIONS THE BED CONSTANT WAS CALIBRATED ON — batch-wide, measured, not inferred.**
  The AUDIO MIX LAW fixes bed `data-volume="0.065"`, and that constant was derived from the
  run-6/7 recordings. Measured with `ffmpeg -af volumedetect` on the cut audio: run-7
  chatgptphone sits at mean -19.2 dB, while ALL EIGHT run-8 cuts sit at -25.3 to -26.7 dB
  (airtable -26.0, buzzteams -26.7, geministt -25.9, inkling -26.4, revolut -25.6, selfoptimize
  -25.3, skillssh -25.6, vendorlock -25.5). The bed's own level is unchanged (-14.3 dB mean,
  -11.35 dBFS RMS), so the SAME legal constant that delivered the approved batch-B margins of
  19.4-23.0 dB delivers **~12-14 dB on this whole batch**. On airtable the delivered mix measures
  speech -21.78 dBFS against a bed isolated at -35.46 dBFS = **13.68 dB**, and the isolated bed
  agrees with the -35.09 dBFS predicted from the bed's own source level, so the constant IS
  correctly applied — the voice is simply quieter. Nothing was hand-adjusted: 0.065 shipped,
  because the law is explicit that the constant is not a free parameter and a hand-set 0.16 is
  already in this ledger. **This is one batch-wide remix decision for Miguel, not eight builder
  judgement calls**, and it is exactly the shape of the batch-B remix (decoded pixels identical,
  margins restored). The good news in the same measurement: run-7 cuts CLIP (peak +2.2 to +2.4
  dBFS) while run-8 peaks cleanly at -1.58 dBFS — the new session level is the healthier
  recording, it just needs the bed re-scaled to match it.

- **2026-08-17 (run 8, airtable): TWO SHARED REGISTRY LOGO ASSETS WERE BROKEN, and the free 1080
  still sweep found both before a single 4K render was spent.**
  (1) `assets/logos/automation/zapier-color.png` was NOT the Zapier mark at all — a single flat
  #FF5000 rectangle (alpha bbox (146,426)-(494,507), 6.88% ink, **2 distinct colours**) that
  rendered on screen as an orange DASH inside its plate. Replaced with Zapier's own CDN logomark
  (`cdn.zapier.com/zapier/images/logos/zapier-logomark.png`, the official app tile, 1024px, ink
  98.8%), cross-checked against Wikimedia Commons `File:Zapier_logo.svg` (Artist "Zapier", Public
  domain) and Simple Icons' brand hex FF4F00; registry entry rewritten with full provenance and
  the broken original preserved as evidence. Zapier's official logomark IS a coloured tile, so it
  now ships BARE like ChatGPT's (plate-on-plate ban).
  (2) `assets/logos/ai-models/chatgpt-color.png` has a **square bottom-right corner**: measured
  corner radii 240 / 240 / 231 / **0** px on the 1024px raster. It has been painting one hard
  corner in every short that uses the tile, run 6 onward. Repaired STRUCTURALLY instead of by
  patching a shared raster mid-run (seven other builders were rendering): a `tile_radius_frac()`
  helper measures the artwork's own four corner radii from its alpha channel, takes the largest,
  and `bare_tile` clips to it with `overflow:hidden`. Resolution-independent, so it holds in the
  1080 copy and the 4K `zoom:2` copy alike, and the build ASSERTS the defect is still present so
  the clip gets re-judged the day the raster is fixed.
  **Transferable rule: run the ASSET HEALTH sweep as a MEASUREMENT (ink fraction, distinct
  colours, per-corner alpha radii), not as a glance.** A 2-colour, 6.9%-ink "logo" and a 0-radius
  corner are both one line of numpy away, and both survived every AI gate for months because a
  judge looking at a small orange rectangle has no reason to call it wrong.

- **2026-08-17 (run 8, airtable): a chip carrying a bar and a pill READS AS AN iOS TOGGLE SWITCH.**
  The bespoke scene flies "records" from an Airtable grid into a ChatGPT thread, and v1 built each
  flying record as a rounded container holding a grey name bar plus a 15.6x11 accent pill. At chip
  scale that is exactly a track and a knob: three of them stacked in the chat card read as a
  settings screen, not as data. v2 makes the two CELLS explicit — name cell, a vertical cell
  DIVIDER, status cell — and stretches the status swatch to 3.2:1, with a build-time assert
  (`CHIP_STAT_W / CHIP_CELL_H >= 2.0`) so it can never round back into a knob. The general lesson:
  at chip scale, shape ALONE carries the semantics, and a rounded rect + horizontal bar + blob is
  a switch in every UI vocabulary the viewer owns. Draw the structure (a divider), not just the
  contents.

- **2026-08-17 (run 8, airtable): "delay the entrance so the card is not empty" and "no blank
  frames at the section head" are the SAME dial pulling in opposite directions — the answer is
  SEATED CAST, not a timing compromise.** Pass 1 opened the b1 base card at t0+0.12 and its first
  record 1.10s later: an unfinished card with an empty body. Pass 2 delayed the card's `pop` to
  t0+0.42 and the deterministic ink sweep then measured **12 fully blank frames** at the top of the
  section (plus 4 and 5 at the b2 and b4 heads, 21 total). Pass 3 fixed both at once by giving the
  section's FIRST element `settle` instead of `pop` — opacity 1 from the section's very first
  frame, scale-only entrance — and by making the card's identity header seated cast with it, so
  frame one already reads "an Airtable base". Result: **21 fully blank frames -> 0**, and the
  remaining under-1%-ink run is a deliberate kicker-only opening (min ink 0.67%, min channel
  deviation 97, i.e. demonstrably not blank). Builders: `pop` is for elements that JOIN a beat;
  the element that OPENS a beat is seated cast, and that is also what keeps the blank-frame count
  at zero.

## Run 8 — buzzteams / DIAGRAM (2026-08-17, Opus 5 builder)

The first single-take raw in the ledger, and the first build whose two worst defects
were both found by an instrument rather than by an eye. Genuinely new lessons only.

- [intake] **AN ELEVENTH RAW SHAPE: the SINGLE-TAKE raw, where every rule degenerates
  and only the ABSENCE facts carry weight.** Ten shapes in the ledger describe raws with
  2-27 attempts; the rules exist to choose among them. Here there is nothing to choose:
  the opening key `ai can` fires ONCE, the sign-off fires ONCE, and the span between them
  is the entire word list. Writing "all three rules agree" would be a false comfort — a
  rule with one candidate has not been tested. So the assertions are inverted: the marker
  rule is INAPPLICABLE at exactly zero (no spoken "No.", no truncation, no ellipsis
  anywhere), and the gap rule is INAPPLICABLE **by its own threshold** — the largest
  inter-word gap in the whole raw is 0.720s (w42, "you." -> "Now,"), pinned as a number so
  a re-transcription that splits this raw into attempts fails loudly instead of quietly
  re-deciding the take. **When a rule cannot discriminate, assert what makes it unable
  to.**

- [ink][gate1] **The pre-render pixel sweep is not a formality — on this build it found
  BOTH of the defects no gate reports, before a single frame was encoded.** Run at both
  thresholds over the encode's own band it reported (a) four consecutive samples at
  max-channel deviation **33** across the b3 opening — metrically BLANK on the 34/255
  instrument — and (b) six consecutive samples at **0.826%** across the b4 opening. Gate 1
  was 0 errors / 0 warnings on the same project at the same time. Two rounds of fixes
  later the same sweep read min 1.111% at 13, 0 under-1%, 0 blank, and the shipped encode
  agreed (min 1.122%). **Gate 1 measures boxes; only pixels measure ink.**

- [law8][craft] **Placeholder greys are a legibility defect, not a style.** The b3 thread
  cards were first drawn with the usual mock-UI alphas (.13 greys, a .30 accent) and the
  whole opening measured blank: at .13 over white a bar lands 19 levels off the ground,
  under the 34 threshold and under a phone. At .30/.62 the same furniture sits 49-100
  levels off and the card reads at arm's length. The MOCK-UI ANATOMY note says build real
  anatomy; the corollary is that real UI does not whisper — and an honest composer field
  at the card's foot is both more anatomy and more ink than another grey bar.

- [law19][ink] **A beat that opens on ONE white plate is thin as a metric AND as a
  composition, and the same fix cures both.** A 76du plate alone measured 0.826%; a 96du
  plate alone measures 1.11% (b0's own frame 0), which clears the floor but only just. The
  fix was not a bigger plate: it was giving the beat its real subject — YOU flanked by the
  TWO DASHED SEATS the two errands will fill — which is 1.5% of ink, a symmetric opening
  composition, and honest under LAW 16 because both seats are filled inside the beat.

- [law16][craft] **A dashed seat with no drawn relationship to its owner is a stray box.**
  The three output seats around the peak's mesh were first placed on each agent's outer
  side with a 16-20du air gap and nothing else; on the contact sheet they read as three
  empty rectangles scattered around a diagram rather than as three agents' outputs. Adding
  one 20du stub per seat — drawn FROM the plate outward, after the seat exists — converts
  them into declared ports at the cost of three connectors. The build asserts all three
  gaps are equal, so the stubs cannot drift apart.

- [law15][verify] **An in-place swap must coincide in INK, not in boxes.** b8 replaces a
  terracotta "?" with a terracotta check at the same seat. Authored from equal box tops
  the first encode measured their ink centroids at y=206.46 and y=216.86: a **10.4du drop**
  on the short's last beat, because a centred glyph's ink sits high in its own line box
  (no descender on "?") while an svg's ink is concentric with its viewBox. The fix is one
  shared ink axis and two MEASURED per-atom offsets (the mcphidden per-STRING rule), with
  a build-time assert that both atoms resolve to it. **Two things at "the same seat" are
  only in the same place if you measured the thing the eye actually sees.**

- [verify] **A threshold inherited from another palette measures the background.** The
  sibling `white_px` rule (min channel > 215) is a statement about a darker ground: on
  this cream (#F6F1EA, min channel 234) it counts the BACKGROUND as plate, so every card
  probe returned its full box at every timestamp and discriminated nothing. The plates are
  #FFFDF9 (min 249), so 242 splits the two populations with ~7 levels of margin on each
  side. Same class, twice more in one build: `dark_px`'s <90 rule is a statement about
  FULL-opacity glyphs and reads a deliberately dimmed plate as absent (the b5 opening
  needed a <200 companion), and a probe box drawn around the mesh's hollow centre included
  the mesh's own diagonal links, so the "?"-vs-check bbox measured 92du of ink at every
  timestamp. **Every probe threshold and every probe BOX is a claim about the palette and
  the geometry it is pointed at; re-derive both, then report the number.**

- [craft] **Plate-on-plate has a small-object form: a tinted chip inside a white card
  reads as a smaller agent.** The order chip and the three work tiles were first drawn as
  white plates carrying a terracotta glyph — at 36-46du the white frame dominates and the
  eye files them with the agents. Tinting the PLATE itself (terracotta ground, white
  knocked-out glyph) separates the two vocabularies completely: white plates are actors,
  solid terracotta plates are the work moving between them, and the peak's last beat reads
  in one glance.

- [buzzteams_diagram] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1758 frames, 58.603s container /
  58.597 authored, 168946537 bytes, 62 captions, 10 sections, 156 ids (70 section-prefixed), 71
  tween targets, 0 untweened children, 21 `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 0 `data-glyph-ok`,
  42 `pathLength=100` paths, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 arrowheads, 0 svg scale tweens, 0 caption
  echoes, 0 caption identities, 5 typeset atoms; take detection on the ledger's FIRST single-take
  raw (1 opening, 1 sign-off, 0 markers asserted, max inter-word gap 0.720s asserted), head by
  SUSTAIN with the onset holding 23 windows against 15 required and ZERO pre-roll windows above
  threshold, the cut keeping all 203 spoken words with a token-for-token diff of exactly two
  PUNCTUATION-only differences and the caption cleaner dropping zero; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0
  warnings on both rounds**; 71 pre-render stills over 3 rounds plus a 293-sample dual-threshold
  PIXEL sweep that found two defects no gate reports; Gate 2 **55 distinct states from 176
  samples**, 121 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, 18 pop-in markers and 1 stillness marker all
  resolved on exact decodes, all 55 states read; `idle_motion_scan` frames=234 idle_drift=no
  long_static=no; encode sweep **0 of 1758 frames under 1% top-zone ink at 13/255, 0 blank**, min
  1.119%, median 4.589%, min max-channel deviation 79; the CONVERGENCE counted rather than
  asserted (scatter seats 9968/9885/9735 dim-ink -> 0, mesh seats 0 -> 20552/20585/20622; links
  5970 -> 10305 terra px); all five dashed promises measured filled; the b8 swap re-measured
  coincident at **0.04du** after a 10.4du first cut; caption band pill-free on 12 frames, 8 before
  the first word at 0.239s and 4 after the last pill closes; ONE brand mark (Buzz, three
  placements, 8.433s measured from pixels, 0.703x at 4K); sync **lag 0 on both streams** (audio
  r=0.9680 at 1ms, video r=0.9994 at 1 frame), 0.000s cut-master delta, NO remux, mouth crop
  re-derived from five decoded candidates; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual / 0 semantic
  / 0 minor** (1 Gemini call); **2 renders**, the second bought by the b8 ink axis and by nothing
  else. Full record: shorts_run8/paperwork/buzzteams_diagram.json.

## Run 8 (impeccable) — geministt / KINETIC (2026-08-17, Opus 5 builder)

The batch's shortest short (31.2s of finished video from a 175.6s raw) and the first
build whose bespoke scene is a LAG rather than an object. Genuinely new findings only.

- [law13] **A LAG is drawable as choreography, and the way to make it read is to give
  the two processes ONE GEOMETRY and let only their timing differ.** THE MIMIC stacks
  two wordmark rows — `[ChatGPT mark] C H A T G P T` and `[Gemini mark] G E M I N I` —
  solved onto ONE width, ONE text left edge (137.0du) and ONE text right edge (523.0du),
  with each row's letter tracking DERIVED from that shared width (14.018du and 32.388du)
  rather than set by hand. Seven letters and six letters, one span. A terracotta voice
  bar then sweeps a row's 386.0du span while each letter lights at the instant the bar's
  leading edge reaches its own centre, and 0.72s later row B runs the IDENTICAL move.
  Nothing else differs — same bar width, same duration, same origin, same ease — so the
  only thing on screen is the distance between the two fronts, which IS "copying". This
  is livetranslation's THE LIVE REWRITE principle (two processes on one substrate, the
  offset is the whole picture) transposed from latency to imitation, and it generalises:
  **when a story's subject is one thing IMITATING another, draw both doing the same move
  and make the delay the only variable.**
- [law13][verify] **A per-INDEX lag is not the lag, and a builder who measures it will
  think the scene is broken.** The k-th letter of row A lights at `start + D*f_A[k]` and
  of row B at `start + LAG + D*f_B[k]`, and the two rows carry different letters at
  different fractions of the span — so the measured per-index differences came back
  [0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9, 1.0]s against an authored LAG of 0.72s, which looks like a
  failure and is not. The exact claim lives on the BAR FRONTS: row B's front at t+LAG is
  row A's front at t. Measured by interpolating the decoded bar extents, the maximum
  absolute error is **1.6du over a 386.0du span (0.41%)**. Rule: measure the claim's own
  invariant, and when a derived quantity disagrees, compute what it SHOULD be from the
  authored geometry before calling anything wrong — the authored per-index differences
  are [0.72, 0.768, 0.84, 0.899, 0.936, 0.969]s and every measurement agrees within one
  0.10s sample.
- [law13][motion] **An EASE shortens the visible overlap of two staggered tweens, so the
  authored overlap and the measured overlap are different numbers and both belong in the
  record.** The two waves overlap by 0.83s by construction, but `power3.out` puts bar A
  within 0.4% of full width by 12.74 — well before its tween ends at 13.089 — so the
  window in which both rows are strictly partially lit measures 0.50s, not 0.83s. A
  paperwork line that quotes only the authored figure is a claim a clerk can falsify with
  one decode. Publish both, and say which one the ease bounds.
- [law2][law7] **A brand mark's FILE BOX is not its INK, and sizing marks by the box
  makes them optically unequal and pulls centred rows off axis.** `gemini-color.png`
  carries a 4.06% transparent margin on every side, so an 88du box paints 80.9du of
  spark — 8% smaller than a full-bleed tile at the same box, and enough to put the roll
  call's cast-of-2 ink centre at 285.6du against an axis of 288.0. The fix belongs in the
  PRIMITIVE, not in the call sites: `Z.mark()` now takes an INK centre and an INK width,
  solves the `<img>` box from the file's own alpha bbox (`box = ink_w / bbox_frac *
  max(W,H)/W`), registers the INK rect for every geometry assertion, and a guard refuses
  to build if any beat paints two marks at unequal ink. Post-fix the four cast centres
  measure 287.86 / 287.60 / 288.00 / 288.00. This is the appsdistrib "box proximity is
  not ink proximity" rule promoted from a probe caveat to a layout primitive, and every
  future build with a mixed cast of tiles and glyphs needs it.
- [law15] **A conveyor whose LAST state has a different silhouette cannot use grid park
  offsets.** chatgptphone's `row_seats` derives park offsets as `(n-k)(w+gap)/2`, which
  assumes every cast's ink extent ends at a mark's right edge. Here the fourth seat is a
  DASHED box 14du wider than a mark on each side, so the k=4 state's ink is 12du wider
  than the grid says and the row lands 6du off. The general form computes each cast's ink
  span explicitly — `ink_right = base + (k-1)*pitch + mark + extra_k` — and solves the
  park from THAT. Cheap, and it made the b7 assertion exact instead of approximately true.
- [law11][law16] **"Soon enough" is drawable, and the honest drawing keeps the difference
  after the payoff.** He says "even ChatGPT, Gemini, Siri, and soon enough, Claude" —
  three shipped, one pending. A dashed seat arrives EMPTY on "soon enough" and the Claude
  mark lands inside it on "Claude", and the dashed border STAYS. The temptation is to
  resolve the seat into a solid one on arrival, which would silently claim Claude has
  shipped it; the temptation the other way is to leave the seat empty, which is law 16's
  dead slot. Keeping both — filled slot, unresolved border — is the only reading that
  matches the sentence.
- [ink][mock-ui] **A settings card whose body is a near-ground tint is INVISIBLE to the
  ink metric by construction, and the threshold that decides it is 13, not 34.** b6's
  plate was authored at `rgba(246,241,234,0.05)` over `#101012`, which deviates 12/255 —
  under the encode sweep's own threshold. The whole 460x108du panel counted as zero ink;
  only its 2.5du border, its track and its knob registered. At 0.12 alpha the body
  deviates 29 and the beat measures normally. deepseekbox's white-plate-on-cream finding
  has a dark-ground twin, and the number to check a surface against is the metric's
  threshold, not whether a human can see it.
- [ink][tooling] **A sweep that emulates section visibility must not sample at exactly
  t == dur.** The first run of the pre-render sweep reported one under-1% sample; it was
  at the final instant, where every section's `[start, start+duration)` window has just
  closed, so the instrument painted an empty canvas the encode never contains (its last
  frame is (n-1)/fps). Bound the loop at `dur - 0.5/fps`. The chatgptphone rule — a sweep
  that does not reproduce the encode metric is a different instrument — has a boundary
  corollary: it must not reproduce artifacts the encode cannot have either.
- [captions] **The backward merge is worth running as a RULE, because the pill it rescues
  may be the one that would have collided.** deepseekbox introduced merging a lone
  function-word pill into the phrase before it. Here the general rule (any single-word
  phrase merges backward) fired three times, and the third was `ChatGPT,` — token-identical
  to THE MIMIC's row-A wordmark, and separated from b4's first frame only by the razor-thin
  coincidence that the pill's window ends at the same rounded instant the section opens.
  Merged, it reads "regular GPT voice from ChatGPT," and the law-4 collision cannot arise
  at all. Declaring the count (3) and pinning the three resulting strings keeps it honest.
- [law4][guards] **A wordmark spelled across one-letter atoms is STRUCTURALLY INVISIBLE to
  the caption-identity guard.** Every `l0j` atom is a single character, so its token set is
  `{"c"}`, `{"h"}` ... and can never equal a pill's. The row still SPELLS "CHATGPT" on
  screen. The fix is a VIRTUAL atom: register `(section, name, "CHATGPT", cue, end)` in the
  guard's input alongside the real atoms, so the check runs against what the viewer reads
  rather than against what the DOM happens to be chunked into. Any lane that composes type
  from sub-word atoms needs this or the guard is decorative.
- [intake] **An ELEVENTH raw shape: two script families where the OPENING stem is the
  intersection and the winner's own second sentence is a minority form fired once.** All 14
  attempts share "Gemini is"; 13 add "now"; and the second sentence is rewritten seven ways
  across the session, the winner's ("On their newest macOS release...") appearing exactly
  once on the whole raw. So the key had to CONTRACT to the 2-token intersection, and the
  minimality argument runs both ways at once: one token ("Gemini") collides INSIDE the
  winner at word 332 ("even ChatGPT, Gemini, Siri"), three tokens ("Gemini is now") drops
  family A. Asserting both failure modes — the in-take collision set AND the missed-opening
  set — is what makes "2 tokens" a fact rather than a preference.
- [intake] **Five clean punctuated abandons in one raw, and the marker rule demoted twice
  over.** Four attempts die on "...copying ChatGPT." and one on "Now, go ahead and try." —
  none carries a truncation, and the raw contains ZERO punctuated "No." anywhere. So the
  marker rule can never see more than 9 of 14 attempts, and its 9 markers agree without
  deciding. The gap rule is also THRESHOLD-FRAGILE in the deepseekbox sense but in a new
  place: its last opening is the winner at >=1.0/1.5/2.0s and becomes an ABANDONED attempt
  (word 245) at >=2.5s. Recording all four thresholds' answers in the edl is cheaper than
  defending one constant.
- [paperwork][clerk] **A pixel-key premise of the form "X is the only Y in the short" is a
  claim about the WHOLE timeline, and a clerk will decode the one frame that breaks it.**
  The real-tweet screen-time metric was described as "keyed on pure #fff — the card is the
  only pure-white surface in the short". It is not: the ChatGPT tile's knocked-out knot is
  also pure #fff, 60,099 pixels of it at full resolution, and the verifier's own printed
  `non_card_max_px = 614` residue WAS that knot on the downsampled grid — the builder
  published the refutation of its own premise and did not read it. What actually separates
  card from knot is AREA, via an undisclosed `CARD_MIN_PX` threshold. Rule: never justify a
  measurement by an exclusivity claim you have not swept; state the threshold that does the
  separating, and prove the separation is WIDE (here the card peaks at 13,857 px against
  614, so every threshold from ~1,500 to ~40,000 returns the identical window). A number
  that is right for an unstated reason is one clerk decode from being a material finding.
- [paperwork][clerk] **The finishing pass of a builder that died after clerk pass 1 must
  re-derive the gates itself, not inherit them from a report file.** This build's first
  incarnation reached clerk pass 1 (paperwork_ok false: three material findings, all prose
  and cleanup, zero on the encode) and stopped mid-repair. The cheap, sufficient proof that
  the repaired paperwork still describes the shipped artifact is a HASH TRIPLE plus one free
  gate: `output/<id>.mp4` sha256 == the staged copy's sha256 == the sha256 the paperwork
  claims (d6683ed8...), the 1080/4K `index.html` hashes still match the audited/rendered
  pair, and Gate 1 re-run from scratch on the 1080 project. If any of the three legs move,
  the render is stale and the paperwork is fiction — if none move, the only thing left to
  repair is prose and cleanup, which is exactly what pass 1 found.
- [geministt_kinetic] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 936 frames, 31.210667s
  container / 31.20 authored, 93485756 bytes, 27 captions, 8 sections, 117 ids, 65 tween
  targets, 0 untweened children, 4 `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 0 `non-scaling-stroke`,

  atom windows (2 of them VIRTUAL wordmarks); take detection on a 14-opening TWO-family raw
  keyed on the 2-token intersection "Gemini is" with minimality asserted in BOTH directions
  (1 token collides in-take at word 332, 3 tokens drops family A), sign-off "catch you in
  the next" (1 hit, the sibling key asserted at 0), gap rule an agreement with one
  documented disagreement each way and its threshold fragility recorded at four thresholds,
