## Run 8 — selfoptimize / COUNTER (2026-08-17, Opus 5 re-verification pass over the Opus fleet build)

Re-verified an already-shipped build end to end rather than rebuilding it: all three gates
re-run live, every checkable paperwork number reproduced from disk, no re-render warranted.
Record: `shorts_run8/paperwork/reverify_selfoptimize_counter.json`. Three lessons are new.

- **THE AUDIO MIX MARGIN IS AN ESTIMATOR ARGUMENT, NOT A DEFECT — STOP RE-LITIGATING IT.**
  The AUDIO MIX LAW prescribes CONSTANTS (voice 1, bed 0.065, SFX 0.18); its "18+ dB" is a
  DESCRIPTION of what 0.065 achieves, not an independent acceptance test with a named
  instrument. Measured on the same shipped file, this one mix reads **20.81 dB** (loud-decile
  voice vs the bed stem in isolation), **19.70 dB** (p90/p10 of 1/30s frame RMS), **15.89 dB**
  (p85/p15 — the estimator the airtable clerk used), **11.81 dB** (median speech vs median
  bed) and **7.75 dB** (naive pause floor that lets SFX windows in). Same file, five answers,
  a 13 dB spread. THE DECISIVE CONTROL: applying p85/p15 to ALL SEVEN run-8 renders yields
  15.55-17.38 dB — **every single one "fails"**, including mixes whose HTML carries the
  mandated constants exactly; the same seven all pass at p90/p10 (19.04-21.26 dB). The
  geministt entry independently records two APPROVED run-7 shorts measuring 13.55 and 17.42 dB
  on its instrument. An instrument that condemns the entire run and Miguel-approved shipped
  work is measuring itself, not the mix. Consequence: `paperwork/clerk_airtable_icon.json`
  returns FAIL-MARGINAL at 17.05 dB on this basis and is very probably an artifact.
  **Rule going forward: if the shipped HTML carries voice 1 / bed 0.065 / SFX 0.18, the mix is
  compliant — report the margin as a diagnostic WITH its estimator named, and never hand-set a
  bed gain to chase a number** (hand-setting 0.16 is what put a builder in the ledger, and at
  0.16 the median-speech margin here would collapse to 3.98 dB). STANDARD should pin one
  estimator; until it does, name yours.

- **Mouth-openness x audio cross-correlation is UNRELIABLE ON A BEARDED SUBJECT — use bilabial
  closure strips.** The whole-video adjudicator returned r<=0.096 at EVERY lag on this take
  (both a grayscale dark-fraction aperture proxy and an inter-frame motion-energy proxy):
  beard texture dominates the window, so the "peak" was pure noise and would have supported any
  verdict you wanted, including a false +100ms. What settled it in one shot: decode a bilabial
  onset at -4/-2/0/+2/+4 frames and LOOK. At 'But' 14.340s, 'by' 21.359s and 'better' 30.000s
  the lips are closed at the onset and release within 2 frames — lag 0, unambiguous. A near-zero
  peak correlation is a FAILED MEASUREMENT, not a small offset; say so instead of reporting the
  argmax. (Also: the builder's own mouth window `crop=300:200:910:2935` had its TOP edge at the
  mouth CENTRE, framing chin and beard — the claim "lips fully inside with ~50px clearance"
  did not survive a decode. Correct window for this framing: `crop=520:380:890:2740`. Always
  eyeball the window before trusting anything computed from it.)

- **Check the bed by HASH, not by filename.** The staged bed is named `bed_split.mp3` — the
  banned v1's name — but is byte-identical to canonical `bed_split_v2.mp3`
  (sha256 `8a4268f0...` vs v1's `7bb89f12...`). The generator stages v2 under the generic name.
  A filename-only check reads as a banned-asset violation and would have forced a pointless
  4K re-render; a hash check clears it in one command.

Verification highlights, all reproduced independently: take detection re-derived from the raw
without reading the builder's reasoning (`ai is` -> exactly 5 openings, one sign-off, last
complete take w154 @96.540s / 153 words, marker equality `last_marker + 1 == take_start`, and
the gap rule confirmed BOUND-ONLY — >=1.0/1.5/2.0s answer the MARKER one index early, >=2.6/3.0s
answer a mid-abandon); Gate 1 0 errors / 0 warnings on the 1080; Gate 2 43 states / 133 samples /
90 collapsed / 11 markers; Gate 3 first-call pass; REAL TWEET 3.600s in ONE contiguous run
measured by counting #1D9BF0 badge pixels (a colour present nowhere else), zero metrics rendered
though the payload carries them, card text BYTE-IDENTICAL to the fetched payload; the wash
annotation observed from INSIDE its active window per the VERIFICATION RULE. The b1 empty-slot
self-report ("0.30s") measured 0.133s — the builder over-reported against itself, which is the
right direction to be wrong in.


## 2026-08-17 — run 8, revolut / Icon Choreography (completing builder, Opus 5)

Build finished from a hand-off: builder 1 passed all three gates and wrote the paperwork, then
its session ended before staging. The interesting findings are all from the RE-VERIFICATION, not
from the design.

- **GATE 2's MANIFEST LABELS LAG ITS OWN PIXELS BY EXACTLY 4 FRAMES (+0.1336s). Every builder
  reading claim-sync off `manifest.md` is checking the words against the WRONG instant.** Found by
  accident: the frame labelled `f_0016_333.jpg` showed the outro handle already painted, but an
  exact decode at 16.333s showed no handle at all (it enters at 16.37). Matching all 22 kept frames
  against individually-extracted source frames gave a *perfectly constant* offset — mean +0.1336s,
  min +0.1333, max +0.1340, zero scatter. Root cause is `pipeline/frame_review.py`'s filter chain
  `crop=...,fps=3,scale=512:-2`: ffmpeg's `fps` filter maps input frame n to output slot
  round(n*out/in) and emits the LAST input frame landing in each slot, so at 30->3 fps slot 0 is
  fed by input frames 0..4 and ships frame **4**, not frame 0. Proved by construction: the same
  chain with `round=down` ships frames [9,19,29,39] (the last of 0..9), and `fps=3:start_time=0`
  changes nothing. So the true time of the sample the manifest calls `t` is **t + 0.1336s** at the
  default 3fps on a 30fps encode; the general form is `t + (floor(in/(2*out)))/in`.
  Consequences, in order of how much they cost: (a) claim-sync, highlight-match and key-term-timing
  checks read the transcript ~half a word early — at this take's 3.7 words/s, 0.134s is 0.5 words;
  (b) a builder verifying "the element is absent before its cue" can see it PRESENT and rework a
  correct build (this nearly happened here); (c) pop-in adjudicators centred on manifest labels
  still work, but only because they sweep a +-0.2s window that happens to swallow the offset.
  **Do not fix this by editing the shared script** (append-only, eight concurrent builders). Fix it
  in your own head: adjudicate every timing claim on an exact `select='eq(n\,N)'` decode, which is
  what this build's paperwork does throughout. STANDARD's VERIFICATION RULE should arguably be
  sharpened to say the decode must be addressed BY FRAME INDEX, never by a sampler's label.

- **A render that predates its generator's last edit is UNPROVEN until you bind it to pixels — an
  "it was comments-only" note is a claim by the party it exonerates.** The encode here was written
  at 21:45; the generator was re-run at 22:14. Both diffing the generator against itself (it is
  deterministic — re-running reproduced both index.html files and the geometry dump byte-identical)
  and re-running Gate 1 clean prove things about the PAGE, and nothing at all about the MP4. The
  cheap decisive test (`gen/verify_revolut_binding.py`, ~90s): load the same 4K page the renderer
  loaded, seek the paused timeline to frame n/FPS, screenshot the visual zone, compare to the
  decoded frame n. Read three statistics, because a small mean alone can hide a moved element:
  mean |delta| (1.32-3.00 here — h264 noise, higher on the dark section), the fraction of pixels
  past a structural threshold (worst 0.2312%) and Pearson r (worst 0.9938). That converts "trust
  me" into evidence and saves a 4K re-render that would also have orphaned a Gate 3 verdict already
  bound to those bytes. Generalise: **whenever output mtime < generator mtime, bind or re-render.**

- **The mouth-openness adjudicator failed again, on a different take — and this time the bilabial
  fallback failed too.** Corroborating the earlier bearded-subject entry, but worse: across THREE
  lip windows (270x130, 460x300, 700x500) and FOUR openness metrics (dark-pixel fraction, dark
  mass, window std, vertical-gradient energy) every peak correlation sat between r=0.076 and
  r=0.218 and the peak lags actively disagreed — +2, -6, -7, +7 frames. The bilabial strips
  scattered the same way here: 'bank' +33ms, 'perks' 0ms, 'because' -67ms, 'more' +167ms. The
  mechanism is not just beard texture: on a 20s clip the head walks the mouth out of any FIXED
  box, so the window stops measuring openness partway through. **When both direct estimators are
  noise, the chain is the instrument, and it is a strong one**: raw carries start_time 0.000000 on
  both streams -> the cut applies a single `-ss` BEFORE `-i` (which seeks both streams together)
  -> cut master video-minus-audio delta 0.000s -> render places audio at lag 0 (r=0.9796) and video
  at lag 0 (r=0.9995) against that cut. Report a failed instrument as failed and keep its artifact
  (`_mouthsync_revolut.json`, in_sync:false) rather than quietly deleting it or mining its argmax.

- **The AUDIO MIX LAW is a margin law, so the STATISTIC you pick is part of the claim.** Builder 1
  reported 27.88 dB by comparing speech **p90** against pause **p05** — loudest speech vs quietest
  pause, the most flattering pair available. Like-for-like medians on the same shipped mix give
  16.93 dB, and 20.24 dB once you exclude the pause windows containing SFX tails (the section-bound
  whoosh/pop fire in speech gaps BY DESIGN, so they belong in the exclusion, not in the floor).
  Both describe a compliant mix at bed=0.065; only one of them would survive a reviewer repeating
  the measurement. Fleet context measured identically, all authoring the bed at 0.065: revolut
  20.24 dB, airtable 12.33, buzzteams 10.41, selfoptimize 8.70 — the constant is not the whole
  story, room tone is, exactly as the law says. **Publish the pair you used.**

- **A new take-detection shape: the FULLY STABLE OPENING, where minimality is vacuous in BOTH
  directions.** All eight attempts speak the identical opening sentence, so the key `your bank`
  fires 8 times, the bare token `bank` fires 8 times at exactly opening+1, and the 7-token
  `your bank is now giving you free` still covers all 8 — contraction and extension both decide
  identically, and both were asserted rather than one being assumed. What actually decided the take
  was the sign-off: `next one` fires **exactly once** in 192 words, so only ONE attempt is complete
  and the last-complete rule and the only-complete rule coincide on word 117 (t=62.500, 75 words).
  Two traps in this raw worth carrying forward: (1) there are **zero punctuated 'No.' markers** and
  the 5 discard markers are **ELLIPSIS truncations** ('free...', 'giving...', 'just...'), so a
  marker test written as `endswith("-")` finds NOTHING and silently demotes the marker rule to
  useless — test `^no[.,!?]$ OR trailing hyphen OR trailing ellipsis`; (2) the gap rule is
  threshold-fragile in the now-familiar way, answering the correct word 117 at >=1.0s but the
  ABANDONED seventh attempt's word 107 at >=1.5s, >=2.0s AND >=2.5s. Three thresholds agreeing with
  each other and being wrong together is exactly why the gap rule is a bound, never a decider.

## Run 8 — vendorlock / KINETIC (2026-08-17, Opus 5 builder, a RESUMED pass)

The first build in the ledger to inherit a run folder mid-flight, and the run's first
short whose worst defect was a correct logo. Genuinely new lessons only.

- [provenance] **A RENDER IS A CLAIM ABOUT A FILE, AND THE CLAIM EXPIRES SILENTLY.** This
  pass inherited a project that had been rendered at 22:12 and REGENERATED at 22:26 —
  timestamps that say everything and prove nothing, because a generator re-run can be a
  no-op. The instrument that settles it is cheap and should be standard on every resumed
  build: screenshot the PAUSED 1080 timeline at N timestamps, decode the 4K encode at the
  same timestamps, and diff. Every beat came back at encode noise (mean|d| 1.03-2.75)
  except b5, which read **10.1 / 17.0 / 17.9 / 18.1 / 16.8 / 17.1** across 29.2-42.5s with
  6.4-14.8% of pixels differing by >40. A whole section had been redesigned under a render
  that four verification files were still quoting. **Never trust an encode you did not
  launch; diff it against the project before you measure anything from it.**
- [provenance] **The face video is the confound that makes the whole-frame version of that
  test useless.** Run naively over full frames it reported 4.4-17.5 EVERYWHERE, because the
  bottom half is a `<video>` whose playhead a paused screenshot does not reproduce. Cropping
  to the encode scan's own band (1610/3840) both excludes the face and reuses a band the
  factory already trusts. The first pass of an instrument is where its artifacts live: a
  detector that fires on every sample is measuring itself.
- [law2][assets] **NO GATE CAN SEE THAT A CORRECT LOGO IS THE WRONG LOGO.** The dock shipped
  `automation/hermes-agent.png` — the right file for the right tool, correctly coloured,
  correctly sized, inside its card with margin, 0.286x downscale. Gate 1 measures boxes,
  Gate 2 reads 512px thumbnails, Gate 3 saw a logo where a logo belonged. All three passed
  it. The defect is that Miguel's standing rule says **Hermes = the Nous girl, never the H**
  ("nobody recognises the H glyph"), and the only detector for that class is a builder
  reading the operator's own rules against the build. Asset checks belong in the same pass
  as law checks.
- [assets] **Two files of the same artwork are not two options — measure the ALPHA before
  choosing.** `nous-girl.png` and `nous-girl-line.png` are the same mascot; the first is
  **99.93% opaque** (a white box with a black rule = plate-on-plate on a cream machine) and
  the second is the transparent cutout (52.34% ink, ONE colour, aspect 0.968). One line of
  numpy separates a shippable mark from a defect, and the airtable rule generalises: run
  asset health as a MEASUREMENT (ink fraction, opacity, distinct colours, bbox aspect), and
  run it on the CANDIDATE, not only on the incumbent.
- [law12][law17] **A brand's own mascot is a brand mark, not a coded figure.** The Nous girl
  has a drawn face and so does OpenClaw's crab. Law 17 governs figures the GENERATOR draws
  (the heygen class); law 12 governs marks a brand publishes. Reading law 17 as a ban on
  third-party mascots would have shipped the unrecognisable glyph the operator explicitly
  rejected. Likewise "ONE colour" is only a monochrome reduction if the original had more:
  Nous draw this mascot as black line art, so the cutout IS the original palette.
- [design][law2] **When a story names N tools and only M have marks, the constraint is the
  ROW, not the marks.** The plan had ruled all four open-source marks out because a row of
  four where one carries a text pill breaks FILL THE SHAPE — sound reasoning about a
  layout that was never built. ONE DOCK whose occupant changes dissolves it: the three
  honest marks have aspect ratios **0.97 : 1.09 : 5.57**, which cannot share a row of
  square seats but share one seat sequentially without trouble, and the tool with no
  published mark simply never takes the seat. Render 1's four anonymous slots had already
  earned the Gate 3 finding "Hermes Agent is mentioned without displaying its logo" —
  **four slots promise four identities and deliver none; one seat promises one at a time.**
- [verify] **An absence has to be ASSERTED on pixels, or a reviewer reads it as an
  oversight.** The a3 cue ("PyAgents") deliberately carries no visual event. Rather than
  leave that as a silence, it is measured: across **35.65-36.85s the visual zone is
  bit-identical at every 50ms step — 25 consecutive samples at 0 changed px** — while the
  caption band moves twice (35.70, 36.55). That single scan simultaneously resolved the
  Gate-2 pop-in marker at 36.67 as CAPTION-ONLY and turned a design ruling into a fact.
  **Deliberate inertness is a claim; claims get probed.**
- [gate2][verify] **A marker adjudicator inherited across a redesign measures a band that no
  longer exists.** The b5 probes still pointed at "four 28du slots" from render 1 and were
  reporting terracotta counts for furniture that had been deleted. Retargeting them onto the
  dock's TWO channels — the border (a real 0.28s tint: 0 -> 3011 -> 6314 -> 6432) and the
  occupant (an instant `tl.set`: 0 -> 11896 between 32.74 and 32.82) — is what made the
  marker legible at all. The probe-box rule has a version for resumed work: **a probe box
  must be exclusive to the thing it measures AND must still exist.**
- [gate2] **Third sighting of the thumbnail-clock class, and this time it fooled the
  builder's eye rather than the clock.** On a 290px contact-sheet tile the OpenClaw crab and
  the OpenCode wordmark are the same smudge, and the frame captioned "OpenClaw, OpenCode,"
  read as OpenCode. The decode is unambiguous: red-channel count inside the dock is **321
  (Nous line art) -> 12,037 (33.95-34.70, the crab) -> 321 with ink rising to 13,818 (34.80+,
  the grey wordmark)**. A contact sheet is for finding questions; only a decode answers one.
- [docs] **Documentation that disagrees with the artifact is a defect, and it comes in
  pairs.** The redesign had left the plan's b5 ruling AND the generator's own `sec5`
  docstring describing four tokens and marks "ruled out" — two files confidently describing
  a build that no longer existed, either of which a clerk would have cited as a false claim.
  The rule the livetranslation clerk taught about cleanup ("write the claim after the
  thing") extends to design: **when a beat is redesigned, its plan row and its docstring
  are part of the beat.**
- [audio] **The run-8 quiet-session finding, independently reproduced.** With bed at the
  legal 0.065 the shipped mix measures speech -18.83 dBFS against a pause floor of -35.03
  dBFS = a **16.21 dB margin**, under the 18 dB standard — because this cut is -25.5 dB
  mean where run-7 sits near -19.2 dB. The bed adds 0.2 dB to the mix's overall mean, i.e.
  the constant is correctly applied and the voice is simply quieter. Shipped unmodified:
  the AUDIO MIX LAW is explicit that the constant is not a free parameter, and a hand-set
  0.16 is already in this ledger as a violation. Recorded as one more data point for the
  single batch-wide remix decision, not as a builder judgement call.
- [vendorlock_kinetic] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 1893 frames, 63.104s container /
  63.07 authored, 178,289,884 bytes, 56 captions, 8 sections, 158 ids, 69 tween targets, 2
  `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 0 pathLength paths, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 arrowheads, 0 svg
  scale tweens, 1 declared `data-name` exemption (HOSTAGE), 1 declared law-6 REPEAT_OK pair (the
  sentence-boundary "tools. Tools", a NEW stutter class — personalapps' discriminator only protects
  a trailing comma); take detection on a 594-word raw with ONE script family and 18 openings keyed
  on the minimal 2-token stem `claude is` (contraction `claude` collides in-take at words 434/436,
  extension to the full spoken line MISSES the self-truncated restart at 361 — pinned from both
  ends), the marker rule an EQUALITY (last marker 397 'H-', take opens 398, 1.22s clearance, 1
  punctuated "No." + 6 truncations, 0 in-take), the gap rule THRESHOLD-FRAGILE and decisive at no
  threshold (decision-equality at >=1.0s, abandoned attempts at >=1.5s and >=2.0s, largest gap
  10.02s sitting 226 words from the winner); head measured on a 10ms envelope 0.22s inside true
  silence with Scribe 0ms late, tail by the trailing-silence rule; the cut kept ALL 196 spoken
  words; Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings on all three rounds** (inherited project, post-fix, and a
  ship-time re-run against the exact html that rendered); 63 full-resolution stills x2 rounds plus
  a 631-sample dual-threshold PIXEL sweep (ink>13 min 1.658%, ink>34 min 1.472%, 0 under 1%, 0
  blank) run before either render; Gate 2 **62 distinct states from 189 samples**, 127 collapsed, 0
  idle candidates, 0 stillness markers, **all 9 pop-in markers resolved on exact decodes** (two
  proven CAPTION-ONLY on a bit-identical visual zone); encode sweep **0 of 1893 frames under 1% ink,
  0 blank**, min 1.3691%, median 8.8226%, min max-channel deviation 154; THE CROSSING counted rather
  than asserted (their ghost runs 6->5->4->2->0->0 as your solid runs 0->1->2->4->6->6 on six
  decodes); the meter complete at 291.73du measured against 292.0du authored; the model socket's
  three occupants classified by hue on decodes; caption band pill-free on exactly 11 frames, 6
  before the first word at 0.199s and 5 after the last pill; REAL tweet **3.467s measured from pure
  white**, contiguous, first-party asserted, zero metrics, no badge; 9 colour marks, nothing
  upscaled (largest 0.9141x), the dock's three occupants verified inside their card on native-4K
  crops; the outro underline 281.1du authored against a 281.33du measured word span; sync **lag 0 on
  both streams** (audio r=0.9761 at 1ms, video r=0.9998 at 1 frame) re-verified against THIS encode,
  0.000s cut-master delta, NO remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual / 0 semantic / 0
  minor** (1 Gemini call); **1 render this pass**, bought by the stale-encode finding and by nothing
  else. Full record: shorts_run8/paperwork/vendorlock_kinetic.json.

## Run 8 — skillssh / COUNTER (2026-08-17, Opus 5 completion pass over an Opus fleet build)

The build shipped from one session — three gates green, staged, paperwork filed. This session
finished it after the first clerk's RE-verification died on a Fable session limit
(`gen/_clerk_skillssh_pass2.json`, `api_error_status 429`). Record:
`shorts_run8/paperwork/skillssh_counter.json`, completion_pass section. Five lessons are new,
and the first is a hole in how this factory proves anything.

- **A GENERATOR RE-RUN AFTER THE RENDER SILENTLY VOIDS EVERY GATE, AND NOTHING ON DISK SAYS SO.**
  Here the mtimes read: Gate-1 report **22:00:41**, shipped mp4 **22:05:34**, Gate-3 verdict
  **22:09:09**, clerk pass 1 **22:21:24**, and then `index.html` **22:21:57** — the generator was
  re-run 33 seconds after the clerk's verdict landed, rewriting both project copies 16 minutes
  after the render. Every gate on disk certified a file that no longer existed in that form, and
  nothing flagged it: Gate 1's report does not record the hash of what it audited, and the
  paperwork happily cited both. The tempting defences are both worthless — mtimes cannot say
  whether a re-run changed a painted pixel, and "the generator is deterministic" proves
  `html == generator`, never `html == encode`. **The only thing that settles it is paint-vs-decode:**
  seek the CURRENT html in headless Chromium at time t, decode the encode's frame at t, compare
  the visual zone on a coarse grid (`gen/verify_skillssh_html_matches_render.py`). 24 probes here
  ran 1.15-3.20 mean units against a noise floor of ~1.2 — no pixel changed, no re-render needed.
  Any builder who edits a generator after rendering owes this check or a re-render; run 8's
  revolut and vendorlock lanes hit the same class independently on the same day (vendorlock's
  stale render was real and got replaced), so this is now three of eight in one run.

- **A CORRESPONDENCE CHECK WITHOUT A NEGATIVE CONTROL IS A RUBBER STAMP — AND HELD BEATS CANNOT
  DISCRIMINATE TIMING AT ALL.** Before trusting "everything matches", compare the html at t
  against the encode at t+delta and confirm the metric blows up. It did in moving beats (mean
  11.0 at +2.0s vs 1.18 aligned) — but the control also exposed the instrument's blind side: in a
  HELD beat a time offset is not a difference, so the outro scored *identically* at t and t+1.0s.
  State agreement therefore never proves timing agreement, which matters when the render history
  claims a re-time ("outro books 0.22s earlier"). The fix is to sweep the MOVING windows
  frame-by-frame and check that the aligned comparison is the minimum: across four windows it was,
  decisively where the picture moves (outro books aligned max 3.27 vs 1-frame-shift max 34.13).
  Also expect exactly one false spike per hard cut — 47.7 at t=42.683 with neighbours at 1.40 and
  3.27, caused by the verifier's own `t >= start - 0.01` visibility epsilon disagreeing with the
  renderer's boundary rule by one frame. Profile the cut frame by frame before believing it.

- **CONTACT-SHEET PANELS ARE NOT A CENTRING INSTRUMENT — I nearly filed a Law-19 violation that
  did not exist.** Reading the Gate-2 sheets, b7 looked exactly like the mcphidden defect: a lone
  channel sitting left of centre for ~3s before its partner arrived. Measured on decoded frames by
  column mass, the channel sits at **exactly 288.00du — 0.00 off-axis — for the entire 3.2s wait**,
  starts moving at 37.067s (0.113s before "upskill"), and the settled pair's midpoint returns to
  288.00du. What fooled me was thumbnail panel geometry: a 380px panel edge is not the composition
  axis, and the eye happily reads a centred element as off-centre when the frame around it is
  cropped differently per cell. This is precisely what the VERIFICATION RULE is for — decode the
  frame, measure the ink. Sheets are for *finding candidates*, never for adjudicating geometry.

- **Gate 2's 16x16-gray dedup can swallow an ENTIRE logo beat.** The manifest kept no frame between
  3.33s and 5.67s — exactly the window where "for Claude or ChatGPT" is spoken and both brand marks
  are on screen. Two small plates on a large cream field do not move a 16x16 signature, so a Law-2
  and Law-12 beat appeared in **zero** kept frames and would have shipped unseen by Gate 2. Decoding
  3.9/4.3/4.9/5.4/5.6s directly showed both marks present and fully chromatic, with the solo Claude
  mark centred before ChatGPT displaces it. Consequence: **stop writing "read every distinct state"
  in paperwork** — the gate delivers every state it KEPT. When a short's logo beat is small-area,
  check it out of band; the manifest will not tell you it is missing.

- **Paperwork sequencing trap: the cleanup claim and the manifest claim cannot both be measured.**
  `cleanup.gate2_frames_dir_exists` is only honest AFTER the frames are deleted; the frame-review
  header and pop-in count can only be read WHILE they exist. The first assembly chose cleanup, so it
  published `popin_markers: 0` — a zero that reads as a finding of zero — while the same file's
  `marker_adjudication` listed all 13. Fix is a snapshot: parse the manifest into
  `gen/_gate2_skillssh.json` while it lives, delete, then assemble from the snapshot. (Watch the
  regex too: `^- t=` matches the frame rows as well as the marker rows and gave 70 = 13 + 57.)

Cross-model FABLE clerk, pass 3, told to attack the completion pass hardest: **58 checks,
paperwork_ok, 0 material, 3 cosmetic** — and all three were worth fixing rather than arguing.
(1) The Gate-1 re-run note went stale the moment the re-run overwrote `report.json`. (2) The
law-19 lead was published as 0.08s off a 0.1s sampling grid; the clerk's frame-resolution
re-measure said 0.113s, the instrument was re-cut to 1/30s and now reproduces the clerk exactly —
**a coarse grid rounding in the build's own favour is the failure direction that matters**, even
when the guard passes either way. (3) Correspondence maxima are sample-bound, not global; the clerk
probed 20 times this build never sampled and found 5.734% where I reported a 5.544% max. Two
independent probe sets agreeing is strong, but it is not a per-frame proof, and the paperwork now
says so. Independently reproduced by both of us: output probe + sha256 (run copy == staged copy),
every build-guard count re-parsed from the html, the audio mix constants (voice 1 / bed 0.065 x2 /
sfx 0.18 x9) with the bed cleared by HASH not filename, take detection (177 raw words, 0 discard
markers, 0 gaps >= 1.0s, the raw->tight diff being exactly two spelled-out numbers), captions ==
tight transcript verbatim, card text byte-exact from the payload's entity offsets with no badge and
no metrics, and audio placement at lag 0 (r=0.9747, identical top-lag structure).

## Run 8 — geministt / KINETIC addendum: the clerk cycle (2026-08-17, Opus 5 builder)

THREE adversarial clerk passes on one short's paperwork, four material findings and
nine cosmetic ones across them, and **not one of them touched the encode** — every
material finding was a sentence, never a frame. Four lessons that generalise beyond this build.

- [paperwork][clerk] **A robustness range measured on one instrument's grid cannot be
  transplanted onto another's.** Clerk pass 1 wrote that "any threshold between ~1,500 and
  ~40,000 ON MY GRID gives the identical answer". The builder lifted that range into the
  paperwork as if it described the ENCODE verifier's 270x201 grid — where the card's own
  printed peak is 13,857, so the top of the quoted "safe" band returns an EMPTY window. Pass 2
  caught it; the builder's own sweep caught it in parallel. A number a clerk hands you is
  evidence about the CLERK's instrument, not yours. Re-derive it on your own grid before it
  enters the record.
- [paperwork] **When a claim's NUMBER is stable and its JUSTIFICATION keeps breaking, stop
  rewriting the justification and publish the sweep.** The real-tweet screen time (3.567s,
  frames 56-162, contiguous) survived three drafts and was reproduced independently three
  times; what failed twice was the prose explaining WHY the metric works — first "the card is
  the only pure-white surface" (false: the ChatGPT knot is 60,099 px of #fff), then the
  transplanted threshold range. The fix that ended it was publishing the sweep itself: max
  count OUTSIDE the window (614), min INSIDE (11,518), the comparison operator (strict `>`),
  and therefore the exact integer band (615..11,517), both ends checked. A measured interval
  cannot be re-refuted; a remembered pair of round numbers can.
- [paperwork][guards] **An inventory sentence needs the same derivation discipline as a
  measurement, and counting its own items is part of that.** The guard-lineage line was
  repaired once (after "byte-for-byte" was refuted for six guards) and the REPLACEMENT then
  said "FOUR are new" while listing FIVE items, one of them a `guard_row_seats` that does not
  exist — `row_seats()` is a plain helper. The instrument that settles it is four lines of
  Python: extract every top-level `def guard_*` body, diff against each parent, print the three
  buckets. Run it and paste the output; do not type the inventory from memory, and do not type
  a count that disagrees with the list right next to it. The same class produced
  `law15_moved_states: 19` against a geometry dump that records 16 and a generator with exactly
  16 non-loop `.moved(` call sites.
- [paperwork][tense] **"N clerk passes" written while pass N is still running is the cleanup
  lie in a new costume.** The ledger and the CLAIMS row both said "TWO clerk passes" while the
  second pass was mid-flight, and pass 2 flagged it — the same rule ("write the claim AFTER the
  fact") that the same build had already broken once on `scratch_deleted`. Any sentence whose
  truth depends on a process you started and have not read is a forecast; hold it until the
  process returns. The corollary that made this build finishable: a builder that dies mid-clerk
  leaves paperwork in exactly this state, and the cheap way to re-establish trust before
  touching a word of it is the HASH TRIPLE (output == staged == claimed) plus one free gate
  re-run — if none of those move, only prose and cleanup can be wrong.


## 2026-08-17 — run 8, inkling / Icon Choreography (completing builder, Opus 5)

Chain finished from a hand-off: builder 1 took it all the way through Gate 3 and staging, then
its session died at the clerk step (the clerk file held the harness's session-limit line, not a
verdict). The completion pass re-derived everything before running the clerk, then ran a
cross-model Fable 5 clerk. Both instruments found real defects, and every one of them was in the
same place.

- **Every number a GUARD computes reproduced exactly; every defect lived in prose no guard
  touches.** Re-derived independently of the build scripts: Gate 1 0/0, Gate 2 32 states / 98
  samples / 66 collapsed / 7 markers, 108 unique ids, 44 tween targets, 977 frames, sha256 output
  == staged, the take-detection indices, the dead-frame scan to four decimals, the bespoke-scene
  ink counts at full precision. Not one moved. All four discrepancies the two instruments found
  were hand-written sentences: an SFX count (filed 4, page carries 5), a "widest use" that named
  the second-widest, a "clean silence" span that had a transient in it, and "the take names the
  company four more times" when three of those four hits are in abandoned attempts. **The audit
  surface is the prose, not the pipeline.** When filing, mark every sentence a guard cannot prove
  and re-measure exactly those — that set is small and it is where 100% of the errors were.

- **A no-upscale assert can guard a NON-MAXIMAL use, and the constant will never tell you.** The
  generator derives `MARK_WIDEST` from one card's geometry (`LAB_W - 2*LAB_PAD` = 164du -> 615
  physical px at 4K), so the staging assert proved the b2 lab-card header was a downscale and
  nothing else. The same wordmark ships three times, and the b0 hook plate sizes it by HEIGHT with
  `width:auto` — it never passes through the width constant at all, and it renders **705 px**
  (0.2689x), not 615 (0.2346x). Measured by decoding the shipped 4K encode at each plate's own
  authored rect and taking the wordmark's dark-ink bbox. The verdict survives (0.269 << 1.0) but
  the filed number named the wrong use. Two instruments found this from opposite directions — the
  builder by grepping every `<img src>` in the page, the clerk by resolving the CSS of an
  absolutely-positioned replaced element. **Derive "widest use" from the rendered INK of EVERY
  use, never from a layout constant that only one of them flows through**; any `width:auto` or
  `height`-driven lockup is invisible to the constant by construction.

- **A "clean silence" claim is a claim about a WINDOW — state it on the window the decision
  actually rests on, not on the comfortable span around it.** The first filing measured
  94.49-95.92 and called it clean at max 0.00008 RMS. It is not: a 0.00956-RMS transient sits at
  94.96-94.98, ~120x that figure and 16x the one blip the filing did report — a 25ms event a
  coarse envelope steps straight over. But the head choice never depended on that 1.4s span. What
  it rests on is **95.97-96.06**, which measures max 0.00005, with the sustained onset at 96.21
  and Scribe's word start 30ms EARLY at 96.18. Restated on the narrow window, the ruling is
  stronger, shorter, and has nowhere for a missed transient to hide — and it still kills the
  sibling `scribe-0.22` formula (95.96), which would have opened on the 95.93-95.96 blip. **The
  wide window buys nothing the narrow one doesn't, and it is exactly where the falsification
  lives.**

- **MIXED marker morphology is more dangerous than uniform morphology.** The revolut entry logged
  that `endswith("-")` finds NOTHING on an all-ellipsis raw. This raw is the worse case: 7 markers
  split 3 dash truncations (`laun--`, `l--`, `s--`) and 4 ellipsis trail-offs (`brother...`,
  `the...`, `is...`, `the...`). A dash-only test returns **3 of 7** — a plausible non-zero answer
  that silently understates the marker rule's standing while looking like it worked. A zero result
  gets investigated; a wrong-but-reasonable result gets believed. Test
  `^no[.,!?]$ OR trailing hyphen OR trailing ellipsis` and assert the COUNT, which is what
  `build_cut_inkling.py` does (`EXPECTED_MARKERS_BEFORE = 7`).

- **When the cross-model clerk is rate-limited, the ccx/Codex lane is a BETTER fallback than the
  builder's own model.** Fable 5 returned "You've reached your Fable 5 limit" on pass 2. Falling
  back to Opus would have made the clerk same-model as the builder and forfeited the whole point
  of the two-key rule; `ccx sol -p` keeps the audit genuinely cross-family and is
  subscription-covered. Note the ccx lane prints an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY takes precedence` warning
  and needs `< /dev/null` or a stdin wait — neither is fatal, both look alarming in a log.

- **The AUDIO MIX LAW's constant and its measurement disagreed on this batch, and the builder must
  not resolve that alone.** Shipped at exactly 0.065 as the law binds, and measured: bed median
  -15.02 dBFS, voice median -26.91, bed-in-mix -38.76, margin **11.85 dB** — not the ~18 dB the
  constant is meant to buy. The clerk called this a law violation. It is a BATCH property, not a
  per-video one: the 2026-08-17 recordings run ~5 dB quieter than run 7 (-26.91 vs a run-7
  median-of-medians of -19.76), and siblings authoring the same 0.065 measured 20.24 / 12.33 /
  10.41 / 8.70 dB. Re-tuning one short would break the constant AND make its music quieter than
  its seven batchmates. The law itself records a hand-set 0.16 putting a builder in the ledger, so
  "measure, then escalate, then ship the constant" is the only move available to a builder;
  **a gain change on a whole recording day is Miguel's call, not a builder's.**

### inkling addendum — the clerk cycle (renders 2 -> 3, 2026-08-18)

- **A guard that tests ATOMS can be defeated by splitting the thing you are hiding across
  two atoms — and the split can be innocent.** The hook printed the LAW 9 key term as two
  one-token divs, `INKLING` and `SMALL`, stacked to rhyme with the brand's own two-line
  wordmark. The caption-identity guard compares each div's token set against the pill's, so
  neither atom ever equalled the pill `Inkling Small.` — while the screen plainly read both
  at once for 0.54s. A textbook double caption, in the beat that opens the video, and it
  cleared Gate 1, Gate 2, Gate 3 and a builder's own frame review. **A double caption is a
  property of what the EYE ASSEMBLES, not of one element**, so the identity test now also
  sweeps the UNION of every group of 2 and 3 atoms in a section against each pill. Proven
  against the old page before shipping: per-atom returns False, union returns True on
  exactly (`inkling`,`small`). Generalise to every "no element may equal X" guard in the
  factory — ask what happens when the offending content is authored as two elements.

- **The declared SPLIT is the missing half of the declared GLUE.** GLUE (join two chunks)
  was the factory's only tool for the LAW 9 vs LAW 4 collision, and on this raw it was the
  wrong one: merging cap0+cap1 makes a 46-char pill at the 19du font floor, and **no pill in
  run 7 or run 8 is under 24.8du or over 34 chars** — the fix would have traded LAW 4 for
  LAW 8. Breaking one token EARLIER cost nothing at all: `Thinking Machines just` /
  `launched Inkling Small.` both land at the 30du cap and the other 28 pills come out
  byte-identical. `SPLIT_AFTER` ships with the same discipline as GLUE — a written reason
  and an asserted hit count — and takes priority over every other chunk rule. **When a pill
  collides with a key term, you can move the boundary in EITHER direction; check the font
  cost of both before reaching for glue.**

- **Fix the CITED files, not just the paperwork.** Pass 1 falsified two numbers; the builder
  corrected them in `paperwork/inkling_icon.json` and pass 2 found both still alive in the
  files that paperwork points readers to — the retired `164du / 615px / 0.234x` in
  `plans/asset_verdict_inkling.json`, and `94.49-95.92 is clean silence (max 0.00008)` in
  `cuts/inkling/edl.json`, in `build_cut_inkling.py`'s docstring, AND in the code that
  writes the edl record. Four sites for one wrong sentence, because a build serialises its
  reasoning into every artifact it touches. **After correcting a measured claim, grep the
  whole run tree for the retired string** — a correction that stops at the paperwork just
  moves the falsehood somewhere a reviewer is more likely to believe it.

- **Pick the fallback clerk for INDEPENDENCE, not availability.** Fable 5 hit its limit
  mid-cycle and the ccx/Codex lane 429'd at the same moment, so pass 2 ran on Opus — the
  builder's own model. It still worked (it found the LAW 4 defect the cross-model pass had
  missed), but the pass is labelled same-model in the paperwork rather than quietly counted
  as cross-model. Pass 3 went back to ccx/Sol once the lane recovered. **Three passes on
  three different footings found three different classes of defect** — cross-model Fable
  caught the measurement errors, same-model Opus caught the law violation, and the
  disagreement between them is the actual product of the two-key rule.

- **A Gemini PASS is not evidence of compliance.** Gate 3 passed the render-2 encode with 0
  errors and 0 minor notes on both layers, including its own double-caption detector, on a
  short carrying a verbatim double caption in its opening beat. The free gates and the paid
  gate all missed it; a reader with the law in hand found it in one frame. Judge noise cuts
  both ways, exactly as the run-6 verdict says — **a green gate is a floor, never a proof.**

- **A RE-RENDER invalidates every measured number in the paperwork, not just the hash and
  the size.** After render 3 the builder updated `output.sha256`, size, render count and the
  b1 ring counts — and clerk pass 3 still found `staged.sha256_matches_output` holding render
  2's hash (the one machine-readable field asserting staging integrity, disagreeing with the
  `output` block three keys away) and the whole `frame_review.marker_resolutions` block still
  quoting render-2 pixel counts, while `gen/_render_inkling.json` had already been
  regenerated with the correct render-3 values sitting right there. **The re-verification
  scripts refresh themselves; the prose does not.** After a re-render, diff the paperwork
  against every `_*.json` record the build writes and treat any number that disagrees as
  stale — do not re-read only the fields you remember touching.

- **`ffmpeg -ac 1 -f f32le` is NOT a faithful stereo downmix, and it will manufacture an
  audio-law violation.** Clerk pass 3 filed the bed at -12.01 dBFS (margin 8.84 dB) against
  the filed -15.02 and called the AUDIO MIX LAW violated on that basis. Sample-exact
  refutation: RMS of `(L+R)/2` in numpy = 0.191457, RMS of `-ac 1 -f s16le` = 0.191457
  (ratio 1.0000), RMS of `-ac 1 -f f32le` = 0.270762 — **ratio 1.41421, exactly +3.0103 dB,
  the missing 0.5 factor** — and the float path's peak sample is **1.267**, above full scale,
  which no honest downmix can produce. ffmpeg normalises the downmix matrix when the output
  is an integer format and does not when it is float. The bed's channels are 0.9836
  correlated and its left channel alone medians -15.37 dBFS, which corroborates -15.02 and
  excludes -12.01. Two lessons: **decode audio to s16le (or do the arithmetic yourself) for
  any level measurement**, and **DECLARE the convention next to every dB figure you file** —
  this challenge only existed because the block carried numbers with no stated instrument,
  in a file that had just added a `blip_peak_rms_convention` field for exactly that reason.

- **Three clerk passes on three footings found three disjoint classes of defect.**
  Cross-model Fable (pass 1) found the measurement errors. Same-model Opus (pass 2) found the
  LAW 4 violation that had cleared all three gates. A third pass (pass 3) found the
  re-render's own fallout plus one false positive worth refuting. No pass found what the
  previous one found, and the builder's own sweep between passes found two more sites neither
  clerk named. **The two-key rule's product is the disagreement, not the sign-off** — and a
  pass that returns `paperwork_ok:false` on prose while confirming the encode is sound is the
  system working, not failing.

- **The AUDIO MIX LAW's "18+ dB margin" had no pinned instrument, so it failed shorts Miguel
  had already approved and published.** Run-8 clerks filed AUDIO-MIX failures on six of eight
  videos at 15.9-17.4 dB against a >=18 dB reading of the law, every one of them authored at
  the mandated `data-volume="0.065"`. Running the SAME estimator (mono 16 kHz s16le decode,
  frame RMS, p85 minus p15) over the thirteen **approved and published** run-7 finals settles
  it: at 33 ms frames run 7 spans **15.85 to 23.70 dB, median 18.29** — five of thirteen sit
  under 18, and the lowest (appsdistrib 15.85) shipped to Miguel's channel with no remark.
  Run 8 spans **15.90 to 17.73, median 17.11**. The batch is inside the approved band, in its
  lower half, missing only run 7's loud outliers (chatgptphone 23.70, doers 22.01) because
  tonight's takes are quieter and more uniform. The margin is also strongly frame-size
  dependent — the same file reads 18.03 at 10 ms, 16.88 at 33 ms and 14.33 at 100 ms — so a
  bare dB figure with no stated frame size decides nothing. **Never file an audio-law verdict
  against an unpinned threshold: measure the approved corpus with the identical instrument
  first, and report the candidate's position in that distribution.** Two consequences worth
  keeping: a clerk finding that would condemn already-shipped work is evidence against the
  metric, not against the build; and a batch that lands at the bottom of the approved band is
  a judgement call for Miguel's ears (inkling 15.90 and selfoptimize 16.10 are the two closest
  to the floor), not a defect a builder should silently "fix" by moving the constant.

- **One eight-builder Opus fleet exhausted three model lanes in five hours.** Round 1 lost six
  of eight builders to the Claude session window at 22:05-22:37 (all six had already rendered;
  the kill landed during paperwork), the resume lost four Fable clerks to a 429 and then the
  Fable daily limit, and the ccx/Sol fallback returned `429 usage limit reached` on both
  replacement clerks. Grok was the fourth lane and the one that ran. Renders and gates are
  cheap in tokens; **multi-pass self-verification is what drains a window**, and eight of them
  in parallel drains three. Four concurrent builders would have finished inside one window.


## mcpupgrade / Icon (run 8, round 2) — 2026-08-19

- **Five inherited "measurements" in one build measured the wrong thing, and every one of
  them would have PASSED.** A dead session left a verifier whose numbers all looked
  plausible. In fact: the b1 wash probe spanned y=0..seam and so counted the caption chip,
  reading 157415 terra BEFORE the cue against 131909 after — backwards, and it would have
  "verified" the short's only annotation while watching captions. The Law-19 b4 probe was
  `du_box(l_x - solo_dx, ...)` = x **-300px**; a negative numpy start slices from the RIGHT
  edge, so it returned ink 0 at every sample and a centroid at -214.6px, off the raster, and
  nothing complained. The mark table point-sampled Notion at t=15.60 when "Notion" is spoken
  at 15.62 and recorded ink 4612 — which is the measured EMPTY-SLOT plateau (4614-4616), so
  a LAW 2 logo claim was one point-sample from shipping unverified. METERS COMPLETE compared
  a STADIUM fill's area to its RECTANGLE probe (89.2%) and would call a complete fill
  partial. The bank's "centering" used an INK centroid (-38.85du) on a row whose left half
  holds dense colour logos and right half a flat wash. **A probe that returns a number is not
  a probe that answers the question. Before believing any measurement, ask what else is
  inside the box, and check the probe against a case whose answer you already know.**

- **The wash needed THREE instruments before it measured the annotation, each failing for a
  different reason.** Box too big (caught the caption chip) -> white-bbox detection (caption
  TEXT is white, so the bbox stretched back to the seam) -> terra difference (the @ClaudeDevs
  avatar is a red pixel mascot holding a constant 4117 terra px inside the card). What
  finally worked: find the card body as the contiguous run of rows with >40% white coverage,
  then isolate the annotation as a **pixel difference against a settled pre-cue frame**. The
  deeper finding: **the terra hue rule is not a highlight detector.** This wash measures mean
  R-G of 27.5 against the rule's R-G>35, because a highlight is a pale blush and the caption
  pill is saturated terra. A hue rule calibrated on one element silently returns ~0 for
  another. Final read: 0 changed px at all five settled pre-cue samples, 126285 px settled
  across two bands from 4.40s.

- **A one-frame binding failure is a CLOCK question before it is a document question.** The
  paint-vs-decode sweep bound 215 of 216 comparisons and failed exactly one — f403, where a
  caption swap and the b2 app-row displacement land together — at struct 2.04% / r 0.851
  against a 0.18% noise floor. Two probes settled it without a re-render. First, cross-match:
  paint(403) best-matches **decode(404)** at 0.1811%, i.e. better than its own index, while
  paints 404-409 each match their own. Second, the decisive one: sweep sub-frame seek times
  and ask whether the page can paint encode frame 403 **at all**. It can, at **-3.92 ms**
  from n/fps, at 0.2008% — indistinguishable from every other frame. So the renderer samples
  frame n about 0.12 frame earlier than a naive `n/fps` seek, and that offset is invisible at
  215 frames because nothing is mid-tween and visible at the 216th because something is.
  **Add the epoch probe to the binding kit: without it the honest conclusion was "re-render",
  which would have cost an hour and invalidated every measured number in the paperwork.**

- **Ink centroid is not geometric centre, and one-sided edge detection is not an off-centre
  element.** Two Law-15/19 "misses" in this build were both instrument artefacts. The bank's
  ink centroid sat 38.85du left of the axis purely because colour logos carry more ink than a
  flat wash; its geometric extent centre is -0.13du. The b4 solo plate measured 11.87du right
  of the axis because its extent's RIGHT edge landed on the authored pixel while its LEFT
  edge came up 89px short — the plate is shadowed on one side and near-white on cream on the
  other. Measured on the plate's **dark type**, which is centred in the plate by
  construction, it reads **+0.27du**, and the displaced pair reads -129.87/+129.33du against
  an authored solo_dx of 130. **For a centering claim, measure the highest-contrast thing
  that is centred by construction, not the outline of the thing you care about.**

- **Storing probe frames at full 4K is a silent 8 GB.** The inherited encode verifier kept
  every wanted frame as 2160x3840x3 = 24.9 MB; its probe set is ~330 frames, i.e. >8 GB
  resident with three builders sharing the machine. Sweeps that only need a scalar (a
  181-frame white-pixel count, four marker ink sweeps) should be reduced INSIDE the streaming
  loop, and frames that really must be kept should be cropped to the visual zone. Same
  single-decode discipline, an order of magnitude less memory.

- **The watchdog rule, learned the expensive way twice.** Sessions 1 and 2 of this video died,
  the second because it sat in one foreground command — a full 1300-frame 4K decode — for
  over three minutes. Every long job here (render, geometry audit, ffmpeg pass, Gemini QC)
  belongs in the background with a log file and a short polling loop. Polling is not
  overhead; it is the thing that keeps the session alive to finish the work.

- **A generator whose mtime predates the render, plus byte-identical re-run output, is
  necessary and not sufficient.** mcpupgrade's generator was last touched at 12:04, the
  render started 12:05:20, and re-running it in a later session reproduced both index.html
  files byte for byte. That is a strong argument and it is still not a pixel proof — the
  proof is the 216 comparisons. Keep the determinism check as the cheap pre-filter that tells
  you the pixel proof is worth running, never as its replacement.

## Run 8 — brainsdontmatter / COUNTER (2026-08-19, Opus 5, a RESUMED build finished from a hand-off)

Builder 1 reached one 4K render and stopped; this session re-derived the intake, proved the
inherited encode rather than re-rendering it, ran all three gates and every measurement, and
shipped. Three gates green, ONE render, zero re-renders. Record:
`shorts_run8/paperwork/brainsdontmatter_counter.json`. The genuinely new lessons are all about
INSTRUMENTS, and three of them are my own instruments being wrong.

- [verify][probe-box] **THREE probe boxes in one build were not exclusive to what they measured,
  and every one of them produced a plausible wrong number rather than an obvious failure.** (1) A
  caption-band box at y=1725..2400 keyed on "terracotta" as `R-G>40 and R-B>40` reported
  **0 pill-free frames** — because that band is mostly the FACE plate and skin is red-dominant.
  The exclusive box (y=1620..1720: cream ground above the seam, below the composition's YMAX and
  above the face plate) reports **3, all before the first word at 0.079s**. (2) The b6 ring was
  measured INSIDE the rows rect and read **0 px at every probe** — the ring is drawn AROUND that
  rect, so none of its ink was ever in the box; an absent-looking annotation that is actually
  present. (3) The b8 ring was measured in a box containing the PERFORMANCE bar it encircles and
  read **232,686 px BEFORE its own cue** — the bar, not the ring. Re-measured on ANNULI (outer
  minus inner), both rings read 0 before the cue and ~43k/~45k after. **Rule: for an annotation,
  the exclusive probe is the annulus, never the target's rect — and a probe that reads zero and a
  probe that reads huge are the same bug wearing different clothes.**

- [verify][colour] **A colour tolerance of 30 is not a neutral choice: it can sit ONE unit away
  from a colour you did not intend to catch.** The b2 "where is the greyed fader now" measurement
  read a centroid of **199.44du** against an authored left-seat centre of 172.00 — a 27du error
  that looks exactly like a real centring defect. Cause: the two EMPTY sibling channels border at
  `rgba(20,20,22,0.28)` over cream = **(183,179,175)**, whose Chebyshev distance to the greyed
  fill (164,156,144) is **31** — one unit outside tol 30, so h264 noise leaks it in and drags the
  centroid toward the axis. At tol<=8, and on the strong-column run at every tolerance, the answer
  is **[138.13, 206.13], centre 172.13du**. Two habits fall out: compute the distance from your
  target colour to every OTHER colour in the box before picking a tolerance, and prefer a
  **structural** estimator (the widest contiguous run of columns carrying >30% of the element's
  height) over a centroid — the run was correct at all four tolerances while the centroid was
  wrong at three of them.

- [law4] **A LAW-4 candidate is settled by the approved CORPUS, not by the builder's nerve.** The
  tightest label-vs-pill overlap here is typeset `NOT INFINITE` against the pill `is not infinite,`
  — a SUBSET (one extra function word), co-visible 0.48s. Post-inkling that reads alarming, and
  the temptation is either to ship it quietly or to re-cut a clean beat. Neither is necessary:
  sweeping every (caption, live-atom) pair across the run-7/run-8 geometry dumps that carry both
  tables shows the identical shape in **skillssh_counter — approved, clerked by two cross-model
  clerks, staged** — as `TWO WORLDS` vs `the two worlds.`, co-visible for **1.60s, 3.3x longer**.
  The inkling defect was EQUALITY of what the eye assembles; a subset is structural, because LAW 9
  requires the key term on screen in his own words. **Same discipline as the audio law: measure the
  approved corpus with your own instrument before filing, and report the candidate's position in
  that distribution rather than against a remembered threshold.**

- [audio] **The pinned instrument reproduces STANDARD's band exactly, which is what makes it usable
  as a reference.** Measuring all thirteen approved run-7 finals with mono 16 kHz s16le / 33 ms
  frame RMS / p85-p15 returned **n=13, min 15.85, max 23.70, median 18.29** — identical to the
  numbers STANDARD.md pins. That agreement is the point: it licenses the comparison. This mix reads
  **17.76 dB at 33 ms** (19.43 at 10 ms, 14.43 at 100 ms), inside the band and above five published
  finals, so no audio finding is filed. **Before quoting the pinned band, re-derive it; a reference
  you have not reproduced is a remembered number.**

- [provenance] **The binding test needs a GROSS control, not only a one-frame control, when the
  build's motion is slow.** This short's picture moves in small increments (a fader climbing a few
  px per frame), so the per-sweep discrimination between aligned and +1-frame is only 0.26-0.54
  mean units — technically correct, rhetorically weak, and one sweep (the outro, largely held)
  separates by just **0.032**. What actually establishes dynamic range is the ±2.0s control:
  **1.362 aligned against 11.579 and 9.901**, an ~8x spread. Report both, and say plainly which
  windows cannot discriminate timing — a held beat never can, and pretending otherwise is how a
  rubber stamp gets written into paperwork.

- [gate2] **Second and third sighting of the dedup swallowing a whole beat, in ONE video.** Gate 2
  kept no frame in 22.84-23.42 (the three labelled faders, the b2 payoff) and none in 44.58-45.56
  (the ChatGPT mark). Both are small-area changes on a large cream field that never move a
  16x16 signature. Both were decoded out of band by frame index and both were correct — but a
  builder who wrote "read every distinct state" would have shipped a LAW-2/LAW-12 beat and the
  bespoke scene's own payoff frame unseen. **Derive the out-of-band list from the AUTHORED event
  table (every mark cue, every label fade, every terminal state) and diff it against the manifest's
  kept times; do not wait to notice a gap.**

- [brainsdontmatter_counter] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 2000 frames, 66.666667s
  container / 66.640 authored, 189,025,921 bytes, 61 captions, 10 sections, 192 ids, 108 pure-id
  tween targets (112 selectors incl. 4 class targets — both counts published so neither reads as a
  discrepancy), 4 `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 `text-decoration`,
  0 repeat/yoyo/ease-none, 29 typeset atoms, 531 caption-identity unions with 0 collisions, ZERO
  numerals in the visual zone as an EQUALITY (he states no number in 227 words but "two", which
  ships as two objects); take detection on a 571-word TWO-FAMILY raw decided by a sign-off that
  fires EXACTLY ONCE (`next one`, w570) so last-complete == only-complete at w344, the opening key
  the 2-token `brains don't` with minimality pinned BOTH ways (the 1-token contraction fires 14
  times and one hit is IN-BODY inside a LOSING attempt — a new disqualifier shape; the extension
  resolves to the identical 11 indices), the marker rule a LOWER BOUND with UNIFORMLY ELLIPSIS
  morphology (7 markers, 0 punctuated "No.", 0 dash truncations — an `endswith("-")` test returns
  zero here), the gap rule bound-only and threshold-fragile in the worst direction (right at >=1.0s,
  and four thresholds agreeing on a wrong w313); head on a 10 ms envelope with the decisive window
  stated as the 120 ms it rests on (222.40-222.52, max RMS 0.008937) and Scribe 20 ms late; the cut
  kept all 227 words with 5 tokens differing from the raw pass — 3 punctuation/case, 2 word-form —
  all of them Scribe re-rendering the SAME audio, and captions == the tight transcript verbatim;
  Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings, re-run at ship time against the exact shipped html**; Gate 2
  **61 distinct states from 200 samples**, 139 collapsed, 22 markers all resolved (8 section cuts,
  10 progressive, 4 proven CAPTION-ONLY at ink_zone_changed_px [0,0,0,0]), 0 idle candidates,
  longest stillness 3.4s at 1.21 mean abs diff; encode sweep **0 of 2000 frames under 1% ink at
  BOTH thresholds, 0 blank**, min 3.4493% / 2.6159%, median 14.828% / 8.9958%, min max-channel
  deviation 192; caption band pill-free on exactly 3 frames, all before the first word at 0.079s;
  REAL TWEET **3.500s measured from pixels**, frames 319-423, contiguous, with the threshold's safe
  band published (3,520..138,526 — max outside 3,519 against min inside 138,527, a 39x separation)
  and **zero metrics drawn from a payload carrying all six**; 2 colour marks, both downscales
  (0.4922x, 0.3076x), the ChatGPT knot verified chromatic on a native-4K decode; THE DESK measured

  0.10s AHEAD of its siblings to a measured 172.13du against an authored 172.00, the master

  0.065 with the bed cleared by HASH not filename, margin 17.76 dB (33 ms, pinned instrument);
  sync **lag 0 on both streams** (audio r=0.9791 at 1 ms, video r=0.9996 at 1 frame) on a mouth
  window re-derived and eyeballed for this framing, 0.000s cut-master delta, NO remux; Gate 3
  **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual / 0 semantic**; **ONE render, zero re-renders** — the
