## Run 8 — hermesbuzz / KINETIC (2026-08-19, Opus 5, the run's third resumed build)

The run's last short, inherited twice-dead (a network drop, then the harness watchdog), and
the only one of the three round-2 videos that arrived with NO encode on disk. Genuinely new
lessons only.

- [provenance] **A BYTE-IDENTICAL REGENERATION is the cheapest binding proof there is, and it
  is available before the render rather than after.** The two sibling resumptions this round
  had to prove an inherited mp4 was pixel-bound to an html they did not write (216 paint-vs-
  decode comparisons on mcpupgrade; frame-by-frame sweeps on skillssh). hermesbuzz had no
  encode, so the question inverted: is the PROJECT the generator's output? Re-running
  `hermesbuzz_kinetic_gen.py` returned both index.html files byte-identical
  (md5 `cd8497d9…` 1080, `c6fc9fa1…` 4K), which settles in 25 seconds what a decode sweep
  settles in twenty minutes. **On any resumed build, regenerate BEFORE you gate: if the html
  changes, every inherited measurement is void; if it does not, the inherited Gate-1 record is
  about the document you are going to render.** The expensive proof is only needed when an
  encode already exists.
- [law13] **When a story is about two products JOINING, the peak must not be about the
  RELATIONSHIP between the actors — make the accumulator the GROUND they stand on.** The
  neighbouring buzzteams shipped THE CONVERGENCE the same night on the same subject (plates
  riding inward into a triangle, drawing peer links between themselves). THE EXCHANGE inverts
  every axis: nothing moves after it lands, no node is ever joined to another node, and the
  only travelling object is a pulse in a lane BENEATH the actors, whose arrival advances a
  single track by exactly the fraction of total distance it covered — 148 + 148 + 296 of 592du,
  so the meter reads 0.25 / 0.50 / **1.0000** and completes on the word "work". *What they made
  is literally the distance they talked.* The transferable primitive: **a linear accumulator
  under a static row is a completely different picture from links between the row's members,
  and it is the one available when the actors must not move.**
- [law16][verify] **THE RECEIPT — a round trip is a claim about COVERAGE, and coverage is
  countable.** The trip order 0→1→2→0 addresses targets 1, 2, 0, i.e. every agent exactly once,
  so "they talk to each other" is not decoration but an enumeration. Asserted at build time
  (`sorted(receipts) == [t0,t1,t2]`) and then measured on the encode by plate mean luminance:
  47.11/52.05/49.30 at rest → t1 74.54 → t2 72.49 → t0 70.80, each lighting exactly once and
  none un-lighting. The three baselines differ (by 5 luma) only because the depth bars differ
  by design, which is why a THRESHOLD would have been the wrong instrument and a per-plate
  before/after comparison is the right one.
- [design] **Two bar vocabularies is the ceiling; a third collapses them.** The agent token
  already carries a grey name row (identity) and a terracotta depth row (hand one's
  specialism). Adding a third terracotta bar as the receipt made the plate unreadable on the
  contact sheet — three horizontal bars in two colours stop being a taxonomy and become
  texture. The fix was to move the receipt to a DIFFERENT channel entirely: the plate's own
  background lights. **When a surface is out of bar slots, light the surface.**
- [gate2][verify] **A ±0.30s adjudication window is blind to an event that ENDS inside it.**
  Five of six pop-in markers resolved instantly (three CAPTION-ONLY on a bit-quiet visual zone,
  two section cuts). The sixth, t=3.67, read `[416, 28, 0, 0, 0, 0]` — a decaying tail with no
  ramp, which under the usual rule looks like "one step then still". It is the last 0.1s of a
  0.34s wipe that opened at 3.24, i.e. the window started too late, not the entrance too fast.
  **When the marker's changed-px sequence is monotonically DECAYING from its first pair, widen
  backwards before concluding anything: you are looking at an ending, not a beginning.**
- [verify] **A detector that fires on the page itself is measuring the page.** The first tweet
  screen-time probe used "all channels > 225" as "white card", and this build's CREAM ground is
  (246,241,234) — every channel over 225. It reported the card present from 2.60s while b2 does
  not begin until 2.96. The correction is one threshold (>248) plus one CONTROL sample on a
  cream frame (446 px against a 92,705 px peak). Same class, same night, second instance: the
  caption probe cropped y=1840 while the pill straddles the seam at y=1725 and duly reported
  all 917 frames pill-free. **Every band probe needs a positive control and a negative control,
  and "the answer is 100%" is a bug report.**
- [assets] **The transparency of a cutout has to be verified in the RENDER, not only in the
  file.** `nous-girl-line.png` measures 43.6% fully opaque / 47.7% near-transparent with four
  transparent corners — the vendorlock alpha rule, correctly applied. But on the contact sheet
  the mark still *looked* like it carried a faint plate. Sampling the still settled it: inside
  the mark's bounding box the ground reads (246,241,234), bit-equal to the page ground 25px
  away. **File alpha proves the asset; a pixel sample proves the composite.**
- [law19][escalation] **The chassis's own outro is a literal law-19 miss, and it is in the
  approved corpus.** The outro pre-positions the whole four-element lockup (FOLLOW / FOR DAILY
  AI / underline / chip) centred as a unit and displaces it once when the miniature arrives —
  but only FOLLOW is painted for the first 0.80s, so the beat's opening element sits **300.5px
  above the axis waiting for items that have not appeared yet**, which is the mcphidden defect
  Law 19 was written for. Measured on decodes: ink rows 418..586, centre 502.0px against an
  802.5px axis, settling to −19.5px by 28.6s. The identical numbers come off
  `vendorlock_kinetic.mp4` (418..586, centre 502.0) — a short that shipped with a cross-model
  clerk PASS and zero discrepancies, and geministt and the other run-8 Kinetics share the same
  outro. Escalated to Miguel as a CHASSIS-level question rather than fixed: either law 19 does
  not reach inside a single composed outro lockup, or every Kinetic outro needs re-choreography,
  and neither is a decision one builder should take inside one video. Note which detector found
  it — not a gate (Gate 1 does not test law 19, Gate 2's 3fps sampling collapsed all 0.80s into
  one state, Gate 3 was clean) but a builder reading the operator's own law against a decoded
  frame, the same detector class that caught the Hermes H glyph.
- [audio] **The pinned instrument turned the batch's recurring "violation" into a non-event,
  which is what pinning is for.** 16.107 dB (mono 16 kHz s16le, 33 ms frame, p85−p15) against
  an approved run-7 band of 15.85–23.70 — inside it, and the whole run-8 corpus now measures
  15.899–17.759 on the same instrument. The voice-only control is the useful new number: the
  cut alone reads 29.465 dB, and adding the bed at the mandated 0.065 moves speech by 0.17 dB
  while lifting the floor 13.5 dB. **The margin is set by the bed exactly as designed; the
  constant is doing its job and the recordings are simply quiet.** Frame-size sensitivity on
  this same file: 17.513 at 10 ms, 16.107 at 33 ms, 13.689 at 100 ms — 3.8 dB of spread from
  the frame size alone, which is why STANDARD pins it.
- [sync] **A sibling's mouth crop is a starting point, and this raw proved why.** The
  vendorlock window (380x220 at 800,1090) lost the mouth entirely by t=20s because his head
  drifts upward mid-take; widening to 420x420 at (870,1060) and re-checking at t=3/12/20/28s
  before use gave lag 0 at r=0.9996. Checking the window at FOUR times rather than two is the
  cheap version of this lesson.
- [hermesbuzz_kinetic] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 917 frames, 30.570667s container /
  30.56 authored, 88,470,034 bytes, sha256 `b5d5e0d5…`, 29 captions, 7 sections, 98 ids, 78 tween
  calls, 1 `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 0 svg, 0 non-scaling-stroke, 1 declared `data-name`
  exemption (BOTH WORLDS, protected by a declared backward GLUE so the pill can never be
  token-identical to it); take detection on a 735-word raw with ONE script family and 19 openings
  keyed on the minimal 3-token stem `you can now` (`you` collides in-take six times, `you can`
  over-counts two mid-sentence fragments, `you can now connect` drops four restarts), sign-off
  firing EXACTLY ONCE at word 729 so the winner is the only complete take, the marker rule an
  EQUALITY (last marker 633, take opens 634, zero punctuated "No."), the gap rule agreeing at all
  five thresholds and used as agreement only; head at the END of a 1.860s sub-threshold run
  (278.280–280.140, max 0.00334) with 73 body-noise windows in the preceding 10.5s proving the
  head could not go earlier, Scribe 0 ms late; the cut kept all 100 spoken words in 30.564s;
  Gate 1 **0 errors / 0 warnings on both rounds**; 64 full-resolution 1080 stills before the
  render, one per held state plus one each side of every travelling pulse; Gate 2 **38 distinct
  states from 92 samples**, 54 collapsed, 0 idle candidates, all 6 markers resolved on exact
  decodes; encode sweep **0 of 917 frames under 1% ink, 0 blank**, min 3.1344%, median 9.5730%;
  caption band pill-free on exactly 9 frames, 8 before the first word at 0.259s and 1 after the
  last at 30.399s; REAL tweet **3.08s measured** from pure white with a cream control, contiguous,
  first-party through a two-deep quote chain, zero metrics; 2 colour marks, nothing upscaled
  (largest 0.8789x); the b1 connector clear of both marks' ink by 85px / 32px on a decode; the
  outro underline 1054px against 1054px of measured word ink; sync **lag 0 on both streams**
  (audio r=0.9701 at 1 ms, video r=0.9996 at 1 frame), 0.000s cut-master delta, NO remux; Gate 3
  **pass on the FIRST call, 0 visual / 0 semantic / 0 minor** (1 Gemini call); **1 render, 0
  re-renders**. One escalation open (the law-19 outro, above). Full record:
  shorts_run8/paperwork/hermesbuzz_kinetic.json.

- **A brand PNG can carry an invisible plate: `nous-girl-line.png` is 43.25% alpha=1 and only 2.84%
  alpha=0.** hermesbuzz's paperwork asserted twice, with pixel values, that the Nous cutout leaves no
  plate — "inside the mark's bounding box the ground reads (246,241,234), bit-equal to the page
  ground". The clerk measured (245,240,233) inside vs (246,241,234) outside on the builder's own
  still, and (243,239,231) vs (245,240,233) on the shipped encode, over a 456x450 rectangle whose
  boundary is one pixel sharp and NOT macroblock-aligned — so not codec ringing. The cause is a
  near-transparent black wash across the asset's full file box: alpha=1 is not alpha=0. Impact is
  ~0.8% luminance, at the visibility threshold, so it does not warrant a re-render — but it is real,
  it invalidated the stated reason for preferring this file over `nous-girl.png`, and **it hides from
  the usual check: vendorlock's cross-model PASS missed it because that build places the mark small
  inside a white plate where the wash cannot show.** Fix at the registry level (threshold the alpha),
  and when a mark sits directly on page ground, sample INSIDE vs OUTSIDE its box rather than trusting
  the file to be a clean cutout. The builder's own eye caught this on the contact sheet and a wrong
  measurement talked it down — when the eye and the number disagree, re-measure, do not overrule.

- **Paperwork can assert guards that do not exist in the generator.** mcpupgrade filed
  `build_guards.law19_asserts` naming three derived displacements — `AI_SOLO_DX`, `APP_SOLO_DX`,
  `AUD_SOLO_DX`. None of those three identifiers appears anywhere in the generator; only `B4_SOLO_DX`
  is real. The same file described b2 choreography (two marks opening centred, then displaced by a
  derived dx) that the encode disproves — at t=8.50 both seats are already dashed at final positions
  and nothing ever moves; the generator's own docstring states the true, law-compliant mechanism.
  **The video was clean in both cases: the defect was purely in the description.** Two rules follow.
  A guard is only real if its identifier `grep`s in the generator — assert the grep, not the memory.
  And a paperwork claim about MOTION must be verified against decoded frames from the window it
  describes, because a claim can be more law-abiding than the build and still be false.

- **Three motion metrics, three false condemnations: the "static opening" remark is not measurable
  as motion.** Miguel rejected brainsdontmatter's opening ("two gauges not doing anything for like
  5-10 seconds"). The obvious response is a motion gate. Measured against all 23 approved shorts,
  every candidate instrument condemned work he had praised: mean frame motion over the first 5s put
  the candidate lowest of 24 but only 3.7 units under an approved short; VISUAL-ZONE motion over the
  first 10s rated doers (1.84) and harness (1.98) BELOW the candidate (2.84); longest inert
  visual-zone run rated harness (4.2s) and gpttranscribe (5.2s) WORSE than the candidate (3.8s). A
  per-element "parked" rule fails hardest of all: harness's right-hand dashed slot sits unchanged for
  **5.2s**, longer than the dead performance bar that drew the complaint. **The Law-13 named
  reference — the build Miguel called "fucking amazing" — is objectively stiller than the build he
  rejected, by every instrument tried.** The real distinction is WHAT THE FRAME CONTAINS: harness's
  still moments show a completed structure (marks, connectors, a drawn tree); brainsdontmatter's show
  an empty gauge and an unfilled bar, i.e. a vessel waiting to be filled, which reads as "not started
  yet". Hence Law 20 is scoped to the opening and phrased compositionally, with an explicit ban on
  converting it to a threshold. General rule, third time this session: **before turning a taste
  remark into a gate, run the proposed instrument over the APPROVED corpus. If it fires on work the
  reviewer has praised, the instrument is wrong — not the work.** (Same failure shape as the >=18 dB
  audio threshold that condemned five published shorts.)

- **A "missing" logo can be the real logo.** Miguel: "having the inkling icon (i don't even know if
  it exists) instead of the black block would have been nice." Thinking Machines Lab's actual mark IS
  a black rounded square — pulled from their own `apple-touch-icon.png` — and the Inkling model has
  NO icon of its own, only a wordmark (verified on the model card and launch post). The build was not
  missing an asset. What made it read as a placeholder is that the size metaphor used sharp-cornered
  black squares, which collide visually with the brand's rounded-square mark. **When a mark reads as
  a placeholder, check the brand's real identity before "fixing" it — and avoid geometry that mimics
  a brand's mark for a different purpose in the same frame.**

## Run 8 — brainsdontmatter / LAW 20 FIX PASS (2026-08-19, Opus 5)

One remark, one beat, one re-render. Genuinely new lessons only — the "don't turn a taste
remark into a motion threshold" lesson is already logged above and is not repeated.

- [instruments] **A frame-DIFFERENCE probe cannot see an empty vessel; it can only see one
  appear.** The review reported that the dead PERFORMANCE bar "first paints at 1.2s". It
  didn't: the trough was on screen at FRAME 0 and 1.2s was merely its `settle` scale tween
  finally producing enough pixel delta to register. Adding an INK-COVERAGE column to the same
  per-region instrument exposed it immediately — coverage 0.6253 in the 0-1s bin, before any
  measurable motion. Law 20 asks two questions a diff cannot answer: **is the vessel PRESENT,
  and how FULL is it.** So the deciding instrument is a presence+fill probe on 4K frames by
  index (`gen/probe_law20_state_brainsdontmatter.py`), and the diff probe is kept only for
  continuity with the review's own numbers. Generalises: when the defect is *what the frame
  contains*, measure content (coverage, fill fraction, presence), never change.

- [law 20, as a buildable shape] **"Withhold the vessel" is only honest if the reveal and the
  first fill are the SAME instant** — otherwise you have simply moved the empty trough later
  and made it shorter. Authored as a guard rather than a habit: the generator greps its own
  emitted timeline and fails the build unless `tl.set("#b0-mf",{opacity:1},T)` and the first
  `tl.to("#b0-mf-f",…,T)` carry the same T. Its twin guard forbids any tween on `#b0-fi*`, so
  the opening fader must OPEN pegged rather than climb to pegged. Both are the b8 payoff
  guard's shape reused: state the absence you are relying on, then make it unauthorable.

- [story] **Opening on the maxed state made the argument better, not just the frame.** The old
  hook climbed the intelligence dial at 5.6s, which spent the reveal's ammunition early: by b2
  the audience had already watched that dial move. Pegging it from frame 0 turns b2 into "the
  dial has been at the ceiling this whole time, and PERFORMANCE walks away from it anyway" —
  the same pixels, a stronger claim. When a law forces you to state something as a STATE rather
  than illustrate it as an EVENT, check whether the event was stealing from a later beat.

- [geometry] **A solo element parked for a law-19 ride can collide with the very element whose
  arrival releases it.** The b0 pair is centred as a two-item stack, which parks it 46.71du
  BELOW its final seat — 16.71du inside the master meter's own rect. Solved by leading the ride
  0.14s ahead of the master's `pop` (still within law 19's "caused by the arrival" window), so
  the pair has travelled 68% of the way out before the trough is opaque. Gate 1 sweeps at 0.5s
  and would have caught it; the cheap fix is a lead, not a redesign.

- [probe boxes, third instance on this video] The first law-20 master probe used the meter's
  full authored rect and reported it **15.4% full before it existed** — it was reading the
  parked fader's foot. **A probe box must be exclusive against every PARKED position too, not
  just against final seats.**

## Run 8 — brainsdontmatter / LAW 13 REBUILD OF THE HOOK (2026-08-19, Opus 5, fix pass 3)

Two passes were spent on the wrong law. Logged because the failure mode is procedural, not
visual, and it will recur.

- [the big one] **A taste remark names a SYMPTOM; do not let the law you write from it become
  the whole diagnosis.** Miguel's first note was "the opening is very static — two gauges not
  doing anything for like 5-10 seconds." That produced Law 20 (never open on an empty vessel),
  which is a true and useful law — and pass 2 satisfied it exactly: the fader opened pegged,
  the trough was withheld and arrived filling, every number was measured green, all three gates
  passed. He rejected it in one line: *"It sucks so bad. Why don't we have some unique
  visualization with a brain or something?"* The actual defect was **LAW 13** the whole time.
  A short called `brainsdontmatter`, whose first spoken word is "Brains", opened on generic
  chassis furniture. **When a reviewer rejects the same beat twice, stop refining compliance
  and re-ask what the beat is FOR.** Compliance is falsifiable; ambition is not, and only one
  of them was missing.

- [law 13, operationally] **"Bespoke visualization" means an OBJECT, not a compliant frame.**
  The reliable test is whether a stranger could name the thing on screen in one word. "A brain"
  passes; "a gauge" does not, no matter how correctly it behaves. Every Law-13 named reference
  in STANDARD is a nameable object — the ocean, the balance scale, the constellation, the desk.

- [method] **Draw the object in a throwaway harness and LOOK at it before it enters the
  generator.** Three drafts, three headless screenshots, ~4 minutes total: draft 1 read as a
  brain but flat-bottomed; draft 2 read as a CLOUD; draft 3 added the full-length central
  fissure and a stem and became unmistakable. Committing draft 1 or 2 into the generator would
  have cost a 4K render (~9 min) to discover the same thing. **A cheap visual loop outside the
  build is worth more than any amount of careful blind authoring.**

- [svg] **A self-imposed "this build codes no X" guard is a liability the moment the design
  needs X.** The audit here banned svg outright with the honest note that an unclassed-svg
  guard "would be a lie." The right move was not to work around it in divs but to convert the
  ban into an EQUALITY — exactly one svg, and it must be the brain wrapper — so a second one
  cannot arrive later and inherit the exemption. Ban → equality is the general upgrade.

- [svg, concrete] **`stroke-dasharray="100"` on a `pathLength="100"` path does NOT hide it.**
  The single value means [100 on, 100 off], so at offset 100 the path paints nothing except
  its ROUND CAPS at positions 0 and 100 — which render as little dots scattered over the
  object. Caught on the frame-0 still, not by any gate. Fix: a gap far longer than the dash
  (`"100 400"`) leaves exactly one dash, and parking the offset a few units PAST the dash
  length pushes its caps off the path entirely; tweening to 0 still finishes fully drawn.

- [law 19] **A rigid-body ride is not always available, and faking one is worse than declaring
  two parks.** When the element between two atoms CHANGES SIZE, the solo composition and the
  final composition cannot both be centred with a single shared delta — the algebra only closes
  at scale 1.0. Here the brain's centre travels 40.71du and the word above it travels 71.31du,
  because the brain is growing. Declared as two parks in PARKS and asserted; the differing
  speeds read as the composition making room, which is what the beat is about.

- [probe boxes, again] The brain is measured as terracotta AREA, so its effective scale is
  `sqrt(area / area_at_ceiling)` — which reproduced all four authored steps within 0.002. Note
  the frame-0 reading comes out HIGHER than the settled one (0.7011 vs 0.6574) because the
  cream gyri have not yet been cut out of the solid mass. **An area probe measures the object
  MINUS whatever is subtracted from it; know which state you are comparing against.**

- **A hook made of chassis furniture reads as "nothing happening", no matter how you pose it.**
  brainsdontmatter took TWO fix passes on the same remark. Pass 1 read the complaint as "don't open
  on an empty gauge" and satisfied it precisely: the INTELLIGENCE fader opened PEGGED at its ceiling
  from frame 0, the PERFORMANCE trough was withheld until the beat that filled it, all three gates
  went green first call, and a clerk confirmed by ink measurement that no empty vessel was ever
  parked. Miguel's verdict on that render: *"It sucks so bad. Why don't we have some unique
  visualization with a brain or something? ... no dynamism whatsoever."* The miss was a missing
  SUBJECT, not a missing state. A gauge is furniture whether it is empty, pegged, or climbing; the
  hook needs the video's idea as an OBJECT, built to Law 13 standard. Pass 2 shipped a
  two-hemisphere brain that draws its folds on the opening line then grows in four word-synced steps
  with the meter answering each growth 0.18s late — 13 events in 9 seconds, dead seconds down from 4
  to 1. **Procedural lesson: when a remark is about how something FEELS, the first fix attempt
  usually addresses the measurable proxy rather than the thing itself.** The proxy here (empty
  vessel) was real, checkable, and insufficient. Before shipping a taste fix, ask whether the change
  would still be praised if the measurable defect were the ONLY thing wrong — if the answer is "it
  would merely stop being bad", it is not a fix.

- **A remark sent to a subagent never reaches the main session.** Miguel replied directly to the
  running builder ("fix this again please"), believing he was talking to the orchestrator. The main
  session kept reporting pass 1 as verified and complete while the builder was already rebuilding
  around a brain, and the staged file silently became a THIRD render with no Gate 3, no paperwork and
  no clerk record — while the main session was telling Miguel the staged file had PASSED. **When a
  builder's report references feedback the orchestrator never sent, treat every downstream claim as
  suspect and re-derive the staged state from disk before reporting anything.** Cheap detector: hash
  the staged file against the paperwork before every status report.


## 2026-08-20 — hermessubagents / DIAGRAM (run 8, Opus 5 builder, round 3)

- **A verifier that RETYPES a design constant reports on a line the design does not have.** The
  geometry dump carried `"rail_y": round(L3_Y + LL_PAD + 172.0, 2)` — the literal 172.0 copied out
  of the lane spec. A later fix moved the rail to local y=176.0 to make room for a status row, the
  dump was not touched because nothing in it looked wrong, and the encode verifier dutifully scanned
  a horizontal line **4du above the rail** and reported **METERS COMPLETE = 0.0 on three rails that
  were visually full**. The bug is not the number, it is the RETYPING: `spec_large(...)["rail"][0]`
  cannot go stale. Rule promoted: **anything a probe measures must be DERIVED from the same
  expression the build draws from, never re-entered.** (doers already said this about design
  constants; this is the same rule for the geometry DUMP, which is the layer probes read.)

- **A probe time inside a running tween is a probe of nothing.** The Law-20 hook probe sampled the
  shutter at t=1.20 and t=1.75 and compared each reading to a step's END value. Both times sat
  INSIDE the tween (step 1 runs 0.96-1.26, step 3 starts 1.84 with a 0.035 stagger), so the readings
  disagreed with the authored values and looked like a build defect. **Derive probe times from the
  authored tween windows, not from round numbers** — and state the window next to the reading, so
  the next reader can see the sample is in a hold rather than in flight.

- **A crop that cannot contain the thing it measures reports 0.0% and looks like a pass.** A
  "peak dynamism" probe cropped `h * 460 / 1920` = 920px of a 3840px frame (245du) instead of the
  1725px visual zone, i.e. it looked entirely ABOVE the status rows and the rails, and returned
  **0.0% change across a window in which three checks, three carets and three rails all move**. A
  zero from a probe is only evidence when the probe's own field of view has been shown to include
  the elements in question. Cheap detector: run the probe across a window you KNOW changes and
  assert it is non-zero before trusting a zero anywhere else.

- **Gate 2's 16x16 dedup cannot resolve anything under ~half a cell, and that is a design signal,
  not just an instrument limit.** The first render collapsed **15.7s-20.0s into one state** — the
  emotional peak of the short — because the only moving things there were three 16du status pips,
  three checks inside them, three 5x18du carets and three rail fills, together about **1.2% of the
  visual zone's area**. The dedup was right that nothing much was happening. Rebuilding the beat as
  a STATUS ROW (a 26du pip beside a 78du bar going terracotta, plus a 3% growth per card) added a
  distinct state immediately. **Treat a long dedup collapse over a beat you consider important as a
  question about the beat's SIZE, not only about the instrument** — then measure the pixels to
  decide, and measure the same window shape on approved work before calling it a defect (Law 20:
  a metric that condemns shipped work is wrong about the metric). Here: candidate peak steps
  0.66-1.02% of the zone changing by >60 levels, against approved buzzteams' own 0.13-1.97%.

- **The pre-render still sweep at 0.2s steps cannot see a one-frame hole; the encode can.** Render 1
  measured **0.4789% ink at 4.467s**, its thinnest frame by a factor of three, because a term's
  fadeout finished **0.02s before** the next element's pop began. The 0.2s pre-render sweep sampled
  4.4 and 4.6 and missed it entirely. The doers rule ("overlap the dissolve with the arrival or the
  canvas empties") is not satisfied by "they are adjacent" — it needs a real overlap, and the only
  gate that can prove it is a per-frame sweep of the encode.

- **A brand PNG can be 43.6% opaque and still carry no plate — measure, do not infer either way.**
  `nous-girl-line.png` reads 43.64% alpha=255, which sounds like a fill; it is INK (a dense black
  line-art mascot). The discriminator is not the opaque fraction but (a) how many distinct colours
  the opaque pixels have — one, #000000 — and (b) what a CORNER of the file composites to over the
  page ground: (245.08, 240.10, 233.13) against cream's (246, 241, 234), a 1-level difference. Both
  checks now run inside `stage()` and raise. The mark also needed ink-true placement: its alpha bbox
  touches the file's own bottom edge and carries a 61px top margin, so a box-centred placement sits
  ~1.15% of its height low.

- **A square-cornered overlay on a round-rect needs an inset derived from the radius.** A slat at
  inset `d` over a card of corner radius `r` is only ON the card when `d >= r(1 - 1/sqrt2)` = 0.293r.
  At r=23.8du the first pass used 6.0du and the top slat's corners hung off onto the dark ground.
  The geometry audit could not see it (it measures BOXES, and the box was inside); only a
  full-resolution still could. The inset is now asserted against the lane's own `rad()`.

- **The GAP rule can be a real witness, and when it is, bound it by measurement.** Ten of the
  ledger's raws made the gap rule either degenerate (one candidate) or unbounded. On this raw,
  openings computed from silence alone at a 1.0s threshold are EXACTLY the ten content openings —
  so it corroborates rather than agrees by construction. What makes that a fact rather than a
  coincidence is the **separating band**: smallest opening gap 1.120s, largest non-opening gap
  0.620s, so any threshold in (0.620, 1.120] returns the same ten. **Report the band, not the
  threshold.**

- **An opening key can need a third token because of a TRAIL-OFF, not a collision.** `hermes` and
  `hermes agent` both fire 11 times here; the extra hit is an attempt that dies mid-sentence INSIDE
  the phrase ("...features that you have in the Hermes Agent") and then falls silent for 11.38s.
  That is a restart point, not an opening, and only the third token separates them. When asserting a
  key is minimal, say WHICH utterance the extra hit is — "it collides" is not a reason a clerk can
  check.

- **A cross-fade group authored in every beat and fired in only some is a silent Law-16 miss.** The
  lane primitive carried a `.gb` job glyph; it fired in b0, b2 and the outro and never in b1 or b3,
  so the peak rendered three identical cards while the narration claimed you could see what each one
  was doing. Nothing failed: the ids were tweened, the guards passed, the audit was green. The
  detector was reading a full-resolution still and asking "does this frame say what the sentence
  says". **Add to the pre-render pass: for every primitive with an alternate state, confirm the
  alternate is reached in every beat that draws it.**

- **Three of the same card is a repeat pattern unless its content is ragged.** Identical title-bar
  widths and identical activity-line lengths across three lanes read as wallpaper. Per-lane widths
  (ragged on purpose, the way a column of real task text is) cost nothing and are what makes three
  cards read as three different jobs.

## Run 8 — hermesvoicemagic / ICON (2026-08-20, Opus 5, round 3)

The first build authored under Law 20, so the hook object was designed before anything else.
Genuinely new lessons only.

- [svg][the big one] **An SVG viewport CLIPS a path traced on its own boundary, so half your
  stroke silently disappears — and no gate can see it.** The peak beat's sealed wall is an 8du
  terracotta stroke on a rounded-rect path whose box was authored as the bezel's own rect. It
  rendered as a **4.0du line hugging the INSIDE of the bezel**: a scanline across the left wall
  at t=22.0 reads INK `(19,19,19)` from du 0.00-3.73 and terracotta `(195,86,56)` from du
  4.00-7.73. Gate 1 was 0 errors / 0 warnings, the pre-render stills looked right, Gate 2's
  3fps sampling kept the beat and it read as a wall, and Gate 3 passed the previous render.
  The only detector was an annulus probe reading **0.4656 where ~1.0 was authored**, followed by
  a pixel scan. Fix: the viewport is the WHOLE object and the path is inset by half the widest
  stroke it will ever carry (`rrect_path(..., ox, oy)`); coverage went 0.4656 -> 0.9001 at the
  same cue. **General rule: a stroked path needs stroke/2 of viewBox margin on every side, and
  the way you find out you did not leave it is to measure the stroke's WIDTH, not its presence.**

- [anchors] **`find(phrase)` returns the start of the phrase's FIRST word, and that is invisible
  in every output the build produces.** Authoring `"using Jarvis?"` when the cue word is
  *Jarvis* fires the beat 0.22s early; the section still holds, the terminal-hold guard still
  passes, and the only symptom is that a still taken at a nominally-quiet moment already shows
  the move. Caught by probing this build's own 1080 stills for the door's x-position
  (`doorL_ink=597, doorR_ink=29555` at t=0.95, before the authored 1.02 ride). FOUR of 27
  anchors were wrong. Closed structurally with a `CUE_WORD` table that asserts the resolved
  TOKEN for every anchor and dumps `gen/_anchors_<vid>.json`. **Anchor phrases are two claims —
  where the phrase is, and which word in it you meant — and the second one is never checked
  unless you write it down.**

- [law19] **The law-19 miss you are most likely to ship is in the calm beats, not the busy
  ones.** Two beats here open on a lone brand mark and then bring in a name and a rule. Both had
  the mark pre-positioned at its final seat — a literal "pre-positioned in anticipation of items
  that have not appeared yet", the mcphidden defect, in the least dramatic section of the video.
  The fix is a derived VERTICAL park (`otop(size)`) and a ride, which is also the shape the open
  hermesbuzz outro escalation is asking for. **Sweep every beat that opens with one atom, not
  just the ones with choreography.**

- [law20, operationally] **Designing the hook FIRST changes what the rest of the video can be.**
  The door was chosen before a single beat was laid out, and it then earned four appearances
  with a MONOTONE state (0 -> 17 -> 40 -> 66 degrees, asserted strictly increasing in the
  generator and measured on the encode as light revealed 0 -> 37,326 -> 95,869 -> 198,356 px).
  A hook object that only exists in the hook is a decoration; one that advances every beat is
  the continuity the harness reference earned. **Ask what the hook object DOES at 60% through
  the video before committing to it.**

- [law20][method] **The throwaway draft sheet is worth two rounds, not one.** Sheet 1 (bell /
  door / key / speech-bubble / "machine slab") killed the chassis-furniture candidate instantly
  and picked the door. Sheet 2 was the one that mattered: the door drawn as a rounded slab with
  a flat `scaleX` open read as **a tablet closing**. Adding a THRESHOLD BAR WIDER THAN THE FRAME
  and swapping the squash for a perspective `rotateY` hinge made it unmistakable. Both sheets
  cost about four minutes against ~1 minute per 4K render plus the gate cycle. **The second
  draft round is where the object stops being a category and starts being a thing.**

- [law13] **When the claim is that something never LEAVES, do not draw the road it does not
  take.** The obvious peak for a privacy beat is an outbound lane to a provider, crossed out. An
  empty lane is a dead slot (LAW 16) and a named provider is a claim he never makes (LAW 11) —
  he says "any AI provider out there" and names nobody. So the wall CLOSES instead: one stroke
  drawing itself all the way round a machine that has a neck and a foot, and the only travelling
  object moves inward. The claim then becomes a chain of measured inequalities rather than a
  picture of a refusal: utterance right edge 288.80du < panel left 307.80 < panel right 485.96 <
  inner wall 508.00.

- [probe-box, three more instances, all in one video] The voice probe was re-cut **twice**: at
  `inr` it read 508.0du — the sealed BEZEL, i.e. the wall reported as the voice reaching the
  wall; at `inr - 6` it read 473.87du — the session panel's live DOT, which turns terracotta
  mid-beat. Third instance: the frame-0 "the door has not ridden yet" control used the whole
  final rect, which overlaps the SOLO rect by 136du, and duly reported **408,554 px of ink for a
  door that had not moved**. All three produced plausible wrong numbers rather than obvious
  failures. **The exclusive box must be exclusive against every other atom of the same COLOUR,
  not just against the target's neighbours — and against parked positions.**

- [ink-sweep] **A two-ground `min(dist_to_cream, dist_to_dark)` classifier counts a near-black
  object on a cream section as GROUND.** The first sweep reported frame 0 at **0.1977% ink** —
  a frame whose entire subject is a solid black door covering 22% of the visual zone. The hook
  object was being measured as emptiness by the very instrument meant to prove it was there.
  Ground is a property of the SECTION, so decide it by TIME (the generator now dumps
  `b4_dark_window`), never per pixel. Corrected, the same frame reads 19.37% and the sweep's
  minimum over 999 frames rises from 1.0954% to **2.1009%**.

- [scribe] **A parenthetical gloss in a keyterm leaks verbatim into Scribe's flat `text`
  field.** `"Nous Research (NOT News Research)"` repaired the mishearing in the `words` array
  correctly and then produced `"Thank you, Hermes and Nous Research (NOT News Research) yet
  again."` in `text`. Captions are built from `words`, so nothing shipped — but any audit or
  downstream consumer reading `text` sees it. Also measured: Scribe **rejects any keyword of 50+
  characters** with `400 invalid_keyword_length`, which the shared vocabulary's house style
  ("Term (gloss, NOT 'wrong')") exceeds. Keyterms are now asserted `< 50` chars and
  parenthesis-free in the generator.

- [sync] **The sibling "r=0.97 / r=0.9996" sync numbers are a render-vs-cut BINDING test, not
  lip-sync.** Read as lip-sync they are unreachable: a mouth-openness x audio-RMS correlation
  over 24 searched windows peaks here at **r=0.2933**, with lag 0 (0.2889) and lag +1 (0.2933)
  statistically indistinguishable. The test that actually adjudicates is cross-correlating the
  ENCODE against the CUT on both streams — audio envelope at 1 ms (**lag 0, r=0.9725**, with
  neighbours at 0.73) and face-band inter-frame motion at frame resolution (**lag 0, r=0.9954**,
  neighbours at 0.52). Report the weak lip-sync figure as a sanity check and say plainly which
  instrument decided.

- [gate2] **A pop-in marker can be a half-pixel TEXT RE-RASTERISATION.** The t=22.0 marker showed
  4,358 changed pixels in a frame where nothing is authored — 3,743 of them on one label's glyph
  edges. The label's ink bbox is identical across the change in y (32.533-44.533) and on its
  right edge (468.400); only the left edge crosses an antialiasing threshold by 0.267du = 0.5
  device px, with ink area 16,527 -> 16,967 (+2.7%). The file has exactly ONE keyframe (f0), so
  it is not a GOP boundary. **Before writing "unexplained", measure the element's BBOX: a
  rasterisation change moves edges, an authoring event moves boxes.**

- [audio] **A margin can fall below the approved corpus by less than a tenth of a decibel, and
  that still has to be filed.** 15.766 dB against a re-derived run-7 band of 15.85-23.697
  (median 18.287 — reproducing STANDARD's pins to three decimals, which is what licenses the
  comparison). That is 0.084 dB below the corpus minimum and 0.133 dB below run 8's next-lowest.
  The temptation is to round it into the band; STANDARD's rule is explicit that below-corpus is
  the violation line. Filed as a batch escalation with the diagnosis attached: the voice-only
  control reads 25.231 dB, so the bed at the mandated 0.065 is doing exactly what it was set to
  do and the recording is simply quiet. **The honest move on a hairline is to publish the
  hairline, not to pick the side of it you prefer.**

- [hermesvoicemagic_icon] Clean shipped record: 2160x3840, 30fps, 999 frames, 33.301333s
  container / 33.300 authored, 96,409,773 bytes, sha256 `c0a8783a…`, 32 captions, 8 sections,
  137 ids, 72 tween calls, 1 `data-overlap-ok`, 0 `data-bleed`, 2 svg (both connector/seal
  wrappers), 0 non-scaling-stroke, 0 `text-decoration`, 0 repeat/yoyo/ease-none, 24 build
  guards; take detection on a 191-word TWO-attempt raw where every cross-check is an EQUALITY —
  the opening key the 2-token `have you` with the contraction DISQUALIFIED because its stray hit
  (w84, "you simply HAVE to install") sits INSIDE the WINNING take, a new disqualifier shape
  (brainsdontmatter's sat in a LOSING one), the marker rule an equality on a single `start...`
  at w70, and the gap rule an equality across the whole band 0.8-2.26s that then ABSTAINS above
  2.5s rather than answering wrongly; the cut kept all 120 spoken words as 118 tokens with the
  numeral reconciliation stated; Gate 1 **0/0 on four runs**; 37 pre-render 1080 stills that
  found 5 defects before any render; Gate 2 **37 states / 100 samples / 63 collapsed / 0 idle
  candidates / 9 markers all resolved**; encode sweep **0 of 999 frames under 1% ink AND 0 under
  2%**, min 2.1009%, median 13.1528%, 0 blank; caption band pill-free on exactly 9 frames, 4
  before the first word at 0.119s and 5 after the last at 33.0s; REAL TWEET **3.233s measured**,
  frames 152-248, contiguous, first-party with **chain depth 0 asserted**, zero metrics from a
  payload carrying all six; 1 colour mark, the Nous girl, its alpha wash measured composited
  onto the PLATE (250.3 vs 255) and NOT onto the page (245,240,233 identical both sides);
  Law 18 underline 149.87du inside 158.13du of word ink; audio at the mandated 0.065 with one
  escalation filed; sync lag 0 on both streams, no remux; Gate 3 **pass on the FIRST call**.
  Full record: shorts_run8/paperwork/hermesvoicemagic_icon.json.

- [gate3] **Gemini QC is NON-DETERMINISTIC on identical bytes, and it can fire as well as
  miss.** Measured on the shipped `brainsdontmatter_counter.mp4` (sha256 `e1c13b47…`): three
  Gate-3 runs on the SAME file returned **pass / FAIL / pass**. The failure was one semantic
  `highlight_match` at 11.4s — the b1 ring on the tweet's claim while he names its author. That
  beat is untouched by either fix pass: render 3 vs render 2 and vs render 1 read mean |diff|
  0.128-0.139 with **~140 of 3,240,000 px** differing by >8 (0.004%, h264 residue), and the same
  pixels had already cleared Gate 3 in renders 1 and 2 — **4 passes out of 5 on one beat.** The
  known lesson was "a green gate is a floor, never a proof" (inkling); this is its mirror, and it
  creates a NEW hazard: once a gate has failed, re-running it is indistinguishable from shopping
  for the verdict you want. The discipline that fixes it is procedural, not statistical —
  **commit in writing to recording whatever the extra run returns BEFORE launching it, then
  record every run including the failure.** A gate result is now a distribution, so paperwork
  states the run count, not "Gate 3: pass".

- [paperwork] **Stale render numbers hide in PROSE, not in the fields you sweep for.** Closing
  render 3's paperwork, a token sweep for the superseded hash/size/html digests found every
  obvious field — and still left FOUR live render-2 claims behind, because they were sentences
  inside sections that looked content-stable and were carried forward wholesale:
  `bespoke_visualization.the_setup` still narrated the pegged-fader hook that no longer exists,
  `law19_start_centred` still quoted ride 4.62 / master 4.76 (render 3 authors 2.50 / 2.64),
  `law20_opening_state` still reported "measured fill 0.9387 at t=0.10" for a fader the render
  replaced with a brain, and a `unions_checked: 511` sat in a law-4 block while the guard block
  three keys away had been corrected to 519. **Sweep the file twice: once for the numbers you
  know changed, and once by re-reading every narrative key against the new render.** The cheap
  detector is a flatten-and-scan that flags any leaf carrying a superseded value whose PATH is
  not inside an explicitly-labelled retained/corrected home.

## FORMAT LAB — CLOSED (2026-09-01, six formats integrated into STANDARD.md)

Opened 2026-08-15 as an isolated workspace that was forbidden from touching the
production factory; closed 2026-09-01 when Miguel approved all seven definitive
videos. Six formats × three variants = **18 prototype renders on ONE source cut**
(`hermesinfinite`, the shipped 54.06s "infinite tools" video), so every
comparison in every round was a format comparison and never a content one. Six
review rounds later: **5 formats adopted, 1 killed, 17 global laws, 7 definitive
videos, 5 back-catalogue ports.** The lab's laws are now STANDARD.md Laws 21-36
plus the Law-20 amendment; the chassis is `formats/<name>/`.

- [format-lab][method] **Holding the CONTENT constant is what made the lab
  legible.** One transcript, one cut, one palette, one SFX family, 18 renders.
  Miguel could rank facesplit against takeover in a single sitting because the
  only variable on screen was the frame architecture. The cost is that no format
  was ever stress-tested against a transcript it did not fit — which is exactly
  what intake assignment now exists to prevent, and what the five cutout ports
  were the first real test of.

- [format-lab] **The flywheel produced its laws in a fixed shape: a taste remark
  became a MEASUREMENT, and the measurement became the constant.** "You zoom in
  way too much on my face" became a 64-frame head-position union sweep, a derived
  0% window (`crop=1216:2160:1270:0`, the widest 9:16 crop a 2160-tall master can
  physically give), a 5-level ladder, and a shipped recommendation of 5% default /
  10% ceiling backed by three independent arguments. "The head cutout is not
  stable" became a flicker instrument, a SAM2 track, and a $0.17 Modal budget per
  video. "The pen squeak is a big no" became seven normalised files at three
  measured level classes. **No law in this lab is a preference someone typed.**

- [format-lab] **Four of the six rounds were the same round: the builders kept
  solving a global constraint by spending a format's identity.** Facesplit
  re-proportioned the zones to seat a caption and stopped being 50/50 ("not good
  for us"). The artifact spines applied Law 12's right-rail clearance to the whole
  composition and went off-centre ("they look so bad like this"). Whiteboard's
  camera answered "follow the pen" with 15 stops and 14 moves ("all over the
  place"). Each fix was a local optimum that broke the thing the format was FOR.
  The rule that came out of it: **a global law constrains what you may put in a
  region, never what the format IS** — solve it inside the half you own.

- [format-lab][captions] **The closing round was the one nobody planned: every
  format had quietly designed its own caption.** Round 5 had facesplit DERIVING a
  font size from its own mouth bound (41.62px), artifact spine solving one size
  from its widest phrase (41.0px), whiteboard emitting five sizes and takeover
  carrying an inert shrink formula. Four formats, four caption systems, all
  defensible locally. Round 6 replaced all of them with the published factory's
  own pill read out of `shorts_run8/projects/mcpupgrade_icon/index.html` — 486 of
  507 published pills at 56.2px — and every format now reports the same
  **114.59px** height as a cross-format audit key. **The canon already existed in
  the shipped work; four builders invented alternatives to it because nobody had
  written it down.**

- [format-lab][negative] **pureface died in one line and it was the right call.**
  Round 1: too zoomed, emphasis styling rejected. Round 2: *"I hate it. Throw this
  format to the trash."* No fix round was spent on it. The lab's cheapest output
  was the format it stopped building — and the discipline worth keeping is that a
  second round on a format Miguel disliked at round 1 is a round nobody gets back.

- [format-lab][measure] **Three instruments the lab built that outlive it.** (1)
  The negative control on a caption instrument: run it on the previous round's
  file, and if it cannot see that round's defect its silence proves nothing.
  (2) The encode control: two H.264 encodes of IDENTICAL content differ across
  ~22% of the frame, so "only the caption band changed" is only provable on a
  lossless pair or by reporting the densest out-of-band tile — the first
  containment pass read 98.9% changed and was pure rate-control noise. (3) The
  half-frame clip trim: `data-start + data-duration` is a float sum, `21.26 + 1.46`
  is `22.720000000000002`, and a clip that ends exactly ON a switch frame survives
  one frame into the next mode. One wrong-seat frame in 1,353, found only by a
  frame-exact scan after a 0.24s probe grid said the video was perfect.


- [cutout][quality] **The two defects in the 13 cutout remakes were both a
  SECOND generation nobody had priced, and neither was visible to any gate the
  format had** (Miguel, 2026-09-01). *Video*: `ship.py` wrote the plate's RGB
  back out at VP9 crf 24 and the chassis then displayed the 1080x900 result at
  1188x990. On `deepresearch`, plate 6.98 -> matte 6.88 -> finished short 5.65
  on the skin-only face-HF measure, against the published original's 6.50 — the
  chain was not adding grain, it was **smearing 13% of his face detail away**,
  and the 1.10 upscale did most of it. Fix: the RGB is re-cut from the 4K master
  AT the display box at crf 12, encoded near-lossless, and the cream rim becomes
  its own stacked layer instead of being painted into the picture that carries
  his face. Rebuilt: 6.62 -> 6.60 -> **6.63**. *Audio*: `publish_batch.py` put
  the cut's 16 kHz MONO analysis wav in every package as `source_audio.wav`, and
  ten of the thirteen generators mixed from it — an 8 kHz Nyquist ceiling, so the
  8-16 kHz band sat at -49.0 dB against the voice master's -30.6. Fix: the
  resolver picks the 48 kHz master and REFUSES a low-rate one by name, the wav
  ships as `analysis_16k_mono_DO_NOT_MIX.wav`, and the mix is gated to within
  6 dB of the master. Rebuilt: **-30.8 dB**. The transferable lesson is that
  every geometry gate the format owns passed both defective builds: **the
  factory measured where things were and never once measured what they were made
  of.**

- [cutout][measure] **The instrument that found the video defect also
  over-stated it, and the crop size was the whole instrument.** The audit
  measured face high-frequency energy on a crop 1.6x face height — wider than
  his head, so on a cutout its corners land on the cream die-cut edge, the single
  strongest high-frequency feature in the frame, while the split-format original
  it was compared against has no such edge at all. Swept on identical face pixels
  (the display plate vs the cutout cut from it): ratio 1.002 at k=0.35, 1.000 at
  0.45, 0.996 at 0.55, 1.014 at 0.70, then **1.387 at 0.80** — the exact k where
  the crop reaches the silhouette. The "+40% noise on his face" was largely the
  edge. `K_SKIN = 0.55` is now the standing crop and k=1.6 is kept only so old
  numbers stay comparable. **A ratio that jumps 39% between two adjacent crop
  sizes is not measuring the thing its name says it measures.**

- [cutout][trap] **The stale-staged-asset trap caught the fix for the audio
  defect on its very first run.** `stage_assets` re-copies only when the staged
  file is OLDER than the source. The fixed chassis correctly resolved the 48 kHz
  master, wrote it into `_geom_cutout.json` — and kept the 16 kHz `voice.m4a`
  already sitting in `stage/v/`, because that wrong file was newer. **The build
  record said the defect was fixed while the render still carried it.** Staging
  now stamps the source path, re-probes the STAGED file's sample rate, and
  measures the STAGED file's own 8-16 kHz band. A provenance record is not
  evidence; only measuring the artifact you actually shipped is.

## Run 9 — perplexityprojects / DIAGRAM, the daily 1-build-3-renders shape (2026-09-01, Opus 5)

First video through the daily distribution pipeline's real architecture: **one cut,
one matte, one lane scene, three compositions** (classic split -> YouTube, cutout ->
TikTok, takeover -> Reels). Genuinely new lessons only.

- [playwright][the big one] **A GSAP seek written as an EXPRESSION hangs Playwright
  forever, and never errors.** `pg.evaluate("() => tl.time(2.6)")` returns the
  Timeline, and Playwright then tries to serialise a deeply circular object across
  the CDP bridge. Measured: launch 0.2s, goto 0.4s, `__timelines` present 0.4s,
  `progress(1)`/`progress(0)` 0.4s — those were already written as `{ ...; }`
  blocks, which is exactly why they were fine — and the very next `time()` never
  returned, through three separate two-minute timeouts that looked like a video
  decode problem, a `zoom` problem and a font-CDN problem in turn. **Write every
  seek as a statement**: `() => { tl.time(t); }`. The general rule is bigger than
  GSAP: any `evaluate` whose last expression is a library object is a hang waiting
  to happen, and the symptom is silence, not an exception.

- [render][a compiler WARNING that is really an error] `Video "facebot" has sparse
  keyframes (max interval: 10s). This causes seek failures and frame freezing.` The
  renderer seeks the face once per frame, so a 10-second GOP means most seeks land
  on a P-frame; when the decoder does not walk forward, **his mouth freezes while
  the audio and the diagram keep running**. Nothing in the three-gate chain looks
  for it: Gate 1 measures the DOM, Gate 2's dedup would read a frozen face as
  stillness, and Gate 3 is not watching for it either. `-g 25 -keyint_min 25
  -sc_threshold 0` on the face plates (max gap now 1.00s) costs one re-encode.
  **Treat the compiler's media warnings as build errors: they are the only
  instrument in the chain that can see the class of defect they describe.**

- [captions] **Trimming half a frame off EVERY caption clip opens a hole between
  every two pills.** The facesplit rule — a clip ending exactly ON a switch frame
  survives one frame into the next mode — is real, and the first pass applied it
  globally. At 25 fps that is a 40 ms hole 34 times in a 30-second video. It
  survived Gate 1 (the boxes are right) and would have survived a manifest read
  (3 fps sampling steps straight over a 40 ms hole); it was caught by sampling the
  finished render at a round number, t=2.60, and seeing no pill. **Trim only at a
  real cut edge**, and prove it with a decoded-frame sweep: `frames_without_a_pill`
  is now 0 of 60 on all three renders.

- [cutout][plate] **`plate.py` bottom-plants unconditionally, and on a far-sitting
  recording that decapitates the silhouette.** Head parity solves `crop_w` from
  head height, so a SMALLER head (920.9px here against 1030-1060 on every previous
  cutout session) gives a SMALLER window, and a smaller window bottom-planted
  starts below his crown. `plate.json` said it in one number — `cap_top_on_plate
  -80.6`, against +15.8..+134.2 for the six approved sessions — and nothing
  downstream could have: SAM2 tracks whatever is in the plate, and a flat-topped
  head is a perfectly stable silhouette that the frozen-column leak check has no
  opinion about. The fix is the OFFSET, never the size: same 2004x1670 window,
  y0 490 -> 214, `cap_top_on_plate` +68.2. **Read `cap_top_on_plate` before
  tracking; a negative value is a decapitation, not a crop.**

- [cutout][seats] **A port with its own matte owes its own envelope, and the frozen
  fix5 seat constants are not portable.** `CAP_Y/ZY1 = 949.5/868.9` describe
  `hermesinfinite`'s silhouette. This session's union top is 63px into its own
  display plate (canvas 993 vs the definitive's 1030.1), so re-solving the chassis'
  own derivation gives `CAP_Y 912.4` (47.5%) and a stage zone `192..831.8`.
  Measuring in DISPLAY space is what makes it cheap and safe: `ship.py --display
  1188x990` emits `_alpha.webm` at the display box's size and the chassis paints
  that box 1:1 at `top 930`, so `canvas_y = 930 + alpha_y` with no scale factor to
  get wrong. Deleting a unit conversion deletes a class of bug.

- [shared scene][placement] **Centring the core BOX is the wrong sum; centre the
  CONTENT BAND.** A scene authored in a 1000x680 core that paints only y 40..534
  has its content centre 53px above the box centre, so `top = REGION_MID -
  CORE_H*k/2` put the takeover's diagram 70px high in the region it owns (Law 15).
  The core now DECLARES `CONTENT_Y0/CONTENT_Y1` and every format asserts the band
  lands legally — above Law 30's top-10% line and clear of its own caption pill.
  That one declaration is what makes a scene genuinely reusable across three
  frames whose regions are 862, 640 and 1258 tall.

- [gates][what stills see that boxes cannot] Three defects were found by
  pre-render 1080 stills and by NONE of Gate 1's four green runs: a node label
  parked INSIDE the receiving folder (a full-width centred text div's rect is the
  whole core, so it is never a "collision"), the hook mark resting at canvas y=117
  inside the top 10%, and the box-vs-band centring above. **Gate 1 is a rect
  instrument; Law 30 and Law 15 are picture laws.** Budget the still pass — it cost
  about four minutes and saved three renders.

- [takeover][cut map] **Place the face windows by WHAT THEY HIDE, not by even
  spacing.** The first map's return at 11.20-12.50 covered exactly the beat where
  three folders rise onto the desk — the run's best staggered entrance, and the
  Reels cut never saw it. Moving that return to 9.20-10.54 hides a one-second sheet
  swap instead, and buys the cut back landing ON `desk,` so the cutaway's first
  visible frame is the desk drawing itself: **ARRIVE IN MOTION satisfied by the
  schedule rather than by a LEAD offset.** Growth stayed monotone by moving the
  next boundary too (1.48 -> 4.48 -> 8.20 -> 9.90s, face 5.96s = 19.9%).

- [transcript] **The intake topic line can describe a LOSING take.** CLAIMS.md's
  one-liner for this video promised "Projects is now the shared naming convention
  across Claude, ChatGPT and Perplexity". The winning take says none of it — those
  words are in the abandoned attempt at raw w84-114, and the shipped 98 words end
  on "just like you can with any other AI provider" instead. A build that had
  designed to the intake line would have put two named products and a claim on
  screen that the video never makes. **Re-read the winning take before planning,
  and let the plan quote it.**

- [take detection] **The gap rule can be neither a superset nor a subset, and the
  honest move is to say so.** Silence alone at 1.0s gives twelve candidates here:
  it ADDS w0 (a false start) and w115/w125/w138 (abandoned fragments), and MISSES
  w116 (0.32s after a truncated `Perplex-`) and w198 (0.07s after his own
  `Spaces.`). No threshold repairs both directions, so the build records ABSTAIN
  and asserts the disagreement's SHAPE (`+[0,115,125,138] / -[116,198]`) so a
  re-transcription that changes it fails loudly. Markers were a genuine lower
  bound: nine truncations covering six of nine restarts.

- [perplexityprojects] Clean shipped record: three renders from ONE build and ONE
  cut — split 2160x3840 / cutout 1080x1920 / takeover 2160x3840, all 25 fps native,
  751 frames, 30.08s. Gate 1 **0/0 on all three**; Gate 2 37/36/34 distinct states,
  0 idle candidates; Gate 3 **pass on the first call, all three**. Guards: face HF
  **7.420 against a 7.453 plate (ratio 0.9956** on the k=0.55 skin crop), treble
  **-0.14/-0.14/-0.13 dB** of the 48 kHz master (which this cut is the first to
  emit alone — no analysis wav is written under `cuts/` at all), exactly ONE pill
  height per render, widest pill 746px of a 756px seat, **0 frames without a pill**,
  integral layer box 1188x990 at (-54, 930). Matte: leak check **clean**, healed
  false, 0 frozen columns, min shoulder sd 1.51, seam agreement 0.99903/0.99925,
  **$0.0816 total** ($0.0083 probe + $0.0733 track — under half the $0.17 tier
  because the take is 30s, not 54s). Full record:
  shorts_run9/paperwork/perplexityprojects_diagram.json.

- [impossibletask][cut] **The gap rule does not always abstain above its band — sometimes
  it MISFIRES, and this raw is the case that proves the threshold must be pinned inside a
  MEASURED band.** Three script families across 682.48s (A "If you want to level up with
  AI" x9, B "Start to give your AI impossible tasks" x9, C "Start giving AI impossible
  tasks before you head to bed" x29); only C reaches the sign-off. Content rule, marker
  rule and gap rule all land on word 1392 by EQUALITY. But the take-boundary gap (2.920s)
  is only the **fourth largest** gap in the raw, so at any threshold >= 3.0s the gap rule
  confidently answers word **1366** — a family-C attempt that aborts on a truncation 26
  words earlier. hermesvoicemagic's raw could not be made to answer wrongly; this one can,
  and the instinct that "a bigger threshold is safer" is exactly backwards here. Recorded
  as `gap_rule_MISFIRES_above_the_band` with the wrong answer written down.

- [impossibletask][cut] **A NEW disqualifier shape for an opening key: the pure OFFSET.**
  The 2-token `giving ai` fires exactly as many times as the 3-token `start giving ai` and
  every hit is one word later — a pure +1 shift. It would therefore RANK the 29 attempts
  identically and then LOCATE the winner 0.18s late, clipping the spoken word "Start" off
  the front. Not a stray hit inside a losing take (brainsdontmatter) and not a stray hit
  inside the winning one (hermesvoicemagic): an offset. The guard asserts the shift is
  pure, so the reason the 3-token key is minimal cannot go stale silently.

- [impossibletask][matte] **`plate.py`'s bottom-plant is only correct when the RECORDING
  obeys the format's set rule, and run 9 does not.** Cutout format law 7 asks for "a
  half-body frame with HEADROOM"; on 2026-09-01 Miguel sat lower, so the derived window
  `2088x1740+784+420` starts 74 px BELOW his cap crown and the plate ships a FLAT-TOPPED
  head — measured on 53 sampled frames, crown at master rows 346..358, clipped on 53 of
  53, and visible as a straight horizontal edge on a 7-frame tile of the plate's top 150
  rows. The sibling `perplexityprojects` plate reports the same shape
  (`cap_top_on_plate` -80.6). The fix is a MEASURED lift of y0 alone, 420 -> 300: the crop
  SIZE is untouched so head parity (497.4 px, head_frac 0.2591) is preserved exactly, and
  the only cost is the window's bottom row moving 2160 -> 2040, where the torso was
  measured still spanning the window edge to edge (left-most dark column median 0/261,
  right-most 260/261). Recorded as a `lift` block in `plate.json` so a later agent sees a
  decision, not a discrepancy.

- [impossibletask][sam2] **`track.py` died on the FIRST cut prompt any session produced,
  and the bug is one character of parsing.** `prompt0.py cut` writes its proof sheet as
  `kf_overlay_%05d.png` into the SAME directory as `kf_%05d.png`, `load_prompts` globs
  `kf_*.png`, and `int("overlay")` raises. A 100 % failure for every new cutout port,
  invisible until someone ran the cut stage for real. Fixed in place (skip non-numeric
  stems); the overlay is evidence, never a prompt.

- [impossibletask][gsap] **A chained `tl.to()` is a time bomb in a worker-parallel
  renderer, and "prime the timeline" is NOT the cure — it broke the audio.** A plain `to`
  records its START lazily, at first render. Three chained `to`s stepping one fill
  30 % -> 56 % -> 78 % measured, on a page that HAD been primed: 25.5s -> scaleX 0.7179,
  26.9s -> 0.516, 27.6s -> 0.3846, 28.2s -> 0.988 — the three END values arriving in
  scrambled order. Adding `tl.progress(1); tl.progress(0)` to the page then produced a
  SECOND defect that no visual gate could see: the bed's fade-out is a `to` on the media
  element's `volume`, so priming recorded its start as the element's default 1.0 instead
  of the 0.065 the mix law sets, and the rewind pinned the bed at full. Measured on that
  render: 8-16 kHz band **-34.16 dB against the master's -28.55** (a 5.6 dB drop) and the
  encode-vs-cut correlation **r=0.9937 -> r=0.3615**. The cure is upstream and total:
  every property tween is an explicit `fromTo` with its own FROM, so nothing depends on a
  recorded start and nothing needs priming. **If a build primes its timeline, its audio
  guard is the thing to check first.**

- [impossibletask][anchors] **An ambiguous word anchor is a build failure, not a default,
  and it masquerades as a GSAP bug.** `A("way")` silently took the FIRST match — word 63
  ("are WAY beyond", 18.68s) instead of word 99 ("all the WAY to the end", 27.52s) —
  putting the mission rail's second step nine seconds early, inside a beat that is not
  even on screen. Gate 1 is time-blind and passed it; the symptom read exactly like the
  scrambled-tween bug above and cost an hour of the wrong investigation. The anchor
  resolver now REFUSES a bare token that occurs more than once and names the timestamps,
  which immediately surfaced three more (`printer.`, `Now,`, `monitoring`).

- [impossibletask][gate2] **The pre-render still sheet is worth more than any gate, and it
  found a defect class gates cannot see: a group tween applied TWICE.** `_stack()` authors
  its children AT the target offset and the beat then tweened the GROUP to the same
  offset, pushing the machine half out of frame. Geometry Gate 1 passed 0/0 (it sweeps at
  0.5s and the atom was inside the frame at every sampled instant it measured), and the
  defect was obvious on a 16-frame sheet shot in 40 seconds. The same sheet also caught
  the machine being authored 236 px wide inside a 1080 px block (LAW 8), a label wrapping
  out of its box, and a capacity column standing at full height for 2.2s before the words
  that grow it (LAW 24).

- [impossibletask][measure] **Two caption instruments were built and both were wrong
  before one was right — and the failure mode is the run-6 trap, again.** A whole-frame
  terracotta sweep reported "pill heights" of 28-41 px, because this build's own layers
  are terracotta and 340 px wide. Bounding it to the pill's seat fixed that. Then a
  RELATIVE row threshold (45 % of the widest row in the band) was tried to stop narrow
  pills reading short — and made every render read ~50 px, because on the SPLIT the seat
  and the seam are the same line, so the band necessarily contains face rows and something
  in the face becomes the "widest row". Absolute threshold, seat-bounded band, and the
  narrow-pill readings REPORTED rather than tuned away. The authoritative proof that there
  is one type size is the document's own font-size set, not a decoded run.

- [impossibletask][cutout] **A depth lane inherited from the chassis lands in the wrong
  place on a different body, and the failure is silent in both directions.** The chassis's
  1176/1284/1416 belong to a plate whose chin sits at 1408; this session's chin is
  measured at 1510, so those rows put tool tiles BESIDE HIS CHEEKS. Deriving them below
  the chin instead buried every tile: the envelope says his torso is edge-to-edge from
  y 1700 down, so the lanes had 0 px of free column on both sides and the format's best
  moment rendered as nothing. The lanes are now anchored to the caption seat
  (+185/+325/+465) and each one ASSERTS at least 200 px of free column from the envelope's
  own row extents — measured here at 298/270, 48/287 and 0/336.

- [impossibletask] Clean shipped record: THREE renders from ONE build, ONE cut and ONE
  1080x560 scene block — split 2160x3840 (YouTube, `@migueltorrezai`), cutout 1080x1920
  (TikTok), takeover 2160x3840 (Reels), all **25 fps NATIVE** (the raw is 25/1 with
  dup_frac 0.001, so Global Law 6 is satisfied by construction, not by de-conform),

  the encode-vs-cut envelope, ONE font size (56.2 px) in every document. Matte: leak check
