## 2026-09-01 — A GUARD THAT IS NEVER CALLED IS NOT A GUARD (run 9, GLOBAL LAW 8)

**Defect.** `impossibletask_cutout` and `kimiram_cutout` shipped with their depth
lanes hard-chopped at x=0 and x=1080. 5 of 22 tiles per video, held for 24 s.
All three gates were green. The sampled audit caught it by eye.

**Cause.** Both generators wrote their own `depth_lanes()`, emitting tiles as
direct children of the full-frame `#lanes` layer. The chassis
(`formats/cutout/chassis_gen.py`) has always done it correctly — a per-lane
wrapper exactly canvas-wide, `overflow:hidden`, carrying a 90deg
`linear-gradient` mask with `EDGE_FADE = 46` — and has always shipped a
`guard_edge_fade`. Neither generator imported either one.

**The part worth remembering.** The guard was not merely uncalled, it was
*structurally blind*. `guard_edge_fade` walks the clipping containers and asks
"does each one carry a mask". With no wrapper there IS no clipping container:
the chop is done by `#root`, which is exempt because it is the frame. Run the
round-1 pages through the string guard today and it returns `{"masked_containers":
2}` and exits 0. **A defect that removes the thing a guard inspects cannot be
caught by that guard.** Any guard whose subject the author can simply not create
needs a second check that measures the OUTCOME.

**Two fixes, and only the second one is load-bearing:**

1. Shared, so nobody re-derives it: `EDGE_FADE`, `hmask`, `vmask`, `lane_wrap()`
   and `guard_edge_fade()` moved into `formats/cutout/lib/cutout_core.py`; the
   chassis now re-exports `EDGE_FADE` from there. Both generators call
   `C.lane_wrap(...)` and `C.guard_edge_fade(html)`.
2. **Gate 1 now measures the outcome on the emitted DOM.**
   `pipeline/geometry_audit.py` gained an `edgefade` sweep: any PAINTED box that
   STRADDLES a frame edge with no mask on itself or an ancestor is an ERROR,
   whoever built the page. Three refinements were needed to get it to zero false
   positives, each one a real lesson:
   - **Judge an `<svg>` by its ink, not its canvas.** Every svg here is
     `width:100% height:100%`; one in `impossibletask_takeover` has a layout box
     of -86..2246 and draws entirely inside the frame. `getBBox()` +
     `getScreenCTM()` gives the real painted extent.
   - **Apply every ancestor clip EXCEPT `#root`.** A meter fill is authored
     825 px wide and slid inside a 300 px track; its own box runs to -499 but the
     track already cut it. Clipping by `#root` too would erase the violation
     itself, because `#root` IS the frame edge.
   - **Report the outermost offender only**, or one tile reports three times.
   Verified: 5 errors on each round-1 cutout page, 0 on the fixed ones, 0 across
   7 other run-9 projects and 4 run-8 projects.

**A THIRD reason it survived: Gate 2 could not see it.** `frame_review.py`
defaults to the top 50% of the frame. The cutout depth band lives at y 1071-1475.
For any format whose content lives below the seam, run Gate 2 with `--full`.

**The decoded proof that settles Law 8** is now shared at
`formats/cutout/lib/cutout_edgefade.py`. Do not eyeball an edge and do not
measure "distance from cream" alone — the background at a lane's own rows can be
his silhouette. Take the OLD render as the unmasked reference and invert the
composite: `a(x) = (new_dev(x) - bg_dev) / (old_dev(x) - bg_dev)`, where bg_dev is
read at the frame edge (where a is 0 by construction). A correct fade traces
`a = x/46` exactly. Measured: a(edge) 0.001-0.042, a(>=46px) 0.991-1.004, mean
|a - x/46| 0.018-0.121, and nothing past 46 px moved. Two traps in that
instrument: a lane whose end tile is entirely inside the fade window has NO
signal past 46 px (not a failure), and a naive "delta must decay to zero"
test fails wherever the tile's own logo makes the local signal large — the
residual is proportional to the LOCAL signal, which is why the alpha inversion
is the right statistic and a raw delta ratio is not.

**Cost of the round:** two 1080x1920 re-renders. Match the ORIGINAL hyperframes
quality flag when re-rendering for a fix — `impossibletask` was built `-q high`
and `kimiram` `-q standard`; rendering kimiram at `high` produced a 40 MB file
against its 24.8 MB prior and would have shipped an unrelated change.

## Takeover switch law — perplexityprojects Reels rework (2026-09-01, opus-5)

**The rejection.** Miguel on the first daily takeover: *"the switches of the face
are happening way too often, they should happen at transition moments ideally,
right now you are cutting key visualizations."* One sentence, two independent
faults, and only one of them is about frequency.

**Fault 1 — RATE.** v1 switched 7 times in 30.016s = **13.99/min**. The
DEFINITIVE takeover switches 7 times in 54.04s = **7.77/min**. Nearly double.
Nobody had ever measured a takeover's switch rate against the reference; the map
was tuned by "which claims earn a takeover", which is an argument about content
and says nothing about tempo.

**Fault 2 — THE FACE WINDOWS SAT ON TOP OF THE BUILDS, and this is a property of
the LANE topology, not of taste.** The chassis lays scene clips over one
continuous face plate: outside a scene clip there IS no scene, so a face window
hides nothing. The lane builds invert it — ONE continuous scene timeline with
face clips on top, which is exactly what makes ARRIVE IN MOTION free (the world
has been developing behind the cuts, so an interior tween is already mid-gesture
when its clip appears). The cost nobody had priced: **a face window ERASES
whatever is drawing underneath it.** v1 lost, at full opacity, behind his face:

| face window | what drew behind it |
|---|---|
| 3.40-4.72 | `#h-open`, its draw-on, `#h-ls`, the arrow line AND its head (3.94-4.76) — the entire SPACES -> PROJECTS payoff. The frame came back to a finished picture. |
| 9.20-10.54 | `#b1-s1` (9.40-9.74), the sheet swap |
| 18.74-20.12 | `#b3-nlo`, `#b3-llo`, `#b3-slo` line + head (18.74-19.62) — the whole THIRD ARM of a three-arm diagram. 18.74 also cut away on the branch's first build frame. |

**THE LAW (chassis law 11, STANDARD §3):** switches only at beat transitions; a
visualization is never cut before it lands and holds; switch rate bounded by the
DEFINITIVE. Formally — a departure (scene → face) may not land inside a build
window nor within `HOLD_MIN = 0.30s` of one finishing; no build may overlap a
face RETURN window by more than `LEAD = 0.18s` (the chassis's own arrive-in-motion
lead); rate <= `7.77 x 1.30 = 10.10/min`.

**THE CHECK: `formats/takeover/lib/takeover_switch_law.py`.** Deterministic,
offline, reads the emitted page — clips plus every `tl.*` call — classifies each
tween BUILD / EXIT / MOVE, derives the face and scene windows and exits 1 with a
named defect (`D` departure, `H` hidden build, `R` rate). Lane generators call it
inside `build_takeover()` and refuse to write. Calibration is the whole point:
**10 build defects plus the rate ceiling on the rejected v1, silent on the
DEFINITIVE.**

Four traps found while building it, each one of which had it silently passing:

1. **`fromTo` carries TWO object literals.** Reading `opacity` off the raw call
   text finds the FROM value, so every entrance classified as an EXIT and the
   quiet windows came out inverted. Split the braces first.
2. **The DEFINITIVE's face plate has no `class="clip"`.** Matching only
   `class="clip"` found zero face elements, the checker reported "0 switches,
   face 0.0%" and printed OK. A checker that is silent on its own reference is
   not calibrated, it is broken. Match on `data-start` instead.
3. **A `set(scaleX:0.34)` at t=0 is the first half of a build.** Only
   opacity/dash parking was recognised, so the laptop's screen line
   (20.68-21.02) read as MOVE and merged two quiet windows into one — it would
   have licensed a face return straight across a build.
4. **`stagger` extends a build's real end.** `at + dur` is short by
   `stagger x (n-1)`; count the matched elements out of the HTML rather than
   guessing n.

**THE RE-TIME, placed not guessed.** `--quiet-windows` prints the legal switch
moments (gaps between builds, minus the hold), and the map is chosen from that
list intersected with Scribe word starts:

```
face 0.00-1.92 | T1 1.92-5.48 | face -6.58 | T2 -21.40 | face -22.54 | coda -30.016
5 switches = 9.99/min      takeovers 3.56 -> 14.82 (GROWING) + coda 7.48
face 4.16s = 13.9%   (v1: 7 switches, 13.99/min, 19.9% face)
```

Both returns are real argument seams that are also quiet: `5.48-6.58` = *"will
allow you to"* (b0's diagram landed 4.76 and holds; b1's sheet starts 6.58), and
`21.40-22.54` = *"You can now store them in"* (the three arms landed 19.62, the
laptop screen 21.02; the fills start 22.54).

**Face time falls when the law is obeyed, and that is the correct direction.**
13.9% against the DEFINITIVE's 20.7%. This is forced, not chosen: this lane's
scene builds almost continuously, so the legal face windows are exactly its quiet
gaps and there are only a few. Miguel's own round-4 brief was *"I would rather
have more time for the illustrations than my face, they're more important"*, so
the constraint pushes the right way — but note it as a structural consequence,
not a preference, and do not "restore" face time by putting a window back over a
build.

**A ghost arrival is still a bad arrival.** The first re-time returned at 6.46
and the frame's first visible content was the OLD diagram at ~15% opacity,
mid-fade — legal (an EXIT may hide, only BUILDs may not) and still wrong. Moved
to `turn` (6.58) so the cut lands on b1's first sheet stroke and the b0 fade-out
runs out behind the face. **Hiding an EXIT is legal; hiding a BUILD is not; and
arriving onto an exit's residue is neither, it is just weak.**

**QC v3 called idle motion that does not exist, and deterministic evidence
settled it.** Call 1 returned `pass=false`, "the document icon above ONE-OFF
continuously sways and wiggles" at t=8.0. In the sheet's own crop every frame
pair from **t=7.02 to t=9.26 differs by exactly 0.0000** — 56 consecutive
identical pairs; the only deltas in the window are the entrance tail (6.98, 7.02)
and the scripted swap (9.26, 9.30). `idle_motion_scan.py` independently reports
`idle_drift=no, long_static=YES at 6.5s` — the exact opposite of the claim. Call
2 returned `pass=true`. Judge noise, adjudicated on pixels, never on a re-read.

**File size dropped 31.3 MB -> 23.0 MB at the SAME `-q high`.** Not a quality
regression: 6.1 percentage points less camera footage in a CRF encode, and flat
vector cream costs a fraction of a face per frame. Check the flag AND the reason
before treating a size change as a defect (compare the 2026-09-01 kimiram entry,
where a size change WAS the defect).

## THE CUTOUT BACKGROUND IS THE CHASSIS'S, NOT THE BUILD'S (run 9, 2026-09-01)

**Problem.** Miguel rejected all three run-9 TikTok cutouts (`impossibletask`,
`kimiram`, `perplexityprojects`) on sight, with every gate green:

> *"what happened to the background of the TikTok videos? We used to have a
> beautiful regular background. You should have standardized what we were doing
> before. The previous cutouts (Grok Publish, Hermes voice magic) use really nice
> space in between all of the elements. Take the one from Grok Publish and use
> that as a FOUNDATION — right now you changed the perspective and you changed
> the space, which makes it look off. The only thing that would need change are
> the logos behind and also the nice little animation you used to pop behind me
> as a detail from time to time."*

Every word of that was a number, and every number was decidable from the emitted
page. Measured, rejected against approved:

| | grokpublish (approved) | run 9 (rejected) |
|---|---|---|
| tile sides | 78 / 116 / 148 | 78 / 116 / **168** |
| tile gap | 30 / 36 / 44 (0.38/0.31/0.30 x tile) | **0.72 x tile** = 56/84/121 (it, km); 0.52 x tile (pp) |
| pitch | 108 / 152 / 192 | 134 / 200 / 289 |
| cream between lanes | 26 / 26 | 43 / **-2 (the mid and near lanes OVERLAP)**; 90 / 106 (pp) |
| band height | 394 px | 403 px; 558 px (pp) |
| step events | **12**, one per spoken beat | **1**, for a 41 / 48 / 30 s take |
| step direction | left | left; **right** (pp) |
| seat instrument | 5th pct of the PER-FRAME gutter, p05 >= tile | one union row, "> 200 px free somewhere" |
| pop-behind card | yes, crossing the mid lane, host lane clears | **absent from all three** |
| tile ink | 0.50 x tile | 0.54 (it, km) / 0.56 (pp) |

Two of those are the entire complaint. A 0.72 x tile gap scatters a regular wall
of app tiles into isolated islands ("we used to have a beautiful regular
background"); a 168 px near lane against an unchanged 78 px far lane, with the
mid and near lanes overlapping, destroys the even 78/116/148 staircase ("you
changed the perspective"). The pop-behind was simply never built.

**Root cause — the same shape as the Law 8 failure two entries above, and it is
becoming the factory's signature defect.** The approved look lived ONLY inside
`format_lab/cutout_backfill/grokpublish/gen/grokpublish_cutout_gen.py`. Three
builders each wrote their own `depth_lanes()` from scratch, and each drifted
independently. Nothing downstream measured the LOOK: Gate 1 asks whether atoms
collide, Gate 2 samples frames for pop-ins, Gate 3 asks Gemini for defects, and
the guards measure face noise, treble and the caption pill. **Not one of them
could tell that the format had stopped looking like itself.** A build can be
wrong in a way that every correctness gate calls right.

**Fix, and only the second half is load-bearing:**

1. **The geometry is promoted and frozen.**
   `formats/cutout/lib/cutout_depthfield.py` carries the constants, the seat
   solver, the field builder, the step schedule and the pop-behind card, taken
   off the approved grokpublish render. A build now chooses TWO things: the cast
   (real registry marks, repeats allowed, never the story's own subject mark) and
   which mark the pop-behind carries on which beats. The seat is still solved per
   body — the RIGID stack slides down the legal band, scored on the 5th
   percentile of the per-frame gutter, and among the safe seats the one nearest
   the foundation's own +63.6 px offset from the caption pill wins. All three
   rebuilds landed within **0.4 px** of that offset; strip extents came out
   identical to grokpublish's to the pixel (-216/2064, -304/3032, -384/4344).
2. **`cutout6_check.check_depth_field()` measures the emitted HTML.** Tile size,
   pitch, inter-lane gutter, band height, wrapper width and step count are
   re-derived off the page, downstream of whoever wrote it. A guard inside the
   module cannot fire for a builder who never imports it — that is exactly how
   run 9 got here, twice in one day. Verified: passes on all three rebuilds,
   fails on the rejected `_v1` pages with four named violations.

**Two instrument lessons from the round:**

- **A step schedule is part of the look.** One step tween for a whole take makes
  the field read as wallpaper. The foundation's 12 hand-picked words do not port,
  so `DF.step_beats()` reproduces the CADENCE instead: divide the take into `n`
  slices and take the word start nearest each slice centre — every step still
  lands on a real spoken word.
- **A band-bounded colour sweep is not enough to isolate the caption pill.** The
  seat-bounded terracotta sweep in `guards_*.py` also catches the outro lockup's
  terracotta chip (120 px wide) when it crosses the caption band — 22.39 s on
  `perplexityprojects`, in the v1 render too, reported as a bogus 92 px "second
  pill height". Raising the row threshold instead TRUNCATES real pills, whose
  rounded caps are narrower than their middles (103 / 88 px readings). The fix is
  to keep the proven row test and reject the candidate by its TOTAL WIDTH: every
  caption pill here is >= 322 px, the chip never exceeds 120.

**Cost of the round:** four 1080x1920 re-renders (perplexityprojects twice, after
its `#depth` / `#tz` ids were corrected so Law 8's string guard could finally be
called on that build at all — it never had been). Quality flags matched per
project: `impossibletask` and `perplexityprojects` `--quality high`,
`kimiram` `--quality standard` (rendering kimiram at `high` produced 43.2 MB
against its 26.0 MB prior, and was discarded).

# 2026-09-01/02 — THE FACTORY HAD NO SEMANTIC GATE (impossibletask, run 9)

Miguel, on the day's `impossibletask` delivery: *"I'm not happy at all with
impossible tasks. The visualization makes literally no freaking sense. Were
there even clerks in this loop?"*

There was a clerk. It re-measured gates, caption canon, audio 8-16k vs master,
face HF vs plate, matte leak, pill heights, sync lag and the integral layer box.
**Every single reading was green on the render he rejected.** Gate 1: 0 errors.
Gate 2: 43 states, 0 idle candidates. Gate 3: pass on the first call, 0 visual /
0 semantic findings. Face HF 0.9769. Treble -0.14 dB. Sync lag 0 ms, r = 0.9937.

## The root cause is structural, not a mistake

Every gate the factory owned was an **instrument**. Not one of them decodes a
frame against the sentence being spoken. Geometry is time-blind. Frame review
counts distinct states and hunts idle motion. Gate 3's rubric hunts visual
defects and format-law breaches. The guards measure signal. **Meaning was
nobody's job**, so a build could be perfectly made and argue nothing, and the
whole chain would sign it off.

A frame-by-frame decode of the shipped split — 27 frames, three questions each,
judged as a first-time viewer on a phone — scored **10 SENSE / 17 NO-SENSE
(37 %)**. Full table: `shorts_run9/review/impossibletask_autopsy.md`.

## The four defect classes it found (all new, all recurring-shaped)

1. **THE OBJECT DID NOT READ.** The hook was a 3D-printer build plate drawn as
   stacked rounded bars. To anyone who was not in the planning room it is a stack
   of pancakes. **A plan that names an object does not make a viewer see it.**
2. **THE SCENERY WAS DRAWN INSTEAD OF THE SUBJECT.** The story's noun is a
   *monitoring system*; the build drew the *printer*. Both words are in the
   sentence, only one is what the sentence is about.
3. **THE KEY TERM WAS NEVER ON SCREEN.** "Impossible task" is spoken at 0.9 s and
   printed nowhere in 41 s. LAW 9 was treated as satisfiable by an *object*
   standing in for the term — and when the object failed to read, the video had
   no thesis on screen at all. **LAW 9 is a semantic law: if the core term is
   never legible, the frame set cannot pass.**
4. **THE COMPARISON COMPARED DIFFERENT AXES.** "ONE NIGHT" (a duration) next to
   "WHAT THEY CAN DO" (a capability), heights compared. Noise, however well
   animated. **Check that both labels answer the same question before looking at
   the bars.**

Plus a whole family of **symbols that needed a key**: square brackets for
restraint, a 34 px crescent for night, a grey dot for dawn, an unlabelled nozzle
for a printer. If explaining the shape takes a sentence, the viewer does not have
that sentence.

## The gate that closes it: THE VIEWER TEST — `pipeline/semantic_review.md`

Frames at every beat boundary plus 8 evenly spaced samples. Per frame, three
questions — *what am I looking at / what is he saying / does the picture argue
it* — answered as a first-time viewer on a phone, then SENSE or NO-SENSE with a
one-line reason. **PASS = 100 % SENSE. Any NO-SENSE frame HOLDS the render.**
No warning tier, no budget.

Three rules make the answers honest, and each one was learned by getting it
wrong:

- **Name the object from the PIXELS, never from the plan.** Write "a stack of
  pancakes", not "a build plate". This is the single highest-yield rule.
- **Never use the beat plan as the answer key.** Decode cold. Re-reading the plan
  first makes you see what you meant instead of what you drew.
- **An empty visual zone is always NO-SENSE.** Stillness is explicitly fine and
  must never be gated; *emptiness* is a dead slot.

**Where it now lives:** Gate 0 in both `SKILL.md` mirrors (it runs FIRST, before
any instrument), and STEP 1 of the clerk prompt in
`.claude/workflows/daily-shorts.js`.

## It runs on EVERY video, not the sample

Instruments can be sampled: a geometry defect in one build is usually a chassis
defect that will show up in its neighbours. **Meaning cannot be sampled** — every
video argues a different thing, so a passing video tells you nothing about the
next one. `impossibletask` *was* one of the two sampled videos. Full instrument
re-measurement stays at 2 of 10; the semantic gate is universal.

## New format law: A TAKEOVER SWITCHES ONLY AT BEAT BOUNDARIES

v1's cut map switched face -> scene at 0.92 s, which sits **inside** beat 1, so
the Reels viewer never saw the hook object arrive — only the second half of a
build already in progress. Word-aligned is not enough; **the unit of a takeover
cut is a whole scene beat.** If the face wants a shorter unit, split the beat in
the scene module (v2 went 10 beats -> 12 for exactly this). Enforced by
`assert_beat_boundaries()` in the generator, alongside the existing word check.

## Two build-mechanics lessons from the rebuild

- **A beat edge must land on the word its first element answers, or the beat must
  INHERIT something.** The Viewer Test caught two dead slots in the *rebuild's*
  own first render, both of this shape: b3 opened at 4.06 with its first pop on
  "Codex" at 4.64 (0.58 s of empty stage), and b9 opened at 29.44 with `/goal`
  at 30.26 (0.82 s). Fixed by ending the previous beat ON the word, and by
  inheriting b8's rail at its exact seat instead of fading it in. A related third
  case: a beat that opens exactly on its anchor must author its first element
  **already visible** — a 0.4 s opacity pop spends the beat's first frames on an
  empty stage, so the CUT is the entrance and the tween only scales.
- **`min-width` on a progress fill makes an unstarted track show a coloured
  dot.** LAW 23's anti-sliver floor is correct while a fill is filling and wrong
  before it starts. An unstarted track is EMPTY: the fill carries `opacity:0`
  until its own word. This defect was in the rejected render AND survived into
  the first rebuild.

## Verified fix

Same procedure, same video, after the rebuild: see the "after" table in
`shorts_run9/review/impossibletask_autopsy.md`. The scene is
`shorts_run9/gen/impossibletask_stage_v2.py` (a drop-in for the old scene
module); the plan that produced it is `shorts_run9/plans/impossibletask_plan_v2.md`.

# 2026-09-02 — SELF-REVIEW IS NOT A GATE, AND NOTHING WAS MEASURING HOW IT LOOKS

Two defects reached Miguel through a chain that was green from end to end. They
have different symptoms and one root cause.

## Defect 1: the moon

A bespoke Law-13 object was **illegible and ugly at phone size**. Every gate
passed it.

- **Gate 3 could never have caught it.** It is a rubric screener: it asks "does
  this video break rule X", and a model answering a rubric will answer "no" about
  a frame it never actually parsed. There is no rubric line for *is this object
  readable*, and a screener does not volunteer one.
- **The Viewer Test should have caught it and did not — because the BUILDER ran
  it on its OWN work.** This is the real lesson. The Viewer Test's central rule
  is "name the object from the pixels, never from your plan". That rule is
  correct and it is **not sufficient**, because a builder cannot un-know its own
  plan. It looks at an orange crescent and its own intent supplies the word
  "moon". The frame reads as SENSE to the one agent in the world for whom it is
  guaranteed to, and to nobody else.

  **The only reliable way to name an object from the pixels is to have no other
  source of names.** So the Viewer Test is now administered by a FRESH agent per
  video that receives the staged MP4s and the tight transcript and nothing else,
  and builders no longer administer it at all. Self-review is craft. It is not a
  gate, and it is never reported as a verdict.

- **A second, quieter miss: the Viewer Test judged whole frames at ~500 px.**
  That is generous. A phone renders a 9:16 short at about **405x720**, and an
  object gets a fraction of that. The Phone Test now crops each bespoke object
  **alone at 405x720** and a fresh judge must name it in **three words or fewer**
  with no context. Withholding the context is deliberate: with the sentence in
  hand, a judge retro-fits any shape to any meaning. A failure is a redesign, not
  a caption that explains the shape — an object needing a sentence has already
  lost the viewer it was drawn for. Helper: `pipeline/phone_crops.py` (the builder
  emits the crops because only it knows the bboxes; the clerk judges them).

## Defect 2: the off-centre face

A takeover shipped with **his face not centred** in the full-face segments.
Nothing in the factory decodes the RENDER and asks where the head is: Gate 1
measures the authored DOM, Gate 2 is a self-read, Gate 3 is a screener, the Viewer
Test asks about meaning. The defect was invisible to a chain of four gates because
it belongs to a class none of them measures.

`pipeline/face_center_check.py` measures it. Calibration:

| render | worst dx | mean abs dx | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| rejected `impossibletask_takeover` v1 | -9.81 % | 7.68 % | FAIL, 13/13 face frames |
| approved `perplexityprojects_takeover` v2 | -0.93 % | 0.56 % | PASS |
| `takeover - DEFINITIVE.mp4` | -2.87 % | 1.56 % | PASS |

Two things worth keeping:

- **A near-constant dx across every face sample means the PLATE, not the
  animation.** The rejected cut is off by roughly the same amount at every
  sample. The full-bleed crop derives from a measured `face_cx_px` in
  `_faces_<id>.json`; if that measurement drifts or the wrong window is used, the
  whole video shifts by one constant. Look at the crop before looking at the
  timeline.
- **BlazeFace will call a flat vector graphic a face.** The DEFINITIVE takeover's
  "CONTEXT WINDOW" grid at t=23.0 s scored 0.47 confidence and would have
  hard-failed an approved reference. Every hit is now validated: confidence
  >= 0.70 **and** >= 40 % skin-tone pixels in the box. Measured separation is
  enormous (real faces 0.88-0.99 at 79-91 % skin; the grid 0.47 at 11 %), but the
  check only exists because a first calibration run failed on a video that is by
  definition correct. **When a new instrument fails the reference, the instrument
  is wrong.**

The same instrument immediately found a live defect nobody had reported:
`kimiram_facesplit` sits at **+7.69 %** in its closing full-face lockup.

## The shared root cause

The factory's gates were all instruments plus one self-administered semantic
review. Instruments cannot see meaning, and a self-administered review cannot see
its own blind spot. Both fixes are the same shape: **move the judging to an agent
that has no access to the intent**, and **add an instrument for the class of
defect that was invisible**.

## Also landed

- **Gate 3 now DESCRIBES before it judges** (default; `--no-describe` restores the
  old behaviour). Gemini writes a one-line plain description of each sampled frame
  naming objects from the pixels, plus the words spoken at that instant;
  `unidentifiable_object` and `beat_mismatch` fall out mechanically and are hard
  errors. A description is much harder to fake than a rubric answer: to write "an
  orange crescent" the model has to look, and once that sits next to the words
  "one night of compute", the mismatch writes itself. Verified on the approved
  `kimiram_split`: 14 frames described, e.g. *"Upper graphic shows a stack of red
  memory modules labeled '1.5 TB ABOUT 48X YOURS'"* — 0 findings, still PASS.
- **The contact sheet is a mandatory build output** (`pipeline/contact_sheet.py`):
  12 frames at beat boundaries +0.35 s, 3x4, <=1800 px wide, one per staged
  format. Miguel reviews by scrubbing; the factory kept handing him prose.
- **Platform mapping is fixed**: YouTube = split (builder picks the best LANE and
  justifies it), TikTok = cutout, Instagram/Reels = **whiteboard always**
  ("we'll change if I see that it's not good"). Takeover and facesplit leave the
  daily deliverable set and stay available formats.

## THE CLIP-BOUNDARY GHOST (found 2026-09-01, in every render ever shipped)

- The producer keeps a clip on screen for `data-start <= t <= data-start +
  data-duration` — **inclusive at both ends**. Beats and caption pills are
  authored back-to-back (one clip's out IS the next clip's in), so whenever that
  instant lands on the frame grid (a multiple of 0.04 s at 25 fps) **both clips
  render for one frame**.
- Decoded evidence, `impossibletask` v3: frame 706 of the split reads
  `"tl  of its mission,  d"` — the outgoing pill painted behind the incoming
  one; frame 116 of the cutout still shows the job card, the clock and the X
  mark standing behind b3's Codex mark. Split and takeover hide the same overlap
  only because their sections paint an opaque cream ground.
- **Cure: hand over half a frame early.** `CLIP_EPS = 0.02`; every clip that
  hands to another emits `duration = t1 - t0 - 0.02`, the last clip of a track
  keeps its full length. It cannot open a hole: a 0.02 s window inside a 0.04 s
  grid can never contain a frame time, so the last frame before the boundary
  (t1 - 0.04) is still inside the shortened clip. Verified on the re-render —
  frames 115/116/117 and 705/706 are each a single clean state.
- It is INVISIBLE to gate 1 (DOM geometry is time-blind), to gate 2 (the frame
  set samples at 3 fps and never lands on the boundary frame) and to gate 3
  (same). The contact sheet is what caught it. Reference: `CLIP_EPS` in
  `shorts_run9/gen/impossibletask_gen.py`.

## BESPOKE OBJECTS SHIP ONLY AFTER A PHONE-SCALE NAMING TEST (Miguel, 2026-09-01)

- Miguel on the `impossibletask` v2 moon: *"for every single impossible task
  video, the moon makes no sense. It's not clear, it's ugly as shit."*
- **The rule:** render the object ALONE at phone scale — the finished frame
  downscaled to 405x720, the object then cropped out of *that* frame, never
  re-rendered at a convenient size — and it must be nameable cold by a stranger.
  Write the crop to `<run>/review/legibility_<video>_<object>.png` and keep the
  path in the paperwork.
- **Prefer plain literal objects over symbols.** A crescent is a CONVENTION: the
  viewer has to accept "crescent = night" before the picture means anything, and
  at 405 px a 124 px crescent is a grey comma. The replacement is an ANALOG
  CLOCK — face, twelve ticks, two hands, a pin — whose hands sweep 11 PM to
  7 AM, with the hour written under it. 83x104 px at 1:1 and it still reads
  "clock". No crescents, no abstract glyphs.
- Generator: `shorts_run9/gen/legibility_overnight.py` (derives the crop from
  the scene module's own geometry and the format's measured block seat).

## THE CAPTION ENGINE MADE A LINKEDIN BADGE OUT OF THE WORD "in" (run 9, 2026-09-02)

- The independent Viewer Test held `perplexityprojects_split` and `_cutout` on a
  frame at 22.36-22.52 s: *"a small orange square containing the LinkedIn 'in'
  logo, where the caption pill should be. A stranger reads LinkedIn in a
  Perplexity video."* The clerk's diagnosis was that the caption engine
  substituted a brand mark for a preposition.
- **Root cause — and it is not what the report says. There is no
  brand-substitution code anywhere in this factory.** `command grep -rli linkedin`
  over every `.py/.json/.md/.js/.html` returns six files and not one of them is a
  pipeline file. The emitted HTML at that timestamp is a plain
  `<span class="scappill">in</span>`. Nothing swapped a logo in.
- **What actually happened.** `phrases()` in
  `shorts_run9/gen/perplexityprojects_diagram_gen.py` flushes a caption group at
  punctuation, at a 0.30 s pause, or at six words. "You can now store them" hit
  the flush and left the preposition **"in" standing as its own beat**. The
  canonical pill is `white-space:nowrap` with fixed 33.8 px horizontal padding and
  ONE height of 114.59 px, so a two-letter beat renders **116.1 px wide — an
  aspect of 1.01, a SQUARE** carrying a bold white lowercase "in". That object is
  the LinkedIn badge. The pill's own geometry made the logo; the chunker handed
  it the two letters.
- **The law is stated on the measured shape, not on grammar.** Every candidate was
  laid out in the render browser at the canonical size:

  | beat | pill width | aspect |
  |---|---|---|
  | `in` | 116.1 px | **1.01** |
  | `you` | 163.1 px | 1.42 |
  | `day.` | 174.8 px | 1.53 |
  | `one.` | 179.6 px | 1.57 |
  | `Now,` | 202.7 px | 1.77 |
  | `you can` | 270.3 px | 2.36 |

  `PILL_MIN_ASPECT = 1.45` sits in the measured gap between "you" and "day.", so
  the boundary is read off the evidence rather than chosen. Note what it
  deliberately does NOT refuse: "day.", "one.", "Now," and "you can" all read as
  text and the published factory ships pills like them constantly. Widening the
  law to cover them would trade one defect for a chunker that mangles every
  sentence ending.
- **Two independent refusals, in `pipeline/captions.py` section 3b:** a beat of ONE
  token that is a pure function word (it argues nothing, whatever it measures),
  and a beat whose rendered pill is squarer than `PILL_MIN_ASPECT` (it reads as a
  badge, whatever it says). `merge_orphan_beats()` folds an offender into a
  neighbour — FORWARD first, because a preposition binds to what follows it
  ("in dedicated folders") — and `assert_no_function_only_beat()` fails the build
  if one survives.
- **The merge runs over the WHOLE beat stream, not inside one phrase.** Orphans
  are produced AT phrase boundaries, so the neighbour a beat needs is in the next
  phrase by construction. The first attempt merged per-group and left six
  offenders standing.
- **`brand_token_ok()`** is the gate for any FUTURE caption-token → brand-mark
  substitution: exact registry token, >= 3 characters, not a function word. "in"
  fails all three tests it is subject to. Nothing calls it today; it exists so the
  next person who reaches for the idea inherits the rule instead of the defect.
- Tests: `pipeline/test_captions_function_words.py` (42 assertions, run it).
  The whiteboard was never affected — `whiteboard_fix6_core.build_captions`
  already merges any single-word phrase into its predecessor — but the assert is
  called there too, because the law is the canon's and not a format's.

## A REAL LOGO THAT READS AS A BROKEN IMAGE (run 9, 2026-09-02)

- The Viewer Test failed the cutout's Phone Test on one recurring tile: *"a blue
  outlined rectangle with a large X and internal division lines. Named cold, in
  three words: a broken image."*
- **It was not a missing asset. The file was there and it was correct.**
  `assets/logos/platforms/exa-color.png` IS Exa's real mark, and Exa's real mark
  is a thin single-colour outline rectangle crossed by its own diagonals — stroke
  for stroke the browser's missing-image glyph, at tile scale on a white plate.
- **Every existing guard passed it**, which is the whole lesson: `stage()` checked
  existence, `measure_mark()` checked the alpha channel was not empty, `field()`
  checked the cast key was staged, and check 25 measured geometry off the HTML
  without ever looking at a pixel. Nothing asked *does this artwork read as a
  picture, or as the absence of one?*
- **`cutout_depthfield.assert_cast_resolves()`** now runs before any frame is
  rendered, as two gates: (1) every cast key resolves to a file that exists, is
  non-empty and DECODES (PIL for raster, cairosvg for SVG); (2) the rasterised ink
  is refused when it is a single flat colour, mostly hollow, and inked along BOTH
  diagonals of its own bounding box. Measured over all 24 marks the run-9 roster
  could draw from, `exa` is the only one whose ink runs the full length of both
  diagonals (1.000 / 1.000) and it clears the next single-colour mark, `notion`
  (0.636 / 0.388), by 0.36 — the threshold is not a tuned number. A deliberately
  minimal mark can be passed by name via `allow_placeholder=` rather than by
  weakening the test.
- **`registry.json` is NOT the source of truth for these paths.** The generator
  joins hardcoded relative strings to the logo root (the registry says
  `deepseek → ai-models/deepseek.png`; the code uses `.svg`). A guard that reads
  only the registry checks a path nothing renders.

## A DECORATIVE WALL COMPETES WITH THE ARGUMENT IT SITS BEHIND (run 9, 2026-09-02)

- The Viewer Test's systemic finding on the cutout: *"For ~25 of the 30 seconds
  the largest, highest-contrast objects on screen are brands the narration never
  mentions. It is decoration that competes with the argument, and at the two
  frames above it actively misdirects. It pays off exactly once, at 25.5 s."*
- Two frames were held outright: **0.50 s**, the hook, where the dominant mass was
  a dozen consumer apps and the subject was a 40 px glyph; and **7.50 s**, where a
  large crisp ChatGPT tile sat at his jaw while the sentence named Perplexity.
- **Four changes, each aimed at one of those:**
  - the cast is now TOPICAL and nothing else — nine AI providers / research
    surfaces, which is the exact comparison the script makes. `DEPTH_BANNED`
    keeps the consumer wall out as a named, asserted rule rather than as an
    absence, because an absence is not a rule and the wall grew back once already.
  - `DEPTH_TEXTURE = 0.70` recesses the field so it reads as texture. It is
    applied at the CALL SITE, never in `FOUNDATION_LANES`, so the foundation's
    0.34 / 0.66 / 1.00 stay frozen for every sibling build.
  - `HOOK_CLEAR = 1.30` holds the lanes off the frame until the hook has landed:
    the first thing a scroller sees is the Perplexity mark on cream.
  - the pop-behind is re-keyed from word 11 (4.90 s) to word 18 (6.82 s) — the
    Perplexity that OPENS the product claim. The card is now mid-crossing at
    7.50 s and the lane it hosts is CLEARED there, so the misdirecting tile
    cannot exist.
- The hook mark itself went 118 → 210 design units and shrinks back to its
  approved resting size on `launched`, so only the first 0.72 s is bigger and the
  rest of the composition is byte-identical in geometry.

## A LABEL THAT ARRIVES AFTER ITS OBJECT IS A DEAD FRAME (run 9, 2026-09-02)

- Split and cutout both held 6.70 s and 7.50 s: *"a small blank sheet of paper,
  alone in a wide empty cream field ... Nothing on screen says Perplexity,
  one-off, tool or research. Its key (ONE-OFF) does not arrive for another 1.6 s."*
- The card appeared on `turn` (6.58 s) and its key on `oneoff` (8.34 s). Between
  them the visual zone argued nothing at all, because an unlabelled generic page
  is not an object — it is furniture.
- **THE LAW: a bespoke object and its printed key are ONE BLOCK and arrive on the
  same beat, the beat the word is spoken.** The fix is never to bring the label
  early (it would then precede its word); it is to HOLD THE OBJECT. The hook
  diagram — still exactly on topic while he says "Now, Perplexity Projects will
  allow you to turn Perplexity from a" — now holds until 8.04 s, and card and key
  land together at 8.34 s.

## The clip-boundary hole — `impossibletask` v4 (2026-09-02, opus-5)

**The defect.** The independent Viewer Test decoded a **single fully blank cream
frame at 20.60 s and again at 25.36 s** in both the split and the cutout. It is
40 ms, so no gate could see it: Gate 1 samples at 0.25 s, Gate 2 at 3 fps, Gate 3
describes fourteen frames. On a phone it reads as a flicker at a beat seam.

**The root cause was the previous round's own fix.** v3 had found real clip
GHOSTING (one frame drawing two beats) and blamed an inclusive producer. The
producer is not inclusive: `packages/cli/dist/hyperframe-runtime.js` computes
visibility as `p >= start && p < start + duration` — **already half-open**. The
ghost was a float artefact, and so was the cure. Shortening every clip by
`CLIP_EPS = 0.02` put each clip's computed end EXACTLY on a frame time, where one
ulp of double arithmetic decides the frame:

```
b6:  16.70 + (20.62 - 16.70 - 0.02) = 20.599999999999998
     frame 515 is at 20.60 -> 20.60 < 20.599999999999998 is FALSE
     b6 gone, b7 (start 20.62) not yet there  ->  ONE BLANK FRAME
b7:  20.62 + (25.38 - 20.62 - 0.02) = 25.360000000000003
     same construction, opposite rounding, frame kept
```

Same code, opposite outcomes, decided by the last bit of a double. **An eps that
lands on the grid does not avoid the boundary; it IS the boundary.**

**The law.** Clip intervals are **half-open and FRAME-QUANTISED at the producer**.
A frame belongs to exactly one clip, and no arithmetic happens near a frame time:

```
start = k0 / fps                 k0 = round(t0 * fps)
dur   = (k1 - k0 - 0.5) / fps    k1 = round(t1 * fps)
end   = (k1 - 0.5) / fps         -> 0.02 s clear of BOTH neighbouring frames
```

The half-frame of slack is a trillion times any float error. `frame_of`,
`clip_start` and `clip_dur` in `shorts_run9/gen/impossibletask_gen.py` are the
reference implementation; the whiteboard lane gets it through a local override of
`whiteboard_fix6_core.caption_clips` rather than an edit to a chassis two sibling
videos were building against in the same session.

**The instrument, and it is permanent: `pipeline/clip_coverage_check.py`.**
Two halves, neither of them sampled.

* **the page** — parse the emitted `index.html`, snap to its own frame grid, and
  for every frame ask which clips of each track group are live under the
  producer's exact rule. Reports every frame owned by two clips (ghost) and every
  interior frame owned by none (hole).
* **the render** — decode every frame and measure ink in the visual zone. An
  INTERIOR empty frame, bounded on both sides by frames that are not, is a hole
  that reached the file. Leading/trailing empties are reported, never failed.

Run against the SHIPPED v3 split it immediately found **four** blank frames, not
the two the clerk caught by hand: 8.52, 16.68, 20.60, 25.36 s — and seventeen
one-frame CAPTION dropouts on the same page, plus seventeen more in the
whiteboard. After the frame-quantised rebuild: `holes=0 ghosts=0` on every track
of all three pages, and 0 interior blank frames in all three renders.

**Two general lessons.**
1. A fix that moves a boundary ONTO the sample grid has not removed the boundary
   problem, it has centred it. Move to the middle of the gap, never to its edge.
2. Never infer a runtime's interval semantics from a symptom. Read the runtime.
   Six lines of `hyperframe-runtime.js` would have saved this round.

**Also fixed this round, from the same Viewer Test** (`impossibletask` v4):

* **the "toaster oven"** — the rig's 130x170 printer was 49 px wide on a phone and
  named cold as a kitchen appliance. Now 190x230 with a terracotta cone-tipped
  nozzle, a bed with a part standing on it, and the printed key `THE 3D PRINTER`.
  (The key is not `3D PRINTER`: `caption_identity_guard` refuses that string
  because the pill at 7.62 s is the words "3D printer." verbatim. The article is
  the difference between a diagram label and a second caption.)
* **the "black staple"** — a LID on the tall bar for 0.7 s, unnameable. Deleted.
  The level is now the SHORT BAR'S OWN TOP extended right as a dashed line under
  the label it already carries, so the surge is measured against a line the
  viewer has been reading for four seconds and nothing transient has to be named.
  The dashes start clear of that bar's right edge: drawn from its left edge they
  print as notches across its flat top.
* **the evaporating bar** — the tall bar grew 61 px past the scene block and the
  overflow was hidden behind a 54 px alpha mask, which at phone size reads as a
  failed render. Heights re-budgeted (260 -> 430 px on a 470 px baseline) so the
  surge lands INSIDE the block with a hard flat top. **A masked top is not a top**
  (LAW 34's corollary).
* **the clock that contradicted the script** — v3 swept the hands 11 PM -> 7 AM
  under "And before he even got to bed". The tight transcript was read end to end
  for words claiming a night passed, a morning, or a waking: **there are none**.
  The clock holds at 11 PM for the whole take and the beat's motion is a single
  tick on the word "bed,". The hour that has not moved IS the argument.
* **`guards_whiteboard.pill_heights` swept the WHOLE FRAME** for the largest
  terracotta component and called it "the pill". That holds only while nothing
  else is a big terracotta shape — and the rebuilt whiteboard draws a 169x424 px
  terracotta comparison bar, so the guard reported pill heights of 113, 382, 422
  and 448 and FAILED a render whose captions are perfect. Bounded to the pill's
  own seat, which is the fix `guards_impossibletask.pill_heights` already carries
  and documents. **The band is the instrument** — third time this factory has
  learned it.

# 2026-09-02 — CLOSING THE DAILY TRIAL: what three rounds cost, and what each round caught that no instrument could

The first `daily-shorts` batch (3 videos x 3 platforms) took **three review
rounds** before it was deliverable. Every round was opened by a HUMAN or an
INDEPENDENT reader, and every round closed by adding an instrument. That order is
the finding: the factory has never yet detected a new defect class with the
instruments it already had.

## Round 1 — the instruments were all green and the video argued nothing

Miguel: *"The visualization makes literally no freaking sense. Were there even
clerks in this loop?"* Gate 1: 0 errors. Gate 2: 43 states, 0 idle. Gate 3: pass
on the first call. Face HF 0.9769, treble -0.14 dB, sync 0 ms, r = 0.9937.
**Every reading on the rejected render was green.**

What the round caught that no instrument could: **meaning**. A frame-by-frame
decode against the spoken sentence scored 10 SENSE / 17 NO-SENSE. The object did
not read (a build plate drawn as a stack of pancakes); the scenery was drawn
instead of the subject (the printer, not the monitoring system); the key term was
never on screen; a comparison compared a duration against a capability. No
geometry check, no state counter and no rubric screener asks any of those
questions, and a rubric screener will answer "no violation" about a frame it
never parsed.

Closed with: the **Viewer Test** (`pipeline/semantic_review.md`), universal — not
sampled, because meaning cannot be sampled: every video argues a different thing.

## Round 2 — the reviewer was the builder, and nothing measured how it LOOKS

Two defects reached Miguel through a chain that was green end to end: a takeover
whose **face was not centred**, and a bespoke **"moon"** that was illegible at
phone size.

What the round caught that no instrument could: **that a self-administered
semantic gate has a guaranteed blind spot.** The builder ran the Viewer Test on
its own work; its own intent supplied the word "moon" for a shape nobody else
could name. The rule "name the object from the pixels" is correct and **not
sufficient** — the only reliable way to name an object from the pixels is to have
no other source of names.

Closed with: **the independence rule** (a fresh agent per video, frames plus
transcript, nothing else), **the Phone Test** at 405x720 with a three-word cold
naming, **`face_center_check.py`** (which immediately found a live +7.69 % defect
in `kimiram_facesplit` that nobody had reported), **Gate 3 DESCRIBE-before-judge**,
and **the contact sheet** as a mandatory build output.

## Round 3 — the fix for round 2's defect was itself the next defect

The independent clerk decoded **a single fully blank cream frame at 20.60 s** —
40 ms, invisible to every sampled gate. Its cause was round 2's own cure: an
epsilon shortening every clip put each clip's computed end EXACTLY on a frame
time, where one ulp of double arithmetic decides the frame. The same construction
kept frame 634 and lost frame 515.

What the round caught that no instrument could: **that a boundary moved onto the
sample grid has been centred, not removed** — and that a runtime's interval
semantics must be READ, never inferred from a symptom (six lines of
`hyperframe-runtime.js` would have saved the round). The same round also found a
real logo that reads as a broken image, a decorative wall competing with the
argument it sits behind, a label arriving 1.6 s after its object, a caption
chunker turning the preposition "in" into the LinkedIn badge, and a whiteboard
that drew seven things and named none of them.

Closed with: **frame-quantised half-open clips** + `clip_coverage_check.py` (which
found four blank frames where the clerk had found two, plus 34 one-frame caption
dropouts nobody had seen), **`assert_zone_never_blank`**, **`assert_cast_resolves`**,
**captions §3b**, **the whiteboard LABEL LAW**, and **the windowed protrusion gate
inside `ship.py`**.

## The through-line

Three rounds, three closures, one shape each time: **the defect class was
invisible because nothing was asking that question**, and the fix was always an
instrument plus a reader who could not see the intent. Two corollaries worth
keeping:

* **A guard is only a guard if it is called.** The edge-fade guard, the depth-field
  guard and the leak check all passed builds that violated them, because a
  generator that rolls its own path never calls the guard, and with no wrapper
  there is nothing for it to inspect. Every one of them was re-closed DOWNSTREAM,
  on the emitted page or the encoded file, where it does not matter who built it.
* **When a new instrument fails an approved reference, the instrument is wrong.**
  `face_center_check` hard-failed the DEFINITIVE takeover on a vector grid
  BlazeFace scored as a face; the answer was validation (confidence ≥ 0.70 and
  ≥ 40 % skin-tone pixels), not a looser threshold.

**Consolidated 2026-09-02** so the next run inherits all of it without
remembering any of it: the ten laws are indexed in `STANDARD.md` →
**ROUND-2/3 LAWS**, the twelve mandatory steps with their exact script paths are
in the builder brief of `.claude/workflows/daily-shorts.js` and mirrored as a
table in both `shorts-factory` SKILL.md copies, and the whiteboard harness was
promoted out of the run folder to `formats/whiteboard/lib/whiteboard_build.py`
(a run folder is not a home for a law) with a re-export shim left behind.
