# ROUND 4 — 2026-09-02: seven laws, and the two audits that could not see them

Miguel reviewed the run-9 renders a fourth time and produced seven verdicts.
Codified as `STANDARD.md` → **ROUND-4 LAWS** (37-43). What is worth keeping is
not the laws — those are written down — but the three things the codification
taught, each of which cost real measurement.

## 1. Gate 1 was blind, and had been for the whole run

`geometry_audit.check_sample()` collects atoms as `Array.from(sec.children)` —
the DIRECT children of each active clip. Every run-9 generator wraps its scene in
ONE positioned `<div>` (`blk-b3`) or ONE `<svg>` (`#cam > svg`). So the audit was
judging **one atom per clip**, and `impossibletask_split` reported 0 findings
while the CODEX label sat 2.0 px off the panel it named.

The fix is a second element model (`LAYOUT_JS` + `check_layout()`) that walks the
WHOLE subtree and judges every element carrying an `id`. The `id` filter is the
load-bearing decision: a raw deep sweep of `kimiram_split` yields **244 objects
per sample and 176,321 pairs at 3 px** — tick rows, dot grids and glyph
sub-paths, none of which are objects in an argument. In this factory an author
writes an `id` when they mean "this is a thing"; that is the semantic boundary,
and it is free.

The old atom model is untouched, so no calibrated check regressed.

## 2. A progressively drawn SVG cannot be measured from a DOM box

The whiteboard draws every shape with `stroke-dashoffset` over a full-length
path. `getBoundingClientRect()` on that path returns its **final** shape at
frame 0. Running the new DOM lane on `kimiram_whiteboard` — a board Miguel
APPROVED — produced 7 cramp errors between shapes that were not on screen
together.

So the whiteboard is judged on its **AUTHORED BOARD** instead: `Board.rigids`
already carries every object's box in board units WITH its time window, which is
strictly better information than any rendered frame. Gate 1 now skips any clip
containing `#cam > svg` and any element with a live `stroke-dasharray`, and the
same six laws run inside `whiteboard_build.build()`. Two lanes, one law text.

**Corollary, new:** *the right surface for a geometry law is the one that knows
TIME.* Every false positive in this round — cross-chapter pairs, entrance
placements, transitional twins — was a time error wearing a geometry costume.

## 3. When the number Miguel says fires on work Miguel approved

Miguel's spacing law was "minimum gutter ≥ 24 design px". Measured:

| page | tightest non-block gutter |
|---|---|
| `impossibletask_whiteboard` (rejected) | 0.0 u — touching |
| `impossibletask_split` (rejected) | 2.0 px |
| `perplexityprojects_cutout` (APPROVED) | 19.3 px |
| `kimiram_whiteboard` (APPROVED) | 19.1 px |
| `kimiram_split` (APPROVED) | 25.0 px |

At 24 px, two approved boards fail. This is the same shape as the
`face_center_check` lesson from round 3 — *when a new instrument fails an
approved reference, the instrument is wrong* — but with a twist: here the
instrument was Miguel's own number. The resolution is to keep both, explicitly:
**16 design px is the REFUSAL line** (the largest round value strictly under the
approved floor, and the same number in both lanes: 8.5 board units), **24 px is
the AIM** the plan targets and the clerk reads by eye. A refusal line that fires
on approved work is not a law, it is noise.

## The blocks are the hard part, not the gutter

A pairwise gutter check is trivial and useless. Everything is in what counts as
ONE object. Four blocks are inferred, because each is already a law elsewhere,
and every one of them was found by a false positive on `kimiram_whiteboard`:

* a key welded to the object it names (GLOBAL LAW 9 / ROUND-4 LAW 39),
* everything one container holds (`monitor-card` holding TEMP, PROGRESS and both
  tracks — 2.8 u apart and entirely correct),
* a paragraph: printed lines sharing a column, within 1.2 line-heights,
* a stack: identical shapes on a shared column, tighter than their own height
  (kimi0/1/2 memory bricks at 3.0 u).

Plus, in the DOM lane, a **series**: ≥3 identical shapes in one section is one
object drawn in parts (`b3-fill0..3`, `b10-dot0..2`).

Two more discriminations that each removed a whole false-positive class:

* **A connector is exempt from the gutter law and is the only thing the crossing
  law judges.** A wire is *supposed* to touch what it joins.
* **The CORE BAND.** An underline or a strike grazes a word's edge; a crossing
  goes through the letters. Inset the type box 22 % top / 28 % bottom / 4 % each
  side and the two stop being the same event. Without it, `Board.label()`'s own
  pen path flags the word it is writing.

## The highlight was already ours

Miguel asked for "the nice clean highlight that you used to use". It was
`shorts_run6/gen/mathvoice_kinetic_gen.py`, carried into run 7:
`.hl { background: rgba(198,103,72,0.32); border-radius: 6px }`, wiped open
left-to-right by `wipex()` over 0.34 s, staggered 0.10 s per line, **one fill per
LINE** with the comment that says why: *"a union box would cover the whole tweet
and scope nothing, which is the one job law 5 gives a highlight."* It never
existed on the whiteboard, which is why that format reached for a ring. It does
now (`whiteboard_build.highlight()`), and ring/ellipse emphasis is retired
everywhere. **Amended 2026-09-02** — see *"A law written from ONE instance banned
a tool Miguel likes"* below: the highlight is for TEXT ON AN IMAGE; a drawn
object or board type is BOXED (`box_emphasis()` / the panel border flip), and
only the ring is banned.

## Calibration, as shipped

| page | Gate 1 (DOM lane) | board lane |
|---|---|---|
| `impossibletask_split` (rejected) | **4 errors** (`b3-codexlbl \| b3-panel` 2.0 px + 3 more) + 3 sidelabel warnings | n/a |
| `impossibletask_whiteboard` (rejected) | 0 (delegated) | **LAW 38 ×2, LAW 39 ×1, LAW 41 cramp + crossing, LAW 42 ×6** |
| `kimiram_split` (approved) | **0 errors** | n/a |
| `kimiram_whiteboard` (approved) | 0 | **all six silent** |
| `perplexityprojects_cutout` (approved) | **0 errors** | n/a |

The board lane's crossing check reports `a stroke drawn at 6.42 s crosses
'type:CODEX'` — the arrow Miguel pointed at, found from the authored geometry
without decoding a frame.

## A law written from ONE instance banned a tool Miguel likes (2026-09-02)

Round 4 produced LAW 38 as *"emphasis is a clean highlight — never a circle, an
ellipse OR A BOX"*, and every format retired its boxing. The next day, watching
the fixed videos ("those look fantastic"), Miguel corrected it: *"do not use
highlight for everything, it's just for when you need to highlight text on an
image, for the rest you can use the boxing you were using before, which are
perfectly fine."*

**What actually happened.** Two complaints made the law: an orange ELLIPSE
around a clock (*"circling of the clock looks off"*) and a box crushed against
TEXT inside a cramped whiteboard panel. Neither was an argument against boxing
a drawn object. The generalisation from those two frames to "no box anywhere"
deleted a primitive the factory had shipped since run 3 and that Miguel had
approved dozens of times — the **panel border flip**
(`.node.hero { border-color: TERRA_L }`, tweened via `borderColor` over 0.38 s),
whose own run-4 comment records why it beat a ring: *"never ring a node that
connectors land on"*. The over-correction then propagated into four CHASSIS
files, the builder brief, the clerk's NO-SENSE list and both skill mirrors
before anybody re-read it.

**The rule the amendment encodes: a law names its TARGET, not just its shape.**
- text living inside a raster (post card, screenshot, document, UI capture)
  → the marker HIGHLIGHT;
- a drawn object or board/scene type → BOXING (`box_emphasis()` on the board,
  the border flip on the DOM) — explicitly fine, still owing the 16 px gutter
  to its NEIGHBOURS;
- a ring / ellipse / circle → retired everywhere. That, and only that, was the
  thing he pointed at.

**And the checks earn their severity.** `assert_no_enclosure()` REFUSES a ring
and REFUSES a box on a raster, but a highlight with no raster under it is only
`wrong_tool_advisory` — because the approved `impossibletask_whiteboard` swipes
a track bar and a written key, and a check that failed an approved build would
be the same mistake in code. Gate 1 mirrors it: ERROR on a ring, ERROR on a box
over image text, WARNING on a misplaced highlight, and a rectangular box around
a drawn object is no longer a finding at all. Calibration after the amendment:
the retired ring board still refuses, all three staged whiteboards pass (the
impossibletask board reporting 4 advisories and its `post-card` raster), and
`kimiram_split` / `impossibletask_split` / `kimiram_cutout` /
`kimiram_facesplit` show no `enclose` finding.

## 2026-09-02 — plate.py solved for a 1:1 plate; the cutout paints it at 1.10
**Problem:** every cutout's head landed ~10% oversize (perplexityprojects +10.2%, kimiram 545 px vs the 496 law) and no instrument measured it until the round-6 clerk compared head heights across the three cutouts.
**Root cause:** `pipeline/sam2/plate.py::window` targets 496 px of head assuming the plate is shown 1:1, but the cutout chassis paints the 1080x900 plate at PLATE_SCALE 1.10 (1188x990).
**Fix:** `PAINT_SCALE` constant + `--paint-scale` CLI in plate.py; the solver now targets HEAD_ON_CANVAS / PAINT_SCALE on the plate. Face-HF/plate-box guards never saw it because they compare render to plate, not plate to law — a head-scale-vs-law guard (canvas head px within FRAMING ±38.4) belongs in cutout6_check.

## 2026-09-02 — the whiteboard harness asserts caption §3b but never merges for it
**Problem:** `deepseekflash`'s whiteboard would not build. `whiteboard_build.build()`
calls `CAP.assert_no_function_only_beat(phrases)` on the output of
`whiteboard_fix6_core.build_captions`, and this take produced the beat **`it is`**
— 164 px wide at aspect **1.43**, under `PILL_MIN_ASPECT` 1.45 and composed only
of function words. It is the `in`/LinkedIn badge defect one word wider.
**Root cause:** the core chunker merges phrases of ONE word only, so a two-word
function-only phrase produced at a comma survives it; and `build()` has the
SECOND half of STANDARD §3b (assert) without the FIRST (merge over the whole beat
stream). Every take the format had shipped happened not to produce one.
**Fix (per-video, deliberately not in the shared file):** `deepseekflash_whiteboard.py`
wraps `core.build_captions` in this process only — the wrapper calls the original
and de-orphans its output forward-first, and the chassis' own assert then runs on
the repaired stream and is still the thing that would fail the build. No shared
byte was edited while five sibling builders were running.
**The permanent fix belongs in `whiteboard_build.build()`:** one merge call before
the assert, using the `words` list each phrase already carries.

## 2026-09-02 — `core.caption_clips` is not frame-quantised, so pills can share a frame
**Problem:** `clip_coverage_check` failed the first `deepseekflash_whiteboard`
render with **GHOST frame 618 @ 24.72 s (cap18|cap19)** and **frame 886 @ 35.44 s**
— two caption clips owning one frame. Gate 1, Gate 2, Gate 3 and the zero-ink scan
were all green.
**Root cause:** `whiteboard_fix6_core.caption_clips` writes `data-start = t0` and
`data-duration = t1 - t0` at two decimals, and the chunker sets `t1` to the NEXT
phrase's `t0`. That is a closed interval at the boundary frame, which is exactly
what ROUND-2/3 LAW 2 forbids: *never a bare epsilon, quantise at the producer.*
**Fix:** the same per-video wrapper snaps every phrase to `start = k0/25` and
`t1 = start + (k1-k0-0.5)/25`. At 25 fps both are exact at two decimals, so the
core's rounding cannot move them and the half-open interval survives the format
string. Result: 32 clips, holes=0, ghosts=0, 0 interior blank frames.
**The DOM lane already had this** (`beat_clip`/`caption_html` in the run-9
generators); the whiteboard chassis is the one place it was still missing.

## 2026-09-02 — the third headroom lift, and the second over-wide plate, from ONE filming day
**Problem:** `deepseekflash`'s derived plate clipped the cap crown on **48 of 48**
resolving frames (crown never rose above master row 371 against a derived
`y0` of 380), and after the lift `ship.py`'s LAW 44 gate refused the matte:
`plate-border limb margin R 0.0 px`, three windows, his raised left hand sliced
flat with the rim cut off along the cut.
**What is new:** the over-wide remedy can preserve `k` EXACTLY rather than
approximately. `plate.py`'s solve gives `k = PW/CW`; choosing the new width from
the SAME family (`CW = 89 m`, `PW = 45 m`, m even) holds `k` at 45/89 to the last
bit, so head parity, the face centre and the visible master window are
byte-for-byte the narrow plate's and only the plate's own borders move. Extending
the crop on the side the measurement asks for (right only, x0 untouched) also
keeps the box's left canvas edge at −54, so nothing downstream has to be re-derived.
**And the lift SURVIVES an over-wide plate when only the width moves** — kimiram
retired its lift because widening changed the crop HEIGHT and bottom-planted the
window again; here `y0 = 300` and every measurement behind it stand.
**Set note, three for three:** impossibletask 74 px, kimiram 106 px, deepseekflash
41 px. Sit higher, tilt the lens up, and keep the hands inside the frame.

## 2026-09-02 — a retry-heavy raw with ZERO discard markers: the marker rule can ABSTAIN
**Problem:** the take-detection ledger had the marker rule (`^no[.,!?]$` or a
trailing hyphen/ellipsis) as an EQUALITY on `impossibletask` and as a
wrong-by-five LOWER BOUND on `kimiram`. On `deepseekflash` it has **nothing to
say at all**: five attempts of one script family in 100 s, and not one truncation
or spoken "No." in the entire raw — every abort ends on a clean, fully-punctuated
word because the speaker simply stopped and started over.
**And the gap rule's "success" was luck.** It is correct at exactly ONE threshold
of ten (0.8 s) because the keeper's own boundary pause (0.86 s) is SMALLER than
the abort's (0.90 s) — it wins only by being LAST in the file, not by
discriminating. At >=0.9 it already answers 6 words early.
**The rule that survives:** the CONTENT key plus the CLOSURE test are primary and
the AUDIO ENVELOPE is the confirming instrument; the two word-timing cross-checks
are recorded at every threshold precisely so a build cannot lean on one that
happens to work. Record an abstention as an abstention — it is a cross-check
whose precondition (that a discarded take announces itself) the speaker did not
meet, not a cross-check that failed.

## 2026-09-02 — `sparkchrome` (daily distribution, Diagram Build)

**A 6-word phrase cap can strand a function word the merge cannot save.**
`phrases()` flushes at punctuation, at a real pause, OR at a word count, and the
word count is the one that hurts: it cuts a clause BEFORE `split_to_fit` sees
it, and the partitioner then minimises the widest beat of a fragment instead of
the clause. On this take the outro was chopped after `follow for more AI news
and`, whose only legal partition strands `and` — 166.6 px, aspect **1.4538**,
under `PILL_MIN_ASPECT` 1.45 — and neither neighbour merge fits the 756 px seat
(862 px forward, 851 px backward), so `assert_no_function_only_beat` refused the
build, correctly and unhelpfully. **Raise the cap (12 here) rather than fight
the merge**: the whole clause reaches the partitioner and it strands nothing.

**A frame quantiser must take k1 from the NEIGHBOUR, not from the beat's own
end.** The beat stream carries a minimum-duration floor (`max(0.24, …)`) so a
short pill stays readable. Applied BEFORE the quantiser, that floor pushes a
beat's own end past the next beat's start, and `k1 = round(own_end*fps)` then
lands one frame inside the neighbour: `clip_coverage_check` found exactly one
ghost, frame 537 @ 21.48 s, on both DOM renders. `k1 = ks[i+1]` makes the
overlap arithmetically impossible and keeps the half-frame trim doing its real
job.

**ROUND-4 LAW 40 cannot be satisfied by two ends on one vertical side.**
`assert_anchor_law` requires `level` for BOTH its verdicts (mirrored implies
level), and two connectors entering a card's left edge at the same y would have
to overlap. `anchor_points(box, 2, side="left")` therefore always fails for
n = 2 on a vertical side. The layout that satisfies the law is the better
picture anyway: put the TARGET between its two sources and take
`anchor_points(box, 1, side="left")` and `…side="right"` — one shared y,
mirror-symmetric about the card's axis, and a centred composition (LAW 15).

**An emphasis that never leaves stops being emphasis.** LAW 38's border flip is
beat-scoped. Left on for the rest of the take it becomes decoration and it
competes with whatever terracotta the NEXT beat needs — here the connector
arrow. Revert the border when the beat ends; LAW 42's rule for marks is the same
rule for emphasis.

**Gate 3's describe pass earns its cost.** It held the whiteboard on one
semantic error — *"when 'Gemini' is spoken at 0.2 s the visual displays text
'GEMINI SPARK' rather than the official Gemini logo"* — which is GLOBAL LAW 2 at
the opening frame, and which every geometric gate had passed. A key term is
written type; a named tool is a MARK; the opening owes both.

**`--out` on `geometry_audit.py` is a DIRECTORY.** Passing
`--out …/_gate1_<id>_<fmt>.json` creates a directory of that name and moves
`report.json` out of `<project>/geometry_audit/` — where
`cutout6_check.check_edge_fade` reads it, so check 24 fails with "no Gate 1
report next to the project" while Gate 1 itself reports clean. Run Gate 1 with
the default out dir for any project whose cutout checks will follow.

**`cutout_facehf.py` names its aggregate `face_hf`, not `hf`.** `hf` is the
per-sample column inside `rows`. A guard that reads the top-level `hf` KeyErrors
into the except branch and the verdict silently never lands — the same class of
miss as a gate that is never called.


## 2026-09-02 — codexvoice: five things the instruments caught that a plan could not

**The video:** `codexvoice`, daily distribution (split / cutout / whiteboard).
Everything below is a defect a gate or a decoded frame found in a build that
looked right on paper.

### 1. `--display WxH` is handed to x264, which refuses an ODD width
The first over-wide plate solved cleanly to `1410 x 1.10 = 1551`, and `ship.py`
died with `width not divisible by 2 (1551x990)`, exit 187 — **after** the whole
track had been paid for and after 4 minutes of display-plate encoding. The
whole-pixel rule the CHASSIS states (`guard_plate_box`: box width and height are
WHOLE PIXELS) is necessary and not sufficient: the display box must also be
**EVEN**. A plate width that is a multiple of 20 makes `plate_w * 1.10` even for
free; otherwise force the box to the largest even value at or under it and
record the ~1 px of scale that costs.

### 2. BiRefNet re-decides the chair at EVERY framing, and the wings MOVE
`prompt0.py birefnet` was clean on the 1080-wide head-parity plate — the
headrest wings were provably outside the mask (columns 340/360, luma 29/23, ZERO
mask rows). At 1410 wide it swallowed BOTH wings (+40,125 px, the cap band 34 px
too far left). Widen again to 1530 and the wings moved *again*: the right one
120 px further in and 120 rows higher, so the windows that worked at 1410 held
only 85.5 % of the disagreement. The `perplexityprojects` remedy generalises —
subtract the session's OWN earlier tracked silhouette, shifted by the exact crop
delta — but the wing windows are **not** a translation of the previous ones and
must be re-derived from the disagreement profile at each framing. The coverage
assert (`>= 90 %`) is what turns a stale window into a refusal instead of a
silent under-cut.

### 3. `max(0.24, …)` in a caption duration is a GHOST factory
The inherited beat rule `dur = max(0.24, next_start - start)` stretches any beat
whose neighbour starts sooner than a quarter second over that neighbour, and
`clip_coverage_check` reads it as two pills owning one frame. Then, having
fixed that, deriving a clip's END from `start + dur` produced a HOLE:
`1.080 + 1.140` evaluates to `2.2199999999999998`, which rounds to frame 55
while the next beat's own `2.22` rounds to 56. **A caption's floor is ONE FRAME,
and each clip's end IS the next clip's start** — no float sum gets a vote. That
is ROUND-2/3 LAW 2 restated as code rather than as intent.

### 4. THE SAME GHOST LIVES IN THE WHITEBOARD CHASSIS
`whiteboard_fix6_core.caption_clips` writes `data-start` / `data-duration` as
2-dp floats, and the APPROVED, STAGED `kimiram_whiteboard` reports the identical
defect — 2 ghosts, `cap12|cap13` at 13.76 s and `cap20|cap21` at 23.72 s. It is
a property of the chassis' caption emitter, not of any drawing. `codexvoice`
re-quantises its OWN emitted page in its own generator rather than editing a
shared chassis that sibling sessions were building against at the time; **the
fix belongs in `caption_clips` and should land in the next quiet moment.**

### 5. A LOGO CAN BE THE RIGHT MARK AND STILL NOT BE A MARK
Gate 3 filed `missing_logo: Claude Code is mentioned without displaying its
official logo` twice against a build that WAS displaying it.
`coding-tools/claudecode-color.png` and `coding-tools/claude-code.png` are the
same Claude Code pixel critter — LAW 35 is satisfied by either — but the thin
variant has no white keyline and no readable eyes at the 92 px a monitor dock
gives it, and it reads as an orange smudge on cream. The chunky variant carries
both. **LAW 2 asks for the logo; LAW 8 decides which FILE of it is a logo at
this size**, and the describe pass is the instrument that tells them apart.

### And one non-defect worth writing down
`geometry_audit.py --out X.json` writes a **directory** `X.json/` containing
`report.json` plus one annotated PNG per violation. A paperwork assembler that
opens the path as a file gets `IsADirectoryError` — or worse, silently reports
`exists: false` — and then reports on a line the build does not have.

### 6. `plate_w` must be a MULTIPLE OF 60, and the gate that says so runs three steps late
The over-wide plate has to satisfy three separate constraints at once, each
owned by a different file, and only their intersection ships:

    box_w / 1.10 is a WHOLE plate    ->  plate_w is a multiple of 10   (cutout_depthfield.plate_wh)
    box_w is EVEN                    ->  plate_w is a multiple of 20   (x264, via ship.py --display)
    plate_w = crop_w * 15/31         ->  plate_w is a multiple of 15   (the head-parity scale k)
    ==============================================================================
    plate_w must be a multiple of 60

`codexvoice` widened to 1410, then to 1530. **Neither is a multiple of 60**, so
both were unshippable for a reason nothing checks until the CUTOUT BUILD runs -
two SAM2 tracks and two display encodes after the plate was chosen. The
constraint now lives as an assert at the TOP of
`build_plate_overwide_codexvoice.py`, where it costs nothing:

    if plate_w % 60:
        raise SystemExit(f"plate width {plate_w} is not a multiple of 60 ...")

1500 is the largest multiple of 60 this 3840-wide master allows with the right
border held where it already passed, and it restores the visible master window
exactly (823.45 -> 2852.55, the head-parity numbers to two decimals; face dx
-0.02 % of frame width).

### 7. `--out X.json` writes a DIRECTORY, and `check_edge_fade` reads a DIFFERENT path
Two separate traps in the same command. `geometry_audit.py --out X.json` writes
a **directory** `X.json/` containing `report.json` plus one annotated PNG per
violation - a paperwork assembler that opens the path as a file gets
`IsADirectoryError`, or silently reports `exists: false`. And
`cutout6_check.check_edge_fade` does not read your `--out` at all; it reads
`<project>/geometry_audit/report.json`, next to the project. Run Gate 1 for a
cutout with `--out <project>/geometry_audit` and the string half of Law 8 and
the sweep half of Law 8 both have their evidence. Otherwise check 24 fails with
*"no Gate 1 report next to the project"* against a build that is actually clean.

### 8. The cutout's IDLE-MOTION marker is a chassis property, not a defect
`frame_review.py --full` flagged three windows on the cutout
(`12.0-21.3s`, `26.0-33.0s`, `35.0-44.0s`) and none on the split or whiteboard
of the same video, from the same beats. The marker fires when no 3 fps sample
survives the 16x16 dedup for over 6 s - and the cutout's DEPTH FIELD drifts
continuously by design, so no two samples are ever duplicates. Its own header
says to corroborate: `shorts_run3/idle_motion_scan.py` returns `idle_drift=no`,
exit 0, and all four approved sibling cutouts in this run report the identical
`long_static=no` signature. **Every cutout will trip this marker. Corroborate,
record the corroboration in the paperwork, and do not chase it.**


## MOST CLERK FLAGS WERE ANIMATION FRAMES — a still frame cannot judge a transition (Miguel, 2026-09-02)

**Problem.** Daily batch 2's four fresh clerks returned **21 NO-SENSE flags** and
held every render. Miguel read them and ruled **most of them false positives**.

**Root cause — structural, not sloppiness.** `pipeline/semantic_review.md` told
the clerk to sample a still frame **0.2-0.4 s after each visual boundary**. Entry
animations in this house style run **1-2 s**, so that frame is taken *inside* the
animation. The clerk then honestly describes what it sees, and what it sees is a
picture still arriving:

| the clerk wrote | what was actually on the timeline |
|---|---|
| "an EMPTY outlined tag, the DeepSeek mark is not on screen" (deepseekflash 0.40) | the tag drops in empty and the logo fills it by 1.2 s |
| "Opus is spoken and NO Opus mark exists anywhere" (deepseekflash 4.15) | the Opus mark settles at ~4.6 s, 0.24 s after the word |
| "a completely blank cream field, dead slot" (deepseekflash 13.80) | ~1 s of clear ground between one graphic leaving and the next entering |
| "an UNLABELLED box, the shape needs a key" (deepseekflash 16.30) | the label ONE COMPUTER slides in under it ~1.5 s later |
| "the GEMINI SPARK wordmark is gone and the browser card has not arrived" (sparkchrome 1.30) | a 0.25 s crossfade |
| "Chrome named with no Chrome mark" (sparkchrome 1.48) | the favicon lands 0.1 s after the word |

**A still frame cannot tell a TRANSITION from a HELD STATE.** Every one of those
rows would have triggered a re-render against an animation that was working.

**What Miguel confirmed as REAL** — and the pattern is exact: the ones a frame
*can* legitimately see. `codexvoice` 16.15 (cup jammed into the phone), 18.55
(sound arcs overlapping the monitor), 21.0/22.8 (label baselines at different
heights — "odd but not the worst"), and 38.80 (the second Codex logo cut in half
**while moving** — "it has motion"). He ruled `codexvoice` 5.10 FALSE: the Claude
Code mascot is recognisable, people know it.

**Solution — four changes, all shipped 2026-09-02.**
1. **Sample at boundary + 1.5 s**, not + 0.3 s (`semantic_review.md` §1).
2. **Absence claims carry a duration test** (§3a): emptiness counts only if it
   persists **>= 1.5 s**; a LAW 2 "named tool with no mark" only if the mark is
   still absent **>= 2 s after the word**.
3. **Cramp/overlap/clipping is judged on a HELD frame, or declared a MOTION
   DEFECT** (an element crossing a border while moving). Motion never excuses a
   collision — that is why 38.80 is real and 0.40 is not.
4. **`pipeline/verify_flags_gemini.py`** — every candidate flag is cut out of the
   render (t-2.5 s .. t+3.5 s, audio kept) and watched by `gemini-3.8-flash`:
   CONFIRMED / TRANSITION / REFUTED. **Only CONFIRMED counts.** TRANSITION and
   REFUTED go in the autopsy's new DISMISSED table with the model's reason.

**Impact.** Re-run cold over all 21 batch-2 flags, the moving-clip verifier
CONFIRMED **7** and dismissed **14** (11 TRANSITION, 3 REFUTED) — a **67 %
false-positive rate** on the old still-frame procedure, and 14 rebuild items the
factory would have chased for nothing. It **agreed with Miguel on all 5 of his
rulings**, cold, without being told them: 16.15, 18.55, 21.0 and 22.8 CONFIRMED,
38.80 CONFIRMED with `motion_defect: true` ("the moving logo is clipped by the
phone's border"), and 5.10 REFUTED ("the pixel-art mascot is the official Claude
Code character"). It confirmed two Miguel had not ruled on: codexvoice 26.80 (two
contradictory labels held on one object for 2.2 s) and codexnondev 22.50 (an
empty speech bubble for 1.7 s — over the 1.5 s bar). Full table:
`shorts_run9/review/batch2_flags_verified.md`.
Cost: **$0.12 for all 21 flags across 4 videos** (~3 cents a video), which is
noise against one 4K re-render.

**The generalisable lesson:** a gate that samples stills must never be allowed to
report *timing*. Give it a duration test or give it the moving picture; otherwise
it reports your animations as your defects, and every one of those reports costs
a render.

## 2026-09-03 — ONE DECODE FOR THE WHOLE CHECK LIST: `pipeline/qc/qc_pass.py`

**Problem.** The daily check list is twelve numbered steps and each one opened
the same MP4 and decoded it again. Measured on the staged run-9 renders, the
same checks run one at a time cost **101.9 s** on the `sparkchrome` cutout and
**220.3 s** on its portrait-4k split — five to eight full decodes of a file that
was already in memory a moment earlier, plus sixty `ffmpeg -ss` seeks for the
caption-pill sweep alone (28.2 s on the cutout, **88.5 s** on the split). None of
that was a property of the laws; it was a property of every instrument being its
own CLI.

**Root cause, and the thing that made a naive fix wrong.** The two frame
instruments the laws are written against — `clip_coverage_check.zone_ink_series`
(which the zero-ink law is also built on) and the clerk's ink / double-exposure
scan — are DEFINED on OpenCV's pixels, and `face_center_check` is defined on
ffmpeg's own `fps=2,scale=540:-1` PNG grid. **The two decoders do not agree.**
Measured on `codexvoice_cutout`, a plain `ffmpeg -pix_fmt bgr24` frame is up to
**13 levels per channel** off `cv2.VideoCapture`'s, which moves the ink count by
~0.3 %; `scale=in_color_matrix=bt601` closes that to **zero on 1080x1920** but
only to **3 levels on the portrait-4k split**, still worth **1.7 %** on
`min_ink_frac_judged` (0.01861 vs the recorded 0.01831). A law measured on a
different number is a different law.

**Solution.** `qc_pass.py` decodes with `cv2.VideoCapture` — the way the laws do
— reducing each frame ON THE FLY to (a) a per-ROW ink table at full resolution,
so a prefix sum answers `zone_ink_series` for ANY `zone_bottom` exactly, and (b)
the 405x720 phone-scale readable-ink mask the clerk's scans are defined over;
full-resolution frames are never all held at once. ffmpeg's 2 fps face grid runs
in a thread BESIDE it, so wall clock is the slower of the two, not their sum.
Then **nothing is re-implemented**: each module's own function is called with its
decode primitive monkeypatched to serve from that pass —
`clip_coverage_check.zone_ink_series` and `face_center_check.decode_grid` — and
`whiteboard_build.assert_zone_never_blank` picks the shim up for free, because it
imports `zone_ink_series` inside its own body. The DOM audit, Gate 2, Gate 3, the
audio guards, the cutout HTML checks and both review sheets run in a thread pool
alongside the decode.

**Impact — parity is exact, on all three formats, against the recorded run-9
paperwork.** `sparkchrome` staged renders (byte-identical to `shorts_run9/output`):

| | cutout | split | whiteboard |
|---|---|---|---|
| frames / min ink / lead+tail / interior blanks | 633 / 0.0 / 4 / 0 ✓ | 633 / 0.0 / 4 / 0 ✓ | 633 / 0.0 / 1 / 0 ✓ |
| page coverage (clips, holes, ghosts) | scap 27, 0, 0 ✓ | tz 1 + scap 27, 0, 0 ✓ | tz 1 + scap 28, 0, 0 ✓ |
| `min_ink_frac_judged` @ s | 0.00895312 @ 25.28 ✓ | 0.01078905 @ 25.28 ✓ | 0.00203147 @ 0.2 (zone 799.205) ✓ |
| face centring, band n / worst dx% | 51 / 3.8 ✓ | 51 / 3.61 ✓ | 51 / 3.52 ✓ |
| treble mix / delta / speech margin | -28.92 / -0.08 / 21.84 ✓ | -28.95 / -0.11 / 21.829 ✓ | -28.95 / -0.11 / 22.418 ✓ |
| face HF render / plate / ratio | 7.057 / 7.092 / **0.9951** ✓ | n/a | n/a |
| edge clip, defect frames per border | 0/0/0/0, rises 17/30/24/16 ✓ | n/a | n/a |
| caption pill | {113: 60}, widest 752 ✓ | modal 227, widest 1504 ✓ | {113: 60}, widest 712 ✓ |
| **wall clock, single pass vs summed** | **20.4 s vs 101.9 s (5.0x)** | **32.2 s vs 220.3 s (6.8x)** | 17.9 s |

Every ✓ is byte-for-byte the number in `gen/_clipcov_*`, `gen/_zeroink_*`,
`qc/facecenter_*`, `gen/_guards_sparkchrome.json` and the session's
`matte_*_v5_ship.json`. The clerk's double-exposure scan reproduces exactly too:
the same two flagged frames on the split at 0.60 s and 0.64 s with the same pixel
counts (783/748 and 1397/641). And the number that exposed the decoder problem
in the first place now lands on the nose: `codexvoice_split`'s
`min_ink_frac_judged` reads **0.01830623 @ 45.68 s**, the recorded value, where
the ffmpeg-decoded version read 0.01861326; its sync lag reads **0 ms, r 0.996**,
the recorded pair.

**Four defects the parity work found in the existing tooling**, all of them
things that would have bitten a builder on a new video, not just this test:

1. **`cutout_facehf.TIMES` is a hard-coded `(5, 12, 20, 30, 40)`** and a 25 s
   short has no frame at 30 or 40 — ffmpeg returns nothing and `cv2.imdecode`
   raises. The standalone guard on `sparkchrome` exits **1** for this reason.
   `qc_pass` spreads five probes inside THIS take, which reproduces the run-9
   guards' own `3,8,13,18,23` on a 25.3 s render and its exact 0.9951 ratio.
2. **`formats/cutout/lib/cutout6_check.py` cannot be imported on its own**: it
   pulls in `cutout3_check` / `cutout5_check`, which never left
   `format_lab/cutout` when the format was promoted. And the lab ALSO holds an
   older `cutout6_check` and an older `cutout_core` — put the lab first on
   `sys.path` and check 24 vanishes (`no attribute 'check_edge_fade'`), put it
   last but let the lab's `cutout_core` get imported first and it dies on
   `no attribute 'guard_edge_fade'`. Promoted libraries win; the lab is the
   fallback that supplies what they need, and `cutout_core` is imported first.
3. **The caption-pill guard's tolerance was a 1x accident.** The published form
   is `min(heights)` against `3.0 px` of `114.59 * scale`. That is a DESIGN-px
   tolerance applied in ENCODED px: on the portrait-4k `codexvoice_split` the
   minimum is 226 against a 229.18 canon and **fails by 0.18 px**, while the
   modal 227 (47 of 60 samples) is 2.18 px off — the same 1.09 design px the
   cutout passes with. `qc_pass` judges the **modal** height against
   `3.0 * scale` and allows a `1 + scale` cluster, which reproduces every
   recorded verdict and stops flagging a legal split.
4. **`frame_review.py --video-id` only accepts a key already in its
   `TRANSCRIPTS` dict**, so a video filmed today cannot run Gate 2 at all.
   `qc_pass` hands it `--transcript cuts/<id>/transcript_tight.json` instead —
   the same file that dict points at.

**The generalisable lesson.** A cache is a legitimate way to reuse a check; a
re-implementation is not. Every number above is exact because the shim hands the
ORIGINAL function the ORIGINAL bytes — and the one place a shim could not do
that (the pill sweep decodes through ffmpeg's PNG in the guards, through OpenCV
here) is the one number that moves: the split's antialiased pill lands on 226 in
11 of 60 samples instead of 228 in 21 of 60. Same modal height, same widest
pill, same verdict, different decoder — which is exactly why the ink laws are
decoded the way the ink laws are written.

## 2026-09-03 — THE PREP STAGE: the batch's mechanical work, once, before the builders

**Problem.** Before a run-9 builder could design anything it had to cut its raw,
derive a plate, build a frame-0 prompt, dispatch a Modal track, wait for it, ship
the matte, and scan for pointing cues. Ten builders did that ten times, each one
waiting alone on its own GPU job, and not one step of it needs a model.

**Solution.** `pipeline/prep/prep_batch.py` + the libraries it is assembled from:

| file | what it owns |
|---|---|
| `cutlib.py` | take detection as a LIBRARY, generalised out of the `build_cut_*.py` family: the CONTENT rule (last scripted opening that reaches the spoken sign-off) as primary, the MARKER rule and a ten-threshold GAP SWEEP as cross-checks recorded at every threshold with the answer each gives, the envelope head measurement, the ffmpeg trim/concat master, the two native-4K face plates measured on THIS master, and the tight Scribe transcript on the cut audio |
| `platelib.py` | plate measure + build, and the OVER-WIDE solve — now the DEFAULT, not the LAW 44 remedy after the gate fires |
| `birefnet_master_sweep.py` | the master-space silhouette, run through the bake-off venv because rembg / BiRefNet are not in the workspace venv |
| `promptlib.py` | the frame-0 prompt and the wing cut |
| `sourcelib.py` | the generic X source fetch (quote resolved to original) and the embed-style card render |
| `prep_batch.py` | the orchestrator: one thread per recording for cut / plate / prompt0 / cues, then ONE fan-out that dispatches every track to Modal at once, then ship |

Two things it deliberately does NOT decide, and both are recorded as obligations
rather than guessed: **the wing cut** (the instrument abstains — 9/9 correct on
sessions needing no cut, 0/4 recall on sessions that did, exactly as
`pipeline/sam2/README.md` predicts the plate statistics would be, so the ids it
cannot rule on come back in `wing_review` for a human glance at
`kf_overlay_00000.png`) and **which post answers a pointing cue** (no url
supplied → `NEEDS_SOURCE`, still the builder's LAW 37 obligation). **No LLM
anywhere**: Scribe is ASR, BiRefNet and SAM2 are segmenters, everything else is
measured off a file.

**A stage that fails does not kill the batch.** Every stage carries its own
`status` and `wall_s` under `stages`, and a package with a good cut and a failed
track is still worth having, because the cut is the expensive thing to redo.

**Measured, on a scratch run over the `sparkchrome` raw (25.3 s, 633 frames):**

- **the whole chain, per stage: cut 162.0 s, plate 1863.6 s, prompt0 12.6 s,
  track 410.2 s, ship 61.6 s, cues 0.0 s.**  With the sweep cached the plate
  stage is **28.2 s**, which is what a re-run costs.
- **cut: 162.0 s** end to end, including the Scribe call, producing a 25.24 s
  master with `analysis_wav_written: false` — the 48 kHz-only rule holds by
  construction rather than by remembering it.
- **prompt0: 12.6 s**, and the wing instrument ABSTAINED (`wing_review: true`,
  `removed_px: 0`) rather than guess — which is the designed behaviour, and the
  reason the id comes back for a human glance at `kf_overlay_00000.png`.
- **cues: 0.0 s** — this take raises no pointing cue, so `needs_source` is empty.
- **the over-wide solve works and costs the viewer nothing**: crop
  `2576x1840+530+320` at k 0.48913, plate box **1386x990 at left -153** (the
  head-parity default would have been 1188x990 at -54), `overwide_applied: true`,
  head 451.6 plate px x 1.10 = **496.8 canvas px** against FRAMING.md's 496, face
  **dx 0.035 %**, and **visible_window_drift_master_px 0.0** — the frame does the
  cutting, the plate never does, and nothing the viewer receives moved.
  **`ship.py` passed every gate on the first try**: protrusion `clean`, edge-clip
  windows `[]`, **0 defect frames on all four edges**, and limb margins at the
  plate's own borders of **64.0 and 47.0 canvas px** against the 24 px floor the
  solve designed to — where run 9's REACTIVE head-parity plate for this same
  recording measured 31.0 and 39.0.  Solving before the GPU rather than after it
  is not just fewer round trips; it lands further inside the law.
  The lattice is DERIVED from k rather than copied: at k = 45/92 it independently
  reproduces `build_plate_overwide_chatgptchrome.py`'s hand-derived answer exactly
  — plate 1620x900, extensions 736/368, crop `3312x1840+16+320`, box
  `1782x990 @ -450`, drift 0.0.
- **plate: the BiRefNet master sweep is the bottleneck, and it is not close.**
  MEASURED, from the sweep's own record: **1787.6 s — 29.8 minutes** of wall
  clock at 600-700 % CPU to sweep **106 frames** at stride 6 on a 631-frame
  master, i.e. **16.9 s per swept frame**, and that is already only one frame in
  six.  The rest of the plate stage — measure, the over-wide solve and the
  build — is **76.0 s** of the 1863.6 s total, so the sweep IS the stage.
  The rate is
  also contention-inflated: run 9's own sweep logs run **~5 s/frame** (336 frames
  in 1730 s, 159 in 750 s) and this machine had three builders on it, so 16.9 is
  the pessimistic end of a 3x band — the conclusion does not depend on which end
  you take.  Modal's GPU track, by contrast, measured **$0.0604 for all 631
  frames in 410.2 s** (A10G, 143.5 s GPU, 153.3 s billed: gpu $0.0469 / cpu
  $0.0080 / mem $0.0054), leak verdict `clean`, unhealed, one chunk seam at frame
  350 with IoU min 0.99876. **At ten videos a day the sweep dominates every other prep cost
  combined**, so the obvious next move is to put it on Modal beside SAM2 rather
  than to tune the stride: it is the same shape of job (a per-frame segmenter
  over a whole take) that was already moved to a GPU once, for the same reason.
  Batch wall clock for the one-video scratch run was **2038.2 s**, of which the
  sweep alone is 88 %.

**Parity with the hand-built work.**  Take detection **reproduces all ten run-9
cuts** with every hand-verified `EXPECTED_*` constant asserted and matched — word
index, start time, take length, marker counts, and the recorded gap bands
(lunacheaper 0.8-1.5, minimaxh3 0.8-2.0) — and all three corroboration shapes
appear: equality, bound (`kimiram`), abstains (`deepseekflash`, `minimaxh3`).  The
card renderer matches bit for bit: same quote resolved to the same original, same
2460x1194 px at device scale 3, same 3 raw / 2 inked claim rects, and
`claim_line_rect_fractions` identical to five decimals.  The cut differs in
exactly two places, both deliberate: `head_s` 178.85 vs 178.79, because
`sparkchrome` used `HEAD_LEAD` 0.16 and the library carries lunacheaper's 0.10 —
now a per-row `head_lead` instead of a fork — and `face_cx` MEASURED at 1832.5 on
this master rather than inheriting sparkchrome's typed 1823.1.

**A second bug the test caught, in `ship.py`'s contract.**  `--master` and
`--display` travel WITH `--edge-box`, all three or none.  Without `--display`,
ship emits the layers at the plate's own size, the chassis upscales them in the
browser — that is the v4 face-detail defect — and `--edge-box` is refused
outright, because the box must BE the encoded size.  Prep does this correctly;
the trap is waiting for anyone who re-ships a matte by hand.

**A bug the run surfaced, in the prep harness itself.** `Stage.__enter__` wrote
`{"status": "running"}` and `Stage.__exit__` called
`self.rec.setdefault("status", "ok")` — and `setdefault` does not overwrite an
existing key, so **every finished stage was recorded as `running` forever** while
the log line cheerfully said `ok`. That field is the whole downstream contract
("do not re-cut unless a stage's status is not `ok`"), so with the bug in place
every builder would have re-cut and re-tracked a perfectly good package. Fixed by
setting the status rather than defaulting it, and only when it is still the
placeholder — a stage that reported its own terminal status (`reused`,
`skipped`, `SKIPPED_NEEDS_KEY`, `REFUSED`) keeps it.

**The generalisable lesson.** Moving mechanical work out of the builders is worth
it twice over — the builders start on a finished cut, and the batch's Modal jobs
run concurrently instead of ten agents queueing one GPU each — but a CPU-bound
segmenter in the middle of it will quietly become the new serial bottleneck. The
prep stage is only fast if every per-frame model in it runs where SAM2 runs.

## THE MODAL RENDER LANE, MEASURED ON A WHOLE VIDEO (chatgptchrome, 2026-09-03)

First daily trio rendered end to end on `pipeline/render/modal_render.py` instead
of locally. Three numbers worth keeping, all read off the tool's own record
(`gen/_modal_chatgptchrome_split.json`, `_tt.json`):

| render | pack | render | wall | billed | cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| split 2160x3840, 684 f | 48.4 MB | 122.3 s | **546.7 s** | 126.9 s | **$0.0178** |
| cutout 1080x1920, 684 f | 36.5 MB | 177.7 s | **474.8 s** | 182.4 s | **$0.0256** |
| whiteboard 1080x1920, 684 f | 18.2 MB | 69.7 s | **228.1 s** | 73.0 s | **$0.0102** |

**Wall clock is four to six times the render.** The GPU-side render of a 27 s
short is one to three minutes; the wall is dominated by packing and by the
upload of a 48 MB tar over a home connection. So the lane is worth it because the
three run CONCURRENTLY and the laptop stays free — not because any one render is
fast. Whole trio: **$0.0536**, one batch wall of 546.7 s.

**`--resolution` and `-q` are GLOBAL flags, not per-project.** The daily mapping
needs `portrait-4k` for the split and native 1080x1920 for the other two, so the
trio is TWO calls fired together in the background, not one. A single call with
`--resolution portrait-4k` would silently render the cutout at 4K and break
`guard_plate_box`, because the matte layer box must BE the encoded size.

**Modal's mux lands the audio half a frame early.** Measured with the guards'
own cross-correlation instrument (10 ms envelope, +/-250 ms search) against the
cut master: **-20 ms on all three renders**, r 0.983-0.986, where the locally
rendered siblings of the same batch report **0 ms, r 0.996**. Half a frame at
25 fps, consistent across formats, so it is a property of the lane and not of a
build. Sub-perceptual and not gated — but the next person to compare a Modal
render against a local one should expect it rather than hunt for it.

**`cutout_facehf.TIMES` is hardcoded to a 46 s take.** `(5, 12, 20, 30, 40)` —
two of those five seeks land past the last frame of a 27.4 s short, ffmpeg
writes no PNG and `cv2.imdecode` raises `!buf.empty()`. The fix is to pass
`times=` scaled to the take (the same list for the render AND the plate, which
is the only property the ratio depends on); the module default should probably
become a fraction of the duration.

**`geometry_audit.py --out` is a DIRECTORY, not a file.** Passing
`--out gen/_gate1_<id>_<fmt>.json` creates a directory of that name holding
`report.json`, and then `cutout6_check.check_edge_fade` fails with "no Gate 1
report next to the project" — because check 24 reads
`<project>/geometry_audit/report.json`, which the redirect had moved. Run the
audit with no `--out` and COPY the report where you want it.

## 2026-09-02 — TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT CANNOT SEE THE DEFECT THEY GATE (lunacheaper)

Both were found by LOOKING at a contact sheet, after every instrument in the
chain had returned green. Both are one-line fixes to the way the check is
*called*, not to the check.

### 1. `--zone-bottom 862.5` DISABLES THE ZERO-INK LAW ON SPLIT AND CUTOUT

**Problem.** The daily brief says to run `assert_zone_never_blank` with
`--zone-bottom 862.5` for the split and the cutout. 862.5 is the SEAM — and the
caption pill is centred on the seam (`translateY(-50%)`), so its **top half is
inside the measured zone on every frame that carries a caption**. The pill alone
is enough ink for the check to declare the zone non-blank forever.

**Measured**, on the first `lunacheaper_split` render (2160x3840), at 30.43 s
where the visual zone is provably empty cream:

| zone_bottom | rows measured | ink pixels | ink fraction |
|---|---|---|---|
| **862.5** (the seam) | 0..1725 | **94,561** | 2.538e-02 |
| **805.2** (the pill's painted top edge) | 0..1610 | **0** | 0.000 |
| 799.205 (`CAP_BAND_TOP_PX`, the whiteboard's own default) | 0..1598 | **0** | 0.000 |

Over the whole take the same file reports `min ink = 0.000 @ 28.28 s` at 805.2
and 799.2, and **never reaches zero** at 862.5. The empty window was 2.76 s long
(28.28-31.04 s, "But if you really want to make the most out of this model") and
the instrument could not see it; the CONTACT SHEET saw it in one glance.

**Root cause of the empty window itself**, worth stating because it is a class:
a beat clip is opaque, so the frame it starts on shows exactly what that beat
authors — and an element whose entrance tween begins at its own clip's start is
at `opacity:0` on that frame. Any beat whose first event is later than its
window start opens on cream. The cure is the sibling's `#b10-carry` pattern:
the incoming beat draws the OUTGOING beat's terminal stage and cross-dissolves
it as its own subject lands.

**Solution.** Call the zero-ink check on split and cutout with the pill's TOP
edge, not the seam: `--zone-bottom 805.2` (= 862.5 − 114.59/2). Report both
numbers if you like, but gate on 805.2. The whiteboard was never affected: its
default is already `CAP_BAND_TOP_PX`.

### 2. `idle_motion_scan.py` MEASURES THE WRONG REGION ON A 4K RENDER

**Problem.** The scan crops `1080:820:0:0` — written for the 1080x1920 canvas.
On the portrait-4k split (2160x3840) that is the top-LEFT eighth of the frame,
not the visual zone, so its verdict describes a region nobody composed.

**Measured** on the same file: `long_static=YES at 18.8s` on the 4K master, and
`idle_drift=no long_static=no` on a 1080x1920 downscale of **the same render**.
`idle_drift` (the only clause that exits 1) agreed either way here, but the
static clause did not, and the next build might not be so lucky.

**Solution until the tool takes a size:** run it on a 1080-wide proxy
(`ffmpeg -vf scale=1080:1920`) for any portrait-4k render, and say which file
the number came from.

### The generalisable lesson
Both of these are the same shape as the 2026-09-02 still-frame clerk finding:
**an instrument pointed at the wrong window will report green forever.** Before
trusting a check, ask what REGION it measured and in whose coordinate space —
and keep the contact sheet, which is the only artefact that looks at the frame
a viewer will actually see.

**Gate 3 cannot upload an 80 MB 4K master on this connection.** `qc_v3.upload_retry`
PUTs the raw file; all three attempts on `chatgptchrome_split.mp4` (80,287,169 bytes,
2160x3840) died with `[Errno 32] Broken pipe` after ~8 minutes each. The 1080x1920
siblings (25 MB) upload in about a minute. The workaround that shipped: judge a
**lanczos downscale to the delivery resolution** — same 684 frames, same audio,
no re-composition — and record the substitution in the gate log. Gate 3 judges
CONTENT, and 1080x1920 is what a phone is served; object legibility at real size
belongs to the PHONE TEST, which crops 405x720 out of the 4K master itself. The
proper fix is for `qc_v3.py` to downscale before uploading whenever the render is
over ~30 MB, rather than for every builder to discover this at 1 a.m.

## minimaxh3 (run 9, daily distribution, 2026-09-02) — five things that are new

1. **AN OPENING KEY CAN BE A UNION OF TWO DIFFERENT SCRIPTS, AND THE ASSERTION
   MUST BE ON THE SET, NOT THE COUNT.** `2026-09-01 14-36-13` has three attempts
   and the speaker CHANGED THE SCRIPT after the first, so no single phrase key
   sees all three heads. The trap: the two-token key `minimax h3` fires exactly
   THREE times — the same COUNT as the attempt heads — but two of its hits are
   the mid-sentence *"Minimax H3 is now available"*. A count assertion passes and
   is wrong. `build_cut_minimaxh3.py` asserts the SET, and asserts that the
   two-token form DISAGREES with the openings, so the recorded reason for the
   three-token key cannot go stale.

2. **INTAKE'S 2.5 s WALK-BACK IS NOW A NAMED FAILURE MODE, NOT A SUSPICION.**
   Every `*` row `CLAIMS.md` flagged is the same mechanism: intake stops at the
   first inter-word gap ≥ 2.5 s. On this raw the ONLY gap over 2.5 is the 9.84 s
   of dead air after attempt 1, so it walks straight past the 2.239 s boundary
   that is the real one — 13 words and 6.66 s early. The gap sweep in the cut
   script now records this by construction: the rule is right at 0.8–2.0 and
   wrong at 2.5 and above, which is the mirror image of deepseekflash (right at
   exactly one threshold, by ordering luck).

3. **THE OVER-WIDE PLATE HAS A FOURTH SHIPPABILITY CONSTRAINT AND IT IS THE CROP
   ORIGIN.** `codexvoice` recorded three (`plate_w % 30` for an integer crop,
   `% 10` for a whole display box, `% 20` for an even one). A fourth is
   `x0 = X0 - e*61/30` must be EVEN, or yuv420p sites the chroma plane half a
   pixel off his face for the whole take. On this session the measurement's own
   answer `e = 210` passes all three published constraints — plate 1500, crop
   3050, box 1650 — and gives `x0 = 273`, odd. **The per-side extension must be a
   multiple of 60, not 30.** Asserted in `build_plate_overwide_minimaxh3.py`
   before a cent of Modal is spent.

4. **`plate.py::build` HARD-SCALES TO 1080x900 AND HAS NO KNOB.** Calling it with
   an over-wide crop does not widen the plate, it SQUASHES the take: measured, the
   BiRefNet silhouette's area fell 506,952 → 387,888 px and every band narrowed.
   The failure is silent — the file is valid, the frame count is right, and only
   the mask bands say anything is wrong. Every over-wide build carries its own
   local copy of the filter graph for exactly this reason; this one now says so.

5. **THE HEADROOM LIFT HAS A SECOND SHAPE: A STARVED MARGIN, NOT A CLIP.** The
   three sibling lifts were all remedies for a crown the derived window CUT. Here
   the crown's highest row (353) stays below the derived `y0` (330) on 0 of 49
   resolving frames — nothing is clipped — and the window still has to move,
   because it leaves **2.95 plate px** of air against an 18 px floor and the cream
   rim is DILATED 7 px from the alpha: a crown 3 px under the plate's own top
   border has nowhere to put its rim, and the rim is then cut flat by the border,
   which is the shape LAW 44 refuses at the SIDE borders. The lift script asserts
   which of the two shapes it is remedying, so a future session cannot inherit the
   wrong justification.

**Two smaller ones, both caught by artefacts rather than by gates.**

* **THE CONTACT SHEET IS THE INSTRUMENT FOR "TOO EMPTY".** No gate measures how
  much of the visual zone a composition uses, and none should — but the 12-frame
  sheet showed a split whose zone was mostly cream on nine of twelve frames. The
  objects were re-solved from 300 to 380/360 design px and the content band grew
  538 → 583 px, still landing 30.2 px clear of the pill. Look at the sheet before
  the clerk does.
* **AN AUTHORED-AT-ZERO ELEMENT NEEDS A TWEEN PER INSTANCE.** `clip_inner()`
  authors the bird and the play triangle at `opacity:0`; only `#clipA`'s were
  ever switched on, so the second tile shipped as bare hills — missing the glyph
  the Phone Test names the object by. Nothing catches this: it is not a hole, not
  a ghost, not a collision, and the zone is full of other ink. Local stills
  (`whiteboard_stills.py` works on any project, not just a board) found it for
  the price of 20 seconds and no render.

**And a chassis note.** `BOARD_BOX`'s TOP is a claim about where the MARKER may
reach, not just about the ink: `build()` takes
`min(stroke tips + [board_box[1] + 2]) - PEN_REACH_U`. A board box at y0 = 130
refuses the build at 90.7 u even when the topmost real stroke is at 167.0 u.
150 is the chassis's own value and it is the value to use.

## THE BIREFNET MASTER SWEEP MOVED TO A MODAL A10G (2026-09-03)

**The problem.** `platelib.py` cannot choose the over-wide plate window without
knowing, in MASTER pixels, how far the silhouette ever reaches — and that
measurement only exists off the cut master, from a BiRefNet-general mask. On the
laptop that ran on `CPUExecutionProvider`: **1,787 s for 106 frames** on the
2026-09-02 prep test, **96 % of the whole plate stage**, for a number that ends
up as two integers per side.

**What shipped.** A second GPU app, `shorts-factory-birefnet`
(`pipeline/prep/birefnet_modal_app.py`), deployed separately from
`shorts-factory-sam2` so a mid-track builder is never disturbed by a prep deploy.
`birefnet_master_sweep.py` now calls it **by default**; `--local` is the CPU
fallback and the only path that still needs the bake-off venv. The cache is
unchanged and lane-blind.

| | laptop CPU | Modal A10G |
|---|---|---|
| 106-frame sweep (prep test) | 1,787.6 s | **57.9 s** GPU, ~70 s warm end to end |
| 159-frame sweep (run-9 perplexityprojects) | — | 86.9 s GPU, 0.547 s/frame |
| cost | free, machine unusable | **$0.031 / $0.045** |

**Parity, and the honest shape of it.** The four numbers `measure_silhouette`
produces — the shoulder baseline row and the extreme column above it, per side —
came back **identical** on both parity subjects, and both solved to the same
over-wide crop, the same plate size and the same per-side extension as the
plates that actually shipped:

| | laptop | Modal | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| preptest L/R baseline row | 2013 / 1908 | 2013 / 1908 | 0 |
| preptest L/R extreme x | 645 / 3012 | 645 / 3012 | 0 |
| perplexityprojects L/R baseline row | 1929 / 1899 | 1929 / 1899 | 0 |
| perplexityprojects L/R extreme x | 666 / 3126 | 666 / 3126 | 0 |
| take-wide extremes, both videos | — | — | 0 |

**Row for row the JSONs are NOT identical, and that is a property of BiRefNet,
not of the port.** Max per-row deltas of 234-549 master px appear on a minority
of rows. Two independent causes, both measured:

- **the 720p proxy.** Running the *laptop's own CPU* BiRefNet on the same crf-12
  proxy reproduces the disagreement (1,804 master px on frame 6). Raising quality
  narrows it (crf 10 yuv444p → 114 px) and lossless does not exist as a proxy:
  yuv444 qp 0 is 189 MB and rgb24 FFV1 is 260 MB against an **84 MB master**.
- **CUDA vs CPU kernels.** CPU and A10G on the *identical* proxy still differ by
  up to 108 master px on ~40-100 rows of 720.

The mask is near-binary-unstable at a handful of rows, and where the
silhouette's connectivity flips, a row's extreme jumps hundreds of px. **The
decisions are stable because the solve takes an extremum over the whole take and
the extreme frames agree.** When the raw rows must match, `--full` sends the
master and the input is bit-identical.

**Two traps worth remembering.**

1. **`onnxruntime-gpu` fails OPEN, silently.** Without `ort.preload_dlls()` the
   session builds happily on `['CPUExecutionProvider']` — no exception, no
   warning — and returns *correct numbers* 30x slower. Any ORT GPU function must
   assert `"CUDAExecutionProvider" in sess.get_providers()` and refuse otherwise.
2. **Do not pin a `nvidia/cuda` base image to match an ORT wheel.**
   `12.6.2-cudnn` silently gave CPU-only because ORT 1.29 wants **CUDA 13**
   (`libcudart.so.13`). `pip install "onnxruntime-gpu[cuda,cudnn]==1.29.0"` on
   plain `debian_slim` pulls the exact wheels the build was compiled against.

**And one about the corpus.** The prep-test master had been cleaned up, so the
parity subject was **rebuilt from `cuts/preptest/edl.json`** — same source take,
same keep segments, same encoder settings. The rebuild is exact: 631 frames, and
the laptop CPU sweep on it reproduces the 2026-09-02 JSON with **0 delta on all
720 rows** of frames 0, 300 and 630. An EDL is a real reproduction recipe; a
deleted master is not a lost measurement.

Numbers, failure modes and the operating instructions: `pipeline/prep/README.md`.
