## 2026-09-03 — REJECTION MOVES BEFORE THE RENDER, and the design becomes an artifact

Four changes, all of them about paying for a defect at the cheapest moment it is
visible. Every measurement below is from the staged `sparkchrome` projects of
2026-09-02 (approved, shipped), into scratch dirs; no Daily file was touched.

### 1. `pipeline/prerender/` — three tools, and a project that fails one does not render

| tool | measured, per project |
|---|---|
| `prerender_check.py` | **6.4-6.6 s**, identical across split / cutout / whiteboard (Gate 1 at `--step 0.25` is 3.2-3.4 s of it; the whole page load, the pill measurement and every import-level assert is the other 3 s) |
| `phone_test_page.py` | **7.6 s** for 6 declared objects with the parity comparison included; **8.7 s** for the 8-frame fallback sheet |
| `draft_watch.py` (cutout, 25.3 s / 633 f) | Modal draft **107.9 s render, 111.7 s billed, $0.0078**; the Gemini watcher **38.3 s, $0.108654**; wall **413.7 s** end to end, of which **255.5 s was an unbilled cold start** |

**The Gemini watcher is 93 % of the draft stage's cost and the render is 7 %.**
$0.0078 against $0.1087. That is the number to keep in view: the cheap thing is
the render, and it always was. What the draft stage actually buys is the chance
to spend the $0.109 while the page is still free to change, instead of after a
portrait-4k render.

**Negative control.** A copy of `sparkchrome_cutout` with two injected defects —
a tween target that does not exist and one caption pill rewritten to `"in"` —
comes back `FAIL` with exit 1, and the pill measures **116 px at aspect 1.01**,
which is the exact "in"/LinkedIn number `captions.py`'s header documents. The
clean project on the same run is `PASS`, exit 0.

### 2. Three traps found while wiring it, each one a real defect in an existing tool

**`whiteboard_build.audit_page`'s dead-tween half cannot be used on a DOM-lane
page.** Its membership test strips `#` and looks the token up in the id set, so
it only understands `#id`. Every run-9 DOM page tweens DESCENDANT selectors, and
on `sparkchrome_cutout` it reported **14 live targets as dead** (`b1-open .shead`,
`bw .bwchrome`, …). The law is right and the test is not: asked of the loaded
page — `document.querySelectorAll(sel).length` — it is exact for any selector.
`prerender_check` takes the duplicate-id half from the module and asks the
browser for the other half. `audit_page` itself is untouched; the whiteboard's
own pages do not use descendant selectors, so it is still correct where it runs.

**`cutout6_check.check_edge_fade` reads Gate 1's report by a hard-coded path**
(`<project>/geometry_audit/report.json`) — that report is the *geometric* half of
Law 8, the half a string guard cannot see. So Gate 1 must run BEFORE the cutout
checks and its report must stay in the project. Sending `--out` elsewhere turns
check 24 into a fail that is really a missing input; `--gate1-out` therefore
takes a copy and never moves the canonical file.

**`offsetHeight` cannot measure the caption canon.** Chrome rounds it to an
integer, so the 114.59 px pill reports 115 and a 0.41 px error is invisible.
`getBoundingClientRect` is sub-pixel but lives in ZOOMED space (a split sets
`zoom:2`), so the page's own scale factor is taken from the widest pill
(`rect.width / offsetWidth`, smallest relative rounding error) and every pill is
divided by it. Measured that way: cutout and split **114.66**, whiteboard
**114.54**, spread 0.0 on all three.

### 3. A REAL instrument bug in `geometry_audit.py`, logged not patched

`check_sample`'s lane measures raw `getBoundingClientRect` against
`FRAME_W = 1080`. The newer `check_layout` lane normalises
(`scale = 1080 / root.dataset.width`); **the older one does not.** A split page is
authored 2160 wide at `zoom:2`, so a caption pill that IS centred reports its
centre at 1080 and `offcenter` fires at exactly `FRAME_W/2 = 540 px` — **7
warnings on `sparkchrome_split`, an approved render**, and the same on every
split ever built.

It follows that on a split EVERY threshold in that lane is being applied at half
its intended size in design px: `EDGE_MARGIN` 20, `SEAM_MARGIN` 24,
`MIN_OVERLAP_PX` 3, `CENTER_TOL` 4, `STATIC_EPS` 4. **Not patched tonight** —
normalising it moves five thresholds on every split at once and that is a
measured change, not an overnight one. `prerender_check` carries ONE named
waiver, pinned to the arithmetic (type `offcenter`, page zoom > 1, offset
540 ± 1) and listed in its report; a genuinely off-centre box does not land on
exactly half the frame width. **Everything else in Gate 1 is still 0 errors,
0 warnings.**

### 4. The Phone Test does not need a video, and the page proves it

`phone_test_page.py` seeks the project's own GSAP timeline in headless Chrome
with `geometry_audit`'s clip gate and prime pass, screenshots at the
composition's encoded size, downscales to 405×720 and crops each declared object
alone. Against the staged `sparkchrome_split` render, six objects:

```
every phone box identical: True
edge-mask IoU  min 0.969  mean 0.9824   (0.9891 / 0.9894 / 0.9942 / 0.9706 / 0.9821 / 0.969)
```

Whole-frame fallback crops on the cutout come back at **0.68-0.91**, and the
reason is worth writing down: a browser `currentTime` seek lands on the nearest
DECODABLE frame while the renderer lands on the exact one, and a whole frame is
mostly the live face band. **Judge a declared object, not a whole frame.**

The sheet, the judge's manifest and the sealed key are `phone_crops.emit()` —
factored out of `phone_crops.py` and imported, so the sealed-key discipline has
exactly one implementation. Regression-checked: the refactored `phone_crops.py`
reproduces the pre-refactor `phone_sparkchrome_split.json` geometry row for row.

### 5. There is no 540×960 render, and the reason is in the CLI

`hyperframes render --resolution` takes PRESETS only (landscape, portrait,
landscape-4k, portrait-4k, square, square-4k) and its own rule is that the scale
must be an INTEGER MULTIPLE of the composition, so **nothing smaller than the
composition exists to ask for**.

**And there is no resolution to drop either — I got this wrong first and the
measurement corrected me.** The daily SPLIT page is authored
`data-width="2160" data-height="3840"` with `zoom:2`, so it renders at 2160×3840
with no `--resolution` flag at all: `portrait-4k` on a split is a **1× no-op**.
The cutout and whiteboard are authored 1080×1920.

**The whole draft saving is `-q draft`, and it is large.** `sparkchrome_split`,
633 frames at **2160×3840: 80.1 s of render, 86.5 s billed, $0.0061** — against
the high-quality **1080×1920** cutout's 100.2 s / $0.0146 and whiteboard's
68.9 s / $0.0102. **2.4× cheaper on a frame four times the size.**

Cold start dominates the wall and is NOT billed: 255.5 s on the cutout draft
(`render_c4`), 373.7 s on the split. A warm lane is render-time plus the upload.

The 540×960 file is one `ffmpeg` scale off the draft (0.3-0.5 s, 1.2-1.4 MB) and
is an eyeballing artefact only: the watcher is fed the NATIVE draft,
because `clerk_video_gemini` re-encodes to 720×1280 itself and handing it a
540-wide file would make it upscale — a different input to the same model is a
different verdict, and this stage only earns its place if its verdict predicts
the post-render one.

### 6. The plan is an artifact now, and two authors build from it

One builder holding the plan in its own head emitted three platform renders that
argued three slightly different things, because the plan was never written
anywhere a second agent could read it. So `daily-shorts` gained a **PLAN AGENT**
per video that designs and builds nothing — `plans/<id>_plan.json` +
`plans/<id>_plan.md`, carrying beats with word timestamps, the picture per beat,
the bespoke objects with bboxes and three-word names, labels with above/below,
lifetimes and anchors, connectors, blocks, the pointing cues and the card
answering each, highlight-vs-box per target, board mode and chapters, the cast,
and the lane with its reason — and then **two authors run concurrently from that
one plan**: the SCENE AUTHOR (split + cutout, one shared scene) and the
WHITEBOARD AUTHOR. Neither re-plans; a disagreement goes to
`plans/<id>_{scene,wb}_notes.md` and the plan is built anyway unless a LAW
forbids it.

**The clerk's forbidden list now names `<run>/plans/` explicitly.** A plan that
is a real file is a plan a clerk can accidentally read, and a clerk that has read
the plan sees what was meant instead of what was drawn.

**The wave cap did not change, but what it caps did.** Five VIDEOS in flight is
now five plans and then ten authors. The 2026-08-17 session-window kill was 8
concurrent builders each running its own cut, plate, track and three LAPTOP
renders; these authors do none of that — prep did the mechanical work once and
every render is on Modal, so the Mac only authors and the ten agents are ten text
streams, not ten Chrome fleets.

### 7. The builder brief no longer lists check commands

The twelve-item numbered list is gone. An author gets the law pointers and the
ORDER; the commands live in `pipeline/prerender/` and
`pipeline/render/render_and_check.py`. **A numbered list inside a prompt is
something an agent can skip a line of and still return "followed"; an exit code
is not.** Three laws still have no tool and the brief names them explicitly: the
depth cast resolve, `guard_plate_box`, and `merge_function_only_beats()` before
`assert_no_function_only_beat()` — `prerender_check` proves the merge's result,
it does not do the merge.

### 8. `pipeline/render/render_and_check.py` — measured, and it found something on its first run

Two 1080×1920 renders of the approved `sparkchrome` projects, submitted
together, `--no-watch`:

```
[02:15:27] sparkchrome_whiteboard     render dispatched
[02:15:27] sparkchrome_cutout         render dispatched
[02:19:01] sparkchrome_whiteboard     render landed  633f  wall 213.8s  $0.0102  -> checks start NOW
[02:19:07] sparkchrome_whiteboard     qc_pass done   5.8s
[02:21:26] sparkchrome_cutout         render landed  633f  wall 358.4s  $0.0146  -> checks start NOW
[02:21:31] sparkchrome_cutout         qc_pass done   5.4s
batch wall 363.8s against 583.4s of the same work one render at a time
modal $0.0248
```

**The whiteboard's checks finished at 02:19:07, two minutes and nineteen seconds
before the cutout had even landed.** Under the old shape those 5.8 s ran after
the slowest render. On a full day (30 renders, three of them portrait-4k splits)
that is the whole post-render check bill hidden inside the render window.

**And it caught a real defect on the first file it checked.** Both fresh Modal
renders fail `audio_guards` on ONE number:

| file | sync lag | envelope r | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| fresh Modal `sparkchrome_whiteboard` | **-20 ms** | 0.9858 | FAIL |
| fresh Modal `sparkchrome_cutout` | **-20 ms** | 0.9843 | FAIL |
| **staged, approved** `sparkchrome_whiteboard` (2026-09-02) | **0 ms** | 0.9977 | PASS |
| **staged, approved** `sparkchrome_cutout` (2026-09-02) | **0 ms** | 0.9973 | PASS |

Treble is fine on all four (delta -0.05 to -0.11 dB against a 6 dB tolerance)
and so is the speech margin (22.3-22.4 dB). It is only the sync. The audio
streams differ by **one AAC frame** (1188 vs 1187) and 2.67 ms of duration, both
files carry the same ffmpeg build tag (`Lavf63.1.101`), and **-20 ms is 960
samples at 48 kHz — one AAC encoder priming delay (1024 samples = 21.3 ms)**.

**Related, and found while chasing it: the Modal render image's version pin has
drifted.** `pipeline/render/modal_app.py` pins `HF_VERSION = "0.7.107"` with the
comment *"laptop: npx hyperframes --version -> 0.7.107"*. The laptop now resolves
**0.8.26**. `pipeline/render/README.md` states in as many words that the parity
guarantee depends on Node, the HyperFrames CLI and ffmpeg staying pinned to the
laptop's versions. **They are not.** Whether that is the cause of the 20 ms is
not proved here — what is proved is that a fresh Modal render of an approved
composition now fails a law the staged file passes, reproducibly, on both
formats. **This must be settled before stage 2's benchmark**, because a lane
that fails `audio_guards` on every render cannot produce a clean end-to-end run.

Reproduce in one line, no render needed (the scratch MP4s are gone; re-render
first):

    $V pipeline/qc/qc_pass.py <render> --vid sparkchrome --fmt whiteboard \
       --run shorts_run9 --voice-master shorts_run9/cuts/sparkchrome/audio.m4a \
       --skip gate1,gate2,gate3

**One bug in the driver, found by the same run and fixed.** It first read
`checks[<name>]["pass"]`, and reported every green check on an approved render
as a FAIL. `qc_pass` does not put a `pass` key on every check — some report
`{"rc": 0, "stdout": ...}`, some `{"ok": true, "result": {...}}` — it computes a
top-level `verdicts` map (PASS / FAIL / SKIP / ERROR / REPORTED) and a top-level
`pass` from it, and **that** is the verdict. The driver now reads those.
Re-verified against both fresh renders (`pass=False`, `failed=['audio_guards']`)
and both approved staged renders (`pass=True`, `failed=[]`).

## 2026-09-03 — THE -20 ms WAS NEVER THE CLOUD: a version pin matched to a version this laptop never ran

`render_and_check.py`'s first run reported that fresh Modal renders of an
approved composition fail `audio_guards` at **-20 ms** where the staged,
Miguel-approved file of the same project passes at **0 ms**. The obvious
suspects were all container-shaped: SwiftShader, the static ffmpeg, the cores,
the screenshot capture path. **None of them.**

### The measurement, before the theory

A sample-accurate FFT cross-correlation of each delivered mix against
`cuts/<vid>/audio.m4a` — not the guard's 10 ms envelope, the raw thing:

| file | lag | |
|---|---|---|
| laptop `sparkchrome_cutout` | **0** samples | staged, approved |
| laptop `sparkchrome_whiteboard` | **0** samples | staged, approved |
| Modal `sparkchrome_cutout` | **-1024** samples = -21.33 ms | |
| Modal `sparkchrome_whiteboard` | **-1024** samples = -21.33 ms | |

-1024 samples at 48 kHz is **one AAC encoder priming interval** exactly, and
-20 ms is that number inside the guard's 10 ms quantisation. So the question is
never "what shifted the audio" — nothing shifted it — but "what decided whether
1024 samples of encoder priming are played or skipped".

### It is one container field. Not one sample of media.

```
laptop : st0 elst media time 0, dur 324096 | st1 elst media time    0, dur 1215488 | initial_padding 0    | 1187 aac frames
Modal  : st0 elst media time 0, dur 324096 | st1 elst media time 1024, dur 1215360 | initial_padding 1024 | 1188 aac frames
```

The **video** edit list is identical. Decode the Modal file with
`-ignore_editlist 1` and it reproduces the laptop's PCM at lag 0 exactly, with
the same first non-zero sample (1067). The two renders disagree about one
`elst` entry on the audio track and about nothing else.

### The cause, found in the CLI's own source

HyperFrames mixes the composition's audio to an AAC sidecar and muxes it with
`-c:a copy`. In **0.7.107** (`dist/cli.js`, `muxVideoWithAudio`):

```js
const copiesContainerizedAac = !isWebm && shouldCopyAudio
                            && config?.preserveAudioPrimingEditList === true;
if (!copiesContainerizedAac) args.push("-avoid_negative_ts", "make_zero");
```

`-avoid_negative_ts make_zero` **discards the sidecar's priming edit list**. In
**0.8.x** the flag is gone from that function entirely, with a source comment
naming upstream issue #3487: `make_zero` can write an empty leading VIDEO edit
that QuickTime and Safari render as a black first frame. So newer builds keep
the priming edit list, and an edit-list-honoring decoder now skips 1024 samples
that older builds played.

### And here is the part that cost the evening

`modal_app.py` pinned `HF_VERSION = "0.7.107"` with the comment
*"laptop: npx hyperframes --version -> 0.7.107"*.

**The laptop does not render through `npx`.** It runs the agent-tools checkout,
`infra/agent-tools/hyperframes/packages/cli/bin/hyperframes.mjs`, and that
checkout's built `dist` reports **0.7.71** — its `package.json` says 0.8.17 and
the `dist` is stale from 26 July, and the `dist` is what executes. Every
approved master in `shorts_run9` was written by **0.7.71**. Meanwhile
`npx hyperframes` resolves the `latest` tag, which is **0.8.26** today.

So the pin was matched to a version this machine had never used, sitting
between two versions that behave alike and unlike it.

**The proof that closes it:** a **local** render of `sparkchrome_cutout` on
this laptop, with 0.7.107 out of the npx cache, produces `initial_padding=1024`,
1188 audio frames and **-21.33 ms**. The container reproduced on the machine it
was being compared against. The cloud was never in the story.

> **A version pin is a claim about an artifact, and it has to be measured on the
> artifact.** `npx <pkg> --version` answers "what would the registry give me",
> not "what wrote the file I approved". The second question is the only one a
> parity pin is about, and the answer is `node <the binary the script runs>
> --version`.

### Which side is correct — because the guard was the thing under suspicion

HyperFrames' mixer places the voice **1024 samples early on its own timeline**:
the file whose priming a decoder skips correlates against the voice master at
-1024, the file whose priming is played correlates at 0. The undischarged
priming is what puts the voice back onto the picture's timeline. So the 0 ms law
is the correct law, the approved masters satisfy it, and loosening the guard
would have shipped a mix running 21 ms ahead of its own captions. **The guard
was right and the renderer was wrong**, which is the outcome a guard exists for.

### The fix, on both sides, and neither one re-encodes anything

- **Container** — `modal_app._normalize_delivery_audio()` runs after every
  render, before the probe and before anything is persisted. If the delivered
  MP4 carries `initial_padding > 0` it is remuxed
  `-c copy -avoid_negative_ts make_zero -movflags +faststart` — literally the
  argument 0.7.71's own mux passes. Stream copy, so frame parity and the
  `--verify` table are untouched by construction. The run record gains
  `audio_elst` (`applied`, padding before/after) and the function **raises** if
  any padding survives.
- **Laptop** — `pipeline/render/hf.sh`, now the only entry point to the CLI. It
  resolves the checkout (`HF_BIN` overrides, `npx --yes hyperframes@$HF_PIN` as
  a last resort), **asserts** the resolved version equals `HF_PIN=0.7.71`, and
  after a `render` **asserts the delivered MP4 carries no priming edit list**.
  Nothing in the factory may call `npx hyperframes` again.

The image stays at 0.7.107 on purpose: the whole parity section of
`pipeline/render/README.md` was measured against it, the single disagreement is
now an explicit stream copy that can be read back, and moving the image pin
costs a rebuild plus a full re-verify.

### Proved on a fresh render, and it is one line of the report now

`render_and_check.py` on `shorts_run9/projects/chatgptchrome_cutout` (1080x1920,
684 frames, quality high) against `cuts/chatgptchrome/audio.m4a` — the same
project whose pre-fix Modal render is still on disk:

| `audio_guards` | sync lag | envelope r | `initial_padding` | treble delta | speech margin | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Modal, **before** | **-20 ms** | 0.9855 | 1024 | -0.23 dB | 22.12 dB | **FAIL** |
| Modal, **after** | **0 ms** | **0.9969** | **0** | -0.22 dB | 21.54 dB | **PASS** |

Every other check on the fresh render passed too (`decoded_blank_frames`,
`zero_ink_law`, `clip_coverage_page`, `face_centring`, `pill_canon_rendered`,
`cutout_checks_24_25`, `contact_sheet`; `double_exposure` REPORTED). The run
record carries `audio_elst = {"applied": true, "initial_padding_before": 1024,
"initial_padding_after": 0, "wall_s": 0.17}` — **0.17 s** inside a 464.6 s
batch, $0.0185 for the whole render-and-check.

`qc_pass`'s `audio_guards` also reports **`audio_initial_padding_samples`** now.
It is reported, not judged, and it is the whole point: **1024 there IS the
-20 ms.** The next agent that sees this verdict reads the cause on the same
line instead of bisecting for an evening.

`hf.sh`'s delivery assert was proved the same way, by deliberately breaking it:
`HF_BIN=<npx cache 0.7.107> hf.sh render sparkchrome_cutout -q draft` renders
fine and then **exits 4** with `carries an AAC priming edit list
(initial_padding=1024)`.

### The 80-second `npx` tax is gone, so nothing was installed globally

Measured, cold shell, 2026-09-03:

| | |
|---|---|
| `npx hyperframes --version` (unpinned) | **1.55 s** |
| same, with `NODE_OPTIONS=--dns-result-order=ipv4first` | **1.29 s** |
| `npx --yes hyperframes@0.7.107 --version` | **1.43 s** |
| `hf.sh --version` (two CLI invocations: assert + pass-through) | **1.24 s** |

The 79.9 s recorded in the benchmark table was the broken-IPv6 registry hang
(`reference_macbook_broken_ipv6`); it is not reproducing. `npm i -g` would have
bought nothing measurable, and the reason it was wanted was never speed — it was
the `latest`-tag roulette, which `hf.sh` removes outright.

# 2026-09-03 — THE CUTOUT CLIPPED HIS HEAD (`supergrokplus`, run 10)

Miguel, on the staged TikTok cutout: *"the caption pill sits on top of my cap —
the crown of my head runs under the pill"*, *"the cutout video is clipping my
head"*, *"first time this has happened"*.

## The defect, measured

| | shipped `_rejected_v1` | after the fix |
|---|---|---|
| `cap_top_on_plate` | **-10.1 plate px** (-11.1 canvas) | **+22.1** (+24.3 canvas) |
| envelope `union.y0` | **0** — the plate's own top row | **0**, but on 11/938 frames, not 938/938 |
| frames whose alpha touches row 0 | **938 of 938 (100 %)** | **11 of 938 (1.2 %)** |
| crown on the canvas | **930.0 — a flat ~490 px slice** | median **945**, a rounded cap |
| `CAP_Y` / pill bottom | 849.4 / 906.7 | 846.2 / **903.5** |
| clearance the seat CLAIMED | 26.5 px | 26.5 px |
| clearance the viewer GOT | **23.3 px, under a flat cut** | **26.5 px, under an arc** |

## Root cause: bottom-planting with no headroom rule

`pipeline/sam2/plate.py::window()` sizes the crop off head height alone and then
plants it on the master's bottom edge — `y0 = mh - ch`. Nothing in that
arithmetic knows where his head is. Every run-9 session cleared the crown by
14.3 - 134.2 plate px purely by where he happened to sit that day; run 10's two
prep-stage plates were the first to come out NEGATIVE (`supergrokplus` -10.1,
`moleculezoom` -17.1), because he sat high in the 4K master (`head_top` 350
against a crop top of 370) and the crop simply ate the top 20 master px of his
cap.

**No gate could see it.** LAW 44's edge-clip check gates the plate's LEFT and
RIGHT borders only — the plate's TOP is a legitimate crop of the master
everywhere else in the pipeline. The per-video envelope script had even written
the mistake down as a rule: *"THE HEAD MAY REACH THE PLATE'S TOP ROW, AND THAT
IS NOT A CLIP."* True of LAW 44; false of the viewer. The plate is painted 1:1
from canvas y 930 to 1920 with nothing but background above it, so an alpha that
touches row 0 IS a flat horizontal slice on the delivered frame — and the seat
then hangs the pill the canon clearance above that slice.

## Second, quieter bug found on the way

The seat was derived with `CAP_H` = 108.2, the frozen fix5 seat CONSTANT, while
the pill renders **114.59**. So every seat ever derived this way delivered
`26.5 - 6.39/2 = 23.3` px and reported 26.5. It never mattered while the crown
was an arc that only touches its apex. Per-video envelopes now use `CAP_H_TRUE`
for the clearance arithmetic and keep `CAP_H` only for Law 31's audit of the
pill's own box.

## The fix, at three levels

1. **`plate.py::window(head_top=…)`** — the crop is bottom-planted UNLESS that
   cuts the crown, in which case it slides up until the cap has
   `HEADROOM_ON_CANVAS` (24 canvas px) of clear plate above it. `k` and `x0` are
   untouched, so head height (496.8 px, law 496.0) and face centring
   (`face_dx_pct` 0.0) are untouched — the re-plate moved `y0` 370 -> 306 and
   `visible_window_drift_master_px` came back **0.0**. It spends the bottom of
   his chest, which the format runs off the canvas anyway.
2. **`platelib.build_plate` crown gate** — refuses a plate under
   `HEADROOM_HARD_FLOOR` (8 canvas px, the rim dilation) and records a
   `headroom` block in `plate.json`.
3. **`cutout6_check.check_crown_clearance` (check 27)**, wired into `qc_pass`'s
   cutout block — measured on the DELIVERED mp4, every 0.5 s: the caption pill's
   bottom edge (via `cutout3_check.pill_component`, because terracotta is the
   brand accent and a row-wise colour count picks up stage rules and card
   headers) and the first row of him underneath it.

## Calibrating check 27 — clearance alone cannot do it

| corpus | min clear | median | samples with the crown ON the plate's top row |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 approved run-9 cutouts | 25.0 - 38.0 | 33 - 58 | **0 - 1 %** |
| `supergrokplus` REJECTED | 25.0 | 25.0 | **100 %** |
| `moleculezoom` (same plate bug) | 25.0 | 25.0 | **100 %** |

The rejected build sits at the same 25 px as the approved `codexvoice`, because
the seat solver always puts the pill the same canon distance above whatever it
believes the crown to be. **What separates a head from a cut is WHERE the crown
is**, so the CUT test (`>= 25 %` of samples on the plate's top row) is the
discriminator and the 24 px clearance floor is only the backstop, set just under
the corpus minimum so no approved cutout is retro-failed.

## Cost of the repair

Sweep cached (free) · re-plate 355 s local · prompt0 55 s local ·
`track --tag v4` **$0.0939** Modal (238.3 s billed, 246.0 ms/frame, seams
0.99919/0.99953) · `ship.py` 112 s, **PROTRUSION clean, EDGE CLIP CLEAN** ·
one re-render. Gemini gate 3 and the clerk watcher were **BLOCKED-BILLING**
(`GEMINI_API_KEY_GENIAL` out of credits) and were skipped explicitly rather than
allowed to fail silently.

Fix: no CSS pivot, `svgOrigin:"x y"` in user space. Chassis now passes `svgOrigin` in user space on the set and the tween. No other fractional-scale or fill-box use remains in the format libs (grepped). ## 2026-09-04 — dgxspark cutout frame 0: the mirror pad decides frame 0, so frame 0's own alpha is dead

- **Miguel's finding:** "slight splash of my background on the first frame" on `dgxspark_cutout`. Measured: a 6,412 px blob of the wooden object behind him plus a grey/yellow strip, retained INSIDE the cut-out beside his raised right hand — canvas x 910-1020, y 1483-1627 on frame 0 only (a 27x25 px sliver of the same wood also survived on frame 2). Frames 1, 5 and 12 were clean.
- **Root cause: frame 0's own alpha never reaches the screen.** `ship.py`'s temporal median is MIRROR-padded (2026-08-31, and rightly so), so output frame 0's window is `[f1, f0, f1]` — and a 3-vote median with a duplicated vote IS that vote. **Output 0 is decided entirely by alpha frame 1.** His hand was travelling ~100 px/frame at the open, so f1's silhouette laid over frame 0's OWN picture uncovered the wood behind where the hand was about to be. SAM2 was never wrong: `alpha[0]` excluded that wood correctly. This is a registration defect of the smoother, not a tracking defect, which is why every gate passed it (protrusion clean, edge clip CLEAN, leak check clean) and why bolsterfix/wingfix would have had nothing to cut.
- **The fix that costs nothing: SWAP alpha frames 0 and 1.** Then output 0's window is `[f0, f1, f0]` -> f0, its own silhouette, and output 1's window is the same three votes in a different order, so **output 1 is bit-identical**. Only output 2's third vote changes (f0 instead of f1). Measured with each frame's own tracked silhouette as ground truth (`out_n & ~f_n` = pixels the composite reveals that the tracker did not claim): out0 7,195 -> **0**, out1 359 -> 359 (unchanged), out2 635 -> 312 (the frame-2 sliver went with it), out3-out5 identical. `alpha[1] := alpha[0]` also zeroes out0 but costs 2,030 px of hand on frame 1; the swap costs nothing anywhere.
- **Generalisation for the cleaning stage:** any fast limb at the open reproduces this, on every recording, and no existing gate can see it — the gates read the alpha, and the alpha is right. The cheap check is at ship time: for output frame 0 only, count pixels where the composed alpha is on and the frame's OWN pre-median alpha is off; over ~0 on a still open, thousands on a moving one. The remedy is mechanical (swap 0 and 1) and provably free on frame 1.
- **Run-13 review change 1, the clerk stops re-watching (2026-09-04):** `render_and_check` already ran `clerk_video_gemini.py` on each staged file as it landed and left `review/cands_<id>_<fmt>.json`; the clerk then ran the same script, same model, same 720x1280 encode, same prompt, on the same bytes into `clerk_cands_*.json` at $0.10-0.15 a video. Miguel: "remove the pure duplication in the second watch." Clerk step 1 is now a READ of `cands_<id>_<fmt>.json` (rows AND beat logs) and its own frame decode stays mandatory - run-13 recall was the watcher 0 of 2 real defects, the clerk 2 of 2. A missing cands file is reported, never backfilled; a render no driver watched may still be watched, because that is the first watch. `pipeline/semantic_review.md` v3.1, `STANDARD.md → RUN-13 REVIEW CHANGES §1`, `daily-shorts.js` CLERK.
- **Run-13 review change 2, the phone test goes cold and moves before the render (2026-09-04):** `phone_test_page.py` had cut the crops off the page since 2026-09-03 but only the builder looked at them, and a builder cannot un-know its own plan (that is how the moon shipped). The workflow now stops each author at BUILD-GREEN, has it copy the crops to `review/cold/<md5(<id>_<fmt>)[:8]>/NN.png` so not even the path names the video, and a fresh cheap agent (`effort: 'low'`, model inherited) names each crop in <=5 words with nothing else in its context. The author's SECOND stage opens the sealed key, scores by STANDARD's rule, writes verdicts into the manifest, and on a FAIL redesigns + re-runs both prerender tools + re-copies to a fresh cold folder for a DIFFERENT namer. At most 2 rounds, then it renders anyway and writes `review/phone_flag_<id>_<fmt>.md` for the clerk. There is no scripted key comparer in the factory (grepped: `judge_answer` exists only in `phone_crops.py` and the procedure), so the scoring is the author's, in the manifest. Economics: dgxspark's tank cost 31 min and $0.18 for ONE post-render redesign round.
- **Run-13 review change 3, only the cutout waits for the silhouette (2026-09-04):** the cut is ~70 s of an ~11 min prep and the plate sweep + prompt0 + track + ship (~10 min) serve the CUTOUT alone, yet every lane waited for the whole batch to close. `prep_batch.Stage.__exit__` now calls the new `mark_stage()`, which writes `<run>/prep/stages/<id>.<stage>.json` = {id, stage, status, wall_s, at, keys{}} the instant a stage lands (swallowed on failure - a marker is never a gate; `--emit` is the matte emit name and was never a per-stage record). The workflow LAUNCHES prep instead of awaiting it, a cut-gate agent per recording waits on that one marker, and the old SCENE AUTHOR is split into a SPLIT AUTHOR + a CUTOUT AUTHOR so the split and the whiteboard never wait on the matte; the cutout is gated on the ship marker. The shared lane scene had to become an artefact to survive the split: `plans/<id>_scene_handoff.md`, with the plan as the contract and the file as the convenience. Expected saving ~9-10 min per recording on 2 of 3 renders, and the recordings now flow through `pipeline()`, not `parallel()`, so no lane waits on a sibling.
- **Run-13 review change 4, an open doubt stops and asks (2026-09-04):** the plan schema gains `open_doubts[{question, changes_what_viewer_sees, options, your_lean}]` beside `open_questions`, and the workflow branches on it - any doubt that changes what the viewer sees logs one line, skips every builder for that recording, and returns it under `needs_miguel`. viberesearch is the case: three renders held by three clerks over a question ("the sentence says X, the card is the LinkedIn screenshot that X post carried") that one line to Miguel would have settled before a frame rendered.

## 2026-09-04 — LAW 48 is a gate now (outline.py), and the end frames stopped borrowing their neighbour's mask

### The finding

Miguel, on run 13: *"reasoning level cutout has a problem, the chair next to my head (left
side of the screen) is present as my outline. only this one will need redoing. we should add a
self-improving loop to that outline."* Same class as run 12's hermeskanban. Both had shipped
with `protrusion: clean` and `EDGE CLIP: CLEAN`.

### Root cause

`protrusion.py` only ever asks a TOP-Y question — a tab standing above a fitted shoulder line,
or a ledge hanging off the head. The defect is the half of a headrest WEDGE that survives to
the body side of a rectangular `wingfix` cut: it stands above nothing, it is welded to the
shoulder so `keep-largest` keeps it, and it hangs no higher than his own jaw. Structurally
invisible to both existing detectors.

### The two instruments, and the one thing that made them work

LAW 48 had already named them (straight silhouette column; retained plate-dark pixels). What
was NOT in the law and had to be measured is **where to look**. Over the whole crown-to-bottom
span neither instrument separates a rejected matte from an approved one:

- straight-run p95: 42-75 rows approved vs 46-132 rejected — no separation. Cause: his black
  CAP's side is a genuinely straight vertical edge for 40-107 rows.
- retained dark: 29,000-40,000 px on EVERY matte in the corpus, clean or not. Cause: his black
  T-SHIRT. The defect is a 2x on a five-figure baseline of his own clothes.

Windowed to the **head band** — the 180 rows ending at the shoulder arrival (jaw, neck,
shoulder-top) — both separate cleanly and nine of nine corpus verdicts come out right:

    straight-run p95      33-50 approved   ->  59-132 rejected     ceiling 60 rows
    frames at the 40-row line  0.018-0.264 ->  0.466-0.993         ceiling 0.40
    retained dark p95, share of band  0.14-0.62 -> 0.99-1.00       ceiling 0.78

The band is safe to derive because the plate solve freezes the geometry: over nine tracked
alphas the crown sits at row 13-28, the head is 323-334 px wide, and the shoulder arrival lands
at row 466-499. **This is the transferable lesson: an instrument aimed at furniture beside the
head must exclude the two black things that ARE him, and in this factory their rows are
constants.**

Both instruments are needed. hermeskanban v2 (rejected) is caught by the straight-edge test
alone; hermesdesktop v1 and dgxspark v1 far more loudly by the dark test; reasoninglevel v1 by
both.

### The self-improving loop

`prep_batch`'s third repairable gate. `wingfix` on the refusing side with the window the gate
MEASURED: band rows with the top lifted 20 and **the bottom left exactly at the shoulder
arrival** (no bottom margin — wingfix cuts every pixel darker than its guard and his shirt is
black; the hand-driven hermeskanban repair stopped 15 rows above its arrival for the same
reason), the cut column from the deepest inward retained-dark column plus 10 px, and
`--chunk 40`. **The gate reproduces the human's window to 1 px**: cut column 509 vs the 510 a
human read off `wingfix --measure` and shipped.

The saturation trap, worth knowing: instrument 2 counts inside a fixed 50-column band, and the
count SATURATES when the furniture is wider than that (reasoninglevel: 9,048 of 9,050 px). A
saturated count cannot size a repair window, so the cut column comes from a separate `reach`
walk with no ceiling. First version of that walk counted quiet columns from the outermost
silhouette column — where one or two rows carry mask and nothing clears the floor — and ended
before it started, returning no window at all. The gap rule only applies once the wedge has
been found.

### Result

reasoninglevel refused in **0.77 s** of CPU (the whole gate, 765 frames, both files decoded at
stride 5), one repair round, $0.1523 of H100, PASS. Left side straight p95 87 -> 42 rows,
at-line 99.4 % -> 9.2 %, dark p95 9,048 px (100 % of band) -> 1,388 px (15 %). The left edge
moved off the frozen chair column onto his body (row 360: column 472 -> 540) and began MOVING
like a human edge — jitter p95 1 px -> 3 px against costpertask's accepted 4 px. **The frozen
edge was the tell all along: a chair does not move, and the pre-repair alpha read jitter 0.25
px mean / p95 1 px at rows 240-420 while every accepted matte reads 1.8-3.0 / 3-5.**

### Known limit, accepted by Miguel

The law says p95, so p95 refuses, and a sub-second burst is invisible to it. hermesdesktop v2's
right side maxes at 8,873 px (0.98 of the band) on ONE frame at 1.4 s — the chair splash at the
start of that take Miguel saw and told us not to redo. Every other approved matte's max is
<= 5,671, so a max test at ~7,000 would catch it and pass everything else. Not built: it would
refuse a file its owner accepted. `dark_frac_max` is recorded and never gated.

## 2026-09-04 — the temporal median gave frame 0 its NEIGHBOUR's silhouette (LAW 49)

Found by the dgxspark frame-0 agent, fixed here because it lives in `ship.render`.

A BINARY MEDIAN WITH A DUPLICATED VOTE IS THAT VOTE — and the two padding modes duplicate
DIFFERENT frames. `replicate`'s window at output 0 is `[f0, f0, f1]` and resolves to f0.
**`mirror`'s is `[f1, f0, f1]` and resolves to f1.** So from 2026-08-31, when mirror became the
default for a measured reason, the opening frame of every matte carried frame ONE's silhouette
over frame ZERO's picture, and the tail frame carried the second-to-last's.

Measured on the alphas with `post.spatial`, pixels the neighbour's mask adds that the frame's
own does not have: dgxspark alpha_v2 frame 0 **7,195** (tail 1,466), viberesearch 2,140 (1,573),
reasoninglevel 1,340 (2,044), hermeskanban 705 (97). On dgxspark those 7,195 px are background
revealed inside a hand that moves ~100 px in that frame, **on a track SAM2 had got right.**

**The measurement that justified mirror was measuring the wrong frame.** The 2026-08-31 note
records frame-0 right-edge curvature 0.794 under replicate against 0.483 under mirror and reads
that as mirror smoothing frame 0. It was not smoothing frame 0; it had REPLACED it with frame
1, and 0.483 is frame 1's curvature. A number that looks like an improvement can be a number
measured on a different object.

The fix is independent of `pad`: an end frame takes its window's own centre frame and skips the
median (exactly what a replicate window resolves to, for any window size), and `windows()`
carries one frame of lookahead so the LAST output frame can be named in a streaming pass. Only
two frames of a take change; both `workers` paths carry the flag, so the workers-1 = workers-12
md5 parity is untouched. `end_frame_check` in the ship json records `revealed_px` (0 by
construction, recorded anyway) plus `median_would_add_px` / `median_would_lose_px` per end
frame — reasoninglevel's redone matte reports 1,340 and 2,044, i.e. exactly the defect it no
longer ships.

## 2026-09-04 — the chair is a SECOND SAM2 OBJECT, and that ends the rectangle era

Miguel, on the shipped `reasoninglevel` cutout: *"my left shoulder is chopped on a straight
vertical line, and at the end a piece of the headrest arm sits by my left ear."* Both are the
same defect, and neither is a tracking failure: SAM2 got one positive prompt and nothing in the
pipeline ever said **that black thing beside the black cap is not him**. So every repair had to
be a RECTANGLE (`wingfix`) carved out of a wedge that slants one column per 3.3 rows — the
window's bottom amputates the shoulder, its top leaves the arm by the ear.

**SAM2 is a multi-object segmenter and the factory used one object.** `_track` now takes
`exclude=` (`--exclude-box` / `--exclude-points` / `--exclude-dilate`): extra objects prompted on
frame 0, tracked in the SAME propagation loop, and the emitted alpha is
`obj1 AND NOT (union of them)` per frame, each dilated 2 px so no fringe survives. Obj 1 is
handed the SUBTRACTED mask across a chunk boundary, so its memory bank stops carrying the
furniture instead of re-acquiring it every 350 frames. `exclude=None` is byte-identical to
every track before it.

**One box and seven clicks beat 80 corrective keyframe masks, on every instrument.**
`reasoninglevel`, chair residue in `x 440..570 / y 190..450` (mask ∧ plate luma ≤ 60):

| | median | p95 | max | frames > 1,000 px |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1, the file Miguel rejected | 12,339 | 15,764 | 16,895 | 383/383 |
| v2, the shipped wingfix repair | 723 | 1,964 | 3,383 | 81/383 |
| **chair as obj 2** | **487** | **925** | **1,051** | **5/383** |

The ear band alone (`y 190..290`, above where the wingfix window started) drops from a 3,357 px
max to 888, and the LAST 2.6 s of the take — Miguel's "at the end" — from mean 965 / max 3,357
to mean 224 / max 330. Edge jitter on the amputated rows collapses: row 480 goes from
15.58 px mean / **p95 75** / 28.1 % of frames moving ≥ 5 px to 0.78 / **p95 1** / 0.9 %, and row
460 from 4.98 / 27.0 / 14.5 % to 0.98 / 2.0 / 0.7 %. Both are then BETTER than `costpertask`,
the matte Miguel accepted. Cap rows and the whole right side are unchanged to the pixel
(median diff 0.0), so nothing was traded for it.

**It is also cheaper and simpler than the repair it replaces.** Two objects tracked at
117.0 ms/frame against 157.6 for the one-object wingfix re-track (80 keyframe masks cost more
than a second object does), **$0.1156 against $0.1523**, and all three gates passed on round 0 —
no refusal, no wingfix, no second GPU run. The rejected v1 + the v2 repair cost two H100 tracks;
this cost one.

**Why it works when a rectangle cannot.** The subtraction boundary is SAM2's own contour of the
chair, which slants exactly as the chair slants and moves as the chair moves. A rectangle has to
choose between his shoulder and the chair's upper arm; a tracked object does not choose.
Corollary for the gates: the new matte's retained-dark p95 is HIGHER than the wingfix's
(1,973 px vs 1,388) because the wingfix was removing HIS OWN dark shirt. A furniture instrument
reading lower can mean the mask is holding less chair, or it can mean the mask is holding less
Miguel — the two are only separable by looking at what was removed.

## 2026-09-04 — the 4 px chair margin: it works, it is not what Miguel is seeing

Miguel approved the chair-as-second-object outline and asked to see the exclusion margin at
4 px, because a faint 1-2 px dark sliver still reads along his left temple and ear at ~8 s and
~16 s.  Same plate, same obj-1 prompt, same chair prompt, `--exclude-dilate 4`, new session
`reasoninglevel_chair2obj_d4`.  **The gates cannot tell 2 px from 4 px** (left straight p95 39 /
at-line 5.2 % in both; left dark p95 1,973 → 1,858 px), so this was decided by instruments and
by looking.

**THE SLIVER IS HIS CAP AND THE CREASE BEHIND HIS EAR, NOT CHAIR.**  A diagnostic that paints
every mask pixel within 8 px of the left edge whose plate luma < 45, at f200 (8 s) and f400
(16 s), puts every one of those pixels in ONE place: a small blob at rows ~185-215 where his
BLACK CAP BRIM meets the wall, above the ear.  Along the ear and temple contour, rows 220-330,
there is not a single dark pixel inside the edge in either run — the surviving edge sits on
bright skin and the chair's own boundary runs 2-4 px outside it.  Measured the same way at the
two frames he named, the jaw/cheek sliver (rows 300-420, gated on the edge's outside neighbour
also being dark, so his hair cannot masquerade as chair) is **already 0 px at 2 px of margin**.
No margin can remove what he is seeing, because removing it means cutting into his cap.

**What 4 px genuinely buys.**  On the jaw/cheek rows the residual sliver goes 0.7 → **0.0** px
per frame (deepest run max 4 → 1), and the whole-band chair residue (`x 440..570 / y 190..450`)
goes median 488 → 387 px with **frames over 1,000 px 11/765 → 0/765**.  Real, and small.

**What it costs.**  A flat 736 px per frame of him (−0.141 % of the silhouette), and the
left-edge contour moves exactly **+2 px** at every chair-contact row (200, 240, 280, 320, 360,
400), +3 at row 440 and **+5 at row 460** — the shoulder transition the wingfix used to
amputate.  The four no-chair control rows (60, 150, 540, 700) move **0.0 px**, so the mechanism
is clean: the margin costs only where the chair touches him.  Jitter is unchanged (row 240
0.95 → 1.01, row 460 0.98 → 0.92).

**THE COST IS SPENT ON THE WRONG PIXELS, AND ONE NUMBER SAYS SO.**  Of the 720 px/frame the
wider margin removes, **401 are bright (luma >= 110) — his skin — and only 230 are dark**
(luma < 45, chair or hair).  So 56 % of the extra cut buys nothing.  Classifying the chair
mask's own boundary by what sits just outside it: **54.2 % is a body-contact seam and 42.8 %
faces bright wall.**  A CONTACT-AWARE margin is therefore the wrong shape — the extra margin is
free precisely where the chair faces the WALL and expensive where it touches him, i.e. the
opposite of "wide where it touches".  The right refinement is simpler and already has a
precedent in `wingfix`'s `luma_guard`: **dilate the exclusion mask by 4 px but only into pixels
darker than luma ~60.**  That keeps the 230 px/frame of extra dark removal — which is exactly
what closes the jaw sliver and the 11 over-1,000-px frames — and gives back all 401 px of skin.
Estimated from these two runs; it needs one more track to confirm.

**The default was NOT changed.**  `EXCL_DILATE` stays 2.  d4 cost $0.1084 on the H100 (91.5
billed s, 110.4 ms/frame, seams 0.99915 / 0.99924, leak clean) and passed all three gates on
round 0.

## 2026-09-04 — the luma-gated dilation: the ear-top junction, and why a flat margin is the wrong tool

Miguel, after approving the chair-as-second-object outline: *"there's just something right at the
top of my ear, it's the headrest right at the junction with my ear."*

**LOOKING FIRST FOUND THE PIXELS AND SETTLED WHAT THEY ARE.**  Painting every plate-dark
(luma < 60) pixel the mask still keeps, at 13-14x on the ear top, at 1 / 8 / 16 / 24 / 29.5 s:
they are a thin vertical strip at **plate x ≈ 502-512, rows ≈ 194-232**, running from under his
cap brim down to where his ear tip begins, **60.8 px per frame** on average (median 71, p95 101,
max 119; present on 653 of 765 frames).  Their plate luma is mean 25 / p95 40 / max 59, so the
`wingfix` guard of 60 catches all of them.  Two things sit in that band and both are black: the
strip that is CONTIGUOUS with the chair (the headrest arm passing behind his ear — the thing he
means) and, further right, his own CAP BRIM, which on many frames is separated from the chair by
a bright sliver of wall.  Any tool that cannot tell them apart will eat his cap.

**A DARK-GATED GEODESIC DILATION CAN TELL THEM APART, BECAUSE A BRIGHT PIXEL STOPS IT.**  New
option (default OFF, `luma_dilate: 0`): grow the exclusion mask a further N px by geodesic
dilation inside `{plate luma < luma_max}`, seeded from the UNDILATED chair mask, fenced to
`luma_rows`.  Run on `reasoninglevel` at `luma_dilate 8, luma_max 60, luma_rows 194..432`
(the fence protects the two black things that are HIS and touch the chair: his cap above, his
t-shirt below — unfenced, 333 of the 375 px/frame a reach of 6 removes are his SHIRT).

| | junction px rows 194-232 (mean / p95 / max) | takes from him | of which BRIGHT SKIN | left-edge shift on the 3 skin control rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 px flat (approved) | 60.8 / 101 / 119 | — | — | — |
| 4 px flat | 33.1 / 55 / 75 | 720 px/frame | **401** | +2, +2, +2 |
| **2 px + 8 px dark-only** | **15.9 / 43 / 53** | **65 px/frame** | **0.6** | **+0, +0, +0** |

**Twice the reduction of a flat 4 px, for 9 % of its cost and 1/670th of its skin.**  The
column-shift table is the proof it is aimed: `+0.0 px` at rows 320, 360, 400 (his jaw, where 4 px
cost 2 px each), `+0.0` at 440 and 460 (where 4 px cost 3 and 5), `+0.0` at all four no-chair
controls, and `+1.0` at row 200 — the junction, and nowhere else.  Of the extra cut, 59.1 of
64.7 px/frame land in rows 194-232.  In the shipped `cut` layer it removes a median of 91 px
(p95 146, max 182 at 8.88 s) and gives back 12.

**The cost, honestly.**  Edge jitter rises at the two junction rows and only there: row 200 goes
1.16 px mean / p95 3 / 1.6 % of frames moving >= 5 px to **1.61 / p95 6 / 7.9 %**, row 215 from
1.05 / 4 / 3.8 % to 1.38 / 6 / 8.1 %.  That is the flood's reach flipping frame to frame with
whether the dark region happens to be contiguous.  It is still at `costpertask`'s own row-180
numbers (2.19 / 5 / 7.2 %), the matte Miguel accepted, and every other row is unchanged to two
decimals.

**It does not remove ALL of them, and it should not.**  15.9 px/frame survive because on many
frames a bright wall sliver separates the chair from his cap and the flood correctly stops there
— what is left is his cap brim.  Pushing the reach to 16 px does clear it, and the simulation
shows exactly what that costs: a 383 px bite out of his cap at 1 s and 215 px at 24 s.  8 px is
the last value that takes the strip and leaves the cap.

**Nothing became a default.**  `EXCL_DILATE` stays 2 and `luma_dilate` stays 0.  Deployed v17,
$0.1184 on the H100 (99.9 billed s, 118.8 ms/frame, seams 0.99915 / 0.9993, leak clean), all
three gates clean on round 0 and the gates cannot see the change (left dark p95 1,973 -> 1,972).

## 2026-09-04 — the chair object became the MAIN PASS, and the automatic prompt that made it possible

Miguel: *"sure make it the main pass! let me know once our system is ready again."*  So the
two-object matte with the dark-only margin stopped being a test and became what `prep_batch`
runs, with no human choosing a box.

**THE DEFAULTS LIVE IN ONE PLACE, AND THE FENCE IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED.**  `modal_app.py` holds
`EXCL_DILATE` 2, `EXCL_LUMA_DILATE` 8, `EXCL_LUMA_MAX` 60; `track.py` sends only the flags a
caller actually gave, so a driver can no longer silently pin an old value.  The fence — the rows
the dark flood may grow in — comes from `derive_band()`, a by-value copy of `outline.py::_band`,
as `crown + 180 .. shoulder arrival - 48`: crown-relative at the top because the ear-top
junction's rows are set by his head, arrival-relative at the bottom because what it protects is
his black t-shirt.  On `reasoninglevel` the deployed container derived **[194, 433]** — the
hand-measured value of the day before, to a row.  **When no band is measurable the gate turns
ITSELF off** and the flat margin still runs, because an unfenced flood removes 333 px/frame of
his shirt out of the 375 it removes at all.

**THE DETECTOR'S FOUR REAL LESSONS**, each one a bug I hit and measured:

1. **The signal is a sandwich, not a dark region.**  `bright wall | DARK HEADREST | bright skin`
   is specific; "a dark connected region beside the head" is not — his cap, his t-shirt and his
   hair are all dark regions beside his head.
2. **Label connected regions; never chain rows.**  A row-by-row chain follows whichever run is
   outermost and drifts: `hermesdesktop`'s right-hand chain drifted 194 px of columns and every
   width test then rejected it.
3. **The search must not start in his cap.**  With no floor, one cap run joins the component and
   every wing becomes 260 rows tall and 200 px wide.  `cap_floor` = `crown + 165` fixed
   `hermesdesktop`, which had been failing on both sides.
4. **The band that finds the wings is inflated BY the wings.**  BiRefNet takes them, so the
   silhouette width reaches 1.35x too early: `hermesdesktop`'s arrival read 405 against a true
   ~470.  Two passes — find, subtract, re-derive — and the second band is the one recorded.

Two smaller ones with real teeth: a positive click on the wing's FIRST row is a click on the
cap/wing boundary, which is how you tell SAM2 his cap is the chair (`pos_inset` 12 %); and the
obvious shoulder negative — "below the box, at the wing's centre column" — lands **ON THE CHAIR**
whenever the box stops short of the wing's bottom, so it now steps inboard of the wing first and
walks down from the arrival to the first row that is mask-on and plate-black.

**Seven of eight left wings, one right, and the right miss is where the defect is NOT.**  On the
right his hair and sideburn are dark and touch the wing, so the sandwich fails.  LAW 48's own
calibration says the same from the other end: every approved matte's right side runs dark p95
0.50-0.62 and was accepted, and both files Miguel rejected were LEFT.  `viberesearch` finds
nothing on either side because no wing is beside his head on that plate, and it gets the old
pass byte-identical — which is what it shipped with.

**`dgxspark` proves it does not regress an approved matte.**  Three gates clean round 0, right
side at-line 26.7 % -> 2.6 % and dark p95 5,251 -> 5,155, left residue median 389 -> 311 and
p95 803 -> 659, straight p95 +1 row (46 against a 60 ceiling), jitter identical within noise on
14 rows of both edges, area -923 px/frame.

**`reasoninglevel` proves the whole chain.**  Standard prep matte stages, no manual prompt: the
automatic box came out `[460,176,566,443]` against the hand-picked `[450,188,566,458]` — within
10-15 px on every edge — and its four positives within 5-17 px of the hand clicks.  Track PASS in
**round 0** (LAW 48 left p95 37.8, at-line 4.6 %, dark 1,991 px = 22 %, against the wingfix v2's
42 / 9.2 % / 1,388), one GPU run, $0.1228.  Cutout page only, split project byte-identical
(md5 of md5s unchanged), prerender_check PASS 0/0, render_and_check PASS in 136.2 s
($0.0143 + $0.0375 watcher, qc_pass 16/16 with `double_exposure` REPORTED as always and
`gate3_gemini_describe` PASS, watcher PASS on the one known non-blocking `empty_zone`).  In the
DELIVERED composites the black stub that used to poke out of the cream rim beside his ear at f25,
f200, f400, f600 and f760 is gone from all five.

**What is honest about the cost.**  The pass is cheaper than the repair it replaces — 117 ms/frame
for two objects against 157.6 for a one-object wingfix re-track, and one GPU run instead of two —
so making it the default lowers the factory's per-video spend rather than raising it.

## 2026-09-04 — the shoulder arrival was measuring the chair, and a rejected fix worth keeping

**THE ARRIVAL TEST READ THE WINGS AS A SHOULDER.**  `_band` finds the shoulder where the
silhouette's width reaches 1.35x the head's — and while the headrest wings are inside the
silhouette, the silhouette's extreme columns ARE the wings.  On `hermesdesktop`'s frame-0 mask
`left` sits at 519-530 and `right` at 943-966 for a hundred and fifty rows, so the width creeps
416 -> 448, clears 442.1 at row 406, and reports a shoulder seventy rows before the real one at
476 (where `right` jumps 965 -> 995 -> 1017).  `reasoninglevel` escaped the same trap by ELEVEN
PIXELS of width.  Every plate in the corpus was one plushie away from this.

**A head-plus-furniture column is near-vertical; a shoulder FLARES.**  The fix walks forward from
the 1.35x candidate to the first row whose width grew 20 px over the preceding 20 rows.  It can
only move the arrival later.  hermesdesktop 405 -> **474**, reasoninglevel 481 -> 484, the other
six unchanged; hermesdesktop's chair box bottom 368 -> 437 and its fence 357 -> 426.

**The same code runs inside the GATE, so the calibration had to be re-proved, and it held.**
`reasoninglevel` v1 still refuses at 87 / 99.4 % / 9,048; `hermeskanban` v2 still refuses at
132 / 20.0 % / 4,212, matching the LAW 48 calibration table to the pixel; four approved mattes
came back byte-identical.  The one alpha that moved is `hermesdesktop` v1 — the only one that
still contains its wings — and it refuses HARDER (at-line 46.6 % -> 82.2 %).  A fix that changes
a measurement everywhere is only safe if you re-run the calibration; this one was, and it is.

**A FIX CAN FIGHT THE FIX BEFORE IT.**  The two-pass band existed to stop the wings inflating the
width.  With the flare test in place it does harm: subtracting the wing over the rows the detector
labelled, and NOT below them, leaves an artificial width STEP at the wing's last labelled row, and
a step is exactly what a flare test looks for.  Pass 1 read 474, pass 2 read 434 — its own
artifact.  The rule now is that a second pass may only move the arrival LATER.

**THE REJECTED FIX IS THE MOST USEFUL THING I MEASURED TODAY.**  With the arrival corrected,
hermesdesktop's right-hand component merges and the tallest search window loses that wing.
Shortening the window rescues it — and invents a right-hand "wing" on SEVEN of the eight
recordings, every one a box over his cheek and nose with positive clicks on his skin.  A false
chair object CARVES HIS FACE, so a detector that trades false negatives for false positives is
strictly worse than one that abstains.  Both obvious discriminators fail: "the component's
outboard edge must touch the silhouette edge" passes the false positives, and "outside the head's
bright core" fails the true wings, whose wedges slant inboard as they descend.  The ladder is one
entry long and the finding is in the config comment where the next person will look.

**THE GUARD: a repair is never silently re-derived.**  `prompt0` now compares
`prompts/kf_00000.png` against `prompts/_original/kf_00000.png` — one standard backup name,
written the first time anything touches the prompt, replacing four ad-hoc ones — and KEEPS a
repaired prompt unless `--reset-prompt` says otherwise.  It costs 0.2 s instead of 14 s when it
fires, and it is what stops the standard pass from undoing a repair the way it did on
hermesdesktop.  The replate branch resets unconditionally, because a new plate size makes the old
prompt's pixels meaningless.

**hermesdesktop, with everything fixed, is STRICTLY BETTER OR EQUAL AND STILL NOT SHIPPED.**  The
guard kept its repaired prompt, the chair object's box reached the wing bottom, three gates clean
round 0: left residue (rows 180-390) median **137 -> 49** px/frame, p95 686 -> 552, max 1,077 ->
936; LAW 48 left p95 40 -> 40.5, at-line 6.2 % -> 5.5 %, dark 2,307 -> 1,998; area -723 px/frame
that ADDS only 24 and removes 758, i.e. it takes the chair and gives nothing back (against c1's
+11,434).  But the RIGHT side is unchanged — median 1,842 -> 1,838, the 0.24 s splash 10,106 ->
9,964 px — because no right wing was found, so there is nothing to improve it with.  The ship
condition was "left p95 under 52 AND the right residue better than v2"; the right is EQUAL, not
better, so it was not staged and v2 was restored.  Equal is not better, and a rule that only
binds when it agrees with me is not a rule.

## 2026-09-04 — THE COST LEDGER: a number re-added by hand is a number reported wrong

Miguel: *"add native cost tracking to all of this. by the end of the video I want
to know modal cost per video plus per total run as well as gemini costs ... every
paid service I want to quantify."*

**Problem.** Every paid call in this factory already prices itself correctly. The
run TOTAL did not exist anywhere. `prep/_batch.json` held the prep Modal spend,
each `gen/_rc_*.json` held its own renders and watchers, `review/cands_*.json`
and `clerk_cands_*.json` each held one Gemini bill, Gate 3's cost was PRINTED by
`qc_v3.py` and stored by nobody, `pipeline/sam2/sessions/*/run_*.json` held every
hand-run track, and ElevenLabs Scribe was never priced at all. Assembling a run's
cost meant opening six file families and adding by hand — which is exactly what
`RUN13_E2E_REPORT.md` did, and it came out at ~$2.7.

**What the artefacts actually say.** Run 13 = **$4.3291** over 12 staged files
(**$0.361 per delivered short**): Modal $2.5821, Gemini $1.6653, ElevenLabs
$0.0816. Run 12 = **$3.2718** over 11 files ($0.297 each). Reconciliation against
the hand table, item by item:

| item | hand | ledger | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| prep Modal (sweep + 4 tracks + re-prep) | 0.78 | 0.7810 | agrees |
| author-side re-tracks | ≈0.22 | 0.2032 | the two v2 tracks, measured not estimated |
| renders | 0.22 | 0.2904 | 24 render records on disk, not the 17 counted |
| post-render watchers | 0.84 | 0.9981 | 24 `cands` files incl. every `.priorN` fix round |
| clerk re-watch | 0.50 | 0.4996 | agrees |
| Gate 3 | ≈0.16 | 0.1676 | the guess was close; the number was always recoverable |
| reasoninglevel outline redo | — | 0.1523 | re-tracked after the bench note was written |
| ElevenLabs Scribe (2 passes/video) | — | 0.0816 | never priced by anything |
| chair job (9 GPU containers) | (excluded) | 1.1552 | the report said "before the chair job" |

So the hand total was **$0.45 low on the run itself**, and $1.61 low once the
chair job is in. Nothing exotic went missing: it was fix rounds, one late re-track, and
a service nobody had a rate for.

**Solution.** `pipeline/costs.py` — an append-only `<run>/costs.jsonl`, one line
per paid call, written at the moment the price is measured, out of the number the
caller already computed. Key = `service|stage|video|fmt|ref`, replace-by-key, and
`ref = <path relative to the run>@<the call's own identity>` (the container's
`t_import_epoch` or `container` id, the render's epoch for the watcher that
watched it, the audio duration for Scribe). That is what makes a retry a new row
and a re-read a replacement. `pipeline/cost_report.py` totals per service, per
stage, per video, per format, per run, plus cost per delivered short, into
`<run>/review/COSTS.md` + `costs.json`; `render_and_check --stage` runs it after
its last render so the number exists by the end of the video.
`pipeline/costs_backfill.py` reconstructs a pre-ledger run from its artefacts —
and its docstring is the map of where every dollar used to hide.

**Three things the reconciliation taught.**

1. **A `.priorN` archive is money, and every hand table forgets it.** The
   archive discipline (`_archive_prior`) saved the reports; the arithmetic never
   read them. The $0.23 the hand table missed on renders and watchers is exactly
   the fix rounds it did not open.

## 2026-09-04 — run 14's three prep failures, and three fixes that live in the pipeline

Miguel: *"every time you encounter bugs like this fix them; the idea is to have a self-healing
loop."*  Run 14 was the first batch on the standard chain and all three cut-outs failed prep.
Each fix went in at the source with a regression check
(`pipeline/prep/test_regressions_2026_09_04.py`, 5 checks, asserted against the run-14 case).

**1. trycrm — a paid track was lost by the LAST LINE of the driver.**  `track.py` writes the run
record after downloading the alpha and collecting the remote ship, and it died on
`TypeError: Object of type bytes is not JSON serializable`.  The culprit is `alpha_preheal`: when
the leak heal runs and the second sweep STILL fires, `_track` hands back BOTH tracks, and the
driver popped `alpha` and `alpha_exclude` but never the third.  trycrm was the first take to trip
it — leak `furniture`, healed, `needs_human`.  Three fixes, not one: pop the third blob by name;
wrap the write in a `json_safe` walk that turns any stray bytes into a marker naming its size and
WARNS, so no future field can ever cost a track again; and — because the artifacts all survive a
crash there — teach the ship stage to `recover_run_record()` from the container's own copy on the
volume when the local one is missing.  **A record written last is a record that can lose
everything that came before it.**

**2. grokbuild — the outline gate was refusing HIS OWN JAW.**  LAW 48's right side refused at
straight p95 78, two wingfix rounds ran (61, then 79 — worse), and it arrived as "the known
right-side miss".  It is not a miss.  The refusal window is cut column 494 with the silhouette
edge at 768: a **275 px** "wedge", and on frame 0 the dark inside the mask there is his beard,
lips, jaw and neck, with the chair correctly EXCLUDED just outside the edge — cut column 494 sits
in his chin.  He is leaning, so his jaw-to-shoulder line is near-vertical for 61-79 rows and
instrument 1 fires on anatomy.  **The two carves punched 7,719 and 8,174 px per frame of holes in
his dark neck** (8,119 px/f of removed dark against 36 px/f of bright skin) while moving the right
edge 0-10 px.  So v1 uncarved is the correct matte and it shipped with `--allow-outline` carrying
all of that as its written reason.  Only `straight_p95` fails (61 vs 60); at-line 29.3 % and dark
59.4 % are both well inside.  **Whether the 60-row ceiling — calibrated on nine alphas of him
sitting UPRIGHT — should widen for a pronounced lean is a calibration decision for Miguel, and I
did not touch it to make one video pass.**

**3. THE SELF-HEAL: a chair object derived from the gate's own refusal.**  Both gates hand back
the window they are complaining about, so that window is a seed for an exclusion object and the
repair loop can now reach for the right tool before the blunt one:
`chairprompt.from_refusal()` + `prep_batch.chair_from_gate()`, tried BEFORE wingfix in both the
protrusion and outline branches.  It worked first time on **trycrm AND game33c** — both refused
protrusion on the right, both had a real wing there, both derived a prompt from the gate's numbers
and passed after one round with **no cut and no human**.  A chair-object fix reuses the previous
round's prompts, because it changes `exclude=`, not the frame-0 mask.

**THE GUARD MATTERS MORE THAN THE FEATURE.**  A first cut grew the seed into its connected
component so the wedge's inboard slant would come along — and at those rows every dark thing is
connected, so the region ran through his beard, neck and shirt: grokbuild 291 px, trycrm 349.  So
the window is now used VERBATIM (a chair object does not need a precise box; SAM2 refines from the
clicks) and it must LOOK like a wedge: wider than `max_box_w` 150 and it is called **"not a
wing"** and no prompt is produced.  That single test is what stops the self-heal carving a face,
and it is why grokbuild's false positive came out as a FINDING — *"that is a body, not a wedge …
the remedy is a reasoned --allow-outline, NOT another cut"* — instead of a third automatic carve.
**A self-healing loop needs a way to say "this is not my kind of problem" or it will confidently
break things.**

## 2026-09-05 — run 14 did not fail on craft, it failed on quitting

Two things ended run 14, and neither was a bad video.

**The workflow quit a lane on a transient failure.** The ship gate read `trycrm.ship.json` status
`"error"` and `grokbuild.ship.json` `"REFUSED"`, reported STOP, and the cutout lane was over.
`trycrm`'s "error" was a crash on the LAST LINE of `track.py` **after a successful paid track**,
with every artifact intact; `grokbuild`'s "REFUSED" was fixed by a repair agent twenty minutes
later, which rewrote the marker to `"ok"` — with nothing left watching it. The cutouts were only
built when the run was resumed by hand. `game33c` lost its plan and all three lanes the same way,
on a cut refusal that turned out to be the inner-stumble rule bug. **A marker is a snapshot of a
moving thing: prep's own auto-repair re-stamps it in place, so reading one non-ok marker and
quitting is reading the middle of a repair as if it were the end of one.**

**The Claude usage cap killed the run, twice in two runs.** Agents died with API 429
"session limit · resets HH:MM", the remaining `agent()` calls returned null, the run ended at
staged 2/9, and it was resumed 3.5 h later by hand with `resumeFromRunId`. Nothing was wrong with
the factory; the workflow simply had no way to wait.

**The fix, all of it in `.claude/workflows/daily-shorts.js` (the Workspace one, not $HOME)** (see STANDARD.md "THE RUN NEVER
QUITS"):

1. **Gates wait through a repair.** `error`/`REFUSED` is not final. The gate keeps watching for the
   marker to be rewritten, accepts a `<id>.<stage>.override.json` from a repair agent, and is
   polled three times with a wait between. Only `SKIPPED_NEEDS_KEY`, `not_a_short` and a
   still-non-ok marker at timeout are final.
2. **One repair round per recording.** A non-ok gate or lane spawns a REPAIR agent modelled on the
   prep fixes of 2026-09-04 — root-cause on the artefacts, fix at the source with a regression
   check, re-run only that recording's failed stages via a one-row intake + `--skip`, rewrite the
   marker — and then the gate and the lane run again. After that, `needs_miguel`, and the run
   carries on around it. Every non-ok lane lands in the result under `needs_repair` with the error
   verbatim.
3. **A cap is a wait.** One wrapper around every `agent()` call: detect the cap by the error text
   (or by a cheap sentinel probe *also* failing, which is the same signal from outside), log
   `USAGE CAP at <label>; waiting`, sleep ~10 min in a `sleep 570` sleeper agent — a workflow
   script has no clock, `Date.now()` would break resume — and retry the SAME call. Six ticks in the
   first hour, up to 6 h. Any other failure retries twice, then is recorded and the run continues.
   **Nothing throws out of a lane any more.**
4. **Two sentinels per brief.** `agent()` returns *null* on a terminal API error, with no reason and
   no way to tell a killed agent from one that finished and lost its return. So every brief writes
   `review/agent_started_<label>.txt` first and `review/agent_done_<label>.json` last, and **reads
   its own done file before doing any work** — returning it verbatim if it is there. That is what
   makes `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})` after a cap continue instead of rebuild.

**Smaller things that came with it.** The clerk now runs on whatever staged, so a failed lane no
longer costs a video its audit, and the result carries per recording: staged formats, missing
formats with reason, clerk verdict. `costs:report` is Bash-only, low effort, and cannot fail the
run. `costs:report` + the Drive push are a `Deliver` phase, and the push goes only to
clerk-PASS recordings (`push_run_to_drive.py --ids …`) — a HOLD does not land in Miguel's Drive
folder looking finished. `DEFAULT_RUN` is `shorts_run15`.

**And the workflow is now testable without spending a cent.** `pipeline/workflow_dryrun.mjs` loads
the real script with stubbed `agent()/pipeline()/parallel()/log()/phase()` and drives the five
cases that used to be silent: error→ok on the 3rd poll, null twice then a value, a cap error text,
a resume where the done-files exist, and a marker that stays non-ok until the repair agent fixes
it. All five pass. **Run it after any edit to `daily-shorts.js`** — one of its assertions is that
*every* brief carries its own done-file check, so a new brief added without a sentinel fails the
harness instead of failing a run at 2 a.m.
- **"Groq" in captions (Miguel, 2026-09-05):** Scribe wrote Groq for Grok despite the keyterm hint, and captions print the transcript verbatim; grokbuild shipped with "Groq Build" on screen. Fix at the source: `execution/transcription_vocabulary.json` now carries a `corrections` map and `cutlib.apply_corrections()` rewrites every transcript word after Scribe (multi-word keys, punctuation kept, changes recorded under `corrections_applied`); regression test added. Generators that anchor on a word's text must use the corrected spelling (grokbuild's "groq" anchors were updated). Grok Build re-rendered x3, $0.17.

## 2026-09-05: the fix that removed the chair also removed his face

The 2026-09-05 flicker repair worked and the clerk still held it. The chair back was gone on all 691 frames of `game33c` — 0 dark pixels attached to or standing outside the rim, by the clerk's own decode as well as the fixer's guard — and the same carve had cut into his beard, jaw and hairline on the same side: enclosed cream holes inside the silhouette **max 938 px, p95 190, 11 frames over 300 px**, sustained 8.48-8.88 s, against **46 px** on the render it replaced, plus 1,265 px of open serration. At 405x720 it read as a torn white gash. Protrusion, LAW 48, edge clip, gate 3 and the watcher were all green on the frames carrying it.

**The stage that punched the hole was the temporal chair support inside the GPU track, not the ship post stack.** Measured frame by frame over 8.20-9.12 s on the saved masks: `alpha_v2` (flat+luma only) holes 0-161 px; `alpha_v3` (with the support, straight out of the H100) already 154-800 px; the local stable step and the post-stack guard only carried that forward (485 -> 944 at 8.56 s, and the guard changed nothing). The bug is one line of reasoning in `apply_temporal_support`: the carried support was gated on **darkness alone** (`plate luma < 60 + 10 codec slack`), and his beard, his sideburn and his hairline are dark. A support built from "pixels this chair owned on 20 % of the chunk" therefore owned his face on every frame he leaned into that column.

**The rule, now in code and in STANDARD.md as NO REPAIR MAY REMOVE SKIN.** A carried support is a *bridge over a gap in the current frame's own evidence*, valid only within `EXCL_TEMPORAL_REACH` = 20 px of this frame's flat+luma chair mask and worth nothing at all on a frame where that mask is empty. 20 px was measured: the bridge the anti-flicker support exists for (obj3's dropped lower wing, 3.8-5.4 s) sits p95 7.7 / max 19.6 px from the current chair, the support that ate his face sits 20-107 px away. Second rule: no exclusion may leave a pocket **enclosed** by the presenter — anything enclosed is handed back, in the tracker and again in ship before the polish and after the resample. Third: `ship.py` now REFUSES (`gate="presenter_loss"`) when guard-attributable enclosed holes exceed 50 px/frame or the guard removes more than 60 px/frame of luma >= 110, with the numbers in the message. A hole the guard does not touch is a tracker artefact and is recorded, not charged to the repair.

**No second GPU call.** `pipeline/sam2/support_refit.py` re-applies the deployed rule to the saved diagnostics — the old effective exclusion, the pre-temporal effective exclusion as the current-frame reference, and the pre-temporal alpha as the only place the wrongly-removed presenter pixels still exist — and emits `alpha_v4.mkv` plus its corrected guard in 8 s on the laptop. It imports the rule from `modal_app.py` so the local repair and the deployed tracker cannot drift. The delivered result: enclosed holes **max 52 px on 2 of 691 frames** (938 before, 46 on the prior render), 0 frames over 300, and every residual speck is at the same canvas coordinates as one in the approved prior render — the ship gate attributes **0 px on all 691 frames** to the guard. Serration 1,265 -> 20 px. Bright loss 0. The 90,877 pixels handed back measure **92.9 % skin-toned**, mean BGR (25, 38, 82), against (21, 27, 48) for what both mattes agree is not him. Chair removal was kept: the pre-fix reading was median 194 / p95 1,433 px per frame and the repaired matte reads median 6, with its residual confined to the four windows where he physically occupies the support region.

**What this says about the instruments.** The defect was invisible to every gate the factory had because they all measure the OUTSIDE of the silhouette — where the edge runs, how straight it is, what dark pixels are beside it. Nothing measured whether the shape was **complete**. The new gate does, and it is cheap: `fill_holes(alpha) & ~alpha`, per frame, attributed to the mask that made it. Sam2 app deployed as v23; mirror at `projects/personal/infra/modal/apps/shorts-factory-sam2/modal_app.py`. Cost of the whole repair: **$0.059** (Modal render $0.017 + watcher $0.042), zero GPU.

Rule for planners/authors: never draw a "game world" as a grid plane; draw platforms.

## AN OVERLAP EXEMPTION IS NOT A LICENCE TO DRAW OVER INK (geminitools, run 15, 2026-09-05)

**Not a chassis bug — a chassis blind spot, and it cost three renders.** The clerk
held all three `geminitools` formats on one defect: the terracotta "charge" ran out
of the plug's cord, straight across the plug's face (both prong slots, both
prongs, the outline twice) and then diagonally through the Gemini spark, slicing
its lobes. **721 px of red inside the plug body box, held from 7.60 s to 13.68 s**
(684 on the whiteboard, 715 on the cutout). The one object the video exists to name
was delivered with a line drawn through it.

`whiteboard_build.anchor_points` was innocent and so were the anchors: the two real
connectors landed on the tiles' virtual rectangles, level to 0 px and mirror
symmetric, and `assert_anchor_law` passed before and after. The offending stroke was
never a connector at all. It was a **decoration with a hand-written `d`**, and the
author who wrote it read "the charge runs the whole path" as licence to route it
through two objects on purpose.

**Why no gate saw it, and this is the transferable part.** Both lanes exempt exactly
this kind of ink, for good reasons, and the exemption is total:

* DOM lane — `data-overlap-ok`. A connector MUST carry it (it is supposed to touch
  what it joins), and it also removes the element from Gate 1's `anchorline` check.
  Anything else wearing that attribute is invisible to every overlap and gutter
  measurement in the factory.
* Whiteboard lane — `b.stroke(...)` is pen ink, not a rigid. `assert_spacing_law`
  reads rigids; nothing ever measures a gutter against a stroke.

So a stroke with `data-overlap-ok`, or any `b.stroke`, is **unmeasured geometry**.
Gate 1 was green, `prerender_check` was 0/0, `qc_pass` passed, and the Gemini
watcher raised **0 candidates on all three files** with `touching_or_clipped:
"none"` logged on every beat where the collision was on screen, fully settled.
Recall 0 of 3.

**The rule.** *An element that is exempt from the overlap gate must carry its own
measured clearance assertion in the generator, and the assertion must name the INK
boxes it is held off — never the wrapper, never the plate.* The geminitools fix
ships two of them (`assert_charge_clearance()` in `gen/geminitools_scene.py` and in
`gen/geminitools_whiteboard.py`): they sample the stroke's own path and refuse the
build under a 4 px / 4 u ink-to-ink gutter to the hero object's body, cord and
prongs and to the mark's ink box, and they write the numbers into the build record
as `law40_charge`. A future author who reroutes a charge cannot silently put it back
over the mark.

**Get the mark's box from its INK, not from its plate.** `cutout_core.mark_img`
sizes a mark by ink AREA and corrects the ink centroid, so the spark's real box is
`side x side/aspect` centred in the host's PADDING box — for geminitools, 84 px of
ink at core **498,200-582,284**, which is 17 px smaller on every side than the
124 px plate it sits in. A clearance check written against the plate would have
passed the stroke that cut the lobes.

**The route that is always safe:** start on the source's own bounding-rectangle
edge, TRACE the target's boundary (accepted-behaviour #10, a rim drawn *around* an
object), and terminate on an anchor — never cross into the box. Cost of the whole
repair: **$0.059** (Modal $0.026 + watcher $0.033), 108.3 s of batch wall, 3/3 PASS
with 0 watcher candidates, no cold namer re-bought because no bespoke object moved.
