Seven cold namers, five designs, three formats, and one object: a shape sorter
carrying *"small models for very specific use cases"*. Every failing answer had
the same shape — "three punched cards", "three shapes on a shelf", "three
geometric shapes", "toolbar with geometric shapes" — and the two rounds run here
isolate why, because each bought exactly one thing and no more.

**Round 4 bought the openings and lost the object.** Inverting the values (a
solid INK slab with the cream ground punched clean through it, terracotta pieces,
one seated / one falling with a motion line / one hole empty) is genuinely the
right way to draw a hole in this palette — the split's own round-0 namer proved
it by saying "punched **cards**", i.e. it saw holes. It still failed, and a
namer supplied the word: **"toolbar"**. A 2.3:1 slab with three marks on it is a
toolbar whatever the marks are. *The holes were never the problem; the container
was missing.*

**Round 5 bought the container and lost the openings.** Drawing the toy as a
three-quarter BOX — INK front face, CARD lid, the lid's far edge narrower than
its near edge, holes cut in the lid and squashed to 0.62 — made all three namers
say **"box"**, a word none of the seven had ever used. And all three then read
the holes as marks *on* the lid: *"an orange square, black triangle and black
oval **on its top face**"*. At 33 phone px a dark shape on a light plane is a
shape lying on it, and making the hole the same value as the box's own front
face merges the two into one dark mass rather than explaining either.

**The transferable rule: at phone scale, VALUE says "dark" and only OCCLUSION
says "through".** A hole is not proved by being dark, by being the ground, by
being the same colour as the object's shadowed face, or by having something
hovering over it — all four were tried and all four failed. What is left
untried, and what this run's notes hand to the next author, is a piece whose
lower half is *cut off by the hole's rim* (drawn as a partial silhouette, not a
whole shape held above) plus a lighter cut-edge on the far side of each hole so
the material has thickness. Budget two rounds for it, not one.

Second, cheaper lesson from the same run: **run the cold namer on the lane the
workflow specifies.** A first pass was spawned on Haiku and returned "pixel fox
on platform" for an object that a proper namer had already passed twice as
"logos on a step ledge" — the failure it reported on object #4 was real and was
reproduced, but three of its five rows were noise, and a noisy namer costs a
redesign round it did not earn.

### Postscript — the two-candidate method, and what finally shipped (2026-09-05)

The paragraphs above end with "budget two rounds for occlusion". Occlusion was
then built and it lost. The clip window whose bottom edge IS the hole's near
rim, the piece sunk in its hole, the tall upright block with its base swallowed,
the lighter cut edge on every hole's far side — a fresh cold reader looked at
that crop and said **"black box with three shapes" (unsure)**, the seventh
variation on the same answer in seven designs. **At phone size a viewer will not
read a hole in a lid, however it is drawn.** That is now a measured fact and not
a hypothesis, and it cost seven designs to establish.

What shipped instead is the method, and it is the transferable part. Rather than
guess an eighth time, TWO candidates were built for the fastest lane only, cut
at the same instant, and each was named by its own fresh cold reader that saw
one crop and nothing else:

| candidate | cold answer | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| the sorter, with occlusion | "black box with three shapes" | unsure |
| a KEY going into a PADLOCK | **"an orange key beside padlock"** | **sure** |

The second metaphor was not better drawn than the first — it was better KNOWN.
"Small models for very specific use cases" claims a fit, and a key in a lock
carries "this fits, and only this fits" without asking the viewer to read a hole
at all. Ported to all three formats it was confirmed by a fresh namer each
("Orange key entering black padlock" / "key next to a padlock" / "orange key
beside open padlock") and rendered 3/3 PASS with 0 watcher candidates for
$0.1224.

**The rule: when an object fails a cold read twice, stop refining the drawing
and change the METAPHOR — and prove it with two candidates and two readers
before paying for a render.** Two throwaway variant projects and two cheap
namers cost minutes; six redesign rounds on one idea cost a day. The mechanism
is already in the split generator (`SORTER_VARIANT` picks the design,
`SORTER_CAND` builds it into a throwaway project and build record so the
canonical project and geom are never touched) and it is worth keeping.

One detail worth carrying: both DOM readers hedged, and both hedged on the same
part — the SHACKLE ("a bag or a jar", "robot head or coffee machine"), never the
key. The whiteboard's version, one thin marker stroke with clear board around
it, is the only one that read **sure**. A thick stroke on a filled body of the
same value merges into one silhouette; the arch needs air.

## run 16's plantsite: one missing verb, three dead lanes, and the fix that lives in the pipeline (2026-09-06)

`plantsite` returned "split: no staged path | whiteboard: no staged path | cutout: no staged path".
Nothing had crashed and nothing was stale. Every prep stage was ok; all three projects were
build-green with strict geometry 0 errors / 0 warnings and prerender PASS. What actually happened:

**The ARTWORK author had no agent-spawn verb.** Its own return says it: `cold_reads_run: 0`,
`cold_reads_outstanding: 3`, `blocking_before_render: true` — and `verdict: PASS`. The workflow's
artwork gate only checked `verdict === 'PASS' && scene_handoff`, so an unread shared scene module
was handed to three format lanes.

**Two lanes improvised, one did not.** Split and cutout, with the same missing verb, launched one
`claude -p` per crop from /tmp and got real reads. Four independent readers named the shared peak
object **"flower"**; the intended object was "a website about plants". (The crop is not the
problem — the browser chrome IS in the frame; at 166x142 the flower is simply the whole silhouette,
which is the run-15 shieldstral rule again: identity that lives in thin chrome loses to identity
that is the outline.) The whiteboard author took the brief literally, could not dispatch, wrote a
dispatch brief for somebody else and returned with nothing staged.

**And then nobody owned the fix.** The drawing lives in the SHARED `gen/plantsite_scene.py`. Each
lane said, correctly, that it may not redraw the shared module — split's own note adds the reason
with numbers: seating the plan's sanctioned replacement moves LAW 40's two connector anchors, which
`visual_laws.py` recomputes from `#plant-page`'s box, leaving them 46 px and 19 px short of ink on
the laptop. A shared artefact with no live owner deadlocks the recording by construction, because
the repair round re-runs the LANES and never the artwork stage.

Three fixes, all at the source:

1. `pipeline/cold_read.py` — the improvisation, promoted. One independent `claude -p` per crop from
   /tmp, blind copies under a random token, **absolute paths** (run 16's first dispatch used paths
   relative to /tmp and two readers answered "file not found"), prompt on **stdin** (`--allowedTools`
   is variadic and swallows a trailing prompt into the tool list; the CLI then exits 1). Emits the
   exact `{names:[{i,path,name,confidence}]}` `phone-pass` consumes, and exits non-zero on a
   dispatch failure, because a reader that never saw the image is not a read.
2. `pipeline/production.py` — `artwork-pass` / `artwork-check` bind the shared module and handoff to
   a cold read of every bespoke object; `read_rows()` is now the one place reader evidence is
   validated and it refuses evidence carrying `dispatch_failures`. `daily-shorts.js` refuses an
   artwork PASS with `cold_reads_run: 0` or no `artwork_pass` record.
3. The ownership rule (STANDARD.md, and the repair-round clause in `daily-shorts.js`): on a repair
   round the shared module has an owner — the lane that takes `<run>/gen/.<vid>_scene.lock`
   atomically. "Not mine to change" is not a terminal reason on that round.

Regression: `pipeline/prep/test_regressions_2026_09_04.py`, the "RUN 16" block (11 checks -> 15).

## 2026-09-06 — kimiwork: the seal was won on one draw of a noisy instrument, and the lock the law names did not exist

The gate said `split: no staged path | cutout: no staged path`. Prep was untouched by it: all eight
kimiwork prep markers were `ok`, the MatAnyone matte was final, and nothing needed re-running. Both
lanes were build-green with strict geometry 0/0 and both held on ONE object in the shared module,
object 1, the app window.

**What the artefacts say.** The split ran four independent reader rounds on a BYTE-IDENTICAL crop
(sha `9459266e`) and got four different answers: "Browser window app icon" unsure, "Refrigerator"
unsure, "browser window" sure, "Refrigerator" unsure. The artwork seal, two hours earlier, had read
the same drawing once, got "browser window with app icon" sure, and sealed on that single sample.
Objects 4 and 5 are the control and they are worse: on crops identical across all five rounds
(`3837d9ff`, `a084e51d`) the presentation screen read sure/sure/unsure/unsure/sure and the receipt
read "document with download arrow" unsure on the very crop the seal had called "receipt", sure.

**So two different things were true at once, and the pipeline could express neither.** The window is
a real defect: two independent readers naming the same WRONG object off identical pixels is the
drawing, not the noise (it is 188x202, taller than wide, a bar across the top sixth and a dark tile
below, which is an appliance silhouette). Objects 4 and 5 are pure instrument: every reader named
the right thing and some blinked. `read_rows` gated a binary on ONE draw per object, so a six-object
sheet had almost no chance of a clean sweep in any lane, and the one sweep that did land is what
sealed the bad object.

**And the failure had no owner.** STANDARD.md has said since this morning that on a repair round the
lane taking `<run>/gen/.<vid>_scene.lock` owns the shared module, and that *"not mine to change" is
not a terminal reason*. That lock existed **only as prose**: no implementation anywhere in the
pipeline, no mention in kimiwork's own handoff, and `CLAIMS.md` telling every lane it does not touch
the shared scene. Both authors read the claim, said the forbidden sentence, and stopped. The gate
had no vocabulary for that beyond "no staged path".

Three fixes, all at the source, in `pipeline/production.py`:

1. `SEAL_ROUNDS = 3`. `--evidence` takes several reader files, comma separated, and `artwork-pass`
   refuses a single-sample seal by name. Three dispatches at the seal cost minutes; a seal that
   fails downstream costs the recording.
2. `consensus()` rules on the SET. The author still judges whether a noun is a synonym, per read
   (`reads: [{name, confidence, match}]`); the code owns the arithmetic. A second reader naming a
   different object fails the object however many rounds run; one in four or more is noise and is
   recorded; at least half the reads must be `sure`. No per-read judgement keeps the old rule
   exactly, so every existing lane still passes unchanged.
3. `scene_lock()` and `production.py scene-lock`: `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, reentrant for its holder,
   refuses another lane by name, releases with `--release`. `check_artwork` now answers a changed
   module by naming the holder and the next move rather than dead-ending on "evidence changed".

On kimiwork's measured numbers the new rule fails exactly one object, the window, and clears the two
the old rule was failing at random. The redraw itself is still owed by whichever lane takes the lock.

Regression: `pipeline/test_production.py`, 12 checks -> 15, asserted on the five measured rounds.

## run 17's eudisclosure: the gate agent that never returned, over a marker that said "ok" (2026-09-08)

**What happened.** Prep did not fail. Every stage marker for `eudisclosure` was `ok`, the batch log
closed with "PREPARED", and `matte_eudisclosure_v5_{cut,rim,alpha}.webm` were on disk at 1584x990,
25 fps, 692 frames each, sha256-equal to the hashes in `ship_v5.json`, from 00:45:23. What failed was
the `gate:ship` AGENT: it came back null on all three `spawn` attempts and never even wrote its
started sentinel. `gateErr(null)` turned that into the string "the gate agent never returned",
`gateWithRepair` could not tell it apart from a refused encode, and the recording spent its ONE
repair round on an answer that had been lying on disk for half an hour.

**The rule.** A NULL AGENT IS NOT A FACT ABOUT THE ARTEFACT. The gate is the only place in this
workflow where an agent's job is to read one file and repeat it, and that is exactly the job that
should never have needed a model at all.

**The fixes, both at the source.**

- `pipeline/prep/gate_marker.py` (new) is the gate's judgement in deterministic python and it always
  answers: the override wins, `--wait-s` blocks in ONE bounded command so a gate agent no longer has
  to keep itself alive through a forty-minute poll, a half-written marker is `unreadable` rather than
  a verdict, a missing one is `missing` rather than an exception, and even an internal bug prints a
  pollable non-final state instead of nothing.
- `.claude/workflows/daily-shorts.js`: both gate briefs now run that one command instead of inventing
  a monitor or a background loop, and `gateWatch` never believes a null gate. It spawns the
  one-command `marker:<stage> <id>` reader and uses what the marker itself says, so an
  agent-dispatch failure can no longer spend a repair round or lose a lane.

**Checks.** `pipeline/prep/test_regressions_2026_09_04.py` went from 13 to 16, the three new ones
bound to this recording's numbers (692 frames, `cf367be5…` ship source, $0.0185 track). The workflow
suite `pipeline/test_workflow.mjs` gained a fourth scenario: a null `gate:ship` must reach the marker
reader, must cost no repair round and must still run the cutout lane. Removing the fallback fails it.

**Also found.** `test_workflow.mjs` had been silently broken since the run-16 shared-scene change on
2026-09-06: its `artwork:` stub returned no `artwork_pass`/`cold_reads_run`, so the fixture blocked at
stage 8 and the review-HOLD scenario asserted against a workflow that had never reached a lane. The
suite guarding the workflow was passing nothing. Fixed with the stub.

**Collateral, and the remedy Miguel named.** Editing the workflow mid-run invalidates
`stage_cache.py` fingerprints. Seven of run 17's sixteen seals were valid before the edit; those
seven were re-sealed with `stage_cache.py save` and verified `found: true`. The other nine were
already stale for their own reasons and were left exactly as they were: re-sealing those would forge
a validity they did not have.

### run 17's second gate, and the two holes the first fix left (cursorworkspace, 2026-09-08)

Three minutes after the fix above landed, the SECOND recording of the same run failed the same way:
`gate:ship cursorworkspace` returned nothing, and `prep/stages/cursorworkspace.ship.json` had said
`"ok"` since 00:35:38 with all three matte layers on disk, 538 frames at 1386x990/25fps, sha256-equal
to `ship_v5.json`. Nothing in prep had failed, nothing was re-run, and no Modal call was made. But
the second occurrence showed two things the first fix did not cover.

**One reader is not a fallback.** `markerRead`, the thing written that morning to answer a null gate,
is itself an agent. When it comes back empty the workflow is exactly where it started. `gateWatch`
now spawns it `MARKER_READS` (2) times - fresh spawns, distinct labels and sentinels, on top of
`spawn`'s own three attempts - and if all of them are empty it logs *the marker on disk is UNREAD*,
never a fact about the stage. `gateErr(null)` now names the agent-dispatch failure and hands the
repair agent the exact `gate_marker.py` command as its first move, instead of a sentence that reads
like a refused encode.

**An `ok` did not prove its own files.** `gate_marker.outputs()` checked `is_file()` and nothing
else, so an `ok` marker over a truncated, empty, half-copied or stale webm still read `ok` and
`outputs` came back with two layers instead of three - and BOTH run-17 repair agents ended up
re-hashing the three webms by hand against `ship_v5.json`. A check two humans-in-the-loop had to do
by hand twice belongs in the rule. `gate_marker.verify_outputs()` re-hashes the three layers against
the manifest the ship stage already writes; a passing marker whose files disagree becomes
`outputs_incomplete`, which is not a pass and not final, so the gate polls (a layer still flushing
settles) and then repairs rather than building a lane on a broken matte. No manifest, no downgrade.

**Checks.** `pipeline/prep/test_regressions_2026_09_04.py` 18 -> 20, the two new ones bound to
cursorworkspace's numbers (538 frames, 1386x990, `cf367be5…` ship source, $0.01658 track, its three
recorded sha256, and the real bytes copied back to prove a good layer set still passes).
`pipeline/test_workflow.mjs` 4 -> 5 scenarios: a null gate plus a null reader must be retried, must
cost no repair round and must still run the cutout lane.


### 2026-09-08: Match descriptions to the Short

The factory publisher consumed VOICE.md, whose uniform two-sentence/follow/news-tag instructions bypassed the newer upload-to-youtube description advice. VOICE.md now owns transcript-based news/tutorial/explainer classification, concise or useful detailed copy, promised resources, and platform-specific CTAs/tags. Both runtime skill copies point to it; the existing title checklist is unchanged. YouTube Shorts URLs are non-clickable, so the long-form three-link opening does not transfer directly. The publisher runs description_policy.py before any pending-platform upload. Its source-hash/evidence and structural checks complement the required author semantic readback; they do not perform model classification. Existing queued/published posts are unchanged. Fourteen local regressions/register checks and three source-grounded previews passed; evidence: output/shorts-descriptions/2026-09-08/verification.json.

### 2026-09-08: A dash draw-on measures itself, and `pathLength` wins

Miguel caught it by eye on the delivered `hermesdoctor` split: the warning
triangle's apex and both base corners were open and the stethoscope's tubes
stopped short of the Y junction. Cause: the `draw()` helper copied into every
run-17 and run-18 scene module wrote a LITERAL `strokeDasharray:100`, which is
a 100-unit dash followed by a 100-unit GAP, repeating. Any path longer than 100
user units shipped with holes: the triangle is 547 u, the stethoscope stem
109 u, the grokstripe card crack 219 u, its connectors 174 u.

Run 17 had solved the same thing the other way: every drawn path there declares
`pathLength="100"`, which renormalises the path to 100 units so the literal dash
is exactly the whole path. Run 18's authors declared it on SOME paths and not
others, so the bug was live only on the undeclared ones.

The fix is one expression that is correct in both worlds:

    strokeDasharray:(i,t)=>t.getAttribute("pathLength")||t.getTotalLength()+1

A declared `pathLength` is the unit the dash is measured in, and
`getTotalLength()` still returns the GEOMETRIC length there - feeding the
geometric length into a normalised path sets a dash roughly twice the path and
POPS the drawing on instead of drawing it (measured on grokstripe's connectors:
fully painted 0.10 s into a 0.24 s draw). Neither failure is visible to the
Phone Test or the clerk, because both look at the drawing at rest, after the
animation has finished. Fixed in `shorts_run18/gen/{hermesdoctor,grokstripe,
saascut}_scene.py`; both affected videos re-rendered and re-staged.

Second finding from the same repair: `pipeline/edge_clip_check.box_from_geom`
could not read a plate box spelled as a MAPPING (`plate.box = {w,h,left,top}`),
which is how the cutout generator writes it, and it signalled that by raising
`SystemExit` - which `qc_pass`'s `except Exception` could not catch, so the
whole `cutout_checks_24_25` check reported ERROR. Both are fixed: the mapping
shape is read, and the guard catches `BaseException`.

### 2026-09-08: Open item — the exclamation mark inside the warning triangle

Miguel, on the delivered `hermesdoctor` split: "the exclamation mark ! is not
centered but I don't mind anymore, you can fix it in the next pass and rule
changes." Measured on the render at t=25.6 s, `tri_svg()` in
`shorts_run18/gen/hermesdoctor_scene.py`:

* horizontally the mark is centred to within half a pixel of the triangle's
  interior midpoint at every interior row, so the defect is NOT left/right;
* vertically the bar and dot sit LOW. In the 244 px rendered glyph the mark
  spans rows 111 to 206: the whole taper above it is empty and only 37 px of
  triangle remain below it. The docstring's own numbers say so (dot bottom at
  y 139, base inner edge at y 164, 25 units of clearance).

A triangle is not a box. Its ink is bottom-heavy, so a mark that clears the
base by a fixed margin reads as sinking. The next pass centres the bar+dot
group on the interior's AREA centroid (two thirds of the way down from the
apex, y ~117 in this viewBox) rather than hanging it off the base, and the same
rule applies to any mark set inside a tapering outline. Not applied to the
delivered file: Miguel accepted it and asked for no further render.

## 2026-09-14 geo (run 19): the cutout that took five attempts, and what finally worked

Miguel rejected the geo cutout three times ("way below anything we've done before", "it's cutting part of my face") and approved the fifth as perfect. What failed: (1) the MatAnyone2 soft alpha rendered fast-moving hands as translucent smears and welded the black headrest to the black shirt and cap; (2) hand-cutting the raw alpha with luma/window rules removed the chair but never restored the hands; (3) the SAM2 lane WITH the chair-as-second-object guard carved the image-right temple, ear, cheek and jaw on 1331/1335 frames (up to 27 display px) while every automated gate said clean. What worked, done by Codex Astra: redraw the frame-0 contour from the source with explicit exclude polygons, track with SAM2 from that contour with NO chair object (`no_chair_object: true`), finish with temporal 1 (temporal 3 clipped fast fingers), verify every frame against the six worst face cases and the gesture windows before installing. Rules: never patch an alpha by hand; when a matte is rejected on sight, delegate the matte to Codex Astra with the frame-level evidence and rerun the standard selection-and-track lane; a chair exclusion object must be checked against the face band before it is trusted; a gate verdict of "clean" is not a visual pass. Evidence: shorts_run19/review/astra_geo_matte/, final_geo.json fix_round_4.

Plan and artwork are one agent; seal rounds run concurrently; authors confirm sealed objects with one read; law cards per role; batch marker watchers; heavy-stage wave cap; per-video delivery with cover and captions; cap wrapper; selection preflight and retry; plan-time refusal of UI-glyph silhouettes. Everything before the change is under `workflow_versions/2026-09-14-pre-levers/`. ## 2026-09-14 fluxvideo (run 20): the matte fallback resumed a paid track that belonged to the OLD contour

The cutout lane held on a chair headrest lobe riding on the viewer-right
shoulder through the whole take, and it held AFTER the SAM2 fallback, which is
the lane that exists to remove exactly that. The fallback had not failed; it
had never tracked. `fallback_sam2.py` keyed its "a previous call was
interrupted after the paid track, resume it instead of paying again" shortcut
on the alpha's FILE NAME alone (`if (S / f"alpha_{a.tag}.mkv").exists()`), so
the 21:40 fallback copied the astra-reviewed mask (`e0fafdaa`, both chair
polygons excluded) into `prompts/kf_00000.png`, wrote a note saying "reviewed
frame-0 contour as the only prompt", and then shipped `alpha_fb1.mkv` — tracked
at 17:12 from the pre-review birefnet contour (`46bbf6ba`, the mask
`selection.json` still records as `base_mask_sha256`, chair included). The
give-away in the artefacts: the installed triple is stamped 21:41 while the
alpha it came from is stamped 17:12, the ship marker's `wall_s` is 35 s when
the track alone bills 80 s, and `chair_band` p50 went 728 → 2102 px — the
"repair" was measurably WORSE than the MatAnyone matte it replaced.

The fix is in the pipeline, not in the run: the tag is now bound to the
prompt. Every paid track writes `alpha_<tag>.prompt.json` naming the contour it
was tracked from, `resume_tag()` resumes an alpha only when that receipt
matches this reviewed mask, and a changed (or unrecorded) contour tracks under
`<tag>_p<sha8>` — its own file, its own `/vol/<session>` path. The same contour
still resumes for free, so a genuine interruption is not paid for twice, and
the caller no longer has to remember to pass a new `--tag` by hand. Regression:
`fluxvideo: the paid-track resume is bound to the reviewed prompt, not the tag`
in `pipeline/prep/test_regressions_2026_09_04.py`, asserted on the two real
hashes.

Two things that suite taught on the way: it had been dying on a `NameError`
because the grok1080 test was appended BELOW the `if __name__ == "__main__":`
block, so the last checks never ran and no tally ever printed; and that test's
ordering assertion matched `ship_all(` in the module docstring rather than the
call, so it could not have failed. A check that cannot fail is not a check.

Still open, deliberately not done mid-run: `pipeline/stage_cache.py`'s
fingerprint does not include the matte triple, so a cached `matte_review_<id>`
verdict is not bound to the matte it judged. Editing `stage_cache.py` re-keys
every cached stage in the live run, so it lands between runs.

## A whiteboard phone crop cut at the plan's time reads the PEN, not the drawing (fluxvideo, 2026-09-15)

`phone_test_page.py --plan` cuts every object at the time the plan declares,
which is when the object ARRIVES. On the split and the cutout an object is
simply there at that instant, so the crop is the finished drawing. On the
whiteboard lane the marker is still inside the box: the pen tip has drawn part
of the shape and is sitting on top of it.

Three independent cold readers, given the fluxvideo whiteboard's plan-time
crops, answered `paintbrush / paintbrush / paintbrush` for the pencil at 12.45 s
and `pencil / pencil / pencil` for the photo stack at 13.9 s. Neither is a
design failure. The pencil was half inked, and the photo stack had not started,
so the box still held the previous object's pen stroke. Re-cut at this lane's
own earlier approved times the pencil read `pencil` 3/3 sure, and the photo
stack STILL read `pencil drawing on paper` 3/3, because at 15.6 s the marker tip
is inside that box. At 19.5 s, the first instant the stack is complete and the
pen has moved on, it read `stack of photographs` 3/3.

So the rule for this lane: **a whiteboard crop is cut at the first instant the
drawing is complete AND the pen has left the box**, not at the plan's arrival
time. `production.py phone-pass` is right to refuse the alternative: its
`consensus()` only accepts `match` of `intended|synonym|different`, so there is
no vocabulary in which "the readers described the medium" can be recorded as a
pass, and an unchanged-drawing argument cannot be laundered through it. Moving
the crop is the honest fix; arguing with three readers is not.

## A lane with no phone approval does not render, and it looks like a missing cutout (fluxvideo, 2026-09-15)

The fluxvideo cutout shipped its first clerk round with no cutout in it at all.
The cause was four hours upstream: its cold read ran at 22:10, exactly when the
org monthly spend limit hit, so all five `claude -p` readers exited 1 and
`phone_reader_fluxvideo_cutout.json` recorded five rows of `name: ""`,
`confidence: cannot tell`, with the limit text preserved in
`dispatch_failures`. With no valid read there was no scoring file, with no
scoring there was no `phone_pass_fluxvideo_cutout.json`, and with no approval
the lane never got an `_rcspec` and never rendered. Every artefact was honest;
nothing reported an error at the top.

Two things follow. A harness failure is already refused as a read (that rule is
in `cold_read.py`), but nothing yet notices that a RECORDING has an approval
for two lanes and not the third, so the run can reach a clerk with a lane that
was never built. And a spend limit is not a defect: after the reset the same
crops read 5/5 clean on the first try. Re-dispatch is the whole remedy.

## A repair agent without a browser can edit the source and clear nothing (fluxvideo, 2026-09-15)

Codex Astra fixed the DRAFT MODE label in all three generators and rebuilt all
three projects correctly, then reported every browser-dependent gate as
BLOCKED: Chromium would not launch in its sandbox
(`bootstrap_check_in ... Permission denied (1100)`), so strict geometry,
`prerender_check`, the phone crops, the cold reads and the approvals never ran.
It did the right thing by refusing to call any of that a pass and by handing
back the exact commands with their exit codes. The parent session ran them in
about twelve minutes and all three lanes came out 0 errors / 0 warnings,
prerender PASS and phone-pass PASS.

The lesson is about how to delegate, not about the sandbox: **a delegated fix
whose verification needs a browser must be scoped to the source edit, with the
gates named as the parent's job from the start.** Astra's own note said exactly
that, which is why the round cost one handoff instead of a rebuild.

## The live workflow is project-scoped (2026-09-15)

`daily-shorts.js` lives at `~/Documents/Workspace/.claude/workflows/daily-shorts.js`.
There is no `~/.claude/workflows` directory at all. Every consumer in the
pipeline resolves it from the repo root and is correct (`stage_cache.py`,
`test_stage_register.py`, `production.py`, `test_workflow.mjs`), but
`shorts_run20/post_run_workflow_patch.py` had it spelled `Path.home() /
'.claude/workflows/...'` and would have died on its first `shutil.copy2`
before patching anything. It now resolves the Workspace path and asserts the
file exists.

## The structure test had been silently green-less since the plan+artwork merge (2026-09-15)

`pipeline/test_workflow.mjs` is the ONLY place the run-17 protection is measured:
a null `gate:ship` must be answered by the marker reader and must cost no repair
round. The nine scenarios in `workflow_dryrun.mjs` do not cover a null gate.

It had been failing since production v3 landed, for five separate reasons, each
of which alone made every assertion below it stop measuring what it names:

1. v3 merged the plan and artwork agents into one `plan_artwork:` label. The stub
   still answered the retired `plan:` and `artwork:`, so the merged agent fell
   through to nothing and the recording reported "no clerk - the plan agent
   returned nothing".
2. The `deliver:local:` stub returned no `package_dir`, which v3 requires, so
   delivery failed, was retried three times, and the cover and Drive stages never
   ran.
3. That stub asserted the brief contains `dependencies_reviewed`. v3 asks the
   agent for a `dependency_review` sentence set (the spec KEY that
   `production.py` reads is still `dependencies_reviewed`). The stale spelling
   threw INSIDE the stub, which the workflow's own retry logic caught and
   swallowed as a failed agent.
4. The Drive contract flipped. Drive is the archive, so v3 pushes for every
   delivered Short and skips only on an explicit `driveArchive: false`. The test
   still asserted the pre-v3 opt-IN behaviour.
5. `execute(hold, driveArchive=false, ...)` gave the flag a default of `false`,
   so there was no way to express "the key is absent". The absent case IS the
   default-on contract, and the parameter default was quietly testing the
   opt-out and calling it the default.

Fixed, and it now reports all five scenarios passing. The pre-v3 file is kept as
`pipeline/test_workflow.mjs.pre-v3`.

The rule this adds to "a check that cannot fail is not a check": **a check that
always fails is not a check either.** The dry run passing 9/9 was read as the
workflow being covered, while the one test that covers the null gate had been
red since the merge. When a workflow's SHAPE changes, every stub that names its
labels is part of the change.

## TRANSCRIPT IS TRUTH governs the captions, not a printed product name (grok1080, 2026-09-15)

Miguel says "Grok Imagen" on the recording and Scribe transcribed it faithfully,
so the caption pill reads "Grok Imagen now" and must keep reading that: the
captions are his words and the law forbids a visual correcting him.

The PRINTED LABEL is a different object. `GROK IMAGEN` was set as a plated label
in the top zone of all three lanes, and on the cover, as the name of a real
product. The official product is **Grok Imagine**. A product name on a label or
a cover is a fact about the world, not a quotation, so it takes the official
spelling even when the speaker said something else.

Fixed on the cover and in every outward-facing caption, title and tag (v2, with
v1 kept). Miguel declined the three re-renders needed to change the on-screen
label, so this Short ships with the label as rendered. The rule stands for the
next run: when a plan names a product, the printed label uses the official
spelling, and only the caption follows the transcript.

## A number carries its unit's case, and a bad path should say so (2026-09-15)

Two things went wrong while scheduling the day's batch. Both are fixed in code,
with a test, not in a note telling the next agent to be careful.

**1. The tag gate mangled a real word.** `execution/youtube_tag_style.py`
upper-cased the first letter of every token, so the tag `1080p AI Video` became
`1080P AI Video`. That is not Title Case applied correctly; a resolution, a
frame rate or a parameter count is written one way in the world and the rule
does not reach it. It blocked two finished Shorts at the publish gate, and I
first "fixed" it by writing the mangled form into their captions, which put a
wrong rendering into a deliverable to satisfy a buggy check. The gate was
wrong, not the tag.

`_number_unit()` now returns the conventional form for a number followed by a
known unit: 1080p, 720p, 4K, 8K, 60fps, 7B, 100ms, 50Hz. Regressions in
`execution/test_youtube_tag_style.py` (5 tests), including that
`validate_tag_casing` still catches a genuinely lower-case tag. The live
YouTube video that had already been uploaded with `1080P AI Video` was
corrected through `update_existing_youtube_metadata.py` and read back from the
API.

The rule: **when a gate refuses correct content, fix the gate.** Rewriting the
content to satisfy it puts the error in the deliverable, where it ships.

**2. A shell loop split three package paths on the wrong colon.** Scheduling
looped over `"title:time"` pairs; the titles and the ISO timestamps both
contain colons, so every package resolved to a path that does not exist.
Nothing uploaded, but the publisher answered `captions.json missing`, which
reads as a package needing work rather than a package that is not there.

Both halves fixed. `publish_short.py` now reports `no such package: <path>` and
lists nearby package names. And a batch is data, not a shell string:
`pipeline/publish/publish_batch.py --batch <day>.json` validates every row
before writing any (package exists, captions, all three exports, `at` parses,
`at` is in the future, no package listed twice), dry-runs each payload, and
refuses the whole batch rather than leaving half a day scheduled. Verified
against a batch carrying all four faults at once.

## The hedge was routed to a clerk nobody told (2026-09-15)

Two regression tests had been failing since before this session and I had twice
written them off as pre-existing. They were not noise. Chasing them found a real
hole.

`production.consensus()` used to REFUSE an object no reader was sure of. It now
PASSES it and marks it `hedged: true, clerk_must_adjudicate: true`, which is the
right call and is written down in STANDARD ("THE PHONE TEST"): a hedge is
settled on the DELIVERED render, where the object moves, carries its label and
lands on the word being spoken, which is the only view that can settle one.

The clerk was never handed the list. Nothing in the clerk brief mentioned
`hedged`, `clerk_must_adjudicate` or `phone_scores_*`, so every routed object
arrived nowhere and the second half of the rule had never run. The brief now
carries the handoff under the same discipline as the existing `phone_flag_`
file: read it only AFTER writing your own Phone Test answers, because it names
the intended objects and would void a cold read; then adjudicate each hedged
object on the render in motion and report a HEDGED OBJECTS table, SETTLED or
CONFIRMED. A hedge alone is never a CONFIRMED row.

The safety property underneath survives and is now what the test asserts: a
`sure` read that named a DIFFERENT thing, or that overran the five-word cap,
does not count toward `sure_agreed`. A confidently wrong reader cannot carry an
object; it leaves the object with zero sure reads and routes it. Two other
assertions were stale in a duller way: whole-dict equality against
`consensus()`'s return broke when the function gained two fields, so they now
compare the fields they are about.

Two lessons. **A test that fails on arrival is not background noise** - I
reported "two pre-existing failures" twice before reading them. And **a rule
with two halves needs both halves wired**: consensus did its job, STANDARD
described the handoff, and the sentence that would have made the clerk act on it
was never written into the brief.

## The production matte lane had no furniture check at all (grokemail, run 21, 2026-09-15)

grokemail's cutout matte shipped `"status": "ok"` and the stage-17 viewer test
held it on two independent conditions: a black chair tab standing on his
frame-left shoulder for the whole 43 s, and a pale slab beside his head for the
first four seconds that then vanished, so neighbouring playback tiles flickered
between a wide silhouette and a clean one. The SAM2 fallback then refused its
own alpha with `PROTRUSION` at columns 595:617, `bolsterfix` exited twice with
"insufficient removable pixels" (median cut 32 and 143 px against a 200 px
floor), and the Astra round could not reach Modal at all. Nothing was healed and
$0.00 of it was the model's fault.

**What really happened.** The reviewed frame-0 selection cut both chair wings in
the head band and stopped at the shoulder-arrival row. Three strips of the same
chair stayed inside the person: x644-694 y514-535 and x603-639 y531-544 on the
frame-left shoulder, x992-1073 y504-558 on the frame-right. MatAnyone was
therefore told that half of one connected dark object is him and half is not.
It held the frame-left boundary pinned to the chair for the entire take — the
matte's top edge across columns 596-631 has a standard deviation of **0.76 px**
over 216 sampled frames while the flanking shoulder columns wander by **16.35** —
and it needed **96 frames** to settle the contradiction, re-admitting the
excluded wing at alpha 12-40 until it did. That low-alpha ghost is the pale slab.

**Why every existing number said the matte was fine.** codexdetail, the matte
that PASSED the same gate the same day, reads WORSE on every metric the review
prints: chair band p50 698 vs 604, p95 5803 vs 4968, max 11242 vs 9164, IoU p05
0.9293 vs 0.9461. Soft-alpha counts the ghost as ordinary edge softness; the
component and hole counts binarise at 127 and never see it; the chair band only
looks at DARK plate pixels far outside the frame-0 contour. The two detectors
that DO own this defect — the frozen-column sweep in `sam2/modal_app.py` and
`sam2/protrusion.py` — live in the retired SAM2 lane and have never run on a
production MatAnyone matte. The fallback's ship gate found the same tab at the
same columns the first time it was pointed at it.

**The fixes, in the pipeline.**

- `pipeline/matting/matte_review.py` now measures two things and prints an
  `auto_hold` verdict with the metrics: `frozen_edge()` (runs of >= 12 columns
  whose top edge sd <= 1.5 px while the flanking 30 columns move >= 4x that —
  the pipeline's own "frozen columns are furniture" rule, finally applied in the
  production lane) and `background_haze()` (fractional alpha more than 14 px
  from the opaque core; a window of it >= 1.0 s is a HOLD, a single sampled
  frame is a motion-blurred hand). Measured: grokemail frozen x596-631 ratio
  21.6 and haze 2.2 s; codexdetail no frozen run and 0.2 s.
- `pipeline/prep/prep_batch.py`'s plate stage: `--skip plate` now REUSES the
  validated plate on disk instead of stamping a bare "skipped". `build_plate`
  has no reuse path, so a matting repair that only corrects the selection would
  otherwise re-encode `plate_wide_25.mp4`, break the identity the reviewed
  contour is bound to, and force a whole new selection review; a bare "skipped"
  left the production adapter with no plate path and it died on "No valid
  prepared plate".

**How the contour was corrected, and what was deliberately not touched.** Every
removed pixel was chosen by measurement, not by eye: the plate's per-pixel
temporal standard deviation over the whole take separates the chair (sd 0.8-2.4,
mean luma 3-32) from his t-shirt (sd 10+, luma 20-32), and the three exclude
polygons follow each measured component's own contour. 2,030 px left the mask,
none of them in the head/cap band or the lower/hands band. The dark static patch
beside his jaw at x705-723 y480-510 was LEFT IN rather than risk his neck: run
19 already cost three mattes to a chair-exclusion object that carved his ear,
cheek and jaw.

Regression: four checks in `pipeline/prep/test_regressions_2026_09_04.py`
(33 -> 37), asserted on grokemail's own numbers and on codexdetail as the
passing control.

## Run 21: the production matte path had no furniture gate at all (2026-09-15)

Two recordings, one delivered, one held. The run's real finding came from its
repair round, and it is a gate that was missing rather than a gate that failed.

`grokemail`'s reviewed frame-0 selection cut the chair wings in the HEAD band
and stopped at the shoulder-arrival row, leaving three strips of the same gaming
chair inside the person mask (plate x644-694 y514-535 and x603-639 y531-544
frame-left, x992-1073 y504-558 frame-right). MatAnyone then pinned the
frame-left silhouette to the chair for the whole 43 s: matte top-edge standard
deviation 0.76 px across columns 596-631 against 16.35 on the flank, a ratio of
21.6. That is a frozen edge, and a frozen edge is furniture.

**The gate that would have caught it existed, in the wrong lane.** The
frozen-column furniture rule and the protrusion gate live only in the retired
SAM2 path. The production MatAnyone ship path had NO furniture check and NO
background-haze check. The matte viewer (stage 17) was the only thing looking,
and it looks with an agent's eye rather than a measurement. `matte_review.py`
now computes `background_haze()` and `frozen_edge()` itself and returns them as
an auto_hold verdict, with four regressions asserted on grokemail's own numbers
using codexdetail - the matte that PASSED the same gate the same day - as the
control.

Note what the old numbers could not see: `chair_band_px` barely moved across the
repair (p95 4968 -> 4929, max 9164 -> 9040) because it is measured against the
reviewed contour, and the contour was exactly what was wrong. The measures that
moved were the new ones: frozen-edge runs 1 -> 0, background haze 2.2 s -> 0.2 s.
**A metric defined against the thing under suspicion cannot indict it.**

Cost of the whole run $1.371 ($0.229 per staged short), prep 15.7 min at a 1.89x
parallel win, repair 10 cents.

## A named workflow runs a CACHED copy, not the file on disk (2026-09-15)

Run 21 was launched as `Workflow({name: 'daily-shorts', args})`. The script it
actually ran, persisted at 08:32:23, still contained `DRIVE_ONE` and no
`deliver:drive:verify` - although the only `daily-shorts.js` on the machine was
edited at 08:28:21, four minutes EARLIER, and does contain the new version.
Three changes made at 00:32-00:40 were present; the two made at 08:15-08:28 were
not. So the name resolves against a copy cached earlier in the session, and
editing the file does not change what runs.

Consequence: the per-Short Drive agent still blocked the critical path ~11 min,
and the clerk ran at inherited rather than the intended effort - both changes
went untested while appearing to be applied.

**LAUNCH BY PATH, NOT BY NAME**, whenever the workflow has been edited in this
session: `Workflow({scriptPath: '<repo>/.claude/workflows/daily-shorts.js', args})`.
Verify after launching, before trusting a change: grep the persisted script the
tool reports for a string unique to the edit.

## Run 21 review: the clerk caught the symptom and missed the cause (Miguel, 2026-09-15)

Miguel watched all six renders. The Grok Build email short: "amazing". The Codex
one gave three notes, and two of them are gaps no instrument in the factory
could have found. Neither video is being fixed; the rules are.

**1. The label inconsistency UNDER the collision (now LAW 50).** The clerk
confirmed that the balance beam struck through BIG FEATURES. True, and the fix
list would have nudged that one label. But the same drawing already had the
right answer: SMALL DETAILS sat UNDER its pan. The real defect was that two
sibling labels took two different placements, and the collision was only what
that produced. LAW 39 passed here, because the label WAS welded to its nearest
object. Consistency INSIDE one drawing was never a rule, so nothing looked for
it. It is one now, and a second placement for the same class of label is a
CONFIRMED row whether or not anything touches.

**2. Nothing in the factory compares the lanes to each other (now LAW 51).** The
balance appears in all three lanes. In the whiteboard the pans follow the beam as
it tips; in the split and the cutout the beam tips and the contents stay put.
Every still frame is correct, so the phone test could not see it; the DOM is
correct at every sampled time, so the geometry audit could not see it; and the
watcher and the clerk judge each render ALONE, so neither ever held two lanes
side by side. The clerk is the only stage that receives all three files, so the
comparison is now its job: same beat, all lanes, do the parts move together.

The general lesson, and it is the one worth keeping: **an instrument that judges
one artifact at a time cannot see a rule about the relationship between two.**
Both misses are of that shape - label A against label B in one drawing, and lane
A against lane B for one object. Every check we own was pointed at a single thing
in isolation.

## Run 22: three plumbing failures, none of them about the content (2026-09-15)

Two recordings in, nothing approved. One recording was genuinely unusable and
Miguel dropped it after watching. Everything else that went wrong was plumbing,
and all three causes are now fixed in code rather than in a brief.

**1. A transcript belongs to a RECORDING, not to a RUN.** `prep_batch._raw_transcript`
looked only in THIS run's `intake/transcripts/`, so a recording transcribed in an
earlier run came back missing and the whole batch died in 0.2 s - cut
FileNotFoundError, plate "no cut master", cues "no tight transcript". Run 21
survived only because its launcher agent happened to copy the files in by hand;
run 22's did not. The resolver now searches sibling runs and copies the file in,
so the run stays self-contained. Cost: ~25 minutes and two dead prep passes.

**2. The matte must default into the RUN's folder.** `--sessions` defaulted to the
shared `pipeline/sam2/sessions`, so the matte shipped there while
`matte_review.py` only ever looks in `<run>/matting`. The viewer reported "no
matte exists", held the cutout, and the repair round could not find it either -
all while three healthy .webm files sat on disk. The default is now
`<run>/matting`. Run 21 worked only because its launcher passed the flag; run 22's
did not. **A path that one agent passes and another forgets is not a default, it
is a coin flip.**

**3. A first-frame contour review cannot see a tracker defect.** I approved
aieducation's auto contour with zero polygons because at frame 0 the chair sits
cleanly outside the mask. The haze gate then held the shipped matte: a streak of
chair hanging off the left of his head at 0.48 / 1.00 / 1.60 s, 4.0 s of held
background haze. This is the SAME shape as run 21's grokemail, where the frame-0
contour stopped at the shoulder-arrival row. The lesson is not "review harder" -
it is that the review and the defect live at different times, which is exactly
why the matte viewer exists as a separate stage and why its new measures earn
their keep.

**What the new gates bought.** `background_haze()`, added by run 21's repair only
a day earlier, caught defect 3 on its first outing on a different recording. The
clerk separately caught the X source card sliced at the left frame edge for five
consecutive samples around 6.5 s. Both are real, and neither existed as a check
two days ago.

**The bad recording cost nothing in compute and 71 minutes in waiting.** Its cut
refused in 0.0 s with NO INDEPENDENT WITNESS - nine attempts at the opening and
exactly one sign-off, which itself truncates mid-word. The gate then polled it
three times (28.7 + 28.8 + 13.2 min) before it was marked `not_a_short`. The
refusal was correct; the polling of a permanent refusal was not.

## cold_read.py: --tag does not namespace the evidence, so a second dispatch overwrites the first (2026-09-15)

Found by the run-22 cutout author. `cold_read.py dispatch` writes its evidence as
`<out stem>_r<N>.json`, and `--tag` only namespaces the blind copy directory, not
the output. So a follow-up dispatch meant to WIDEN a sample (`--rounds 2 --tag r2`)
silently overwrote rounds 1 and 2 of the original five-round set. The author
noticed, refused to score a set assembled from two dispatches - which would have
quietly dropped the two worst reads - and re-dispatched the whole set once as
`--rounds 5`, writing every discarded read verbatim into the scores file.

That is the right instinct and it should not depend on the agent having it. Two
things to fix: `--tag` must appear in the evidence filename, and a dispatch must
refuse to overwrite an existing `_r<N>.json` unless told to.

The same round exposed a second thing worth knowing: at `--rounds 3`,
`consensus()` refuses a single `different` read, because 1 > 0.25 x 3, even though
its own docstring calls one different name in four or more reads instrument noise.
A three-round sample is therefore the WORST size to use - it is large enough to
catch a stray read and too small to outvote it. Use five.

## Scheduled is published (Miguel, 2026-09-17)

A Short that is queued on all three platforms reads **Published** on its Notion
row from that moment, not "Ready to Publish". Miguel's reason, and it is the
right one: by then the decision is made, the slots are booked and the package is
already on Drive, so an in-between status for six hours only creates doubt about
whether anything is still owed.

Nothing is lost, because the per-platform fields hold the real state - they say
Queued until the sync reads the live post back and flips each to Posted with its
URL. Only the headline stops lagging reality.

`notion_sync.py queue` now sets it automatically once every platform is stamped,
so it cannot depend on anyone remembering. Drive archival stays where it already
was: at packaging, before scheduling.

## `Published On`: a per-platform tag, because "Published" was hiding a real gap (2026-09-17)

Auditing the inbox showed 100 rows marked Published, but only 45 carried TikTok
and Instagram links. The other 55 are shorts from 10-25 August, before
multi-platform posting began on 2026-09-07, and they only ever went to YouTube.
Nothing on the row said so: the headline status claimed "Published" for both
kinds, and telling them apart meant opening three separate fields.

There is now a `Published On` multi-select (YouTube / TikTok / Instagram) on
every row. A platform is tagged when it has a live link, or a booked slot, since
scheduled counts as published here. Backfilled from evidence across all 102 rows:
55 read YouTube alone, 47 read all three.

It is computed, never typed. `notion_sync.published_on()` derives it from the
package's own status file, and both `queue` and `sync` write it, so it cannot
drift. That matters more than the tag itself: the fields it replaces drifted
precisely because they were only ever set by whoever remembered.

One bug of my own on the way: the queue path's log line formatted values as
`v['select']` or `v['status']`, and the new multi-select is neither, so it threw
KeyError the first time it ran. Caught in a dry run, before any write.

## A test that borrows live state fails for the wrong reason (2026-09-17)

`t_run22_aieducation_session_is_resolved_from_prep` pinned its fixture to the
LIVE `pipeline/sam2/sessions/aieducation` folder and asserted the shipped triple
was still sitting there. When I renamed that folder aside - the very stale
duplicate whose existence caused the confusion the test exists to prevent - the
test failed, and it failed with "run-22 shipped triple is gone", which points at
the wrong thing entirely.

The logic under test only needs SOME directory holding the three layers plus its
plate. It now builds one inside its own temp dir. Two small things that fixture
taught: `resolve_session.shipped()` requires `plate_wide_25.mp4` beside the
layers, which is exactly what separates a real session from an empty convention
directory, and on macOS a temp path must be `.resolve()`d on both sides or
/var and /private/var compare unequal.

The rule: **a regression test may not depend on mutable state outside itself.**
Live run folders get cleaned, renamed and archived; a test that reads them is
testing the housekeeping, not the code.

## 2026-09-21 — A BAKED FILE IS NOT A LIBRARY (run 23)

The helper consolidation of 2026-09-20 made `pipeline/sam2/ship.py` import `media.py`. ship.py is copied verbatim into the shorts-factory-matting image and the client compares the deployed copy's sha256 with the local file, so run 23's first two mattes (cursorspacex, geminigems) refused with "Deployed finishing source differs" while primeagent's track was still running. Fixed by making ship.py self-contained again (its own `ffprobe_bin` and `probe_wh`), redeploying the app (8 s, layers cached) and adding `pipeline/matting/test_baked_sources.py`: ship.py, post.py and worker.py may import nothing from pipeline/. Also this run: claudesessions' cut refused on cross-check 2b (0.29 s drift at a restart, tolerance 0.20 s); Miguel asked whether a 0.2 s waveform disagreement should refuse a cut the transcript already places, decision pending.

## 2026-09-21 — A REVIEWED SELECTION IS A SENTENCE UNTIL SOMETHING MEASURES IT (run 24, claudesessions)

The matte review held claudesessions: a black gaming-chair wedge beside his head on every sheet,
chair band p50 2,993 / max 11,279 px. The frame-0 selection was signed `status: reviewed`,
`edits: []`, "the black chair back ... is outside; no edits needed", and the approved mask was the
raw BiRefNet mask with 6,822 px of the right headrest wing still inside it (plate luma mean 14.6).
`pipeline/matting/client.py` hands that mask to MatAnyone 2 as the only prompt. Nothing had ever
measured the claim, because the detector that can — `chairprompt.py` — was wired only into the SAM2
lane, and it had abstained here anyway: the right wing's bbox is 182 px wide (ceiling 150) because
its inner edge walks 789 → 664 as it descends, so the slant rescue now retries a too-wide component
on its own narrow rows, guarded by darkness alone (chair 15–25, beard/jaw 35–60).

New: `pipeline/matting/chair_audit.py`, run from `prep_adapter` BEFORE the paid track. It measures
every wing against the reviewed contour; a leak under 1,500 px is the reviewer doing their job (this
recording's left wing: 157 px), a leak that is not chair black is REFUSED and never carved ("that is
a body, not a wedge"), and a chair-black leak corrects the contour and HOLDS the track.

And the carve is not a cure, which is the expensive half of the lesson: the obvious repair was tried
and re-tracked (mask a39d3252, alpha 9dc321eb, $0.04) and MatAnyone 2 kept 9,077 of the 9,077 carved
pixels on every sampled frame, reproducing the held matte's chair band to the digit. It is a
refinement model and re-grows a contiguous dark region welded to his shirt whether the prompt holds
it or not. The contour is still corrected — `matte_review.py`'s chair band measures dark pixels kept
outside the reviewed contour, so a contour containing the chair blinds the one instrument that could
see the wedge — but the recording then goes to the chair-aware lane or to Miguel, and the hold is
sticky so a rerun cannot pay for the matte the audit just held. Five checks in
`pipeline/prep/test_regressions_2026_09_04.py` (36 → 41), fixture
`pipeline/prep/fixtures/claudesessions_chair_leak/`.
